defects.name: Kinetic Pinnacle
defects.detail: Nothing at all reaches the sheet: `sheetDiff` is empty, `registries` is empty, and the core.json record carries only level/category/traits/prerequisites/actionCost — no note, no marker, no field of any kind. The feat is `actionCost: passive`, so MainTab's `isActionCost` filter correctly keeps it out of the actions list, meaning the level-20 kineticist capstone has literally zero surface anywhere except the Feats tab. This is NOT a no_lane — the app has built exactly this lane and applies it to every sibling capstone. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts RECORD_MARKERS carries `{ on: 'condition', id: 'quickened', value: 'always on', note: '<source>: you're permanently quickened; the extra action can be used only to …' }` for `eternal-boost` (3266), `eternal-composition` (3267), `full-automation` (3274), `panache-paragon` (3275), `peerless-captain` (3276), `perfect-readiness` (3277), `supreme-spellstrike` (3287), `swift-paragon` (3290), `weapon-supremacy` (3297) and `abundant-vials` (3302) — nine of them level-20 class capstones with word-for-word the same "You're permanently quickened. You can use your extra action only to …" text. `kinetic-pinnacle` appears in no source file under src/ at all (grep is clean; the only hits are the audit JSON fixtures). The anchor exists: core.json conditions/quickened is present. This is also the shape Q11 prescribes — the effect cannot be shut down, so it is a passive condition marker, not a mode — and it carries the restriction note (Channel Elements / 1-action Elemental Blast / 1-action stance impulse) on the row where the player sees the extra action, satisfying the `note` requirement in the same stroke. One row of data is missing from a table that already has ten of its siblings in it.

defects.name: Favored Terrain
defects.detail: Six of the seven requirements have no surface at all, and the seventh is wrong. The core.json record carries no choice/effectChoices, so the nine-option terrain pick (aquatic/arctic/desert/forest/mountain/plains/sky/swamp/underground) is never recorded — and every other clause keys off it, so nothing downstream can exist. Absent: the swim Speed = your Speed (Aquatic) and climb Speed = your Speed (Forest/Mountain/Underground), including the "+10-foot status if you already had one" fallback; the Plains +10 land and Sky +10 fly (if you have one); the Arctic/Desert/Swamp prose (one-tenth consumption, unaffected by severe/extreme cold or heat, ice/snow and sand at full Speed without Balancing, bogs at full Speed overriding greater difficult terrain and the need to Swim); the "ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain" marker on Speed/Stride (compare the working shape at situationalBonuses.ts:3332 for unimpeded-journey, which does exactly this); and any gate on possessing the Unimpeded Journey class feature (unimpeded-journey exists in core.json classFeatures but nothing reads it as a condition). The single surface the feat does have is also spurious: situationalBonuses.ts:2220 gives every holder one star, targets [{kind:'speed'}], bonus "+10-foot status", when "while in your chosen favored terrain, if you have unimpeded journey…" — it is applied to Speed generally rather than to the named movement type, and stars fire on feat ownership alone (featSituationalFor, situationalBonuses.ts:3154), so it shows for all nine choices including the six (Aquatic, Arctic, Desert, Forest, Mountain, Underground, Swamp) that grant no +10 at all. Note: the empty sheetDiff is not evidence here — scripts/feat-evidence.mjs samples situational stars only for AC/Perception/saves/skills, never for kind:'speed', so a speed star is invisible to the harness.

defects.name: Control Tower
defects.detail: One of four requirements is delivered: FEAT_SITUATIONAL['control-tower'] (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:618) stars Perception at "+2 circumstance" — right value, right TYPE, and its `when` carries the positional condition inline, which is exactly Ruling M's chosen shape. The other three printed benefits have no surface anywhere. (a) Q2 requires the ACTION starred as well as the skill: there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry {on:'action', id:'seek'}. core.actions.seek exists and MainTab.tsx:525 / StatDetailModal.tsx:185 render action marks, so the route is live and simply unused. (b) "You and your allies don't have to succeed at a flat check to target a concealed creature within your overwatch field" has no {on:'condition', id:'concealed'} marker — the concealed condition exists in core.conditions and the route is already in use by multisensory-mask (situationalBonuses.ts:3317). (c) "reduce the DC of the flat check to 5" has no {on:'condition', id:'hidden'} marker; per Ruling G it must read as the DC being 5 rather than a separate −6 line, and choker-of-elocution's deafened "DC 3" is the exact working precedent. (d) No modifiesGrant or marker on overwatch-dedication, the record that actually grants the overwatch field — Principle A + C make this the one place the ally half is allowed to show, and core.json contains only 2 `modifiesGrant` occurrences in the entire dataset. Nothing spurious: the app does nothing the text does not call for.

defects.name: Dark Persona's Presence
defects.detail: The enemy-facing half is handled correctly: the free action reaches the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0]) with its trigger and the frightened degree table in its popup, which is the whole surface per Q4, and the emanation rightly gets no positional model per Ruling M. What is missing is the SELF-facing clause — "While your Psyche is Unleashed... You can Cast a Spell only if it can directly damage an enemy or object or can impose a detrimental condition or penalty on one" — which has no surface beyond being buried in this feat's own prose. By Q11 it is a mode (it ends when the Psyche is no longer Unleashed), by Ruling E case 3 a display-only one, and by Principle B the mode must carry the printed text even though the app cannot judge which spells qualify; Q3 additionally requires the sheet to make plain a mode is active and what changed, which matters here because part of the player's own spell list goes off limits. This is gold answer #3's shape exactly (Shield the Faithful's mode carrying Healing Sanctuary's text). The blocker is upstream: core.json has NO mode for Unleash Psyche at all — classFeatures/unleash-psyche and actions/unleash-psyche both carry no `modes`, and none of the 429 entries in core.modes references it — so there is nothing for this feat to ride on, and the feat itself carries neither `modes` nor `modifiesGrant`. The fix is two-part: give Unleash Psyche a mode, then have Dark Persona's Presence contribute its restriction text to it. Separately, the stored description lost two printed values on import: AoN feat-8327 reads "30-foot emanation" and "a Will save"; the app reads "in a when you Unleash your Psyche" and "attempt a save" (same import-loss class as Leverage Anguish).

defects.name: Fiend Eternal
defects.detail: One of eight requirements is delivered: grantsCreatureTraits ['fiend','unholy'] is stored and reaches the Details tab through creatureTraitsOf (derive.ts:1844 → DetailsTab.tsx:404), satisfying Q6. sheetDiff is completely empty and nothing else is stored on the record. Absent: (a) immunity to the realm's damage type — no `immunities` / `passiveEffects.immunities` (39 records carry one, so the lane is live); (b) the realm's planar location — no `choice`; the named list ending in "or some other planar space of your choosing" is Principle I's free-text case, and no feat in core.json carries a free-text choice at all (even Guerrilla Dedication, where the owner asked for one in gold answer #15, has only an option array); (c) the three-action concentrate telepathy activity — no `grantsActions`, so a printed activity with a printed cost and a printed trait appears in no actions list; this is the plainest single defect here; (d) the 10-minute enter/exit ritual — also ungranted, and its "only if you lack Seat of Power" gate has no route: the app cannot make a granted action's PRESENCE conditional on owning another record, only note the condition in its text, so that half is closer to no_lane; (e) no `modifiesGrant` widening Enter Seat of Power's destination; (f) the death replacement ("whenever you would die, instead 0 HP, unconscious, transported to your seat of power; after 1 hour, or 1 round with Seat of Power, regain 5 HP") has no {on:'condition', id:'dying'} marker, though the-survivor, draddeths-edge and hero-gods-bond all prove that route; (g) the crit-fail→failure adjustment on Recall Knowledge / Gather Information has no `degreeShifts`. ⚠ Finding worth more than this feat: `degreeShifts` has a complete reader — explain.ts:249 degreeShiftRecords plus degreeShiftMarkers, with DEGREE_SHIFT_TEXT/DEGREE_SHIFT_SHORT rendering both the skill star and the action row exactly as Q2 asks — but ZERO writers. `degreeShifts` occurs 0 times in public/core.json. The entire degree-of-success lane is dark across the whole dataset, so every feat that shifts a degree of success is currently silent.

defects.name: Pathfinder Agent Dedication
defects.detail: Two of the four live clauses are unbuilt; the Lore grant is correct. CORRECT: "trained in Pathfinder Lore, or an expert if you were already trained" — featGrantsAuto.ts:245 carries `conditionalSkills: { 'lore:pathfinder': { base: 'trained', upgraded: 'expert' } }`, the exact better-rank shape Q10 requires, and sheetDiff confirms stored.proficiencies.skills['lore:pathfinder'] null → trained. Access clause and wayfinder access correctly get nothing (Q5). MISSING #1, the serious one — "When using a skill untrained, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level instead of 0." The reader flagged this as having NO LANE; that is wrong, the app has one. derive.ts:334 `untrainedSkillBonus()` reads `db.feats[featId].untrainedProficiency` and derive.ts:420-423 applies it as max(0-untrained, that value). Exactly two feats in public/core.json carry the field — `eclectic-skill: {levelMinus: 0}` (identical clause, "equal to your level") and `untrained-improvisation: {levelMinus: 2}`. Pathfinder Agent Dedication carries no `untrainedProficiency`, so the fix is a one-field copy of eclectic-skill's value. The cost of the omission: sheetDiff shows every untrained skill unchanged on a 20th-level host, i.e. every untrained skill row is understated by the character's full level (−20 at level 20). MISSING #2 — "You become trained in one skill of your choice, OR expert in a skill of your choice in which you were trained." featGrantsAuto.ts:245 stores a flat `skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }]`. The needed shape exists and is documented at featGrants.ts:137-140: `conditionalRank: { base: 'trained', upgraded: 'expert' }` ("trained in your choice of X; expert if already trained" — Lion Blade uses it). With the flat rank, a player who picks an already-trained skill gets a silent no-op instead of expert.

defects.name: Deadly Poison Weapon
defects.detail: The record carries nothing at all: storedFields is level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only — no modifiesGrant, no note, no situational — registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and grep finds the id in no src registry and no scripts/data/*.json file. So both clauses are inert. (1) "When you apply a simple poison with Poison Weapon, the poison deals 4d4 damage instead of 1d4 poison damage" — Poison Weapon is itself a 1-action feat that appears in the actions list, and its shipped description still reads "they deal 1d4 damage with no saving throw" with no marker anywhere. A 12th-level rogue who took this feat is told 1d4, which is false (principle C: it must be reflected IN the thing it modifies). The lane exists and fits exactly — GrantModification.actionRider {actionId?, value?, note} at src/rules/types.ts:775-785, applied and gated on actually owning `from` at src/rules/build.ts:3435-3445, rendering a RecordMarker with an inline value on that action row — so `modifiesGrant: [{ from: 'poison-weapon', actionRider: { value: '4d4', note: '…' } }]` is all it needed. (Strict Ruling G replacement of the "1d4" inside imported prose is beyond the lane, but the valued marker is the shipped shape for exactly this.) (2) "the DC to resist that poison increases by 2, to a maximum of your class DC" — no marker on Poison Weapon and none on injury poisons in inventory (Ruling D + Ruling H would put it on both). Note the cap is character-derived and the actionRider `value` is a plain string, so the ceiling would have to be written as text rather than resolved.

defects.name: Tremor
defects.detail: The action entry exists (sheetDiff: actions[7] = "Tremor", from the feat's 2-action actionCost), but the text it shows the player has been gutted, so the entry states neither its area nor its damage nor its save. Shipped description in public/core-descriptions.json: "You unleash a small, localized tremor in a within 30 feet. Each creature in the area takes damage with a save against your class DC." The pristine AoN record (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-4224.json) reads: "…in a 10-foot burst within 30 feet. Each creature in the area takes 1d8 bludgeoning damage with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC." Three substituted templates — the burst, the 1d8 bludgeoning, and the basic Fortitude — were stripped at import. The correct sentence IS present in the app, in public/ast/feats.json under key `tremor`, and the Feats tab reaches it because src/sheet/FeatDetail.tsx:93 passes astKey/astId to DescBody; the Actions-tab popup does not — src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:660 calls <DescBody description={a.fullDesc ?? a.desc} …/> with no astKey/astId, and featActions (MainTab.tsx:255-264) never sets fullDesc for feat-derived actions, so DescBody falls through to the legacy markdown. Net effect: the same feat reads correctly on one tab and unusably on the tab a player opens mid-turn. Separately, the "**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d8" clause is raw prose for every character — a granted action has no damage field at all (types.ts has grantsActions: string[] and nothing for an action's damage or scaling; only strikes/blasts get derived dice), so at 20th level the player must add 10d8 by hand. That half is a genuine no-lane and I would not fix it here; the stripped text is the actionable defect.

defects.name: Earworm
defects.detail: Nothing at all is built. Empty sheetDiff, empty registries, and public/core.json feats['earworm'] is metadata only — no `grantsActions`, no `choice`/`effectChoices`, no `modes` entry (0 of 429 modes mention it), no `note`, no action record (0 in content.actions). Four of the five owed surfaces use lanes this app already has and none is present: (1) the FREE ACTION to activate the earworm — a plain grantsActions target carrying the Performance check, the highest-Will-DC rule and both outcomes; (2) the recorded pick of one composition cantrip, re-picked in play (choice / dailyChoices); (3) the display-only implanted mode required by Ruling F+N, naming the chosen cantrip and its three end conditions; (4) the note that lingering composition / fortissimo composition cannot modify an activated earworm. The 10-minute activity itself is the one half with no route: `ActionCost` declares `{type:'duration'; text}` (types.ts:136) but MainTab.tsx:224's `isActionCost` accepts only actions/reaction/free/variable, so a duration-cost activity can never reach the actions list — and no feat in core.json uses `duration` (0 of ~6,300; the 173 with no actionCost at all are a separate shape). So even a correct authoring of the Earworm activity would be invisible until that filter is widened.

defects.name: Fight Through Oblivion
defects.detail: The record carries nothing but metadata (level/category/prereq/archetype/aonId) and the sheetDiff is completely empty — `registries` is empty too, so neither harness limit applies. Two lanes the app demonstrably has are unused. (1) The dying/unconscious marker: `RECORD_MARKERS` supports `{on:'condition', id:'dying'}` and `dying`/`unconscious`/`wounded` all exist in core.json conditions — this is the exact precedent Ruling D names, and "the-survivor" is already in that registry at situationalBonuses.ts:3239. Nothing marks the Dying condition to say this character neither falls unconscious nor gains dying at 0 HP. (2) The damage-immunity state: modes support `immunities` and `resistances`, `all-damage` is a live type string (Unstoppable Juggernaut, Ghostly Resistance, The Tyrant Falls!), and a mode with duration "until the start of your next turn" already ships (adept-benefit-amulet) — so the Q1 duration objection does not block it. No mode exists for this feat, so the immunity, the no-healing restriction, the 4d8+30 Strike clause and the wounded-escalation cycle appear nowhere the player will look. A level-20 mythic capstone with zero sheet surface.

defects.name: One For All
defects.detail: The grantsAction requirement is met — sheetDiff shows "One For All" entering the actions list at 1 action. Everything else in the sentence is absent, and the printed text has lost a word it cannot spare. (1) THE FEAT'S OWN DESCRIPTION DROPS "DIPLOMACY". public/core-descriptions.json stores "…you can roll in place of the usual check…" while the AoN source (aon-2e-archive feat-6133) reads "you can roll [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) in place of the usual check" — the skill link's LABEL was stripped at import while the Aid link survived as a descRef. The sentence is now unusable: it names no skill to roll. The reader who extracted these requirements hit exactly this and had to flag the substituting skill as unreadable, which is the proof the text no longer carries it. (2) NO Aid MARKER. storedFields and registries are both empty — no RecordMarker {on:'action', id:'aid'}, though situationalBonuses.ts:3223 proves the route works (the-publican marks Aid). So the sheet nowhere records that this action supplies Aid's preparation (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing), nor that Aid gains the bravado trait when used this way — and a trait is what other records key off. (3) NO skillSubstitutions entry, so "roll Diplomacy in place of the usual check" reaches neither Aid nor Diplomacy; Principle D wants it visible where the player looks up the number. The ally-side bonus correctly produces nothing (Ruling F/N).

defects.name: Ghostly Resistance
defects.detail: The HP half is right: maxHpBonus {perLevel:-1} gives 208 → 188 at level 20, attributed to the feat. The resistance half is wrong at every level in BOTH directions, because the stored entry is the bare {type:'all-damage', value:'floor((@actor.level+2)/6)'} — the formula's level table is correct (1 at 4-9, 2 at 10-15, 3 at 16+), but it is the only thing stored. (a) THE EXCEPTIONS ARE GONE. The sheet shows a flat all-damage 3, which grants resistance against force, vitality, and ghost-touch weapons — the three things the text explicitly excludes. That is an effect applied unconditionally where the text conditions it. (b) THE NON-MAGICAL BRANCH IS GONE. At level 20 the text gives 5 against a non-magical source; the sheet shows 3 and offers no way to see the other value. The player is understated by 2 for the entire back half of the career. Root cause is one type: IwrEntry (src/rules/types.ts:310) is {type, value} only — no exception list, no paired conditional value — and a survey of public/core.json confirms every resistance on every feat and item carries exactly those two keys, so no record anywhere expresses this. This is plumbing, not a new subsystem: DefenseSource already has a `condition` string (derive.ts:1287) that DefensesPills.tsx:41 and VitalsRail.tsx:106 render as the clickable `*`, but derive.ts:1548 pushes a feat with no condition, so the route is unreachable from a feat record. Adding the exceptions and the "or 5 if the source is non-magical" as that condition would satisfy Ruling H's requirement that the open-ended "any other source that acts like a ghost touch rune" survive as printed text.

defects.name: Witch's Bottle
defects.detail: The record is completely inert. `storedFields` holds only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `grantsActions`, no `choice`, no `dailyChoices`/`dailyItems`, no `note`, no `focusPoolBonus`. `registries: []` (no situationalBonuses, no featUses, no modes entry), sheetDiff is empty, and there is no featPickGrants so harness limit 1 does not apply. Nothing exists in content.actions matching bottle/render-inert/witch, no mode keyed to the feat, no item. Every clause the text makes is unbuilt: the 10-minute/1-Focus-Point brewing activity (grantsAction), the hex pick filtered to hexes that target a creature (choice, and Q9 requires the picker show only legal options — here a subset of hexes the character already holds), the bottle as a daily-expiring object recording which hex it carries (dailyChoice), the Cackle branch and its extra Focus Point (note), and the 1-action concentrate render-inert action (grantsAction). The most serious omission is the focus lockout — "You can't regain the Focus Point you spent... until the potion is consumed or loses its magic" is the one clause that moves a number on the sheet, and a witch running with an outstanding bottle should show a focus pool one point smaller across Refocus and daily preparations. That last piece may genuinely lack a route: `focusPoolBonus` is a build-time integer and `refocusRestore` a build-time cap, and I found no play-state mechanism for a pool reduction driven by an item's continued existence. The other five clauses all have live lanes and are simply unwritten.

defects.name: Burning Demand
defects.detail: Everything except the numbers is right. The impulse enters the actions list (sheetDiff `actions[2] = Burning Demand`) with its 2-action cost and all seven traits; the four degree-of-success paragraphs are present as popup prose exactly as Answer #7 requires; the five commands are correctly NOT modelled as a builder `choice`; and "your class DC" resolves to a real displayed stat (src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:297). The defect is the printed damage. public/core-descriptions.json stores "the sigil ignites as it vanishes, dealing damage and damage to the creature" in BOTH the Failure and the Critical Failure branch. The AoN mirror record (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-8977.json) reads "dealing 8d6 fire damage and 2d6 persistent fire damage to the creature." Both dice expressions and both damage types have been stripped, so a 12th-level impulse's entire numeric payload is invisible, and the surviving "Level (+2) The damage increases by 1d6" rider has nothing to scale — at the level-20 host it should read 12d6 fire plus 6d6 persistent fire. This is corrupt description text, not a lane gap, and the app-side pipeline caused it (all four AoN text variants carry the numbers). The same signature is confirmed against the mirror in 9 other records: needle-darts, grim-tendrils, divine-immolation, phantom-pain, savor-the-sting, live-wire, sawtooth-terrain, worms-repast, dragontooth-leiomano. Separately and secondarily, resolving "Level (+2)" to the character's own level has no route at all — core.json feat records carry no heighten/scaling key (only `level`, `strikeDamage`, `critSpecLevel`) — but that is moot until the base value is restored.

defects.name: Lightless Litheness
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert — core.json carries only level/category/rarity/actionCost/edition/aonId, registries are empty, and the sheetDiff is empty. Both clauses are unmet: "When you critically fail at Squeezing, you get a failure instead" (owed a critFailToFail star on Acrobatics + a mark on the `squeeze` action) and "when you roll a success at an Escape check, you get a critical success instead" (owed a successToCrit star on Acrobatics and Athletics + a mark on the `escape` action). This is NOT a no_lane case: the exact lane exists and is live — `DegreeShift` in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3117 supports shift:'critFailToFail' and 'successToCrit' with skills/saves/actions fan-out, wired through degreeShiftRecords/degreeShiftMarkers (src/rules/explain.ts:249-290) so one authored entry reaches both the skill star and the action row. Sibling feats of the identical shape are already authored (e.g. RECORD_MARKERS 'experienced-professional' carries value "crit fail -> fail" on earn-income; the comment at situationalBonuses.ts:3114 cites `sure-feet`). The app also has both target actions in core.json (`squeeze`, `escape`). The Step-instead-of-Stride rider is correctly not modelled per Q15, but it has no note to ride in because no marker exists at all. Fix: add degreeShifts: [{shift:'critFailToFail', when:'when you critically fail at Squeezing', skills:['acrobatics'], actions:['squeeze']},{shift:'successToCrit', when:'on Escape checks (on a critical success you can Step instead of Striding up to 5 feet)', skills:['acrobatics','athletics'], actions:['escape']}].

defects.name: Elaborate Scroll Esoterica
defects.detail: "In addition to your daily scrolls from Scroll Esoterica, add a scroll with a 3rd-rank spell. At 14th level… 4th-rank… At 16th level… 5th-rank." The feat delivers nothing: core.json has no dailyTemporaryItems, no choice, no modifiesGrant; sheetDiff is empty on a level-20 thaumaturge. The lane exists and is proven by this feat's own neighbours — `grand-scroll-esoterica` (its direct successor, prereq Elaborate) carries dailyTemporaryItems with a spellRankByLevel filter, and `expert-scroll-cache` — whose printed text is word-for-word the same clause with Basic Scroll Cache substituted — was already backfilled as [{id:'expert', label:'Temporary scroll', count:1, filter:{spellRankByLevel:[{level:1,rank:3},{level:14,rank:4},{level:16,rank:5}]}}] in scripts/backfill-daily-items.mjs. Elaborate was simply skipped by that pass. Note that the project has ALREADY ruled the interpretation in that script's own comment — "one scroll whose RANK rises, not three scrolls" — so the fix is a single count:1 slot with the level-stepped rank filter, matching expert-scroll-cache exactly, not three cumulative slots. Consequence today: a thaumaturge aged 12-20 gets zero extra daily scroll from a class feat whose entire content is that scroll, and the base Scroll Esoterica picker (feats.scroll-esoterica.choice, flag 'esotericaScrolls', picks:2) still offers only its printed two.

defects.name: Kineticist Dedication
defects.detail: Only the last clause works. The sheetDiff shows Nature trained and nothing else; the whole first three-quarters of the text is unbuilt. (1) "trained in kineticist class DC" — the lane EXISTS and is unused here: build.ts:3657-3679 builds secondaryClassDcs from feats carrying `classDcGrant`, and six dedications carry it (fighter, ranger, rogue, alchemist, gunslinger, commander); kineticist-dedication does not, so no kineticist class DC row appears. Knock-on: expert-kinetic-control carries classDcRank {classId:'kineticist', rank:'expert'} and is therefore inert — it upgrades a statistic that was never created. (2) "and impulse attack rolls" — no impulse attack statistic anywhere; no field, no row. (3) "Choose one element…" — the choice IS stored (choice.flag 'kineticElement', six gate options) but is read by NOTHING: `kineticElement` appears in no file under src/, build.ts:4432 populates character.kineticist only when ownsClass('kineticist'), and the choice lacks `ownsFeature`, which is the flag (build.ts:2165) that would make the picked fire-gate/air-gate classFeature owned. So the pick is displayed and downstream-unreadable — no gate junction, no aura, no blast. This is NOT harness limit 1: registries is ['featGrantsAuto'], there is no featPickGrants, and the missing grants below do not depend on the pick. (4) "You gain a kinetic aura" — classFeatures['kinetic-aura'] exists (and itself carries grantsActions:['channel-elements']) but the feat has no grantsClassFeatures, so it is never granted. (5) "and the Channel Elements action" — both classFeatures['channel-elements'] and actions['channel-elements'] exist; the feat has no grantsActions, so neither is listed. (6) the "you don't get to use an Elemental Blast or stance impulse" restriction — nothing to modify, no modifiesGrant on the record. (7) "You gain the Elemental Blast action" — deriveBlastStrikes (derive.ts:2888) returns [] because c.kineticist?.elements is empty for a non-kineticist, so no strike, no attack number, no damage. (8) "does not automatically gain additional damage dice every four levels" — unbuilt in both directions: derive.ts:2896 computes `dice = 1 + [5,9,13,17].filter(l => c.level >= l).length` unconditionally with no suppression hook, and improved-elemental-blast carries no fields at all (only maxTakable:3), so it cannot switch scaling back on. Correctly delivered: "trained in Nature" plus the redundancy fallback — featGrantsAuto.ts:188 has { skills: { nature: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }.

defects.name: Grave's Voice
defects.detail:
The record is entirely inert: storedFields are level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/archetype/edition/aonId and nothing else — no `choice`, no `skillSubstitutions`, no situational entry, registries empty, diff empty. All three requirements are unmet:

1) The Spirit Lore / Haunt Lore pick is not recorded anywhere (the `choice` lane with kind 'array' is the shape, cf. archfiend-dedication's realmDamage).
2) The substitution is absent. `skillSubstitutions` is a live lane (derive.ts:366; 26 feats use it) and a conditional one surfaces automatically as a star on the substituted skill reading "<when> — roll <skill> instead" (explain.ts:322-331). Grave's Voice needs one entry covering BOTH Make an Impression and Request, restricted to incorporeal creatures.
3) Consequently no marker appears on Diplomacy, on either action, or on the chosen Lore's own row.

One genuine plumbing caveat for whoever builds it: the pick cannot drive the substitution today. `EffectGrant` (types.ts:1017-1046) has no skillSubstitutions field, and `skillSubstitutions.use`/`forSkill` are typed SkillId, so a `lore:` key is outside the declared vocabulary (0 records currently use a Lore as `use`). The workable shape is a recorded `choice` plus one conditional substitution/situational entry worded against the chosen Lore.

The GM-discretion sentence correctly needs nothing.

defects.name: Devil's Eye
defects.detail:
Two of the five mechanical clauses are missing and one surface is spurious.

MISSING 1 — the rank progression. Text: expert now, "At 7th level you become a master of Legal Lore, and at 15th level you become legendary". featGrantsAuto.ts:107 carries only `{ skills: { 'lore:legal': 'expert' } }`. On the harness's LEVEL 20 character the sheet reads stored.proficiencies.skills['lore:legal'] = "expert" where the text says legendary — a wrong number, not just a missing note, from level 7 onward. The lane exists and takes arrays (featGrants.ts:187, "Level-gated rank upgrade(s) on everything this feat grants"); this feat just does not use it. An earlier pass already wrote the exact fix (scripts/audit/chunks-fixnow/chunk-003.json, verified end-to-end through buildCharacter) and it was never applied.

MISSING 2 — Legal Lore in place of Perception. No `skillSubstitutions` on the record and no situational entry naming Perception, so Perception carries no marker and the player never learns the option exists. Note the shape: this is a cross-kind substitution, and the substitution lane cannot express it (a conditional substitution renders as targets [{kind:'skill', detail: forSkill}], which can never match a kind:'perception' ref). It IS expressible today as a hand-authored FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry with targets [{kind:'perception'}] and the swap in its `bonus`/`when`, so this is missing rather than no_lane.

SPURIOUS — the feat itself is listed as a reaction. core.json stores actionCost {type:'reaction'} on devils-eye, so the actions list gains a "Devil's Eye" row (diff actions[0]) alongside the correctly granted "Objection" (actions[1]). AoN feat-8404 has `<actions string="" />` and no actionType/actions field — the feat is passive; it GRANTS a reaction, it is not one. The player sees two reactions where the text promises one.

Correct and NOT to be chased: Objection is granted and its record carries Frequency/Trigger/Effect in its popup (principle E satisfied); Legal Lore does appear as a skill row (VitalsRail.tsx:1197 lists lores from proficiencies.skills). The +1 circumstance star DOES reach Legal Lore, Society and Diplomacy — situationalBonuses.ts:778 uses detail:'all', and targetMatches (line 3042) returns true for every skill ref including lore keys. The harness only enumerates the 16 core SKILLS (feat-evidence.mjs:117,144), which is why lore:legal is absent from the diff; that is a harness blind spot, not a gap. Starring all skills with the printed trigger in the note is Ruling H's "stay open".

defects.name: Cobra Stance
defects.detail: Five of six requirements are delivered; ONE trait is inert because of a one-character data spelling. Verified by building a level-10 monk and toggling the stance: Fortitude 14 → 15 (typed circumstance, pooled in deriveSave:201-212, so the displayed save DC — VitalsRail.tsx:608 renders `DC 10 + d.modifier` — rises with it; the separate dcOnly lane is for DC-ONLY bonuses like Mountain Stance's Reposition clause and is correctly not used here); poison resistance [] → poison 5, resolved live from `floor(@actor.level/2)`; cobra fang injected as strike instanceId `stance:0`, 1d4+2 P, group brawling, all five traits carried; agile is live (mapStep 4, attacks 15/11/7) and finesse is live (atkAbility 'dex'); the stance is an exclusive single-slot toggle whose note — "…and can only make cobra fang Strikes" — renders in the stance bar directly above the Strikes list (MainTab.tsx:905), which is the "unmissable statement beside them" the restriction requirement allows. THE DEFECT: deadly d10 never fires. scripts/data/stances.json spells the trait `"deadly d10"` (space) while the crit-rider extractor matches /^deadly-(d\d+)$/ (derive.ts:3055, and the weapon path at :2801); core.json spells it `deadly-d10` 115 times and with a space only 5 times. A/B proof: as shipped the strike reads `1d4+2 P`; with the trait respelled `deadly-d10` and nothing else changed it reads `1d4+2 P (plus 1d10 on a crit)`. The player loses the extra die on every critical hit. The same spelling bug makes kaiju-stance's `fatal d12` inert (verified: `1d8+2 B`, no fatal rider) and claw-stance's `versatile piercing` / vitality-manipulating-stance's `versatile vitality` non-canonical. Second, smaller issue in the stance engine rather than the data: the Fortitude popup itemizes only Proficiency 14 + Con 0 against a total of +15 — explain.ts's save branch never lists the stance's contribution the way its AC branch does (explain.ts:818), so the +1 is unexplained where Q3 asks the mode to make plain what it changed.

defects.name: The Dead Walk
defects.detail: The action reaches the sheet (sheetDiff actions[0] → "The Dead Walk") and the three Cursebound tiers are legible in its popup, which satisfies the note lane (Ruling G — the mark lives on the thing you are reading). Correctly no companion entry, no stat block, no star on spell attack (referenced, not modified), nothing for flanking. The defect is the stored text, and it is the worst of the three in this batch: the popup reads "Two ghostly warriors manifest within a of you" — a visibly broken sentence with the range deleted — and "each deal 4d6 damage" with the damage type deleted. AoN feat-6071's markdown reads "within a 30-foot emanation of you" and "4d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage". Both losses come from C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/import-core.mjs: the label-less macro strip (~line 281) eats `@Template[emanation|distance:30]` whole, and the @Damage handler (~line 271) rebuilds only the dice formula, dropping the nested `[spirit]` type bracket. A player cannot recover the emanation size from anything on the sheet. 16 records app-wide show the same "within a <gap>" break (items/whispering-staff, items/soulcutter, items/soulcutter-heroic, classFeatures/break-the-suns-legs, feats/slip-into-shadow, feats/undying-conviction, feats/zombie-horde, feats/leshy-familiar-secrets, …); 7 of the 498 sampled feats lost a damage type (deadly-poison-weapon, the-dead-walk, tunnel-roll, greater-enhance-venom, forests-heart, thlipit-contestant-dedication, lesser-enhance-venom).

defects.name: A Little Bird Told Me...
defects.detail: The form IS built and IS reachable — scripts/data/stances.json authors it into `content.stances` with `form:true`, so MainTab.tsx:292 surfaces it as a toggle even without the `stance` trait. The empty sheetDiff is only because the form is off by default; I judged the authored record, not the diff. It correctly delivers `speeds:{fly:25}` and `senses:[low-light-vision, scent imprecise 30]`, and its `note` carries the full printed text. BUT it is authored into the WRONG LANE. The app has a purpose-built battle-form override lane — `BattleForm` (src/rules/types.ts:2603) reached via `activeModes[].battleForm`, read by src/rules/derive.ts:1184 and explain.ts:757 — whose fields are exactly this feat's clauses: `ac` ("Your AC IS this while the form runs — not a bonus"), `size`, `strikes` ("REPLACE your own"), `speeds` ("Replaces the Speed block outright"), `senses` ("present is the whole list"). ⚠ **`battleForm` occurs ZERO times in public/core.json** — a full reader with no writer, so the override lane can never fire for any record. Consequences for this feat, all authored into the additive `StanceDef` (types.ts:2641) instead: (1) AC is NOT overridden — StanceDef has only `acBonus` (a typed additive bonus) and none is authored, so a bird-form character keeps their full armoured AC instead of 20 + level; derive.ts:1172 would have returned the override had the record used `battleForm.ac`. (2) Size is never set to Tiny — `size` exists on BattleForm but not on StanceDef, and 0 of 27 form stances carry one. (3) "you can't make Strikes" is not honoured — StanceDef.strikes is purely additive, so every weapon and unarmed Strike stays on the sheet; BattleForm.strikes replaces. (4) Land Speed is retained alongside fly 25 — stance speeds apply OVER the base block (derive.ts:3358), where the form should leave fly 25 only. (5) Weakness 5 to physical never reaches the defences display — StanceDef has no `weaknesses` key at all and derive.ts:1603 pushes only `resistances` from a stance (the sibling `modes` bucket DOES support `weaknesses`, so this is a one-key omission, not an architectural gap). Genuinely routeless clauses, worth naming separately: the animal creature trait (Q6 names the Details tab but no form/mode field carries a creature trait), the skill-modifier SET (+10 Acrobatics/Stealth take-the-higher, −4 Athletics — mode modifiers target 'skill' but are additive bonuses, never sets), and suppressing the worn armour's check penalty and Speed reduction. Scale: this is not one feat. 36 of the 38 polymorph-trait feats in core.json have no mode or form record at all (only dire-form and greater-transformation do), against the 44 battle forms Q3 named.

defects.name: Majestic Presence
defects.detail: The action entry itself is delivered — the diff shows "Majestic Presence" entering the actions list, via MainTab.tsx:257 which lists any owned feat with a real actionCost, and the temporary immunity is correctly NOT modelled as limitedUses. But Q4 makes the popup's prose the WHOLE surface, and that prose is corrupted in the shipped data. public/core-descriptions.json stores: "Each creature in a must attempt a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC." I verified the real text against the AoN mirror (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-5744.json, Player Core 2 pg. 47): "Each creature in a **20-foot emanation** must attempt a **Will** save…". Both the area and the save type have been silently deleted, so the one surface the ruling says must carry the whole action is missing the two facts a player most needs to run it. ⚠ **This is a systemic import bug, not a one-off.** Root cause is scripts/import-core.mjs:283: `.replace(/@[A-Za-z]+\[(?:[^\[\]]*\[[^\]]*\])*[^\[\]]*\](?:\{([^}]*)\})?/g, (_m, label) => label || '')` — it deletes every label-less inline macro outright, on the comment's stated assumption that they "have no readable text". That is false for `@Template[emanation|distance:20]` and `@Check[will|…]`, which carry the area and the save type. I measured the blast radius across public/core-descriptions.json: **334 records lost an area phrase this way — 88 feats, 179 items, 31 spells, 17 actions, 12 class features**, e.g. harm now reads "You disperse void energy in a ." and summon-kaiju "Each foe in a is pulled 50 feet". Fixing the regex to render these macros (emanation/burst/cone + distance; save type from @Check) repairs all 334 at once. Secondary, and a genuine no-route point rather than a build failure: the requirement that the popup RESOLVE max(class DC, spell DC) has no lane — a feat-action entry is name + cost + prose + traits (MainTab.tsx:259-266) with no DC field and no computed-DC surface anywhere. The player can read both DCs off their own sheet, so I did not weight it, but it is the one open design question on this feat.

defects.name: Monkey Spirits
defects.detail: The proficiency clause is not delivered. Text: "You become an expert in primal spell DCs and primal spell attack rolls." sheetDiff shows stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].proficiency = "trained". build.ts:4273 computes it as maxRank(caster?.proficiency ?? 'untrained', profile?.proficiency ?? 'trained') where `profile` comes from the record's `spellcastingGrant`; monkey-spirits carries no spellcastingGrant (storedFields has only innateSpells), so the rank falls through to 'trained'. The route exists and is used for the identical clause elsewhere — shadow-power carries spellcastingGrant:{tradition:'occult',keyAbility:'cha',proficiency:'expert'} for "You become an expert in occult spell attack rolls and DCs". Result: on the fighter/vanara host the primal innate spell DC and spell attack roll are two proficiency steps low (trained instead of expert), a number the player rolls with. Q10 does not excuse it — trained→expert only ever improves the rank, and maxRank already guards a class caster. Same defect on the two sibling records with the same sentence: kitsune-spell-expertise and nagaji-spell-expertise (both also lack spellcastingGrant). Second, smaller gap: the flagrant-burglary substitution ("have the monkeys use your Thievery modifier instead of your spell DC – 10") carries no marker on the granted Mad Monkeys entry — no `note` on the feat, nothing on the spell entry beyond spellSources naming "Monkey Spirits" (Principle C wants it reflected in the thing it modifies). CORRECT parts: innate grant is right — repertoire.5[0]=mad-monkeys with tradition primal and cast rank 5 over a base rank of 3, so the feat-stated rank is expressed and legible; grantedSpells[0]="innate:mad-monkeys"; spellSources names the granting feat; and the once-per-day use is delivered by the engine's default (build.ts:4254 records innateUses only when the count differs from 1, so an absent usesPerDay IS 1/day).

defects.name: Greater Enhance Venom
defects.detail: Clauses "You upgrade the vishkanyan venom you can apply with Envenom to greater vishkanyan venom" and "Envenom's frequency becomes once per minute" reach nothing. (a) The record carries no `modifiesGrant`/`actionRider` and no `grantsActions`, so the Envenom entry is untouched — and Envenom is not on the sheet at all: `public/core.json` has `actions['envenom']` but NO record references it (AoN's vishkanya ancestry feature Innate Venom, "You gain the Envenom action", is absent from `ancestries['vishkanya']`, which has no grantsActions). What the player can reach — the Envenom action description — still reads "Frequency once per day" and minor venom 1d4/1d4/1d4; the greater block (7d6/9d6/11d6, once per minute) is readable only inside this feat's own description. (b) The frequency clause was authored as its OWN pool: `limitedUses {max:1, per:'minute'}` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json), where the sibling Moderate Enhance Venom correctly uses `usesUpgrade {featId:'lesser-enhance-venom', max:1, per:'minute', every:10}`. Since Lesser Enhance Venom keeps its own `limitedUses {1, hour}` (retuned to 1/10 minutes by Moderate), `featUses()` returns TWO rows for one ability at level 17 — "Lesser Enhance Venom 1 per 10 minutes" and "Greater Enhance Venom 1 per minute" — each with its own spendable pip. That is precisely the failure `usesUpgrade`'s own doc comment (src/rules/types.ts:1446) says the field exists to prevent: "if given a `limitedUses` of their own, invented a second pool next to the one they were supposed to be replacing."

defects.name: Essence Overflow
defects.detail: CONFIRMED against the AoN mirror: the shipped text has dropped three inline-markup payloads, and the loss is in the app's own data, not in the harness. public/core-descriptions.json feats['essence-overflow'].d reads '…all creatures (except you) in a from your spectral dragon take damage with a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC.' AoN feat-8094 (Draconic Codex p.219) prints '…in a 10-FOOT EMANATION from your spectral dragon take 6d6 damage with a BASIC REFLEX save…'. So the area, the base damage dice and the save type are all absent from the record the player reads. The reader called this a blocker in the source text; it is repairable — the exact replacement text is above. Root cause looks shared with swaggering-initiative below: a Foundry-style inline-markup cleaner is DELETING @Template/@Damage/@Check payloads instead of substituting their display text. I measured the fingerprint across public/core-descriptions.json: 637 of 19,245 described records show it, 141 of them feats (e.g. unexpected-shift 'Roll a .', natural-illusionist 'Illusory Disguise, Item Facade, or .', boasters-challenge 'attempt a , , or check', armor-rune-shifter 'Energy-Resistant, , Raiment, , Shadow, Slick'). Everything else this feat owes IS delivered: it is an action row (sheetDiff actions[0]) with actionCost {actions:2} and the Requirements line in the popup; no limitedUses is owed for a 1d4-round cooldown; the enemy-facing damage and save correctly produce no sheet surface.

defects.name: Searing Restoration
defects.detail: The action itself is delivered (sheetDiff adds actions[2] = 'Searing Restoration', 1 action), but the healing NUMBER is gone from the app entirely. AoN feat-3054 prints 'You or a living creature adjacent to you regains 1d10 Hit Points'; the stored description in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json reads 'You or a living creature adjacent to you regains Hit Points.' — the '1d10' was dropped in import. So the base value is absent, and the per-level clause ('At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, increase the healing by 1d10') has nothing to scale from: on the level-20 host the popup should read 10d10 and shows no dice at all. textNumbers confirms it — the only number the record knows is the 1d10 from the scaling sentence. This is not Ruling E territory (nobody is asking HP to move a stat); it is the printed value missing from the text the action displays, which Q12's 'least confused' test fails outright. Not isolated: 67 records in core-descriptions.json say 'regains Hit Points' with no number, so the stripper likely ate a whole class of damage/healing tokens. The flat-check and minion clauses are correctly left as prose.

defects.name: Quick Recognition
defects.detail: The owner answered this feat personally (gold set #13: 'have Recognize a Spell apear as both free action and raction and on the pop up have explanation') and it is not built. Verified by building a level-20 fighter with Recognize Spell and then adding Quick Recognition: the action list reads 'Recognize Spell [reaction]' in both builds — the free-action cost never appears, and there is no popup explanation of the master-skill free-action route. Nothing in src/ references quick-recognition, and the codebase has no alternate-action-cost mechanism at all (no altActionCost / actionCostOverride / dual-cost field anywhere), so Principle H has no carrier here. What the app does instead is spurious: it writes `limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}` on the feat, the only thing in the sheetDiff. The owner ruled rounds are not tracked (answer #3, 'we dont truck rounds'), so a per-round limit should contribute no spendable resource — and worse, featUses.ts:110 classes 'round' as SUB_DAILY, which refills only when the player presses the encounter reset, so a once-per-ROUND ability reads as exhausted for the rest of the encounter after one use. That tracker should be removed, not just left inert.

defects.name: Qi Spells
defects.detail: The chosen spell never reaches the sheet. This is not the empty-diff harness limit — I made the pick and rebuilt. A level-20 monk with `effectChoices: {'qi-spells:qi-spell': 'inner-upheaval'}` produces zero spellcasting entries, no repertoire, and `focus: undefined`; the control (Empty Body, which carries a fixed `focusSpells`) on the same host produces entry 'monk-focus', repertoire {9:['embrace-nothingness']}, spellSources {embrace-nothingness:'Empty Body'} and focus {current:1,max:1}. Root cause, in src/rules/build.ts: grantForSpellPick (spellChoice.ts:41) returns `{focusSpells:[id]}` for `grantAs:'focus'`, but the focus-collection pass at build.ts:2246-2266 reads only `ch.options` and never `ch.spellFilter`, and applyAlwaysOn (build.ts:3293) handles skills, innateSpells and mergeEffect — mergeEffect has no focusSpells branch. So the grant is produced and dropped. It hits every record using this shape: qi-spells, advanced-qi-spells, master-qi-spells, grandmaster-qi-spells (the only four in core.json with spellFilter.grantAs==='focus'). Second miss: the Special ('select more than once, a different spell each time'). maxTakable:null makes it repeatable, but the pick is stored under `${featId}:${choiceId}` (Builder.tsx:1752 and shared.tsx:3925), so a second taking shares the first taking's single answer, and the picker offers no exclusion of already-chosen spells — 35 repeat-takable feats carry effectChoices and share this key collision. What IS correct: the picker is scoped exactly as Q9 requires (traits monk+focus, rank 1 → exactly Inner Upheaval and Qi Rush, the two the text names). Minor and separate: `archetype: 'bullet-dancer'` on a monk class feat 1 makes every taking count toward the Bullet Dancer archetype in canTakeNewDedication (build.ts:559) and archetypeFeatCounts (derive.ts:1327), which the text does not call for.

defects.name: Commander's Companion
defects.detail: One of five requirements delivered. DELIVERED: companionGrants.ts:57 registers 'commanders-companion' as kind 'animal', and companions.ts:355 defaults maturity to 'young', so the young animal companion with its own stat block and inventory is correct; the empty sheetDiff is expected under the standing companion ruling. MISSING: (a) Clause "determining the effects of your commander's banner … from your companion's space" — the `commanders-banner` class feature record has fields id/name/traits/rarity/source/level/actionCost/edition/aonId only. No permanent star, no note; Ruling M's positional-condition marker is absent. (b) Clause "always counts as one of your squadmates and does not count against your maximum number of squadmates" — the number exists and is displayed: build.ts:4405 computes commanderTactics.squadmates = 2 + Int mod, and MainTab.tsx:936 prints "{n} squadmates". This feat neither marks the companion as a permanent squadmate nor exempts it from that cap, so the sheet's squadmate figure is unchanged by a feat whose text explicitly modifies it. (c) Clause "it gains a reaction it can only use in response to your tactics… lost if it is not used by the end of your turn" — the companion's block carries nothing. CompanionMod.note (companionGrants.ts:176) is exactly the field that could hold the restricted reaction text; this entry carries only the boilerplate "Grants an animal companion — choose its type and advance it in the Edit tab." (d) Clause "When you use Command an Animal to command the companion granted by this feat" — no RECORD_MARKERS entry on the command-an-animal action, though RecordMarker supports on:'action'.

defects.name: Directed Poison
defects.detail: Nothing reaches Toxic Cloud. Clauses "modify its duration to be sustained up to 1 minute" and "modify its standard effect to include the following: The cloud doesn't move away from you each round…" — the feat stores no `modifiesGrant`, and SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3371), the lane built for exactly Ruling G's "put it on the spell, since that's what you're looking at when you cast it", has no `toxic-cloud` key (it holds 2 entries total). So a player reading their Toxic Cloud sees the printed duration and effect unchanged and never learns the feat rewrote both, failing Principle C. The description's `r` link to Toxic Cloud runs feat→spell, the wrong direction. The duration REPLACEMENT is additionally unroutable as things stand: SpellMarker is {source, when, bonus} — an additive conditional note — and there is no per-character override of a spell's own duration field, which Ruling G requires to replace rather than sit beside the printed line. SPURIOUS SURFACE: the one thing this feat does do is not asked for. scripts/data/effect-backfill.json writes limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}, and sheetDiff shows limitedUses[0] = 'Directed Poison: {"max":1,"per":"round"}', so a passive feat that is never "used" grows a spendable 1/round pip on the sheet. The printed "once per round" governs how often Sustain the Spell may move the cloud — battlefield geometry the app rules out of scope — not a feat resource.

defects.name: Psi Strikes
defects.detail: The feat's entire mechanical payload — the extra 1d6 force damage — reaches no strike surface at all, by any of the three routes the app owns. storedFields carries only level/category/actionCost/limitedUses; `registries` is empty, so there is no situational entry; core.json has no `strikeDamage`/`weaponTraits` on the feat; and there is no mode for Psi Strikes or for Unleash Psyche (core.json `modes` contains only the three psyche-salts item modes, and the `unleash-psyche` class feature carries just `grantsActions`). All three lanes exist and fit: StrikeDamageRider (types.ts:2930-2957) has `strikeName` AND `fromChoiceFlag` for exactly the "one weapon the player chose" shape, and mode-level `strikeDamage` with a typed extra die is live (see mode `item-iron-wine`: 1d4 fire on unarmed). Duration is not the excuse: ironblood-surge in this same batch gets a situational star for a bonus that also lasts only until the start of its next turn, so the app's own convention stars sub-round riders. Delivered: the activity appears in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0]) with Frequency and Requirements in its description popup, and the once-per-turn pip is a deliberate designed feature with a "new encounter" refill (featUses.ts:110-137 SUB_DAILY), NOT spurious. One live ambiguity I did not treat as the finding: Unleash Psyche runs 2 rounds, so Q1's "longer than 1 round gets a mode" and Principle B's "rounds are not tracked" point opposite ways for the Unleashed branch — but a star on strike damage is owed under either reading.

defects.name: Hypnotic Gaze
defects.detail: The modifiesGrant requirement is not delivered at all. The whole sheetDiff is one line — limitedUses[0] "Hypnotic Gaze: {max:1,per:'day'}" — and nothing whatever appears on Hypnotic Lure. I confirmed this against the data rather than the diff: hypnotic-gaze carries no `modifiesGrant` field, and the only record in public/core.json that mentions 'hypnotic-lure' is hypnotic-lure itself. This is `missing`, not `no_lane`: the lane exists and is built (draconic-paragon carries modifiesGrant with an `actionRider` {value, note} shape aimed at kobold-breath — exactly the shape needed here), so Principle C and Q8 are unmet by an empty field, not an absent capability. The result on the sheet is the worst combination: Hypnotic Lure looks unchanged, and the 1/day pip sits on the general uses list with no visible connection to it, where it reads as a limit on some ability the player cannot identify — the placement the reader's second requirement specifically warns against. Second, separate defect: the stored description is truncated. public/core-descriptions.json has "you can affect all creatures in a , rather than one creature within 30 feet" — the area was lost in ingest. AoN feat-6891 (Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 51) prints "all creatures in a 30-foot cone"; the source markdown is "in a 30- foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386)", so the hyphen-split number and the link-bearing word 'cone' were both dropped. The area is recoverable and must be restored before the marker's popup is written — per Q12 the truncated phrase must not be printed as-is. The 1/day count itself is correct (AoN: "Once per day, when you use Hypnotic Lure"), and correctly nothing is written for the sense lane.

defects.name: Triple Shot
defects.detail: The feat is entirely inert: sheetDiff is empty and the core.json record carries no mechanical field at all (level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost:passive/archetype/edition/aonId only). Because it grants nothing of its own, the empty diff is not by itself proof — so I checked the modification route directly, and it is unused. Principle C's lane exists and is exercised: `modifiesGrant` is consumed at src/rules/build.ts:3421-3446, which gates on the modified record actually being owned and then emits a RecordMarker {on:'action', id: mod.from, value, note} onto that record's row — draconic-paragon already uses precisely this to hang an actionRider note on kobold-breath. Triple Shot needs {from:'double-shot', actionRider:{note:…}} and has nothing; only 2 feats in the whole database carry modifiesGrant, and this is not one of them. grep finds no `triple-shot` key in RECORD_MARKERS or anywhere else in src/. So all three clauses go undelivered on the record they belong to: the same-target permission (a player reading Double Shot alone is still told the two Strikes must hit different targets — the misleading-record case Principle C exists to prevent), the –4 three-Strike variant, and the MAP exception ("the penalty doesn't increase until after you've made all of them"), which is the clause most likely to be silently contradicted by a strike display that steps MAP per attack. One nuance worth the owner's eye: the –4 variant is Principle H (an action appearing under BOTH costs), and the app has no field for a second action cost on one entry — no altActionCost/costVariants exists, and Quick Recognition, the owner's own Principle H example, is likewise unbuilt (its record carries only limitedUses). So the dual-COST DISPLAY may be a genuine no-lane; the same-target clause and both notes are not — the actionRider note route is built and available today.

defects.name: Loremaster Dedication
defects.detail: Only the first clause works. loreTrained is delivered — featGrantsAuto.ts:205 trains lore:loremaster (sheetDiff confirms). Everything else is absent or dead. (1) The +1 circumstance bonus on Bardic Lore is a DEAD STAR: situationalBonuses.ts:645 targets `{kind:'skill', detail:'lore:bardic-lore'}`, but the skill the app actually creates for the Bardic Lore class feat is `lore:bardic` (featGrantsAuto.ts:69). targetMatches does an exact case-insensitive compare on lore keys (situationalBonuses.ts:3055), so the two never meet and the star can never render on any character — Principle C unmet. One-character fix, but verified dead. (2) The rank upgrade is entirely unbuilt: 'If you have legendary proficiency in a skill used to Decipher Writing, you gain expert proficiency in Loremaster Lore' has no rankUpgrade, no conditionalSkills, nothing — and note that the existing lanes could not express it anyway, since `rankUpgrade` keys off character LEVEL and `conditionalSkills` keys off the rank of the SAME skill, whereas this triggers off any OTHER skill reaching legendary. (3) The usage restriction is unrecorded: no `note` saying Loremaster Lore performs only Recall Knowledge but on any topic, and nothing makes it an eligible option wherever Recall Knowledge skills are gathered (Principle D / Mastermind's Eye), so a player looking at the skill sees an ordinary Lore. (4) 'you can't increase your proficiency rank in Loremaster Lore by any other means' — a skill that is INELIGIBLE for skill increases is a shape no lane covers; the vocabulary has ranks and rank upgrades but nothing that forbids raising one, so the builder will happily offer it. (5) The Enigma Muse prerequisite WAIVER for loremaster additional feats has no route either; under Q9 those feats must become legally pickable for a character lacking the prerequisite, and nothing widens the pool.

defects.name: Advanced Order Training
defects.detail: Clause: "You gain the greater order benefit for the Hellknight order to which you belong." The record delivers nothing at all — public/core.json's entry for advanced-order-training has no effectChoices, no grant field, not even a `note`; storedFields is bare and the sheetDiff is empty. This is not a harness artefact (no featPickGrants, and no field exists that an unmet prerequisite could have suppressed): a level-12 archetype feat is a no-op. Everything needed is already in the data. The order is recorded: hellknight-dedication carries `choice.flag = 'hellknightOrder'` with all seven orders, and each option's description already names its greater benefit (Chain→Sturdy Bindings, Gate→Devil Allies, Godclaw→Blessing of the Five, Nail→Reveal Beasts, Pyre→Spiritual Disruption, Rack→Silence Heresy, Scourge→Seek Injustice). All seven benefit records exist as feats in core.json with real mechanics on them (devil-allies has innateSpells; blessing-of-the-five and seek-injustice have limitedUses). And the resolve-from-an-earlier-pick lane exists: `derivedGrant` (src/rules/derive.ts:2262-2268) is built for exactly this sentence shape — "You gain the instinct ability for the instinct you chose for Barbarian Dedication" — and is used by instinct-ability and implement-initiate. One caveat on reusing it as-is: derivedGrant only resolves to classFeature ids, while the seven Hellknight benefits are stored as feats, so it needs either a feat-target branch or the benefits re-homed. Related, outside my scope but the same family: order-training (the LESSER benefit, level 8) re-asks the player which order they belong to via effectChoices and grants only a note — the requirement's "must NOT re-ask" is already violated there, and whatever fixes this feat should fix that one.

defects.name: Second Ikon
defects.detail: The built record carries nothing but level/category/prerequisites/archetype/aonId — no choice, no grant, no note (public/core.json feats['second-ikon']; storedFields confirms). (1) "You gain an additional ikon" is not offered anywhere: ikons exist in this app as the exemplar class's ChoiceGroup 'ikon' (21 options with immanence/transcendence text, pickByLevel {1:3}) and as classFeatures (e.g. skin-hard-as-horn carries a daily choice in effect-backfill.json), but extraPickCount(build.ts:607) reads only pickByLevel and level — no feat can add a pick, and this feat carries no `choice`/`effectChoices[].grant` of its own. So the pick is never offered and nothing the chosen ikon confers reaches the sheet. This is the exact shape the owner already ruled on in gold-set answer 9 (Devout Blessing: grant the feature AND offer the choice), and the lane exists (cutting-without-blade uses `choice.from {type:'feat',traits:['ikon']}`). (2) The "your spark moves automatically to the other ikon" clause owes a marker on Spark Transcendence (principle C / Ruling D); the record has no `note` and no RECORD_MARKERS entry. Not a featPickGrants empty-diff case — registries is empty. Note for context (not this feat's defect): exemplar-dedication itself grants only the shift-immanence class feature and no first ikon, and the ikon item designation in InventoryTab.tsx:672 is gated on classId === 'exemplar', so an archetype character currently has no ikons at all.

defects.name: Invisible Hand
defects.detail: Delivered: the once-per-day pip (storedFields.limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'}, drawn on the Feats tab), and the Mythic Point pool the second clause spends from exists app-wide (src/rules/play.ts, MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS, reset per session). Four of the six requirements are absent, and `registries` is empty. (a) No mode for the 1-minute invisibility: core.json's `modes` bucket holds 429 modes and none is keyed to this feat — `eyes-that-see-eternity` is the exact precedent shape already in the data (duration '1 minute', senses/modifiers empty, note beginning 'Costs 1 Mythic Point'). (b) No second mode for the 'invisible for as long as you continue to Avoid Notice' clause. (c) No `*` on Stealth for the roll-Stealth-for-initiative trigger — situationalBonuses.ts carries no entry for invisible-hand, though the identical shape is already used for become-shadow ('when you spend a Mythic Point to Hide, Sneak, or roll Stealth for initiative'). (d) No `*` on Avoid Notice, although the action-marker shape exists ({on:'action',id:'avoid-notice'} on wary-skulker, situationalBonuses.ts:3293). Net effect: the whole sheetDiff is one unexplained per-day pip; nothing anywhere tells the player that invisibility is available, what it costs, or that a minute of it is running.

defects.name: Signature Spell Expansion (Psychic)
defects.detail: The feat grants nothing at all: storedFields hold only metadata (level, category, rarity, actionCost, aonId), `registries` is empty, and the sheetDiff is completely empty. The signature lane itself exists — BuildState.signatures with signaturesAt()/toggleSignature() at build.ts:1025-1048, and build.ts:252 names this exact feat in a comment ('Signature Spell Expansion grants two additional signature spells') — but nothing connects the feat to it. No picker offers the two designations, so Q9's filter (only spells whose minimum rank is 3rd or lower) does not exist; no +2 is reflected in the class's signature-spells feature (principle C); and there is no allotment anywhere for it to modify, since the builder's star chips (Builder.tsx:818) are ungated and let any number be toggled at any rank whether or not the feat is taken. Worse for the third requirement: the play-side toggle at SpellsTab.tsx:606-613 enforces one signature per rank ('toggling a new one drops any existing same-rank signature'), so on the sheet the extra designations are actively removed rather than merely unrecorded.

defects.name: Ranged Combatant
defects.detail: The eidolon never gains the attack. Clause: "It gains a ranged unarmed attack with a range increment of 30 feet that deals 1d4 damage and has the magical and propulsive traits." storedFields carry ONLY a `choice` (flag `rangedCombatant`, 10 damage-type options); sheetDiff is empty and registries is empty. Nothing in src reads the `rangedCombatant` flag (grep: zero hits outside the data), so the pick writes through to nothing — there is no strike for it to type. This is not a no-lane: the route exists and is used for a near-identical record. COMPANION_MODS in src/rules/companionGrants.ts carries `grantedStrikes?: {name, dice, die, damageType, range, traits, note}[]` (line 162), consumed onto the companion block at src/rules/companions.ts:447, and `billowing-wings` (line ~236) is the same sentence — "gust ranged unarmed attack, 1d4 bludgeoning, range 30, air and propulsive" — built as `{dice:1, die:'d4', damageType:'bludgeoning', range:30, traits:['air','propulsive','range-increment-30','unarmed']}`. Ranged Combatant has no COMPANION_MODS entry at all (17 eidolon-kind mods exist; this is not one), so the eidolon's stat block is unchanged. Note the extension needed: CompanionMod.grantedStrikes has a fixed `damageType` and no way to read a player choice, so wiring the pick through needs a choice-aware damageType (the player-side feat lane already does this — build.ts:1369 passes `f.choice?.value` into a feat's own grantedStrikes). Secondary, lower-severity: the stored option list has TEN entries — the printed nine plus `spirit` — offered to every eidolon unconditionally, while the text gates the extra alignment damage type on "a celestial, fiend, or monitor with an alignment other than true neutral" (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick). `spirit` is a defensible remaster rendering of the alignment clause, but it is ungated.

defects.name: Kindle Inner Flames
defects.detail: Three of the five requirements are undelivered. (1) YOUR half of the +1 status bonus is never a real number. The feat has the `stance` trait and core.json.stances['kindle-inner-flames'] exists, so MainTab's exclusive stance toggle picks it up — but that stance record carries ONLY a `note`; it has no `saves` block. Comparable stances DO carry one (cobra-stance and assume-earths-mantle both ship `saves:{fortitude:{value:1,type:'circumstance'}}`, applied in derive while active), so the route exists and is used elsewhere. Instead the bonus lives at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:470 as a display-only star ("+1 status (+2 at 12th level)", when: "while you're in the Kindle Inner Flames stance…") on reflex and acrobatics — and that file's own header says "It is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number." Q11 makes a shut-down-able effect a mode, and Q1's Shield the Faithful shape says the mode carries REAL NUMBERS for your half and text for the ally half; you always shed the embers yourself, so Ruling M's aura caveat does not apply to your half. At the level-20 host the sheet shows no Reflex/Acrobatics number at all for a bonus that should be +2. (2) No indication on Strikes for "When an affected creature takes a move action, its Strikes deal an extra 2 damage until the end of its turn." `strikeDamage` is a supported SituationalTarget kind and is used by 204 other entries (pennant-of-victory, warpipes, telluric-power), but kindle-inner-flames targets only save:reflex and skill:acrobatics. Q1 makes this indication-only (no computed number), and Ruling D + Q2 put the indication on the Strike itself. (3) The level-12 rescaling of the Strike rider is surfaced nowhere: the stance note stops at "...Strikes deal an extra 2 fire damage until end of turn after they take a move action" and never mentions that at 12th the Strikes gain the *Flaming* rune instead — principle B requires the mode to print the full text. Only the save/skill half of the level-12 clause is carried ("(+2 at 12th)"). Delivered correctly: the feat itself appears in the actions list at its 1-action cost (actions[7]), the stance toggle exists, and the ally half is text-only per Ruling F/N. One further clause has no route rather than a defect: "can Step as a free action once per round" needs principle H's both-costs shape (gold-set #13) and the app has no alternate-cost mechanism — core.json actions carry a single `actionCost`, there is no altCost/second-listing field anywhere in src/ or the data, and quick-recognition itself is stored as a bare passive with limitedUses 1/round. Correctly, no limitedUses pip is owed here (scripts/apply-self-uses.mjs deliberately excludes this feat as an ally-facing frequency).

defects.name: Claim Cardinal Domains
defects.detail: The feat's central mechanic — claiming domains — is entirely absent, and `sheetDiff` is empty. `storedFields` carries only `focusPoolBonus: 1`, `archetype: 'godling'`, and a single free-text daily choice (`choice: {flag:'activeDomain', kind:'text', daily:true}`) whose own note admits "no domain filter exists in `from`, so this is free text". Undelivered: (1) "You can lay claim to up to three additional domains, to a total maximum of four" — no `domains`, no `alternateDomains`, no `effectChoices`, no pick of any kind, and no counter that sees the domain already claimed by Godling Dedication (which DOES model its single claim properly, via `effectChoices` with one option per domain each granting that domain's initial focus spell — so the shape exists and this feat simply does not use it); (2) "you can choose not to lay claim to one or more domains immediately" — no persistent empty slots (the Q14 point-8 shape); (3) "This domain remains a part of your portfolio forever and cannot be changed" — no one-time-write lock (Q14 point 9), which is the opposite of an ordinary re-editable builder pick; (4) "You learn the advanced domain spell for any domain that you have claimed" — zero focus spells are granted; instead the record carries a bare `focusPoolBonus: 1`, which the text never mentions, so the character gains a Focus Point with no spell to spend it on and is short up to three advanced domain spells; (5) "spend a Mythic Point as a single action to claim a domain" — no `grantsActions`, no action of any cost, even though the Mythic Point resource exists and is tracked (play.ts:44, MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS); (6) "spend a Mythic Point to overcharge … for the next minute" — no `modes` entry (a >1-round duration earns a mode per Q1, and Q3 requires it be plain a mode is running and what it overrode). Only the daily active-domain choice is present, as free text (legitimate per Principle I, though Q9 wants the list filtered to the claimed domains, which requires (1) to exist first), and its note does at least mention the mid-day switch and the post-overcharge retention.

defects.name: Plant Shape
defects.detail: Only the innate-spell half is built. `innateSpells: [{spellId:'plant-form', tradition:'primal', usesPerDay:1, heightenHalfLevel:true}]` — the rank IS a live formula (build.ts:4226 `Math.max(base, Math.ceil(level/2))`, which equals a druid's highest slot rank at every level; the diff puts plant-form in `repertoire.10` on a level-20 druid) and the 1/day use is stored, so those two requirements are met. Missing: (a) 'resistance 5 to poison whenever you're polymorphed using untamed form' — nothing in the record, no `resistances`, no situational, and there is no untamed-form mode in core.json's 429 modes for it to ride on, even though Q3 decided battle forms get modes; the harness detected the number (`textNumbers: resistance 5`) and nothing consumes it. (b) 'add the shapes listed in Plant Form to your Untamed Form list' — no `modifiesGrant`, no note; the Untamed Form record (feat `untamed-form` → focus spell `untamed-form`) carries no shape list and no marker, so Principle C is unsatisfied. Both gaps are systemic across the whole shape family: insect-shape, ferocious-shape, soaring-shape, elemental-shape, dragon-shape and monstrosity-shape all store `{}` for these clauses (elemental-shape's 'resistance 5 to fire' and dragon-shape's 'resistance 5 to bludgeoning or poison' are equally absent). SEPARATE, SPURIOUS: the innate grant is unconditional. The text gives Plant Form ONLY 'if you don't have untamed form', but nothing gates the grant, so a druid who has Untamed Form (the other half of the feat's own prerequisite line, 'leaf order or Untamed Form') gets a 1/day Plant Form the text does not give them.

defects.name: Proteankin
defects.detail: Only the save clause is built: the diff stars Fortitude, Reflex and Will with `when: 'vs effects that would make you controlled'` and `bonus: '+1 circumstance'` — correct type, kept out of the flat totals (Ruling B), all three saves per Q2, and left deliberately broad per Ruling H. Missing entirely: 'resistance to a single damage type equal to half your level' plus the daily determination of acid/electricity/sonic. No `resistances`, no `passiveEffects.resistances`, no `choice`, no `effectChoices` — the record stores only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, and the defences diff is empty, so a 20th-level character loses a resistance 10 the text gives them. Both halves are squarely in-lane and used elsewhere: level-scaling resistance formulas (`{type, value:'floor(@actor.level/2)'}`) appear on 108 records, a chosen-type resistance via `effectChoices[].grant.resistances` is the standard shape (nephilim-resistance, draconic-resistance, wormskin, perfect-resistance), and the once-a-day re-set is `choice: {daily: true}` — 71 records use daily choices, with jotunborn Planar Resilience the exact 'which resistance today' precedent. Recording a randomly rolled type rather than a freely picked one uses the same storage, so this is unbuilt, not unbuildable.

defects.name: Creature of Myth
defects.detail: The record carries ONLY a bare `choice` (5 labelled options, kind 'array') and nothing else — core.json feats['creature-of-myth'] has no companion mod, no grantsActions, no sub-choice, no option descriptions. Four requirements are unbuilt, and the lanes for three of them exist and are heavily used: (1) NONE of the five options' effects reach the united companion's stat block. `COMPANION_MODS` in src/rules/companionGrants.ts:179 expresses exactly these shapes — `senses` (all-around vision), `maxHpBonus` (+30), `iwr` ("weakness 10 cold iron"), `speeds:{fly:'land'}` + note (mount ability), `note` (the Baleful Body retaliation) — and 'aon-celestial-mount' is a near-identical precedent (darkvision + maxHpBonus 40 + flyEqualsLand + weakness 10). There is no 'creature-of-myth' key. Principle C says the effect must be reflected in the companion; absence from the CHARACTER sheet is correct, absence from the companion's block is not. (2) No `grantsActions` for the five Mythic-Point activities (2-action cone/line, the double Strike, the concentrate-trait aura extension, the two-action Fly-and-Strike, the fast-healing activation) — so the player who picks an option is taught no new activity anywhere. (3) No dependent second choice for Baleful Body's acid/fire/poison or Energy Aegis's acid/cold/electricity/fire, so neither the retaliation damage type nor the immunity/trait the +1 status bonus keys off is ever named. (4) The five options carry `label` only; `FeatChoiceDef.options[].description` exists (src/rules/types.ts:1388) and each option here packs several distinct promises, so the pick is made blind at the point of choosing. Two smaller points I did NOT count as defects: Chimeric Heads is offered unfiltered despite "must have a head and at least one unarmed attack that uses its mouth or head" (Q9 says filter, but the test reads another record's granted creature — worth an owner decision); and the empty sheetDiff is correct on its own, since all effects land on the companion.

defects.name: Alchemical Discoveries
defects.detail: All three clauses are unbuilt; the record carries no mechanical field at all (level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only). (1) The doubled per-level formula grant: src/rules/formulaBook.ts FORMULA_GRANTS has ten entries and neither 'alchemical-discoveries' nor the grant it modifies — 'alchemical-sciences-methodology' — is one of them, so there is no per-level formula slot to double and no book is ensured (Q14 point 6). The methodology record's only stored mechanic is grantsActions:['quick-tincture']; its printed book + 'one formula each level' is itself missing, which is why Principle C has nothing to attach to.
