(2) The elixir-or-tool picker: the lane exists and would express it exactly (FormulaGrantPart traits/anyTraits/maxLevel:'self'/count), but no spec is authored, so no filtered picker and no empty slots. (3) The versatile-vial increase: CLASS_RESOURCES (src/rules/classResources.ts:39-120) grants 'versatile-vials' to the alchemist ONLY — an investigator has just devise-stratagem — so the pool this feat enlarges does not exist on the character, and AlchemyPanel.tsx:31 reads the alchemist bucket directly. The existing raise-a-resource field, `resourceMaxSet` (types.ts:1539, used by 4 feats), can only SET absolute values indexed by how many times a repeatable feat was taken; it cannot express '+1 expert / +2 master / +3 legendary' re-evaluated live off Crafting rank, so that sub-clause additionally needs a field shape the app does not have (formulaBook's `countByProficiency` is the nearest existing precedent).

defects.name: Manifold Modifications
defects.detail: The extra modification is picked and then thrown away — nothing lands on the innovation. The pick is a plain feat `choice` (flag 'modification') with no `ownsFeature: true`, and choiceOwnedFeatureIds (src/rules/derive.ts:2248-2257) admits a choice value into ownedFeatureIds ONLY when that flag is set (deliberately, per its comment), so the chosen modification's own mechanics never fire — e.g. picking Razor Prongs never applies its weaponTraits {match:{designated:'innovation'}, add:['tearing','trip','versatile-s']}, and Segmented Frame's bonus never appears. Only 4 feats in core.json carry choice.ownsFeature and this is not one of them. Nor does the pick reach the real subsystem: build.ts:4412-4428 resolves c.inventor.modifications from build.inventorModifications with exactly three tier slots (initial/breakthrough/revolutionary), each validated by inventorModificationOptions, and derive.ts:2194 only adds THOSE ids to owned features — a feat-granted fourth modification has no slot there. Second defect in the same record: the option list is not filtered to the innovation's type. All 17 options are offered to every inventor — 7 armour modifications and 10 weapon ones in one list, including power-suit-only Muscular Exoskeleton regardless of the armour base, and no construct entries at all — while inventorModificationOptions (build.ts:1308-1325) already does precisely the type/suit/tier filtering Q9 asks for. The choice also carries the placeholder prompt 'Prompt' (contrast light-mortar-innovation, which prints a real prompt and an explicit `inert` note; this record has neither, so it reads as an unfinished import rather than a decided 'record only').

defects.name: Battle Hymn to the Lost
defects.detail: grantsAction OK (own 2-action entry in the actions list) and limitedUses OK (1/hour; Shift Immanence's 1/round survives beside it). DEFECT: the app's stored description dropped three inline values that the AoN source for feat-7168 actually carries. Source (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-7168.json): "They appear in a 30-foot cone if you make a melee Strike or in a 10-foot emanation around your target... Each enemy in the area takes 2d10 damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC". App (public/core-descriptions.json feats/battle-hymn-to-the-lost): "They appear in a if you make a melee Strike or in a around your target... Each enemy in the area takes damage with a save". So the granted action's popup cannot tell the player the AREA (30-foot cone / 10-foot emanation), the DAMAGE (2d10), or the SAVE TYPE (basic Reflex), and the "at 12th level and every 4 levels thereafter the damage increases by 1d10" clause has no base value to scale from - the note-lane requirement is unsatisfiable as the data stands. Looks systemic, not one record: 147 of 19,245 core-descriptions entries match this narrow dropped-inline-macro pattern (spells/horizon-thunder-sphere, spells/protection, spells/bramble-bush, ...), consistent with a Foundry-style @Template/@Damage/@Check strip that deleted rather than substituted.

defects.name: Quick Jump
defects.detail: The feat is entirely inert. core.json feats['quick-jump'] carries no mechanical field at all (only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId); no modifiesGrant, no note, no entry in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, and no 'quick-jump' key in RECORD_MARKERS or FEAT_SITUATIONAL (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts). High Jump and Long Jump (core.json actions, both cost 2 actions) therefore show only their native 2-action form with no mark, no 1-action alternative, and no popup text about skipping the initial Stride or the 10-foot-Stride failure - all three requirements unmet. This is NOT no_lane: the exact route is shipped and in use - 'instant-manifestation' is {on:'action', id:'manifest-eidolon', value:'1 action', note:'...you can use Manifest Eidolon as a single action instead of a three-action activity'}, and 'dancing-leaf' already marks both 'high-jump' and 'long-jump'. HARNESS NOTE: the featFeatGrants/featPickGrants registry hits for this feat are INBOUND mentions (slip-with-the-breeze grants Quick Jump; pitborn and a skill-feat pool offer it as an option), not a pick this feat makes - bakeoff.js defines registries as 'which registries MENTION this feat' - so harness limit #1 does not excuse the empty diff.

defects.name: Embolded With Glorious Purpose
defects.detail: Two of five mechanical clauses are built; three have no surface. Built: situationalBonuses.ts:685 carries BOTH Will entries — "+1 status" when "after you Consult the Spirits, until your next daily preparations" and "+2 status" when "…against emotion and fear effects". The sheetDiff showing only the +2 is a harness artifact, not a defect: scripts/feat-evidence.mjs's `flat()` keys array elements by x.id, and both entries share the feat id, so the second overwrites the first. Different `when` strings means both render, which is the documented stacking display. Missing: (a) "Roll an attack roll twice and use the better result" has NO surface anywhere — no `strikeAttack` target on this feat, so nothing appears beside any Strike; (b) the blessed-skill reroll has no `skill` target, so it appears on no skill; (c) the Will entries' `when` text does not mention the once-per-day Will reroll either. The app has the exact idiom already: ascended-celestial-dedication (situationalBonuses.ts:606) writes {kind:'save',detail:'will'} / when "once per hour, on a Will saving throw" / bonus "roll twice and use the higher result (fortune)", and derring-do (:2643) does it for skills; `strikeAttack` is a supported target kind (:35, used by pennant-of-victory at :305). Also absent: any modifiesGrant/marker on Consult the Spirits (Rivethun Emissary) showing this feat rides on it (Q8) — the parent feat exists as consult-the-spirits-rivethun-emissary. Two reader requirements I judge over-specified and did NOT count against the app: the `limitedUses` ask for three separate trackable counters (gold exemplar #16, The Truth as I See it, settles that the owner wants a once-per-day fortune reroll expressed as a `*` carrying the clause, not a use counter), and the `dailyChoice` ask to record the blessed skill (the parent record already handles it Ruling-H style, starring all skills with the condition in text at situationalBonuses.ts:684). ⚠ Data hygiene, separate: core.json holds TWO feat records for this feat, 'embolded-with-glorious-purpose' and 'emboldened-with-glorious-purpose', each with its own situationalBonuses block (:685 and :1020) — any fix must be applied to both or one spelling will silently keep the old behaviour.

defects.name: Broken Chain Dedication
defects.detail: Only the action grant landed. THREE findings. (1) MISSING — the entire first clause has no surface: `registries` is empty, so there is no situational entry for 'spend a Mythic Point when you attempt an Escape or Force Open check to do so at mythic proficiency'. The app has this exact lane and uses it on identically-shaped mythic feats: binds-that-tie = targets [{kind:'skill',detail:'athletics'}], when 'when you spend a Mythic Point to Grapple a foe an ally already grabbed', bonus 'roll at mythic proficiency'; also avoid-fates-gaze ('roll at mythic proficiency'), steadfast-grip ('calculated at mythic proficiency'), prescient-parry. So no star reaches Athletics (Force Open, Escape) or Acrobatics (Escape) per Ruling C + Q2. The Mythic Point resource itself is fine — VitalsRail.tsx:941-1011 renders a spendable/restorable pip pool backed by play.ts mythicPoints — so the clause is inert only because nothing points at it. (2) SPURIOUS, verified against the AoN mirror — storedFields.actionCost is {type:'actions', value:1} and the dedication therefore appears in the encounter ACTIONS list as a 1-action activity (sheetDiff actions[0] = 'Broken Chain Dedication', alongside the real actions[3] = 'Ultimatum of Liberation'). feat-7357 in the AoN archive has no `actions`/`action_type` field at all; the cost belongs to Ultimatum of Liberation, not to the dedication. This is systemic, not local: 46 of 240 dedication feats in core.json carry a non-passive actionCost, including archfiend-dedication (2 actions) and ascended-celestial-dedication (1 action). (3) NO SURFACE FOR THE ANATHEMA — `anathema` exists only as a field on Deity (types.ts:2230) and nothing in src/sheet or src/builder renders it; even deity anathema are visible only inside the deity's own description popup. The feat carries no `note` and no marker on the granted Ultimatum of Liberation, so the constraint lives only in the dedication's description. Requirement 4 is met: ultimatum-of-liberation is in core.actions with its 1-action cost, traits (auditory/linguistic/mental/mythic) and full description, sourced to this feat via aonParentId feat-7357. The GM-adjudication and flavour clauses correctly generate nothing.
defects.question: Anathema that comes from a FEAT rather than a deity has no route today — the app renders no anathema list anywhere, so even deity anathema are only readable inside the deity popup. Do you want (a) a general anathema/edict surface on the sheet fed by both deities and feats, (b) just a marker on the granted action (Principle C — mark Ultimatum of Liberation as anathema-constrained), or (c) nothing, on the grounds that the player reads it in the dedication's own text?

defects.name: Master Monster Hunter
defects.detail: The whole feat is inert: public/core.json feats['master-monster-hunter'] carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `skillSubstitutions`, no `situational`, no `modifiesGrant`; registries [] and sheetDiff [] confirm nothing reaches the sheet. Three separate promises fail, and each has an existing lane. (1) 'You can use Nature to Recall Knowledge to identify any creature' — `skillSubstitutions` {use, forSkill, when} is live (derive.ts:366, 26 feats use it) and can express this as one entry per knowledge skill with when: 'to Recall Knowledge to identify any creature'; none is present. (2) No `*` on Nature and none on the Recall Knowledge action, so Q2's 'star both' is unmet. (3) 'you gain the benefits of Monster Hunter (and Monster Warden, if you have it) on a success as well as a critical success' — the records it modifies still read the narrow band: situationalBonuses.ts:513 monster-hunter when: 'on your next attack roll against hunted prey you critically identified…', and :515 monster-warden 'after Monster Hunter's critical identification…'. The pattern for exactly this shape already ships one line below at :2747, where legendary-monster-hunter carries its own situational reading 'replaces Monster Hunter's +1' (with SITUATIONAL_SUPERSEDES available to drop the superseded entry, and ownership-gating giving the Monster Warden conditional for free). Master Monster Hunter has no equivalent.

defects.name: Leading Dance
defects.detail: The action half is delivered — sheetDiff shows 'Leading Dance' entering the actions list at its printed 1-action cost, and I rendered the popup body: all four degrees of success render IN FULL as styled degree rows. But the printed '**Requirements** You are adjacent to an enemy.' is DROPPED and never appears. Verified empirically by rendering AstRenderer with the same props DescBody passes (bodyOnly hideMeta) — output starts at 'You sweep your foe into your dance' with no Requirements line. Cause: src/sheet/DescBody.tsx:72 passes `hideMeta` unconditionally on the AST path; src/sheet/AstRenderer.tsx:162 META includes `requirements?|trigger|frequency|duration|cost`, and line 308 returns null for those paragraphs when hideMeta is set. Leading Dance's Requirements paragraph additionally sits inside a Source-led `column`, which isMetaishBlock (line 181) drops wholesale at line 347. src/sheet/FeatDetail.tsx renders Prerequisites from its own field but has NO Requirements/Trigger/Frequency surface to catch them. ⚠ SCOPE: this is systemic — scanning public/ast/feats.json with the app's own isMetaP/isMetaishBlock predicates, 1,939 Trigger/Requirements/Frequency paragraphs across 1,543 distinct feats are hideMeta targets, including every reaction's trigger (e.g. nanite-surge and merciful-elixir both lose Frequency AND Trigger). Gold-set Ruling E ('a reaction needs to appear in the reactions list, with its trigger and requirements in its popup') is not being met for any of them.

defects.name: Munitions Crafter
defects.detail: The feat's central mechanic — advanced alchemy — is entirely absent, and three of six requirements are undelivered. (1) MISSING, the daily budget: no feat record in public/core.json carries `advancedAlchemy` for munitions-crafter (the only eight that do are master-alchemy, efficient-alchemy, advanced-efficient-alchemy, alchemist-dedication, advanced-alchemy, herbalist-dedication, poisoner-dedication, morning-side-dishes). In build.ts:3353-3380 the base is `ownsClass('alchemist') ? 4 + intMod : 0`, so a gunslinger ends with `advancedAlchemy` undefined — no budget, no daily-prep picker, no bombs/ammunition filter. The sheetDiff confirms it: nothing under advancedAlchemy changed. Foundry's own record implements exactly this with `CraftingAbility {maxSlots: "4 + ceil(@actor.level / 2)", craftableItems: ["item:group:bomb"], isDailyPrep: true}`. Worse, the existing `advancedAlchemy` field shape (items / addInt / atLevel) cannot express "4 + half your level rounded up" at all — it has no per-level formula, so the field would need extending, not just filling. (2) MISSING, batches of 4: nothing anywhere in src/ implements a prepared quantity differing from budget points spent (Foundry's `batchSizes … quantity: 4` for black-powder-dose and alchemical ammo has no counterpart). (3) MISSING, the horns/kegs exclusion: no `note` on the feat and no daily-prep entry to print it on. DELIVERED: Crafting trained (featGrantsAuto.ts:222, diff shows untrained→trained); the formula book itself (inventory[0] = formula-book-blank, grantedBy "Munitions Crafter" — Q14 point 6); and FORMULA_GRANTS['munitions-crafter'] in formulaBook.ts:120 with black-powder as a `fixed` formula plus 4 picks at maxLevel 1, rarities common+uncommon, written as a one-time copy into the book (Q14 point 9). PARTIAL on that picker: its own note admits it offers bombs only — "The feat also allows alchemical ammunition, which nothing in the data marks as ammunition — pick those with Add formula" — so Q14 point 7's "only the options this feat allows" is narrower than the text, by a data limitation. SEPARATE over-grant worth the owner's eye: featFeatGrants.ts:100 hands the character the Alchemical Crafting feat, which the printed remaster text does not grant (it says "gain the advanced alchemy benefits"), and that feat carries its OWN FORMULA_GRANTS entry for 4 common 1st-level alchemical formulas — so the character gets 8 formula picks where the text grants 4 plus black powder. Foundry does the same GrantItem, so this may be deliberate parity rather than a bug.

defects.name: Sprout Fruit
defects.detail: The action lane is fine — sheetDiff puts "Sprout Fruit" in actions[2] at its printed 1-action cost. What is missing is the amount the whole feat is about. AoN feat-7630 prints "is healed 1d4 Hit Points for every 2 levels you have"; Foundry's source (.import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/miscellaneous/deviant/sprout-fruit.json) carries it as @Damage[(floor(@actor.level/2)d4)[healing]]. The app's stored text (public/core-descriptions.json, feats/sprout-fruit) reads "is healed  Hit Points for every 2 levels you have" — no die, no quantity, no note, no level-scaled value. Root cause is the @Damage cleaner's guard at scripts/import-core.mjs:279: the recovered formula must match /^[\dd+\-\s()]+$/, so any actor-scaled formula (floor(), @actor.level, *) fails the test and is replaced with an empty string. I reproduced it exactly: 'is healed @Damage[(floor(@actor.level/2)d4)[healing]] Hit Points' -> 'is healed  Hit Points'. The same deletion empties the Awakening parenthetical — source @Damage[(floor(@actor.level/2)d6)[healing]] renders as "from d4s to d6s ()". BLAST RADIUS: 141 records in .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e carry an actor-scaled @Damage of this shape (wicked-thorns ceil(@actor.level/2)d8, raise-slabs, toxic-skin, barbed-quills, drain-realm, administer-ambient-magic …), so this is systemic, not one feat. Everything else here is correctly nothing: the eater's three-action cost and the ally-side healing/condition-reduction owe no sheet number (Ruling F + Ruling E's HP clause).

defects.name: Celestial Magic
defects.detail: The empty sheetDiff is the expected pick-a-choice harness limit (registries lists featCantripGrants), so it is not the defect — the defect is in the store's shape. The text says "Choose TWO of the following spells", but BuildState.pickCantripChoices is typed Record<string, string> (src/rules/build.ts:217) — one spell id per featId. The builder renders a single PopupSelect (src/builder/Builder.tsx:1786-1804) and build.ts:4210-4216 pushes exactly one innateGrant. So only one of the two granted spells can ever be chosen; the second is unreachable. The six options are correct and closed (src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:25: clear-mind, sure-footing, share-life, revealing-light, humanoid-form, everlight), and 1/day per spell is right (absent usesPerDay defaults to 1). SECOND DEFECT, wrong value: the grant is pushed as {spellId} with no tradition, so the innate entry's tradition falls back to content.spells[id].traditions[0] (build.ts:4258-4264). The feat makes all six DIVINE innate spells, but revealing-light, everlight and humanoid-form all list arcane first — humanoid-form is not divine at all — so a character who picks one of those three sees their innate entry labelled arcane. That is the sheet stating something false about the spell (Q12). Rank is safe by luck: all six are base rank 2, matching the feat's 2nd-rank clause.

defects.name: Hellbreaker Dedication
defects.detail: Only the two Lore trainings land (sheetDiff: lore:devil, lore:hellknight = trained, via featGrantsAuto.ts:166). Four promises are unbuilt. (1) "When you roll initiative, you can attempt a ... check to Recall Knowledge ... as a free action" — no grantsActions on the record and no action in the diff; the free action, its trigger and the GM-arbiter caveat exist nowhere. The grantsAction lane exists, so this is buildable. (2) No `*` on Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, Society, or Recall Knowledge — situationalBonuses.ts has no 'hellbreaker-dedication' key (it has hellbreakers-resolve, hellknight-preferment, etc., but not this one). (3) "If you were already trained in one or both of those Lore skills, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice" — featGrantsAuto.ts:166 has no redundantFallback, and build.ts:3097 guards the fallback with `!key.startsWith('lore:')`, so a lore collision can never fire it even if the flag were added; the lore-collision fallback has no route today. (4) "You gain the Additional Lore general feat for BOTH" — one bare `additional-lore` is added (grantedBy hellbreaker-dedication) with no subject, and FEAT_GRANTS['additional-lore'] is `{ loreChoices: 1 }` with no rank progression; build.ts:3146-3151 hardcodes 'trained' for a lore choice and never applies `at()`. So at the harness's level 20 both Lores read trained when Additional Lore's 3rd/7th/15th skill increases should have taken them to legendary. Separately, the popup renders the raw AoN template literally: "you can attempt a recall-knowledge skill=devil-lore, recall-knowledge skill=hellknight-lore, or recall-knowledge skill=society check" (core-descriptions.json). The pristine archive (aon-2e-archive feat-8534) reads "a Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, or Society check".

defects.name: Venipuncture
defects.detail: The activity itself is delivered — sheetDiff adds actions[2] = "Venipuncture" with its 2-action cost, and the Cost line prints as the first paragraph of its description. Three things are not. (1) The stored description has two holes and renders a broken sentence at the player: "lacerating foes in a ." and "Creatures caught in the blast must attempt a save." (core-descriptions.json). The pristine archive (aon-2e-archive feat-7768) reads "lacerating foes in a 30-foot emanation" and "must attempt a basic Reflex save" — the area and the save type, both load-bearing at the table, were dropped at import. (2) "Cost all your remaining sanguimancy Hit Points (minimum 3)" reaches no machinery. The pool itself exists and is readable/spendable (classResources.ts:48, `sanguimancy-hp`, maxPerLevel 2, initialPerLevel 1, attached to the character via `feat: 'sanguimancer-dedication'`), but nothing ties the action to it: the action is not gated below 3, does not empty the pool, and never shows the variable amount actually spent — which is the input to the damage the player then rolls. actionGates.ts only knows four resource gates (rage, panache, hunt-prey, unleash-psyche), all trait/prose-detected booleans, so a NUMERIC spend against a counter has no route in the app today. (3) "The DC for this save is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher" — no resolved number and no `note` on the record; the popup restates the rule for finding the DC instead of showing it. Unlike a target-side number this one is computed entirely from the player's own sheet, so DECIDED SCOPE does not excuse it. Correctly absent, per DECIDED SCOPE and Ruling E: the damage and the enemies' saves move nothing on your own sheet.

defects.name: Armament Paragon
defects.detail: The record is completely inert — storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prereq/actionCost, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty. Four separate clauses land nowhere. (1) The five-rune widening has an existing lane and is simply unused: `choiceOptionAdditions` (src/rules/types.ts:571, consumed at derive.ts:1016) is exactly how Radiant Armament adds astral/brilliant to blessed-armament's `blessedRune` daily list (effect-backfill.json), yet Armament Paragon adds no Animated / Greater Fearsome / Grievous / Keen / Greater Vitalizing, so the blessed-armament pick at Rest still offers only the base five (fearsome, ghost-touch, returning, shifting, vitalizing). (2) No `grantsActions` entry for the 1-action concentrate/divine rune swap (104 feats carry that field), so the action never reaches the actions list. (3) No route re-opens the daily rune pick outside Rest: dailyChoices are editable only inside the 'Prepare for the day' modal (CharacterSheet.tsx:844-880), whose confirm button also fires onRest() — which is precisely what the feat's last sentence forbids ('Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times'). (4) No `note` carrying that caveat. One sub-point that is a genuine schema gap rather than an authoring gap: `choiceOptionAdditions` supports only `add` and `addIfSanctified`, so there is no field for the conditional 'if you have the Radiant Armament feat, add Greater Astral and Greater Brilliant' — Q9 (show only what may legally be picked) needs an owned-feat gate that does not exist today.

defects.name: Dual Studies
defects.detail: Two clauses fail. (a) "At 7th level, you each become an expert in the chosen skills" — the data DOES author it (`src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:114` → `'dual-studies': { skillChoices: [{options:'any', rank:'trained'}], rankUpgrade: {level:7, rank:'expert'} }`) but the engine drops it: in build.ts the level upgrade `const at = (r) => up ? maxRank(r, up) : r` (line ~3081) is applied to `armor`, `weapon`, `save`, `perception`, `skills`, `conditionalSkills` and the armorCascade, but the `skillChoices` loop at build.ts:3131-3143 uses `slot.rank` raw with no `at()`. Sheet value that is wrong: on the level-20 host the chosen skill shows `skills.acrobatics.rank = "trained"`, `modifier 22` (20 level + 2 trained + 0 Dex); expert would be 24. The feat's entire level-7 half is inert, on your own sheet, at every level 7-20. This also silently breaks `initiate-benefit-tome` (level-5 expert), the only other feat with rankUpgrade and no static `skills` entry. (b) "Your eidolon becomes trained in one of those skills" / "These skill proficiencies are not shared" — the pick is captured but explicitly discarded: the record's own `effectChoices.eidolon-skill` prompt reads "recorded only — eidolon skill proficiencies aren't tracked". EidolonBlock.skills (companions.ts:673, rendered at CompanionsTab.tsx:821 as "Trained skills") is populated ONLY from `opt?.grants?.skills` — the summoner subclass option — so no feat can add to it, and the list is bare names with no rank, so the eidolon's level-7 expert step has no place to live even if the trained grant were wired. Requirement 2 (your own trained skill) IS delivered, and correctly no redundancy fallback was invented.

defects.name: Instant Armor
defects.detail: Both promised activities are absent. Text: "You can perform a 10-minute ritual, which has the conjuration and magical traits, to divert a set of heavy armor…" and "…you can use a three-action activity, which has the concentrate, conjuration, and teleportation traits, to phase the armor back and instantly don it." Sheet: storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost:{type:'passive'}/archetype/edition/aonId — no `grantsActions`; registries [] and sheetDiff [] (empty). No action records exist for either activity in core.actions (searched every actions record for 'instant armor', 'extradimensional space connected', 'phase the armor' — zero hits). Because the feat's own actionCost is `passive`, MainTab's isActionCost gate (MainTab.tsx:224) excludes it, so neither activity ever reaches the encounter action list and the whole feat is invisible outside the Feats tab. This is not a no_lane: `grantsActions` is the built route and a sibling feat in the very same archetype uses it (aegis-of-arnisant → grantsActions:['absorb-into-the-aegis']). The stowed/carried state (requirement 3) needs nothing new — inventory already has worn/equipped flags — and the auto-phase triggers (requirement 4) are text that would ride in the two popups that do not exist.

defects.name: Exemplar Dedication
defects.detail: Delivered: "trained in martial weapons" (featGrantsAuto.ts:131 `{ weapon: { martial: 'trained' } }` — no diff only because the harness host is a level-20 fighter already legendary in martial), and the Shift Immanence action (grantsClassFeatures:['shift-immanence'] → ownedFeatures[16] + actions[2]). MISSING, two separate gaps. (1) The ikon. The record carries no ikon choice, no grant, no mode and no transcendence action, so the whole middle of the feat is inert: "You gain one ikon, the ability to use the ikon's immanence and transcendence actions and effects." The app plainly has the route — core.json holds 21 `ikon` records, the exemplar class offers them through `extraChoices` (pickByLevel 3 at level 1), situationalBonuses.ts:892+ carries per-ikon immanence bonuses keyed by ikon id, and the transcendence activities exist as records (break-free, drink-of-my-foes, captivating-charm) — but build.ts:4345 reads `extraChoices` off cls/cls2 only, so an archetype character never reaches it. Other dedications that hand out a class extra-choice do it with a `choice` on the feat (thaumaturge-dedication → flag 'dedicationImplement', kineticist-dedication → 'kineticElement'); Exemplar Dedication has no such choice. (2) "You become trained in exemplar class DC" is absent: the feat carries no `classDcGrant`, which is the only field build.ts:3662 reads to populate `secondaryClassDcs`, so the second class DC the archetype adds — the number the ikon's transcendence effects are resolved against — never appears. fighter-dedication has `classDcGrant:{classId:'fighter'}`; exemplar-dedication does not. Systemic: 10 multiclass dedications name a class DC in their text and carry no classDcGrant (inventor, kineticist, barbarian, champion, investigator, monk, swashbuckler, exemplar, guardian, thaumaturge). Also worth a look while fixing: the feat DOES carry a `choice` prompting "Class DCAbility Score" (str/dex) that nothing reads, so the builder asks a question with no consumer.

defects.name: Haunting Memories
defects.detail: The proficiency half is well built: a `choice` with `daily:true`, 32 options across the two branches, each gated by `requiresSkillRank` ({max:'untrained'} for the expert branch, {min:'trained'} for the master branch) and filtered by `qualifiesForOption` at rest, so the branches really are mutually exclusive; exactly one answer is stored per key so tomorrow replaces today; `dailySkillRank` (derive.ts:1054) never lowers a rank, satisfying Q10; and deriveSkill (derive.ts:415) folds it into the modifier. The prerequisite restriction is honoured too — `checkPrerequisites` (build.ts:5505) reads `character.proficiencies.skills`, which the daily rank never enters. What is NOT delivered is the feat's entire second half: 'You also gain one skill feat with a minimum requirement of your new rank in the chosen skill… your level is equal to half your level.' There is no picker — haunting-memories is absent from FEAT_PICK_GRANTS, and the `open`/`feat` daily-choice route (openChoice.ts `featsMatching`) filters only on featCategory/maxLevel/traits, so it cannot express 'skill feat whose prerequisite is the NEW rank in THAT skill' nor a level ceiling of half the character's level. Worse, the authored fallback prose is write-only: the clause is stored in `choice.note`, but `DailyChoice` (src/rules/dailyChoices.ts) has no `note` field, `dailyChoicesFor` does not copy it, and the Rest dialog (CharacterSheet.tsx ~755-800) renders only prompt + option chips — `def.note` is rendered ONLY in the builder (Builder.tsx:419, shared.tsx:2648), which a daily choice never reaches. So the player is never told, anywhere, that this feat grants a skill feat. Minor third point: the borrowed rank drives the skill number silently — nothing on the skill row or in its breakdown marks it as this morning's temporary rank.

defects.name: Blessing of the Five
defects.detail: The innateSpell clause — "You cast the 3-action version of Heal, heightened to a rank one lower than half your level rounded up" — reaches the sheet nowhere. The stored record (public/core.json) and scripts/data/effect-backfill.json carry only `limitedUses:{max:1,per:'day'}`; there is no `innateSpells` field, and sheetDiff shows no grantedSpells. Heal exists only as a description ref-link (core-descriptions.json `r:[{label:'Heal',key:'spells'}]`), so it is named in prose but never castable from the ability and no rank is ever resolved or re-resolved on level-up. The lane is built and the identical shape is already in use: `mortal-herald-dedication` stores `{spellId:'heal',tradition:'divine',usesPerDay:1,heightenHalfLevel:true}`. This feat's rank is one LOWER than the standard ladder — `heightenHalfLevel` computes exactly ceil(level/2) at src/rules/build.ts:4226 — so it needs the explicit `heightenAt` ladder ([{3,1},{5,2},{7,3},{9,4},{11,5},{13,6},{15,7},{17,8},{19,9}]) rather than the half-level flag. The other two requirements ARE delivered: the ability appears in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0]) and one shared per-day use is tracked (limitedUses[0]), covering both the mass-Heal and raise-dead branches from a single pool as the text requires. The asserted 3-action cost is NOT a defect — AoN's source record (by-category/hellknight-order/hellknight-order-3.json) prints `<actions string="Three Actions" />` on the ability itself.

defects.name: Uncanny Bombs
defects.detail: The weaponRider clause — "When you throw an alchemical item with the bomb trait, its range increment increases to 60 feet" — is delivered nowhere, not even as text. The uncanny-bombs record in public/core.json has no `weaponTraits`/range rider and effect-backfill.json has no entry for it, so all 171 bomb-trait weapons keep their printed `range:20` and the strike line an alchemist reads still says 20 ft after taking a 12th-level feat that sets it to 60. The lane exists and takes exactly this shape: applyWeaponRiders (src/rules/derive.ts:2658) honours `range:{set:n}`, and its `match.anyTrait` filter is trait-scoped and trait-family aware — so `{match:{anyTrait:['bomb']}, range:{set:60}}` covers every bomb the character ever buys or crafts, which is precisely the by-trait scoping the text demands. Note the prerequisite feat Far Lobber has the same structural gap but at least papers over it with a text-only star (situationalBonuses.ts:2717, "range increment 30 ft instead of 20 ft"); Uncanny Bombs has not even that, so the two feats also disagree with each other. The OTHER two clauses are delivered correctly: situationalBonuses.ts:2989 carries both strike stars, including the text-only "automatically succeed at the flat check" with no phantom number attached, correctly scoped by `when` rather than by weapon name. The empty sheetDiff is a harness limit, not evidence of failure — feat-evidence.mjs samples situational refs only of kind ac/perception/save/skill and never strikeAttack, and the test build carries no bomb.

defects.name: Unified Theory
defects.detail: The feat does absolutely nothing. Its record in public/core.json carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `skillSubstitutions`, no `situational`, no RECORD_MARKERS entry — and the sheetDiff is completely empty with `registries: []`. All three substitutions are missing: Arcana for Nature, for Occultism, and for Religion. The lane exists and is exactly the right shape: `skillSubstitutions?: { use, forSkill, when? }` (src/rules/types.ts:483-495), whose `when` field was built precisely for a RESTRICTED substitution — its own doc comment cites Natural Medicine as the case that must NOT silently replace the skill everywhere. It is resolved at src/rules/derive.ts:366-381 and surfaced at src/rules/explain.ts:322, so three entries with `when: "for a skill action or skill feat that requires the check because of the magic tradition involved"` would reach Nature, Occultism and Religion and be readable where the player looks the number up. The second promise is also absent: no note/marker on the Identify Magic action (id `identify-magic` in the RECORD_MARKERS lane, situationalBonuses.ts:3221) saying the usual penalty and higher DC for using Arcana on non-arcane magic no longer apply — per Ruling D the DC half needs no surface, but the penalty-suppression text does. This is a 15th-level feat gated behind legendary Arcana that is entirely inert.

defects.name: Changeling Lore
defects.detail: Two of the text's clauses are not delivered. (1) THE REDUNDANCY FALLBACK IS NOT BUILT. featGrantsAuto.ts:91 reads {skills:{deception:'trained', occultism:'trained', 'lore:hag':'trained'}} with NO `redundantFallback: true`. Verified by building: on a bard host (class already trains Occultism) c.skillFallbacks is undefined and no replacement picker is offered — the redundant grant silently evaporates and the character simply gets less, which is the exact failure mode the clause exists to prevent. The lane works and is one flag away: conrasu-lore, which carries the flag, correctly reports skillFallbacks [{featId:'conrasu-lore', skill:'occultism'}] on the same host, and build.ts:3097 already handles the two-fire case per skill key and correctly exempts lore: keys. (2) HAG LORE IS FROZEN AT TRAINED. At level 20 deriveSkill(c,'lore:hag') returns {rank:'trained', modifier:22}; Additional Lore promises "an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory" at 3rd, 7th and 15th, i.e. legendary by 15th. FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] is {loreChoices:1} with no `rankUpgrade`, and upgradeRankAt already accepts exactly this multi-step shape ({level,rank} steps). I confirmed a directly-taken Additional Lore is also stuck at trained, so this is the granted feat's own gap surfacing through the grant. What IS right: Deception and Occultism reach trained with real modifiers; additional-lore appears in stored.feats with grantedBy:'changeling-lore'; lore:hag reaches the skills list as a rollable row; and no spurious Lore picker is offered for the granted feat (Builder.tsx:1689 only renders loreChoices for a slot-PICKED feat), which is correct since the text made the pick.

defects.name: False Priest Form
defects.detail: Only the innateSpell lane is built. storedFields.innateSpells grants divine-lance and haunting-hymn at-will with tradition "primal" as printed, and the sheet shows spellSources.divine-lance / .haunting-hymn = "False Priest Form" with the pool reading tradition primal — Q12 satisfied. Four requirements reach nothing. (1) The mode: core.json feats['false-priest-form'] has no toggle and core.stances has no 'false-priest-form' key, so there is no way to turn the form on or off and nothing tells the player it is active (Q3/Q11). The route is proven — core.stances holds 27 entries with form:true, including the directly comparable shape-changes 'long-nosed-form', 'among-humanity' and 'devil-in-plain-sight'. (2) modifiesGrant on Change Shape: core.actions['change-shape'] exists and carries no marker naming the false priest form; there is no modifiesGrant on the feat and no RECORD_MARKERS entry with id 'change-shape' anywhere in situationalBonuses.ts, so the player who looks up Change Shape never learns this option exists (Principle C, Q8). (3) skillSubstitution: the feat has no `skillSubstitutions` — the lane is live and used by 26 other feats (e.g. social-camouflage: use deception forSkill diplomacy when "to Gather Information while in that settlement"), and the needed entry is use:deception / forSkill:religion / when:"while in false priest form, to Recall Knowledge". Deception carries no star and recall-knowledge carries no marker, so neither of Q2's two surfaces exists. (4) The break-and-lockout clause has no mode to live in; it survives only in the feat's own description text. One knock-on that reads as spurious: because there is no mode, both cantrips are granted unconditionally — a character who has never assumed the form still shows Divine Lance and Haunting Hymn at-will on the Spells page, where the text conditions them on "while in your false priest form". The religion-of-your-choosing flavour correctly produces nothing.

defects.name: Bonded Animal
defects.detail: The feat delivers nothing: storedFields holds only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, sheetDiff is empty, and the lone registries hit ('featFeatGrants') is Bonded Animal being GRANTED by another feat (featFeatGrants.ts:98 'moray-eel-mount': ['bonded-animal']), not this feat granting anything. (1) No companion record — 'bonded-animal' is absent from FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS, and companionGrants.ts's own header comment says moray-eel-mount was deliberately 'held back for a distinct model' as 'a Bonded-Animal minion, weaker than a companion', so the model is an acknowledged deferral, not a built lane. (2) The minion trait is recorded nowhere, since there is no animal record to put it on. (3) The Nature-rank-derived maximum minion level (−1 / 3 at master / 11 at legendary) is the number that tells the player which animals still qualify, and it appears nowhere — the `note` lane exists and is unused here. (4) No swap/clear surface. (5) The **Special** mutual exclusion is unenforceable: eligibleFeatsForSlot (featSlots.ts) has no anti-prerequisite mechanism at all, so a character can take Bonded Animal alongside an animal companion. Two caveats on scope, not on the verdict: the SimpleCompanion lane (kinds 'pet'/'follower') is explicitly 'informational, no full stat-block math' and carries no level field, and the app has no route to attach an arbitrary bestiary creature — so full fidelity for a level-11 bonded animal is genuinely beyond current lanes, while the note and a lightweight companion entry are not.

defects.name: Devastating Shield Wallop
defects.detail: The record is completely bare: public/core.json holds only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `modifiesGrant`, and no entry at all in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. This feat's entire content modifies a grant another record made, so Principle C applies: Shield Wallop's own entry must show that it now forces a save against your class DC, with the four outcomes and the tower/fortress-shield –2 readable there. Shield Wallop is itself a feat (`shield-wallop`, actionCost 1 action, flourish/guardian) that appears in the action list, so a Guardian who takes this feat and then opens Shield Wallop mid-combat still reads only the old stupefied-1/2 text — the save, the prone, and the stunned 1 are nowhere on the thing they are looking at. The lane exists and is live: `GrantModification.actionRider` (src/rules/types.ts:785) is documented as "A rider on the action `from` grants — or IS, when `from` is itself an action record — for an addition that changes no number the sheet holds. Rendered as a RecordMarker on that action row", and `draconic-paragon` ships using it against `kobold-breath`. So `modifiesGrant: [{from: 'shield-wallop', actionRider: {note: …}}]` is the exact fit. The –2 belongs in that same note per Ruling H (its trigger is your own equipment and the "or another shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus when you Take Cover" clause must stay open, printed rather than narrowed). The four degree-of-success outcomes themselves are correctly NOT a sheet stat — they are readable in this feat's own popup, and DECIDED SCOPE puts enemy conditions off your sheet.

defects.name: Witch's Hut
defects.detail: Nothing at all is delivered. storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, registries is empty (so harness limit 1 does not apply) and sheetDiff is []. The grep over src/ finds no reference to 'witchs-hut' anywhere, and src/rules/companionGrants.ts FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS — the table that is the app's only route from a feat to a companion entity — has no entry for it, though it already carries construct-companion grants ('construct-innovation', 'prototype-companion', 'rise-my-creature'). So four requirements are unmet with lanes that exist: (a) the hut as an addressable creature (companion lane, incl. its 150 HP / Hardness 10); (b) the 1-action auditory+concentrate command in the character's own actions list (grantsAction — the feat has no grantsActions); (c) the five standing commands and their text, incl. Move's Speed 60 (mode lane); (d) the construct armor −4 AC text. Two sub-parts may genuinely need new capability rather than being simple omissions and are worth the owner's eye: deriving the hut's AC, three saves and Perception LIVE from the master's values (companion blocks are built from the companion's own advancement, not mirrored from the character), and hanging a mutually exclusive mode on a COMPANION rather than on the character. But the verdict is missing, not no_lane, because the entity, the action and the readable command text are all expressible today and none of them was authored.

defects.name: Arcane Propulsion
defects.detail: The headline mechanic is absent. Delivered: limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]) and the feat appearing as a 2-action entry (actions[0]). Not delivered: the fly Speed. Clause "You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed while redirecting the energy" — storedFields has no `speeds` at all and sheetDiff touches no speed value, while the exact lane and the exact formula shape are in use elsewhere: core.json's wyrmling-flight stores speeds:{fly:"@actor.speed.land"}, and 19 feats carry speeds.fly today. Also not delivered: the mode. Clause "You can maintain this redirected energy for 5 minutes" — 5 minutes is far longer than a round, so Q1 gives it a mode and Q7 gives the conditional fly Speed its `*`; the feat has no `modes` and no mode record in core.json's 429-entry modes collection references it (feat-sourced modes do exist — feat-eternal-blessing, feat-aegis-for-the-innocent, feat-tweak-appearances). The Enhancement clause is a third gap and a systemic one: nothing records it as taken and nothing removes the two limits it removes. 19 automaton feats carry an Enhancement clause and not one has `modifiesGrant` or `modes` (only 2 feats in the whole file use modifiesGrant). Since the Enhancement's whole content is the DELETION of the daily use and the 5-minute duration, an add-only grant cannot express it — that specific sub-part may need a capability the app lacks, but the verdict is missing because the fly Speed and the mode are both plain omissions in lanes that already work.

defects.name: Talisman Esoterica
defects.detail: Clause: "Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level." core.json stores a free-text choice — {flag:'esotericaTalismans', kind:'text', daily:true, picks:2} — whose own inert note reads "Recorded only — the temporary talismans aren't added to your inventory." The player types two names into a box; nothing is filtered to talismans, nothing is capped at half level, nothing is produced. The app already has the purpose-built lane for exactly this shape: Feat.dailyTemporaryItems (src/rules/dailyItems.ts), whose filter carries traits + maxLevel, and maxLevel accepts a STRING formula run through resolveFormula (derive.ts:1363, supports floor/@level), so 'floor(@level/2)' recomputes as the character levels. The data supports it: 196 items carry the 'talisman' trait, 79 of them common at level 10 or below. A sibling thaumaturge esoterica feat — grand-scroll-esoterica — already uses this lane, and Herbal Forager uses its fromKnownFormulas flag for the same "you must know the formula" clause, so this feat is the odd one out rather than the lane being absent. Two further points the owner needs before fixing it: (1) dailyItemOptions applies no rarity filter, so a talisman picker would offer uncommon and rare talismans the text excludes — Q9 ("only what the player may legally pick") governs a picker even though Q5 leaves the shop open; (2) PlayState.dailyItems is written at rest and read only back into the same rest dialog (CharacterSheet.tsx:241 and 870) with no other reader anywhere in src/, so even after switching lanes the requirement "the talismans reach the inventory as real, usable items" stays unmet — the lane stops at the picker.

defects.name: Celestial Armaments
defects.detail: Only the daily pick is built: choice {flag:'blessedWeapon', kind:'open', daily:true, from:{type:'own-item', itemType:'weapon'}} with an honest note about pre-statted handwraps bundles (handwraps-of-mighty-blows is itemType 'weapon', so the plain item does appear). Everything the pick is supposed to carry is absent from the core.json record — nothing else in core.json even references this id. Missing: the +1d8 spirit rider (no strikeDamage/weaponTraits), the critical specialization (no critSpec/critSpecWeapons), the 'sheds light like a torch' note, the crit-blind rider note (which per the text must say 'class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher' rather than assert one DC), BOTH granted single actions (the concentrate recall-the-weapon action and the 1-Mythic-Point ally-blessing action — no grantsActions at all), and the 1-minute display-only ally mode (core.modes has 429 entries, 97 feat-gated, none for this feat). The Mythic-point pool itself exists (play.ts MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS, VitalsRail pips), so the cost is expressible; the action carrying it just isn't granted. Not a harness artifact: registries is empty (no featPickGrants), and the two actions are unconditional so they would diff regardless of the pick. Note also that dailyChoiceGrants (derive.ts ~1064) applies grants only for fixed options[].grant or an open SPELL pick with grantInnate — an open own-item answer grants nothing, so even after the player picks a weapon there is currently no route for a rider to attach to it.

defects.name: Daywalker (Vampire)
defects.detail: sheetDiff is completely empty and storedFields carries no grant field of any kind (only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/archetype/aonId) — every clause of this feat is inert. (1) 'You gain the Advanced Undead Benefits' — no `grantsClassFeatures`, and the named package exists only as a stub: public/core.json `rules.advanced-undead-benefits` is {id, name, edition, aonId} with no description (all 2,008 `rules` records ship description-less, and core-descriptions.json has no `rules` bucket). So neither Principle G half happens: the details are not surfaced and the contents never flow through — per Book of the Dead pg. 44 that package is darkvision if you lack it, the disease/poison bonus rising to +2, poison resistance equal to half your level (10 at the tested level 20), and +1 circumstance vs effects that would make you paralyzed or have the sleep trait. None of those reach AC/saves/senses/resistances. (2) "can't be destroyed by sunlight" — no `immunities`/`passiveEffects.immunities` entry, so nothing appears where the player looks up what can harm them (Q11: non-suppressible, so a passive entry, not a mode). (3) The same fact is not reflected on the vampire's sunlight vulnerability either — no `modifiesGrant`; note that Vampire Dedication never models the vulnerability as data at all (it mentions 'Revulsion and Sunlight vulnerabilities' only in prose), so there is currently no record to strike through. (4) The 'slowed' caveat has no home because clause 2 has no entry to ride on. Also worth flagging: the feat's descRefs list only 'slowed' — it does not even link to the Advanced Undead Benefits record it names.

defects.name: Dwarven Lore
defects.detail: Clause: "If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice." featGrantsAuto.ts:117 is `'dwarven-lore': { skills: { crafting: 'trained', religion: 'trained', 'lore:dwarven': 'trained' } }` — with NO `redundantFallback: true`. The lane exists and works per-skill (build.ts:3097 pushes one `skillFallbacks` entry per redundant key, and Builder.tsx:1670 renders a replacement picker for each), and ~20 sibling records use it — including the exact structural twin duskwalker-lore (featGrantsAuto.ts:115, medicine+religion+lore:boneyard+redundantFallback). The defect is observed, not inferred: I rebuilt the harness's own host (dwarf fighter, default background Acolyte, which trains Religion) — before Religion=trained, after Religion=trained, skillFallbacks=undefined. The Religion half of the grant silently evaporates and the player is never offered the replacement skill; that is why Religion is absent from the sheetDiff while Crafting shows untrained->trained. Second, smaller finding on the same record: at level 20 `lore:dwarven` is still only 'trained'. The granted Additional Lore promises skill increases at 3rd/7th/15th to its subject, and 'additional-lore' appears in src/ exactly once (featGrantsAuto.ts:22 `{ loreChoices: 1 }`) — those increases are implemented nowhere, so Dwarf Lore never advances. That half is arguably additional-lore's record rather than this one's, but it is what Ruling C asks to see reflected here.

defects.name: Sacred Defender
defects.detail: Only clause 1 is delivered. `resistances: [bludgeoning 5, piercing 5, slashing 5]` reaches the defences breakdown with "Sacred Defender" as the attributed source — correct. Clause 2, "If you're holy, this resistance increases to 10 against unholy creatures, and if you're unholy it increases to 10 against holy creatures", has NO surface anywhere: the record has no second resistance entry, no `note`, no `situational`, no mode. So a 20th-level holy champion's defences panel reads a flat 5 in exactly the fight the capstone was written for. The shapes to say it already exist — 15 live records carry a qualified resistance type string (`type: "attacks by demons"`, `"damage from siege weapons"`, `"weapon/unarmed damage (except your cursed weakness type)"`), and the character-side half is already derivable: `derive.ts:986 sanctificationOf()` returns 'holy'|'unholy'|null from the `sanctification` effectPick. Clause 3, "creatures and effects that roll a natural 20 on an attack roll against you don't improve their result by one degree of success", is likewise absent: no `note` (FeatsTab.tsx:77 renders one if present) and no `situationalBonuses` entry (`registries: []`). Ruling D puts it on AC, and `{kind:'ac'}` entries carrying a degree-of-success phrase instead of a number are established practice — situationalBonuses.ts holds ~50 of them (e.g. `predictable`, `on-my-best-day`). Sacred Defender is the only record in the data whose text contains this nat-20 clause, so there is no counter-precedent for leaving it out.

defects.name: Wortwitch
defects.detail: Every one of this feat's four mechanical clauses is absent; the record in public/core.json carries nothing but level/category/rarity/actionCost/edition/aonId, and registries is empty. (1) No leshy familiar: `wortwitch` is not in FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS (src/rules/companionGrants.ts), even though the table already holds `leshy-familiar`, `familiar-witch`, `leaf-order` and `cultivation-order` — so the leshy typing this feat promises never reaches the Companions tab. (2) No replacement: the `supersedes` field that exists precisely for this (`'improved-familiar-attunement': supersedes ['familiar']`) is unused here, so nothing tells the player the old familiar is gone. In practice the witch class already grants `familiar-witch`, so the character is not left holding two familiars — the silent failure is that Wortwitch changes nothing at all. (3-5) None of the three situational stars exist: no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry for `wortwitch`, so there is no `*` on spell attacks or Perception for "no circumstance penalties from foliage", and no `*` on attack rolls for "no flat check against a target concealed only by vegetation". Ruling B/H put all three squarely in the `situational` lane with the printed trigger in the `when` — and the app already has a near-identical authored example to copy at situationalBonuses.ts:3336 (`woodland-elf`, foliage clauses as action markers). A level-1 class feat with four concrete promises currently delivers zero.

defects.name: Heart of the Kaiju
defects.detail:
Only the damage-type choice is built. `core.feats['heart-of-the-kaiju']` carries exactly one mechanical field — `choice:{flag:'damageType', options:[acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic]}` — and the entire battle form is absent. The sheetDiff contains nothing but the feat's own name appearing in the actions list.

Missing: no mode exists for this feat anywhere (0 of 429 modes in public/core.json match /kaiju/, and the only kaiju stance is the unrelated Kaiju Stance). So there is no Gargantuan size override, no Speed 40 override, no physical resistance 5, no jaws strike (1 action, reach 20 ft, 3d12+20 piercing), no claws strike (1 action, agile, reach 20 ft, 3d8+20 slashing), and no Breath Weapon action (2 actions, evocation/primal, save vs your spell DC, 1d4-round lockout as text). This is squarely inside Q3 ('a battle form gets a mode that really overrides the stats it names, and must make plain that a mode is active and what changed'), so it is a defect and not out of scope. The recorded damage-type pick also dead-ends: nothing reads the `damageType` flag, because there is no breath weapon entry for it to flow into.

Also missing: no `modifiesGrant` on Monstrosity Shape, and that feat is itself a bare record (id/name/level/traits/prereqs only), so a player opening Monstrosity Shape to pick a form sees no kaiju option — Principle C is unsatisfied.

⚠ Worth escalating beyond this feat: the engine for this already exists and no data uses it. `BattleForm` is fully specified in src/rules/types.ts:2603 (ac, attackMod, strikes with printed fixed damage, speeds that REPLACE, senses, size, tempHp) and is read at src/rules/derive.ts:1184 and src/rules/explain.ts:757 — but `grep -c battleForm public/core.json` returns 0 and no file under scripts/data/ writes it. Every battle form in the app is therefore unbuilt, not just this one.

Secondary: `actionCost` is stored as `{type:'actions', value:1}`, which puts a 1-action activity called 'Heart of the Kaiju' in the actions list. The feat itself has no action cost — the ⟨1⟩ glyphs in its text belong to the jaws and claws Strikes — so this looks like an importer picking up the first action glyph in the body text.

defects.name: Robust Recovery
defects.detail:
Only one of the three required surfaces exists. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2219 gives `{targets:[{kind:'save', detail:'all'}], when:'on your save against a disease or poison after anyone uses Treat a Disease or Treat a…', bonus:'+4 circumstance (instead of the usual +2)'}`, which correctly puts the self-facing half — the case where someone treats YOU — on the saving throw as a restricted situational rather than in the flat total (Ruling B). Starring all three saves rather than only Fortitude is within Q2/Ruling H and I am not flagging it.

Not delivered:

(1) No star on Medicine. Q2 is 'both — star the skill AND the action', and Ruling C says a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it. The sheetDiff contains no `situational.skills` entry at all, so a player reading their Medicine number sees nothing.

(2) No marker on the Treat a Disease / Treat a Poison actions. Both action records exist in public/core.json as `treat-disease` and `treat-poison`, and RECORD_MARKERS is the exact route with a live precedent one line away — src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3237 marks `treat-wounds` for magic-hands. `grep robust-recovery` finds it only in FEAT_SITUATIONAL, never in RECORD_MARKERS.

(3) The degree-of-success upgrade is nowhere. 'If the result of the patient's saving throw is a success, the patient gets a critical success' is the more valuable half of the feat, and the requirement is only that it be READABLE in the same markers as the bonus. The stored `when` and `bonus` strings mention the +4 and nothing else, so the upgrade has vanished from the sheet entirely.

Minor, on the surface that does exist: the `when` string is truncated mid-phrase ('Treat a Disease or Treat a…'), which also drops the qualification that the +4 lands on the save and not on the Medicine check.

defects.name: Boaster's Challenge
defects.detail: Two defects. (1) DATA: the app's own description has lost the three skill names — public/core-descriptions.json stores 'For your challenge, attempt a , , or check against that creature's Will DC' where AoN (feat-1068) prints 'attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation check'. The feat's central instruction is unreadable on the sheet. This is systemic: 31 feat descriptions carry the same stripped-inline-name pattern (quill-spray, trick-shot, cannon-corner-shot, spirits-anguish, corpse-stench, devrins-cunning-stance, shard-strike, …). (2) No `*` on Deception, Diplomacy or Intimidation. situationalBonuses.ts:569 authors one entry only — targets [{kind:'strikeDamage'}], when 'against a foe you successfully challenged, until the end of your next turn (3 rounds on a critical success)', bonus '+2 status (+4 with master, +6 with legendary in the skill used)' — which correctly delivers the Strike-damage star with all three tiers and the crit rider, but no skill target, so the three skills that roll the challenge show nothing. Gold answer #6 (Mastermind's Eye) settles this exact shape: 'i want the feat to have a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the use can see what happens when he cheks his recall knolladge number'. Delivered correctly: the 1-action activity itself (sheetDiff actions[0] = Boaster's Challenge) with the linguistic/auditory/visual clause in its popup text, and no surface for the witnesses' +4 Will DC (target-side, DECIDED SCOPE).

defects.name: Torrent in the Blood
defects.detail: The granted action is right (actions[7], 2 actions, traits intact) and it correctly adds NO limitedUses for the 10-minute per-target immunity. What fails is the text itself: both printed values are deleted from the shipped description. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json feats/torrent-in-the-blood reads "creatures in a , its cleansing water" and "regains HP" — the real clauses are "in a 30-foot cone" and "regains 3d8 Hit Points" (verified against the AoN mirror feat-4273 and the Foundry source .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/class/kineticist/level-6/torrent-in-the-blood.json, which has @Template[cone|distance:30] and @Damage[(floor((max(6,@actor.level)-6)/2)+3)d8[healing]]). Root cause is the importer: scripts/import-core.mjs:283 deletes label-less @Template/@Check macros outright, and the @Damage recovery at :271 splits the formula on the comma inside max(6,@actor.level), fails its own numeric test, and returns ''. Consequence for the heightening requirement: "Level (+2) The healing increases by 1d8" survives but has no base to increase, so the entry states nothing usable at any level (should be 3d8 at 6th, 10d8 at 20th). This is systemic, not one record: 953 label-less @Template and 2,387 label-less @Check occurrences across 2,308 imported source files (623 feats, 1,399 equipment, 131 spells), and ~775 shipped descriptions already show a visible hole.

defects.name: Cursebreaker
defects.detail: Four separate failures. (1) The counteract modifier choice is unresolvable: the shipped text in public/core-descriptions.json reads "you use either your or modifier as your counteract modifier" — the real clause is "either your Occultism or Religion modifier" (Foundry source has @Check[occultism] / @Check[religion]; both deleted by scripts/import-core.mjs:283). No choice is offered and no computed value is shown, and the player cannot even learn the two options from the text. (2) "your counteract rank is half your level rounded up" is left as prose — the feat carries no `note` and no computed value (should read rank 10 for the level-20 host). (3) SPURIOUS surface: the +1 circumstance bonus is authored as {kind:'skill', detail:'all'} at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2447, so the sheetDiff stars all 16 skills — Acrobatics, Athletics, Crafting, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Performance, Stealth, Survival, Thievery included — for a check the text restricts to two named modifiers. The registry supports naming skills (detail:'occultism', detail:'religion'), so this is a guessed mapping, not the open-rules case Ruling H protects. (4) The 10-minute activity reaches no action list: actionCost is `passive`, and MainTab's isActionCost (src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:224) admits only actions/reaction/free/variable — even the existing {type:'duration'} cost, which 0 feats use, would not surface it. Correct: limitedUses 1/day, and nothing was emitted for the cursed-item degree-of-success prose.

defects.name: Adapted Cantrip
defects.detail: The feat is authored as a recorded-only pick and delivers none of its three mechanical clauses. storedFields.choice = {flag:'adaptedCantrip', kind:'open', from:{type:'spell', cantripsOnly:true}, inert:"Recorded only: the cantrip is not added to your prepared options or your repertoire — add it yourself, cast as a spell of your own class's tradition."}. So: (a) "you can choose this spell when you prepare your cantrips, in addition to your other options" — no pool membership, the cantrip never reaches the daily-preparation picker; (b) "replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell" — no second choice for which known cantrip is given up, and nothing enters or leaves the repertoire; (c) "You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition" — it never appears in the class spellcasting entry and is never relabelled to the class tradition, so it is castable with neither the class spell attack nor the class DC. Also a Q9 violation: `from` carries no tradition constraint, so spellsMatching returns EVERY cantrip including the character's own tradition — an illegal pick the builder offers by default. The record's own note concedes it ("the picker can't filter that, because your tradition depends on your class"), but openChoiceOptions already receives opts.character (openChoice.ts:47) and OpenChoiceFrom already has a `traditions` allow-list, so only an exclude-my-tradition filter is absent. This is not no_lane: the near-identical Mysterious Repertoire shape is already built — SpellAccessGrant {traditions:'any', max:1, as:'repertoire'|'list'} (types.ts:3024) is exactly "one spell from off your list, cast as your own tradition", consumed by build.ts:3468 and by the Builder's listAdditions memo (Builder.tsx:508). Finally, types.ts:1395 states `inert` has exactly two agreed shapes (Kingmaker kingdom feats; legacy content whose Remaster referent was deleted) and "Never used to paper over a pick that SHOULD work" — Adapted Cantrip is a current Player Core feat whose referent fully exists, so this use of `inert` is the misuse its own contract forbids. The empty sheetDiff is uninformative here (the host is a fighter with no spellcasting); `inert` is what settles it.

defects.name: Convocation of Earth and Moon
defects.detail: The bookkeeping lands and the entire form does not. Delivered: limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} shows and is spendable (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]), and the 1-action ability reaches the action list. Missing: there is no mode at all. registries is [] (modes.ts contains no entry for this id), core.json holds zero records with a `modes` field, and the catalog in modes.ts:209 has no sarangay entry — yet ModeDef.ancestries exists precisely to gate one. So none of the form's content exists anywhere: (a) Enlarge at 4th rank — size Huge, the +10-foot reach, the status bonus to melee damage and the clumsy condition — all absent, though ModeDef.battleForm.size (types.ts:2620) is the field for the size and Q3 explicitly requires a form-mode that really overrides the stats it names and shows the player a mode is active; (b) Fly at 4th rank — no fly Speed, though ModeDef.speeds (types.ts:2547) is the additive grant lane for exactly this. ⚠ the value here is "a fly Speed equal to your Speed", and SpeedGrants stores a literal, which is the same defect Q16 already recorded against core.json's hardcoded speeds:{fly:40}; it must resolve against the character's own land Speed, not be written as a number; (c) the head-gem moonlight aura gets no text. The dazzled condition on adjacent creatures correctly needs no model (DECIDED SCOPE: enemies; Ruling M: position), but the note MUST still exist and MUST state the DC the enemy rolls — the higher of the character's class DC and spell DC — because that is a number read off this sheet. Q1 and Q11 both point the same way (5 minutes, and the player can shut it off), so a mode is unambiguously owed. Because no mode exists, the "use this action again to return to normal form" off-switch also has no surface; when one is built it must toggle the mode without spending the once-per-day use.

defects.name: Twirl Through
defects.detail: The feat does nothing at all: sheetDiff is empty, registries empty, and the core.json record has no `skillSubstitutions`, no `situational`, and no effect-backfill entry. The clause "When you attempt to Tumble Through an enemy's space, you can use Performance instead of Acrobatics" needs `skillSubstitutions: [{ use: 'performance', forSkill: 'acrobatics', when: 'when you Tumble Through an enemy's space' }]` — the lane is fully built (src/rules/derive.ts:366 skillSubstitutions, and explain.ts:322 turns any substitution carrying a `when` into the situational note automatically, so the one authored field would deliver both required lanes at once), and four sampled feats already use exactly this shape: sly-disarm ({use:'thievery',forSkill:'athletics',when:'when you attempt a Disarm'}), mockingbirds-disarm, natural-medicine, the-immortal-attains-the-summit. As shipped the restriction cannot be got wrong because the substitution does not exist anywhere the player looks — Acrobatics shows no star and Tumble Through offers no Performance number. Note one nuance for whoever fixes it: explain.ts files the resulting note under `forSkill` (Acrobatics), so the requirement's "a `*` on Performance" half would still need the reverse-side marker.

defects.name: Vitality-Manipulating Stance
defects.detail: Settling the reader's flagged question first: it IS a stance — AoN feat-2756 carries the Stance trait, and the app models it correctly in core.json stances['vitality-manipulating-stance'], so the empty strike diff (harness never activated the stance) is expected, not a defect. The damage type is also right: AoN prints "1d4 negative damage … versatile positive", and the app stores damageType 'void' + traits ['unarmed','versatile vitality'] — the faithful remaster mapping (the app's own description text is what lost the type word, printing "deals 1d4 damage"). TWO REAL DEFECTS. (1) THE RANGE NEVER REACHES THE STRIKE, and that silently makes it a melee attack. `StanceStrike` (src/rules/types.ts:2627) has no `range` field at all, and the stance branch of deriveStrikes (src/rules/derive.ts:3230) passes name/die/damageType/traits/group only — while the natural-attack branch 25 lines above it does pass `range: na.range` (derive.ts:3204). deriveUnarmedStrike then computes `const isRanged = p.range != null` (derive.ts:2996), which is false, so Vitality Blast rolls STRENGTH to hit instead of Dexterity (derive.ts:2997-2999) and adds the Strength modifier to damage (derive.ts:3019, `dmgAbMod = isRanged ? 0 : strMod`) where a ranged unarmed Strike adds no ability modifier. On a 20th-level monk that is typically ~+2 wrong on the attack and ~+5-6 wrong on damage, and the strike row shows no 30-foot range. The 30 feet survives only as prose in the stance's `note`. No stance strike in the data carries a range (0 of 32), so the field would have to be added. (2) NOTHING MARKS STUNNING FIST. The record has no `modifiesGrant`, so the Fortitude-save-vs-class-DC alternative and its four degrees of success live only in this feat's own entry — Principle C and Q8 want them on the action being modified. The route exists and is unused: GrantModification.actionRider (src/rules/types.ts:785) renders a RecordMarker on the action row. ⚠ Aim it at `stunning-blows`, not "stunning-fist" — the app has no record by that name (Stunning Fist was remastered into Stunning Blows), which also means the feat's description reference to "Stunning Fist", and its prerequisite string "Stunning fist", point at a name nothing in core.json carries. Minor, mentioned for completeness: "versatile vitality" is displayed as a trait label only — there is no route to select the alternate damage type, but that is app-wide behaviour for versatile, not specific to this feat.

defects.name: Catchy Tune
defects.detail: The action itself is delivered — Catchy Tune reaches the action list with its degrees of success in the popup, and correctly nothing else fires (every outcome lands on enemies; the 1-hour immunity is the GM's bookkeeping, not limitedUses; no star on Performance, since no bonus is named). The defect is the one the reader flagged: THE PRINTED AREA IS GONE FROM THE APP'S OWN DATA. public/core-descriptions.json feats.catchy-tune reads "against the Will DCs of all enemies in a ." — AoN feat-2637 prints "all enemies in a 30-foot emanation". The area is load-bearing (it is the only thing that says who the action reaches), so as shipped the action cannot be used from the sheet. This is not an engine gap and must not be patched by guessing a radius — the correct value is in the archive at C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-2637.json. ⚠ IT IS SYSTEMIC, NOT ONE FEAT: 179 records in core-descriptions.json have the same dropped area token — 22 feats (catchy-tune, blazing-wave, smoke-bomb, elemental-explosion, lightning-dash, consecrated-aura, marshal-dedication, …) plus spells and items, including HEAL and HARM, whose 3-action version now reads "You disperse vital energy in a ." (AoN spell-148: "in a 30-foot emanation"). The loss is selective, not global — 223 other descriptions still print "emanation" correctly — so it is a recoverable import bug, and every one of the 179 can be repaired from the archive.

defects.name: Scales of the Dragon
defects.detail: Three of four promises are absent; the record carries nothing but one AC star (situationalBonuses.ts:342 — '+2 item' when 'while unarmored (Dex cap +3)'). (1) "Your resistance from Dragon Disciple Dedication increases to 3 + half your level" — nothing implements it. The dedication grants max(1,floor(@actor.level/2)) via effectChoices, so a 20th-level Dragon Disciple holding this feat still shows resistance 10 instead of 13 — a wrong number on the Defences panel. modifiesGrant exists but its only shapes are innateUsesPerDay / actionRider / deityDomainsFromChoice (types.ts:775-791), none of which can raise a granted resistance's value, and only 2 records in core.json use it at all. (2) The Dex cap of +3 is printed inside the star's `when` but never applied: deriveAc (derive.ts:1112+) reads dexCap only from worn armour or the active stance, so a Dex+5 character unarmored still adds the full +5. (3) The stacking exception ("cumulative with armor potency runes on your explorer's clothing, mage armor, and bracers of armor") cannot be honoured — acItem is a Math.max across potency/bracers/ABP (derive.ts:1148), so item bonuses to AC can only take the highest, never add; nothing on the sheet states the exception either. The +2 item AC itself sitting outside the total as a star is defensible under Ruling B, but Q11 argues the other way (the player cannot shut it off and isUnarmored() at derive.ts:711 makes the condition machine-readable), so I would treat that one clause as a design call rather than a clear defect; the other three are unambiguous.

defects.name: Stonemason's Eye
defects.detail: Two clauses are right: Crafting trained on the main branch (diff stored.proficiencies.skills.crafting untrained→trained), and ONE +2 circumstance Perception star whose `when` already merges both cases — "to notice unusual stonework, or stone/hidden-in-stone traps" (situationalBonuses.ts:375) — which is exactly the single-star shape Ruling B's stacking rule asks for. The redundancy branch is wrong in both directions. Text: "If you're already trained in Crafting, you instead gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat for stonemasonry." The record carries featGrantsAuto.ts:298 `{ skills:{crafting:'trained'}, redundantFallback:true }` and NO feat grant — FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS has no 'stonemasons-eye' key, though artisanal-crafter (line 59/featFeatGrants) and elemental-trade, whose texts grant the same feat, both do. And `redundantFallback` means something entirely different (build.ts:3097): when the skill is already trained it converts the grant into a free "trained in a skill of your choice" pick recorded on skillFallbacks. So a character already trained in Crafting gets no Specialty Crafting (stonemasonry) — losing its +1/+2 circumstance to Craft — and instead gains a trained proficiency in any skill they like, which this feat never grants. That second half is a real number on the sheet, not display prose. (Also unsurfaced, but per convention and Ruling H acceptable via the star's click-through: the GM's secret check and its "this check doesn't gain your normal circumstance bonus" caveat, and no Seek action mark.)

defects.name: Impenetrable Fog
defects.detail: The impulse's BURST AREA is absent from the record, verified against ground truth. The app ships "You call forth a fog bank in a within 120 feet"; AoN feat-4275 reads "You call forth a fog bank in a 10-foot burst within 120 feet." The importer dropped the area (Foundry writes it as an inline @Template[burst|distance:10]), so the entry states a range but no area at all. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the "**Level (+3)** ... Increase its maximum size by 5 feet" clause scales a base radius the record no longer states, so a level-20 kineticist cannot resolve the area from this entry at any level. ⚠ SYSTEMIC — the same stripping hits 209 records in public/core-descriptions.json (spells/heal, spells/harm, spells/cinder-swarm, spells/pollen-pods among them); this feat is one instance of an importer bug, and fixing it here alone would leave 208 behind. Two further points, both downstream of the same blocker and not the basis of this verdict: the level-scaled area has no lane on a non-spell record (a no_lane candidate once the base radius is restored — the minimum acceptable surface is the "(+3): +5 feet" line printed with the entry); and registries is empty, so there is no display-only mode for the fog's duration, which is genuinely arguable — Q1 leaves the base one-round duration as indication only, while Ruling F/N and Ruling E case 3 would earn a mode from the Sustain out to 1 minute. The concealment, difficult terrain and creature-facing clauses correctly produce nothing (battlefield/other creatures; Ruling M on position). The impulse itself does reach the actions list correctly (sheetDiff actions[7], 3 actions).
defects.question: Restoring the 10-foot burst is settled — but should the Sustain-to-1-minute fog also get a display-only mode? Q1 says a one-round base duration is indication only; Ruling F/N and Ruling E case 3 say an ongoing no-numbers effect the player sustains gets one. Which governs when the BASE duration is one round but the player can extend it to a minute?

defects.name: Medic Dedication
defects.detail: Expert in Medicine is correct (featGrants.ts:242, applied via maxRank at build.ts:3295, so Q10's guard holds — which matters here because the last clause keys off master). The defect is the use pool. `storedFields.limitedUses: {max:1, per:'hour'}` — unconditional. The text gives once per DAY, and once per hour ONLY "if you're a master in Medicine". The harness character is a level-2 taker sitting at expert (the feat's own grant), and the diff shows `limitedUses[0] → "Medic Dedication: {max:1, per:'hour'}"`. Every character who takes this feat gets 24x the intended frequency from the moment they take it until they reach master, which is usually many levels later. The correct default is `per:'day'`. Worth telling the owner: the conditional half genuinely has no lane — effectiveUses (featUses.ts:39-63) reads only `maxByLevel` (a LEVEL ladder, not a rank one) and `usesUpgrade`, which keys off another FEAT's id, not a skill rank. So "period changes at master in Medicine" cannot be expressed today; but that is an argument for defaulting to per-day plus a note, not for defaulting to per-hour.
