Second, smaller defect on the healing clause: the marker is on the wrong record. situationalBonuses.ts:2991 puts it on `targets: [{kind:'hp'}]` — a star on the HP stat — while Ruling D's own worked example is "Magic Hands marks Treat Wounds", and RECORD_MARKERS has no medic-dedication entry even though `'magic-hands'` and `'stitch-flesh'` both mark `{on:'action', id:'treat-wounds'}` correctly. So the tier table is nowhere near the Battle Medicine or Treat Wounds rows where the player uses it, and it sits on a stat that Ruling E says HP never moves. Its `when` also adds "on yourself", a restriction the text does not print (the text says "the target"); Ruling F removes the ally's NUMBER from your sheet but Principle A still requires the indication on the record you modify.

defects.name: Accursed Magic
defects.detail:
Two clauses are dropped, both in the direction of the character getting MORE than the text allows.

1) LEVEL GATES IGNORED. Text: "At 10th level, you can also cast Seal Fate, and at 12th level, you can also cast Inevitable Disaster." core.json stores all three grants flat: innateSpells = [claim-curse, seal-fate, inevitable-disaster], each usesPerDay 1, no level field. `InnateSpellGrant` (types.ts:1213-1233) has rank / heightenHalfLevel / heightenAt but NO character-level gate, and build.ts:4198 applies every grant of every owned feat with no level filter. The feat is level 8, so an 8th-level character gets Seal Fate (rank 4) and Inevitable Disaster (rank 5) — a 5th-rank spell four levels early. The harness host is level 20 so the diff looks clean; the defect lives at levels 8-11. Same shape hits `lions-magic`, which solved it the other way by silently dropping its 12th-level spell (only 2 feats in the data have this shape).

2) THE STATE GATE IS ABSENT. Text: "but only while within your curse maelstrom state." There is no mode, no note, no marker anywhere in the curse-maelstrom archetype — 0 of its 8 feats carry `modes` or `note`, and the dedication only grants the Expel Maelstrom action. The spell cards render "rank 3 · 1/day · from Accursed Magic" with a live cast pip, i.e. as freely castable innate spells. Per Q11 (a state you can shut down is a mode) this needs at minimum a note tying the three entries to the state.

Delivered correctly: occult tradition; ONE 1/day per spell rather than a pooled use (innateUses is per-spell, absent = default 1/day, pip is per spell); Wis key attribute and trained spell attack + spell DC via spellcastingGrant.

Minor, worth knowing: the "if you couldn't already cast occult spells" condition is implemented as "if you have no class caster at all" — build.ts:4096 picks any prepared/spontaneous entry and its keyAbility wins over the grant's. A wizard (arcane/Int) satisfies the printed condition and should key these to Wis; the app keys them to Int.

defects.name: Gifted Power
defects.detail: The slot itself is right — `spellSlotBonus {highestOnly:true, perRank:1}` derives the rank from the character rather than storing a constant, and the level-20 oracle host correctly goes stored.spellcasting[oracle-casting].slots.10.max 1 -> 2. The restriction is not applied and not even shown, so the app hands the player an UNRESTRICTED extra top-rank slot where the text conditions it: at level 20 that doubles the oracle's 10th-rank spontaneous casts and lets them be spent on anything in the repertoire, which is wrong in the player's favour. Two separate faults produce it. (1) The restriction sentence is stored in `spellSlotBonus.restriction` ("Only to cast one of your mystery's granted spells, heightened to this rank") and that field has NO reader anywhere in src/ — a grep for `restriction` across src/ returns only comments and unrelated matches, so even the display-only fallback the type doc promises (types.ts:911-914) never renders. It is a write-only field. (2) The record does not use the real lane. `spellSlotBonus.restricted` (RestrictedSlotGrant) is built and live — resolveRestrictedSlots in src/rules/restrictedSlots.ts, applied at build.ts:3719-3724 — and `from:'subclass-granted'` reads `entry.grantedRepertoire`, which build.ts:2312 populates from the subclass option's `grantedSpells`; all 11 oracle mysteries in core.json carry `grantedSpells`, so the mystery-derived allowed list is computable today. The one genuine gap is that RestrictedSlotGrant has byRank/byRankAt/ladder/halfHighest/perRankFrom/rankChoice but no 'at your highest rank' selector, so a small field addition is needed to say what `highestOnly` says on the unrestricted path. The Special clause (widen to Divine Access and Mysterious Repertoire spells when held) is represented nowhere, in the field or in the prose string.

defects.name: Sterling Dynamo Dedication
defects.detail: WRONG VALUE, APPLIED UNCONDITIONALLY. The feat's four `grantedStrikes` carry no `choiceValue` and are ALL named "Label", so collectGrantedNaturals (build.ts:1358-1365) — which skips an entry only when `g.choiceValue && g.choiceValue !== pick`, then dedups on `g.name.toLowerCase()` — pushes the first entry and drops the other three. Simulated against all four choice options, every pick yields the identical strike: "Label", d8 bludgeoning, traits [unarmed, shove], group brawling. That is the MANUAL POWER DRIVER. sheetDiff confirms it on the built character: strikes[0].damage 1d4+9 B → 1d8+9 B, traits agile/finesse → unarmed/shove, mapStep 4 → 5. A player who picks "Automatic Percussive" — clause "a percussive striker dynamo, which deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage and has the agile and finesse traits" — should get 1d4 with agile + finesse (Dex-driven attack, smaller MAP step) and instead gets 1d8 with shove, wrong on the die, the traits, the attack ability and the MAP. The strike also appears on the Strikes list literally named "Label", and the builder prompt is the placeholder "Prompt"; the choice values ("feature:dynamo:automatic-percussive" …) name class features that do not exist in core.json, under a `feature:` prefix nothing in src/ reads — 4 of only 4 such values in the whole database. ALSO MISSING: silver — "made of silver" has no route at all, since neither GrantedStrike (types.ts:2994) nor NaturalAttack (types.ts:2975) has a material field, so target silver weakness can never resolve (a genuine no-lane sub-item); the wind/operational-time state ("1 minute winding … 24 hours … you cannot use your dynamo unarmed attack or any other abilities from this archetype until you wind the dynamo again") has no `modes` entry, though Q11 makes it a mode that must also gate other records' grants; the manual strike's free-hand marker; and the limb placement that forces the manual option.

defects.name: Splinter Faith
defects.detail: The domain-list rewrite works (deityDomainsOf/applySplinter: the four chosen become the deity's domains, the displaced printed ones join the alternates, and every downstream picker reads the rewritten lists) — but the feat also hands out a focus spell and a Focus Point the text never grants. The evidence pack's diff is empty only because the four picks were unanswered; with them answered it is not. Measured: cleric 8, cloistered, Sarenrae, picks cities/family/freedom/nature → focus repertoire gains `face-in-the-crowd` with spellSources = "Splinter Faith", and the focus pool goes from none to {current:1, max:1}. Cause: build.ts:2105, `if (def.kind === 'domains' && DOMAIN_SPELLS[choiceValue]) featFocusSpells.push(...)` fires for ANY domains-choice feat, and applyFeatFocus is called with values[0]; the comment at the call site ("no multi-pick choice in the data grants a spell per pick") assumes a domains choice always means Domain Initiate. Splinter Faith chooses which domains are your deity's and grants no spell and no pool point, so the fix is to gate that push on the feat actually granting a domain spell (e.g. skip it when the feat carries modifiesGrant.deityDomainsFromChoice). Two secondary shortfalls in the same record: the picker's `domainPool: 'deity+alternate'` cannot offer the "up to one domain that isn't on either list", although the choice note tells the player to "pick it here" — so that pick can never be recorded, and the sheet therefore cannot know which pick was the off-list one; and the consequent "always heightened to 1 rank lower" is text in that note only, never a computed rank. The retroactive loss of an earlier Domain Initiate spell whose domain is no longer included is also not re-checked.

defects.name: Battle Harbinger Dedication
defects.detail: Toughness is granted correctly (feat added with grantedBy, maxHp 208→228 at level 20). The skill clause is wrong in three ways. (1) WRONG VALUE: the record carries a `choice` {flag:'skill', options: Acrobatics/Athletics} that renders a dropdown in the builder, but that choice is INERT for proficiency — the feat has no `choiceGrants`, and nothing in build.ts turns a `choice` value into a skill rank. The training actually comes from `FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['battle-harbinger-dedication'] = { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }` (featGrantsAuto.ts:70), a SECOND picker whose default is `opts[0]` (build.ts:3131). So a player who selects Athletics in the feat's own dropdown and leaves the 'Trained skill' sub-card empty is trained in ACROBATICS — which is exactly what the sheetDiff shows (skills.acrobatics untrained→trained, athletics untouched). (2) SPURIOUS OPTION SET: that live picker offers all ~16 skills where the text names exactly two, so the player can legally train Arcana off this dedication — a Q9 violation. Fighter Dedication (featGrants.ts:234) and Aldori Duelist Dedication (featGrantsAuto.ts:25) carry the identical printed clause and are authored `options: ['acrobatics','athletics']`, so the correct shape exists and this record just doesn't use it. (3) DUPLICATE CONTROL: Builder.tsx renders both the inert `choice` dropdown and the FEAT_GRANTS 'Trained skill' picker under the same feat — two 'pick a skill' controls, one a decoy. Also MISSING: `redundantFallback: true` is absent, so 'if you are already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in another skill of your choice' never fires (Aldori Duelist, same clause, has it); and 'If you already have this feat [Toughness], you gain another general feat of your choice' has no FEAT_PICK_GRANTS entry — it is delegated to the player by a `note` telling them to use Setup → Overrides → Grant a feat. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS has no conditional/on-redundancy shape at all, so that second fallback would need a new capability.

defects.name: Dual-Weapon Reload
defects.detail: The app gives this passive feat a fabricated action cost and lists it as an activity. `storedFields.actionCost` is `{type:'actions', value:1}` and the sheetDiff shows it inserted at actions[0], pushing Reactive Strike and Shield Block down. The printed text calls for no such thing: AoN feat-6309 (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-6309.json) has `actions: undefined` — no glyph, no Trigger, no Frequency, no Requirements — and the prose is a standing permission ("While you're wielding two one-handed weapons… you don't need a free hand to reload"), not an activity. The wrong value is authored deliberately and will survive regeneration: scripts/data/effect-backfill.json entry .6692 is `{"category":"feats","id":"dual-weapon-reload","field":"actionCost","value":{"type":"actions","value":1}}`. The practical harm is that the sheet tells the player reloading while dual-wielding costs them an extra action — the opposite of what the feat does. Separately, the requirement the text DOES make is undelivered: no RecordMarker on the `reload` action (which exists in core.json), so nothing on the wielded one-handed ranged weapon says the free-hand requirement is waived. Reporting `spurious` because the fabricated action is the wrong-value defect; the absent Reload marker rides along.

defects.name: Shadow Magic
defects.detail: The granted focus spell is computed with the WRONG tradition, the WRONG key attribute and the WRONG proficiency rank. Clauses: "Shadowdancer focus spells are occult spells" and "You become trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma." The record does store `spellcastingGrant: {tradition:'occult', keyAbility:'cha', proficiency:'trained'}` — but build.ts only ever consults `spellcastingGrants` for the INNATE entry (build.ts:4266). The FOCUS entry is built at build.ts:2615-2617 from the host CLASS: `focusTradition = grantOptions…tradition ?? focusCls?.spellcasting?.tradition ?? FOCUS_CASTING[…] ?? 'occult'` and `focusKey = choiceKeyAbility ?? focusCls?.spellcasting?.keyAbility ?? … ?? focusCls?.keyAbility[0] ?? 'cha'`, with `proficiency: 'trained'` overwritten later by the class track. I built three level-20 characters with the choice resolved to Shadow Jump: DRUID → entry `druid-focus`, tradition **primal**, key **wis**, proficiency **legendary**; WIZARD → `wizard-focus`, tradition **arcane**, key **int**, proficiency **legendary**; FIGHTER → `fighter-focus`, tradition occult (only by the hardcoded fallback), key **dex**, proficiency trained. So a druid's Shadow Jump DC is rolled off Wisdom at legendary instead of Charisma at trained — off by roughly 6 — and it is tagged primal, exactly the inheritance the text forbids. The app already models per-source focus entries (build.ts:2631-2632 splits dual-class focus "so their Focus DCs can differ"), so the capability exists; feat-granted casting profiles just never reach it. Everything else is right: `effectChoices` offers exactly the two legal options (Dance of Darkness / Shadow Jump) per Q9, each granting its focus spell; the pool comes out 1/1 on a non-caster, and build.ts:2133-2137 deliberately suppresses the feat's own `focusPoolBonus` when the spell arrives via an effectChoice (a documented past bug, fixed). Two lesser gaps: the Refocus method ("meditating within an area of dim light or darkness") has no `note` and no `refocusRestore`, so it is absent from the Refocus action (Ruling D); and "If you don't already have one" is not honoured — a druid host went from pool 1 to pool 2, since the app's model gives each granted focus spell its own point rather than treating the clause as a redundancy-conditional grant.

defects.name: Invoke Defense
defects.detail: The resistance is applied UNCONDITIONALLY where the text conditions it on the trance. "You gain resistance equal to half your level to that damage type for the duration of your spirit trance" is stored as a build-time effectChoices pick whose options grant plain `resistances:[{type, value:'floor(@actor.level/2)'}]` (core.json, from effect-backfill.json:41148). build.ts:3198 (mergeEffect) pushes a plain `resistances` grant straight into the character's defences — only `whileActive` grants are state-gated, and that union is rage|panache|hunt-prey|unleash-psyche (types.ts:2515), which has no trance. So once the player answers the builder prompt, resistance = half level to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing is permanent: present without ever spending the 1 action, present outside any spirit trance, and never removed when the trance ends. Q11 settles the shape — the effect can be shut down, so it is a mode — and the app already models this feat's sibling exactly that way: modes.ts:285 defines 'cat-invoke-offense' as a mode with duration "for the duration of your spirit trance", gated to the invoke-offense feat, next to 'cat-spirit-trance'; ModeDef even supports `resistances` (types.ts:2541). No mode references invoke-defense anywhere. Correct parts: the action entry with its printed Requirement exists (sheetDiff actions[0]), and the mutual exclusivity is satisfied incidentally because a single-select choice replaces the previous pick rather than adding a second resistance. Missing alongside the spurious application: the use-time toggle and Q3's "make plain a mode is active and what it changed" — the pick currently shows only as a build-time entry on the Feats tab.

defects.name: Six Pillars Stance
defects.detail: The restricted +4 is ALSO applied as a flat bonus. core.stances['six-pillars-stance'] (authored in scripts/data/stances.json) carries acBonus: { value: 4, type: 'circumstance' }, and derive.ts:1156-1168 pools an active stance's acBonus straight into the AC total, so an unarmored character with the stance toggled on gets +4 AC against everything — where the text restricts it to reactions triggered by your own concentrate or manipulate actions. Ruling B: a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in `situational` with the restriction as its `when`, sitting OUTSIDE the total. That situational entry already exists and is correct (situationalBonuses.ts:495, '+4 circumstance', when = 'while in Six Pillars Stance (unarmored), against reactions you triggered by using a concentrate or manipulate action'), so the same bonus is delivered twice — once unconditionally inside the AC total, once as the star. This is a one-off, not systemic: crane-stance, mountain-stance, rain-of-embers-stance and whirlwind-stance all carry genuinely unconditional stance AC. Everything else on this feat is right — the stance is in the exclusive stance manager with requires: { unarmored: true, text: 'You are unarmored' }, it reaches the actions list, and the second clause (+1 circumstance unarmed Strike damage after Casting a 1+-action spell) is present as a strikeDamage situational rendered on each Strike row (MainTab.tsx:426); that one is invisible in this evidence pack only because the harness probes ac/perception/saves/skills and never strikeDamage. Fix is to delete acBonus from the stance record and keep the star.

defects.name: Forest's Heart
defects.detail: The stance and its strike ARE built (scripts/data/stances.json 'forests-heart' → strike "Roots and Vines", 4d8, brawling, finesse/grapple/reach; exclusive stance toggle; the Handwraps clause in the stance `note`), but the derived strike is wrong in two directions at once, and the second is precisely the thing the text forbids. VERIFIED by running derive against real content (animist 16, activeStance='forests-heart'): with no handwraps the strike derives as **1d8+2 B**, not 4d8. Cause: `StanceStrike.dice` (src/rules/types.ts:2629) is declared but never read — src/rules/derive.ts:3230-3252 maps a stance strike into an UnarmedProfile passing name/die/damageType/traits/strikingFloor and DROPS `dice`, and deriveUnarmedStrike then hardcodes `const dice = 1 + strikingExtra` (derive.ts:3034). Only 3 of the 31 stance strikes have dice>1, and this is one (the others are spirit-guide-form's 3d6 Claws and 3d10 Jaws). Second, with +3 greater striking handwraps equipped the same strike derives as **3d8+2 B**, striking:2 — the striking rune added 2 dice, which the text explicitly excludes ("don't gain additional damage from striking runes"). No suppression flag exists on UnarmedProfile or StanceStrike; derive.ts:3027 applies hwRunes striking to every unarmed strike unconditionally. So the app both loses the 4d8 the text prints and applies the rune damage the text bans — the striking rune is the only thing supplying extra dice. The allowed halves of the same clause do work: potency reached the attack roll (+3, attack 23/18/13) and property runes route through runeDamage. Third, "reach 30 feet" is stored as the bare `reach` trait, which reads as the ordinary 10-foot reach trait; the 30 survives only as prose inside the stance note. Fourth, minor: the app's stored description drops the word "bludgeoning" from "4d8 bludgeoning damage" (the AoN mirror, by-category/feat/feat-7146.json, has it) — the stored damageType is correctly bludgeoning, so this is a text-import defect, not an invented type. Finesse is correct (deriveUnarmedStrike uses Dex when finesse and Dex>Str).

defects.name: Lavasoul
defects.detail:
OVER-GRANT (the reason for this verdict): the feat record carries a bare `critSpec: true` with no `critSpecWeapons` (public/core.json). In derive.ts:2402 `critSpecSources` pushes `{level, weapons: undefined}`, and `weaponMatches` (derive.ts:2477) returns true when `w` is undefined — so a level-1 ifrit with Lavasoul gains critical specialization with EVERY weapon group (a rapier crit makes the target off-guard, an axe crit splashes, etc.). The text grants no critical specialization at all; it only says what happens INSTEAD of the normal effect if you already have it.
Also wrong on the same clause: the substitute effect (1d6 persistent fire + your item bonus to unarmed attack rolls) is stored nowhere, and crit-spec text comes from the static per-group table CRIT_SPEC in src/rules/critSpec.ts, which has no per-record override. So the Magma Spike displays brawling's printed effect ("Fortitude save or slowed 1") — precisely the effect the text says is replaced (Ruling G violated). That sub-requirement is arguably no_lane: nothing can override a crit-spec effect for one strike.
MISSING: (a) the second damage instance "as well as 1 fire damage" — the strike renders `1d4+9 P` with no fire term, although the route exists: `strikeDamage: [{strikeName:'MagmaSpike', flat:1, type:'fire', appliesTo:'unarmed'}]` is read by strikeDamageRiders (derive.ts:2515) and folded in as "plus 1 fire". (b) the "requires a free hand" clause — no `note` on the record, and GrantedStrike (types.ts:2994) has no note field (the COMPANION version at companionGrants.ts:162 does).
CORRECT: the Strike itself exists with agile/finesse/unarmed, brawling group, d4 piercing, rides unarmed proficiency and handwraps runes, and the Fist is kept alongside it.
DISPLAY: the strike is named "MagmaSpike" with no space — one of ~15 camelCase granted-strike names in core.json (BigClaw, EldritchNails, IronTeeth, LivingHair, SpiritTouch, and four Sterling Dynamo strikes literally named "Label").

defects.name: Sweeping Tail
defects.detail: The app puts the companion's activity on the PLAYER's sheet and gives the companion nothing. sheetDiff adds actions[2] "Sweeping Tail" to the CHARACTER's own action list, because public/core.json stores `actionCost:{type:'actions',value:2}` on the feat itself. The source gives the feat no cost at all: AoN feat-5431's title carries `<actions string="" />`, and the "Two Actions" glyph belongs to the inline **Sweeping Tail** sub-activity the companion learns — the importer hoisted the sub-activity's cost onto the parent feat. So the character sees a 2-action activity they cannot perform, contradicting both the printed record and the companions ruling ("a companion's gains mark the companion"). Meanwhile the companion side is entirely unbuilt: COMPANION_MODS (src/rules/companionGrants.ts:179) has no 'sweeping-tail' key, so no companion stat block changes, and nothing is gated on the companion actually having a qualifying tail attack. The lane for this exact shape is built and in use — `maneuvers:[...]` on COMPANION_MODS, rendered as "Advanced maneuver" in CompanionsTab.tsx:719 and applied at companions.ts:518, which loops every animal companion and so handles the text's plural "companions" for free; 'primal-howl' is the working precedent. Fix is two-part: drop the hoisted actionCost from the feat record, and add a `maneuvers` entry (with the tail-attack condition in its note, the way 'billowing-wings' handles "companions with wings").

defects.name: Brandish Authority
defects.detail: The activity IS delivered — the sheetDiff adds `actions[0] = "Brandish Authority"`, and MainTab.tsx:257-266 builds feat actions with `desc: f.description`, so the 2-action cost and the full printed text (manifestation, 1 minute, Demoralize burst, frightened floor, Mythic Point option, start-of-turn save) all reach the popup. The Mythic Point pool is also present already (play.ts:44/183 `mythicPoints`, MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS restored per session; VitalsRail.tsx:967-974 renders the spendable pips), so requirement (a) of the limitedUses item is NOT a gap and NOT a no_lane. What is missing is the Demoralize clause: "These Demoralize attempts don't take any penalty for not sharing a language." `brandish-authority` appears nowhere in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts — neither in FEAT_SITUATIONAL nor in RECORD_MARKERS — while the app ships this EXACT clause in three places: `intimidating-glare` (line 2736, situational on Intimidation, bonus text "…ignores the not-sharing-a-language penalty"), and `dark-fields-kitsune` / `frilled-lizardfolk` (lines 3310/3313, RECORD_MARKERS on the `demoralize` action, note "…you take no penalty against a creature that doesn't understand your language"). The restriction to this feat's own Demoralize attempts is not an excuse: `dragons-blood-pudding-moderate/greater/major` (lines 1102-1104) star Intimidation for a bonus scoped to "an Intimidation check to Demoralize made with the extra quickened action this pudding grants" — Ruling B's shape, restriction in the `when`. Both anchor records exist (core.json actions/demoralize is present). Secondary and less certain: no display-only mode for the 1-minute manifestation. Q1 ("a longer duration gets a mode") and Ruling F/N ("if it runs for a limited time, the character who activated it gets a display-only mode so they can see it running") point one way; DECIDED SCOPE's enemy-effects NOT-lane and Q4 ("an enemy-condition reaction: the entry is the whole surface") point the other. I am not calling the mode a defect — the Intimidation star alone carries this verdict.

defects.name: Twinned Defense (Swashbuckler)
defects.detail: Clause: "you constantly gain the benefits of the Twin Parry action." Twin Parry's own record (core-descriptions.json, feats['twin-parry']) reads "+1 circumstance bonus to AC … or a +2 circumstance bonus if either weapon has the parry trait." The stance record core.json stances['twinned-defense-swashbuckler'] carries acBonus {value:1,type:'circumstance'} and the note "You constantly gain the benefits of the Twin Parry action while wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand." The parry-weapon half is neither computed nor printed: a swashbuckler in this stance holding a main gauche / dueling spear (parry trait) shows +1 circumstance AC on the sheet where the referenced action gives +2, and the note never mentions the +2 so the player cannot even read it inside the mode (principle B). The app can express this shape — see the conditional bonus strings it already uses, e.g. situationalBonuses.ts:845 aldori-parry "+1 circumstance (+2 if your other hand is free)". Everything else is delivered: the activity appears in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[2]), requires.text "You are wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand" is printed (MainTab.tsx:883) with the not-active state at :900, the stance is a real toggleable exclusive mode, and the active acBonus reaches AC and its breakdown (derive.ts:1164, explain.ts:818). The empty AC diff is correct — a stance is off until activated.

defects.name: Leverage Anguish
defects.detail: Both mechanical lanes are correct. The reaction reaches the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0], actionCost {type:'reaction'}), limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} is stored and appears as a per-day use, and the popup description carries **Frequency** and **Trigger** verbatim — Principle E's whole requirement — while Ruling E correctly keeps the healing off every stat. The defect is in the stored TEXT. core-descriptions.json feats/leverage-anguish reads "You regain Hit Points."; AoN feat-7583 reads "You regain 2d8 Hit Points." The base amount was dropped on import while the master 4d8 / legendary 6d8 tiers survived, so a character below master Athletics is shown no number at all and cannot use the feat. This is systemic, not one record: scanning all 19,245 described records in core-descriptions.json finds 114 whose healing dice vanished after "regain(s)/restore(s)" (spells/vital-beacon is the worst — its printed 4d10/4d8/4d6/4d4 are all four gone), 408 reading "attempt a save" with the save type deleted, 181 with an emanation/template deleted, and 67 with the skill name deleted ("attempt a check"). scripts/fix-nomirror-check-gaps.mjs already hand-patches about ten of the @Check cases, so the class is known but was never swept.

defects.name: Timelessness
defects.detail: Only the immunity lane is built. `storedFields.immunities: ["slowed","time effects","aging effects"]` and the diff confirms all three reach `defenses.immunities` with `from: "Timelessness"`. Three things the text promises are absent — `registries` is empty, so the feat is in neither FEAT_SITUATIONAL nor RECORD_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts). (1) "You reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1" — no marker. This is Ruling D's own worked example and the lane exists and is in active use: `'defy-death': [{on:'condition', id:'dying', value:'DC 9 + dying…'}]` and `'the-survivor': [{on:'condition', id:'dying', value:'+2 (+3 at 17th)'}]` (situationalBonuses.ts:3280-ish, 3245). Timelessness has no such entry, so the Dying condition row says nothing. (2) "roll twice and choose your desired result… this is a fortune effect" on the persistent-damage flat check — no marker, and again the exact lane is in use by `'stone-blood'`, `'mutated-fleshwarp'`, `'steelskin-hobgoblin'`, all `{on:'condition', id:'persistent-damage'}`. The word "fortune" therefore never reaches the player, which is what decides stacking. (3) The immunity strings are written bare. Immunities are plain strings (derive.ts:1688, 1798), so the qualifiers the text prints are writable and were dropped: "hostile" is gone from both categories, and "slowed" carries no trace of its printed exception ("except for when you gain the slowed condition through this mythic destiny"). A bare "immune to slowed" states something false about this specific character — Q12 asks for whichever spelling leaves the player least confused, and this is the confusing one. The quickened clause is correctly nothing (Q1: 1-round effects are indication only).

defects.name: Shooter's Camouflage
defects.detail: Half built. The pick is correct: `choice: {flag:'terrain', kind:'array', options:[natural, urban]}` — a recorded two-option list pick, exactly the shape the text asks for, and re-choosing is a builder action (Principle K). What is missing is the whole mechanical half. `registries` is empty and grep finds `shooters-camouflage` in no file under src/ — no FEAT_SITUATIONAL star on Stealth, and no RECORD_MARKERS entries on the Hide and Sneak actions. Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action") and Ruling C (a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it) both call for it, and the lane is in active use for this exact pair: `'quick-refugee': [{on:'action', id:'hide', …}, {on:'action', id:'sneak', …}]` and `'eclipsed-vitality'` (hide/sneak/avoid-notice) in situationalBonuses.ts:3251, 3279-ish. A permission rather than a number is precisely what Ruling B says belongs in a star's `when` outside any total, so "no number moves" is not a reason for silence. Instead the clause was parked in `choice.note` — 'In the chosen terrain you can Hide and Sneak… — applied at the table.' That field is documented in types.ts:1395 as "Why this pick is RECORDED but grants nothing mechanical", and it renders only in the builder (Builder.tsx:419, shared.tsx:2648), never on the sheet's Stealth row or its Hide/Sneak actions. One sub-point the owner may want to rule on: `SituationalBonus.when` is a static string with no route to read a choice flag (no entry in the file interpolates one), so the star can say "in your chosen terrain" but cannot name the terrain the player actually picked without a new capability.

defects.name: Magaambyan Attendant Dedication
defects.detail: Most of this feat is genuinely well built — the defect is one clause. Built correctly: the arcane/primal pick (`traditionOptions: ['arcane','primal']` in casterArchetypes.ts:138), Int-for-arcane / Wis-for-primal (`keyByTradition`, resolved at build.ts:3929), trained spell DC + attack (`proficiency: 'trained'` via archetypeProficiency), and the single innate cantrip (`innateCantrip: true`, build.ts:3947 pushes an innate entry with no slots). The diff's arcane/int values are just the unmade-pick default. MISSING: the skill clause's second branch. featGrantsAuto.ts:207 stores `skillChoices: [{options:['arcana','nature'], rank:'trained'}]` — flat trained only. The text is "either become trained in Arcana or Nature, OR an expert in one of those skills in which you were already trained", and the redundancy branch is the COMMON case here, not an edge case, because the feat's own prerequisite is "trained in Arcana or Nature". A character trained in both gets literally nothing from this clause today; one trained in Arcana can only take trained-in-Nature and can never take the expert the text offers. Both routes for this already exist and are used by neighbours: `slot.conditionalRank: {base:'trained', upgraded:'expert'}` (handled at build.ts:3127, Lion Blade's shape) and `redundantFallback: true` (aldori-duelist-dedication, featGrantsAuto.ts:25). Q10's guard is satisfied either way since the applier is `maxRank`. Secondary, and softer: the branch pick IS recorded (`choice.flag: 'magaambyanBranch'`) but grep finds it read by nothing, and the five branch-locked feats state their gate as free prose — core.json carries "Cascade Bearers affiliation", "Rain-Scribes affiliation" etc. on six feats, which checkPrerequisites (build.ts:5522) shows but deliberately does not enforce. So all five branches' feats are offered to everyone, against Q9. I flag this rather than headline it, because under-enforcement there is a documented global policy ("under-enforcing never wrongly blocks a legal pick") and the owner may prefer it stay that way. The Halcyon Speaker exemption needs nothing — no dedication lock is implemented at all, so no legal choice is being hidden.

defects.name: Culvert's Collapse
defects.detail: The activity is delivered but its damage rider is invisible. Delivered: sheetDiff shows actions[0] = "Culvert's Collapse" in the actions list at its 1-action cost (matches AoN feat-7498 "Single Action"), and the stored description opens with "**Requirements** You are in Flood Stance and were damaged by an enemy since your previous turn.", so the requirement is legible in the popup. MISSING: the clause "That Strike deals an additional 1d8 bleed damage" reaches no surface at all. `registries` is empty and `grep -rn culverts-collapse src/` returns zero hits — the feat appears in no registry in the app. A lane exists and is unused here: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts declares a `strikeDamage` SituationalTarget kind (line 37) whose entries render beside a Strike's damage with the restriction in `when` — exactly the Ruling B shape the requirement calls for ("only on the flooded river Strike made as part of this activity"). Nothing writes one, so a player reading their flooded river Strike's damage sees a number that silently omits the 1d8. SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT in the same clause: AoN's printed text is "an additional 1d8 **persistent** bleed damage"; both public/core.json's description and the evidence text drop "persistent", so even the popup understates it — persistent damage recurs each round until a DC 15 flat check ends it, which is materially different from a one-shot 1d8. Note for context (not charged to this feat): Flood Stance itself carries no grantedStrikes, so the flooded river Strike has no row of its own today.

defects.name: Intimidating Glare
defects.detail: Half the surface is built. DELIVERED: the Intimidation star — sheetDiff shows situational.intimidation[intimidating-glare] with when "when you Demoralize" and bonus "Demoralize is visual instead of auditory and ignores the not-sharing-a-language penalty" (situationalBonuses.ts:2736), correctly kept out of the Intimidation total per Ruling B. MISSING: the mark on the Demoralize ACTION itself. Q2 is explicit — "Both — star the skill AND the action" — and Q8 confirms Ruling D's shape applies to the action a feat modifies. The app has this exact lane and renders it: RecordMarker { on:'action', id, value, note } (situationalBonuses.ts:3207-3218), collected by markersFor()/recordMarkersFor() and rendered on skill-action rows at StatDetailModal.tsx:185 (`recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionSlug(a.name))`) and on granted actions at MainTab.tsx:525. RECORD_MARKERS has no 'intimidating-glare' key — and two sibling records with the WORD-FOR-WORD same clause do have one: 'dark-fields-kitsune' (line 3310) and 'frilled-lizardfolk' (line 3313), both `{ on:'action', id:'demoralize', value:'visual, not auditory', note:'Your Demoralize loses the auditory trait and gains the visual trait, and you take no penalty against a creature that doesn't understand your language.' }`. So a player who opens Demoralize in their Intimidation popup reads the stock entry — which at skillActions.ts:451 still states the −4 language penalty this feat waives — with nothing indicating either the trait swap or the waiver. Grep confirms the only other src/ references to this id are featFeatGrants.ts (seven records that GRANT the feat) and core.json holds no modifiesGrant field, so no other route supplies the mark. Note the harness could not have caught this: snapshot() in feat-evidence.mjs collects only featSituationalFor over stat refs and never calls markersFor, so an action mark is invisible to the diff in either direction.

defects.name: Cleansing Subroutine
defects.detail: Nothing reaches the sheet: storedFields carries no situational and no note, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts has no 'cleansing-subroutine' key. So Fortitude carries no star, and a level-1 android's standing poison benefit is visible only if the player opens the feat itself. Q2 settles the target (a clause attached to saves stars the save; this one names Fortitude specifically, so Fortitude alone, not all three) and Ruling B settles the shape (a restricted, non-numeric clause belongs in situational and correctly contributes nothing to the Fortitude total). The lane exists and already supports text-valued, non-numeric bonuses — see "powerful-alchemy" at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2871 (bonus: "you may use your class DC as the item's DC") and save-targeted entries such as "monks-attire" at :2114 using {kind:'save', detail:'will'} — so an entry of the form [{ targets: [{kind:'save', detail:'fortitude'}], when: "against an ongoing poison", bonus: "a success reduces the poison's stage by 2 (1 if virulent); a critical success by 3 (2 if virulent)" }] is all that is owed. The crit-success clause needs no separate surface and correctly rides in that same note (Q15 — a bigger stage reduction is the same operation with a bigger number, not "complicated", and the owner refused a degree-of-success surface for Minor Omen on identical grounds).

defects.name: Natural Magnetism
defects.detail: The two innate grants are correct: `innateSpells` carries magnetic-attraction and magnetic-repulsion, each `tradition:'primal'`, `rank:2`, `usesPerDay:1`; the diff shows both landing in `spellcasting[innate-casting].repertoire.2` with `spellSources.<spell> = "Natural Magnetism"`, and build.ts only writes `innateUses` when the count differs from 1, so each spell keeps its own independent 1/day use. What is absent is the **Special** clause: "If you chose the gildedsoul lineage, you can replace one of the above spells with Enthrall." The record has no `choice` and no `effectChoices` (public/core.json feats['natural-magnetism'] is innateSpells + metadata only), so a Gildedsoul talos can never make the swap — Enthrall is unreachable and both original spells stay. The lane exists: `EffectGrant.innateSpells` (types.ts:1026) can grant Enthrall, and the replacement is expressible as a three-option effectChoice (keep both / Enthrall replaces Attraction / Enthrall replaces Repulsion), which is how gildedsoul itself is authored. One sub-gap worth knowing: `EffectChoice.options` has no "requires you own record X" field, so Q9's legal-picks-only filter has no route to gate this on the gildedsoul lineage — the option would have to be labelled rather than filtered.

defects.name: Terrain Master
defects.detail: Empty sheetDiff and no stored fields beyond metadata — the feat is inert. The whole feat is "you can change your favored terrain", and there is no favored-terrain pick anywhere in the app to change: public/core.json feats['favored-terrain'] carries no `choice` and no `effectChoices`, and the only expression of the terrain is prose inside a situational star (situationalBonuses.ts:2220, when: "while in your chosen favored terrain, if you have unimpeded journey…") that refers to a choice the builder never offers. So the promise "make it your favored terrain" has nothing to write to, and "reverts back to your original choice" has nothing to restore. Principle K's escape hatch (re-choosing happens in the builder, no sheet surface needed — the Guerrilla Dedication precedent) does not rescue this, because the builder offers no terrain to re-choose. Separately, Principle C / Q8's marker on the Favored Terrain record has no route today: `GrantModification.actionRider` (types.ts:785) renders only as a RecordMarker, and `RecordMarker.on` is `'action' | 'condition'` — there is no way to mark another FEAT record. Root cause sits on favored-terrain, but Terrain Master is the record whose printed promise is unfulfilled.

defects.name: Childlike Plant
defects.detail: Three of four requirements are delivered correctly: featGrantsAuto.ts:92 gives `{ skills: { deception: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }` (diff shows deception untrained→trained), and situationalBonuses.ts:144 carries `+4 circumstance` with when "to Impersonate a human version of yourself" — correctly typed, correctly restricted, and correctly kept OUT of the flat Deception modifier per Ruling B. Missing: the equipment waiver, "You don't require a disguise kit when attempting Deception checks to Impersonate a human." It has no surface anywhere — no second situational entry (the `bonus` field explicitly accepts "a short effect phrase", the exact shape the owner asked for on Guerrilla Dedication's Sneak star) and no RECORD_MARKERS entry. A player reading Deception sees the +4 and nothing about the kit. Also, per Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action") the star should sit on the Impersonate row too; RECORD_MARKERS has no `childlike-plant` key, and StatDetailModal.tsx:185 renders action stars from RECORD_MARKERS only. Note that second point is systemic rather than specific to this feat — only 28 records use RECORD_MARKERS at all and zero of the ~12 Impersonate-situational feats mark the impersonate action.

defects.name: Expert Rivethun Spellcasting
defects.detail: The MECHANICS are built — do not go hunting for an engine bug. `src/rules/casterArchetypes.ts` registers `'rivethun-involutionist-dedication': mk('divine','wis',2,'rivethun')`, and mk() mints `expertId: 'expert-rivethun-spellcasting'` — this exact id. Taking it grants 4th/5th/6th-rank archetype slots at levels 12/14/16 (RANK_UNLOCKS) and raises spell proficiency to expert (archetypeProficiency). The empty sheetDiff is a harness artifact: the host is a fighter with no Rivethun Involutionist Dedication and no Basic Rivethun Spellcasting, so the archetype is inactive. What IS missing is the printed text. `core-descriptions.json` stores the whole description as the 14 characters "You gain the ." — the AoN template link ("expert spellcasting benefits") was dropped on import. Q12 (show the wording that leaves the player least confused) is failed outright: the player reads a broken sentence and is told nothing about the slots or proficiency they just gained. This is a data-repair job, family-wide: 4 feats' entire description is exactly "You gain the ." (expert- and master-rivethun-spellcasting among them), 6 more begin with it (basic-rivethun-spellcasting, the beast-gunner and prophet ladders, poisoner-dedication), and a further 35 read "You gain the benefits." — also missing the named benefit.

defects.name: Drake Rider Dedication
defects.detail: The companion itself is correct — registries lists companionGrants, and the empty sheetDiff is the specified behaviour under the companion ruling (gear and stats live on the companion's own record). Two requirements are not delivered. (1) THE DRAGON-TRAIT RESTRICTION IS ABSENT ENTIRELY. companionGrants.ts:64 is the generic boilerplate — {kind:'animal', label:'Drake Rider Dedication', note:'Grants an animal companion — choose its type and advance it in the Edit tab.'} — and CompanionsTab.tsx:1157 filters the 98 animal-companion options only by construct-vs-not. So the picker offers giant bat, ape, horse, everything, against Q9 ("the builder shows only what the player may legally pick", the Domain Fluency case). The data supports the filter: riding-drake, riding-dragonet and aon-wyvern all carry traits ['dragon','minion']. The note does not even STATE the restriction, which friend-of-the-sea's note does ("Your pet must be an aquatic creature") — so the player gets neither a filtered list nor a warning. (2) NO MARKER ON COMMAND AN ANIMAL for the telepathic bond (100-foot range; no words or gestures required). Ruling D / Q8 put the mark on the action the feat modifies; the route exists and is in use — situationalBonuses.ts:3223 marks Aid via RecordMarker {on:'action', id:'aid'} — but nothing keys 'command-an-animal' to this feat. The clause changes what performing the action REQUIRES, so losing it loses a real rules change.

defects.name: Mountain's Stoutness
defects.detail: The HP half is correct: `maxHpBonus: {perLevel: 1}` yields +20 at level 20 and is attributed by feat name in the HP breakdown (explain.ts:947-950). The recovery-check clause is entirely absent. Text: "When you have the Dying 1 condition, the DC of your recovery checks is equal to 9 + your dying value (instead of 10 + your dying value)... If you also have the Toughness feat... 6 + your dying value." The record has no `note` and no entry in `situationalBonuses.ts` (evidence `registries: []`, confirmed by grep — no hit for `mountains-stoutness` anywhere in src/). The lane exists and is live: `FEAT_SITUATIONAL` carries condition markers of exactly this shape ({on:'condition', id:'dying', value, note}) for `defy-death` ('DC 9 + dying (8 with Toughness)'), `nine-lives-catfolk`, `the-survivor`, `draddeths-edge` and `hero-gods-bond`, and VitalsRail.tsx:1034 renders them on the Dying condition row via `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'condition', c.id)`. Defy Death even models the same 'lower it further if you have Toughness' shape in one string, so Principle C's reconciliation requirement is achievable. Ruling D names the Dying condition as the correct host explicitly. So this is a promised-but-empty registry entry, not a gap.

defects.name: Eidetic Ear
defects.detail: Two defects. (1) The grant is not parameterised. `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['eidetic-ear'] = ['assurance']` (featFeatGrants.ts:61) is a bare id list — `Record<string, string[]>`, no slot for a pre-made choice. Assurance's record carries `choice: {flag:'assuredSkill', prompt:'Skill', kind:'skills'}`, and Builder.tsx:448 `grantedChoicePicker` mounts a picker over ALL 16 skills for it, storing into `build.grantedFeatChoices['assurance']`; build.ts:679 even lists it as a REQUIRED unanswered choice. So the text's "Assurance (Performance)" becomes a free player pick — Performance is neither pre-set nor enforced, and a player who picks Athletics gets a character the feat's text does not describe. Nothing in the codebase can seed `grantedFeatChoices` from the granting record (grep: the only writer besides the picker is the importer at build.ts:5106). Note this is a systemic shape — Builder.tsx:441-444's own comment cites Abadar's Avenger's "Assurance with Religion" and 52 records in the same state; the fix applied was to offer the picker, not to fix the value. (2) The stored description is corrupted: core-descriptions.json has "With a successful , you can accurately recall a sound..." — the AoN source (feat-2831 in the local mirror) reads "With a successful DC 8 flat check". The DC was dropped, so the one clause that is pure prose is unreadable, and there is no `note` starring Performance to carry it either.

defects.name: Quick Fix
defects.detail: One of four requirements delivered. DELIVERED: `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['quick-fix'] = ['rapid-affixture']` lands the feat as a bonus feat with `grantedBy: 'quick-fix'`, and because FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS never checks prerequisites, the 'even if you don't meet the prerequisites' clause is satisfied (the level-20 fighter host is not master in Crafting and still receives it). MISSING: (a) "affix or remove up to four talismans in 1 minute instead of just one" — the record has no `modifiesGrant`, although `GrantModification.actionRider` (types.ts:782-785) is documented as exactly this lane: 'a rider on the action `from` grants... rendered as a RecordMarker on that action row'. Principle C requires the change be visible IN the granted Rapid Affixture entry; Rapid Affixture's own description still reads "You take only 1 minute to Affix a Talisman" with no mention of four. (b) Principle H ("an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under BOTH costs") cannot even begin: `affix-a-talisman` exists in content.actions with `actionCost: {type:'passive'}`, but it is in neither the curated ACTIVITIES table in src/rules/actions.ts (grep 'Affix' returns nothing there) nor any record's `grantsActions`, so Affix a Talisman never appears on the sheet in ANY form — not the ordinary one, not the 3-action one. (c) The two gates on that unlock (character level 12; ignore the base feat's Crafting-proficiency requirement) therefore have nothing to gate. Rapid Affixture as granted is a name and a paragraph — it moves nothing.

defects.name: The Immortal Attains the Summit
defects.detail: The skill substitution is delivered and correctly scoped: `skillSubstitutions: [{use:'occultism', forSkill:'nature', when:'for these rituals'}]`. Because `when` is present, `skillSubstituteFor` (derive.ts:395) skips it, so Nature's number is NOT blanket-replaced; explain.ts:322-330 surfaces it as a situational star reading "for these rituals — roll occultism instead". That is the non-leaking shape the text requires. MISSING: (a) `grantsRituals` is absent, so Control Weather and Plant Growth never reach the Rituals section. The lane is live and used — build.ts:3521-3542 assembles `grantedRituals` from feats, class features, heritage, background and worn items, and 8 feats already carry it (read-the-land, harrower-dedication, awaken-others, witness-of-earth, feast-planner, patron-reborn, ...). Both spells exist in core.json as `ritual: true` (control-weather rank 8, plant-growth rank 4), so the guard at build.ts:3537 would pass. (b) "On a success with one of these rituals, you gain the effects of a critical success instead" has no surface. `grantsRituals[].note` is the documented home for exactly this rider (types.ts:271-274), and it is unreachable while (a) is unfixed. Note `degreeShifts`/`successToCrit` cannot host it — DegreeShift targets skills, saves and actions only, not spells/rituals — so the ritual note is the right route. (c) "regardless of your actual existential state, now register as a living being to effects that can detect living creatures" has no surface: `grantsCreatureTraits` (types.ts:659-670, ruling Q6, rendered on the Details tab via `creatureTraitsOf`) is empty and there is no `note`. A knock-on: the Nature star's phrase "for these rituals" has no antecedent anywhere on the sheet while the rituals themselves are absent.

defects.name: Hobgoblin Lore
defects.detail: Clause: 'If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.' src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:172 reads `'hobgoblin-lore': { skills: { athletics: 'trained', crafting: 'trained', 'lore:hobgoblin': 'trained' } }` — no `redundantFallback: true`, and no hand-authored override in featGrants.ts. Grants RAISE only, so for the very common case (a fighter/barbarian/monk already trained in Athletics by class) the grant is silently swallowed and no replacement-skill pick is ever offered; the redundantFallback + skillChoice lanes are both unfired. The machinery is already there and per-skill and already excludes lore keys (build.ts:3097, picker at Builder.tsx:1670) — every sibling ancestry-lore feat with the identical printed clause carries the flag (android-lore:30, azarketi-lore:65, conrasu-lore:97, nagaji-lore:223), so this is a one-word omission. Everything else on the feat is correct: Athletics and Crafting both reach the skill list as real rank, Additional Lore is granted outright with grantedBy 'hobgoblin-lore' and is NOT asked to pick a subject (the loreChoices picker only renders for slot-picked feats), and lore:hobgoblin reaches the sheet as a rollable Lore (MainTab.tsx:181 builds skillKeys from the lore: proficiency keys).

defects.name: Exultant Blood Magic
defects.detail: Clause: 'when you Cast a Spell from your repertoire and you are at least Drained 2, double the extra damage dealt by that spell from Rage instead.' Nothing carries it — registries is empty for this id, the record has no `modes`, no `note`, no situational entry. The app already ships this exact lane for the feat one tier down: situationalBonuses.ts:2765 gives surging-blood-magic a spellDamage star, when 'raging repertoire spell while Drained 2+', bonus '+2 (total 3)'. Because 'instead' is an upgrade that replaces (Ruling G) and principle C requires the change to show in the thing it modifies, a level-18 character holding this feat currently reads a stale '+2 (total 3)' on their spell damage — the un-upgraded value — with no indication it doubles. The slot half IS correct and its empty sheetDiff is expected, not a defect: spellSlotBonus {perRank:1, entryId:'bloodrager-dedication-casting'} is applied per rank to that entry alone at build.ts:3888-3906, before the entry is built, so it is properly scoped to the bloodrager archetype's own ladder and inert on the fighter test host. Secondary (data-text, not mechanics): the stored description reads 'You gain the benefits.' where AoN feat-7246 prints 'You gain the master spellcasting benefits' — an AoN link-stripping truncation shared by rising-/surging-blood-magic. The mechanic behind it is delivered (casterArchetypes.ts:120 masterId), but the player cannot read what tier they got.

defects.name: Spiral Sworn
defects.detail: Delivered: the action entry appears (sheetDiff actions[2]='Spiral Sworn'), and both damage clauses are authored correctly in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2146 — targets [{kind:'strikeDamage'}] '+status equal to your number of weapon damage dice' and [{kind:'spellDamage'}] '+status equal to the spell's rank'. Bonus TYPE is status in both, matching the text, and the truncated `when` is fine because StatDetailModal.tsx:118-131 renders a 'Full text' click-through per Ruling H. MISSING — the mode. Clause: 'For 3 rounds, your Strikes and spells deal additional damage…'. Q1 rules 1 round = indication only and 'a longer duration gets a mode'; 3 rounds is longer, so Q3's shape (make plain a mode is active and what changed) is owed. core.json `modes` holds 429 modes, 97 of them gated by a feat via `feats:[id]`, and NONE mentions spiral-sworn. Systemic, not a one-off: of 159 situational entries whose `when` names a multi-round or minute duration, zero have a mode — including shield-the-faithful, the very feat Q1 names as 'is a mode'. SECOND, smaller gap: the printed 'Frequency once per 10 minutes' survives only as prose in the description; storedFields carry no `limitedUses`, even though the schema supports exactly this ({max:1, per:'minute', every:10}, types.ts:1204-1208, used by 6 feats). 75 of the 78 feats printing 'once per 10 minutes' likewise carry no tracker. The ally-redirect and 'if your spiral is glowing' clauses need nothing beyond the printed text (Ruling F) and have it.

defects.name: Specialized Megafauna Companion
defects.detail: Delivered: companionGrants.ts:288 gives maturityFloor 'specialized' plus a note naming the four options and the three-times/three-maximum rule, and a chosen specialization really does reach the companion's own block (companions.ts:376-388 layers its abilityBoosts, acRank and speedBonus) — so the standing companion ruling is honoured and absence from the character's own rows is correct. MISSING — the repeat picks. Clause: 'You can select this feat up to three times. Each time, add a DIFFERENT specialization… Your megafauna can't have more than three specializations.' `CompanionConfig.specialization` is a single string (CompanionsTab.tsx:1588 writes `{ specialization: id }`; companions.ts:376 reads `cfg.specialization`), so the second and third instances of a feat the record itself marks maxTakable:3 overwrite the first — exactly the silent-overwrite the text forbids. The companion can never hold two specializations, let alone three. SECOND defect: SpecializationPicker (CompanionsTab.tsx:349-351) does `Object.values(content.companionSpecializations)` with no filter, offering all 11 (ambusher, daredevil, wind-chaser, shade, deep-diver, steadfast-strider, wildfire-scorcher included) where the feat allows only bully, racer, tracker, wrecker. Q9 says the player is shown only what they may legally pick. Nothing excludes a specialization an earlier instance already took either, but that is moot while only one can be stored.

defects.name: Linked Focus
defects.detail: Delivered: limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} is stored and reaches the sheet (sheetDiff limitedUses[1]), and the focus-pool requirement is met by the existing pip control — SpellsTab.tsx:1655-1656 toggles each point with title 'Spend focus point' / 'Restore focus point', which is precisely the one-off restore of a SPENT point the clause asks for, distinct from pool size and from Refocus (line 1672). MISSING — the marker on Drain Bonded Item. Clause: 'when you Drain your Bonded Item to cast one of your arcane school's curriculum spells, you also regain 1 Focus Point.' Ruling D and Q8 put the mark on the action the feat modifies, and the app has that exact route: the MARKS table in situationalBonuses.ts (shape {on:'action'|'condition', id, value, note}, 61 entries, e.g. magic-hands→treat-wounds, black-powder-boost→leap). The sibling feat marks the SAME action — situationalBonuses.ts:3286 'superior-bond': [{on:'action', id:'drain-bonded-item', value:'+1 use/day', …}]. linked-focus has no entry (evidence `registries` is empty), so a wizard opening Drain Bonded Item sees nothing about the daily focus refund, and nothing names their own school's curriculum as the trigger condition — the note must say which curriculum, since that list is per-character. core.actions carries 'drain-bonded-item', so the mark has somewhere to land.

defects.name: Sundown Street Posturing
defects.detail: Delivered: the activity appears in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[2]) with its full text, and the frequency is stored as an ELAPSED-HOUR limit, limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'} — not a daily pip — which is exactly what the Frequency line asks for. MISSING — the substitution surface. Clause: 'You can substitute the result of this check for one Reflex save you would be required to attempt in the next minute.' There is no `*` on Reflex and none on Diplomacy or Intimidation: evidence `registries` is empty, situationalBonuses.ts has no 'sundown-street-posturing' key, and the sheetDiff carries no situational.* path at all. Ruling D puts the mark where the player is looking when it matters (the Reflex save) and Q2 says star the skill AND the thing, so all three surfaces are owed and none exists. Note the `skillSubstitutions` field cannot be the route — types.ts:483-495 types it `forSkill: SkillId`, skill-to-skill only, with no way to name a save. The available route is the situational registry, targets [{kind:'save',detail:'reflex'},{kind:'skill',detail:'diplomacy'},{kind:'skill',detail:'intimidation'}] with the swap phrased in `bonus`, the way athletic-strategist (situationalBonuses.ts:2692) already phrases 'substitute the stratagem roll…'. The two limits (exactly ONE save, only one required within the next minute) would ride in the `when`. Fortitude and Will correctly get nothing — but so does Reflex today. The one-minute holding window has no display-only mode either, though that requirement was derived rather than owner-stated.

defects.name: Oni Form
defects.detail: The toggle half is delivered: core.json `stances['oni-form']` carries `form: true` plus a note holding the whole printed text (Large + clumsy 1, "doesn't change Speed, reach", equipment resize, the Impersonate line, the 10-minute Sustain cap and the 10-minute natural-form cooldown), and MainTab.tsx:862-908 renders it as a player-toggled Form chip with that note printed while active. Three requirements are not delivered. (1) "Using Oni Form counts as creating a disguise for the Impersonate use of Deception" gets no `*` on Deception and no marker on the Impersonate action — `src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts` contains no `oni-form` key at all (evidence `registries: []`), even though both routes exist and are heavily used (FEAT_SITUATIONAL for the skill, RECORD_MARKERS `{on:'action', id:'impersonate'}` for the action; `core.actions['impersonate']` is present). Q2 asks for both the skill and the action; Ruling C/D put the mark where the player looks the number up. (2) "Your size increases to Large" moves nothing: StanceDef (types.ts:2641) has no size field, build.ts:4613-4632 reads `sizeOverride`/`sizeSet` from feats and heritages only, and the one route that could carry a form's size — `ModeDef.battleForm.size` (types.ts:2620, consumed at derive.ts:1184) — is used by 0 of the 429 records in the `modes` bucket. The sheet stays Medium with the form up. (3) Clumsy 1 reaches no number (no −1 status to AC/Reflex/Dex skills); this one matches the app's own precedent (`modes['dire-form']` and `modes['item-hydra-mutagen']` both leave an identical "you are clumsy 1" clause as note text for the player to apply through src/rules/conditions.ts), so it is the weakest of the three. The `*` on Deception/Impersonate is the unambiguous miss.

defects.name: Secrets of Shadow
defects.detail: Two problems, one certain and one a value defect. (1) MISSING, Principle C: "Your shadow reservoir gains an additional spell 1 rank below the highest rank spell you can cast" is reflected nowhere in the reservoir. The app models the reservoir as a free-text/inert record on `feats['shadow-reservoir']` — `choice: {flag:'reservoirSource', kind:'text', inert:"Recorded only: the reservoir itself isn't tracked — note down one spell of each rank at least 2 ranks below your highest..."}` — and that inert text still describes only the base contents. Secrets of Shadow carries no `modifiesGrant` (storedFields shows only `effectChoices`), so a player who owns both reads the base list on the reservoir and never sees the extra spell where they read the reservoir. (2) VALUE: the text says "void resistance equal to the highest rank of spell you can cast FROM SPELL SLOTS", but both effectChoices options store `min(10,ceil(@actor.level/2))` — a character-level proxy, the only record in core.json using that formula. It is exactly right for a full caster and wrong for everyone else this feat is written for: a magus/summoner is over by 1 at 20th, and a multiclass-archetype caster (whose highest slot rank at 20 is 8th) is over by 2 — and Shadow Reservoir's own note explicitly contemplates that population ("Only needed if you have more than one source of spells you can cast from spell slots (e.g. a multiclass caster archetype)"). `resolveFormula` (derive.ts:1333-1366) supports only @actor.level, ability mods, speeds and archetypeFeats — there is no token for highest spell-slot rank, which is presumably why the proxy was written. What IS right: the void/vitality swap is modelled as an exclusive two-option `effectChoices` (never both), which is the correct shape under Ruling H for the open-ended "or are otherwise harmed by vitality damage" parenthetical, and the empty sheetDiff is just the unmade choice.

defects.name: Urban Jungle
defects.detail: Nothing is built for either clause. storedFields carries only level, category, rarity, prerequisites, actionCost, edition and aonId; sheetDiff is empty; `registries` is empty; and the id 'urban-jungle' appears in no file under src/ or scripts/. (a) "You can use your choice of Survival or Society to Track" has an exact existing lane that is left empty — `skillSubstitutions {use, forSkill, when}` (src/rules/types.ts:483, resolved by src/rules/derive.ts:366, already populated on 26 feats) — and wants {use:'society', forSkill:'survival', when:'to Track while in an urban area'}. This is the load-bearing half: it changes WHICH modifier is rolled, and the restriction correctly travels in `when` rather than replacing the Survival number (the type's own doc calls out exactly this Natural Medicine trap). Without it the player has no Society number for Track at all. (b) "You can move at your full Speed while you Track" has no `situational` entry, so no star reaches the Track action, and none reaches Survival or Society where Ruling C says the player looks. Correctly, no Speed number should change — the sheet's Speed is untouched, which is the one thing this record gets right by accident. The feat's entire surface today is its description plus the Track glossary link in its descRefs.

defects.name: Underwater Volcano
defects.detail: Two of three requirements are delivered correctly: the innate grant lands at stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].repertoire.7 — rank 7 as the text demands (volcanic-eruption's own base rank is also 7, so this holds either way), tradition primal, spellSources names "Underwater Volcano", and the once-per-day use is real even though `usesPerDay` is absent, because build.ts:4254 reads (g.usesPerDay ?? 1) — the card renders "rank 7 · 1/day" with a spendable pip. What is missing is the amendment marker. The text grants a MODIFIED spell — "you can only evoke the volcano on the floor of a body of water, and the effects that normally happen to flying creatures happen to swimming creatures instead" — and nothing carries that onto the spell entry, so the player opens Volcanic Eruption from the Spells page and reads the unamended text. The lane for this exists and is exactly the shape Ruling G established ("on the spell, since that's what you're looking at when you cast it"): SPELL_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371, consumed via spellMarkersFor → spellSituationalFor → marksFor on every SpellCard (SpellsTab.tsx:1080, 1777). It currently holds only two entries (harm/sap-life, dancing-blade/the-distant-grasp) and none for volcanic-eruption. Fix: SPELL_MARKERS['volcanic-eruption'] = [{source:'underwater-volcano', when:'granted by Underwater Volcano', bonus:'only evocable on the floor of a body of water; effects that normally hit flying creatures hit swimming creatures instead'}].

defects.name: Illuminating Stories
defects.detail: The bonus half is delivered and correctly typed. FEAT_SITUATIONAL['illuminating-stories'] (situationalBonuses.ts:677) stars every skill with when "after you Offer a Story and choose illumination, on checks to Recall Knowledge for the story's duration" and bonus "+1 status (+2 if master in Religion, +3 if legendary)" — status, not circumstance, and the Religion-rank ladder is spelled out rather than hardcoded at +1, so the scaling clause is met. The skill:'all' target is not spurious: it is this project's settled convention for every Recall Knowledge bonus (tales-of-the-road, thorough-reports, puzzle-solver, uzunjati-recollection, brains, ask-the-bones, i-knew-the-heroes all use it), it is the only way to reach Lore, and the restriction rides in `when` per Ruling H. Situational entries are display-only stars and never enter totals, so nothing is applied unconditionally. THREE clauses are unmet, all on the action side, and none has any entry in RECORD_MARKERS: (1) "can Recall Knowledge about the topic of the story as a free action" — principle H and gold answer #13 require the action under both costs; core.json has action `recall-knowledge` (1 action) and the marker lane can express a cost change (see RECORD_MARKERS['quick-unlock'], value "1 action"), but nothing marks recall-knowledge, so the free action is invisible. This is a real mechanical benefit that is entirely absent. (2) Q2 requires the ACTION starred as well as the skills — recall-knowledge carries no mark. (3) Principle C/A: no mark on `offer-story` (the action exists in core.json) saying this feat adds an alternative benefit choosable in place of the normal one, that the story may be about any topic, and that the creature you share the story with may take the illumination even if you did not — the ally clause has no number owed but per principle A must be visible on the record it modifies.

defects.name: Close Contract
defects.detail: Clause: "gain 15 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour". No mode exists — core.json `modes` has no close-contract entry (429 modes, checked by id), and the feat carries no modes/registries at all. Q1 governs: "Effects lasting 1 round are not implemented — indication only. A longer duration gets a mode", and an hour is far past that; Ruling E case 3 gives the same shape for an ongoing effect that changes no numbers. Q15 does NOT override here — it is scoped by its own words to "an effect that fires on a critical success", and its precedence clause ("Q15 comes first") only arbitrates when both apply; Close Contract is a deliberate 1-action activity, so only Q1 applies. The app's own practice agrees: Form a Flock (up to 1 minute, 25 temp HP) has a display-only mode with modifiers: [] and the temp HP in its note; so do Immortal Techniques and Renewing Cycle ("Enter them in the temporary HP box yourself"). Close Contract is the longest-running of the set and is the one without a mode. Correctly delivered: the activity is in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0], 1-action cost) with its **Requirements** line reproduced in the popup text, and the temp HP rightly move no sheet stat (decided scope). Not counted as a defect: the level scaling — the printed text carries "increases by 5 at 12th level and every 2 levels thereafter" verbatim, which matches how the app states tiers elsewhere rather than resolving them; if a mode is added, its note should carry the character's own figure (15/20/25/30/35/40).

defects.name: Flame Jump
defects.detail: Clause: "You can spend 1 minute in focused preparation, then enter a fire your size or larger to instantly teleport…". The activity never reaches the actions list. core.json stores actionCost {type:'passive'} and no grantsActions, so MainTab.tsx:224-256 filters it out — its local isActionCost accepts only actions/reaction/free/variable, and "passive feats … must NOT be listed as activities". Flame Jump surfaces only on the Feats tab; a player looking on the Actions tab for something to do finds nothing. This is the neighbouring shape to Principle H (an action with NO glyph, stating a time instead), and the app is half-built for it: types.ts:136 already defines ActionCost `{type:'duration'; text}`, but zero records in feats/actions/classFeatures use it (counted), and both isActionCost implementations (widgets.tsx:63 and MainTab.tsx:224) exclude 'duration', so retyping alone would not list it — MainTab's filter has to accept duration too. Not no_lane: grantsAction and the duration cost type both exist, they are just not wired together. Correctly delivered: **Frequency** once per day is stored as limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'} (effect-backfill.json) and draws pips on the feat's Feats-tab entry. Correctly absent: no fire immunity/resistance on the defences block (the protection exists only while using the ability — Ruling B/I), no inventory check for extradimensional spaces, no surface for the fire-location sense.

defects.name: Adaptive Vision
defects.detail: Clause 1 is right: situationalBonuses.ts:99 stars all three saves ({kind:'save', detail:'all'}) with when "against visual effects", bonus "+1 circumstance", and no flat save total moved — Q2 plus Ruling B, exactly as owed. Clause 2 is not delivered: "If you roll a success on a saving throw against a visual effect, you get a critical success instead" appears in no star. SituationalBonus has no note field, so this app's own convention is to carry a degree-of-success clause inside `when` — and every sister feat does: breath-control "against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)", forlorn, emotionless, well-groomed, wind-tempered, dragonblood, abjure-the-false-kin. Adaptive Vision's `when` stops at "against visual effects", so the player reading the save popup at the moment a visual effect fires sees the +1 and nothing about the upgrade. Q15 does not cover this — that ruling governs an effect that FIRES on a critical success; here the trigger is a success. Fix is one string: when: "against visual effects (a success becomes a critical success)". The Access clause correctly earns nothing (Q5).

defects.name: Grasping Limbs
defects.detail: The pick is recorded (core.json choice flag graspingLimbs, options primary/secondary) but the app itself declares the feat inert: "Recorded only — Grab isn't added to your eidolon's attack." Nothing else in src references grasping-limbs; it has no COMPANION_MODS entry, so the eidolon stat block gains neither the Grab action nor even a note. That note lane is live and is this app's established shape for eidolon strike effects (companionGrants.ts COMPANION_MODS — plant-eidolon carries "all its melee unarmed Strikes gain the reach trait" as a note; psychopomp-eidolon uses strikeRider), and deriveEidolon (companions.ts:~810-830) already renders per-attack traits, so a route exists — this is unbuilt, not unbuildable. The DECIDED SCOPE companions ruling puts the mark on the companion, which is precisely the surface that is empty. Secondary, against Q9: the option list offers Primary/Secondary unfiltered rather than only attacks carrying grapple — and it cannot filter today, because the upstream Advanced Weaponry (the only source of the grapple trait) is itself marked inert, so no eidolon attack in this app ever has grapple. Both records need building together.

defects.name: Reliable Squire
defects.detail: Half delivered. situationalBonuses.ts:326 stars every skill ({kind:'skill', detail:'all'}, when "to Aid", "+2 circumstance") and folds into no flat total — Ruling C/H and the skill half of Q2, correct. Three gaps: (1) the critical-failure floor, "If you roll a critical failure on a check to Aid, you get a failure instead", is nowhere — not in `when`, and there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry, even though the app already implements this exact mark for a different record: RECORD_MARKERS['the-publican'] = [{on:'action', id:'aid', value:"crit fail → fail", note:"…critically failed checks to Aid count as failures…"}]. (2) Q2's action half: the Aid row (actions.ts:42) carries no star for this feat, though RECORD_MARKERS is exactly the lane for it. (3) The printed Aid rule allows an attack roll as the check, and Ruling H says stay open — sibling entries fake-out and seasoned-command both carry a {kind:'strikeAttack'} target for Aid; this one has only 'skill'. Note the harness cannot see (2) or (3): feat-evidence.mjs snapshots situational refs for ac/perception/saves/skills only, so I read the registry directly.

defects.name: Legendary Sneak
defects.detail: Nothing at all is stored for this feat. core.json carries only level/category/prereqs/actionCost; `sheetDiff` and `registries` are both empty; grep finds `legendary-sneak` nowhere in src/ or scripts/data/. Both promised surfaces exist and are populated for near-identical feats, so this is an omission and not a lane gap: (a) the lifted precondition "Hide and Sneak even without cover or being concealed" is exactly the shape of RECORD_MARKERS entries `camouflage-tripkee` (hide + sneak, "…without cover or being concealed") and `camouflage-pigmentation` at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3305-3306; (b) the Avoid Notice ride-along is the shape of `wary-skulker` and `eclipsed-vitality`, which both carry `{on:'action', id:'avoid-notice'}` marks. Legendary Sneak has neither, and no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry starring Stealth (Ruling C/Q2 wants both the skill and the action). Result: a 15th-level capstone whose entire content is readable only inside its own feat description. No number is wrong — this is display/reach.

defects.name: Communal Healing
defects.detail: The requirement is Principle A applied to a spell: a marker on Heal saying this feat modifies it, carrying the gate (single-target casting only, not the burst) and the amount (HP equal to the spell's rank). The lane is SPELL_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371), rendered through spellSituationalFor/explain.ts:398 — and its ONE feat entry is the exact structural twin of this feat: `"harm": [{ source: 'sap-life', when: "when your harm damages at least one living creature, and you are living", bonus: "regain HP equal to the spell rank" }]`. Communal Healing is Sap Life's vitality mirror and has no entry on `heal`; `registries` and `sheetDiff` are both empty and grep finds it in no registry. Ruling F correctly keeps the number off this sheet (the HP land on another creature), but the round-1 correction is explicit that the ally-facing half still owes a visible marker on the record it modifies. Side note, inert but stale: src/rules/seed.ts:126 still describes this feat with its LEGACY text ("you regain Hit Points equal to the spell rank"), contradicting the remaster text — core.json wins the merge so the player never sees it.

defects.name: Slay
defects.detail: Lanes are right: the action reaches the sheet (sheetDiff actions[2] null→"Slay"), its Requirements line and the "incapacitation effect" sentence ride in the popup text, the per-target 1-day immunity is correctly NOT limitedUses, and the class DC is correctly given no save-breakdown entry (referenced, not modified — Ruling D's DC-only provision is not triggered). The defect is the stored description itself: it reads "4d6 extra precision damage with a save against your class DC" — the words "basic Fortitude" are gone. AoN feat-7236's markdown reads "with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC". Root cause is in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/import-core.mjs (~line 281): label-less inline macros are deleted outright — `.replace(/@[A-Za-z]+\[(?:[^\[\]]*\[[^\]]*\])*[^\[\]]*\](?:\{([^}]*)\})?/g, (_m, label) => label || '')` — so Foundry's `@Check[fortitude|basic:true|against:class-dc]` leaves a hole. Measured on the 500-feat audit sample: 12 of 498 feats lost the named save this way (tremor, realm-strider, slay, essence-overflow, as-a-thousand-soldiers, battle-hymn-to-the-lost, regurgitate-mutagen, scouring-rage, venipuncture, fiery-rebirth, patrons-claim, heart-of-the-kaiju). scripts/fix-nomirror-check-gaps.mjs already repairs a hand-listed subset of the same loss, so the pattern is known but unswept for save names.

defects.name: Incredible Scout
defects.detail: Nothing is delivered: sheetDiff is empty, storedFields carry no modifiesGrant/situational/note, and the feat appears in no registry. Correct that no number lands on the character's own initiative (Ruling F), but Principle C/A require the upgrade to be reflected on the record it modifies.
