The Scout exploration activity IS on the sheet — src/rules/actions.ts:98 renders it with the text "granting everyone a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative", and MainTab.tsx:525 hangs recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionId(a.name)) on that row. The route is not merely available, it is already used for this exact action: situationalBonuses.ts:3293 gives 'wary-skulker' markers on both 'scout' and 'avoid-notice'. So a character with Incredible Scout reads a Scout row that still says +1, with no mark and no mention of the feat. Fix shape: RECORD_MARKERS['incredible-scout'] = [{ on:'action', id:'scout', value:'+2 circumstance', note:'Your allies get +2 instead of +1 to initiative when you Scout.' }].

defects.name: Tunnel Roll
defects.detail: grantsAction is delivered (sheetDiff actions[2] → "Tunnel Roll") and the terrain conditions survive as text. The mode lane is not: none of the 429 records in core.json `modes` names this feat (97 of them are feat-gated via `feats: [id]`, so the route exists and is in normal use), and storedFields carry no mode, note or situational. The rolling state runs an indefinite number of turns — past Q1's one-round indication-only threshold — and the rules can shut it down (bottom of the incline, or an obstacle), which Q11 makes a mode rather than a passive; the Slowed 2 it imposes is self-facing, so no DECIDED SCOPE exclusion removes it. Note the numeric half is already reachable by hand — 'slowed' is a valued condition in core.json and ConditionsModal gives valued conditions a ± stepper — and mode records have no condition field (their keys are modifiers/resistances/speeds/senses/immunities/weaknesses/spellSlotBonus/strikeDamage/grantedStrikes), so the honest deliverable is a display-only mode carrying "still rolling: Slowed 2 each turn after the first; ends at the bottom of the incline or on an obstacle (you and it take 4d6 bludgeoning)". Secondary defect, same import cause as Slay and The Dead Walk: the description reads "both take 4d6 damage" where AoN feat-5391 says "4d6 bludgeoning damage".

defects.name: Healing Flesh
defects.detail: The skill half is right and should not be touched: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:527 gives Medicine a `*` with `bonus:"+1 item"` — correct TYPE, not a circumstance substitute — and the restriction sits in `when` rather than in the flat total, exactly Ruling B. No flat Medicine change appears in the diff. Two requirements are not delivered. (1) **The healer's-tools waiver is absent.** The `when` reads "when you take 1 damage to give a drop of your blood while Administering First Aid, Treating Disease, or Treating Wounds" — the cost is carried, but "you don't need healer's tools" appears nowhere on the sheet. That is arguably the larger of the feat's two benefits (it removes a printed Requirement on another record's activity, so Ruling C applies), and the app already folds this exact clause in elsewhere: `transposable-compliance` (same file) says "using your own physiology instead of healer's…" in its `when`. (2) **No marks on the three named activities**, which Q2 requires explicitly ("Both — star the skill AND the action"). The lane for this exists and is live: `RECORD_MARKERS` in the same file (structure at line 3207, `{on:'action', id:'treat-wounds', …}`) with 17 action entries including magic-hands→treat-wounds; and all three target ids — `treat-wounds`, `treat-disease`, `administer-first-aid` — exist in core.json's actions bucket, so the marks are authorable today. `grep -rn healing-flesh src/` returns exactly one line, so there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry. Systemic note: this is not unique to this feat — folk-healer, right-hand-blood, vasodilation, healers-toolkit-expanded, violet-ray and natural-medicine all carry the skill star and no action mark, so Q2's action half looks under-delivered across the Medicine cluster. The heart-and-liver clause correctly produces nothing (Ruling F).

defects.name: Experienced Smuggler
defects.detail: Nothing is delivered at all. `grep -rn experienced-smuggler src/` returns zero hits — no situationalBonuses entry, no RECORD_MARKERS entry — storedFields carry only metadata, registries is empty, and sheetDiff is empty. Neither harness limit applies (no featPickGrants; the effect is on the character's own Stealth check). So Stealth carries no `*`, and a player reading their Stealth row has no way to learn the die floor exists. This is NOT a no_lane case: `SituationalBonus.bonus` is a free prose string, and the registry already carries non-numeric values of exactly this shape — `caretakers-calling` uses "attempt the check at mythic proficiency" — so a minimum-die-result is expressible without inventing anything. The proficiency tiering (floor 10 trained/expert, 15 master, automatic success at legendary) can ride in the same string the way `vasodilation` does with "+1 item (+2 master / +3 legendary in Medicine)", satisfying Q12 by printing all three tiers rather than stating a false fixed 10. The Q2 action half is also absent: `conceal-an-object` exists as an action id in core.json, so the RECORD_MARKERS mark has a valid target. The "no benefit when a creature actively Searches you" exclusion belongs inside that same `when` (Ruling H) and is likewise absent. One point I am deliberately not calling a defect: the PFS Earn Income / Underworld Lore clause is organized-play-only and conditional on the character actually having Underworld Lore, so whether it earns a surface is a policy call, not a build failure — I left it out of the verdict.

defects.name: Sacred Ki
defects.detail: The record carries nothing at all. `core.json` holds only id/name/traits/rarity/source/level/category/edition/aonId — no `choice`/`effectChoices`, no `modifiesGrant`, no marker registry entry (grep of src/ finds `sacred-ki` in zero registries). sheetDiff is empty and this is NOT a pick-a-feat harness limit: there is no `featPickGrants` entry, so nothing is waiting on a player pick. Three requirements are undelivered: (1) the build-time choice of chaos/evil/good/law is never offered or recorded, so "your chosen alignment" has no value the later clauses can name; (2) no marker on the Ki Strike focus spell (remaster record `inner-upheaval`) saying its damage may be dealt as the chosen type against an opposite-alignment target; (3) no marker on Ki Blast (`qi-blast`, force damage, present in the data) or the other force-damage ki spells. Both lanes exist and are unused here: `SPELL_MARKERS` in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371 is keyed by spell id with a `source` gate and is exactly Ruling D's shape for a spell surface (currently only 2 entries: harm/sap-life and dancing-blade/the-distant-grasp). One data blocker worth flagging alongside the fix: Q9 wants the picker filtered to the deity's alignment components, and no deity record in core.json carries an `alignment` field (0 of 485), so the filter cannot be built from current data even though the four-option choice itself can.

defects.name: Instrument of Slaughter
defects.detail: The modifiesGrant requirement is not delivered. storedFields carry only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `modifiesGrant`, no `note`, and grep of src/ finds `instrument-of-slaughter` in no registry. sheetDiff is empty and correctly so for the bleed itself (enemy-side; DECIDED SCOPE + Ruling E + Q15 all agree it needs no implementation), but Q8 explicitly settles that Ruling D's shape applies here: the champion's-reaction entry must be marked. Nothing marks it, so a champion reading Retributive Strike / Destructive Vengeance / Liberating Step at the moment it matters sees no sign the feat exists. The lane is built and reachable: `RECORD_MARKERS` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3221) takes `{ on: 'action', id, value?, note }`, and the target action records exist in core.json (`retributive-strike`, `destructive-vengeance`, `glimpse-of-redemption`, `liberating-step`). `GrantModification.actionRider` (types.ts:785) is the equivalent field-side route and renders through the same RecordMarker path. The value must read as a formula ("two of the weapon's damage dice"), not a fixed die count, since the weapon varies.

defects.name: Basic Skysage Divination
defects.detail: Only the first of three picks is built. `FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS['basic-skysage-divination']` (src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:23) is a single spec — `{ prompt: "Choose a 1st-rank spell", options: ['object-reading','sure-strike'] }` — with no level gating and no second or third list. The 6th-level pick (Augury or See the Unseen) and the 8th-level 3rd-rank pick are absent entirely: `CantripPickSpec` has only `prompt` and `options`, so the record cannot hold several picks unlocking at different levels, and a level-20 host is owed all three yet is offered one. The empty sheetDiff is the unmade-pick artefact and is not itself the defect. Two secondary points for the fix: (a) the pick is injected as an INNATE spell at base rank, 1/day (build.ts:4208-4215), not as a repertoire addition — the printed text says "to your spell repertoire" and the Oatia Skysage Dedication is modelled with a `spellcastingGrant` (occult/int/trained), so a repertoire route exists; the 1/day cap is a restriction the text does not print. (b) The stored text's 3rd-rank list is truncated — the app has "…3rd-rank spells to add to your spell repertoire: or Locate". AoN feat-8113 reads "clairaudience or locate", so the correct option set is Clairaudience or Locate; the missing option is an import defect in this record's text, not a design question.

defects.name: Eternal Boost
defects.detail: Two of the three requirements are undelivered. (1) "you are permanently quickened" — situationalBonuses.ts:3266 authors [{on:'condition', id:'quickened', value:'always on', note:'...the extra action can only be used to cast Boost Eidolon or Reinforce Eidolon'}], which correctly carries the restriction, but the only reader for condition marks is VitalsRail.tsx:1034, inside character.conditions.map(...). Nothing ever adds quickened to character.conditions — `grep -rn quickened src/` returns exactly one unrelated hit (featFeatGrants.ts:149, 'quickened-casting') — and the sheetDiff is empty, confirming the stored conditions did not change. So the marker is authored but unreachable: a permanently-quickened character shows no quickened pill, and the note only appears if the player types the condition in by hand. This is the 'write-only-with-a-reader' shape. It also has no home like extraReaction does (build.ts:4542 / VitalsRail.tsx:714 render "N reactions per round" with the usable-for text); there is no extraAction equivalent. Same pattern affects eternal-composition, panache-paragon and full-automation. (2) The exploration-mode clause — continuous casting during exploration, and the cantrip already active before your first turn — modifies how Boost Eidolon and Reinforce Eidolon are cast, so principle C and the Lay on Hands answer (#1/#2) require an indication ON those records. The app has that route — SPELL_MARKERS at situationalBonuses.ts:3371 — but it holds only 'harm' and 'dancing-blade'; boost-eidolon and reinforce-eidolon carry nothing. The feat's descRefs link feat->spell, which is the opposite direction from what the owner asked for. Nothing spurious: the eidolon-facing benefits correctly contribute no numbers (DECIDED SCOPE, Companions).

defects.name: Knowledge is Power
defects.detail: The bonuses themselves are right — situationalBonuses.ts:2221 carries all four targets at the correct type: {kind:'strikeAttack'} and {kind:'spell', detail:'attack'} +1 circumstance on your next attack roll, {kind:'ac'} +1 circumstance, and {kind:'save', detail:'all'} +1 circumstance, which is Q2's "star all three saves". The restrictions sit in each `when` rather than in a flat total, which is Ruling B. (Only ac/fortitude/reflex/will show in sheetDiff because feat-evidence.mjs:142-148 queries only ac/perception/save/skill refs; the two attack targets are real but invisible to the harness — not a defect.) What is missing is the trigger surface: no `kind:'skill'` target at all, so no Recall Knowledge skill carries a `*`, and there is no {on:'action', id:'recall-knowledge'} RecordMarker either (only streetwise and student-of-the-canon have one). The owner's answer on exemplar #6 Mastermind's Eye is directly on point and is the same shape — an effect keyed to a Recall Knowledge check whose payoff lands elsewhere: "i want the feat to have a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the use can see what happens when he cheks his recall knolladge number", plus principle D and Ruling C. The route exists (detail:'all', or the four Recall Knowledge skills plus lore:* — 60 skill-detail entries already use it), so this is missing rather than no_lane. Q15 does not excuse it: the app has already implemented the effect as complicated, so only the trigger's star is absent. Note Mastermind's Eye itself is likewise unimplemented (its core.json record carries no situational entry), so this looks like one unbuilt application rather than a one-off.

defects.name: Shadow Illusion
defects.detail: Clause "You become an expert in occult spell attack rolls and DCs" is not delivered. The record does carry spellcastingGrant {tradition: occult, keyAbility: cha, proficiency: expert}, but that field is only ever consumed by the INNATE entry (build.ts:4266-4274, `profile` is applied when pushing `innate-casting`). This feat grants no innate spell, so no innate entry exists; the Shadow Illusion focus spell lands in the `fighter-focus` entry, which is pushed with a hardcoded `proficiency: 'trained'` (build.ts:2635) and never upgraded by anything except class advancement (applyAdvancement, build.ts:976, matches only `${ownerClassId}-` tracks). Observed sheet value in the diff: stored.spellcasting[fighter-focus].proficiency = "trained" (and keyAbility = "dex", not the Cha the shadowdancer line grants). So the spell attack roll and Focus DC are 2 lower than the text says at level 12+. The other two clauses ARE delivered: the focus spell reaches the Spells page with spellSources "Shadow Illusion", and focus.max goes 0 -> 1. Suggested fix: let a spellcastingGrant also raise the matching-tradition focus/archetype entry, not just `innate-casting`, using maxRank so Q10 is preserved.

defects.name: Journey Of the Sky Chariot
defects.detail: The transcendence half is fully built: grantsClassFeatures ['race-the-skies'] surfaces "Race the Skies" in the actions list at 1 action with (concentrate, transcendence), the effect body the supplied text omitted is present on the action record ("For 1 minute, you gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed or 20 feet, whichever is greater") and reachable via the description's ref link, and there is a well-built `race-the-skies` mode with speeds.fly = max(@actor.speed.land,20), duration 1 minute. What is missing is the ikon binding. The Ikon trait's own rule (AoN trait text): "A feat with the ikon trait imbues one of your ikons with further capabilities. Whenever you gain a feat with the ikon trait, choose which of your ikons gains that ability" - and this feat's Usage narrows that to "a body ikon or worn ikon". The record has no `choice` and no `modifiesGrant`; grep over src/ shows the only ikon plumbing is the exemplar's 21-option `ikon` extraChoices group, an inventory 'Ikon' item designation, and `when:` prose in situationalBonuses.ts. So no ikon is ever chosen, the picker that would have to filter to body/worn ikons does not exist, and Principle C is unmet: the immanence ("you can remain in the air at the end of this turn") and the Race the Skies transcendence are not reflected on the ikon they belong to - a player reading their chosen ikon sees nothing. Both lanes exist in the app (`choice`, `modifiesGrant`), and there is precedent for choosing among your own picks (thaumaturge implementAdept, build.ts:4368). Systemic: all 27 ikon-trait feats are stored this way (only mated-birds-in-paired-flight has a `choice`, and it is an unrelated single/pair prompt with placeholder prompt text "Prompt").

defects.name: Consult the Stars
defects.detail: The clause "gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice" moves nothing. The record has the right shape everywhere except the payload: limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} is present and shows on the sheet, and choice {flag:'consultTheStarsSkill', daily:true} correctly re-asks every daily preparation with exactly the 12 Cha/Int/Wis-keyed skills. But every option is a bare {value, label} with no `grant`, and dailyChoiceGrants (derive.ts:1065-1088) only emits an EffectGrant when `opt.grant` exists - so the answer is recorded and no proficiency, and no skill total, changes. Of the 61 daily choices in core.json, only haunting-memories carries skill grants, and it is the exact fix shape: `grant: { skills: { arcana: 'trained' } }` per option. dailySkillRank (derive.ts:1073) already refuses to lower an existing rank, so Q10 is satisfied once the grants are added, and the grant is already dated-and-cleared by rest because it lives in PlayState.dailyChoices. Two smaller points on the same record: Lore skills are absent from the option list although Lore keys off Intelligence (the text's filter admits them), and the "can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option" restriction has no `note` - moot today only because the rank never appears at all.

defects.name: Twirling Throw
defects.detail: The range-penalty clause has no surface. Text: "Make a thrown weapon strike, ignoring the penalty for making ranged attacks within the second and third range increment." The record carries nothing for it — storedFields is bare (level/category/actionCost/prereq only), `registries` is empty, and grep confirms no entry keyed 'twirling-throw' in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts. This is not an out-of-scope internal step by the app's own convention: (a) the exact same clause is modelled as a situational elsewhere — shootists-edge and masterful-hunter both carry targets:[{kind:'strikeAttack'}] with bonus "ignore the range increment penalty", and far-throw / distant-archer / triangulate model the range penalty likewise; (b) modifiers that live INSIDE an activity are routinely starred with the activity named in the `when` — 219 feats with an `actions` cost carry situational entries, e.g. cover-fire ("on the Cover Fire Strike…"), pivot-strike ("on the Strike made as part of Pivot Strike…"), spell-swipe ("on both Strikes of a Spell Swipe…"). So the missing piece is a strikeAttack situational whose `when` restricts it to Twirling Throw (Ruling B: restricted, so outside the flat total). Without it the player hand-adjusts a −2/−4 on the thrown attack roll. CORRECT parts: the activity itself exists — sheetDiff adds actions[2]="Twirling Throw" and its popup carries the printed text, which is the whole requirement for the return-to-hand clause (Q15).

defects.name: Hidden Magic
defects.detail: "During your daily preparations, you carefully tweak any or all of your magic items to appear non-magical… Objects adjusted in this way remain so until your next preparations" produces nothing at all: sheetDiff is empty, and storedFields hold only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/archetype — no `choice.daily`, so `dailyChoicesFor` offers no row on the Rest sheet, and no inventory item carries any marker or state. Both halves have working precedent in the app, so this is an unused route rather than an absent one: `openChoiceOptions` already has an `own-item` source that builds options from the character's own inventory (openChoice.ts:162), and `InventoryItem.battleforged` is exactly the required shape — a per-instance flag set from the item editor, badged on the inventory row ("Battleforged", InventoryTab.tsx:274), and cleared by rest() at daily preparations (play.ts:1846). One real constraint: `PlayState.dailyChoices` stores a single string per key, so the "any or all" multi-select cannot be expressed as an ordinary daily choice — it needs the per-item flag shape. The absent Deception DC is correctly absent (Ruling D, skill DC gets no surface), as is the caster's Perception check (Ruling F).

defects.name: Roadkill
defects.detail: "When you use Run Over, you can use your class DC in place of the vehicle's collision DC" and the widened targeting sentence both produce nothing: sheetDiff empty, no `note`, no `modifiesGrant.actionRider`, no `grantsActions`. `content.actions['run-over']` exists, but NOTHING in core.json references it, so Run Over never appears in the encounter action list, and the vehicle stat block prints only its Collision line ("Collision 1d4 bludgeoning (DC 14)", CompanionsTab.tsx:1009) with no action rows — the vehicle's collision DC is still the only DC the player can read, and Run Over's printed narrower targeting ("two sizes smaller… ram one target one size smaller or larger") is what its description still says. The routes exist and are simply unused: `grantsActions:['run-over']` puts the action in MainTab's list (MainTab.tsx:230-266), where `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', 'run-over')` already renders an inline value plus a `*` back to the source — the Magic Hands / Black Powder Boost shape. Partial limit worth flagging: `RecordMarker.value` is a static string, so "your class DC" can be worded on the marker but the computed class-DC number cannot be interpolated into it. The "You are piloting a vehicle" requirement is at least present, at the head of the feat's own description.

defects.name: Swaggering Initiative
defects.detail: Two of three requirements are delivered; the third is lost to the same text-hole defect. DELIVERED — grantsAction: action row present (sheetDiff actions[2]) with actionCost {type:'free'} and the Trigger line in the popup. DELIVERED — situational: situationalBonuses.ts:383 carries targets [{kind:'initiative'}], when 'rolling initiative', bonus '+2 circumstance'. Correct type and value, and it DOES surface: VitalsRail.tsx:641-648 stars the Initiative row and explain.ts:701-716 merges the feat's own initiative lines with the underlying statistic's, so the star appears on whatever stat the character rolls initiative with. ⚠ The empty situational section of the sheetDiff is a harness blind spot, not a defect — feat-evidence.mjs:142-147 samples only ac/perception/save/skill refs and never {kind:'initiative'}, and targetMatches() deliberately matches an initiative target ONLY against an initiative ref. MISSING — the final clause. public/core-descriptions.json feats['swaggering-initiative'].d ends 'If you are the first to act in combat, you gain .' AoN feat-6150 (Player Core 2 p.166) ends 'you gain PANACHE.' The word 'panache' is plain text in the printed feat, so this is the same dropped-payload defect as essence-overflow. It matters mechanically: panache is a modelled resource in this app (classResources.ts:83 'panache' toggle, modes.ts:248 cat-panache), so a swashbuckler reading this feat is never told it opens combat with panache and never gets prompted to switch that mode on.

defects.name: Always Ready
defects.detail: The initiative half is right and the off-guard half has no surface at all. DELIVERED: situationalBonuses.ts:109 carries targets [{kind:'initiative'}], when 'on initiative when all your opponents are undead', bonus '+1 circumstance' — correct type, correct value, the all-undead restriction inside the when per Ruling B, and it renders on the Initiative row (VitalsRail.tsx:641). Again the empty sheetDiff is the harness's initiative blind spot, not evidence of absence. MISSING: 'You aren't off-guard to hidden, undetected, or flanking undead of your level or lower. However, the undead can still help their allies flank.' This is the feat's only defensive clause and it reaches nothing — always-ready has no {kind:'ac'} situational and no RecordMarker on the off-guard condition; grepping src/ and scripts/ returns exactly one hit for this id, the initiative line. This is an omission rather than a policy call, because the app already implements this exact clause shape three times over: situationalBonuses.ts:2771 'vanara-battle-clarity' files the identical wording as an AC star ('vs hidden, undetected, flanking or surprise-attacking foes of your level or lower' / 'you aren't off-guard to them'), and :3311 'deny-advantage', :3229 'uncanny-dodge' and :3264 'eagle-eyes' all file it as a marker on the off-guard condition — which is Ruling D's Survivor-marks-Dying shape the reader asked for. Off-guard is self-facing (it moves YOUR AC), so Ruling F does not exempt it. The fix is one registry line each for AC and the off-guard condition, keeping both qualifiers verbatim: 'undead of your level or lower' and 'the undead can still help their allies flank'.

defects.name: Ultimate Mercy
defects.detail: All three clauses are delivered nowhere. (1) "Add ultimate mercy to the types of mercy you can provide" — the `mercy` feat's `choice.options` in public/core.json are exactly [body, grace, mind] with and without this feat; the app HAS the widening lane (`choiceOptionAdditions`, read by `effectiveChoiceOptions` at derive.ts:1001) but only 2 records in the whole database use it (radiant-armament, greater-armament) and Ultimate Mercy is not one, so Principle C is unfulfilled. (2) "returns it to life with 1 Hit Point and becomes Wounded 1… can't if it died from a death effect" — no marker anywhere; the `modifiesGrant` lane with `actionRider` (types.ts:785, the shape draconic-paragon uses on kobold-breath) is the natural host for a rider on Mercy and is unused here (only 2 records carry modifiesGrant at all). (3) "gains the other benefits of Lay on Hands" — SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3371) is the lane for the owner's Resilient-Touch ruling and holds only 2 entries; `lay-on-hands` has none, so the spell shows no indication this feat extends it. storedFields/registries/sheetDiff are all empty. Note on shape: writing 'ultimate' into Mercy's `choice.options` array may be the wrong fix, because that array is a build-time pick of WHICH condition your mercy treats, whereas ultimate mercy is chosen at the moment of use — a rider on the Mercy entry is likelier correct than a fourth option that would consume the pick. Either way nothing is delivered today.

defects.name: Courtly Graces
defects.detail: The +1 circumstance half is delivered correctly and completely: situationalBonuses.ts:520 stars Diplomacy ("to Make an Impression on a noble, if you use Diplomacy rather than Society") and Deception ("to Impersonate a type of noble or a specific noble, if you use Deception rather than Society"), right bonus type, right restriction, and the "if you use X rather than Society" wording makes the load-bearing "instead" legible on both stars. What is missing is the OTHER half — "You can use Society to Make an Impression on a noble, as well as with Impersonate to pretend to be a type of noble or a specific individual noble." The record in public/core.json carries no `skillSubstitutions` field, so the substitution never reaches the app's dedicated substitution surface (derive.ts:366, rendered beside the skill for conditional subs). 26 feats do carry it, including the near-identical Versatile Performance ([{use:performance, forSkill:diplomacy, when:'to make-an-impression…'},{use:performance, forSkill:deception, when:'to impersonate'}]) and its own sibling Streetwise ([{use:society, forSkill:diplomacy, when:'to Gather Information'}]) — Courtly Graces should read [{use:society,forSkill:diplomacy,when:'to Make an Impression on a noble'},{use:society,forSkill:deception,when:'to Impersonate a type of noble or a specific noble'}] and carries neither. Separately, Q2's action half is unmet: there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry keyed 'courtly-graces', so the Make an Impression row (under Diplomacy) and the Impersonate row (under Deception) show no star — Streetwise, by contrast, marks both gather-information and recall-knowledge. The only trace on Society is a prose entry in skillActions.ts:828, which describes the substitution but is not the substitution lane and appears on Society only.

defects.name: Steed Form
defects.detail: Nothing at all is delivered: the core.json record has no fields beyond level/category/traits/prereqs/edition/aonId, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and a grep of src/ and scripts/data/ finds no reference to 'steed-form' anywhere. Owed and absent: (1) "While you ride it, you get your full number of actions each round instead of reducing them to 2" — Q11 makes this a mode, because it can be shut down (you dismount), and Q3 requires the sheet to make plain the mode is active and what changed. The modes lane exists and is feat-gated (`modes` records carry a `feats: [...]` array; 429 modes ship, 97 non-item), and display-only modes that carry an uncomputable clause as text are already the established pattern — item-egg-cream-fizz's note literally says "Speed is not a mode-modifier target in this app, so track it from this note". So the floor the requirement names is reachable and no mode exists. (2) "This applies only when you ride your eidolon, not when anyone else does" — the exclusivity rider has no mode text to live inside. (3) "your eidolon's move actions while you're mounted gain the tandem trait" — under the companion ruling this marks the eidolon, so its absence from YOUR sheet is correct, but nothing conditionally adds a trait to the eidolon's move actions either ('tandem' appears in src/ only as an excludeTraits filter in featPickGrants.ts). Honest scope note: the changed quantity in clause (1) — how many actions you get per round — is not a numeric surface anywhere in this app, so the mode would carry the clause as text and move no number; that part alone is a genuine no-lane. But the mode itself, which the owner's Q11/Q3 require, is simply absent, so the feat is invisible outside its own printed text.

defects.name: Formation Master
defects.detail: The self-facing half is right: situationalBonuses.ts:2627 gives formation-master +1 circumstance AC, +1 circumstance to all saves, +2 circumstance Reflex vs area, each gated by `when: 'adjacent to at least two humanoid allies'` — correct bonus TYPE (circumstance, matching Formation Training's printed text), correct values, and correctly left as a situational star rather than a stat total because adjacency is positional (Ruling M's reasoning). What is missing is the ally-facing clause: 'Hobgoblin allies adjacent to you and at least one other hobgoblin ally also gain the bonuses from your Formation Training feat' has no surface anywhere. RECORD_MARKERS['formation-master'] is null, RECORD_MARKERS['formation-training'] is null, no record in core.json carries a `modifiesGrant` naming formation-training, and formation-master has no `note`. Principle A (from the owner's answers #1/#2) is explicit that Ruling F removes the number but not the indication: the record it modifies — Formation Training — needs a marker saying this feat extends its bonus to hobgoblin allies. Secondary, and worth an owner ruling: with both feats taken the star list shows BOTH conditions side by side ('while adjacent to at least two hobgoblin allies' AND 'while adjacent to at least two humanoid allies'), because the stacking-display rule keeps entries whose `when` differs, while Ruling G says a widening should REPLACE the entry it widens. The hobgoblin line is now a strict subset and is pure noise.

defects.name: Fortified Elixirs
defects.detail: Clause: "A creature that is under the effect of an infused Antidote or Antiplague that you created can choose to reroll a failed Fortitude saving throw…" Sheet: the feat delivers literally nothing — sheetDiff is empty and storedFields contain only metadata (level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId). No `note`, no `situational`, no `modifiesGrant`; grepping 'fortified-elixirs' across src/ and scripts/data/ returns zero hits. (1) Principle A / Ruling C is unmet: the Antidote and Antiplague items and their eight modes (item-antidote-lesser…major, item-antiplague-lesser…major in core.json `modes`) carry only the +N item bonus to Fortitude with appliesWhen 'against poisons'/'against diseases'; nothing on them names this feat, so a player reading Antidote never learns it was modified. The only link is the feat description's own `r` reference to those items, which runs the wrong way. (2) No `*` on Fortitude for the case where you are the drinker. This is buildable, not a missing lane: SituationalBonus supports `saves` + a `when` string, and the shipped entry 'powerful-alchemy' already proves a `when` can say "an infused alchemical item you create", which is exactly the infused-vs-purchased distinction this clause needs. (3) The elixir modes are toggleable, so dismissing early works structurally, but neither mode's text says a used reroll ends the duration (Principle B). No spurious surface — nothing to be spurious with.

defects.name: Blazing Spirit
defects.detail: DELIVERED: the reaction reaches the actions list (sheetDiff: actions[0] before 'Circle of Spirits' / after 'Blazing Spirit') with Frequency, Trigger and Requirements carried in its text, satisfying Principle E; and it correctly creates NO standing resistance row, so "resistance equal to your level against the triggering damage" states nothing false. DEFECT: the popup — which Principle E makes the whole surface — is missing the feat's base damage. AoN feat-7131 prints "the triggering creature takes 1d6 fire damage and 1 persistent fire damage. This damage increases to 2d6…"; public/core-descriptions.json stores "the triggering creature takes damage. This damage increases to 2d6 fire damage and 2 persistent fire damage at 12th level…". The 1d6 / 1 persistent tier was dropped, so the player reads a scaling clause whose base was never printed, and the feat's whole output is unusable below 12th level. This is not systemic: 1 of ~6,200 feat descriptions matches both "takes damage" and "This damage increases to" (only blazing-spirit); textNumbers in the evidence pack likewise show only 2d6 and 3d6. SECONDARY: no `limitedUses` for "once per 10 minutes", so the reaction draws no use pips. The lane exists and names this exact cadence — types.ts:1202 LimitedUses.every, doc comment: "'once per 10 minutes' is { max: 1, per: 'minute', every: 10 }" — and three sibling feats (reminder-of-the-greater-fear, restoring-blood, reflective-defense) carry it. Systemic though: 75 of the 78 feats whose text says "once per 10 minutes" have no limitedUses.

defects.name: Talent Envy
defects.detail: The feat's entire sheet surface is one use pip: sheetDiff shows only limitedUses[0] = "Talent Envy: {max:1, per:minute}" (which is right — featUses.ts renders it "1/minute" and refills it on the encounter reset, not per day). Three requirements are absent. (1) The `*` on Performance is not built: `registries` is empty and situationalBonuses.ts carries virtuosic-performer (line 410) and virtuosic-dancer (409) but no talent-envy entry, so a player looking up their Performance number never learns that a success there enables a free-action Demoralize — this is the Mastermind's Eye shape from gold #6, and it also has to name back the performance type stored by the earlier Virtuosic Performer pick. (2) The free-action Demoralize listing (Principle H / gold #13's Quick Recognition shape) is nowhere; note that no route exists for it today either — MainTab.tsx dedupes the action list by NAME (`!seenActionNames.has(f.name)`), so a second Demoralize at free cost cannot currently be listed even if the data asked for it, and content.actions.demoralize carries only its native 1-action cost. (3) The crit-success one-step degree bump has no entry to be printed on, since the free-action entry does not exist; Q15 owes only that it be readable where the player reads the action.

defects.name: Numb to Death
defects.detail: The Wounded half of the clause has no surface anywhere. Delivered: the once-per-day resource (storedFields.limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'}, visible in sheetDiff) and the HP-regain bonus as a star on the HP row — src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:731 `"numb-to-death": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'hp' }], when: "the first time each day you regain Hit Points while you are dying", bonus: "+circumstance equal to your level" }]`, rendered by VitalsRail.tsx:329. (It is invisible in sheetDiff only because scripts/feat-evidence.mjs snapshots situationals for ac/perception/saves/skills and never queries kind:'hp' — a harness blind spot, not a defect. Placing the HP half on HP rather than on Dying is defensible under Ruling D since HP regained is the thing modified.) NOT delivered: "you neither gain the wounded condition nor increase the value of this condition". The condition-marker lane exists and is live (RECORD_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, 50 condition marks — dying, frightened, doomed, fatigued, off-guard — rendered on the condition row by VitalsRail.tsx:1034), and no record in the file carries a mark on 'wounded' at all. So a player at 0 HP watching their Wounded value tick up gets no indication that this feat suppresses it once per day.

defects.name: Devout Magic
defects.detail: The pick is offered but not restricted, and the text conditions it ("following the same restrictions listed there"). Delivered: storedFields.effectChoices 'devout-magic-spell' lists exactly the three options the PC2 Devotion Spells class feature names (shields of the spirit; lay on hands if the deity allows heal; touch of the void if it allows harm), each with grant.focusSpells, and build.ts:2254-2263 pushes the chosen spell into featFocusSpells with focusSource set to the feat, so it reaches the Spells page attributed here. The empty sheetDiff is the expected unmade-choice shape. Also verified NOT spurious: the stored `focusPoolBonus: 1` is deliberately suppressed for this feat by build.ts:2136 (`!grantsFocusViaEffectChoice`), so the pool grows by the granted spell's own point and never double-counts — matching the remaster general rule (Player Core p.298: pool max = number of focus spells, capped at 3), which the printed text correctly does not restate. NOT delivered: the font filter. EffectChoicesPicker (src/builder/shared.tsx:3948-3955) renders `ch.options` verbatim into PopupSelect with no predicate, and EffectChoice.options (types.ts:1057) has no gating field — so a champion-archetype character whose deity allows only heal can silently select Touch of the Void. Q9 governs and the engine already computes the legal set: `championDevotionOptions` at build.ts:1205 gates on `content.deities[build.deityId].divineFont`. Champion Dedication requires choosing a deity, so the input is always available. The restriction is currently only hinted in the option labels.

defects.name: Ironblood Surge
defects.detail: Principle C is not satisfied: nothing on Ironblood Stance shows that this feat can raise its resistance. `stances['ironblood-stance']` in public/core.json carries only its own note ("resistance 2 to all damage, increasing to 3 at 12th, 4 at 16th, and 5 at 20th") and its scaling `resistances` formula; ironblood-surge has no `modifiesGrant`, and nothing in core.json references 'ironblood-stance' from any other feat. So a player reading the stance sees a resistance that can never become their Strength modifier. The lane fits exactly and is live: GrantModification.actionRider (types.ts:782-785) is documented as "a rider on the action `from` grants — or IS, when `from` is itself an action record" and renders as a RecordMarker on that row by the same route as the shipped ones; Ironblood Stance is a 1-action stance and so has a row to mark. (Only 2 feats in core.json use modifiesGrant today.) Delivered and correct: the activity reaches the actions list (sheetDiff actions[2]) with "Requirements You are in Ironblood Stance" in its popup and the stance also listed as a prerequisite; and the parry benefit is a situational AC star with the correct bonus TYPE and a `when` that names the stance (situationalBonuses.ts, when "until your next turn while in Ironblood Stance", bonus "+1 circumstance") — display-only, so no AC number moves, which is what Q1 wants for a one-round effect.

defects.name: Monster Crafting
defects.detail: The record is bare and the sheetDiff is empty. Two requirements go undelivered, and the first has a well-populated lane the record simply does not use. (1) skillSubstitution — core.json's feat record for `monster-crafting` has no `skillSubstitutions` field (only level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId). The lane is live and consumed at src/rules/derive.ts:366-381, and 26 other feats carry it in exactly the shape this one needs, conditional `when` included — e.g. wilderness-spotter {use:'survival', forSkill:'thievery', when:'to Disable the Device'} and natural-medicine {use:'nature', forSkill:'medicine', when:'to Treat Wounds…'}. Monster Crafting owes {use:'survival', forSkill:'crafting', when:'to Craft an item using a monster's body'}; today Survival carries no mark and the substitution reaches nothing. (2) note on the Craft action — the price-reduction clause ("reduce the Price using the monster's level instead of your own") is a real rules change to a named action, so Ruling D applies and the route exists: RECORD_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3221 attaches {on:'action', id:'craft', note:…} and `craft` is a real action record in core.json. grep finds no `monster-crafting` key anywhere in src/, so the Craft action shows nothing. The two 'nothing owed' clauses (GM-adjudicated valuable materials, Craft requirements) are correctly absent — no defect there.

defects.name: Uncanny Suction
defects.detail: The climb Speed is right: `speeds.climb = "max(5,floor(@actor.speed.land/2))"` resolves through resolveFormula against the finished land Speed (derive.ts:3334), giving 12 for a 25-ft walker and re-deriving whenever land Speed changes — not the hardcoded number Q16 flagged. No `*` is owed on it: Q7 says most granted speeds are permanent and need no star, and this one is unconditional. NOT DELIVERED: 'If you have the Quick Climb feat, your climb Speed is equal to your land Speed.' Nothing anywhere expresses it — the feat has no modifiesGrant, and the only conditional-speed shape, `speedsIf`, gates on a SKILL RANK or a HERITAGE and has no feat-ownership option (types.ts:459); GrantModification (types.ts:775) can only touch innate spell uses, action riders and deity domains, never a speed. The gap is live rather than academic: quick-climb's own record is `speedsIf: [{skill:'athletics', rank:'legendary', speeds:{climb:'@actor.speed.land'}}]`, but Quick Climb's prerequisite is only MASTER Athletics — so a character with both feats and master-but-not-legendary Athletics climbs at half Speed where the text says full. It reads correctly only by coincidence, once Athletics hits legendary and quick-climb's own grant wins the max(). SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT: the Reflex-DC entry (situationalBonuses.ts:648) omits `dcOnly: true`. Its `when` is worded correctly ('to your Reflex DC when someone attempts to Disarm you'), but without the flag explain.ts:346 puts the `*` beside the Reflex SAVE you roll instead of beside the DC, and the automatic '(raises the DC others roll against, not your own save)' clarifier at explain.ts:490 is suppressed — Ruling D's DC clause. Every sibling record with this exact Disarm-DC shape does carry it (sixfingers-elixir-lesser/moderate/greater, acrobats-staff, duchy-defender, steadfast-grip).

defects.name: Leap the Falls
defects.detail: Clause: "You gain the Powerful Leap and Quick Jump skill feats… even if you do not meet the prerequisites." The sheet grants NEITHER feat. The only thing the feat does is write a situational star on Athletics (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2746) whose `bonus` is prose paraphrasing the two feats. `powerful-leap` and `quick-jump` both exist as records in public/core.json, and the exact route is already built and used for the identical pair: src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:142 has `'slip-with-the-breeze': ['quick-jump', 'powerful-leap']` — that grant adds each as a bonus feat with its own entry, text and source. `leap-the-falls` is absent from FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS and from every other grant table (public/core.json carries no grantsFeats on it). Consequences: neither feat appears in Feats & Features, neither names this feat as its source, and nothing dedupes them, so a player can spend a skill-feat slot re-buying Quick Jump. SECOND, unreported lane: the Usage line "imbued into a body ikon" means the ability attaches to one of the character's existing body ikons — AoN's usage field confirms the family pattern ("imbued into a melee weapon ikon", "imbued into the mirrored aegis"), and the text itself says "The imbued ikon gains the following ability." The record has no `choice`, so no ikon is picked, the ability appears on no ikon's entry, and the Athletics star shows even for a character with no body ikon. That gap is family-wide (26+ exemplar ikon feats carry a Usage line and none of them records which ikon was imbued); core.json's `ikon` collection is id+name only, with no kind/usage field to filter a pick against. I am NOT flagging the Immanence-as-mode point: the app's settled convention for immanence is a star whose `when` reads "while your divine spark is in this ikon (immanence active)" (8+ ikons follow it; only warped-by-rage is a mode), so that is a project convention, not a per-feat defect.

defects.name: Invincible Army
defects.detail: The grantsAction lane is delivered — the diff adds "Invincible Army" to the actions list with its full text. The defect is the text itself. Clause as the app stores and displays it (public/core-descriptions.json, feats/invincible-army): "Choose an ally you can see and attempt a or check against the hard DC for the target's level." AoN's own record (feat-7926) reads "attempt a **Deception or Diplomacy** check" — the importer dropped both skill names where they were links, leaving an ungrammatical sentence that tells the player nothing about what to roll. This is a known bug class the project has already ruled on once: work/rulings/DECISIONS.md:115 closes explosive-death-drop as "the importer stripped the skill name out of 'Roll an ___ check'. A data bug, fixed on its own." This record was never fixed, and a scan of core-descriptions.json finds 14 more with the same 'a or check' shape (spells/oceans-roar, spells/wild-feast, spells/forest-of-gates, items/sphere-of-annihilation, items/dullahan-codex, items/heckling-tools, classFeatures/grim-swagger, feats/pistoleros-challenge, …), so a re-import pass is warranted rather than a one-record patch. The ally-side resistance correctly produces nothing on the sheet (Ruling F+N) and the very-hard-DC alternative is present and untruncated. Separate observation, NOT counted as the defect: the "Frequency once per round" is stored as a spendable resource (limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}) and the diff adds a pip. src/rules/featUses.ts:110 deliberately treats sub-daily frequencies as pips refilled by a manual 'new encounter' reset, with a written rationale, so I read it as a standing design decision rather than a violation of answer 3 ('we dont truck rounds'), which was about per-round NUMBERS inside a mode. Worth knowing that in practice the pip reads 0/1 for the rest of an encounter even though the use returns every round.

defects.name: Ultimate Polymath
defects.detail: The main promise is delivered and I verified it in code, not just from the diff: src/rules/build.ts:2331-2335 sets `entry.signature = [...new Set(Object.values(entry.repertoire).flat())]` when the feat is picked, routed through the same path as the summoner's Unlimited Signature Spells, with a comment naming this feat. The evidence's single `signature[0] = sure-strike` is just the harness bard's one-spell repertoire, not a cap. SpellsTab surfaces it correctly (signatureEchoIds + the cast-at picker in SpellDetail). Two parts are not delivered. (1) modifiesGrant / Principle C + Ruling G: the signature-spell picker never reflects the upgrade. src/builder/Builder.tsx:818 gates the per-spell ★ chips only on `sigAvailable` (class has the signature-spells feature) and lights a chip only if it is in `build.signatures` — so a 20th-level polymath bard whose entire repertoire is signature sees mostly UNLIT stars and a picker still inviting per-rank picks that the build then ignores. (2) The rule is not live in play. src/rules/play.ts:351 resolves `signature: play.signatureSpells?.[e.id] ?? e.signature`, and the sheet's manage-spells toggle (src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:606-613 `toggleSig`) still enforces one signature per rank — "toggling a new one drops any existing same-rank signature." One tap on any star in play therefore writes a play override that collapses the feat's whole-repertoire signature list, and the feat cannot restore it. Likewise a spell swapped into the repertoire in play (play.repertoireSpells) is not added to `signature`, so it is not signature until the character is rebuilt — the text's "All of the spells in your repertoire" fails for it.

defects.name: Gigaton Strike
defects.detail: The record carries no `note`, no `modifiesGrant`, and no RECORD_MARKERS entry — grep for 'gigaton'/'megaton' across src returns nothing. The one thing owed is a mark on the action this feat modifies: Megaton Strike is a real record on the sheet (a 2-action inventor feat, public/core.json feats['megaton-strike']), action rows carry marks via recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionId(a.name)) at MainTab.tsx:525, and RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) is exactly this lane — Black Powder Boost marks Leap, Magic Hands marks Treat Wounds. Nothing marks Megaton Strike, so a player looking at the action they perform never sees that a successful unstable Strike forces a save against their class DC. The degrees of success are correctly owed nothing beyond being readable in that popup (all four outcomes are forced movement on the enemy). The **Special** minion half is also unbuilt: the inventor's construct innovation IS a companion in this app (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['construct-innovation'], companionGrants.ts:58; build.ts:1297), so a companion-side note is expressible, and there is none.

defects.name: Explosion
defects.detail: The grant is correct: storedFields.grantsActions ['explode'] and the sheetDiff shows Explode entering the action list, resolving to the real action record (2 actions; fire/inventor/manipulate/unstable). What the entry reaches is gutted. core-descriptions.json actions.explode stores 'The explosion deals damage with a to all creatures in a around you' and 'you can choose either a 5-foot or for the area when you use Explode; ... you can choose a 5-foot, 10-foot, or .' The AoN source (aon-2e-archive action-3656) reads '2d6 fire damage with a basic Reflex save to all creatures in a 5-foot emanation', then '10-foot emanation' and '15-foot emanation'. Damage, save and area were all deleted at import — the signature of stripped Foundry @Damage/@Check/@Template tokens — so the requirement that the granted action's own full text (cost, damage, area, save) be reachable from the entry is not met, and a player who takes this feat cannot learn from the app what Explode does. Not a one-off: 480 records across core-descriptions.json carry the same stripped phrasing, so this is a pipeline fix rather than a per-record one.

defects.name: Shadow Power
defects.detail: Three of four requirements are delivered; the proficiency clause reaches only half the occult casting it should. DELIVERED: (1) Shadow Blast is an innate OCCULT spell — sheetDiff shows spellcasting[innate-casting] tradition=occult, repertoire[9]=shadow-blast, spellSources.shadow-blast="Shadow Power", and SpellsTab.tsx:1766-1786 renders the card as "rank N · 1/day · from Shadow Power". (2) Once per day is real: build.ts:4254 omits innateUses when the count is 1 and the renderer defaults to `1/day` with a spendable pip (`pip`/`onPip`, toggleInnateCast). (3) The rank formula IS correctly re-derived, contrary to the requirement's worry about a hardcoded constant — the stored `rank:6` + `heightenAt [15→7, 17→8, 19→9]` reproduces ceil(level/2)−1 (the automatic focus-spell rank, minus 1) exactly at every level the feat can be held. I built the real chain (fighter + shadowdancer-dedication + shadow-magic + shadow-power) at levels 14-20 and got 14→6, 15/16→7, 17/18→8, 19/20→9. NOT DELIVERED: "You become an expert in occult spell attack rolls and DCs." The feat stores `spellcastingGrant {tradition:occult, proficiency:expert}`, and build.ts applies spellcastingGrants at exactly ONE place — line 4266, the pooled `innate-casting` entry. Focus entries are pushed with a hardcoded `proficiency:'trained'` (build.ts:2631-2645) and only the class advancement track can raise them (applyAdvancement, line 974). Same build, level 20, observed: [{id:'fighter-focus', trad:'occult', prof:'trained'}, {id:'innate-casting', trad:'occult', prof:'expert'}] — the shadowdancer's own occult focus spells, which the same archetype granted, still roll and set DCs at trained after the feat says the character is expert in occult. (Aside, not this feat's defect: that focus entry also comes out keyAbility 'dex' rather than the Charisma Shadow Magic prints.)

defects.name: Infinite Blades Celestial Arrow
defects.detail: The immanence half has no surface anywhere. Clause: "**Immanence** Whenever you successfully Strike an enemy with your weapon ikon, up to two enemies adjacent to the target take spirit damage equal to your weapon ikon's damage dice." storedFields hold only grantsClassFeatures:['heaven-rains-an-ending'] — no `situational`, no `note`, no `weaponTraits`. This is NOT decided scope: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts carries 18 ikon-immanence entries, and two are this exact splash shape — `starshot`: strikeDamage, when "with the starshot, while its immanence is active", "+1 spirit splash damage per weapon damage die"; `hands-of-the-wildling`: "+1 spirit splash damage per weapon damage die". So the owner's chosen treatment for enemy-splash immanence is a star on strikeDamage carrying the text, and this record simply lacks it — a player reading their ranged Strike sees no indication the ikon does anything (Principle C / Ruling D). DELIVERED, and better than the reader could tell from the text: the reader flagged "Heaven Rains an Ending" as having no effect body, but core-descriptions.json has the full text ("You shoot an arrow that multiplies into a dense cloud of weapons. Make one ranged Strike with a –2 penalty against each enemy…all the Strike's damage is spirit damage…"), the classFeature carries traits:['transcendence'] and actionCost 3 actions, and sheetDiff shows it entering both ownedFeatures and the actions list. The weapon designation is only partly routed: an exemplar gets a single exclusive 'ikon' mark in the inventory (InventoryTab.tsx:672, setItemDesignation in play.ts) and riders can gate on it (derive.ts:2484, 2645), but one exclusive designation cannot say WHICH of an exemplar's 3-4 ikons a given weapon carries. Also worth a look, engine-wide rather than specific to this record: the feat itself is listed as a second 3-action entry ("Infinite Blades Celestial Arrow") beside the activity it grants, because AoN put the transcendence cost on the feat record — one activity shown twice, and every ikon feat shares the shape.

defects.name: Kholo Lore
defects.detail: Two of the five requirements are undelivered. (1) The redundancy fallback never fires. src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:187 reads `'kholo-lore': { skills: { stealth: 'trained', survival: 'trained' } }` with NO `redundantFallback: true`, and build.ts:3097 gates the whole fallback path on `g.redundantFallback` — so a character whose class or background already auto-trains Stealth or Survival silently loses that half of the grant instead of converting it into a free skill choice. The clause is verbatim in the printed text, and the directly analogous ancestry-lore feats DO carry the flag (goloma-lore:154, automaton-lore:61, azarketi-lore:65, nagaji-lore:223), so this is a per-record omission rather than an unbuilt lane. Q18 confirms the lane itself is built. With no fallback flag there is also no free skill choice offered in the builder, so the skillChoice requirement fails with it. (2) Kholo Lore never reaches the skill list. src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:90 grants `additional-lore` (the diff confirms stored.feats['additional-lore'] with grantedBy:'kholo-lore'), but additional-lore is `{ loreChoices: 1 }` — an EMPTY free-text lore slot the player must fill (build.ts:3146 reads build.featLoreChoices['additional-lore:0'] and skips when blank). Nothing prefills "Kholo", and there is no `lore:kholo` anywhere in src/ or scripts/data/. The text fixes the subject ("the Additional Lore general feat FOR Kholo Lore"), so the player must not be asked — and today they are asked, and if they leave it blank the Lore is simply absent. Every sibling feat with the same printed shape solves this by carrying the lore in its own skills map: goloma-lore has 'lore:goloma', centaur-lore 'lore:centaur', merfolk-lore 'lore:merfolk', anadi-lore 'lore:anadi'. Delivered correctly: Stealth and Survival both go untrained→trained (both halves of the two-skill clause, the usual failure avoided), and the Additional Lore feat itself is granted transitively with its details surfaced.

defects.name: Insect Shape
defects.detail: The record carries nothing but metadata (level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId) — no `modifiesGrant`, no `note`, no `choice`, no mode — and the sheetDiff is empty. Both mechanical clauses are undelivered. (1) "Add the shapes in Insect Form to your Untamed Form list": there is no Untamed Form shape list to widen. `untamed-form` is stored as a bare focus spell (public/core.json spells['untamed-form'] has only id/name/rank/traditions/traits/cast/duration) and — the systemic finding — `battleForm` appears ZERO times in public/core.json even though src/rules/types.ts:2525 declares ModeDef.battleForm and derive.ts:1183 `activeBattleForm` reads it for AC, senses, strikes and speeds. So Q3's ruling ("a battle form gets a mode that really overrides the stats it names") has an engine but no data anywhere; every one of the 13 ' Shape' feats in core.json is likewise field-empty (ferocious-shape, soaring-shape, elemental-shape, dragon-shape, monstrosity-shape…). This is unbuilt data, not an absent capability, so it is `missing` rather than `no_lane` — a mode per shape gated `feats:['insect-shape']` is exactly the shape the existing machinery takes. (2) The 24-hour duration override for the non-flying pest form shapes is not printed anywhere either; the plain `note` lane is available and unused. Note the harness limits do not apply: `registries` is empty (no featPickGrants) and nothing here lands on another creature.

defects.name: Tongue Tether
defects.detail: The record carries only metadata; `registries` is empty and the sheetDiff is empty. Neither clause reaches the sheet. The free-hand waiver on Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition and Trip is exactly the Ruling D / Ruling J / Q8 shape the app already implements as RECORD_MARKERS with `on: 'action'` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3207-3221; compare "the-harder-they-fall-ranger" which already marks `trip`, and "black-powder-boost" which marks `leap` with an inline value). All four action ids exist in core.json — disarm, trip, reposition, grab-an-edge — and Athletics is a live `situational` target, so the Ruling C companion star on Athletics is equally authorable. Nothing is authored: `grep tongue-tether src/ scripts/data/` returns no hits. The second clause (+5 feet of reach for those four actions, gated on holding Long Tongue) is likewise absent; `long-tongue` is also a bare metadata-only record. That clause is expressible as a RecordMarker `value: "+5 ft reach (with Long Tongue)"` with the condition inline per Ruling H, so it is missing rather than no_lane — but the app has no way to make a marker appear only when another feat is held, so the Long Tongue gate would have to be prose inside the note.

defects.name: Specialized Companion (Ranger)
defects.detail: The first instance is delivered: `maxTakable: 3` is stored, and companionGrants.ts:287 sets `maturityFloor: 'specialized'` with a note pointing the player at Edit; the Companions tab offers a specialization picker (CompanionsTab.tsx:1204-1214) over the 11 companionSpecializations, and companions.ts:376 applies the pick to the companion's own block. The empty sheetDiff is correct per the DECIDED SCOPE companion ruling. What is not delivered is the **Special** clause. CompanionConfig holds a single `specialization?: string` (types.ts:2710), so taking the feat twice or three times records nothing extra — there is one slot, one pick, and no cross-instance uniqueness filter feeding the picker. Instances 2 and 3 are silently inert. Two related defects found while verifying: (a) companions.ts:376 gates the specialization on `maturity === 'specialized'` exactly, so a companion on the savage / indomitable / genie-touched / unseen path ('specialized-savage' etc., all rank 3 in MATURITY_RANK) shows the picker (CompanionsTab.tsx:1134 tests `startsWith('specialized')`) but the chosen specialization contributes no ability boosts, no acRank, no skill ranks and no Racer speed bonus; (b) the maturityFloor loop at companions.ts:359 promotes a 'savage' companion to plain 'specialized', silently moving it onto the nimble path.

defects.name: Hungry Blade
defects.detail: Two of the five requirements are delivered. The activity reaches the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0] = Hungry Blade), and because the record's `text` carries the Frequency and Requirements lines they show in its popup — principle E satisfied. `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` is stored and appears (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]), so the once-per-day pip is real. What is missing is the entire benefit. There is no mode for the Keen effect: no entry in core.json `modes` references hungry-blade, so nothing expresses the 10-minute window that Q1 and Q11 both say earns a mode, and nothing carries the restriction ("only Strikes against the target of the required Strike") or the expiry ("until that target dies") as the `when` text Ruling B/H call for. There is no `situational` entry either, though that is the app's established route for an expanded crit range in prose — see "savage-critical" (situationalBonuses.ts:2755) and "keen-flair" (:2853), both `kind: 'strikeAttack'` with the natural-19 wording in `bonus`. So the crit-range change is missing, not no_lane. The `modifiesGrant` half cannot land at all in its current form: the prerequisite feat `spectral-dagger` carries no `grantedStrikes`, so there is no dagger attack line on the sheet to reflect the change onto, and `GrantModification` (types.ts:775-791) offers only innateUsesPerDay / actionRider / deityDomainsFromChoice — an actionRider on the spectral-dagger action is the nearest available surface.

defects.name: Handy with Your Paws
defects.detail: First half is delivered correctly: situational.crafting[handy-with-your-paws] = "+1 circumstance" when "to Repair non-magical items" (right lane per Ruling B, right bonus type, restriction fully carried in the `when`). Two things are missing. (1) Clause "you don't need a Repair Kit for such repairs as long as you have any amount of junk, spare parts, or debris at your disposal" has NO surface anywhere — the core.json record carries no `note`, and situationalBonuses.ts:233 holds only the one Crafting entry, with no RECORD_MARKERS entry for this feat. Half the feat's printed text is invisible on the sheet. (2) Q2 requires BOTH the skill star and a mark on the named action; the Repair action row is bare. Both are in lane and both are precedented: RECORD_MARKERS already marks id 'repair' (crafters-eyepiece / crafters-eyepiece-greater), and 'repair' is a real action id in core.json.

defects.name: Add Element
defects.detail: Clause "You gain an impulse feat for that element" is not delivered: registries is empty and FEAT_PICK_GRANTS has no 'add-element' entry, so no picker is ever offered and no outstanding choice is shown. This is not the empty-diff harness limit — that limit only applies when featPickGrants IS present, and here it is absent. The lane exists and would even cover the third clause: FeatPickSpec.maxLevel accepts 'half', documented as exactly the "your <class> level is equal to half your character level" case. Clause 1 is stored (choice flag `addedElement`, kind 'array', six gate options) but reaches nothing: 'addedElement' appears only in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json and in no file under src/, and impulse-feat gating reads build.extraChoices['element'] and only when classId === 'kineticist' (featSlots.ts:123, kineticistElements at build.ts:1285), so the archetype's second element widens no later picker — clause 4 fails invisibly. Secondary, against Q9: the option list is the static six and does not exclude the element already chosen by Kineticist Dedication (same six under flag `kineticElement`), so the player can pick the element they already have.

defects.name: Cellular Reconstruction
defects.detail: Clause "The first time you regain Hit Points at the start of your turn, you reduce your wounded condition by 1" has no surface: registries is empty, the core.json record has no `note` and no RECORD_MARKERS entry, so the Wounded condition popup says nothing about this feat. This is squarely in lane and precedented — RECORD_MARKERS takes `on: 'condition'` and already carries the-survivor → 'dying' and face-your-fears → 'frightened', and 'wounded' is a real condition id in core.json rendered by VitalsRail.tsx:1034. Also missing: the clause "For the next 2 rounds, at the start of your turn, you regain Hit Points equal to half your level" runs longer than one round, which Q1 gives a mode (display-only per Ruling E case 3, since HP moves no stat); the record carries no `modes` and the modes registry has no entry. The only surface today is the reaction row (sheetDiff: actions[0]). The two healing clauses themselves are correctly owed nothing.

defects.name: Ratspeak
defects.detail: Nothing at all is delivered: `sheetDiff` is empty, `registries` is empty, and `storedFields` carries only level/category/rarity/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `languages`, no `passiveEffects.grantsLanguages`, no `situational`. Two separate promises go unmet. (1) "You can ask questions of, receive answers from … rodents … but not with other mammals, such as dogs or bats" — a two-way communication grant that should appear where the character's languages/communication live (`language` lane, satisfied by `languages` / `passiveEffects.grantsLanguages`); the sheet shows no change to the character's languages. (2) "…and use the Diplomacy skill with rodents" — a value-less `*` on Diplomacy carrying the permission (Principle J / Ruling C: the mark goes on the specific skill, where the player reads the number); `featSituationalFor('ratspeak', {kind:'skill', detail:'diplomacy'})` returns nothing and 'ratspeak' appears zero times in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts. The third clause ("The GM determines which animals count as rodents") correctly asks nothing. ⚠ This is not a one-off: 24 feats in core.json share the exact phrase "ask questions of, receive answers from" (burrow-elocutionist, aquatic-conversationalist, speak-with-bats, skittertalk, speech-of-the-mammoth-lords, speak-with-flowers, voice-of-the-elements, treespeech, animal-elocutionist, speak-with-kindred, plant-empathy, familiars-language, natural-ambassador, wave-speaker, cattle-speech, small-speak, reptile-speaker, ratspeak, croak-talker, voice-of-the-night, koi-secrets, animal-empathy, animal-empathy-druid, nocturnal-kindred) and NONE of them carries a language or situational field either. One fix pattern closes all 24.

defects.name: Mobile Shot Stance
defects.detail: The Special is not reflected on the record it modifies, and is instead buried behind the stance gate. Clause: "Special If you have Reactive Strike, you can use it with a loaded ranged weapon you're wielding. The triggering creature must be within 5 feet of you for you to do so." The Special makes no reference to being in the stance, so it applies whenever the character has Reactive Strike. The app carries it only inside `core.json → stances['mobile-shot-stance'].note`: "…and if you have Reactive Strike you may use it with a loaded ranged weapon against a creature within 5 feet." MainTab.tsx:905 renders that note only while `character.activeStance === 'mobile-shot-stance'` (otherwise it is reachable only as the chip's hover `title` at MainTab.tsx:883), so the permission is invisible on the Reactive Strike reaction — which is where the player is looking when it matters — and invisible entirely whenever the stance is off. The feat carries no `modifiesGrant` (only 2 records in all of core.json do: splinter-faith and draconic-paragon), and none of the three `reactive-strike` records (actions / classFeatures / feats) carries any marker from this feat. That is Principle C and Q8 ("Yes — Ruling D's shape applies: mark the action the feat modifies") unmet. The two other requirements ARE delivered: the stance exists as a real toggleable, mutually exclusive state in the `stances` bucket (129 entries, `c.activeStance`, with an unmet-requirement warning), the 1-action stance activity reaches the actions list (sheetDiff shows `actions[0]` gaining "Mobile Shot Stance"), and the stance note carries the ranged-Strike immunity in the book's own open wording ("or other reactions triggered by ranged attacks"), per Ruling H.

defects.name: Emberkin
defects.detail: The save half is exactly right: situationalBonuses.ts:192 stars all three saves (`kind:'save', detail:'all'`) with `when: 'against fire effects'` and `bonus: '+1 circumstance'` — correct type, correct restriction, and correctly kept out of the flat totals per Ruling B, with Q2's all-three-saves shape. Missing: the second clause, 'your perception is unaffected by non-magical flames, fog and smoke'. There is no Perception star and no note anywhere on the record (storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/actionCost/aonId; the only registry hit is the save entry). The route plainly exists — `kind: 'perception'` is used by 167 situational entries, and non-numeric `bonus` strings are an established shape in that file (e.g. terrain-scout's 'ally benefit (no roll bonus)'), so a Perception star carrying the clause with the load-bearing 'non-magical' qualifier is in-lane and simply absent. Ruling D/J puts that mark on Perception, the stat the player is reading when it matters.

defects.name: Perfect Debilitation
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert: `sheetDiff` is empty, `registries` is empty, and storedFields carries nothing but level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId. The single surface the text owes — a marker on Debilitating Bomb saying its degree-of-success threshold has changed (only a critical success now avoids the condition), per Principle C and Q8's application of Ruling D — does not exist. There is no `modifiesGrant` and no `note` on perfect-debilitation, and nothing anywhere references `debilitating-bomb`; the whole codebase has only 2 records using `modifiesGrant` (splinter-faith, draconic-paragon). Its siblings greater-debilitating-bomb and true-debilitating-bomb are equally bare, so a player who has all four sees Debilitating Bomb's unmodified wording when they throw one. The condition itself lands on the enemy, so correctly no number moves on this sheet — the missing marker is the entire defect.

defects.name: Focused Juggler
defects.detail: The action half is right: the free action reaches the encounter list (sheetDiff actions[0]) and its "**Trigger** Your turn begins." line is the first line of the stored description, so the popup carries it. What is missing is both modifiesGrant clauses. "Increase the maximum number of items you can juggle by one" and "You continue Juggling until the end of your next turn" never reach the Juggle entry — storedFields carries no `modifiesGrant` and `registries` is empty, so the Juggle row on the sheet still reads "a number of items equal to one more than the number of hands you are using". This is not a route gap: the lane is built and live — `modifiesGrant.actionRider` is applied at src/rules/build.ts:3421-3446 and rendered on each action row via recordMarkersFor at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:525 — and the gate is satisfied, because Juggler Dedication really does hand over the Juggle feat (src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts:89 `'juggler-dedication': ['juggle']`), so `{from:'juggle', actionRider:{...}}` would fire. Principle C plus Ruling D put the +1 on the thing the player is looking at when it matters. (Context, not my feat: quick-juggler carries the identical "Increase the maximum number of items you can Juggle by one" clause and is equally bare, so the Juggle row is short two increments for a character with both.)

defects.name: As a Thousand Soldiers
defects.detail: The lane work is right — the 2-action activity reaches the action list and `limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'}` matches the Frequency line and shows beside it (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]); no fly `speed` is granted, correctly, and no mode is declared, correctly. The defect is in the text the action popup shows. AoN feat-8012 prints "a storm of stings that deals 3d4 piercing damage and 3d4 poison damage, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC". The app's stored description (public/core.json → core-descriptions.json) reads "a storm of stings that deals damage, with a save against your class DC" — the base damage and the words "basic" and "Reflex" have been dropped. So the reader who flagged this as an incomplete printed clause was reading the app's copy, not the book: the text is not incomplete upstream, the pipeline lost it. Consequence: the "increases by 1d4 piercing and 1d4 poison" clause is unreadable, because there is no base to add to, and the save type is gone. The app's own AST has the full sentence (public/ast/feats.json carries "deals 3d4 piercing damage and 3d4 poison damage… basic Reflex"), and the Feats tab renders it (FeatDetail.tsx:93 passes astKey/astId) — but the Main tab's action popup does not (MainTab.tsx:660 renders `DescBody description={a.fullDesc ?? a.desc}` with no astKey, i.e. the lossy legacy string). So the player sees the correct text where they browse and the truncated text where they act. This is systemic, not a one-off: comparing every feat's AoN text with the app's stored description, 164 of the 548 feats whose printed text contains dice are missing at least one die (battle-prayer, megavolt, quill-spray, rain-of-bolts, fatal-bullet, blazing-aura …).

defects.name: Restore Omen
defects.detail: The feat delivers nothing at all — sheetDiff is empty and storedFields holds only metadata. Two separate gaps. (1) The activity reaches no list. It is stored `actionCost:{type:'passive'}`, which is faithful to AoN (feat-4156 has no action icon; it is a 10-minute exploration activity), but MainTab builds its encounter list only from records passing `isActionCost` (1-3 actions / reaction / free / variable), and the exploration and downtime lists come from the hardcoded ACTIVITIES table in src/rules/actions.ts, which no feat can join. So a feat that IS a timed exploration activity has no surface anywhere except the Feats tab — 53 feats are in this shape (improvised-crafting, tame-animal, emblazon-armament, sacred-ground, …). Delivering the Minor Omen shape the requirement asks for needs the exploration list to accept feat records; that wiring does not exist today. (2) The harrow omen itself is recorded nowhere. Nothing in the app models an active omen or its suit — the only trace is prose inside Harrow Casting's situational text (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2218: "+1 status (+2 if your harrow omen is Keys)", "if Books is your harrow omen", …), which asks the player to know a value the sheet never holds. Harrower Dedication draws the omen at daily preparations, which is squarely the `dailyChoices` lane, and Restore Omen re-draws it; neither feat records it. I did NOT count the "Requirements: you do not have an active harrow omen" line as owing a mode on its own — gold answer #7 (Minor Omen) settles that a printed Requirements line needs only to appear in the popup. The gap is that the omen the feat GRANTS is unrecordable, not that the requirement is unenforced.

defects.name: Define "Report"
defects.detail: No situational star on Deception, and none on Diplomacy. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts has no 'define-report' key, and grep across src/ and scripts/data/ finds the id nowhere; storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/archetype/edition/aonId, and the entire sheetDiff is the free action appearing in the actions list. The owner already settled this exact shape in gold-set answer #16 (The Truth as I See it -> "heaving a * on deception"), and the registry already holds a dozen-plus reroll-shaped entries whose `bonus` is a phrase rather than a number ('premonition-of-clarity', 'turn-back-the-clock', 'guarded-mind'), so the lane exists and is simply unused here. Owed: a Deception entry whose `when` carries the whole clause — fail a Deception check, reroll with your Diplomacy modifier; on a success the target's attitude doesn't worsen; on a critical success you may attempt the Deception again — with the Diplomacy star as the lower-confidence second half.

defects.name: Instrument of Death
defects.detail: The feat is entirely inert: empty sheetDiff, empty registries, and core.feats['instrument-of-death'] carries no modifiesGrant, note, or choice — only metadata. Its two added options exist solely as prose in its own description, so a player who opens Lethal Edge (itself a free-action feat whose two native options are also description prose) sees no sign the list was extended, which is what principle C forbids. This is an unused lane, not a missing capability: GrantModification.actionRider (src/rules/types.ts:782) is described as "a rider on the action `from` grants — or IS, when `from` is itself an action record ... rendered as a RecordMarker on that action row", which is exactly this feat's shape ({ from: 'lethal-edge', actionRider: { note: <the two options, curse-effect wording and weakness 10 to spirit included> } }). The two effects themselves land on the enemy, so no number is owed anywhere — only the marker on Lethal Edge.

defects.name: Heroic Defiance
defects.detail: No mode. core.modes has no 'heroic-defiance' key; the app instead files the whole effect as situational stars on all three saves (+1 status, when = 'for 1 minute after this reaction fires (triggered when you gain the doomed condition; once per 10 minutes)'). The entry point is fine — the reaction reaches the actions list, and the trigger and once-per-10-minutes frequency are legible without any use pip, which is right since a 10-minute clock is not a tracked resource. But Q1 rules that a duration longer than 1 round gets a mode and names this precise shape: Shield the Faithful runs 1 minute, includes you, and "its mode carries real numbers for your half". Without a mode the +1 status never enters any save total while the buff is running, and the temporary Hit Points equal to your level have no surface outside the feat's own description (Ruling E means no automatic HP change is owed, but the level-scaled value has nowhere to be carried).
