Context before fixing: this is not isolated — Shield the Faithful itself has only a situational entry ('+1 item' AC) and no mode, and 145 situational entries carry '1 minute' in their `when`, so the app's working practice across this whole class of timed self-buffs is the star, not the mode Q1 calls for.

defects.name: Prescience
defects.detail: The feat's central benefit — "roll your initiative check using mythic proficiency" — reaches nothing. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:599 gives 'prescience' two entries, {kind:'ac'} and {kind:'save', detail:'all'}, and no {kind:'initiative'} target, so the player looking up Initiative sees no mark. The lane exists and is exactly right for this: `SituationalTarget.kind` includes 'initiative' (types comment at situationalBonuses.ts:29 says it is for bonuses applying to WHATEVER statistic you roll for initiative), 32 entries already use it, and the app's own convention for proficiency substitution is a prose `bonus` string — 'become-shadow' (line 2694) says "roll at mythic proficiency" and even names rolling Stealth for initiative, 'avoid-fates-gaze' (2693) says "roll at mythic proficiency", 'acrobats-calling' (2779) says "attempt the check at mythic proficiency". One entry of that shape is all that is owed. Everything else is right: the free action is listed (sheetDiff actions[0]) with the Trigger in the description; the +1 status to AC and all three saves is carried as situational-only with a `when` that names both the Mythic Point spend and the until-end-of-first-turn duration — Q1 (indication only, no computed number) and Q2 (star all three saves) both satisfied, and no number leaks into the AC or save totals. The Mythic Point cost is prose, matching how every other mythic feat in the registry handles it against the existing PlayState.mythicPoints pool, so I did not count that as a gap.

defects.name: Jungle Runner
defects.detail: The record is bare — core.json feats['jungle-runner'] carries id/name/level/traits/source/actionCost and nothing mechanical, there is no 'jungle-runner' key anywhere in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, and the sheetDiff is completely empty. Both clauses are unbuilt and both lanes exist, with near-verbatim precedents already shipping: (1) "You ignore difficult terrain from underbrush within forests and jungles" — the app's established shape is an `{on:'action', id:'stride', note:'…'}` entry, used by 'wildwood-halfling' (situationalBonuses.ts:3335, "You ignore any difficult terrain caused by plants and fungi, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth"), 'rite-of-passage' (3325, undergrowth), and 'stonestep-shisk' (3327). (2) "You can always use the Take Cover action… even if you aren't adjacent to an obstacle" — this is Q8 exactly, and 'woodstalker-lizardfolk' (situationalBonuses.ts:3337) already carries the identical clause as {on:'action', id:'take-cover', note:'You can always Take Cover while in forest or jungle terrain, even if you are not next to an obstacle.'}, with 'woodland-elf' (3336) carrying the forest-only version. Take Cover exists as a reachable action record (src/rules/actions.ts:35) and the feat's description even links to it via descRefs, so a marker has somewhere to attach; the link alone is not the Q8 marker, because a player reading the Take Cover action sees nothing. Neither clause owes a number (the cover is positional and GM-adjudicated), so the whole defect is two missing display markers — but the player currently gets no indication of either on the sheet.

defects.name: Pushing Attack
defects.detail: The choice is recorded and then consumed by nothing — the Push action never reaches the eidolon. `choice.flag = 'pushingAttack'` is the feat's only stored field; grepping src/ for 'pushingAttack' returns zero readers, deriveEidolon (src/rules/companions.ts:745-910) handles expanded-senses / amphibious-form / dual-energy-heart / COMPANION_MODS by name and has no branch for this feat, COMPANION_MODS has no 'pushing-attack' entry, and core.actions has no 'Push' record at all. So the grantsAction / modifiesGrant requirement is delivered nowhere: not on the eidolon's stat block, not in its attack entry, not even as an evoNote. (The empty sheetDiff is expected for a companion effect; the code check is what settles it.) Second, smaller defect: the picker is not filtered to attacks with the shove trait. EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS (companions.ts:706-714) does model shove — only the 'd8-shove' primary carries it, and the secondary is hardcoded agile+finesse, so it can NEVER qualify — yet the feat offers both 'Primary unarmed attack' and 'Secondary unarmed attack' unconditionally, against Q9.

defects.name: Elemental Fist
defects.detail: Principle C / Q8 requirement not delivered: Inner Upheaval's own record shows no sign this feat widened it. The spell's description (core-descriptions.json spells.inner-upheaval) still reads only "force, spirit, vitality, or void" — a monk who takes Elemental Fist and then opens Inner Upheaval at the moment of casting sees four options, not ten. The route exists and is unused: SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3371) is Ruling G's exact shape ("Distant Grasp: on the spell, since that's what you're looking at when you cast it") and holds only two entries, neither for inner-upheaval. Confirmed absent everywhere: empty sheetDiff, empty `registries`, and core.json's elemental-fist record carries no modifiesGrant, no note, no effectChoices — it stores nothing but level/traits/prereq. The six air/earth/fire/metal/water/wood pairs, each changing BOTH the damage type and the element trait gained, live only in the feat's own text on the Feats tab. The per-cast selection itself correctly needs no stored pick.

defects.name: Voice of the Night
defects.detail: The +1 is right; the communication grant is absent. Delivered: situationalBonuses.ts:412 gives Diplomacy `when:"to Make an Impression on bats, rats, or wolves"`, bonus "+1 circumstance" — correct type, correct value, both restrictions in the `when`, restricted rather than folded into the flat total (Ruling B). Missing: "You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with bats, rats, and wolves" has NO surface at all. build.ts:4592 reads `content.feats[...].grantsLanguages`, so the language lane is wired for feats — but ZERO feats in core.json use it, and the voice-of-the-night record carries no languages, no passiveEffects, no note. Nothing on the sheet tells the player they may talk to (or legally Diplomacy) an animal; the star only says a +1 applies to one action against them, which is the narrower clause. ⚠ SYSTEMIC, not one feat: 24 feats share the identical "ask questions of, receive answers from" text (burrow-elocutionist, aquatic-conversationalist, speak-with-bats, skittertalk, treespeech, ratspeak, animal-elocutionist, plant-empathy, small-speak, reptile-speaker, croak-talker, …) and not one carries a communication grant. Worth fixing as a family. I did NOT count the absent star on the Make an Impression action row as a defect: Q2's dual skill+action fan-out is built only for degreeShifts (types.ts:672, explain.ts:301), matching Q2's own '176 by Foundry's count' degree-of-success scope.

defects.name: Sociable Vow
defects.detail: The stars are right; the Principle C reflection on Binding Vow is absent. Delivered (situationalBonuses.ts:782): Diplomacy `when:"to Diplomacy checks to Gather Information or Make an Impression made directly in service…"` and Intimidation `when:"…to Demoralize made directly in service of fulfilling your Binding…"`, both "+1 circumstance" — correct type, correct skills for all three named actions (Ruling C), and the unevaluable "in service of fulfilling the vow" left printed verbatim rather than narrowed (Ruling H). The hardcoded +1 matches Binding Vow's own printed "+1 circumstance bonus" today, so it is not currently wrong — though it is a literal where the text says 'the bonus from your Binding Vow', so it will silently drift if that ever changes. MISSING: Binding Vow's own entry shows nothing. `binding-vow` is a real action on the sheet (pactbinder-dedication.grantsActions), MainTab.tsx:525 and StatDetailModal.tsx:185 already render action marks, and RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) has no sociable-vow key — so a player opening Binding Vow to see where its bonus applies still reads only Request and Coerce. Principle C and Q8 both require the widened scope to appear there. SECONDARY (same feat, different defect): this feat's stored description renders raw Foundry junk the player will read — "attempts to gather-information options=binding-vow, make-an-impression options=binding-vow, or demoralize options=binding-vow" — lowercase slugs plus unstripped `options=` markup, on the exact clause the feat is about. Nothing in src/ strips it. Binding Vow's own description has the same defect ("when you make a request options=binding-vow or coerce options=binding-vow").

defects.name: Fey Skin
defects.detail: Two of three delivered. hpBonus OK: maxHpBonus {perLevel:1} is a level formula, maxHp 206 -> 226 at level 20. weakness OK: defenses.weaknesses[0] cold-iron 5 with defenses.sources.weakness:cold-iron[0].from = 'Fey Skin' (the top-level `weaknesses` field is read here even though the lanes doc warns it is inert on ITEMS). MISSING: the 10-minute-rest clause - 'regain a number of Hit Points equal to your level; this is cumulative with any Hit Points you regain from Treat Wounds' - has no surface anywhere. No `note` on the record, no 'fey-skin' key in RECORD_MARKERS or FEAT_SITUATIONAL, and no mark on the treat-wounds action row. Ruling D's own worked example is precisely this route and precisely this action: RECORD_MARKERS['magic-hands'] = [{on:'action', id:'treat-wounds', value:'d10', note:...}], and 'stitch-flesh' marks the same row. The feat names Treat Wounds explicitly, so the mark has a definite home; the level-scaled amount (HP equal to your level) and the explicit stacking are what the note should carry.

defects.name: Hunter's Sanctum
defects.detail: The note requirement IS satisfied: the description prints both derived values ('using your Religion modifier for the counteract DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract rank'), and its ref list carries {label:'Veil of Privacy', key:'spells'} which resolves - core.json spells['veil-of-privacy'] exists - so the borrowed spell is reachable and not opaque. The three 'none' clauses are correctly owed nothing (week-of-downtime relocation = Principle K; undead Perception vs your Religion DC = enemy-side plus Ruling D's 'a skill DC gets no surface at all'; protection of the place and people inside = Ruling F / Ruling M positional). MISSING: the free-text field where the player names their sanctum's location. core.json feats['hunters-sanctum'] has no `choice` at all (storedFields: level, category, rarity, prerequisites, actionCost, archetype, edition, aonId). This is not no_lane - ChoiceSpec kind:'text' exists and is live on 39 feats (warding-rune, secret-speech, spell-mastery, syncretism, divine-access, ...) - and Principle I plus the owner's own Guerrilla Dedication answer ('have a free text filed where the user typs') settle the shape for exactly this clause. Related: Guerrilla Dedication itself is also still missing its free-text field (featGrantsAuto.ts:160 carries only its skill choice), so this is a small class rather than a one-off.

defects.name: Regurgitate Mutagen
defects.detail: The grantsAction half is delivered — sheetDiff shows actions[2] = "Regurgitate Mutagen" (the feat's own 1-action cost puts it in the encounter list), and the mutagen-ends clause is fine: mutagen modes exist (core.json `modes` carries item-* entries for every mutagen) so the player can see the state running and switch it off, and the popup prints "The mutagen's duration immediately ends." The defect is the clause "with a save against your class DC". AoN feat-5775 reads "…1d6 acid damage for every 2 levels you have, with a **basic Reflex** save against your class DC" — no parenthesis. What the app stores and shows (public/core-descriptions.json, feats.regurgitate-mutagen.d) is "…for every 2 levels you have (), with a save against your class DC": the save type is gone and a stray empty "()" has been inserted. Root cause is scripts/import-core.mjs:281 — the label-less inline-macro stripper drops @Check/@Template whole (@Damage is recovered at line 271, @Check is not), so the Foundry-sourced "@Check[reflex|basic]" left "a save" and the level formula left "()". This popup is the feat's ONLY surface, so the player cannot learn what the target rolls. Same bug on 11 other feats whose description still contains "()": self-destruct, offensive-odor, wing-buffet, imperial-dragon-potion, beautiful-knifework, sprout-fruit, fiery-rebirth, storming-breath, sonic-dash, draining-touch, dream-guise — fiery-rebirth and storming-breath lost their save type the same way, and storming-breath/sonic-dash also lost the emanation size ("to all creatures in a ,"). scripts/fix-nomirror-check-gaps.mjs already patches the "attempt a check" family but not this "with a save" family; the clean text is in the pristine mirror at C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/.

defects.name: Repeating Hand Crossbow Training
defects.detail: The feat carries no mechanics at all. storedFields holds only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/archetype/edition/aonId; registries is empty; sheetDiff is empty. The access clause is correctly nothing (Q5). But the two real clauses are unbuilt: (1) "If you have Running Reload or a similar feat… you can use that action more efficiently with a repeating weapon" needs a marker on the action it modifies (Principle C, Q8). The lane exists and is unused — `GrantModification.actionRider` (src/rules/types.ts:782, `modifiesGrant?: GrantModification[]` at :251) renders exactly this as a RecordMarker on the modified action's row, and per Ruling H the marker should go on Running Reload plus any other reload-plus-action feat held, not only the one named. (2) "You can use the action as a 3-action activity… or as a 2-action activity if you use a magazine from a repeater bandolier" is Principle H (gold answer #13, Quick Recognition): the action must appear under each of its costs with the condition in the popup. I found no route for that in src/ — `actionCost.type: 'variable'` gives a min/max range (16 feats use it) but not named cost variants with per-variant conditions, and quick-recognition itself carries only a limitedUses backfill, so Principle H appears not to be built. The empty diff on the harness host is NOT the explanation: the fighter host holds no Running Reload, but the feat carries no field for either clause on any host, so nothing would fire for a character who does.

defects.name: Kobold Momentum
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert: storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, `registries` is empty, and sheetDiff is empty — and this is NOT the pick-a-feat harness limit (no featPickGrants). Both clauses that Principle C says must be reflected in Kobold Breath are absent. The app has the exact route and uses it on the sibling feat: core.json's draconic-paragon carries `modifiesGrant: [{from:'kobold-breath', actionRider:{value:'3d4 persistent', note:'Creatures that critically fail their save against your Kobold Breath take 3d4 persistent damage…'}}]`, which renders as a RecordMarker on the Kobold Breath row via recordMarkersFor (src/rules/explain.ts:367-387) — the code comment at explain.ts:374 literally names 'Draconic Paragon's rider on Kobold Breath' as the model. Kobold Momentum, whose entire content is a rider on that same record, carries no modifiesGrant and no `note`. So a player looking at Kobold Breath sees the recharge-on-crit condition nowhere, and the 'reroll any 1s on the damage dice, and you must use the new result' clause nowhere. Only 2 feats in the whole dataset use modifiesGrant, so this is a lane that exists and is barely wired. The limitedUses half of the requirement is NOT owed: Kobold Breath's own cooldown is '1d4 rounds', rounds are untracked per Q1, and the record carries no limitedUses/featUses to restore — so 'indication only' is the correct treatment, and even that indication is missing.

defects.name: Lingering Flames
defects.detail: Clause: 'When you cast Fireball, you can modify its effects, decreasing the base damage to 5d6 and causing it to deal 2 persistent fire damage… replace its heightened entry with the following. Heightened (+1) The damage is increased by 1d6 and the persistent fire damage is increased by 2.' The stored record (public/core.json feats['lingering-flames']) carries NO mechanical field at all — no `modifiesGrant`, no `situational`, no `note`; registries [] and sheetDiff [] confirm it. There is a live route for the primary requirement: `SPELL_MARKERS` in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3370 is keyed by spell id with a `source` record id gated on ownership, rendered on the spell row via `marksFor` → `spellSituationalFor` (SpellsTab.tsx:1080). No entry for `fireball` sourced from `lingering-flames` exists (the map holds only 'harm' and 'dancing-blade'), so a player reading Fireball sees only its printed '6d6 fire damage' and 'Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6' with no hint that this feat offers a 5d6 / +1d6 / 2 persistent alternative. NOTE for the owner: the marker route can carry the alternative profile as TEXT, but SpellMarker is only {source, when, bonus} — it cannot SUPPRESS the printed Heightened line, so the strict Ruling-G 'replaces rather than sits beside' half of this requirement has no route today.

defects.name: Iivlar's Boundary Break
defects.detail: Two of three requirements are delivered correctly: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'flicker',tradition:'occult'}]` produces the innate entry seen in sheetDiff (repertoire.4 = flicker — rank 4 comes from Flicker's own base rank via castRank in build.ts, tradition occult, spellSources.flicker = "Iivlar's Boundary Break"), and SpellsTab.tsx:1766 renders the default `1/day` with a spendable pip because `usesPerDay ?? 1`, so 'once per day' is satisfied without an explicit field. MISSING is the third clause: 'When you Sustain the spell, increase the distance you teleport to 15 feet.' Nothing on the record expresses it — no `modifiesGrant`, no SPELL_MARKERS entry for 'flicker' sourced from this feat — while Flicker's own description (core-descriptions.json) still reads 'you automatically teleport 10 feet in a random direction… You can Sustain the spell to teleport in this way.' So the player reads the wrong distance at exactly the moment it matters. The route exists (SPELL_MARKERS is ownership-gated, which also scopes it to this grant rather than every copy of Flicker).

defects.name: Beast of Burden
defects.detail: Clause 1 IS delivered: the record carries `bulkLimitBonus: 4` (public/core.json, backfilled at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:51758) and deriveBulk reads it at src/rules/derive.ts:3503 (`if (f?.bulkLimitBonus) limitBonus += f.bulkLimitBonus`), moving BOTH encumberedAt and max; test/bulk-limits.test.ts:19-24 asserts exactly that. The empty sheetDiff is a harness limit — scripts/feat-evidence.mjs snapshot() never calls deriveBulk, so Bulk limits are invisible to the diff. The requirement author's '⚠ no lane for this' is REFUTED. Clause 2 is NOT delivered: 'You can rest normally while wearing medium armor' has no surface anywhere — no `note`, no situationalBonuses entry, no condition marker; the feat's only fields are level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/bulkLimitBonus/aonId. The app HAS the exact lane: Steel Skin, the same clause from the other side, ships src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3278 `'steel-skin': [{on:'condition', id:'fatigued', note:"Steel Skin: you don't become fatigued if you sleep while wearing armor."}]`. A one-line condition marker on `fatigued` (and/or the Rest control) sourced to Beast of Burden is what is owed and what is absent.

defects.name: Greater Merciful Elixir
defects.detail: The feat's entire content is the modifiesGrant requirement, and nothing carries it. The record has no `modifiesGrant` field, no registry hit (registries: []), and empty sheetDiff. I rendered Merciful Elixir's own popup body through the real path (DescBody -> AstRenderer bodyOnly hideMeta, public/ast/feats.json) and it still reads only '...attempts to counteract one fear effect or one effect imposing the paralyzed condition...' — no blinded/deafened/sickened/slowed, and no mention of this feat. The lane exists and is built: `modifiesGrant[].actionRider` (src/rules/types.ts:775-785) is consumed at src/rules/build.ts:3413-3446, which emits a RecordMarker on the modified action's row and is gated on actually owning that record — precisely Principle C / Q8's shape. A `modifiesGrant: [{ from: 'merciful-elixir', actionRider: { note: 'Greater Merciful Elixir: the elixir can instead counteract blinded, deafened, sickened, or slowed.' } }]` is the missing entry.

defects.name: Flash Forge
defects.detail: Delivered: the impulse reaches the actions list at its printed 2-action cost (sheetDiff actions[7]), and I rendered its popup — the full prose is there, metal-only constraint, compass/poor lock/merchant's scale examples, the GM's call, the 10-minute duration, the DC 5 flat check and destruction. The requirement author's ⚠ about the stray 'Flash Forge / Source Rage of Elements pg. 30' header is REFUTED: that line exists in public/core-descriptions.json (235 feats share the artifact) but the AST renderer's hideMeta drops the level-1 title and the Source column, so it is not printed. NOT delivered: (a) no mode. The formed object lasts 10 minutes, and Q1 says a duration longer than a round earns a mode (display-only here, Ruling E case 3, carrying the object's name, the 10-minute duration, the DC 5 flat check and the destruction outcome as text per Principle B). The modes lane is live — 429 modes ship in core.json, 4 of them kineticist impulses (cyclonic-ascent, fresh-produce, hardwood-armor, metal-carapace) — and flash-forge has none. (b) the pick ('level 0, common, handheld weapon or adventuring gear of 1 Bulk or less') reaches no picker and no inventory; the nearest lane, `dailyTemporaryItems` (src/rules/types.ts:1508-1531), is keyed to daily preparations, so a USE-TIME conjured temporary item has no route at all — that half is genuinely no-lane, and I am reporting the feat as `missing` on the mode, which the app can express today.

defects.name: Stone Blood
defects.detail: One of three requirements is delivered; two are not. DELIVERED: the bleed flat-check DC. RECORD_MARKERS['stone-blood'] (situationalBonuses.ts:3280) carries {on:'condition', id:'persistent-damage', value:'bleed flat check DC 10', note:'…DC 10 instead of DC 15…'}, 'persistent-damage' is a real condition id in core.json, and VitalsRail.tsx:1034 renders the star on the condition pill — Ruling D's shape, with the note wording honouring Ruling G by saying the 10 replaces the 15. MISSING (1), the single concentrate action: the feat has no `grantsActions`, no action record exists for it (searched core.json actions and scripts/data/actions-additions.json for "early flat check" / "binding the wounds" — nothing), so the action never appears in the action list. The clause survives only as a sentence inside the persistent-damage condition note, which means the player can only find the action while already suffering persistent damage — and cannot find it by browsing their actions at all. This is not no_lane: the app authored 104 feats' worth of `grantsActions` plus 100 records in actions-additions.json, so the route exists and simply was not used. MISSING (2), the drained clause: it is folded into the SAME persistent-damage note rather than living on the drained condition. No record in the file marks {on:'condition', id:'drained'} — I checked, the set is empty — even though 'drained' is a real condition id the same renderer would pick up. So a character who is drained but not bleeding sees nothing, which is the exact inverse of Ruling D / Q8 ("the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters", The Survivor marking Dying).

defects.name: Kneel for No God
defects.detail: The one thing owed is a marker on the Call on Ancient Blood reaction saying a critical failure becomes a failure against a divine spell (Principle C; exemplar #7 rules out a degree-of-success surface). Nothing is authored: storedFields has no modifiesGrant, registries is empty, and grep finds no reference to kneel-for-no-god or call-on-ancient-blood anywhere in src/rules. The action exists (core.json actions/call-on-ancient-blood, granted by heritages/ancient-blooded-dwarf via grantsActions), and the lane exists and is exactly the right shape — GrantModification.actionRider (src/rules/types.ts:775-790), whose own comment describes the Kobold Breath case where `from` IS the action record; build.ts:3435-3445 turns it into a RecordMarker rendered on that action row and gated on the character actually owning the modified record, which is precisely the "inert without Call on Ancient Blood" behaviour the text needs. So this is an unauthored record, not an engine gap. Correctly nothing: the three saves (the trigger is one named reaction against one spell trait, not saves generally), the Access line, the flavour.

defects.name: Distracting Performance
defects.detail: The only thing the app does is list the feat as a 1-action row (sheetDiff: actions[0] = "Distracting Performance"). (1) "you roll a Performance check instead of Deception" — the record has no `skillSubstitutions`, and the lane is built and live (types.ts:483, derive.ts:366-410, explain.ts:322). Create a Diversion's own record (core.json actions['create-a-diversion']) and the app's skill-action table (actions.ts:78) both still read `skill: 'Deception'` with no marker, so the player who looks the action up gets the wrong statistic. The correct shape is a conditional sub — `{ use: 'performance', forSkill: 'deception', when: 'to Create a Diversion' }` — which derive.ts deliberately shows beside the skill rather than replacing its number. (2) "the benefits of successful checks apply to an ally of your choice instead of you" — no note or marker anywhere on Create a Diversion, so Principle A (an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies) and Ruling D (the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters) are both unmet; the sheet silently implies you become hidden yourself. Also, the feat's own popup renders the unsubstituted template literally: "You create-a-diversion statistic=performance, except..." (core-descriptions.json). The archive (feat-6474) reads "You Create a Diversion, except...".

defects.name: Iridian Choirmaster Dedication
defects.detail: Fully inert: registries empty, sheetDiff empty, storedFields is metadata only. Three of the six clauses are real requirements and none is built. (1) No free-text student field — the `choice` lane supports kind:'text' (used for Quick Study's Lore subject and Call Gun's bonded weapon per dailyChoices.ts), so Principle I's shape is available and unused; the player has nowhere to record who their student is, which every other clause refers back to. (2) No `grantsActions` entry for the 1-action nonverbal-message activity (concentrate/mental/linguistic, requirement 'you can see each other', effects of Message but explicitly non-magical) — core.json contains no action record for it and the feat carries no grant, so it never appears in the actions list. (3) No `note` carrying 'you gain the benefits of your Iridian Choirmaster archetype feats only if both you and your student are alive and conscious' — Ruling M's permanent-marker shape, which per Ruling D belongs on each Iridian Choirmaster feat the character holds. Worth flagging beyond this record: all 15 feats with archetype 'iridian-choirmaster' carry nothing but id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, so the whole archetype is unbuilt.

defects.name: Jester's Gambol
defects.detail: Three of the four requirements are delivered: the stance-entering action appears (sheetDiff actions[1]); core.json stances['jesters-gambol'] exists so the stance is offered in MainTab's stance list (MainTab.tsx:292) and is exclusive by construction (setActiveStance stores a single slug); its `requires.text` prints 'You are attuned to an apparition that grants Circus Lore or Fey Lore…' as a read-only reminder rather than a computed gate (stanceRequirementIssue only fails on the structured unarmored/armored flags), which is the right shape for a condition that changes day to day; and the difficult-terrain clause lives in the stance note, which MainTab renders while the stance is active. What is missing is the resistance: the stance record has no `resistances` array, so half-your-level resistance against animals/beasts/fey/fungi/plants exists only as prose and never reaches the IWR breakdown. The lane fully supports it — 8 stances carry `resistances`, half-level formulas are standard (rain-of-embers-stance: 'max(1, floor(@actor.level/2))', cobra-stance: 'floor(@actor.level/2)'), and attacker-keyed restriction strings are already live elsewhere in core.json ('all damage from fungus creatures', 'damage from air creatures', 'all damage from undead'). The fix shape is resistances: [{ type: 'damage from animals, beasts, fey, fungi, and plants', value: 'floor(@actor.level/2)' }] on the stance record.

defects.name: Oddity Identification
defects.detail: The +2 circumstance star exists on Occultism (situationalBonuses.ts:294) with the right bonus TYPE, but its `when` covers only half the printed trigger: "to Identify Magic that twists minds, fights fortune, or reveals secrets". The text is "When you Identify Magic OR RECALL KNOWLEDGE to learn more about these effects" — Recall Knowledge is dropped, so a player recalling knowledge about a mental/fortune/scrying effect reads no bonus. Two further gaps: (a) Q2 says star the skill AND the action, and the app has the exact channel for it — RECORD_MARKERS `on:'action'` renders on the skill panel's action rows (StatDetailModal.tsx:185), and Occultism's list already contains both "Recall Knowledge" and "Identify Magic" (slugs identify-magic / recall-knowledge) — yet this feat registers no action marker; (b) "you can always use Occultism without penalty" is a restricted skillSubstitution (use: occultism, forSkill: arcana/nature/religion, `when`: those traits), and the `skillSubstitutions` lane supports exactly that shape with a `when` (types.ts:483, 26 feats use it) but this record carries none. Minor, non-blocking: the fallback description string in core-descriptions.json is mangled — "When you identify-magic skill=occultism or recall-knowledge skill=occultism" — though the shipped AST (public/ast/feats.json) renders the sentence correctly, so the player normally sees the good text.

defects.name: Share Weakness
defects.detail: The grantsAction half is delivered — the 1-action feat appears in the action list with its "**Requirements** You are Exploiting a creature's Vulnerability using mortal weakness" line in the popup — and correctly nothing lands on your own numbers (Ruling F/N). Two requirements are not delivered. (1) Ruling F is explicit that an ally-facing effect running for a limited time gives the activating character a DISPLAY-ONLY mode so they can see it running; this benefit persists until your Exploit Vulnerability ends or you Share Weakness again, so it is not the 1-round case Q1 excludes. The lane exists and is exercised — core.json `modes` holds 97 feat-attached entries, 178 of them with zero modifiers (display-only) — but there is no `share-weakness` mode. (2) Principle A (the round-1 correction: an ally-facing feat still needs a visible marker on the source ability, as Resilient Touch marks Lay on Hands) wants a marker on Exploit Vulnerability / mortal weakness saying this feat can extend the weakness to an adjacent ally. That channel is live for this exact target: situationalBonuses.ts:3333 has 'unlimited-esoterica' with `{on:'action', id:'exploit-vulnerability', …}`. Share Weakness registers no marker, so a thaumaturge reading Exploit Vulnerability sees no sign the feat touches it.

defects.name: Bear Empathy
defects.detail: Clause: "You can communicate with all bears." Sheet value that is wrong: nothing at all — `sheetDiff` is completely empty and the record (core.json feats.bear-empathy) carries no `grantsLanguages`, no `passiveEffects`, no `note`. The feat's entire printed content is invisible outside the feat's own description. The lane is real and wired: build.ts:4592 reads `content.feats[featId].grantsLanguages` into `character.languages`, and mechanic-lanes.md D lists "You can speak with Y" as the `language` lane — but ZERO feats populate it (only 2 heritages and 3 items do), and all 22 "communicate with X" feats in core.json (animal-empathy, plant-empathy, croak-talker, treespeech, wild-speech, green-empathy…) are equally silent, so this is a whole unbuilt shape, not one bad record. One display caveat worth the owner's attention: the only current route renders as a language pill (DetailsTab.tsx:419, VitalsRail.tsx:1100 → `content.languages[id]?.name ?? cap(id)`), i.e. exactly the "spoken-language slot" presentation the requirement rules out, so delivering this needs a communication entry distinct from the language pills.

defects.name: Patron’s Claim
defects.detail: Clause: "Your familiar gains the Patron's Claim activity." Sheet value that is wrong: the activity attaches to YOU, not the familiar. `sheetDiff` adds `actions[0] = "Patron’s Claim"` to the character's own action list, and that comes solely from the FEAT record's own `actionCost {type:'actions',value:2}` — the feat carries no `grantsActions`, and the familiar never learns it. The familiar's stat block is built by deriveFamiliar (src/rules/companions.ts:598-625): its `abilities` list is drawn from `content.familiarAbilities` via `COMPANION_MODS[featSlug].familiarAbilities`, and there is no `patrons-claim` entry in `familiarAbilities` and no COMPANION_MODS entry for `patrons-claim` (only 3 feats use that route: lightning-rings-intervention, lightning-rings-overcharge, tempest-clouds-speed). The activity DOES exist as a standalone record — `core.actions['patrons-claim']`, 2 actions — so it is authored but unattached. Note the partial-route caveat: even wired up, FamiliarBlock abilities carry no `actionCost` field (0 of 111 familiarAbilities records have one), so the "2 actions" half of the requirement needs the familiar ability shape widened before it can display.

defects.name: Thrown Voice
defects.detail: Two of three requirements land; the heritage-derived use count does not. Delivered: `innateSpells:[{spellId:'ventriloquism', tradition:'primal'}]` puts Ventriloquism in the pooled innate entry at its own base rank (sheetDiff `repertoire.1[0] = ventriloquism`, ventriloquism is rank 1), tradition primal, with `spellSources.ventriloquism = "Thrown Voice"`, and SpellsTab.tsx:1770-1786 renders it as "rank 1 · 1/day · from Thrown Voice" with a spend pip — absent `innateUses` means the default 1/day, restored by rest (play.ts:1866 clears `innateUsed`). AoN feat-2651 confirms the lost spell name is indeed ventriloquism, primal, once per day. MISSING: "If you're a songbird strix, you can cast it twice per day instead." The count is authored as a constant (no `usesPerDay`, so 1) and nothing derives it from the heritage — `songbird-strix` in core.json is a bare record with no `modifiesGrant`, and even if it carried one it would be ignored, because `grantMods` (build.ts:3413-3426) collects modifications from FEATS and CLASS FEATURES only, never heritages. So a songbird strix sees 1/day where the printed feat gives 2/day. The adjacent mechanism already exists (`GrantModification.innateUsesPerDay` → `innateUsesBonus`, build.ts:4238-4247, used by Draconic Paragon), so this is an unwired case rather than an absent capability; the fix is either a heritage-conditional `usesPerDay` on the grant or extending `grantMods` to read heritages. Worth knowing while fixing it: use TRACKING for innate spells is a single boolean toggle regardless of the count (types.ts:3178-3180, SpellsTab.tsx:1786), so a 2/day spell would print "2/day" but still offer one pip.

defects.name: Storm Born
defects.detail: All three requirements are missing; the feat is mechanically inert. The core.json record carries no `situational`, no `note`, no marker of any kind (only level/category/prereq/actionCost/edition/aonId), it appears nowhere in FEAT_SITUATIONAL, and it is absent from scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, so nothing would survive a regen either. sheetDiff is empty and the harness's own situational snapshot (which does cover Perception) is empty, so both instruments agree. IMPORTANT — the featPickGrants entry in `registries` is a false positive and does NOT trigger harness limit 1: `registriesFor` in scripts/feat-evidence.mjs:189 is a plain substring test, and 'storm-born' appears in featPickGrants.ts only as an OPTION inside Order Explorer's pick list (line 89) and in Natural Ambition's exclusion list (line 189). Storm Born grants no pick, so its empty diff is a real absence. Every clause is expressible with shapes already in production use: `{kind:'spell', detail:'attack'}` exists (23 spell-targeted entries in the registry) for the weather penalty on ranged spell attacks; `{kind:'perception'}` for the Perception half of the same sentence (Q2/Principle J want the second star on Perception specifically); and the no-flat-check clause has direct precedent in `{kind:'spell', detail:'all'}` phrasing plus the concealment entries on fire-lung ("you ignore the concealed condition (no flat check)"), firesight and superior-sight. fire-lung is the sharpest comparison: it is the sibling of storm-born in the very same Order Explorer list, it is the same shape of clause, and it is authored while storm-born is not.

defects.name: Chemical Trail
defects.detail: Clause: "You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all checks AND SAVES to Sense Direction or reorient yourself." The app delivers only the checks half — situationalBonuses.ts:143 stars Survival with when "to Sense Direction or reorient yourself", bonus "+1 circumstance", and the sheetDiff shows exactly that one entry (situational.survival[chemical-trail]). Two surfaces the owner's own decisions call for are absent: (1) the SAVES half has no surface at all — Q2 says a bonus applying to saves generally stars all three, and Ruling H says the printed trigger goes in the note rather than narrowing it, so Fortitude/Reflex/Will should each carry a "+1 circumstance, to Sense Direction or reorient yourself" star; the diff has no situational.saves.* path. (2) Q2 also says star the skill AND the action; core.json ships an `sense-direction` action record and RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) supports on:'action', but chemical-trail has no entry there. Both are one-line registry additions — the lanes exist and are populated for other records. The Survival star itself is correct (Ruling B: restricted bonus lives in `situational`, not in the Survival total), and the first sentence (leaving/reading trails) correctly produces nothing.

defects.name: Lesser Enhance Venom
defects.detail: Neither modification reaches Envenom. No `modifiesGrant` on the feat; registries []. The Envenom record (core.actions.envenom) is untouched — its description still reads "**Frequency** once per day" and still prints "**Minor Vishkanyan Venom** … Stage 1 1d4 … Stage 2 1d4 … Stage 3 1d4", not the lesser venom's 1d6/1d6/2d6, so Principle C / Ruling G (an upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades) is unsatisfied on both the venom name/stat block and the frequency. The only thing authored is `limitedUses {max:1,per:'hour'}` on the FEAT itself (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json), which the diff confirms surfaces as a use row labelled "Lesser Enhance Venom: {max:1,per:hour}" — the right cadence on the wrong record, and the app already has the purpose-built lane for this shape: `usesUpgrade` (src/rules/featUses.ts:38-61, documented with exactly this case — "You can use Cat's Luck once per hour, rather than once per day"), which is unused here. The hour period itself is supported (featUses.ts:110 SUB_DAILY includes 'hour', cleared by the encounter reset), so requirement 2's independent-clear demand is met by the engine, just on the wrong entry. ⚠ Separate, larger data gap found while checking: nothing in the app can grant Envenom at all. There is no feat named Envenom (this feat's prerequisite string "Envenom" matches no record), the vishkanya ancestry and all six vishkanya heritages list no `grantsActions:['envenom']` (Keen-Venom Vishkanya grants 'venom-draw'), so core.actions.envenom is orphaned and the record this feat upgrades can never appear on a sheet. The same prerequisite is carried by Debilitating Venom, Restoring Blood, Swift Application and Vicious Venom.

defects.name: Hex Master
defects.detail: The feat carries nothing at all: storedFields is level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost:passive/edition/aonId only, registries [] (which covers situationalBonuses.ts, where both RECORD_MARKERS and SPELL_MARKERS live), sheetDiff [] (empty). Clause 2 — "when you cast Cackle to sustain a hex, you gain the effects of Sustain for all your active hexes that have a duration of sustained" — has a built lane it does not use: SPELL_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371) is keyed by spell id with a `source` gate on the owning record, which is exactly Principle A/C's shape (the shipped example is "harm" ← sap-life), and nothing is keyed to 'cackle'. Note `modifiesGrant.actionRider` would NOT work here — RecordMarker.on is only 'action' | 'condition', and Cackle is a focus spell. Clause 1 — "no longer limited to casting only a single hex each turn" — moves no number (turns are untracked), and I checked the removal target: core.trait.hex has no description (only 12 traits have one), so no hex spell in the app currently asserts the one-per-turn limit; nothing is being contradicted, but equally no hex entry shows that this character's limit was lifted.

defects.name: Tree Climber (Goblin)
defects.detail: Requirement 1 is delivered: storedFields.speeds {climb:10}, and the diff shows speeds.climb null → 10, unstarred, which Q7 says is right for a permanent fixed speed. Requirements 2 and 3 have no surface whatsoever. No situational entry exists (registries [] — 'tree-climber-goblin' appears nowhere in situationalBonuses.ts), so the climb Speed carries no `*` and no note about trees; and no upgraded value is expressible as authored either — `speedsIf` (src/rules/types.ts:459) gates only on {skill, rank} or {heritage}, with no "if you also have feat X" gate, so the Cave Climber condition has no engine route today. The pieces for the display half already exist: SituationalTarget supports kind:'speed' (situationalBonuses.ts:37) and deriveSpeeds resolves formula speeds against the character's own speeds (derive.ts:3335, "@actor.speed.land"), which is the Q16-compliant way to express "increases to your land Speed" without hardcoding a number. Cave Climber is real and reachable in the app (feat 'cave-climber', level 9 goblin, speeds {climb:10}), so a goblin holding both feats sees climb 10 ft and no hint that it becomes their land Speed in trees. Harness caveat, not a defect: snapshot() only builds situational refs for ac/perception/saves/skills, never {kind:'speed'}, so a speed star would be invisible to the diff — the empty registries hit is what settles this, not the diff.

defects.name: Wellspring Control
defects.detail: The feat delivers nothing at all: storedFields is bare (level/category/rarity/prereq/archetype/aonId), registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and grep finds no entry for 'wellspring-control' anywhere in src/rules/. Principle C requires the roll-twice-keep-either clause to be reflected in the record it modifies — the character already owns `wellspring-magic` (granted by Wellspring Mage Dedication's classArchetype.addFeatures), whose own description contains the Wellspring Surges table it tells you to roll on, and that record says nothing about this feat. Correct that no stat moves and no star lands on a skill or save (the surge is a table lookup). Note for whoever fixes it: the `modifiesGrant` lane exists (types.ts:775, applied at build.ts:3421, only 2 feats use it) but its display shape is `actionRider` → RecordMarker, and RecordMarker.on is `'action' | 'condition'` only, resolved against action-row name slugs (MainTab.tsx:525) and condition ids (VitalsRail.tsx:1034). wellspring-magic is a passive class feature with no action row, so marking it needs the marker surface widened to class-feature rows — the data entry alone will not display.

defects.name: Release the Light
defects.detail: Every lane the requirements name is built: the 2-action activity exists as its own entry (sheetDiff actions[1] 'Release the Light'), the once-per-day use is real (`limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'}` → limitedUses[0], reset at rest via featUses), and the popup text carries Frequency, the Requirements line ('You're below 20 Hit Points'), both DCs named in the same sentence, and the full degree-of-success prose with live ref-links to dazzled/blinded. No mode for the one-round light, which is right under Q1; no enemy conditions modelled, which is right under Ruling F/Q4; no spurious modifier anywhere. The defect is in the one surface this feat has — the printed text itself is incomplete. The book and AoN (feat-8214) read "must attempt a **Fortitude** save equal to your class DC or spell DC"; the app's stored description (core-descriptions.json → feats/release-the-light) reads "must attempt a save equal to…", so the player is told to have enemies roll a save without being told which one, and no field elsewhere on the record supplies it. This is systemic, not a one-off: of 96 feats whose stored description says 'attempt a save', 88 have a named save type in the AoN archive (gigaton-strike 'a Fortitude save', frightful-moan 'a Will save', dazzling-block, ricochet-legend, …) — the importer strips the save word, and the same pass strips area templates ('forcing each living creature in a to attempt a save', 'An aura surrounds you in a .' on the fetching-bangles ikon). Worth a targeted re-import pass rather than 88 hand edits. Separately and not a defect: nothing resolves 'whichever is higher' into a single number, but the text names both and the sheet carries Class DC (VitalsRail) and spell DC, and 216 records share that phrasing with no field for it.

defects.name: Shared Luck (Halfling)
defects.detail: Nothing is stored and nothing happens: storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/edition/aonId, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty, and no src/rules/ registry mentions 'shared-luck-halfling'. Under principle A + Ruling D the ally-facing reroll still owes a visible marker on Halfling Luck showing its trigger now also fires on an ally's failed skill check or saving throw within 30 feet — and Halfling Luck is exactly the row the player is looking at when the reaction comes up. The restriction 'if you have Guiding Luck, you can't use Guiding Luck's attack-roll/Perception effect to benefit an ally' likewise needs to appear where the player would reach for it, gated on actually owning Guiding Luck. The route is built and unused here: RECORD_MARKERS keyed by source-record id with `{on:'action', id:'halfling-luck'}` renders on any action row, since MainTab.tsx:525 looks markers up by the row's own name slug, and build.ts:3413's grantMods is the gating channel for 'only if you have the modified record'. Correctly NOT done: no extra uses were added — Halfling Luck stays at 1/day (guiding-luck's `usesUpgrade` to 2/day is the only thing that raises it), which matches 'instead of you rerolling your own'.

defects.name: Phantom Resemblance
defects.detail: Only the frequency lands. limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} is stored on the feat itself, so the sheet shows one daily use labelled 'Phantom Resemblance', spendable independently of Phantom Visage's own resource — exactly as required. Both other requirements are absent. (1) No mode for 'the effects of a 3rd-rank Illusory Disguise for 1 hour or until you shift back': the feat appears in no gate in src/rules/modes.ts (registries is empty) and carries no modes field, so nothing expresses what the disguise does, that it runs at 3rd rank rather than Illusory Disguise's base rank 1 (core.json has illusory-disguise at rank 1), or either end condition. Q1 (an hour is far past the one-round line) and Q11 (it can be shut down at will) both put this in a mode. (2) No marker on Phantom Visage. The feat grants nothing of its own — it rides on an ability the character already has — so Principle C puts the surface there, and the route is available: phantom-visage exists in core.json as a 1-action feat, therefore it renders in the action list where recordMarkersFor(...,'action',...) is consulted (MainTab.tsx:525), and modifiesGrant.actionRider (build.ts:3421-3444) is the field that feeds it. The record carries no modifiesGrant; only 2 feats in the whole app do. Net effect on the sheet: a bare 1/day counter that never says what the use buys.

defects.name: My Kingdom, My Blood
defects.detail: The activity itself lands — the feat's own actionCost is 2 actions, so it enters the encounter action list ('My Kingdom, My Blood') with its full text in the popup, which is where the Stride/Burrow/Climb/Fly/Swim substitution correctly lives. Three requirements are absent. (1) No mode for the 1-minute aura: no modes field, and the feat appears nowhere in src/rules/modes.ts (registries is empty), so nothing on the sheet shows the link is running, and the 'ends immediately if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points' end condition has no surface. Q1 puts a 1-minute effect in a mode; Ruling E keeps it display-only; Ruling M's aura caveat does not bite because the emanation is centred on you. (2) No reaction entry for 'you can use your reaction to take half the damage in their stead' — the diff adds exactly one action row and no grantsActions, so the reactions list is unchanged (before: Reactive Strike, Shield Block; after: the same two plus the 2-action activity). Principle E makes the reaction with its stated trigger a requirement in its own right. (3) Because there is neither mode nor reaction, the clause that contradicts the rest of the sheet — 'you don't apply any resistances, weaknesses, or other abilities you have to that damage' — is legible only inside the feat's own prose, not at the point of use. Two things to flag alongside: the printed text is defective ('creating a in an aura around you' — a noun is missing after 'creating a'), so whatever surface is built will display a broken sentence unless the text is repaired first; and the reader's ask that the reaction be shown only while the aura runs has no route at all — no record field gates an action row on an active mode.

defects.name: Halcyon Spellcasting Initiate
defects.detail: (The empty sheetDiff is a host artifact — the harness placed this on a fighter without the prerequisite Halcyon Speaker Dedication, so the archetype entry never existed. The feat IS wired: src/rules/casterArchetypes.ts `halcyon-speaker-dedication.customUnlocks` has `{rank:2, level:10, featId:'halcyon-spellcasting-initiate'}` and the same for rank 3.) The SLOTS are right — `archetypeSlots` yields out[2]=1, out[3]=1, inside the archetype's own spontaneous entry, so they are restricted to the halcyon repertoire and inherit the dedication's shape. What is missing is the SPELLS KNOWN. The text says 'two common 2nd-rank halcyon spells and two 3rd-rank halcyon spells', but src/rules/build.ts (spontaneous-archetype branch) sets `repertoire[rank] = srcSpells[rank].slice(0, count)` where `count` is the SLOT count, and src/builder/Builder.tsx `spellGainsAt` offers `cap = slotsAt(L)[r]` picks per rank. The app conflates spells-known with slots, so the character learns ONE 2nd-rank and ONE 3rd-rank halcyon spell instead of two each — half the printed grant. (Same shape hits the whole archetype: the dedication's 'two common 1st-rank halcyon spells' becomes one, and Adept/Sage's two-per-rank likewise.) Second, smaller miss: Q9's 'only what the player may legally pick'. The archetype spell pool is filtered by `s.traditions.includes(trad)` — the whole arcane OR the whole primal list — not by the halcyon set (spells on BOTH the arcane and primal lists), so the picker offers spells that are not halcyon spells.

defects.name: Fey Influence
defects.detail:
MISSING (primary): "You become trained in primal DCs and spell attack rolls" is not delivered. The record carries no `spellcastingGrant` (public/core.json shows only `grantsCreatureTraits:['fey']`), while the app's established route for that exact sentence is `spellcastingGrant: {tradition, keyAbility, proficiency:'trained'}` — 13 sibling feats carry it (invoke-the-crimson-oath, shadow-magic, blessing-of-the-sun-gods, suns-fury, soul-warden-dedication, divine-healing…). Fey Influence and dragon-disciple-dedication are the ones that don't.
WRONG VALUE on the tradition: the pick is wired through FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS (featCantripGrants.ts:33) with all eight correct options, but build.ts:4211 pushes `{spellId: chosen}` with no `tradition`, and build.ts:4259 then labels the innate entry from `spells[id].traditions[0]`. Only Summon Plant or Fungus is primal-first: Grim Tendrils → arcane, Pest Form → arcane, Fleet Step → arcane, Spider Sting → arcane, Ill Omen → occult, Bane → divine, Heal → divine. The text says all eight are primal innate spells. Fix is `{spellId: chosen, tradition:'primal'}` (InnateSpellGrant already has the field).
CORRECT: the fey creature trait is stored and reaches the Details tab (derive.ts:1852 → DetailsTab.tsx:404), per Q6; the 8-option choice and its 1/day innate spell are the featCantripGrants lane, so the empty sheetDiff is the expected pick-not-yet-made state, not a defect; the ancestry-trait Special line correctly needs nothing (Q9).
MINOR: Cat Sith's "(cat only)" restriction rides nowhere — the Pest Form entry offers every form the spell has.

defects.name: Construct Dynamo
defects.detail:
MISSING: "your dynamo Strikes become magical" is not delivered anywhere. The record has no `unarmedTraits`, no `weaponTraits` and no `modifiesGrant`; the four dynamo Strikes granted by Sterling Dynamo Dedication (`grantedStrikes` on sterling-dynamo-dedication) never gain the magical trait, which is load-bearing against resistance to non-magical damage. The lane exists — an UnarmedRider `{add:['magical']}` is applied by applyUnarmedRiders (derive.ts:3110) — but two upstream problems narrow how it can be written: (1) `fromRecord` matching fails closed for feat-granted strikes because collectGrantedNaturals (build.ts:1359) never records a `source` on the NaturalAttack, so only the `match` name filter works; (2) all four dynamo strikes are stored with the placeholder name "Label" and no `choiceValue`, so they all appear at once and can only be matched as "Label".
CORRECT: the +1 status bonus vs magic is starred on Fortitude, Reflex and Will with `when: "against magic"` (situationalBonuses.ts:153) and stays outside the flat save totals — Q2 and Ruling B both satisfied. The Access clause correctly produces nothing (Q5).

defects.name: Ricocheting Leap
defects.detail:
Nothing this feat promises reaches the sheet. The only stored mechanic is `limitedUses {max:1, per:'turn'}`, which draws a bare "1/turn" pip with no text saying what the use is for.
MISSING (a): the Wall Jump extension ("off creatures larger than you as if they were walls") is recorded nowhere — no `modifiesGrant`. Note the ideal shape has no route: Wall Jump is a passive FEAT (no `grantsActions`, and there is no `wall-jump` record in content.actions), while RecordMarker only supports `on: 'action' | 'condition'` (situationalBonuses.ts:3207) and GrantModification.actionRider needs an action the `from` record grants. There is no lane for putting a marker on another FEAT's entry.
MISSING (b): the free-action Shove/Trip is absent. The exact "listed under both costs" shape (Principle H) is also unbuilt as a data lane — `grantsActions` is a bare `string[]` (types.ts:245) that pulls each action with its own printed cost, and MainTab.tsx dedupes by action name, so a second Shove entry could not appear. The reachable surface today is RECORD_MARKERS entries on the `shove` and `trip` action rows carrying the once-per-turn free-action condition (Ruling D / Q8); neither exists.
MISSING (c): the once-per-turn cap is not printed with anything. The app models it as a spendable per-turn use instead; 'turn' is a supported period used by 13 feats and refills on the manual encounter reset, so I am not calling the use-pool itself a defect — but with no note anywhere, the pip is the only trace of the feat and it explains nothing.

defects.name: Aldori Parry
defects.detail: Clause: "Aldori dueling swords you're wielding gain the parry trait." Not delivered. The feat record (public/core.json) carries only a situationalBonuses entry (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:845) and no `weaponTraits`. Rebuilt a fighter with Aldori Duelist Dedication + Aldori Parry and an equipped Aldori dueling sword: the Strike's traits are ["finesse","versatile-p"] both with and without the feat — parry never arrives, and the sword item itself does not ship with it. The lane exists and fits exactly: `weaponTraits: {match:{items:['aldori-dueling-sword']}, add:['parry']}` (derive.ts applyWeaponRiders, ~line 2614; 7 feats already use it, incl. Hilt Hammer's structurally identical "melee weapons you wield gain versatile B"). Consequence today is display-only — nothing in src/ computes AC from the parry trait, so no double bonus would result; the loss is that the player wielding the sword never sees parry or its glossary text (src/rules/glossary.ts:95) on the thing they are looking at. The other two requirements ARE correct: the AC entry reads when="to AC while parrying with an Aldori dueling sword (requires wielding only an Aldori dueling sword)", bonus="+1 circumstance (+2 if your other hand is free)" — right bonus type, Ruling G's replace-not-stack shape (one entry, never +1 and +2 side by side), and Ruling B/H's restriction printed in the `when` rather than narrowed into a computed test.

defects.name: Improved Hijack Undead
defects.detail: Clause: "When you use Hijack Undead, if the undead fails its save, it becomes your minion for 10 minutes... critically fails... 24 hours." No marker reaches Hijack Undead. The record carries no `modifiesGrant`; grep for "hijack" across src/ returns nothing; and building a fighter with Clockwork Reanimator Dedication + Hijack Undead + Improved Hijack Undead yields `grantMarkers: null`. So a player reading their Hijack Undead action row still sees only the base outcomes from its own description ("Failure: minion for 1 minute / Critical Failure: 1 hour") with no sign those numbers no longer apply to them — exactly the case Principle C and Q8 settle. The route exists and fits without modification: `modifiesGrant:[{from:'hijack-undead', actionRider:{note:'...10 minutes / 24 hours...'}}]` (types.ts:775-785, applied at build.ts:3421-3443, gated on actually owning the modified record). Only one feat in the whole dataset uses actionRider today (draconic-paragon → kobold-breath), which is the same feat-with-an-action-cost shape as Hijack Undead, so the marker would render by the shipped path. The minion outcome itself correctly gets no surface (DECIDED SCOPE / Q4); the durations correctly need no timer.

defects.name: Disrupt Qi
defects.detail: The grantsAction half is delivered — sheetDiff shows the activity entering the actions list (actions[0] = "Disrupt Qi") carrying actionCost {actions: 2} and traits [monk, void], and no spurious strike or damage plumbing was invented. But the DEFECT is in the one surface this feat has. Per Q4 the entry's own text IS the whole surface, and that text is CORRUPTED: public/core-descriptions.json stores "...that creature takes damage and is Enfeebled 1 until the persistent damage ends", dropping the amount and the type. The printed line (verified against the AoN mirror, C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-6024.json, Player Core 2 pg. 124) is "that creature takes 2d6 persistent void damage and is enfeebled 1". So the player is shown a feat whose entire effect is "takes damage", and the surviving third clause — "the persistent void damage increases to 3d6" — now references a base figure that does not appear anywhere (textNumbers holds only 3d6, never 2d6). This is systemic, not a one-off transcription slip: 54 records read "takes damage" the same way — e.g. spells/caustic-blast stores "on a critical failure, the creature also takes damage" where the print reads "takes 1d6 persistent acid damage". Root cause is the @Damage recovery branch in scripts/import-core.mjs:271-280, whose formula regex `/^[\dd+\-\s()]+(?: plus …)*$/` returns '' rather than the dice when the inner token shape is not the one it anticipates. I did NOT flag the 18th-level clause as a separate defect: no sheet number moves (the damage is enemy-facing) and Q4 settles that the entry's text is the whole surface — but that only holds if the text is complete, which here it is not.

defects.name: Robust Health
defects.detail: The bonus's SUBSTANCE is right but it is on the wrong surface, and the second promise is absent entirely. What exists is one situational entry, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:732 — `targets: [{ kind: 'hp' }], when: "on HP you regain from a successful Treat your Wounds, or from Battle Medicine used on you", bonus: "+circumstance equal to your level"`. That gets requirements (a)-(c) correct: the value is prose ("equal to your level") so it can never go stale, it is display-only and correctly refuses to fold into the Medicine modifier or any total (Ruling E), the ally case is worded in, and the success gate is stated. But it stars the HIT POINTS stat — a general stat, which Ruling J rules out — instead of the two actions. The owner's own precedent is the identical shape: Magic Hands also changes the HP you regain from Treat Wounds, and the ruling was to mark the action; it sits in RECORD_MARKERS as `"magic-hands": [{ on: 'action', id: 'treat-wounds', value: "d10", … }]` (situationalBonuses.ts:3237). Robust Health has no RECORD_MARKERS entry at all, so neither the Treat Wounds row nor the Battle Medicine row carries a mark — and Ruling C / Q2 requires BOTH, since the clause names two actions. The lane would work: marks are looked up by name slug (`actionId` in src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:202, `recordMarkersFor` at MainTab.tsx:525), so `id: 'battle-medicine'` attaches to the Battle Medicine feat's action row just as `id: 'treat-wounds'` attaches to the core action. Separately, the third clause — temporary immunity to that Battle Medicine for 1 hour instead of 1 day — has NO surface anywhere: no `note`, no marker, nothing in storedFields. Hours are not tracked so it owes no number, but per Ruling C/D it owes text on the Battle Medicine entry, and that is the half a player is most likely to forget.

defects.name: Deepening Devotion
defects.detail: The save half is delivered correctly: situationalBonuses.ts:759 stars all three saves (verified statHasSituational true for fortitude/reflex/will) with when="against sleep and paralysis effects, while your spectral dragon shares your space" and bonus="+2 status", and the value stays out of every save total. Nothing double-counts either — the base +1 from Channel Draconic Essence is prose-only in that action's description and is modelled nowhere, so the player reads one line, not two (ruling G's outcome, reached by the base never being built). The SECOND clause is delivered nowhere: "you can use Draconic Salvation if you succeeded or failed on your saving throw, not only if you critically failed." core.json actions.draconic-salvation still reads "**Trigger** You critically fail a saving throw against an effect with the same tradition trait as your draconic benefactor", and there is no route to the widened trigger — RECORD_MARKERS has no 'deepening-devotion' key (recordMarkersFor returns [] for a character holding the feat) and the feat carries no modifiesGrant field. Principle C ("a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing") and Q8 ("mark the action the feat modifies") both require it, and RECORD_MARKERS with on:'action', id:'draconic-salvation' is the existing lane for it.

defects.name: Fossil Rider
defects.detail: Three of four requirements land. The innate grant is real: innateSpells:[{spellId:'mask-of-terror'}] produces repertoire rank 7 — the spell's OWN rank in core.json (Player Core, rank 7), not a drifted one — with spellSources mapping it to "Fossil Rider", and SpellsTab.tsx:1770-1790 renders the card as "rank 7 · 1/day · from Fossil Rider" with a spendable/restorable pip, so the once-per-day limit is distinguished from at-will (build.ts defaults an innate grant to 1/day and only writes innateUses when it differs). What is NOT delivered is the "on yourself" narrowing. The base spell record is Range 30 feet, Targets 1 creature; the granted entry says nothing about self-only, and the card's only click-through is Mask of Terror's own detail, which tells the player they may target any creature. SPELL_MARKERS in situationalBonuses.ts:3371 is exactly the ruling-D lane for this (a mark keyed by spell id + granting record, shown on the spell row where the player meets it) and has no mask-of-terror entry — spellMarkersFor('mask-of-terror', ownedIds) returns [] for a character with the feat. Separately observed, not claimed as a defect: the shared innate bucket asserts tradition "arcane" (the spell's first listed tradition of arcane/occult/primal) although the feat names none; arcane is a legal tradition for the spell, so under Q12 this does not mislead.

defects.name: Jotunborn Lore
defects.detail: The two named skills are delivered (featGrantsAuto.ts:185 trains occultism, survival and lore:jotunborn; the diff confirms all three). Three clauses are not. (1) The redundancy fallback: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['jotunborn-lore'] carries no `redundantFallback: true`, so a character who is already trained in Occultism or Survival from another source (a ranger/druid's Survival, a background) silently gets nothing instead of the promised free skill pick. The lane exists and already fires per redundant skill — build.ts:3097 pushes one entry onto `skillFallbacks` per redundant grant and the builder offers a replacement picker (Builder.tsx:1668-1689) — and sibling ancestry lore feats set it ('azarketi-lore', 'android-lore', 'automaton-lore'). (2) Additional Lore is granted (core.json `grantsFeats:['additional-lore']`, diff shows stored.feats[additional-lore].grantedBy = jotunborn-lore) but its own progression never runs against the fixed subject: FEAT_GRANTS['additional-lore'] is only `{loreChoices:1}` and the loreChoices path hardcodes 'trained' (build.ts:3146-3151, no `at()` upgrade applied), so Jotunborn Lore is still merely trained on a 20th-level sheet instead of legendary from Additional Lore's 3rd/7th/15th-level increases. (3) The Special second instance is unreachable: granted feats are deduped by id (build.ts:3000 `if (takenFeats.has(gid)) continue`), so Additional Lore cannot be held twice, and a slotless granted feat gets no Lore picker at all (Builder.tsx:1691 renders loreChoices only for a feat picked into a slot; grantedChoicePicker keys off `content.feats[id].choice`, which additional-lore does not have) — so a Sage Jotunborn can neither hold it twice nor name the second Lore. Positively: no spurious free-Lore picker appears for the first instance, which matches the text fixing the subject.

defects.name: Graceful Guidance
defects.detail: 'You can use the Aid reaction to grant a bonus to an ally's Reflex save.' The feat carries no field, appears in no registry, and produces an empty diff — nothing anywhere on the sheet records that Aid has been widened. Correctly there is no number on your own Reflex save (Ruling F), and correctly no star on any skill (Ruling I — the text names no check for you to roll), but Principle A and Q8 require a marker on the record the feat modifies, and that lane exists and is in use: RECORD_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3221) already carries `{on:'action', id:'aid', ...}` for 'the-publican', the Aid row exists as a rendered reaction (src/rules/actions.ts:42, core.json action id 'aid'), and MainTab.tsx:525 renders the `*` plus inline value and source note on any marked action row. With no entry the feat's entire payload is invisible to the player.

defects.name: Snare Crafting
defects.detail: One of three clauses is delivered: the four-pick picker exists and is correctly filtered — snareFormulaOptions (src/rules/snareFormulas.ts:34-45) restricts the base four slots to the snare trait, level <= 1 and common rarity, gated on the feat (Builder.tsx:1086), satisfying Q9/Q14 point 7. The other two are not. (1) 'You can use the Craft activity to create snares' has no surface at all — no situational entry on Crafting, no RECORD_MARKER on the 'craft' activity (which exists at src/rules/actions.ts:122 and renders marks by the same path as Aid/Treat Wounds), and no note on the record. This is a permission clause of the Guerrilla Dedication shape (snares are not craftable without it), so it is not a restatement of a general rule. (2) The picks never reach a formula book. formulaBook.ts:63-71 deliberately excludes snare-crafting and snarecrafter-dedication from FORMULA_GRANTS ('their formulas already have a lane of their own'), so the chosen ids sit in `build.extraChoices['snare-formulas']` and are read by nothing outside the builder card that wrote them: no '<snare name> formula' entry in the book (Q14 points 1-2), no one-time write into the book's own state and no `formulaPicks` spent-ledger entry (point 9 — losing the book would not lose these), no book ensured for a character who has none (point 6), and no craftable or prepared-snare surface anywhere on the sheet. The card's own copy ('Your formula book holds N snare formulas; you can prepare 4 of them for free each day') promises a book and a daily prep list that the picks never actually touch. Note the requirement writer's 'no lane at all' caveat is now stale — the formula book was built (src/rules/formulaBook.ts, FormulaBookPanel.tsx) and snare-crafting was left out of it on purpose, so this is a promised-but-empty case, not an unbuilt one.

defects.name: Instinctive Maneuvers
defects.detail: The situational half is right: FEAT_SITUATIONAL in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:247 gives Athletics a +2 status star with when = "to Grapple, Reposition, Shove, or Trip after Relinquishing Control" — correct type, correct restriction quoted from the text (Ruling B/H), correctly kept out of the flat Athletics total. Two things are absent. (1) The modifiesGrant requirement — "When you Relinquish Control, you add Grapple, Reposition, Shove, and Trip to the list of actions you can take" — is the feat's headline promise and reaches nothing. relinquish-control is a real record (a free action feat whose description enumerates the permitted actions: Recall Knowledge, Step, Strike, Cast an apparition Spell, Cast a vessel Spell, Sustain a vessel spell, apparition-trait actions) and that list is displayed unchanged whether or not the player owns this feat. core.json feats['instinctive-maneuvers'] has no `modifiesGrant`, and the exact route exists: GrantModification.actionRider (src/rules/types.ts:782, applied at src/rules/build.ts:3421) is documented as "a rider on the action `from` grants — or IS, when `from` is itself an action record", rendered through the shipped RecordMarker path. So this is an unauthored field, not a no_lane. (2) Per Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action") the four action rows are owed a star too; grapple, reposition, shove and trip all exist in core.actions, and RECORD_MARKERS (on:'action') is the working route, but instinctive-maneuvers has no RECORD_MARKERS entry — it appears only once in all of src/.

defects.name: Advanced Weaponry
defects.detail: One of the three requirements is delivered. The trait pick is built: storedFields.choice flag 'advancedWeaponry' offers exactly the printed list — disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, versatile bludgeoning, versatile piercing, versatile slashing — with no free choice of other weapon traits, and it is a permanent builder pick (Principle K). The other two are absent, and the record itself says so: choice.inert reads "Recorded only — the app doesn't track traits added to an eidolon's unarmed attacks. Note in your eidolon's notes WHICH attack (primary or secondary) you chose". (1) The first pick — "Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks" — is never offered; only the trait is asked for. The eidolon has exactly two named starting melee unarmed Strikes built at src/rules/companions.ts (primary from EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS, secondary fixed 1d6 agile/finesse), so the legal option set is known and Q9's "builder shows only what may legally be picked" is directly satisfiable; the app instead pushes the answer into a free-text note. (2) The weaponRider never lands. The chosen trait is not appended to either attack's `traits`, and a versatile choice therefore offers no alternate damage type on the eidolon's Strike. This is a wiring gap, not a no_lane: COMPANION_MODS already carries a `strikeRider` that pushes a trait onto companion attacks (src/rules/companions.ts:517), and the eidolon derivation reads COMPANION_MODS at line ~853 but consumes only senses, iwr, speeds and note — it never reads strikeRider — while three sibling evolution feats (expanded-senses, amphibious-form, dual-energy-heart) are hardcoded there and advanced-weaponry is not. Per the standing companion ruling the surface owed is the EIDOLON's stat block, so the empty sheetDiff on the summoner is correct and is not itself the defect; the defect is that the eidolon's attack entry is silently unmodified.

defects.name: Shattering Blows
defects.detail: The feat carries no mechanical field whatsoever — storedFields is only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty — so all three requirements are unmet, and every one of them has an existing lane the app already uses for exactly this shape. (1) No marker on Rage. There is no rage entry in core.modes (429 modes; the only rage-ish ids are 'raging-stories' and 'warped-by-rage'), but the app's real route for 'a feat changes what Rage does' is a RecordMarker on the rage ACTION — situationalBonuses.ts:3324 does precisely this for 'revitalizing-rage' ({on:'action', id:'rage', value, note}), and 3224/3225 for berserkers-cloak. Shattering Blows has no such entry, so nothing on Rage says melee Strikes ignore Hardness. (2) No `*` on melee Strikes, and the conditional lane exists: types.ts:444 defines whileState?:'rage', and classResources.ts:71 gives the character a real rage toggle. (3) Devastator is not consulted anywhere — the only reference to it in src/ is advancement.ts:273 (class-DC rank at 19). Since neither the 5 nor the 10 is written down at all, the Ruling-G 'replace, don't sit beside' upgrade cannot be judged built. The feat's own description text is reachable in the Feats tab, but principle C requires the modification to be reflected IN the thing modified.

defects.name: Night's Shine
defects.detail: Requirements 1 and 2 are delivered: effectChoices carries exactly one choice ('domain-spell') with exactly the two legal options, each with grant.focusSpells → ['asterism'] / ['touch-of-the-moon'], and both spells exist in core.json (rank 4 focus, cleric). The empty sheetDiff is the expected unmade-pick state. focusPoolBonus:1 is NOT spurious — build.ts:2133 detects grantsFocusViaEffectChoice and suppresses it so the point rides the chosen spell instead of double-counting. The **Special** clause is the failure. maxTakable:2 makes the feat offerable twice (featSlots.ts:48), but the pick has nowhere to put the second answer: build.effectChoices is keyed `<recordId>:<choiceId>` where recordId is the FEAT ID, not the slot — Builder.tsx:1752 builds ecKey as `${picked}:${ch.id}` and build.ts:3305 resolves it as resolvePick(fc.featId, …), reading `nights-shine:domain-spell` for both instances. So the two feat slots render the same picker holding the same single value; changing one changes the other, both takes resolve to the same spell (deduped downstream), and a character who takes Night's Shine twice ends up with ONE focus spell and one pool point instead of both spells and two. The second take is a wasted slot.

defects.name: Viking Weapon Specialist
defects.detail: Half delivered. Crit spec is right: `critSpec:true` with `critSpecWeapons.bases:['battle-axe','hatchet','longsword','shortsword']`, and derive.ts weaponMatches (line 2476) tests `strike.base`, which deriveStrike sets to the base weapon's item id (derive.ts:2837) — all four ids exist in core.items, so the effect reaches the strike and only those four. The empty sheetDiff is just the harness character wielding none of them, not a defect. The second sentence — "whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency rank in the above four" — is not implemented anywhere: no `weaponFamiliarity` for this id in featGrants.ts, featGrantsAuto.ts or featGrantsLane.ts, and no `proficiencies` on the record. The app has the route and uses it for the identically-worded ancestry Expertise feats (`weaponFamiliarity: { weapons: […], mirrorBestCategory: true }`, e.g. featGrantsAuto.ts:52-53), and Q10's betterRank chain already gives the "only when it makes the player better" behaviour the clause needs. Consequence is a wrong number, not just a missing display: a viking cleric/wizard whose class feature grants expert in its own weapons keeps battle axe/hatchet/longsword/shortsword at their untrained martial rank on the attack bonus. Worth fixing alongside: the prerequisite feat viking-weapon-familiarity (core.json) also carries only critSpec and no trained grant for the same weapon list.

defects.name: Open the Blazing Eye
defects.detail: Two of the four requirements are delivered and two are absent. DELIVERED: the activity reaches the action list (sheetDiff `actions[0]` = Open the Blazing Eye, own actionCost 2 actions) and `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` is stored and shows on it. MISSING 1 — the mode. "For 1 minute, you gain the benefits of a See the Unseen spell" is a duration longer than 1 round, which Q1 makes a mode, and Ruling E case 3 makes it a display-only one if it moves no number. No mode exists: public/core.json `modes` holds 429 entries, 97 of them attached to feats via `feats: [featId]`, and none names this feat. The exact shape is already built elsewhere — mode `item-clockwork-goggles-major` carries `senses: [{name:'see-invisibility'}]` plus a note reading "the effects of See the Unseen — invisible creatures are concealed to you rather than undetected", so this feat could reuse it verbatim. MISSING 2 — the Strike star.
