The clause "the attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being concealed or hidden" is two separate printed promises that belong on Strikes as a `situational` entry (kind `strikeAttack`, which src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:24 supports) live while the mode runs. The feat appears in neither FEAT_SITUATIONAL nor its own `situational` field; scripts/data/effect-backfill.json carries exactly one line for it (`limitedUses`), so nothing else survives a `npm run data`. Note the harness cannot show a Strike star in its diff (the `situational.*` diff surface covers only skills/saves/perception/AC) — this finding is from the record, not the diff.

defects.name: Natural Mutagen
defects.detail: The `choice` requirement is delivered and correctly filtered: `choice.flag = 'naturalMutagen'` offers exactly 12 options, which I verified against public/core.json are precisely the family-head mutagen items that are common AND level 1 (war-blood is uncommon, prey/applereed/ichthyosis are rare, fury-cocktail and stone-body are level 4/5 — all correctly excluded), and the values are the base family ids rather than the lesser versions, which is the right storage for a family that scales. All three `dailyChoice` requirements are absent, and the record admits it: `choice.inert` reads "The app doesn't add the daily temporary vial to your inventory — add it yourself at daily preparations (it dissipates by the next ones). It becomes the greater/major version automatically once your level matches that version's level." So the vial is never produced, never cleared at the next preparations, and never resolved to the highest family version at or below character level. This is NOT covered by a standing ruling — the owner ruled the opposite way and named this feat by name: work/choice-lane/DECISIONS.md §1 ("Daily-preparation picks → the Rest button, with a personalization setting") lists "Celestial Armaments (a weapon), **Natural Mutagen (a mutagen)**, Ancient Memories" and decides "the REST button *is* daily preparations… the pick is always made at least once, and the sheet always reflects a real choice." The lane is built and live: `dailyTemporaryItems` (src/rules/types.ts:1508) with `filter.traits` + `filter.maxLevel`, driven by src/rules/dailyItems.ts and stored in `PlayState.dailyItems`, already ships on six feats (scroll-adept, herbal-forager, basic/expert/master-scroll-cache, grand-scroll-esoterica). One shape mismatch worth flagging to whoever builds it: every existing `dailyTemporaryItems` slot presents a PICKER at rest, whereas this feat's vial is determined (the recorded family + the character's level), so it needs a fixed/derived slot rather than a filtered one.

defects.name: Deity's Protection
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert. storedFields has no note, no situational, no resistances; sheetDiff is []; registries is empty; grep finds no 'deitys-protection' in src/. The requirement is only an indication (Q1 rules a 1-round duration is indication-only, so the reader is right that a standing resistance entry or a mode would be WRONG here) — but the app delivers zero indication on the records the feat modifies, which Principle A/C and Ruling D both demand. The route exists and the app already uses it for the identical trigger shape: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:446 gives 'shield-of-faith' a situational entry whose `when` is "until the start of your next turn after you spend a Focus Point to cast a domain spell", and SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3377, spellMarkersFor) exists to hang a source-gated marker on a spell's own row. Clause left unsurfaced: "After you cast a domain spell, you gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn… equal to the rank of the domain spell you cast." One wrinkle worth flagging to the owner rather than treating as a blocker: SPELL_MARKERS is keyed by individual spell id, so reaching EVERY domain spell the character holds (and the ones a later Domain Initiate adds) needs a marker keyed by the domain-spell relationship rather than by spell id.

defects.name: Fortified Flesh
defects.detail: The VALUE lane is right — storedFields.resistances = [{type:'physical', value:'@actor.archetypeFeats.living-monolith'}], resolved live by archetypeFeatCounts (derive.ts:1662/1352), so it recounts as Living Monolith feats are added or removed; the diff shows physical 1 with defenses.sources.resistance:physical[0].from = 'Fortified Flesh'. What is missing is the EXCEPTION. Clause: "resistance to physical damage (except adamantine)". The sheet shows a bare "physical" resistance, so a player reading their defences will apply it against an adamantine weapon — the one material the text carves out. This is not a no_lane: the exception is expressed today by putting it in the type string, and two records already do it — modes:harden-flesh and modes:item-living-statue both store type "physical (except adamantine)" (also "physical (except bludgeoning)", "slashing (except silver)" elsewhere). deriveDefenses treats the type as an opaque display key, so the fix is data-side: change the stored type to "physical (except adamantine)". Note IwrEntry (types.ts:310) has only {type, value} and the feat push path passes no __cond, so the type string is the only home.

defects.name: Slayer's Presence
defects.detail: The feat produces an entirely empty sheetDiff, no registries, and storedFields holds only metadata — no modifiesGrant, no note. Clause "When you use Slayer's Identification and succeed at your check, you can Frighten Undead as a free action": the marker half is a MISSING requirement, not a no-lane. GrantModification.actionRider (types.ts:775-785) is built and live — "a rider on the action `from` grants, or IS when `from` is itself an action record… rendered as a RecordMarker on that action row" — and feats:draconic-paragon already uses it. Slayer's Presence should carry modifiesGrant with an actionRider so Frighten Undead (and Slayer's Identification) show that a successful identification buys a free-action casting; today both rows are silent (Principle C / Q8). The OTHER half — Frighten Undead appearing under BOTH costs (Principle H, the Quick Recognition shape) — has no route: ActionCost (types.ts:127) is a single value with no alternate, and MainTab.tsx:257 dedupes the action list by NAME (`!seenActionNames.has(f.name)`), so a second entry at a different cost is filtered out. The owner's own gold answer #13 is in the same state: quick-recognition stores only limitedUses and recognize-spell carries one cost. ⚠ Context for whoever fixes this: `slayers-identification` exists in content.actions but NO record's grantsActions names it (verified: two string occurrences in core.json, both its own definition), so it never reaches any sheet — that belongs to Undead Slayer Dedication, not to this feat, but it means a marker aimed at that record would land nowhere; aim the rider at frighten-undead.

defects.name: Oni Rampage
defects.detail: The reaction surface is delivered: sheetDiff shows it entering the actions list (actions[0] = 'Oni Rampage') as a reaction, and its popup carries the printed Trigger verbatim, with a working ref-link to Haste in core-descriptions ({label:'Haste', key:'spells'}), so Haste's own text is reachable. What is absent is the state the reaction produces: 'the effects of Haste for 1 minute' has no mode on the record — no feat in core.modes carries quickened, and none is keyed to this feat. Per Q1 (a duration longer than 1 round earns a mode) and Ruling E case 3 (ongoing but moves no number => display-only mode), this should be a display-only mode printing what it does: quickened, extra action usable only to Stride or Strike. That exact shape already exists for items (item-dragons-blood-pudding-*). Principle E covers the trigger/requirement surface for a reaction; it does not cover a 1-minute self-buff, which is Q1's territory.

defects.name: Protective Subroutine
defects.detail: The situational half is exactly right and nothing spurious is added: +2 STATUS (type matches the text) starred on Fortitude, Reflex and Will per Q2's all-three rule, sitting outside the flat total per Ruling B, with an accurate gate — when: 'once per hour, when you spend your Nanite Surge on a saving throw instead of a skill check' (situationalBonuses.ts:486). Missing is the other half: the modifiesGrant/Principle C + Q8 requirement that Nanite Surge's own entry show the widened trigger. The record has no modifiesGrant field and there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) keyed 'protective-subroutine' with {on:'action', id:'nanite-surge'}, so the Nanite Surge action row and popup still present only the skill-check trigger, unstarred, with no mention of this feat. RECORD_MARKERS is the only route by which an action row gets a star (MainTab.tsx:525, StatDetailModal.tsx:185) — Q2 also requires the action starred, not just the stat — and it is unused here.

defects.name: Tales of the Road
defects.detail: The bonus half is delivered as the owner specified for Recall Knowledge feats: +2 circumstance via {kind:'skill', detail:'all'} (situationalBonuses.ts:385), starring every skill, with when: 'Recall Knowledge about a city you've visited' leaving the visited-city restriction as unmodelled prose. Both remaining clauses of the same sentence reach the sheet in no form at all. (a) The associated-Lore substitution: no skillSubstitutions on the record and no mention of it in the `when` — the player reading the star is told only about +2, never that they may roll a city Lore instead. (b) 'with your level as your proficiency bonus even if you're untrained': the only existing field is untrainedProficiency:{levelMinus} (derive.ts:334), which is a GLOBAL untrained bonus across every skill and would be wrong here — a Lore-scoped, Recall-Knowledge-scoped level+0 roll for a Lore the character does not own genuinely has no route, so that computed piece alone is a no-lane. But the prose is missing too, which needs no new system: neither clause appears in the `when`, and there is no RECORD_MARKERS entry on the 'recall-knowledge' action (which Q2 requires in addition to the skill stars). Reporting missing rather than no_lane because the deliverable prose and the action mark are both routable today.

defects.name: Ship's Shadow
defects.detail: Nothing reaches the sheet: registries empty, sheetDiff empty, and the core.json record carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/archetype/edition/aonId. The feat's whole content — 'when in the water within 20 feet of a sea vehicle or climbing aboard one, you can move at your full Speed while Sneaking' — is readable only in the feats list. Ruling C, Q2 and the owner's own Guerrilla Dedication answer ('have a * on sneak with this detail') call for a mark on the Sneak action plus a star on Stealth, the skill that performs it, carrying the clause verbatim. Both routes exist and are already used for this exact shape: RECORD_MARKERS note-only entries on 'sneak'/'hide' (see 'quick-refugee', situationalBonuses.ts ~3283) and FEAT_SITUATIONAL entries whose `bonus` is an effect phrase rather than a number. Nothing numeric is owed — the clause lifts Sneak's half-Speed cap — and the positional condition correctly stays unevaluated in the `when` per Ruling M.

defects.name: Impaling Bone
defects.detail: The spell half is right: `innateSpells: [{spellId: impaling-spike, tradition: occult, rank: 7, usesPerDay: 1}]` puts the spell in the pooled innate entry at repertoire rank 7 (the spell's own base rank is 5, so the 7 is being stated explicitly and not defaulted), tradition occult on the entry heading (the spell's own traditions are arcane/primal, so the override is doing real work), spellSources naming 'Impaling Bone', and SpellsTab.tsx:1766-1790 renders it as "rank 7 · 1/day · from Impaling Bone" with a spendable pip — innateSpell and limitedUses both delivered. MISSING is the second sentence: 'except the spike is made of bone instead of cold iron. The bone from the spell has the effects of the ghost touch property rune and can Immobilize incorporeal creatures as if they were corporeal.' Nothing carries it to the Impaling Spike entry — storedFields has no `note`, and the lane that exists for exactly this (SPELL_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371, read by spellSituationalFor → SpellCard `marks`) holds only two entries, neither for impaling-spike. The spell card's 'from Impaling Bone' is plain meta text, not a link, and clicking the card opens the spell's own unaltered description, so at the moment the player casts it the ghost-touch/incorporeal rider is invisible (Principle C / Ruling D). Lane exists and is empty, so this is a defect and not no_lane.

defects.name: Master Siege Engineer
defects.detail: Clause: "You're permanently quickened. You can only use the extra action to Aim or Launch a siege weapon." The lane the requirement-reader suspected was unbuilt DOES exist — RECORD_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts (export at line 3221) carries ten entries of the exact shape `{ on: 'condition', id: 'quickened', value: 'always on', note: '<feat>: you're permanently quickened; the extra action can be used only to …' }`: weapon-supremacy, supreme-spellstrike, perfect-readiness, panache-paragon, swift-paragon, full-automation, eternal-boost, eternal-composition, abundant-vials, plus the conditional variant on peerless-captain. It carries both halves the text needs (Q11's passive shape and Ruling B's restriction-travels-with-the-grant note) in one entry. master-siege-engineer has no entry — `registries: []`, no `note`, no `situational`, and an entirely empty sheetDiff; the string does not appear anywhere under src/. So a permanent extra action every turn, and the Aim/Launch restriction on it, reach the sheet nowhere at all. Fix is one line in the same table.

defects.name: Impossible Polymath
defects.detail:
The record is inert everywhere. storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId; registries is empty; sheetDiff is empty; and a scan of every bucket in public/core.json finds the id 'impossible-polymath' referenced by exactly one record — itself. No src/ file mentions it. All three clauses fail on Principle C (a feat modifying another record's grant must be reflected IN that record):
(1) "As long as you're trained in Arcana, you can add arcane spells to your book… Nature… primal… Religion… divine" — Esoteric Polymath IS modelled (core.json feats/esoteric-polymath carries choice {flag:'polymathSpell', kind:'text', daily:true, prompt:"Today's spell from your book of occult spells", note:"Any one spell written in your book of occult spells (your repertoire plus spells you've Learned with Occultism)…"}). That prompt and note are byte-identical with and without this feat, so at the Rest sheet — the one place the player acts on it — the eligible pool still reads as occult-only and by omission excludes the three traditions this feat unlocks. Impossible Polymath carries no `choiceOptionAdditions` targeting esoteric-polymath (the lane exists: derive.ts:1001 effectiveChoiceOptions) and no `modifiesGrant`.
(2) "you can add one of these spells… to your repertoire as an occult spell each day" — no `choice` of its own with daily:true (the lane Esoteric Polymath itself uses, dailyChoices.ts), so nothing tells the player the pick is cast as occult rather than as its home tradition.
(3) "you can't retain any spells from another tradition… even if you have Eclectic Polymath" — core.json feats/eclectic-polymath has no fields at all and carries no marker for this exception, so the record whose promise is being narrowed says nothing about the narrowing.
Caveat worth the owner's eye: because Esoteric Polymath's choice is kind:'text' (its own note says "The app doesn't model the occult book"), the ENFORCEMENT halves — Q9's filter-to-legally-trained-traditions picker and the automatic clearing of a cross-tradition pick at the next preparation — have no route on a free-text field. The REFLECTION half (widened pool stated on Esoteric Polymath's daily prompt/note; the occult-recasting and no-retention exception legible on this feat's and Eclectic Polymath's entries) is fully buildable with lanes that already ship, and is what is missing.

defects.name: Impervious Vehicle
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert: storedFields hold nothing beyond level/prereq/archetype, there is no COMPANION_MODS entry, and no situationalBonuses entry. None of the three bonuses reaches anything. Concretely: (a) vehicle stat blocks are rendered straight from content.vehicles — CompanionsTab.tsx:1483-1510 passes the catalog record to VehicleBlock with no owner-feat pass at all, and the HP tracker's max is v.hp, so the displayed AC, Fort and max HP are each short by +1 / +1 / +2x character level for a character with this feat; (b) src/rules/companionGrants.ts CompanionMod has no acBonus and no saveBonus field, its maxHpBonus is a plain number (line 129) that cannot express 'twice your level', and the mod loop (companions.ts:503) is gated on mod.kinds.includes('animal') inside deriveAnimalCompanion, so it never reaches kind 'vehicle'. The signature-vehicle addressing DOES exist — effect-backfill.json gives vehicle-mechanic-dedication a choice with flag 'signatureVehicle' (own-companion picker) — but nothing consumes that flag. Note the archetype's siblings all got a surface: vehicle-mechanic-dedication, superior-propulsion and push-it each carry situationalBonuses entries phrased 'to your signature vehicle's ...', so the app has an established route for stating a signature-vehicle bonus even though the vehicle block itself is unmodifiable. This feat has neither that nor anything else. Not the companion-ruling false positive: the defect is the absence on the VEHICLE (and the absence of any statement anywhere), not on the character's own rows.

defects.name: Reading the Signs
defects.detail: The two bonus requirements are delivered well: +2 status starred on every skill with when = "on skill checks that involve drawing cards or resolving a divination effect" (Ruling H's stay-open shape, detail:'all' so Lores match too), and on all three saves with "on saving throws against a hostile divination effect targeting you" (Q2). What is entirely absent is the draw-2-keep-1 clause, which Principle C and Q8 place on each record it modifies. Probe confirms zero markers: markersFor(['reading-the-signs'],'action','harrow-casting') = [], and spellMarkersFor('harrowing',['reading-the-signs']) = []. The lanes exist and are unused — RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) already marks feat-derived action rows by name slug (MainTab.tsx:525 keys on actionId(a.name)), and feats/harrow-casting is a 1-action feat that renders as an action row with exactly the slug 'harrow-casting'; SPELL_MARKERS already exists for spells/harrowing. The harrow-omen draw itself lives in feats/harrower-dedication's daily-preparation text and likewise carries nothing. So a player with Harrower Dedication + Harrow Casting sees no sign on either that they now draw 2 and keep the one they prefer. One sub-clause may genuinely have no lane: the "once per deck" marker on an activatable magical deck / items/deck-of-many-things would be a feat-to-INVENTORY-ITEM marker, and RecordMarker only accepts on:'action'|'condition' while SPELL_MARKERS is spells-only — I found no feat→item marker route short of the item editor's Advanced section, which is player-authored.

defects.name: Shield your Eyes
defects.detail: The +2 is right and complete: situationalBonuses.ts:355 targets `{kind:'ac'}` plus fortitude, reflex and will (Q2's "star all three saves" plus AC), type `circumstance` matching the text, and the `when` carries both restrictions — "while shield raised, against light or visual effects". Not delivered: the mirror clause on YOUR DC. There is no `dcOnly: true` target on any save, so nothing appears beside any DC at all — Ruling D's DC-only shape is implemented (`SituationalTarget.dcOnly`, used by `commanders-banner`, `mountain-stance`, `sixfingers-elixir-*` and others), it is simply unused here, and Ruling H would have it starred on all three save DCs rather than narrowed to one. Weaker second point: "If you critically fail your save against such an effect while your shield is raised, you fail instead" is not stated on the star line either. The star does carry `sourceId` for Ruling H's click-through to the feat's full text, so it is readable — but the registry's own convention in ~50 places is to state the floor inline, either in the `when` (`familiar-foe`: "…(a critical failure becomes a failure)") or as the `bonus` phrase (`unmistakable-lore`: "critical failure becomes failure"; `paragon-benefit-regalia`; `lethoci`). This feat is the only defence-side one that omits it.

defects.name: Contact with the Enemy
defects.detail: `storedFields` carries nothing beyond level/category/prerequisites and `sheetDiff` is empty — the feat is not a pick-a-feat grant, so the empty diff is not the harness limit. Principle C and Q8 both require the marker to land IN Adaptive Stratagem, and the lane exists and fits exactly: `modifiesGrant: [{from: 'adaptive-stratagem', actionRider: {note: ...}}]`. build.ts:3435-3444 defaults `actionId` to `mod.from` precisely for the case where the modified record IS the action, which is what Adaptive Stratagem is (a free-action feat, so it lists under Feat actions and MainTab.tsx:525 already looks up `recordMarkersFor(..., 'action', ...)` for that row). The gate is also the right one — the rider only fires if the character actually has Adaptive Stratagem, which is this feat's prerequisite. Only two records in the whole data use `modifiesGrant` today (`splinter-faith`, `draconic-paragon`), so this is an under-used lane rather than a missing one. The second requirement is satisfied only by accident: `character.commanderTactics.prepared` is a free play-state toggle over the whole folio (MainTab.tsx:272 + `toggleTactic`, capped at `preparedMax`), with no tier restriction on which prepared entries may be swapped — so master and legendary tactics can already be swapped, but because Adaptive Stratagem's own "expert, mobility, or offensive" restriction was never modelled, not because this feat is built. Nothing on the sheet distinguishes a commander who has this feat from one who does not.

defects.name: Uncanny Dodge
defects.detail: The grant half works: `grantsClassFeatures: ['deny-advantage']` reaches `ownedFeatureIds` (derive.ts:2210) and the feature's mechanics fire. The details half does not. I built a level-20 fighter with Uncanny Dodge and ran `featEntries(character, content)` (the exported, tested function behind the Feats & Features tab): `uncanny-dodge` is listed, `deny-advantage` is NOT. featEntries walks class features from `cls.features`, class-archetype additions, `subOpt.featureIds`, `classChoices`, inventor modifications, `character.grantedFeatures` (Overrides + mythic calling only, build.ts:4444-4472) and heritages — it has no route for a feature a FEAT granted. So Deny Advantage's text is reachable only by opening Uncanny Dodge and clicking the "Deny Advantage" descRef link. That is the same gap display-and-reach.test.ts was written to close for subclass-handed features ("a gunslinger's deeds are LISTED, not just owned"); 89 records carry `grantsClassFeatures`, so this is systemic, and it bites hardest on passive grants like this one, `sneak-attack` (Sneak Attacker, Butterfly's Sting), `powerful-fist`, `on-the-case` and `precise-strike`, which cannot reach the actions list either. Separately, the same probe shows `recordMarkersFor(c, db, 'condition', 'off-guard')` returning TWO near-identical Deny Advantage notes — RECORD_MARKERS carries the clause under both `uncanny-dodge` (situationalBonuses.ts:3229) and `deny-advantage` (:3311), and the character owns both ids, while `markersFor` dedupes only by sourceId. `SITUATIONAL_SUPERSEDES` is the existing mechanism for exactly this and has no entry for the pair.

defects.name: Rapid Manifestation
defects.detail: The free action itself is delivered — sheetDiff shows `actions[0] → Rapid Manifestation`, and public/core-descriptions.json carries the full Trigger line ("You roll initiative or a hazard attacks you"), both halves intact, into its popup. What is missing is the cross-reference the owner's Q8 + Principle H require: nothing marks **Manifest Soulforged Armament** as reachable by this trigger. The app HAS the lane — `RECORD_MARKERS` in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts (rendered on any action row by MainTab.tsx:525) and `modifiesGrant.actionRider` — and `rapid-manifestation` appears in neither (registries: [], storedFields has no modifiesGrant). Worse, the target row does not exist on any sheet: `manifest-soulforged-armament` is a real action record in core.json, but `soulforger-dedication` has no `grantsActions`, so the archetype's central activity never reaches the actions list at all. A player who opens Manifest sees nothing; a player who has the dedication sees no Manifest row to open. This is exactly the Quick Recognition shape the owner answered ("have Recognize a Spell appear as both free action and reaction and on the pop up have explanation"), unbuilt here.

defects.name: Effortless Captivation
defects.detail: The triggered entry is delivered — `actions[0] → Effortless Captivation`, with "**Trigger** Your turn begins" and the full enchantment/illusion restriction printed in its popup description, which satisfies both the grantsAction and the `note` requirement on the entry itself. The Principle H requirement is not delivered: **Sustain** is a standard action row on every sheet (src/rules/actions.ts:47) and nothing marks it as also available free at the start of your turn for enchantment or illusion spells. `effortless-captivation` has no `RECORD_MARKERS` entry and no `modifiesGrant.actionRider` (registries: [], storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prereqs/actionCost/archetype). This is the identical shape to the owner's answer 13 — "have Recognize a Spell appear as both free action and reaction and on the pop up have explanation" — so a player who looks Sustain up sees only its printed 1-action cost. Note for whoever fixes it: the marker id is `sustain` (Remaster), not `sustain-a-spell`; `sustain-an-activation` and `sustain-an-effect` are separate records and must not be marked.

defects.name: Basic Wizard Spellcasting
defects.detail: ⚠ The empty sheetDiff is a HARNESS ARTEFACT, not the defect — the feat was placed on a fighter with no Wizard Dedication, and `activeCasterArchetype` keys off the dedication, so no slots could appear. The spellcasting lane IS built: CASTER_ARCHETYPES['wizard-dedication'] = mk('arcane','int',4,'wizard') mints `basicId: 'basic-wizard-spellcasting'` (src/rules/casterArchetypes.ts:73, 248), and archetypeSlots() opens one slot per rank on the standard ladder. The real gap is the feat's ONLY printed mechanical sentence: "add two common spells of that rank to your spellbook". No spellbook exists for a caster archetype — build.ts:3990-3996 builds the archetype's prepared entry straight from `srcSpells[rank]` with no `entry.spellbook`, and Builder.tsx:304 gates `isWizardBook` on `casterCls?.id === 'wizard' || 'witch'` (the CLASS), so the archetype falls to `capSlots[rank]` = 1 pick per rank instead of 2 written into a book. Two consequences: (1) the player can never record the two spells this feat grants, and (2) with no `entry.spellbook`, SpellsTab.tsx:565 lets the archetype prepare ANY tradition spell of the rank rather than only book contents — broader than the archetype actually grants. There is also no "new rank reached" event to hang a per-rank grant on. The Q14-point-6 shape ("taking a feat that grants a formula book ensures the character has one") applies directly and is unbuilt for the spellbook.

defects.name: Lore Seeker
defects.detail:
Almost everything lands: three separate innate entries (Translate, Sound Body, See the Unseen), each at its printed base rank 2, each with `spellSources` naming 'Lore Seeker', and each with its OWN independent 1/day pip (src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:1785 keys the pip per spell id via `innateUsedSet`), so spending one does not spend the others. Tradition arcane is right for this non-caster host.

What is not delivered: the Intelligence spellcasting attribute. The text's fallback branch — live here, the host is a fighter with no prior spellcasting — says 'you use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability'. The sheet shows `stored.spellcasting[innate-casting].keyAbility = "cha"`. src/rules/build.ts:4271 computes `keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility ?? profile?.keyAbility ?? 'cha'`, and Lore Seeker stores neither a `spellcastingGrant` profile nor an `entryRetune`, so it falls through to the Charisma default. src/rules/derive.ts:467 computes the entry's spell attack and spell DC from `entry.keyAbility`, so the innate entry's displayed Attack/DC is a Charisma number where the text specifies Intelligence. The route exists and fits precisely: `spellcastingGrant: {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}` is read as `profile` and is correctly overridden by `caster?.keyAbility` for a character who could already cast — which is exactly the text's conditional branching. Secondary, and consistent with the requirement's own OPEN flag: the tradition is a stored constant 'arcane' on all three grants, and build.ts:4263 derives the entry tradition by majority vote over the grants, so a bard taking this feat gets arcane innate spells rather than the occult ones the text promises ('these spells are of the same tradition'); the `?? caster?.tradition` fallback only fires when no grant names one.

defects.name: Become Thought
defects.detail:
The defences are right: resistance 10 to physical (the category, one entry, not three) and weakness 5 to mental both appear in `defenses` with `defenses.sources` naming 'Become Thought' and `applied:true` — the downside is not silently dropped.

Two requirements are not delivered.

(1) The appearance-change activity. The text grants a single action with the concentrate trait that HAS THE EFFECTS OF Illusory Disguise and lasts until you change your appearance again. The app instead stores `innateSpells:[{spellId:'illusory-disguise', tradition:'occult', atWill:true}]`, so the surface is a spell card on the Spells page, not an entry in the actions list. Because it is the spell record, the player reads the spell's own cast cost and duration — public/core.json gives illusory-disguise `cast:{type:'actions',value:2}` and `duration:'1 hour'` — where the feat grants a 1-action ability with no duration limit. So the action cost and duration shown are both wrong, and the granted ability never appears where the player looks for actions. `grantsActions` is the route and is unused here.

(2) The once-per-year return to life. Nothing is stored — no `note`, and no RECORD_MARKERS entry. Ruling D's own worked precedent is 'The Survivor marks the Dying condition', and the mechanism exists and is in active use: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3222+ has `{on:'condition', id:'dying', ...}` markers for the-survivor, draddeths-edge and hero-gods-bond. Become Thought carries none, so at the moment the clause matters — the player is dying — the sheet says nothing. The requirement's escape hatch on the per-year frequency is honoured by accident (no pip exists, so nothing refreshes on the wrong schedule), but only because the whole clause is absent.

defects.name: Hybrid Form
defects.detail: The feat is completely inert: sheetDiff is empty, registries is empty, and storedFields carries only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId — no `modifiesGrant`, no `note`, no `grantsActions`. All three promises about Change Shape are undelivered: speaking in a fox form, keeping kitsune unarmed attacks and gaining a tail in a tailless form, and the second, separate use ('You can Change Shape to alter the details of your hybrid form without fully changing into your true form or your alternate form'). The lane exists — `modifiesGrant.actionRider` renders as a RecordMarker on the action row (types.ts:785, RECORD_MARKERS + recordMarkersFor) — but the anchor does not: content.actions has a `change-shape` record, and nothing kitsune points at it. The kitsune ancestry record in public/core.json has no `grantsActions` (only werecreature-dedication grants change-shape), and no kitsune heritage or ancestry feat grants it either, even though the AoN ancestry entry (ancestry-38) lists 'Change Shape — As a kitsune, you gain the Change Shape ability'. So a marker authored on this feat would have no row to sit on until the ancestry grants Change Shape first.

defects.name: Beautiful Knifework
defects.detail: The feat produces no surface anywhere except its own Feats-tab entry: sheetDiff empty, registries empty, storedFields has no `grantsActions`, no `note`, no `modifiesGrant`, and actionCost {type:'passive'} (which matches AoN feat-7477 — it prints no action glyph, so the passive cost is faithful, but isActionCost() excludes passive, so nothing reaches any action or activity list; ACTIVITIES is a curated list and skillActions.ts's 42 feat-gated rows are core skill feats only, so neither picks it up). The clause the app should have honoured is 'This counts as preparing a disguise to Impersonate, taking 10 minutes and requiring a healer's toolkit instead of a disguise kit' — the feat changes how you prepare an Impersonate disguise, and Ruling D plus Q8 ('mark the action the feat modifies') put a marker on that action. The route is live and unused: RECORD_MARKERS accepts {on:'action', id:'impersonate'}, `impersonate` exists in content.actions, and StatDetailModal.tsx:185 already renders a star + inline value on that row inside Deception's 'Actions you can take'. Correctly absent: no Medicine-DC row (Ruling D — a skill DC gets no surface), and no +2 Deception or free action for the disguised character (Ruling F / ★ Companions — it lands on the ally or on the construct companion's block).

defects.name: Enter Divine Realm
defects.detail: The innate grant itself is correct — interplanar-teleport, divine, rank 7, usesPerDay 1, and spellSources names "Enter Divine Realm" on the card. But "with a casting time of only 1 minute" is applied nowhere, and the omission shows a WRONG number: InnateSpellGrant (src/rules/types.ts:1213) carries only spellId/tradition/rank/usesPerDay/usesPer/heightenHalfLevel/heightenAt — no cast-time and no per-grant note — so SpellsTab renders the base spell's own cost, and public/core.json spells/interplanar-teleport has cast {type:'duration', text:'10 minutes'}. The player is shown a 10-minute casting for a casting the feat makes 1 minute. The three remaining clauses also reach nothing beyond the feat's own row: the destination narrowing (deity's realm only, you are the planar key, always the centre), the conditional immunity to the realm's harmful conditions, and the free 1-minute return trip with up to 8 creatures — which is not part of Interplanar Teleport at all, so a player reading only the Spells page loses it entirely. The feat carries no `note`, and `note` is the app's own route for exactly this (26 feats use it; rendered at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:77, and captivating-intensity's note is precisely an innate-spell clarification). Correct behaviour elsewhere: no entry was added to any immunities list, as Ruling I requires.

defects.name: Tiger Slash
defects.detail: The action exists (sheetDiff actions[2]) and its popup carries "**Requirements** You are in Tiger Stance", so the gate is visible. What is missing is the damage rider: "It deals two extra weapon damage dice (three extra dice if you're 14th level or higher)" reaches nothing at all — no entry for tiger-slash in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, no `note` on the feat, and no rider on the strike it modifies (public/core.json stances/tiger-stance carries only the plain 1d8 slashing tiger claw plus a note about the 1d4 persistent bleed). This is promised-but-empty on a built lane, not no_lane: the identical shape is authored ~30 times over, e.g. dual-handed-assault ("on the Strike made with Dual-Handed Assault"), advantageous-assault, pivot-strike, and brutal-critical ("one extra weapon damage die"), all as {kind:'strikeDamage'} with the action named in `when`; level bands already live in the bonus string (deadly-aim: "+4 circumstance (+6 at 11th level, +8 at 15th)"), so "+2 extra weapon damage dice (3 at 14th level)" fits without any new capability. Result: at the harness's level 20 the tiger claw shows its ordinary damage with no indication that this action adds three dice. The 5-foot push needs nothing (enemy-facing, DECIDED SCOPE), and the crit-triggered Strength-to-bleed rider needs nothing under Q15 — I am treating Q15 as governing there, so I am not counting it as a defect.

defects.name: Pounding Leap
defects.detail: Two of three clauses land, one does not. Delivered: the activity reaches the encounter action list (sheetDiff actions[0] null→"Pounding Leap", 2-action cost passes the isActionCost gate) with its full text in the popup; and the +2 is correctly in the situational lane rather than the Athletics total — situationalBonuses.ts:314, targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'athletics'}], when "the High Jump or Long Jump after your fist Strike", bonus "+2 circumstance" (Ruling B satisfied, right bonus type, right value). Missing: nothing marks High Jump or Long Jump. Q2 is explicit ("Both — star the skill AND the action") and Q8/Ruling D put the mark on the action the feat modifies, and the running-start clause — "you count as having a running start and do not need to Stride before this activity to avoid failure" — is the mechanically substantive half, since both actions auto-fail without a 10-foot Stride (skillActions.ts:165, :171 print exactly that auto-fail). The surfaces exist and are empty: RECORD_MARKERS carries no pounding-leap entry, while core.json has actions high-jump and long-jump and StatDetailModal.tsx:185 renders recordMarkersFor(...,'action', actionSlug(a.name)) on every Athletics skill-action row. A player checking their Athletics number sees the +2 star but is never told the auto-fail is lifted. Secondary: the star's `when` says "after your fist Strike", dropping the printed restriction "against an unattended object or unoccupied flat surface" that the +2 is conditioned on ("when you do so"), so as worded it promises the bonus after a fist Strike on a creature too. The PFS AC-10 line correctly gets no surface (DECIDED SCOPE: target-side numbers).

defects.name: Water Sprint
defects.detail: The feat carries nothing whatsoever. storedFields is level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost/edition/aonId only — no situational, no note, no marker; registries is [] and sheetDiff is []. Taking it changes nothing a player can see anywhere except the feat's own entry. Owed and absent: a `*` on the land Speed and on Stride carrying "Stride in a straight line, at least half your Speed over ground, then any of the remainder across a level body of water; if you don't end on solid ground you fall in." Both surfaces are built and would render it today — SituationalTarget already has kind:'speed' and VitalsRail.tsx:695 stars the Speed row from statHasSituational({kind:'speed'}), while core.json has the `stride` action and MainTab.tsx:525 renders RECORD_MARKERS on action rows (the precedent is quick-refugee, which marks Hide and Sneak with no number at all). Ruling H says star everything plausible with the printed trigger in the note, which is precisely this shape, and the extractor is right that NO speed row is owed — the feat grants no movement type (Q7), so the absence of a swim/fly/water-walk Speed is correct and must not be 'fixed'. The one part that may need a route the app lacks is the legendary-Athletics upgrade: Ruling G says the upgraded text REPLACES the straight-line version rather than sitting beside it, and FEAT_SITUATIONAL entries have no proficiency-rank predicate, so a rank-conditional swap would need a new field. That does not soften the verdict — the base marker is simply absent.

defects.name: Unnerving Expansion
defects.detail: The activity itself is delivered (the feat lands in the actions list, actions[2], and its popup carries the full printed text). Two of the three requirements are not delivered — the record in public/core.json is bare (id/name/level/traits/prereqs/actionCost/archetype only), it has no entry in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, and it appears nowhere in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts. (1) situational — "you don't take penalties for not sharing a language with that creature": no `*` on Intimidation and none on Demoralize. The lane is built and this exact clause has three shipped precedents (`intimidating-prowess` bonus "+1 circumstance (and ignore the not-sharing-a-language penalty)", `intimidating-glare`, `animal-call` "ignores the –4 circumstance penalty for not sharing a language"), so the omission is a plain gap, not a lane gap. (2) modifiesGrant — "The radius of the emanation of your curse maelstrom state increases by 5 feet": no `modifiesGrant` field. Curse Maelstrom Dedication (which grants the state and the Expel Maelstrom action, and is itself a 1-action record in the actions list) shows nothing about the +5 ft, so Principle C is unmet; the `actionRider` shape on GrantModification (src/rules/types.ts:785, "a rider on the action `from` grants — or IS") is the existing route. Note the target record's own prose is also damaged upstream: the dedication's description reads "all creatures other than you within a take a -1 status penalty" — the emanation radius the +5 ft modifies is missing from the sentence.

defects.name: Skeptic's Defense
defects.detail: Two of three requirements land: the reaction appears in the actions list (sheetDiff actions[2]) with its popup carrying "**Frequency** once per day", the trigger, the counteract-rank formula and the auditory-linguistic descriptor; and limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} is authored (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json) and reaches the sheet (sheetDiff limitedUses[0]), spendable and rest-restored. What is missing is the situational surface for "attempting a counteract check using your Intimidation modifier": the feat has no entry in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, so Intimidation carries no `*` and the player reading their Intimidation number is never told this reaction rolls off it. That is the same shape the owner asked for on The Truth as I See it (gold set #16, "having a * on deception") and Q2's "star the skill AND the action". The counteract-rank half (half your level rounded up = 10 at the host's level 20) is at least legible as a formula in the popup, so only the skill star is a clear gap.

defects.name: Healing Hands
defects.detail: "When you cast Heal, you roll d10s instead of d8s" never reaches the Heal spell. The only implementation is situationalBonuses.ts:2733 — {targets:[{kind:'spellDamage'}], when:'when you cast Heal', bonus:'roll d10s instead of d8s'} — which surfaces as a line inside a generic "Spell damage" stat popup (SpellsTab.tsx:2001, VitalsRail.tsx:307; explain.ts:880 renders it with total 'varies' and the description "Damage dealt by your spells is rolled per spell"). Two things are wrong with that surface. (a) Heal's own card carries no mark: SPELL_MARKERS — the lane built for exactly this, whose comment cites Ruling G ("on the spell, since that's what you're looking at when you cast it") and which SpellsTab already renders per card — contains only 'harm' (sap-life) and 'dancing-blade'. So the die change is invisible at the point of casting, which is the failure mode Ruling G exists to prevent. (b) It is filed under DAMAGE for a spell that deals none; the field's own header comment (situationalBonuses.ts:51) warns that "31 spells heal, and '+2 to your spell damage' must not add +2 to a heal", so a player will not look for Heal's die under "Spell damage". The stronger half of the requirement — Heal's printed 1-action / 2-action / 3-action and heightened lines actually READING d10 rather than d8, replacing the die per Ruling G — has no route at all: the app renders the spell's stored description text and has no lane that rewrites it. Note this is systemic, not one record: harming-hands (situationalBonuses.ts:2731) is authored identically for Harm.

defects.name: Bullet Split
defects.detail: The activity itself is fine — sheetDiff shows actions[0] = "Bullet Split" at its printed 1-action cost, and the stored description opens with the full "**Requirements** You're wielding a firearm or crossbow in one hand and a slashing (or versatile S) melee weapon in the other" line, so the wielding state is legible in the popup. What is missing is the whole second sentence: "Each of these attacks takes a –2 penalty to the attack roll, but the two count as only one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty." registries is empty and grep confirms no 'bullet-split' key anywhere in src/rules — so neither the –2 nor the MAP concession reaches the strike rows the player is actually looking at when they roll these two Strikes. This is not the "internal steps of an activity" exemption; the app authors precisely this shape elsewhere, twice over: dual-handed-assault (situationalBonuses.ts:455) stars strikeDamage with when "on the Strike made with Dual-Handed Assault", and combination-finisher (line 2705) stars strikeAttack with a pure MAP-arithmetic note ("multiple attack penalty is -4 … instead of -5/-10"). There are 308 strikeAttack situational entries in that file; Bullet Split, which needs both an attack penalty and a MAP note, has none. Owed: a strikeAttack entry whose `when` names Bullet Split's two Strikes and whose text carries both the –2 and the "count as one attack for MAP" clause.

defects.name: Godspeed
defects.detail: The mode is missing. "for the next minute, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to all your Speeds and are quickened" is delivered only as a display-only situational star (situationalBonuses.ts:598 — targets [{kind:'speed'}], bonus '+10 feet status', when 'for 1 minute after spending a Mythic Point on Godspeed — applies to all your Speeds'). Per Q1 a duration longer than a round earns a MODE carrying real numbers; no record in public/core.json carries a `modes` field and RAW_MODES (modes.ts:209+) has no Godspeed entry, so no Speed on the sheet ever moves — land Speed still reads 25 ft with the feat active, and there is nothing to toggle to show the minute is running. The quickened clause and its Stride/Step/Leap restriction survive only in the feat's own description on the action row (actions[] gains 'Godspeed'), not inside a mode as principle B asks. NOT defects: the Mythic Point cost is fine — play.ts models mythicPoints as a session resource and VitalsRail.tsx:967 renders spendable pips. The same gap sits on the owner's own Q1 example, Shield the Faithful (situationalBonuses.ts:682), which is also star-only, so this is one instance of an unbuilt lane rather than a one-off authoring slip.

defects.name: Friendform
defects.detail: Only the Deception star is built (situationalBonuses.ts:499 — '+4 status' when 'to Impersonate a Friendform ritual participant whose token you still hold (you also add your level even if untrained)'), which correctly carries the restriction in the `when` per Ruling B and folds the untrained-level clause in as text (the honest best available — a situational entry contributes no proficiency change). Missing: (1) the daily choice. "During your daily preparations, you can perform a simple ritual with up to five willing Small or Medium humanoids" gets no surface — the record has no `choice` at all, so nothing appears at Rest. The lane exists and is exactly the shape principle I calls for: choice.daily with kind 'text' (dailyChoices.ts:26), used by Quick Study and Call Gun. (2) the Change Shape modification. Per principle C the recorded participants must be visible on the ability they extend; the `change-shape` action record exists in core.json and RECORD_MARKERS ({on:'action', id:…}) is the built route for marking it, but Friendform has no entry there. Also worth the owner's attention: the Anadi ancestry record carries no grantsActions, so Change Shape may not reach an anadi's sheet at all for a marker to attach to. Not a defect: Q2's action half — Impersonate — is unstarred, but SituationalTarget has no 'action' kind, so that half can only be met through RECORD_MARKERS, which is the same miss as (2).

defects.name: Emotional Partitions
defects.detail: The +1 half is right: situationalBonuses.ts:193 stars all three saves (diff shows situational.fortitude/reflex/will[emotional-partitions] = "+1 circumstance", when "against emotion effects") — Q2's all-three-saves shape, kept out of the flat totals per Ruling B. What is not delivered is the second clause, "If you roll a success on a saving throw against an emotion effect, you get a critical success instead." Nothing on the sheet says it: the popup line reads only "+1 circumstance from Emotional Partitions — against emotion effects", and the upgrade is reachable only by pressing the generic "Full text" button that every star has. The app has TWO routes for it and uses neither here: (a) the sibling convention of folding the shift into the same star — forlorn (line 218) "against emotion effects (success becomes critical success)", emotionless (194) "(success becomes crit success)", numb (2147); and (b) the purpose-built `degreeShifts` field (situationalBonuses.ts:3117, fans out to saves/skills/actions via explain.ts:292-315), which no record in core.json populates at all (0 occurrences). Treating the "Full text" button as the surface would make Ruling H's note-plus-click-through meaningless, since every star already has that button.

defects.name: Straveika
defects.detail: The Sense Motive half is delivered — situationalBonuses.ts:378 stars Perception with when "to Sense Motive", bonus "+1 circumstance", restricted so it stays out of the flat Perception total (Ruling B). The DC half of the same sentence, "and Perception DCs against attempts to Lie to you", appears nowhere: the popup line reads "+1 circumstance from Straveika — to Sense Motive" and stops. The app's route for a Perception DC is the `when` text itself (dcOnly is documented as saves-only), and records with word-for-word the same clause all carry it: insightful-goloma (1956) and oathkeeper-dwarf (1942) both read "to Sense Motive, and to your Perception DC against attempts to Lie to you"; also eyes-unclouded (204), lie-detector (265), cynical (493), watchers-armband (1906). So the wording exists and Straveika simply lacks half of it. Secondary, not the verdict driver: no RECORD_MARKERS entry marks the Sense Motive action (Q2's action half) — but no Sense-Motive record in the app does, so that is a class-wide pattern rather than this record's defect.

defects.name: Rocky Flesh
defects.detail: The formula half is right: `resistances:[{type:'physical', value:'@actor.archetypeFeats.stonebound'}]` resolves live through archetypeFeatCounts (derive.ts:1324), which counts every taken feat whose `archetype` is `stonebound`, so the number moves as Stonebound feats are added or removed — the sheetDiff shows resistance physical 1 with the feat's source line attached, and it earns no `*` correctly (Q7: permanent grants need none). The defect is the stored TYPE: plain `"physical"`, which grants resistance against adamantine damage the text explicitly carves out — an effect applied where the text conditions it. This is not a no-lane case: the type string is free-form and rendered verbatim (keyed `resistance:${r.type}` at derive.ts:1678), and two sibling records already store the clause correctly — Harden Flesh and Living Statue both use `type: "physical (except adamantine)"`. Fix is a one-word data change to match them.

defects.name: Unexpected Sharpshooter Dedication
defects.detail: The two real requirements are met — Accidental Shot appears in the actions list, and the once-per-day use rides onto the ACCIDENTAL SHOT row exactly as Ruling D wants (MainTab.tsx:252 'Carry the granter when IT holds the per-day limit', rendered by ActionUses at :457). The spurious part: the feat record stores actionCost {type:'actions', value:2}, so the sheet lists a second, phantom 2-action activity called 'Unexpected Sharpshooter Dedication' beside Accidental Shot (visible in sheetDiff as actions[3]). The printed text calls for no such activity — AoN feat-3272 prints the dedication with `<actions string="" />` (no cost); the 'Two Actions' belongs to the Accidental Shot child section, whose record correctly carries aonParentId 'feat-3272'. This is the parent/child import artifact the owner's own adjudication rules out (docs/gold-set-final.md, entry 11.2: the feat's own action cost 'is an AoN import artifact of the parent/child section split and must not produce a second, trigger-less reaction row'; dedup is by NAME, so the differing names let both through). Fix is actionCost {type:'passive'} on the feat; the frequency must stay on the feat since that is what feeds Accidental Shot's pips.

defects.name: Potent Nectar
defects.detail: The mechanics are right: `effectChoices` (id 'potent-nectar', prompt 'Potent Nectar — permanent, and cannot be changed later') offers Sticky and High velocity, each granting a strikeDamage rider with strikeName 'Nectar' (matching the Strike Caustic Nectar grants) and persistent:true / splash:true. types.ts:2951-2955 documents both flags as 'Not multiplied on a critical hit', and derive.ts:2561-2563 renders them as their own labelled damage terms ('1d4 persistent acid', '1d4 acid splash') rather than folding them into the doubled base expression — so Principle C and the crit exclusion are both satisfied. The empty sheetDiff is expected (unmade pick, and the host has no Caustic Nectar). SPURIOUS: the record ALSO carries a second, inert `choice` — {flag:'choice', prompt:'Benefit', kind:'array', options:[{value:'splash',label:'Splash Damage'},{value:'persistent',label:'Persistent Damage'}]} — with no grant attached and no consumer (the riders key off strikeName, not fromChoiceFlag). Builder.tsx:1632-1638 renders it unconditionally (the only guard skips flag==='feat'), so the player is asked this explicitly-permanent one-of-two question TWICE, and FeatsTab.tsx:87 prints THAT answer beside the feat's name: `${feat.name} (${fc.choice.label})`. A character who answers 'Splash Damage' in the inert picker and 'Sticky' in the real one reads 'Potent Nectar (Splash Damage)' on the Feats tab while their Nectar Strike carries 1d4 persistent acid. The text calls for one choice, not two, and never for a label that can disagree with the effect.

defects.name: Fear No Pain!
defects.detail: WRONG VALUE on the frequency. The reaction itself is right — actions[0] = "Fear No Pain!" with trigger and description in the popup (Principle E, exemplar #7), and correctly nothing on any of the character's own saves for the ally's reroll and +2 circumstance bonus (Ruling F; the reaction entry is the record Principle A asks for). But the app asserts a limit the printed feat does not: stored `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}`, rendered as a 1/day pip. AoN feat-8940 (Hellfire Dispatches pg. 121, the pristine mirror at C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-8940.json) prints "Frequency once per hour". The app's own stored description is corrupt the same way — public/core-descriptions.json has "**Frequency** once per day" — so the popup misinforms the player too, and the reader's requirement inherited the error from that text. The consequence is mechanical, not cosmetic: featUses.ts:110 treats 'hour' as SUB_DAILY (refills on the encounter reset) and 'day' as not (refills only at rest), so the character gets one use per adventuring day where the rules give one per hour. I swept all 585 feats whose AoN record carries a frequency against the app's limitedUses period: only 3 disagree, so this is a one-off data error, not a systematic import bug. The other two are turn-to-mist (AoN "once per day", app per:'hour') and even-the-odds-eagle-knight (AoN "once per 10 minutes", app per:'day' — the `every` multiplier is unused).

defects.name: Sealed Poppet
defects.detail: Clause: "You no longer have the weakness to fire from THE FLAMMABLE ABILITY." The removal itself works and is correctly bounded on the other side — the diff drops the poppet's fire weakness (value 6, from the ancestry record's `weaknesses: [{type:'fire', value:'max(1,floor(@actor.level/3))'}]`) and grants no fire resistance, so the flavour clause "protecting you from fire" correctly adds nothing. What is wrong is the SCOPE. The field is `removesWeaknesses: ['fire']`, and src/rules/derive.ts:1790 applies it as `weak.delete(t)` on a map keyed by damage type only, after every source has merged in — so it erases a fire weakness from ANY source, not just the flammable ability. Failure scenario, reachable today: a poppet who takes Mummy Dedication (feats/mummy-dedication grants `weaknesses: [{type:'fire', value:'floor(@actor.level/2)'}]`) shows NO fire weakness at all — at level 20 a weakness 10 the rules say still applies vanishes from Defences. Same for a poppet under any of the fire-weakness modes: curse-of-creeping-ashes-1..4 (up to 5+level) and the item modes item-iron-wine-second-cup and item-thorn-triad*. The GM applies the curse, the pill never appears, and the player is not told. A source-scoped removal (delete only the ancestry's contribution, then let the attribution map re-elect a winner) is what the clause asks for; note beastkin-resilience ['silver'] and insulated-poppet ['electricity','cold'] share the shape and the same exposure. Secondary, and I am NOT counting it in the verdict because it is the ancestry record's gap rather than this feat's: Principle C asks that the Flammable ability's own entry show the weakness has been negated, but the app has no Flammable entry to annotate — public/core-descriptions.json's poppet description lists HP/Size/Speed/Boosts/Flaws/Languages/Senses and never mentions Flammable, so the weakness only ever existed as a Defences pill.

defects.name: Seasoned Command
defects.detail: The once-per-hour limit is attached to the WRONG thing. Clause: "Special Once per hour, you can Take the Lead of a troop as a free action (rather than 2 actions)." The hourly limit belongs to that free-action option only; the Seasoned Command activity itself is at-will (limited only by a per-ally 1-minute temporary immunity, which is target-side and correctly absent). The record stores `limitedUses: {max:1, per:'hour'}` on the feat itself, and sheetDiff confirms it lands as `limitedUses[0] = "Seasoned Command: {max:1,per:hour}"`. Because `LimitedUses` (types.ts:1202) is documented as "the TRACKABLE limit" and MainTab.tsx:252 hangs use-pips off it via `usesFrom`, the 1-action encounter activity now shows 1 use per hour on the sheet — a false statement about a combat action a player may legally use on several different allies in the same minute. Two further clauses are also undelivered, both against owner-settled shapes: (a) the Special is the Quick Recognition / Principle H shape (gold-set #13, Q8) — "Take the Lead" should appear under both its native 2 actions and this free action, marked on the Take the Lead record itself; there is no `grantsActions`, no `modifiesGrant`, and no "Take the Lead" record anywhere in core.json (only `rules`/`categoryPage` `skirmish-bonds` exist), so nothing carries it; (b) "establish leadership … and grant a skirmish bond in half the normal time (5 minutes and 4 hours)" is real numbers, not GM adjudication, and there is no `note` on the feat and no marker on the `skirmish-bonds` rules page (Ruling D/G: it should REPLACE the printed time). What the app does deliver is good: the 1-action activity reaches the actions list, and the crit-success +1 circumstance to Aid is starred on all 16 skills (Ruling C — every skill that could perform Aid) with the condition correctly in `when` ("on your check to Aid the chosen ally, after a critical success on Seasoned Command") and the correct bonus TYPE. Only the extra restricted reaction from that same crit is unimplemented, which Q15 permits. Note the app starred no attack roll, though the text says "skill check or attack roll to Aid".

defects.name: Know the Beat
defects.detail: CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION: the feat can train TWO Lores where the text trains one. The choice is authored twice — FEAT_LANE_GRANTS['know-the-beat'] in src/rules/featGrantsLane.ts:15 as `skillChoices:[{options:['lore:guild','lore:legal','lore:mercantile','lore:underworld'], rank:'trained'}]`, AND core.json's own `effectChoices` (prompt 'Choose a Lore skill to become trained in', each option granting skills:{'lore:<x>':'trained'}). Builder.tsx renders BOTH pickers on the picked feat with no dedup — the skillChoices SubCard at line 1644 and the effectChoices SubCard at line 1751. The two resolve independently: build.ts:3131-3143 defaults an unset skillChoices slot to `opts[0]` unconditionally, while resolvePick (build.ts:3211-3221) only grants when the player actually picks. I built a level-3 fighter with the feat and effectChoices 'know-the-beat:lore' = 'underworld' and got lore:guild AND lore:underworld both trained; setting the skillChoices slot too collapses it back to one. Any player who uses the Lore picker labelled with the feat's own prompt and picks anything except Guild Lore ends up trained in a Lore they never chose. TWO REQUIREMENTS ARE ALSO MISSING. (1) '…and to checks made to investigate crimes' is narrowed to Diplomacy alone (situationalBonuses.ts:257, targets [{kind:'skill',detail:'diplomacy'}]), where the text names a trigger and no skill — Ruling H says stay open, and the app already does exactly that for the same shape: detectives-kit and sleuths-pipe both use targets [{kind:'perception'},{kind:'skill',detail:'all'}] with 'to investigate a crime scene / to investigate the subject…'. The two clauses are also merged into one `when` ('to Gather Information or investigate crimes'); my-reputation-precedes-me shows the two-entry shape the stacking rule expects. (2) Q2's action half is absent — no RECORD_MARKERS entry putting a mark on the 'gather-information' action, though streetwise marks that very action by that route. The Lore picker's option list itself is correctly bounded to exactly the four printed Lores (Q9).

defects.name: Aldori's Retort
defects.detail: The extraReaction lane fires correctly — VitalsRail.tsx:714 shows "2 per round" with the source — so the reaction economy does show a count above one, as required. But the restriction shown is narrower than the printed one: core.json stores `extraReaction: {usableFor: "Aldori Riposte"}` and the sheet renders "Aldori Riposte (Aldori's Retort)", while the text says "only for Aldori Riposte, Saving Slash, or any dueling action". The sheet therefore asserts a limitation the feat does not impose — a 14th-level Aldori duelist reads that they may not spend it on Saving Slash (a real reaction feat present in core.json) or on any dueling action. This is a stored-value defect, not a lane gap: `usableFor` is free text and already carries compound restrictions elsewhere ('reflexive-riposte': "Attack of Opportunity or Dueling Riposte"). Fix is a one-string edit to "Aldori Riposte, Saving Slash, or any dueling action".

defects.name: Relinquish Control
defects.detail: The +2 circumstance is stored far wider than the text allows. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:590 holds two entries; the second is `{ targets: [{ kind:'skill', detail:'all' }], when: "until the start of your next turn after you Relinquish Control…", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }`. The text limits that bonus to "Recall Knowledge checks made using Lore skills granted by your attuned apparitions" and puts NO duration on it (it sits outside the one-round window). The sheetDiff shows the star landing on all 16 core skills — Acrobatics, Athletics, Stealth, Thievery, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Performance, Survival among them — none of which is a Lore, and several of which cannot Recall Knowledge at all, so even the widest reading (Ruling C / gold-set #6 Mastermind's Eye, "every skill that can Recall Knowledge") does not reach them. The `when` compounds it: it names neither Recall Knowledge nor Lore, so the restriction Ruling B requires to live in the `when` is absent, and it wrongly attaches the one-round window to a permanent clause. The type union already supports `detail: 'lore:*'` and build.ts:1919 resolves each apparition's two named Lores, so the correct target set is reachable. Everything else is right: the free action reaches actions[1] with the trigger and the restricted-action list in its popup text; the +4 status stars all three saves (Q1 indication-only, Ruling H) with the trigger in the note; and the bound-apparition pick is recorded with the decided "Recorded only" warning rather than a live daily-attunement lock, which matches the existing choice-lane pattern.

defects.name: Perfect Ki Adept
defects.detail: focusPool is CORRECT: `focusPoolBonus: 1` is stored, and build.ts:2136 deliberately suppresses it because the granted focus spell already carries its own pool point — net +1, which is what the text means. The defect is the focusSpell clause "the appropriate qi spell for YOUR School of Perfection". The text lets the player choose nothing — the school (already stored as `choice.flag: 'houseOfPerfectionElement'` on Student of Perfection Dedication, values fire/water/air/earth) determines which of the four. The app ships an unconditioned 4-option `effectChoices` picker (id `qi-spell`) whose options are not gated on that flag, so an Unblinking Flame student can select Untwisting Iron Buffer and the sheet grants it. This is a direct Q9 case ("the builder shows only what the player may legally pick… Domain Fluency must filter to the mystery's domains"). ⚠ SCOPE: Q9's own named example is unbuilt the same way — `domain-fluency` in public/core.json carries a full unfiltered domain list too, and `EffectChoice` (src/rules/types.ts:1050) has no field to gate an option on another record's choice, so this is an unbuilt shape rather than a one-off typo. The engine CAN read another record's choice flag today (`fromChoiceFlag`, src/rules/derive.ts:2550), so the data is reachable. Everything else is right: focusSource is set to the feat's name (build.ts:2263), so the spell is attributed to this feat on the Spells page. Empty sheetDiff is the expected unmade-pick case, not a defect.

defects.name: Warding Jewel
defects.detail: Both resistances are level-driven formulas and both are sourced to the feat, so the lane and the presence are right — but the slashing formula is off by one at a quarter of the levels. Clause: "you gain resistance 2 to piercing damage and resistance 1 to slashing damage… increases by 1 at 9th level and every 4 levels thereafter" → correct pairs are 2/1 (levels 5-8), 3/2 (9-12), 4/3 (13-16), 5/4 (17-20). storedFields.resistances stores piercing = ceil(@actor.level/4) (correct at every level) and slashing = floor(@actor.level/4), which equals the piercing value whenever level is divisible by 4. The harness's level-20 build proves it: sheetDiff shows defenses.resistances[1] (slashing) = 5 and defenses.sources.resistance:slashing[0].value = 5, where the text gives 4. Same over-grant at levels 8 (2 instead of 1), 12 (3 instead of 2) and 16 (4 instead of 3). The correct expression is ceil(@actor.level/4)-1 (equivalently floor((@actor.level-1)/4)). Nothing else is wrong: the passive-not-mode reading matches Q11, and piercing is exact.

defects.name: Rule of Three
defects.detail: The +2 lands on the HERO, and the app's own Spin Tale record settles who that is: "designating one of your allies (but not yourself) as the hero" (actions/spin-tale). So the bonus can never apply to you. The reaction listing is delivered correctly (sheetDiff actions[1] = Rule of Three, full Trigger/Requirements in the popup) — Principle E says that is the whole requirement. But situationalBonuses.ts:611 also files the bonus on YOUR OWN stats: situational.ac, .fortitude, .reflex and .will all gain "+2 circumstance (+4 …)" with when = "reaction, to the hero of your spun tale, against the triggering repeated attack/ability/spell". Ruling F/N is explicit — a bonus that goes to a teammate gets "nothing on your sheet. No star, no modifier" — so four stars on your own defences for a bonus you never receive are exactly what the ruling forbids. Confirmed by probe: featSituationalFor(['rule-of-three'], {kind:'ac'}) returns the entry. Note this looks systemic rather than one-off: the same shape appears at fish-from-the-falls-edge ("on the ally you saved from dying"), mythic-allies ("the SUMMONED creature's AC") and terrain-scout, so the owner may want to rule on the class of entries, not just this feat. Secondary, minor: the description's ref link is labelled "Spun a Tale" while the record is actions/spin-tale ("Spin Tale"), so that link likely resolves to nothing.

defects.name: Preserve the Moment
defects.detail: Four of five requirements are met: the feat is a reaction record so it lists in the reactions list with Frequency/Trigger in its popup (Principle E); `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` tracks; `grantsActions: ['restore-the-moment']` puts Restore the Moment in the list as a second, separately-detailed reaction with its own Trigger/Effect; and nothing invents a recorded-actions store. The defect is what the app adds. MainTab.tsx:252 attaches the GRANTER's limit to a granted action (`act && from.limitedUses ? {...act, usesFrom: from}`), so Restore the Moment renders a pip tracker keyed to `preserve-the-moment` — `featUse` reads `c.featUses['preserve-the-moment']` (featUses.ts:69). Two consequences, both wrong against the text: (1) the two reactions share ONE 1/day pool, so the instant you spend Preserve the Moment — the only moment Restore the Moment is legal — Restore's row reads 0/1 and its spend button is `disabled`, and its tooltip says "refills on daily preparations"; (2) the pips sit on the wrong row, because the feat record itself is pushed into `actionRecords` without `usesFrom`, so Preserve the Moment's own reaction row shows no tracker while the button labelled "Spend a use of Preserve the Moment" appears under Restore the Moment. The text gives Restore the Moment no per-day limit at all — it gives it one use inside a rolling 24 hours opened by Preserve the Moment firing. That availability condition is also carried nowhere on the Restore the Moment entry (the action record has no `note` and its imported description does not mention it), so an untriggered reaction is shown as though it were live.

defects.name: Weight of Experience
defects.detail: Both halves arrive but nothing binds them, so the app applies unconditioned what the text conditions. The skill pick is stored (featGrantsAuto.ts:339 `skillChoices:[{options:'any',rank:'trained'}]` → build.featSkillChoices['weight-of-experience:0']; diff shows acrobatics untrained→trained) and Assurance is granted as a bonus feat (featFeatGrants.ts:180; diff stored.feats[assurance].grantedBy = 'weight-of-experience'). But the granted Assurance's own skill comes from a SEPARATE open picker over all 16 skills — Builder.tsx:448 grantedChoicePicker writes build.grantedFeatChoices['assurance'], which build.ts:3032 reads back via grantedChoiceById — with no reference to the pick made one clause earlier. The player can therefore train Acrobatics and take Assurance in Athletics, i.e. Assurance in a skill this feat never gave them (and the picker offers untrained skills, which Assurance's own text forbids). The grantsFeatByChoice route exists but only for backgrounds (types.ts:1324 grantedFeatByChoice, applied at build.ts:428) and is not wired to a feat's own skillChoices. Consequence in the evidence itself: the picker was never answered, so stored.feats[assurance] carries no `choice` and the sheet shows a bare "Assurance" naming no skill.

defects.name: Inner Breath
defects.detail: The single requirement is a marker attaching "+1 hour of held breath" (and the 10-minute recharge text) to the hold-your-breath rule, in The Survivor's shape. There is no route. `RecordMarker.on` is a closed union of 'action' | 'condition' (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3207-3218), and breath-holding is neither: core.json has no Hold Breath action and no suffocating/drowning condition (the condition list runs off-guard…wounded, cursebound). The rule DOES exist as a record — `rules['drowning-and-suffocating']` — but the whole `rules` collection is dead weight in the app: the string 'rules' as a content key appears nowhere in src/ (it is only reachable if some description happens to carry a descRef pointing at it, and Inner Breath's description carries no descRefs at all). So the surface the requirement asks for would have to be built: markable rules records, i.e. `on: 'rule'` plus somewhere those records render. Nothing is stored for the feat either way (empty sheetDiff, empty registries, no `note` field). Owner decision needed: build a rules surface that markers can target, or rule that a duration change to a general rule stays in the feat's own text.

defects.name: Graveshift
defects.detail: Delivered: the once-per-day resource (limitedUses {max:1,per:'day'}, pips on the Feats tab), and the Frequency and Requirements lines survive verbatim in the feat's stored description, so they are readable where the feat is read — the note requirement is met and correctly not modelled as a checkable state. The activity entry is not delivered and cannot be today. The feat carries no `grantsActions`, but adding one would not surface it: MainTab's isActionCost gate (MainTab.tsx:224, mirrored in the harness) admits only actions/reaction/free/variable, so a timed activity is filtered out of the action list; the {type:'duration'; text} ActionCost declared at types.ts:136 is carried by ZERO records in core.json and is read only by SpellsTab.tsx:97 for spell cast times; and the exploration/downtime lists are the hardcoded ACTIVITIES array in src/rules/actions.ts, which feats cannot extend (ActivityDef even omits `cost` for exploration entries). Of the 52 feats whose text says 'spend 10 minutes', only 3 carry grantsActions and all 3 point at encounter-cost actions — there is no precedent anywhere in the app for a feat-granted 10-minute activity reaching a list.

defects.name: Seven-Part Link
defects.detail: Both requirements want the change reflected IN Paired Link's entry — the raised participant count replacing Paired Link's one ally (Principle C + Ruling G), and the 30-foot touch-range clause printed there as added text. There is no route. RecordMarker is declared `on: 'action' | 'condition'` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3207-3218), modifiesGrant.actionRider hardcodes `on: 'action'` when it builds grantMarkers (build.ts:3435-3445), and the only consumers are action rows (MainTab.tsx:525, StatDetailModal.tsx:185), condition rows (VitalsRail.tsx:1034) and spell rows (spellSituationalFor). Paired Link (core.json feats/paired-link) is a PASSIVE feat — no actionCost, no granted action — so it has no row any marker can attach to, and FeatsTab renders only a record's OWN `note` (FeatsTab.tsx:77), which is unconditional and so cannot be used to carry a clause that exists only when Seven-Part Link is taken. Nothing is authored either way (no modifiesGrant, no note, empty registries), but authoring alone would not fix it. The route would be extending RecordMarker's `on` union to feats/class-features plus a marker surface in FeatsTab. Correctly nothing: the daily-prep timing and the roster of linked allies (Ruling F), and the seven-part set as inventory. Note the ally-to-ally reach itself owes no number on your sheet either — the marker IS the whole requirement, and the marker is what has no home.

defects.name: Bless Toxin
defects.detail: The feat produces an entirely empty sheetDiff and carries no mechanical field at all. The enemy-side clause (vitality healing reduced for 1 round) is correctly nothing — DECIDED SCOPE puts effects on enemies out, Ruling E keeps HP off sheet stats, Q1 makes a 1-round duration indication-only. What has no route is the rest: the poisons in your inventory must be markable as *blessed alchemical poisons* carrying the added void trait, displayed where the item's traits are read (Ruling D), with a rank-aware value (5, or 10 at legendary Crafting) rather than a fixed string. Three separate capabilities are absent: (a) the marker channel is `RECORD_MARKERS` and its `on` union is only 'action' | 'condition' (situationalBonuses.ts:3209) — there is no item target, so no feat can put a mark on an inventory item; (b) no feat field adds a trait to an item or item category (I enumerated every key used across all 6,312 feats — nothing of that shape exists); (c) provenance is inexpressible — `InventoryItem` (types.ts:3047) has `grantedBy`, runes, designations, counters and formulas but nothing recording that an item was Crafted rather than made by advanced alchemy or Quick Alchemy, which is the exact distinction the feat's parenthetical turns on (Quick Alchemy output lives in the play overlay's day-list, not as a flagged inventory instance). The closest existing surfaces are the feat-level `note` (renders on the Feats tab, FeatsTab.tsx:77 — but that is not the item, and would carry a static number) and the item editor's Advanced section, which stars stats and is player-authored (Ruling I), not a trait-adder.

defects.name: Attuned Electroreceptors
defects.detail: The base sense lands: storedFields `senses:[{name:'lifesense', range:20, acuity:'imprecise'}]` and the diff confirms defenses.senses[1] = lifesense / 20 / imprecise. Both remaining facts have no route. (1) 'This range doubles while you are underwater, though only in the body of water you're in' — `SenseEntry` is exactly `{name, range?, acuity?}` (types.ts:300) with no note/condition field; `conditionalSenses` is NOT a general condition lane, it is strictly ifPresent-another-sense ({ifPresent, base, upgraded}) and all 8 users are low-light→darkvision or scent 30→60; `SituationalTarget.kind` (situationalBonuses.ts) has no 'sense' member; and the senses row (DetailsTab.tsx:430, VitalsRail.tsx:727) renders a bare pill with no star and no source. So Q7's shape — a `*` on the entry carrying '40 feet while underwater, only in the body of water you occupy' — cannot be stored or displayed today. This is the same gap as the granted-speed star, but for senses. (2) The subject matter is also unstateable and is currently mis-stated: the pill reads 'Lifesense (imprecise 20 ft)' and its popup is the generic glossary line 'detects the vital essence of living and undead creatures' (glossary.ts:42). This feat detects living creatures and creatures with the ELECTRICITY trait — not undead. A custom sense name would at least fall through to the generic 'see the feat that grants it' blurb, so that half is fixable within existing fields; the conditional range is not.

defects.name: Eidolon's Wrath
defects.detail: Two of the four lanes land cleanly: focusSpell (grantedSpells[0] = 'focus:eidolons-wrath', into summoner-focus rank 3 with spellSources tagging "Eidolon's Wrath") and focusPool (stored.focus.max 1→2). The choice is recorded via choice.flag 'eidolonsWrathDamage'. What has no route is the rest of the clause "you determine the damage type when you gain the feat" — the pick cannot reach the spell.
