The Spell type carries baseDamage and damageKind:'damage'|'healing' ONLY; there is no damage-TYPE field on any spell record (fireball conveys fire through its trait and prose alone), and no per-character spell override exists, so "5d6 damage" can never render as "5d6 fire". The only choice→damage-type route in the app is the kineticist's build.blastTypes, which feeds a STRIKE. The app discloses this in the choice's own note, which is the sanctioned convention for a recorded-but-uncomputed pick. Second no-route item, same feat: "if your eidolon is a celestial, fiend, or monitor with an alignment other than true neutral" — Q9 wants the picker filtered, but the 13 summoner eidolon-type options carry no creature traits and alignment is not modelled at all post-Remaster, so the app offers 'spirit' to every summoner with a caveat note (Ruling H's "stay open" shape) rather than filtering. ⚠ One point I could not settle and did NOT count against the feat: the spell is placed in the SUMMONER's own focus repertoire, while the text says the eidolon casts it "instead of you" — and the app elsewhere enforces the opposite principle (Feat.eidolonCantrips exists, per its own comment, because "putting them in the feat's own innateSpells would have granted them to the SUMMONER instead", and share-eidolon-magic's note says eidolon cantrips/innates reach your list only via that feat). There is no eidolonFocusSpells field, and the shared focus pool argues for the current placement, so this needs an owner decision rather than a verdict.

defects.name: Memory of Nothing
defects.detail: Clause: "a save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) at mythic proficiency." The app cannot express a proficiency above legendary — src/rules/types.ts:63 PROFICIENCY_RANKS = ['untrained','trained','expert','master','legendary'] — so no DC can ever be recomputed at mythic proficiency. The project's own working notes already record this (work/choice-lane/spec.json:13057: "'attempt the check at mythic proficiency' has no lane (there is no mythic proficiency rank)"). The other two clauses ARE delivered: the 2-action activity reaches the encounter action list (sheetDiff actions[0] = 'Memory of Nothing') with the whole printed procedure in its popup, and a shared Mythic Point pool exists and is spendable (src/rules/play.ts:26 MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS = 3, reset per session at play.ts:1863, pips in src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:966) — no mythic feat in the app auto-decrements it, so manual spend is house style, not a defect for this feat. Worth noting alongside the no_lane: even the DISPLAY-ONLY route is unused. situationalBonuses.ts has 'classDc' and 'spell'/'dc' targets and already ships 23 'at mythic proficiency' prose stars for skills, but memory-of-nothing has no situational entry (registries: []), so the Class DC and Spell DC rows show ordinary numbers with no marker and the player's only hint is the raw sentence in the popup.

defects.name: Blasting Beams
defects.detail: What IS built is right: the activity appears in the actions list with its full text and free-hand Requirement, and the feat grants dragon-deviant-classification (verified against the AoN mirror — deviant-ability-classification-10 lists feat-8026 as a Dragon deviation), which carries the deviantDamage choice (cold/electricity/fire/sonic) and the Energetic Meltdown backlash feature, so the ownedFeatures additions in the diff are correct, not spurious. What has no route is the attack itself. Per AoN rules-1724 (Deviation Saves and Attack Rolls) the modifier is 10 lower than the higher of your class DC or spell DC, and the damage is floor(level/2)d6 of the chosen type. The app's granted-attack lanes cannot express either: GrantedStrike/NaturalAttack (types.ts:2975, 2994) create UNARMED strikes rolled off unarmed proficiency with a single fixed die and no level scaling, and the only place a level-scaling, class-DC-based attack exists is deriveBlastStrikes (derive.ts:2890), hardcoded to the kineticist's elements. So there is no data-driven way to say 'this feat grants a ranged magical attack at class-DC-minus-10 dealing floor(level/2)d6 of the type you chose', and the deviantDamage pick is recorded but read by nothing. Two of the reader's requirements are REFUTED and should not be counted against the feat: AoN rules-1726 (Awakened Powers) states 'You don't gain the awakening unless you take a feat that grants you those benefits', so the 2-action area version and the agile-d4 eye-beam version are not owed by this feat at all — and the source's area/save are genuinely blank in the print. Only the base attack is a gap.

defects.name: Advanced Maneuver
defects.detail: Clause: "For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your fighter level is equal to half your character level." The grant itself is fine — FEAT_PICK_GRANTS['advanced-maneuver'] (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:174) = {category:'class', traits:['fighter'], maxLevel:'half'}, which correctly realizes the level-substitution as a cap at floor(level/2), and no fighter feat in core.json carries a class-level prerequisite, so that half is right. Repeatability is also right: storedFields.maxTakable=null -> maxTakes()=Infinity (featGrants.ts:330) and picks are stored per SLOT KEY (build.ts:2908, Builder.tsx:1729), so N takes give N independent picks. What is missing is the legality test itself: pickableFeats() (featPickGrants.ts:200-227) filters only on level/category/traits/exclusions and never calls checkPrerequisites — which the app does apply to ordinary feat slots (Builder.tsx:2010, 2118). build.ts:2914 validates the stored pick against that same permissive pool, so it is granted in full. Concretely, a Fighter-archetype character with Advanced Maneuver is offered and can take Improved Reactive Strike (prereq "Reactive Strike"), Combat Grab (prereq "trained in Athletics") or Improved Flexibility-gated feats (prereq "improved flexibility", a fighter class feature an archetype never gets). Q9 says the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, so the offered pool is wider than the text and the ruling allow. The picker prompt is also just "Choose a class feat" — it never states the half-level substitution.

defects.name: Earned Glory
defects.detail: Clause: "When you attempt a Performance check to Make an Impression on an elf, if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead." There is no situationalBonuses entry for 'earned-glory' (the only two hits in src are featFeatGrants.ts:59 and featGrantsAuto.ts:119), and the evidence registries list confirms it — situationalBonuses is absent. So the clause is printed nowhere the player looks up the number: no star on Performance, none on Make an Impression. Q2 requires both, and the lane plainly exists and is already used for this exact trigger 70 times elsewhere in situationalBonuses.ts. This is a degree-of-success conversion, so the star is the whole ask — it must not move the Performance modifier. The other three clauses are correct: featGrantsAuto.ts:119 {skills:{performance:'trained'}, redundantFallback:true} trains Performance (sheetDiff performance untrained→trained), the redundancy fallback is fully built end to end (build.ts:3097 detects it, pushes Character.skillFallbacks, and applies featSkillChoices['earned-glory:fallback:performance']; Builder.tsx:1670 renders the picker over all SKILLS — an unconstrained choice, as the text says), and featFeatGrants.ts:59 grants Impressive Performance as a real owned feat (sheetDiff stored.feats[impressive-performance] with grantedBy 'earned-glory'). One small deviation not counted against it: the fallback triggers whenever Performance is already trained from any source, whereas the text says "would automatically become trained" — it can also convert a rank the player spent by hand, which errs in the player's favour.

defects.name: Snare Commando
defects.detail: The reaction half is right, the Q8 marker half is absent. Right: `actionCost {type:'reaction'}` puts it in the reactions list (sheetDiff: actions[2] -> "Snare Commando"), and the stored description opens with the printed **Trigger** ("A creature fails or critically fails a save against your snare") plus the full expert-proficiency gating text, which is the whole surface principle E and gold-set answer #7 ask for; the enemy-side conditions Create a Diversion and Demoralize inflict are correctly nowhere (DECIDED SCOPE, Q4). Missing: Q8 and Ruling D say to mark the action the feat modifies, and neither Create a Diversion nor Demoralize carries a mark. `src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts` — which houses RECORD_MARKERS as well as FEAT_SITUATIONAL — has no `snare-commando` key at all (evidence `registries: []`), while `core.actions['create-a-diversion']` and `core.actions['demoralize']` both exist as markable rows. The precedent is exact and already shipped: `'fancy-moves': [{on:'action', id:'demoralize', note:"You can roll Performance instead of Intimidation to Demoralize."}]` — a feat that changes when/how Demoralize may be performed gets a marker on the Demoralize row. So a player who opens Demoralize or Create a Diversion is never told this feat lets them perform it off a snare trigger. No star is owed on the Deception or Intimidation totals (the feat grants no bonus to either roll), and the app correctly has none. The "choose one if you have both" is an in-play decision needing no builder picker, and the app correctly offers none.

defects.name: Hag's Sight
defects.detail: The text half is delivered: core.json carries `senses:[{name:'darkvision'}]` and the diff adds `defenses.senses[1].name = darkvision`. The Q13 half is not built anywhere. `deriveDefenses` keys the sense map by RAW name (src/rules/derive.ts:1645-1652, `senses.get(s.name)`), so a superseded sense is never dropped, and both renderers map over every surviving entry (src/sheet/DetailsTab.tsx:434, src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:729). The harness host already shows it: a human's ancestry vision is 'normal', so senses[0] survives and the sheet reads "Normal vision, Darkvision". Worse, Changeling is a versatile heritage, so an elf or gnome changeling (core.json ancestry vision 'low-light-vision') reads "Low-light vision, Darkvision" — the exact collision Q13 rules must show ONLY darkvision. No suppression code exists: the two darkvision paths that do exist (derive.ts:1737 `darkvisionIfAncestryLowLight`, derive.ts:1621 the battle-form rider) both ADD darkvision without removing the low-light entry. Q13 was scoped at 9 feats; none of them can be right today. No star is owed here — the grant is unconditional, per Q7.

defects.name: Faithful Steed
defects.detail: The companion half is delivered. FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['faithful-steed'] (src/rules/companionGrants.ts:68) creates an animal companion; the default config sets `maturity: 'young'` (src/sheet/CompanionsTab.tsx:161), so the YOUNG rank is carried and is the thing later advancement raises; the Companions tab offers and records the type pick. The unfiltered type list is defensible here — the text says "typically" and explicitly hands the alternative to the GM, and COMPANION_MODS carries the mount-ability wording in its note — so I am not flagging Q9 on it. What is missing is the holy/unholy clause, which is text only: COMPANION_MODS['faithful-steed'] (companionGrants.ts:215) has nothing but a `note`. (a) The Strikes half IS expressible today — `CompanionMod.strikeRider` pushes a trait onto every companion attack (src/rules/companions.ts:517, live for 'ghost touch') — and is simply unpopulated, so a holy champion's mount Strikes never carry holy and never trip a target's holy weakness. (b) The creature-trait half has no route: `CompanionMod` declares no traits field, and the animal stat block's trait row is hardcoded to animal/construct + size + maturity + specialization (CompanionsTab.tsx:657-661), so there is nowhere to record it — this sub-part is a genuine no-lane. Note the conditionality is NOT the obstacle: `sanctificationOf(c)` (src/rules/derive.ts:986) already returns 'holy' | 'unholy' from the deity's effect pick, so unlike `stealthy-companion` — which is note-only on purpose because its condition is uncheckable — this one could be gated correctly and would not over-grant.

defects.name: Basic Wilding
defects.detail: The substantive half is right and I verified it rather than assuming it. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS['basic-wilding'] = {category:'class', maxLevel:2, traits:['druid']} (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:118) is the correct filter, and src/rules/build.ts:2901-2925 pushes the chosen feat into `feats` with `grantedBy`, so it is OWNED outright and its own grants, choices, actions and stars expand through the normal pipeline — not merely recorded. Each option's description is passed to the picker (src/builder/Builder.tsx:1390), satisfying Ruling G. The empty sheetDiff is the expected pick-a-feat shape and is not a finding. The Q9 half fails: `pickableFeats()` filters on level, category and traits only and never calls `checkPrerequisites`, and that PopupSelect has no "show options not meeting prerequisites" toggle. 8 of the 17 offered feats carry prerequisites and 7 are order-gated (fire-lung/flame, shore-step/wave, steadying-stone/stone, animal-companion/animal, leshy-familiar/leaf, storm-born/storm, untamed-form/untamed). Druid Dedication grants exactly one order and the app already stores which (`choice.flag: 'archetypeOrder'`), so six of those seven are illegal for any given character — yet they are offered, and build.ts accepts and grants the pick because pickableFeats is also the validator. Contributing cause worth recording: even the main feat picker cannot block them, because `checkPrerequisites` (build.ts:5551) only enforces a has-prereq when `content.feats[slug(line)]` exists, and 'flame-order' and its siblings are classFeatures, not feats.

defects.name: Ravening's Desperation
defects.detail: Clause: "If your current Hit Points are less than a quarter your maximum Hit Points, the circumstance bonus is +2 instead." The sheet never says +2. situationalBonuses.ts:321 writes ONE entry — targets survival + stealth, bonus: "+1 circumstance", when: "while below half your max HP (more below a quarter)". Collapsing the two tiers into one entry is right (Ruling G — the upgrade replaces rather than sits beside, and it avoids the "+1 and +2 shown together = +3" misread), but the higher tier's VALUE is dropped: the `when` hints "(more below a quarter)" with no number and the displayed bonus stays +1, so a character below a quarter HP reads a stale number. The app already has the idiom for this — same file writes "+1 circumstance (+2 at 5th level)" (line 341), "+1 circumstance (+2 if master)" (350), "+1 circumstance (+2)" (413) — so the fix is bonus: "+1 circumstance (+2 below a quarter of your max HP)". Everything else is delivered and correct: a star on BOTH named skills (Principle J), circumstance type, HP stated as a fraction of the character's own maximum rather than a constant, and kept out of skills.*.modifier per Ruling B (the diff shows no change to the flat totals). Mitigating: StatDetailModal.tsx:120-131 gives each star a "Full text" button onto the feat description, so the +2 is one click away.

defects.name: Brightness Seeker
defects.detail: Three of four clauses are delivered. Augury is stored as innateSpells [{augury, tradition: divine, rank: 2, usesPerDay: 1}], reaches the innate entry at rank 2 labelled "from Brightness Seeker", and its card shows the cast as the literal text "10 minutes" (ActionGlyph, SpellsTab.tsx:97) so it does not read as a turn action; the 1/day use is a spendable pip; and Call Upon the Brightness appears in the actions list as a reaction with its Trigger and its +1/+2 status wording in the popup, which is Principle E's whole surface. What is missing is the 30-minute state: there is no mode for it anywhere in core.json's 429 modes, so grantsActions ['call-upon-the-brightness'] hands the reaction over permanently and unconditionally, where the text conditions it on the augury result not being "nothing" and expires it after 30 minutes. Q1 puts any duration longer than a round in a mode, and the app already has 88 display-only modes of exactly this shape (numbers-free, duration + note), so this is a data gap rather than a lane gap. Noting the tension for the record: Principle E says a reaction's entry is often the entire requirement, but that governs the reaction's own surface, not the availability window that switches it on.

defects.name: Assured Identification
defects.detail: The skill half is delivered exactly right: situationalBonuses.ts:2690 stars all four named skills — arcana, nature, occultism, religion, and no others — with when "when you Identify Magic" and text "critical failure becomes a failure; you never misidentify a cursed item", so both distinct promises (the crit-fail remap and the cursed-item protection) are present rather than the second being swallowed, and no computed degree-of-success machinery is invented. What is missing is Q2's second surface: "star the skill AND the action". There is no RECORD_MARKERS entry for this feat, and grepping situationalBonuses.ts finds no marker on the action id 'identify-magic' from any source — so a player who opens Arcana (or Occultism/Religion/Nature) and taps the Identify Magic row, which StatDetailModal.tsx:183 renders with a star slot precisely for this, sees nothing. The app uses this exact shape for the identical remap elsewhere: 'student-of-the-canon' carries {on:'action', id:'recall-knowledge', value:'crit fail -> fail (Religion)'} and {on:'action', id:'decipher-writing'}, and 'experienced-professional' carries {on:'action', id:'earn-income', value:'crit fail -> fail'}. Assured Identification needs the same on 'identify-magic' (which exists in core.actions). Substance delivered; one of the two required surfaces absent.

defects.name: Overwatch Dedication
defects.detail: The number itself is right and correctly restricted: situationalBonuses.ts:616 files it as `{kind:'perception'}`, "+2 circumstance", when = "on Perception rolled for initiative (also for allies inside your 30-foot overwatch field)" — Ruling B satisfied (it stays out of the Perception total), Ruling F satisfied (no ally number), Ruling M satisfied (the positional condition rides in the note, no aura model). What is missing is the second half of Q2's "star the skill AND the action". Measured on a real build (fighter 6 with the dedication): statHasSituational({kind:'perception'}) = true, statHasSituational({kind:'initiative'}) = FALSE, while explainStat(initiative).situational DOES list the +2. So the Initiative row in VitalsRail (line 648) shows no `*`, even though opening it shows the bonus — the player looking up initiative, which is the only roll this bonus applies to, gets no prompt that they have it. Cause: targetMatches (situationalBonuses.ts:3066) matches a perception-filed entry only against the perception ref, and statHasSituational (explain.ts:342) has no delegation to the underlying stat the way explainStat does. This affects every perception-filed initiative bonus, not just this feat. The aura's auditory/visual traits are not on the sheet, but they are readable in the feat's own description and Ruling M asks only for the positional note, so I am not counting that as a defect.

defects.name: Prairie Rider
defects.detail: Only the Q2 action-star half is absent; everything else is right. Delivered: Nature trained via featGrantsAuto.ts:250 `'prairie-rider': { skills: { nature: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }` (sheetDiff shows nature untrained→trained, modifier 1→23); the redundancy swap is real, not decorative — build.ts:3097 detects the already-trained case, pushes a skillFallbacks entry, and Builder.tsx:1668-1689 renders the "Already trained in Nature — replacement skill" picker keyed `<featId>:fallback:nature`; and the Command an Animal bonus sits outside the flat Nature total per Ruling B, with the correct BONUS TYPE and the restriction left open per Ruling H (situationalBonuses.ts:316, when "Command an Animal on a traditional halfling mount", bonus "+1 circumstance"). NOT delivered: Q2's second half — star the ACTION as well as the skill. `command-an-animal` exists as a real action record in core.json and action rows carry stars via RECORD_MARKERS (MainTab.tsx:525, StatDetailModal.tsx:185), but no RECORD_MARKERS entry exists for prairie-rider, so the Command an Animal row is bare. Note this is systemic rather than specific to this feat: ~2,825 situational entries vs 111 records carrying action/condition marks, and Q2 was decided today — so if this is already understood as a batch job, dismiss it here.

defects.name: Sly Disarm
defects.detail: The substitution itself is modelled correctly: skillSubstitutions [{use:thievery, forSkill:athletics, when:'when you attempt a Disarm'}]. Because it carries a `when`, skillSubstituteFor (derive.ts:394) correctly leaves Athletics' number alone, and explain.ts:322 turns it into a situational entry — but that entry's target is `{kind:'skill', detail: s.forSkill}`, i.e. ATHLETICS only. So the star lands on Athletics ('when you attempt a Disarm — roll thievery instead'), and THIEVERY — the skill whose number you actually roll for this Disarm — carries no mark at all. Ruling C / gold-set answer 6 ('a * in every skill that can perform the action, so the user sees what happens when he checks his number') asks for the mark on every skill that could perform Disarm, which with this feat is both. Second, the Disarm action row gets nothing: RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3221) has no 'sly-disarm' key, so the mark-the-action half of Q2 is absent — the action-marker lane exists and is wired (MainTab.tsx:525 recordMarkersFor(...,'action', actionId(a.name))). The off-guard clause is correctly given nothing (Ruling F, Mastermind's Eye precedent). Harness note: the empty sheetDiff here is a harness blind spot, not evidence — feat-evidence.mjs snapshots only featSituationalFor(featIds, ref) from the static registry and never calls authoredSituational, which is where the substitution's star is generated.

defects.name: Acknowledge Fan
defects.detail: The action lane is delivered — the diff inserts 'Acknowledge Fan' at actions[0] and its popup carries the full printed text (targeting restriction, the class-DC-or-spell-DC clause, all four outcome lines, the 1-minute immunity, the Special line). Per Q4 that entry is the whole surface for an enemy-condition ability, so the stunned/paralyzed outcomes and the target's temporary immunity correctly produce nothing, and I do not treat the un-resolved 'whichever is higher' DC as a defect. What is missing is the Special line's trait: the feat has either the arcane or the occult trait, and the sheet shows NEITHER (stored traits are archetype, enchantment, incapacitation, mental, visual). The pick is fully recoverable — Mesmerizing Gaze stores `choice: {flag:'mesmerizingGaze', options:[arcane, occult]}` — but `mesmerizingGaze` is read by nothing in src/, and no field exists to derive a feat's trait line from an earlier choice (modes have `addTraits`; feats do not). A `note` on the feat resolving the trait would satisfy it within an existing lane.

defects.name: Basic Hunter's Trick
defects.detail: The pick lane itself is built and the empty sheetDiff is the expected harness behaviour: FEAT_PICK_GRANTS['basic-hunters-trick'] = {category:'class', maxLevel:2, traits:['ranger']} yields 18 legal-level options, and build.ts:2914-2925 pushes the chosen feat into character.feats with grantedBy, so the pick is OWNED in full and its own lanes fire. What is not delivered is the second half of Q9 — "the builder shows only what the player may legally pick". pickableFeats (featPickGrants.ts:200) filters by category, level, and traits only and never calls checkPrerequisites (build.ts:5505), and buildCharacter validates the stored pick against that same unfiltered pool, so the feat's own prerequisites are neither shown as unmet nor gated. Concretely, this feat's pool offers Monster Warden (prerequisite: Monster Hunter) to a character without Monster Hunter and grants it silently, where the ordinary feat picker (Builder.tsx:2148-2190) dims it, disables Choose, and demands an explicit override confirmation. (Four other options — Heal Companion, Magic Hide, Snare Hopping, Animal Companion — have prerequisites the checker deliberately under-enforces, so those would still pass.) The gap is lane-wide, in the pick-grant picker, not in this feat's data.

defects.name: Offensive Subroutine
defects.detail: The situational half is delivered and correct: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:487 registers `+1 status` on `{kind:'strikeAttack'}` and on `{kind:'spell', detail:'attack'}` with when: "once per hour, when you spend your Nanite Surge on a Strike's attack roll instead of a skill check" — right bonus type, right value, correctly conditioned, correctly outside the flat total (Ruling B), and it reaches every Strike's attack breakdown via featSituationalLines in src/rules/explain.ts:1026-1040. The empty sheetDiff is a harness limit: scripts/feat-evidence.mjs only queries featSituationalFor for ac/perception/saves/skills refs, never strikeAttack. NOT delivered: the modifiesGrant half. The feat has no `modifiesGrant`, so nothing marks Nanite Surge's own entry, and Q8 says explicitly to mark the action the feat modifies. I rendered Nanite Surge's popup body: it shows neither a note that an attack roll now qualifies nor its own printed 'Trigger You attempt a skill check requiring three actions or fewer' (that line is swallowed by the same hideMeta defect reported under leading-dance), so the row the player reads when spending the surge says nothing about attack rolls at all. Low severity because the strike-level star already carries the whole explanation; only the Nanite Surge row is unmarked.

defects.name: Thlipit Contestant Dedication
defects.detail: The mechanics are right; one trait the printed text names is absent from the strike. Delivered: grantedStrikes gives Lash, d4, flail group, traits [grapple, reach]; the diff shows it taking over strikes[0] with mapStep 5 (not agile — attack 29/24/19 is correct), damage 1d4+9 B, legendary unarmed rank and specDamage 8 carried over, group flail so CRIT_SPEC.flail ('the target is knocked prone') is the crit line, and Fist correctly survives as strikes[1]. damageType 'bludgeoning' is NOT invented — the evidence pack's text dropped the word; AoN feat-5474 reads 'deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage'. grapple and reach both render as clickable InfoTerms on the strike row (MainTab.tsx:396) with real glossary text ('this weapon strikes creatures up to 10 feet away… extending your reach' / 'you can use this weapon to Grapple with Athletics'), so neither is an inert label. THE DEFECT: the text says 'a lash melee UNARMED attack', but the granted strike does not carry the `unarmed` trait — derive.ts:3203 defaults to ['unarmed'] only when the record's traits array is EMPTY, so authoring ['grapple','reach'] suppressed it. The player sees 'grapple · reach' where the Fist beside it reads 'agile · finesse · nonlethal · unarmed'. 112 of the 115 grantedStrikes in core.json carry `unarmed`; this is one of only three that do not (the others are slag-may's Claw and mind-projectiles). Display-only in effect — the natural-attack path passes unarmed:true unconditionally, so handwraps runes, unarmed proficiency and spec damage all still apply, and no critSpecWeapons entry keys on the 'unarmed' trait. Fix is one word in the data: add 'unarmed' to grantedStrikes[0].traits.

defects.name: Elver Pet
defects.detail: Almost everything is delivered and delivered well: featFeatGrants gives the Pet general feat (sheetDiff stored.feats[pet].grantedBy = elver-pet), FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['elver-pet'] creates the eel as a familiar-kind companion with lockedAbilities ['fast-movement','damage-avoidance'] and supersedes:['pet'] so the plain Pet grant does not double-show, and companions.ts:636 implements the aquatic clause properly — land Speed replaced (not supplemented) by 'swim 40 feet (aquatic — breathes water, not air)', with Fast Movement raising the base 25→40. The gap is the one value the text pins down: 'the Damage Avoidance familiar ability FOR REFLEX SAVES'. Damage Avoidance's own record reads 'Choose one type of save…', and nothing anywhere records Reflex — not the locked-ability list (a bare id), not the grant's note ('…with Fast Movement and Damage Avoidance in place of the usual chosen pet abilities'), and there is no per-ability save field on FamiliarAbility. The companion card therefore shows Damage Avoidance with no save attached. Secondary, lower-value point: the acquired `aquatic` creature trait shows only inside the Speed string and the note, not as a trait chip beside Minion/Tiny in FamiliarBlockView (Q6's 'record acquired creature traits'). The open ability picker is NOT reported as a defect — the note states the substitution and the picker is uncapped by design.

defects.name: Fiery Rebirth
defects.detail: The mechanics are right: the free action is added to the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0] = Fiery Rebirth, ahead of Reactive Strike) with its Trigger in the popup, nothing suppresses it at 0 HP (actionGates.ts gates only on rage/panache/hunt-prey/psyche), and Mythic Points are a real spendable pool on the sheet (play.ts mythicPoints clamped to MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS, reset per session, rendered as clickable pips in VitalsRail.tsx:967). The defect is in the stored description, which is this feat's ONLY surface. AoN feat-8007 (the pristine mirror at C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-8007.json) reads '…dealing fire damage equal to twice your level to adjacent foes, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC.' The app's public/core-descriptions.json stores '…dealing fire damage equal to twice your level () to adjacent foes, with a save against your class DC.' — the words 'basic Reflex' have been dropped and a stray '()' left behind. So the popup cannot tell the player which save the foes roll or that it is a basic save. Not a generic import limitation: 18 other feat descriptions and 99 spell descriptions retain 'basic Reflex save' intact, and only 12 feat descriptions carry the stray '()' (self-destruct, offensive-odor, wing-buffet, regurgitate-mutagen, imperial-dragon-potion, …).

defects.name: Reactive Distraction
defects.detail: Clause: "You use Perfect Distraction, even if you were observed, as long as you end the movement of your Sneak while concealed or in a location with cover or greater cover." Requirement 1 IS delivered — sheetDiff adds `actions[3] = "Reactive Distraction"`, the record carries `actionCost {type:'reaction'}` so it lands in the reactions list, its description carries all three trigger branches plus the Requirements line verbatim, and no frequency/limitedUses counter was invented (correct — the text promises none). What is missing is Q8 / Ruling D: Perfect Distraction must carry a marker saying this feat alters it (usable on the reaction's trigger, "only while unobserved" lifted, new end-in-concealment condition). Sheet value that is wrong: `core.json` feats.perfect-distraction carries no `note` and no incoming marker, and feats.reactive-distraction carries no `modifiesGrant` — a player reading Perfect Distraction sees nothing. The lane exists (`modifiesGrant`, applied at src/rules/build.ts:3421) but is used by exactly 2 records app-wide (splinter-faith, draconic-paragon), so this is the Ruling-D marker backlog rather than a one-off.

defects.name: Bone Caller
defects.detail: Two of three requirements land. Both spells are granted correctly — innateSpells carries animal-messenger and marvelous-mount, each tradition:'primal', rank 2 (both spells' true base rank), usesPerDay 1 — and the sheet renders them in the 'Innate spells (Primal)' section as two cards reading 'rank 2 · 1/day · from Bone Caller', each with its OWN pip (SpellsTab.tsx:1785, toggleInnateCast keys on entryId:spellId), so spending Animal Messenger genuinely leaves Marvelous Mount available. What is missing is the note lane: 'The animal messenger is always a Tiny dinosaur or lizard, and your innate spell transforms it from bones to flesh, even if there are no dinosaurs or lizards nearby.' This is not flavour — it lifts the base spell's requirement that a suitable animal be present — and Principle C puts it on the spell entry. The feat carries no `note`, no `modifiesGrant`, and the exact route for this (SPELL_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371, which spellSituationalFor feeds to every SpellCard's `marks`) has no animal-messenger key; it holds only 3 entries app-wide. The player opening Animal Messenger from the Spells page reads the unmodified spell and sees only the words 'from Bone Caller' as plain meta text.

defects.name: Dualistic Synergy
defects.detail: The skill half is exactly right: FEAT_SITUATIONAL['dualistic-synergy'] (situationalBonuses.ts:574) targets {kind:'skill', detail:'all'}, so all 16 skills show a star reading when='on a Recall Knowledge check made right after you Cast an arcane Spell from a spell slot', bonus='+1 status (+2 if the spell is 7th rank or higher)' — correct type (status, not circumstance), correct condition (arcane, from a slot, after the cast), and both tiers stated conditionally rather than collapsed to one number. The feat also reaches the action list with its full text, so the primal temp-HP clause and the halcyon clause are legible where it is invoked, and no number is invented for them (Q1 + Ruling E). The gap is Q2's other half — 'Both: star the skill AND the action.' The Recall Knowledge action row carries no mark: 'dualistic-synergy' has no RECORD_MARKERS entry, and only 2 records in the app mark id:'recall-knowledge' (streetwise, student-of-the-canon). Note this is a pattern, not a one-off — the peer feat combat-assessment (situationalBonuses.ts:150) is shaped identically and also stars skills only — so a fix here is a sweep over every action-named situational bonus rather than one row.

defects.name: Warden's Focus
defects.detail: The computed half is correct and should not be reported as a defect: core.json carries `refocusRestore: 'all'`, build.ts:3339-3348 applies it with best-offer-wins, and the Spells-tab Refocus control restores every spent point regardless of pool size (SpellsTab.tsx:1681-1685 — a set/replace, not a +N) with its tooltip replacing the default: 'Refocus (refill your pool — Warden's Focus)'. The empty sheetDiff is a harness artifact, not inertness: the host is a plain 20th-level ranger with no warden spells, so no focus pool is built and `if (focus)` at build.ts:3339 never runs. What is missing is the Ruling G / Q8 half on the entry the feat modifies: the Refocus activity row still reads 'Spend 10 minutes meditating, praying, or practicing to recover 1 Focus Point' (src/rules/actions.ts:103) with no star, no changed value and no source, so the default wording the ruling says must be replaced stays visible. RECORD_MARKERS has no `{on:'action', id:'refocus'}` entry for this feat — the same shape 'quick-unlock' uses on Pick a Lock and 'magic-hands' on Treat Wounds. Secondary: the one place the change is named is an HTML `title` tooltip, which never appears on touch devices.

defects.name: Convergent Tides
defects.detail: The feat stores nothing at all — storedFields carry only level/category/rarity/prerequisites/actionCost, registries is empty, sheetDiff is empty — so the water clause exists only inside the feat's own description. The record it modifies shows no trace of it: core.json `stances['arcane-cascade']` carries only "Melee Strikes deal +1 force damage…", and src/rules/modes.ts:252 ('cat-arcane-cascade') likewise. That is the exact shape the owner answered in gold-set #3 (Healing Sanctuary must alter Shield the Faithful's mode text even though it contributes no numbers) and principle C states it directly: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. No number is owed — terrain cost is not a sheet stat and no Speed changes — so the whole fix is one clause of text on the Arcane Cascade stance/mode, reachable through the existing `modifiesGrant` lane (build.ts:3421).

defects.name: Cast Down
defects.detail: The activity is delivered — sheetDiff inserts actions[0] "Cast Down" at its 1-action cost and the full text is in core-descriptions, so the prone rider and the crit-fail –10-foot Speed penalty correctly produce nothing else (enemy-side under DECIDED SCOPE; the degree-of-success half exempt under Q15, a flat Speed penalty not being complicated). What is missing is the Q8 marker on the two spells it names. SPELL_MARKERS (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3371) holds exactly two entries — `harm → sap-life` and `dancing-blade → the-distant-grasp` — and nothing keyed to cast-down on `harm` or on `heal`, and spellMarkersFor/spellSituationalFor (explain.ts:398) is the route that would render it. Q8 answered "yes — Ruling D's shape applies: mark the action the feat modifies", and the gold-set Lay on Hands answers are the same shape, so a player reading Harm or Heal on the Spells page should see that Cast Down applies. One authoring note: SpellMarker's fields are source/when/bonus, so a prose-only mark ("the target is knocked prone if it takes any damage") has to ride in the `bonus` slot as text.

defects.name: Resilient Shell
defects.detail: Clause "It gains resistance to physical damage equal to its Constitution modifier." The surface is on the right sheet: companionGrants.ts:284 registers 'resilient-shell' with kinds:['eidolon'], and companions.ts:855 folds its iwr + note into the eidolon block, which CompanionsTab.tsx:823-827 renders as an IWR line on the eidolon's own stat block. The empty sheetDiff is therefore expected and correct (companion ruling — the summoner's own defences must not show it). What is missing is the VALUE. The authored entry is the literal string "resistance physical (equal to its Constitution modifier)", so no number is ever produced and it cannot re-resolve as the eidolon's Con changes; the player reads a formula and computes it themselves. The eidolon's own Constitution modifier is in scope at exactly that point — deriveEidolon builds `ab` (its own array + boosts, EIDOLON_DEFAULT_ABILITIES con:3) and the block prints `b.abilities.con` two lines below the IWR line — and the same function already interpolates a computed resistance for the sibling evolution: companions.ts pushes `resistance ${Math.max(1, Math.floor(level / 2))} ${chosen}` for dual-energy-heart. So the lane to emit "resistance 6 physical" exists and is used one branch away; this feat alone stops at prose. Low severity because the correct rule is stated and the Con modifier is on the same block.

defects.name: Feathered Cloak
defects.detail: The skill half is right and the action half of Q2 is absent. situationalBonuses.ts:207 authors ONE entry with two targets — skill deception + skill stealth, when 'Impersonate a non-strix version of yourself (Deception); conceal objects on your person (Stealth)', bonus '+2 circumstance' — and the diff confirms it lands on both (situational.deception[feathered-cloak] and situational.stealth[feathered-cloak], +2 circumstance each). Ruling B is honoured: it sits in `situational`, not in the Deception total. Missing is Q2's other half ('Both — star the skill AND the action'): neither `impersonate` nor `conceal-an-object` carries a RECORD_MARKERS entry, so the star never appears on the two action rows the text names, both of which exist in content.actions and already render markers in StatDetailModal's 'Actions you can take'. Note this is systemic rather than particular to this feat — 2,825 situational entries against 109 RECORD_MARKERS entries, and canonical cases like intimidating-prowess (Coerce/Demoralize) are shaped the same way — so it should be batched, not fixed one feat at a time. Secondary, cosmetic: the two clauses share one merged `when`, so the Stealth star also reads the Deception condition and vice versa; the '(Deception)'/'(Stealth)' parentheticals disambiguate it, but the stacking rule's 'different when → show both' would author them as two entries.

defects.name: Mooneater
defects.detail: The spell half is right: innateSpells [{spellId:'eclipse-burst', tradition:'primal'}] lands as repertoire rank 7 on the innate entry with tradition 'primal', and SpellsTab renders the card as "rank 7 · 1/day · from Mooneater" with a spendable pip — the absent usesPerDay correctly defaults to 1 (types.ts:1220 "Daily castings when not 1"), and atWill is absent so it never reads as unlimited. What is not delivered is the rider: "When you Cast the Spell, the sun or moon appears to eclipse to all creatures within 500 feet of you. For 1 round after Casting the Spell, the area is reduced to dim light." Nothing marks the Eclipse Burst card — the feat has no `note`, and SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3372, the lane whose own comment quotes Ruling G, "on the spell, since that's what you're looking at when you cast it", and which SpellsTab already renders via marks={marksFor(id)}) has no 'eclipse-burst' key. So a player casting from the Spells tab sees only the bare spell; the rider exists solely in the feat's own text on the Feats tab. Q1 makes this indication-only rather than a modelled effect, and principle C says the modification belongs on the thing it modifies — this innate casting, since Eclipse Burst cast any other way produces no eclipse. Low severity: the meta line does name "from Mooneater", so the text is one hop away, and if you consider that pointer sufficient this is a non-finding.

defects.name: Needle In The God's Eyes
defects.detail: Every textual promise IS delivered: the activity is an action row (sheetDiff actions[0]) with actionCost {actions:2} and its full text in the popup, including the multiple-attack-penalty exception and the 'either horizontally or vertically' option; the Leap distance is stated as 'your total Speed' with no number hardcoded anywhere, so the Q16 hardcoded-Speed bug does not apply here; the Leap and the two Strikes are internal steps and correctly get no surface of their own. The defect is a stored field the text does not call for. core.json feats['needle-in-the-gods-eyes'] carries archetype: 'warrior-of-legend', but AoN feat-7269 (War of Immortals p.67) has trait Fighter, no Archetype line and no prerequisites, and the Warrior of Legend archetype page (AoN archetype-286) does not list feat-7269 among its eleven feats. Consequence: build.ts:559-561 counts any feat with an `archetype` value toward canTakeNewDedication's 'two non-dedication feats from each started archetype' gate, so a fighter with the Warrior of Legend class archetype who takes this plain fighter feat can open a new dedication one feat early; derive.ts:1327 archetypeFeatCounts likewise counts it toward any perArchetypeFeat scaling. It is NOT a reachability problem — Builder.tsx:1999 hides class-slot feats by the `archetype` TRAIT, which this feat does not have, so it still appears in a fighter's level-16 slot. Bounded, not systemic: I checked all 404 feats that carry an `archetype` value without the archetype/dedication trait against the AoN mirror, and exactly two are mis-tagged — this one and spear-dancer (AoN feat-7268, also plain Fighter, also War of Immortals p.66-67, so it looks like a same-page scrape bleed). Fix is deleting the field on both.

defects.name: Billowing Wings
defects.detail: The grant is built and lands on the right sheet: COMPANION_MODS['billowing-wings'] (companionGrants.ts:236) gives a Gust strike (1d4 bludgeoning, range 30, traits air/propulsive/range-increment-30/unarmed), companions.ts:445 folds it into every animal companion's attack list (deriveAnimalCompanion is called per companion in CompanionsTab.tsx:1515, so it does reach all of them), AttackLine renders it as 'Ranged … range 30 ft' via attackRange's range-increment sniff, and the crit-push sentence rides the damage line as the note — the empty player-side diff is correct. Two deviations. (1) The wings condition is dropped: the entry is `kinds:['animal']` with no per-companion test, so a Beastmaster — the very archetype that gives several companions — gets the Gust on a wingless bear as well as on the bird. The code comment concedes this ('a companion type carries no winged flag') and the note says 'Remove it by hand if this companion has no wings', but nothing in the companion editor can remove a derived attack, so the instruction is unactionable; note also that companion types do carry speeds.fly (Bat, Bird), and the sibling entry 'stealthy-companion' took the opposite decision on principle ('an over-grant is worse than the gap'). (2) Wrong damage value: companions.ts:452 passes `noStrengthDamage: s.range != null`, and never passes `range` to buildAttack, so the propulsive trait is displayed but not applied — the Gust shows flat 1d4 where propulsive should add half the companion's Strength (the app does implement propulsive for the player at derive.ts:2767).

defects.name: Touch of the Sea
defects.detail: Almost all of it is right. `FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS['touch-of-the-sea']` (featCantripGrants.ts:62) offers exactly ['gale-blast','spout'] and nothing wider, the builder renders it as a PopupSelect with each spell's description readable (Builder.tsx:1784-1803), and the empty sheetDiff is the documented unpicked-grant case. Because both are rank 0, `castRank` returns 0, the pick lands in `innateCantrips`, and `innateUses` is written only for rank > 0 — so it correctly carries NO per-day pip and nothing to restore, and it auto-heightens to half level as a cantrip. `noteSrc` names the feat as the source. The defect is the TRADITION. `CantripPickSpec` has no tradition field, so build.ts pushes `{ spellId: chosen }` with none, and the innate entry's tradition is then a majority vote over `content.spells[id].traditions[0]`. Both gale blast and spout are stored `traditions:['arcane','primal']`, so traditions[0] = 'arcane' wins and the Spells page header renders '· innate spells (Arcane)' (SpellsTab.tsx:1808) for a feat whose text says 'as a primal innate spell'. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` is already honoured at build.ts:4260, so this is a one-field fix. Systemic: every pick-a-cantrip grant is affected, including the ones whose own prompt says 'Choose a primal cantrip' (wildborn-magic, first-world-magic, awakened-magic).

defects.name: Behold My Creation!
defects.detail: The tier bump itself is delivered on the companion, and the character's own sheet correctly shows nothing (empty diff) — COMPANION_MODS['behold-my-creation'] = {kinds:['animal'], maturityFloor:'nimble'} (src/rules/companionGrants.ts:261) and companions.ts:356-362 raises the maturity floor, which recomputes the companion's ability modifiers, HP, ranks and strikes. What the text conditions and the app does not: the mod is applied to EVERY companion of kind 'animal' the character owns. CompanionsTab.tsx:1515 passes `new Set(character.feats.map(f => f.featId))` when deriving each companion, and companions.ts filters only on `mod.kinds.includes('animal')` — there is no binding back to the record that granted the companion, even though feat-granted companions carry a `grantSlug` (companionGrants.ts:118). Construct companions are stored as kind 'animal' (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS['construct-innovation'], 'clockwork-reanimator-dedication'), so a character who holds both a construct companion and an ordinary animal companion — e.g. a ranger taking the Lepidstadt Surgeon archetype — has the animal companion's maturity floor raised to nimble as well, overriding the tier the player chose in Edit (the floor only raises, so it cannot be undone by hand). The text upgrades only 'your construct companion'. Note this is systemic across ~30 entries in the same table, not unique to this feat.

defects.name: Of Lions and Wyrms
defects.detail: Clause "+2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects from beasts and dragons". The shape is right — situationalBonuses.ts:295 stars all three saves (Q2's spread), bonus "+2 circumstance" is the correct TYPE, and it sits in `situational` rather than in the save totals (Ruling B). The RESTRICTION text is wrong: the authored entry reads when: "against animals and dragons (per prose)", and explain.ts:489 renders that verbatim, so the player reads "+2 circumstance from Of Lions and Wyrms — against animals and dragons (per prose)" in the save's StatDetailModal. In PF2e beast and animal are two DIFFERENT creature traits, and the feat's own description (the click-through "Full text" on the same row) says beasts. So the sheet promises a bonus the feat does not give (against a wolf, bear or horse — animal) and withholds one it does (against an owlbear, chimera or other beast). Secondary: "(per prose)" is an authoring artefact leaking into a player-facing string — it is the only occurrence of that marker in situationalBonuses.ts, and it contradicts the display-hygiene rule against synthetic markers in game-data fields. Fix is the one string: when: "against effects from beasts and dragons".

defects.name: You Can't Hide From Us
defects.detail: Clause 1 (grantsAction) IS delivered: sheetDiff shows actions[2] = "You Can't Hide From Us" (the feat's own 1-action actionCost puts it in the encounter list via MainTab.tsx isActionCost), and the popup renders the full description, which in public/core-descriptions.json begins "**Requirements** Your united companion made a successful Strike against a creature this round.\n\n---" — so the Requirements line is on screen, which per exemplar #7 (Minor Omen) is most of the requirement. The enemy-side hidden/concealed clause correctly produces nothing (DECIDED SCOPE + Q4). What has no route is the counteract clause: "Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and your counteract check modifier is equal to the higher of your class DC –10 or spell DC –10." That is a new named statistic with a per-character rank and modifier, and nothing in the app can hold or resolve it. The only formula resolver, resolveFormula/@actor substitution at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/derive.ts:1333-1366, supports @actor.level, ability mods, speeds and archetypeFeats ONLY — there is no classDc or spellDc token — and it is applied to IWR values, speeds and formula-book counts, never to prose. grep for "counteract" across src returns only glossary/flavour text and two unrelated situational notes; there is no counteract surface anywhere. This is exactly the "SpecialStatistic — a new named statistic with its own DC" row in scripts/audit/lane-gaps.json (9 records, no route). Mitigation: the formula is printed verbatim in the popup, so the player can compute class DC − 10 by hand from the Class DC already on the Main tab; nothing wrong is displayed.

defects.name: Free and Fair
defects.detail:
The record carries nothing but rarity/level/category/edition/aonId and the diff is empty — but there is nowhere for it to go. The feat's +2 circumstance bonus is to LOYALTY-based checks in the New Leadership and Pledge of Fealty activities: all three referents are kingdom-side, and the app has no kingdom sheet. There is no Loyalty statistic, no kingdom-activity rows on any character surface (KingmakerRules.tsx renders kingdom activities and kingdom-trait feats as read-only rules prose only), and SituationalTarget's kind union (situationalBonuses.ts:24-41) admits skill/save/perception/initiative/ac/attack/strikeDamage/speed/hp/classDc/spell/spellDamage/ability — none of which can name a kingdom statistic. RECORD_MARKERS can mark an action, but markers are consulted only by MainTab/StatDetailModal/VitalsRail for records the character owns, never by the Kingmaker rules page.

This is already acknowledged policy rather than an oversight: types.ts:1398 says of kingdom feats that "the answer belongs to a kingdom sheet that doesn't exist yet, so it is stored ready for one". The reroll clause (2 RP, fortune, bonus does not apply to the reroll) likewise has no star to ride in, and the 2 RP comes from the kingdom's pool, which also does not exist.

One thing that IS correct and worth not re-litigating: category 'general' matches AoN (feat-3914 has traits General + Kingdom, no action glyph), so the feat being selectable in a general slot is faithful to the source.

defects.name: Sniper's Aim
defects.detail: Two of the three real requirements are cleanly delivered; the fourth needs a capability the app does not have. DELIVERED: the activity exists as a 2-action entry (sheetDiff: actions[3] = "Sniper's Aim") with its full text in the popup. DELIVERED and correctly TYPED: situationalBonuses.ts:625 registers {targets:[{kind:'strikeAttack'}], bonus:'+2 circumstance', when:'on the ranged weapon Strike made with the 2-action Sniper's Aim…'} — circumstance, matching the text, value inline, and explain.ts's strikeAttack case runs featSituationalLines for EVERY strike so it reaches each strike entry rather than one weapon (Ruling C / Principle D), with a sourceId giving Ruling H's click-through to the full text. It also appears on melee strikes, but that is the app's documented deliberate choice (explain.ts:1076: "a target carries no weapon narrowing … the `when` clause on each line is what tells the player whether it applies"), so I do not count it spurious. NO LANE: the kickback waiver. `grep -rn kickback src/` returns nothing — the kickback trait's circumstance penalty for lacking the required Strength modifier and for firing without a stabilizer is not modelled anywhere; derive.ts reads a `strength` requirement only for ARMOR (line 647), never for weapons, though 12 items in core.json carry the kickback trait. So there is no penalty on the strike breakdown for this feat to suppress, and the app has no route for expressing a penalty being waived under a named condition. Practical consequence is mild — no wrong number is shown, and the clause is readable in the action popup and via the star's click-through — but the underlying gap (kickback penalties unmodelled on 12 firearms) is real and larger than this feat.

uncertain.name: Wukong Extension
uncertain.detail: The activity is delivered — `sheetDiff` adds `actions[3] = "Wukong Extension"`, with the 1-action cost from storedFields and the full text (including "your reach for that Strike is 30 feet" and the weapon-innovation restriction) in the popup via MainTab.tsx's `desc: f.description`. The access clause needs nothing (Q5). The open item is the 30-foot reach, and two of the owner's decisions pull opposite ways. AGAINST a further surface: mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list says "the internal steps of an activity — 'make a Strike' … only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane", and unlike Hydraulic Maneuvers (which extends a Disarm/Shove/Trip you take on a LATER action, hence a separate row needing a mark) Wukong's Strike happens inside this same activity, so the player is already looking at the 30 feet at the exact moment it matters — Ruling D/G is satisfied by the action's own row. FOR a further surface: Q8 ("Ruling D's shape applies: mark the action the feat modifies") and docs/gold-set-final.md:412 on Hydraulic Maneuvers, which reasons that "reach/range is not a number the sheet totals anywhere, so the action marker is the only place it can live" — and the route exists, since core.json actions/strike is a real record and RECORD_MARKERS accepts `{ on: 'action', id: 'strike', value: 'reach 30 ft', note: … }`. Nothing is stored for `wukong-extension` in situationalBonuses.ts today, so a player scanning the Strikes list sees the innovation's printed reach and no hint the feat exists. I will not guess which way the owner wants this.
uncertain.question: Wukong Extension is its own 1-action activity, and its popup already reads "your reach for that Strike is 30 feet". Does the 30-foot reach ALSO need a marker on the Strike row / the weapon innovation entry — the way Hydraulic Maneuvers marks Disarm, Shove and Trip with "range 15 feet" — or is a feat's own activity popup the whole surface when the modified Strike happens inside that same activity? (The general rule that would settle it: when a feat's activity contains a Strike with changed reach/range/damage, does the changed value get mirrored onto the Strikes list, or does it stay in the activity's own text?)

uncertain.name: Out of Hand
uncertain.detail: Half is clean: `grantsActions:['lay-down-arms']` puts Lay Down Arms in the action list (sheetDiff confirms), the action record exists with its own description and `aonParentId: feat-3563` tying it back to this feat. The severed limb has no surface at all — `FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS` (src/rules/companionGrants.ts) has no `out-of-hand` entry, so no minion block, no HP, nothing. What I cannot settle is whether it SHOULD have one. The limb is created by an action and reattached by the same action — not a persistent companion — and that registry's own header records two analogous cases deliberately held back: necrologist-dedication ("an activity-summoned undead HORDE, not one persistent companion") and moray-eel-mount ("a Bonded-Animal minion, weaker than a companion"), both "held back for a distinct model". Nothing in gold-set-answers.md or DECIDED SCOPE settles which way this one goes. Two sub-parts have no field regardless of the answer: familiar Speed is hardcoded 25/40 in deriveFamiliar (elver-pet's swim swap is a hardcoded `grantSlug === 'elver-pet'` special-case), and FamiliarBlock carries no strikes at all — so "Speed is 5 feet" and "any unarmed Strike it could have made while attached, sharing your multiple attack penalty and using your attack bonus and damage" could only ever be prose in a note/`specials` entry, never derived numbers.
uncertain.question: Out of Hand's severed limb has familiar statistics and its own Hit Points (Lay Down Arms keys off "if the detached limb was at 0 Hit Points"), but it only exists after you spend an action and vanishes when you reattach it. Do you want it as a Companions-tab card (a FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS familiar entry with abilities suppressed and the Speed-5 / borrowed-Strike text in its note — giving the player a real HP pool), or does it belong to the temporary-minion model you already held necrologist-dedication and moray-eel-mount back for, leaving the limb as text on the feat until that model exists?

uncertain.name: Realm Strider
uncertain.detail:
Two of the three clauses are delivered exactly. innateSpells = [{translocate, tradition divine, rank 4, atWill true}] → the entry lands at repertoire.4, and SpellsTab.tsx:1770 renders "rank 4 · at will · from Realm Strider" with the cast pip suppressed (build.ts:4253 sets innateUses=0 for atWill, SpellsTab suppresses pip/onPip when uses===0). So the explicit 4th rank and the affirmative at-will marker are both there. The divine tradition is honoured even though core.json lists Translocate as arcane/occult — the text's word wins, which is the right call.

The unsettled clause is the rider: "spaces adjacent to the one you leave from and the one you appear in are momentarily filled with a damaging energy … dealing damage of your realm's damage type." Nothing carries it — the record has no `note`, no RECORD_MARKERS/situational entry (registries is empty), and the spell card opens the base Translocate description, which says nothing about a burst. Two owner decisions point opposite ways here and I do not want to guess between them.

(Note for whichever way it goes: "your realm's damage type" IS a recorded value — archfiend-dedication carries choice.flag 'realmDamage' with acid/cold/electricity/fire/poison — so a marker could resolve it to a concrete type rather than printing a blank.)

The save clause ("class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher") is correctly nothing: the enemy rolls it and both DCs are already stat rows.
uncertain.question: The granted Translocate entry shows "rank 4 · at will · from Realm Strider" and opens the plain Translocate text; nothing on it says that every cast also fills the adjacent spaces with your realm's damage type. DECIDED SCOPE says battlefield/enemy damage gets no surface on your sheet, but principle A/C says the record a feat modifies needs a visible indication that it has been modified. Does the granted spell entry need a marker carrying the rider (with the damage type resolved from the archfiend `realmDamage` choice), or does "from Realm Strider" on the entry count as sufficient indication?

uncertain.name: Communal Sustain
uncertain.detail: The grantsAction half is delivered: sheetDiff puts "Communal Sustain" at actions[0], the record carries `actionCost {actions:1}` (the text prints none, so it correctly comes from the record), and the feat text carrying the 30-foot requirement and the Frequency line is what the popup renders. The ally-side clause correctly produces nothing. What I cannot settle is the Frequency. The record stores `limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}` and it reaches the sheet as a spendable use (sheetDiff `limitedUses[0]`), which the requirement reader rules out under Principle B ("rounds are not tracked, so a per-round effect contributes no number"). But the reader's stated reason — that it would create a counter that never refills correctly — is factually wrong about this app: src/rules/featUses.ts:110-137 defines SUB_DAILY = round/turn/minute/hour, excludes them from the rest-refill, and FeatsTab.tsx:437-452 renders a "New encounter" reset button beside them, with the period printed as "per round". So this is a deliberate, documented, app-wide mechanism, not a stray field: 48 feats carry `per:'round'` and 13 carry `per:'turn'` (plus 46 minute, 127 hour). Principle B was given about a per-round effect MAGNITUDE (Healing Sanctuary's temp HP), not about a frequency cap, and no owner ruling in DECISIONS.md, DECISIONS-round2.md or the gold set addresses frequency pips either way — the two readings pull opposite directions and the answer generalises to ~61 records, so I am not guessing at it.
uncertain.question: Should a printed 'Frequency once per round' (or per turn) be a spendable use pip refilled by the 'New encounter' button, as the app does today for 61 feats, or does Principle B mean sub-daily frequencies must be popup text only with no counter?

uncertain.name: Posse
uncertain.detail: The one number that belongs on your own sheet IS built and is correct: situationalBonuses.ts:543 — "posse": targets [{kind:'initiative'}], when "on initiative rolls when entering combat with your designated prey…", bonus "+1 circumstance" — right target, right type, right value, restriction in the `when` per Ruling B, and explain.ts case 'initiative' (line 701) merges featSituationalLines for the initiative ref into the initiative breakdown, so it reaches the surface. The empty sheetDiff is a harness blind spot, not a defect: scripts/feat-evidence.mjs snapshots situational refs only for ac / perception / the three saves / the skills, and never for {kind:'initiative'}. The ally half (Seek/Track/Gather Information) correctly produces nothing (Ruling F+N), and its text is in the feat's own description. What is genuinely unsettled is the persistent-state surface. Two of the owner's decisions pull opposite ways: Ruling F says a limited-time ally effect gives the activator a display-only mode 'so they can see it running' and Q11 says an effect that can be shut down is a mode (Posse must be switched on by spending 1 minute and ends when the prey dies or you designate new prey) — but Ruling M's shape, a permanent star carrying the condition in its note, is exactly what is built, and the app carries no mode for Posse (no `modes` record lists it; only 97 of 6,312 feats have one, 76 of them display-only). Secondary, and systemic rather than Posse-specific: the 1-minute exploration activity appears in no action list — the feat's actionCost is {type:'passive'} (matching AoN feat-6282, which prints no action glyph), MainTab's feat-action list is gated to encounter costs, and the exploration list in src/rules/actions.ts is a curated set of universal activities only, so every exploration-activity FEAT lives on the Feats tab and nowhere else.
uncertain.question: Posse's +1 circumstance initiative star is built and correct. Should Posse also get a display-only mode the player switches on after spending the minute — carrying the up-to-five-creatures limit, the GM-determined 'out of your presence' loss, and the 'until you designate new prey or the prey dies' ending — as Ruling F's limited-time-ally-effect clause and Q11 suggest? Or is the permanent star with the condition in its `when` (Ruling M's shape) the intended answer, with the rest read from the feat's description? And separately: should a feat that is a 1-minute EXPLORATION activity (passive actionCost, e.g. Posse) appear in an activity list at all, given the app currently lists only encounter-cost feats plus a curated set of universal exploration activities?

uncertain.name: Greater Vital Evolution
uncertain.detail: The resource itself is delivered and nothing is spurious: `limitedUses {max:2, per:'day'}` → two spendable pips on the feat row (FeatsTab.tsx:411), refilled by rest(); the count is 2, not 1. What is not delivered is placement. The pips live only on the Feats tab; nothing appears on the Spells page beside the rank rows that have run dry, and "the two spells you cast with this feat must be of different spell ranks" exists only in the feat description. There is no data lane for either surface: `recordMarkersFor` (explain.ts:367) only targets 'action' and 'condition' rows, `spell-rank-note` renders only for restricted-slot groups (SpellsTab.tsx:1492), and `SpellcastingEntry.note` is written only from hardcoded cases in build.ts (bloodrager, arcane school) — a feat cannot declare one. Studious Capacity and Divine Effusion, the two feats with identical text, are stored exactly the same way, so this is a policy question rather than a one-off miss.
uncertain.question: Greater Vital Evolution's two uses are tracked as pips on the Feats tab. Ruling D would put the mark where the player is looking when it matters — the spell-slot display, beside the rank that has just run out — but nothing today can mark a spellcasting rank row from data. Should a per-day resource that acts on spellcasting get a surface on the Spells page (carrying the "the two casts must be of different spell ranks" restriction there), or is the feat-row pip the whole surface? The same answer would settle Studious Capacity and Divine Effusion.

uncertain.name: Eidetic Memorization
uncertain.detail: The grantsAction half is delivered and correct: actions[0] = "Eidetic Memorization", full text in the popup (recreation medium, no need to understand the language, the fade-at-daily-prep clause, the one-at-a-time rule), no usage limit asserted — and AoN feat-2230 confirms "Three Actions", so the stored actionCost {actions:3} is right, not an over-assertion (the reader's "text states no action cost" is an artefact of the stripped glyph). What I cannot settle is the ongoing memorized state. Q1 says an effect lasting longer than a round gets a mode, and Ruling E case 3 says an ongoing state that changes no sheet numbers gets a display-only mode — both point at a display-only "writing memorized" mode expiring at daily preparations, with Principle I's free-text field naming what is memorized. Pulling the other way, DECIDED SCOPE's NOT-lanes excludes the internal steps of an activity and GM adjudication, and the owner's standing answer for uncomputable in-play bookkeeping is that the player remembers it. The memorized page has no mechanical consequence on any roll, unlike Ruling E's examples (fast healing, persistent damage, concealed). Nothing in the gold set settles which side wins, so I am not calling the empty state a defect.
uncertain.question: Eidetic Memorization leaves you holding one memorized page until your next daily preparations — a state with a real duration but no number attached to it. Q1 says a duration longer than a round earns a mode and Ruling E case 3 says an ongoing no-number state gets a display-only mode; but this state changes nothing mechanical and expires in play. Do you want a display-only mode (single slot, replaced each use, cleared at daily prep) with a free-text field for WHICH writing is memorized, or is this popup text the player remembers?

uncertain.name: Snap Out of It! (Pathfinder Agent)
uncertain.detail: The activity and its outcomes are delivered: sheetDiff shows the single expected change, "Snap Out of It! (Pathfinder Agent)" added to the actions list at 2 actions, and the four degrees of success plus the "DC is the DC for the effect that caused the condition" line are in the record text the popup renders. The ally-side condition arithmetic correctly moves nothing (decided scope). What I cannot settle is the Medicine surface. The app HAS the lane — src/rules/skillActions.ts SKILL_ACTIONS + skillActionsFor(), rendered in StatDetailModal.tsx:58, which lists feat-gated actions inside the skill's own detail panel; Medicine's list is Treat Wounds / Administer First Aid / Treat Disease / Recall Knowledge / Treat Poison / Battle Medicine. Snap Out of It is not in it, and neither is any other archetype feat: all 42 feat-gated entries across all skills are GENERAL skill feats (Battle Medicine, Bon Mot, Cat Fall, Pickpocket…). So two of the owner's decisions pull opposite ways. Principle D ("star every skill that could perform the named action, so the player sees it where they look up the number") says a Medicine-rolled activity belongs on Medicine, and Battle Medicine's presence shows that is the intended home for a feat that rolls a skill. Principle E / Q4 ("the entry is the whole surface — no further sheet impact") says the actions-list entry is enough, and the curated list's consistent general-feat-only scope suggests archetype feats were deliberately out of it rather than overlooked. This is a policy answer worth many feats, not one record, so I would rather ask than guess.
uncertain.question: The skill-detail panel lists 42 feat-gated actions, and every one is a GENERAL skill feat (Battle Medicine, Bon Mot, Pickpocket). Should an ARCHETYPE skill feat that rolls a skill — Snap Out of It! (Pathfinder Agent), rolled with Medicine — also appear under that skill so the player sees it where they read their Medicine number (Principle D), or is the actions-list entry the whole surface for archetype feats (Principle E)? The answer decides this for every archetype skill feat, not just this one.

uncertain.name: Disrupting Strikes
uncertain.detail: Clause: "Your weapon and unarmed Strikes gain the effects of a *disrupting* property rune until the start of your next turn… greater at 14th… The DC for the rune's effect is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher." The only sheet surface is the action row (sheetDiff: actions[0] = "Disrupting Strikes"), which exists purely because actionCost is 1 action; the popup prints the book text verbatim. Nothing else: no entry in any registry (registries: []; grep of src/rules finds no 'disrupting-strikes'), so no star on the Strike rows, no level-14 branching, and no resolved max(class DC, spell DC). The lanes for all three do exist — situationalBonuses supports targets of kind 'strikeAttack'/'strikeDamage'/'classDc', and 'dragon-transformation' already uses exactly that shape to say "the DC is your class DC" for a granted effect — so this is not no_lane. What I cannot settle is whether anything more is OWED: Q1 says a 1-round effect is "indication only", and for a feat that is itself an activated action the action row plausibly IS the indication (the shape Principle E blesses for reactions), while Ruling D says the mark belongs on the thing modified, i.e. every Strike row.
uncertain.question: Disrupting Strikes currently appears only as an action row carrying its printed text. Under Q1 ("1-round effects are indication only"), is that action row the whole surface, or does Ruling D still require a star on the Strike rows (weapon and unarmed) carrying the rune's effect — and if so, should that star state the level-appropriate version only (disrupting below 14th, greater disrupting from 14th, per Ruling G) and show the resolved max(class DC, spell DC) as a number?

uncertain.name: Growth Spell
uncertain.detail: The printed activity IS delivered: the feat reaches the actions list (sheetDiff actions[0] = "Growth Spell") carrying its stored 1-action cost, and the three shape-specific expansions (burst +5 ft, cone +10 ft, line +15 ft) plus the wood trait ride in its own description popup — which is everything the text itself asks for. The only unsettled point is the reader's ADDED requirement, an indication on the spells this feat can modify. The app has no spellshape surface at all: grep of src/ for 'spellshape|metamagic' returns one unrelated hit, and Widen Spell, Reach Spell and Conceal Spell are all action-list-only exactly like this one, so Growth Spell is consistent with its whole family. Principle C would extend to it, but unlike Lay on Hands the affected records are identified by a property (non-cantrip + has an area) rather than named, and the owner has not ruled on spellshape. Not settled by any existing decision, so I am not calling it either way.
uncertain.question: Should a spellshape feat put an indication on the spells it can modify — i.e. mark every non-cantrip area spell with "Growth Spell can expand this area", the way Lay on Hands carries a marker from each feat that modifies it — or is the action-list entry the whole surface for the spellshape family (Widen Spell, Reach Spell, Conceal Spell and Growth Spell are all action-only today)?

uncertain.name: Goloma Lore
uncertain.detail: Everything the text states unambiguously is delivered: Stealth and Survival trained and Goloma Lore trained (sheetDiff shows all three, skills.stealth 0 -> 22 and skills.survival 1 -> 23 at level 20), from featGrantsAuto.ts:154 `{ skills: { survival, stealth, 'lore:goloma' }, redundantFallback: true }`; the collision path at build.ts:3095-3101 skips the redundant grant and applies the replacement, and Builder.tsx:1667-1689 surfaces the picker offering ANY skill (correctly NOT restricted to Lore, unlike Hellbreaker's). The single unsettled point is the one the reader flagged. build.ts pushes one `skillFallbacks` entry PER colliding skill and reads a separate `goloma-lore:fallback:stealth` / `goloma-lore:fallback:survival` pick, so a character automatically trained in BOTH gets TWO replacement skills. The text only spells out the single-collision case ("one of those skills"), and nothing in gold-set-answers.md or DECIDED SCOPE rules on doubling. This is an implementation guess either way, so I am not calling it correct or spurious. (Two side notes, not defects: the trigger is "already trained from any earlier source" rather than strictly "automatically", which is broader than RAW but nets the player the same skill count either way; and the same per-collision question governs ~60 other redundantFallback records, so a ruling here settles all of them.)
uncertain.question: Goloma Lore says "If you would automatically become trained in ONE of those skills ... you instead become trained in a skill of your choice." A character automatically trained in BOTH Stealth and Survival currently gets TWO replacement skill picks in the builder (one per collision). Should a double collision yield two replacements, or only one? Your answer also settles the roughly 60 other feats that use the same redundantFallback machinery.

uncertain.name: Healing Transformation
uncertain.detail: The spellshape action itself is delivered: sheetDiff shows actions[0] = "Healing Transformation" (1 action, druid/spellshape), so the player can fire it and the full text — non-cantrip, polymorph, single target, 1d6 HP per spell rank — sits in its popup. Ruling E correctly keeps the healing out of every sheet stat, and Ruling F correctly keeps the ally-facing number off this sheet. What is unresolved is the Principle A/C half: no marker reaches the character's own non-cantrip single-target polymorph spells. I verified the lane rather than the diff: SPELL_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3371, consumed by spellSituationalFor → SpellsTab.tsx:1080, the "Ruling G: a bonus that belongs to a SPELL marks the spell's own card" route) holds exactly TWO entries (harm/sap-life, dancing-blade/the-distant-grasp), is keyed by a single spellId, and has no by-trait or by-target-count selector. No spellshape feat anywhere uses it. So this is not a per-feat oversight — it is an unmade decision covering the whole spellshape/metamagic family (Reach Spell, Widen Spell, Conceal Spell, …), and the two owner rulings pull opposite ways: Principle A/C ("the record it modifies must show it", Lay on Hands shape, display deferred) says mark every eligible spell; Q4/Principle E ("the action entry is the whole surface") says the granted action is enough. I will not guess which governs a class-of-spells target.
uncertain.question: For a spellshape feat whose target is a CLASS of spells rather than one named spell — Healing Transformation applies to any non-cantrip polymorph spell that targets one creature — does the Principle A/C indication requirement apply, so every eligible spell card on the Spells page carries a "Healing Transformation can apply here" marker (which needs a trait+target-count selector added to SPELL_MARKERS, currently keyed by spell id only)? Or is the granted action entry the whole surface for spellshapes, as Q4 rules for reactions? Your answer settles every spellshape/metamagic feat in the app, not just this one.

uncertain.name: Wounded Party
uncertain.detail: Delivered: the feat is a reaction and reaches the actions list (sheetDiff `actions[2] = "Wounded Party"`), its stored `actionCost:{type:'reaction'}` gives it the reaction glyph, and core-descriptions.json carries the Trigger verbatim — BOTH halves ('You or your designated ally takes damage, and you're capable of entering a Rage') — plus a descRef link to Rage. The 'your designated ally' clause correctly produces no picker. What is absent is the reverse mark: clause 'You Rage.' Wounded Party has NO entry in `RECORD_MARKERS` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, the `{on:'action', id:'rage', …}` registry that berserkers-cloak and revitalizing-rage use), so a player reading the Rage action sees nothing telling them this feat gives a second, triggered route into it. I cannot settle whether that is owed: Principle E (Minor Omen — 'the reaction entry is the whole surface, no further sheet impact') says the current state is complete, while Q8 ('Yes — mark the action the feat modifies') and Principle H (Quick Recognition — the action appears under BOTH costs) say Rage should carry a mark. The two pull opposite ways, and the distinguishing fact — Quick Recognition has no action entry of its own, Wounded Party does — cuts against Q8 here.
uncertain.question: Wounded Party is a reaction whose effect is 'You Rage.' The app already lists it in the reactions list with the full Trigger and a link to Rage. Does the Rage action ALSO need a mark pointing back (RECORD_MARKERS: 'also enterable as a reaction — Wounded Party'), i.e. Q8/Principle H's 'appears under both costs'? Or is a self-contained reaction entry the whole surface, per Principle E, whenever the feat has its own action row?

uncertain.name: Legendary Medic
uncertain.detail: sheetDiff is completely empty and no registry carries the feat — no situationalBonuses entry, no grantsActions, no note. The whole surface is the feat's own entry plus its description text.
