Two things are demonstrably RIGHT: the per-target frequency is correctly not modelled as a single character-wide daily pip (no `limitedUses` is stored, so the player is never locked out after one use), and the outside DCs plus the GM-adjudicated +10 rider correctly get nothing. What I cannot settle is the derived `*` on Medicine. Q2 ("star the skill AND the action") and Ruling D ("the mark lives on the thing it modifies — Magic Hands marks Treat Wounds") were both stated about a BONUS on a check; this feat grants no bonus and modifies no existing action, so Ruling D has no target to mark and Q2 is being extended past its stated case. The app is silent on this shape family-wide, which reads as policy rather than oversight: Ward Medic and Advanced First Aid — the other capability-only Medicine feats — carry nothing either, while every Medicine feat that grants a NUMBER (Robust Recovery, Risky Surgery, Folk Healer, Vasodilation) does have a star. The registry can hold a text-only skill star if wanted; ~132 non-numeric skill entries already exist (e.g. paragon-benefit-regalia's "critical failure becomes failure").
uncertain.question: Should a capability-only skill feat — one that adds a NEW USE of a skill rather than a bonus to it — get a `*` on that skill? Legendary Medic (spend 1 hour, Medicine check to remove a disease or blinded/deafened/doomed/drained, once per day per target), Ward Medic and Advanced First Aid currently carry nothing at all on the Medicine row, while every Medicine feat that grants a number does. If yes, this is a family-wide backfill rather than one feat; if no, Legendary Medic is correct as shipped.

uncertain.name: Explosive Expert
uncertain.detail: AGAINST THE TEXT THE APP CARRIES, the record is exemplary: `immunities: ["splash damage from your own Strikes with bombs and firearms"]` lands on defenses.immunities as the FULL qualified string (not a bare "splash damage"), with defenses.sources attributing it to Explosive Expert — precisely the qualified-scope immunity the requirement demanded, and nothing spurious on the strikes. AND that text matches Foundry's pf2e record verbatim (.import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/ancestry/dwarf/level-13/explosive-expert.json, publication.remaster true, ORC, Guns & Gears), which is this project's designated remaster ground truth. BUT the AoN mirror disagrees completely. feat-3290 — the exact aonId this record cites — and its legacy twin feat-8795 both print: "You have continued training in volatile weapons and gained a deeper understanding. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency for simple and martial bombs and firearms." A full-text scan of all 43,686 AoN docs finds NO record anywhere containing "black powder explosions" or "splash damage caused by your own Strikes". Three signs favour AoN: (a) level-1 Explosive Savant (weapon familiarity, both sources agree on its text) + level-13 Explosive Expert is the standard ancestry Familiarity→Expertise pair, and AoN's wording is that template verbatim — compare Vishkanya Weapon Expertise, also level 13, same sentence; (b) Foundry ships `rules: []` on this feat, so even Foundry implements no immunity; (c) every other feat in this batch matches AoN word-for-word. If AoN is right this record is BOTH spurious (an immunity the feat never grants, and it is the feat's only sheet effect) and missing (a conditional weapon-proficiency escalation — the profWeapon/rankUpgrade lane — entirely absent).
uncertain.question: Guns & Gears (Remastered) p. 201: does Explosive Expert grant immunity to splash damage from your own bombs and firearms (Foundry's text, which the app carries), or the standard weapon-expertise escalation — "whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency for simple and martial bombs and firearms" (AoN's text, identical in remaster and legacy)? If AoN is right, the immunity must be deleted and a proficiency-escalation lane built; and it raises the wider question of whether other feats imported from Foundry carry text AoN contradicts.

uncertain.name: Wood Ward
uncertain.detail: Delivered: the reaction reaches the actions list with its full popup text (trigger, "Frequency once per hour", the 30-point reduction, the 3-round persistence, the difficult terrain); limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'} is a real supported cadence that refills on the encounter reset (featUses.ts:110 SUB_DAILY) rather than only at rest; and situationalBonuses.ts:477 puts a star on AC reading "+2 circumstance (standard cover)" when "against the triggering attack when you react with Wood Ward…". I do NOT read that AC star as spurious: +2 circumstance is the correct value and the correct type for standard cover, it sits outside the flat AC total (Ruling B), Q2 already establishes that a general defensive stat is a valid star target, and the registry is full of the same shape for short reaction after-effects (lava-leap, stoney-deflection, tidal-shield). What I cannot settle is the 3-round persistence: the app has no mode for it (429 modes, none for wood-ward; only ONE reaction-sourced mode exists in the whole data set, electric-counter).
uncertain.question: Wood Ward's ward persists 3 rounds when the attack misses, and can be destroyed. Q1 says an effect longer than 1 round gets a mode and Q11 says a thing that can be shut down is a mode — both point at a display-only mode carrying the printed text. But Principle E says a reaction's popup is often the whole surface, and whether the lattice is still between you and a given attacker is positional, which Ruling M says the app can never know and answers with a star-plus-note rather than a mode. The app's own precedent is on the star side (only one reaction in the entire data set ever got a mode). Which wins — does a persisting battlefield object created by a reaction earn a display-only mode, or is the reaction popup plus the AC star the whole requirement? Your answer is a policy call for a class of feats, not just this one. Secondary: if it stays a star, should the star's `when` mention that the ward keeps standing for 3 rounds, or stay scoped to the triggering attack as it is now?

uncertain.name: Rouse the Forest's Fury
uncertain.detail: Three of the four requirements are cleanly delivered. The impulse reaches the sheet as a usable 3-action activity (sheetDiff: actions[7] = "Rouse the Forest's Fury"; MainTab.tsx:255-266 lists feats with a real action cost), and its popup renders the description in full through DescBody (MainTab.tsx:660) with no truncation — the stored description contains AC 40 / Fort +33 / Ref +24 / Will +30 / 200 HP, the +30 attack modifier, reach 10 feet, escape DC 40, the 60-foot increment, the Sustain clause and the Level (20th) line, so the stat block the player reads off the entry is intact. Nothing leaked onto the character's own sheet: no tree stat block, no Strike among the player's Strikes, no HP tracker, no mode or timer for the one-round duration (correct under Q1). What I cannot settle is the level-scaling presentation. The character is level 20, so the live values are +32 and 5d10+9, but the entry shows the base '+30 … deals damage' line as body text and the 20th-level values as a trailing footnote after a horizontal rule — the player has to work out which line is live. The app already resolves this shape for spells (RichText.tsx:255 renders inline ⟦→ X⟧ heightened values), but nothing in src/ reads a '**Level (Nth)**' section, and this is not a one-off: 85 feats carry one. No lane in mechanic-lanes.md covers it (`advancement` is class tables) and no ruling in gold-set-answers.md or work/rulings settles it, so I will not call it either way.
uncertain.question: For the 85 impulse-style feats whose description ends in a '**Level (Nth)**' scaling block (Rouse the Forest's Fury: '+32 and 5d10+9' at 20th vs the base '+30'), should the action entry resolve to the reading character's level the way the Spells page resolves heightened values inline, or is reproducing the book's full text with the level line as a footnote the intended behaviour? Related: this feat's base clause prints no damage die at all ('Either Strike has a +30 attack modifier and deals damage'), so below 20th level there is no damage figure available to surface — do you want that hole flagged in the entry, or left as the book prints it?

uncertain.name: Additional Follower
uncertain.detail: Two of the three requirements are delivered — the empty sheetDiff is only the harness (snapshot() in scripts/feat-evidence.mjs derives no companions at all, so a companionGrants hit can never show). companionGrants.ts:105 grants `{ kind: 'follower', label: 'Additional Follower', note: 'Another novice follower with the minion trait joins you. Repeatable up to four followers in total — add the further ones by hand in the Companions tab.' }`; featGrantedCompanions() turns it into its own card in the Companions tab (CompanionsTab.tsx:1390), the player picks a type from content.followers (5 entries, each carrying traits ['follower','minion'] on its own record per Q6), and the grant note — carrying the printed word "novice" — renders on that card at CompanionsTab.tsx:1676. `maxTakable: 3` correctly models the printed cap of four total (Captain Dedication's own follower being the first). What I cannot settle is the repeat half: featGrantedCompanions keys off a Set of feat ids, so a 2nd or 3rd taking of this feat materialises no additional card, and the grant's own note tells the player to add those by hand instead. That reads as a deliberate, documented decision rather than an oversight, and no ruling covers repeatable grants — hence the question rather than a defect. (Separate observation, not this feat's: captain-dedication grants "a dedicated follower … novice … minion trait" in its text but has no FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS entry, so the FIRST follower never materialises at all.)
uncertain.question: Additional Follower is repeatable (maxTakable: 3), but the companion grant is keyed by feat id, so only ONE follower card appears no matter how many times it is taken — companionGrants.ts:105's own note says 'add the further ones by hand in the Companions tab'. Is that documented manual fallback the shape you want for a repeatable companion grant, or should each taking materialise its own follower card (i.e. count instances rather than treating ownership as a boolean)?

uncertain.name: Proximity Alert
uncertain.detail: Requirement 1 is delivered exactly: situational.perception carries "+2 circumstance" with when = "on Perception checks for initiative", outside the Perception total (Ruling B), and the Perception row shows the `*`. Requirement 2 is delivered in substance but not in cue. The app has a real Initiative stat row (VitalsRail.tsx:640-650) and explainStat's `initiative` case (explain.ts:701-716) delegates to Perception and concatenates Perception's situational lines, so the +2 IS listed inside the Initiative breakdown popup — and only when initiative is actually rolled with Perception, which is precisely the refinement the requirement asks for. What is absent is the star on the Initiative ROW itself: statHasSituational(character,{kind:'initiative'}) is false because targetMatches (situationalBonuses.ts:3060-3067) deliberately keeps `perception` targets from matching an `initiative` ref. Probe confirms: perception star true, initiative star false, featSituationalFor(...,{kind:'initiative'}) = []. So a player scanning the Initiative row sees no cue to click, though the Perception row directly above it is starred and the Initiative row is labelled "Perception". Q2 ("star both") and Ruling D ("the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters") point at adding the star; the code's own comment says perception-filed initiative bonuses "reach the Initiative row through that breakdown's delegation instead", which reads like a decision already taken. I cannot tell which the owner intends.
uncertain.question: Proximity Alert's +2 is filed under Perception, so the Perception row is starred and the Initiative breakdown popup lists the bonus via delegation — but the Initiative ROW shows no `*`, because statHasSituational only matches targets of kind 'initiative'. Should the Initiative row's star delegate to the underlying statistic the way explainStat already does (lighting up whenever the Perception/skill it reads has situational lines), or is the popup-only surface the intended behaviour?

uncertain.name: Extend Elixir
uncertain.detail:
Both mechanical requirements land. `modeAdjust` matches `{traits:['elixir'], minDurationMinutes:1}` with `doubleDuration:true`; `adjustModes` (src/rules/modes.ts:441) is applied in src/rules/play.ts:555 when the elixir's mode goes live, `doublePrinted` doubles the printed duration string, and the running-mode pill (src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1078) shows the doubled figure with a click-through to ModeDetailModal carrying the note that names Extend Elixir. The Quick Alchemy 10-minute cap is carried as printed text in that same note (Ruling H shape) — correct, since the sheet cannot know which vial came from Quick Alchemy. `durationMinutes` returns 0 for round-length and 'until daily preparations' durations, so a 1-round elixir is correctly not matched. Empty sheetDiff is expected (no mode active in the harness).

The one deviation: the text conditions the doubling on the elixir having BOTH the elixir and infused traits, and the match tests only `elixir`. In public/core.json 276 items carry `elixir` and ZERO of them carry `infused` (the trait is applied at Advanced/Quick Alchemy creation, not printed on the base item), so requiring the conjunction as written would make the feat completely inert. The app instead doubles every elixir mode and puts the restriction in the note ('It applies only to an INFUSED elixir you created yourself'). That means a purchased, non-infused elixir shows a doubled duration it should not have — the literal 'applied unconditionally where the text conditions it' shape — but it is also exactly Ruling H's 'stay open, printed trigger in the note'. Two decisions pull opposite ways, so I am not calling it.
uncertain.question: Extend Elixir doubles the duration of EVERY elixir mode of 1 minute or longer, including one the character bought rather than brewed, with the infused restriction stated only in the note. No item in core.json carries the `infused` trait, but play-state does track which items came from Advanced/Quick Alchemy (`infusedItems` in src/rules/play.ts). Should the doubling be gated on that tracked list so a purchased elixir is not doubled, or is the note the intended surface and the over-application acceptable?

uncertain.name: Shadow Reservoir
uncertain.detail: Only the LAST clause is built. storedFields carries a single free-text choice (flag reservoirSource, kind 'text') for "choose one source of spells for your shadow reservoir" — legitimate per Ruling I/K. Everything else is declared untracked by the choice's own `inert` string: "Recorded only: the reservoir itself isn't tracked — note down one spell of each rank…". So the reservoir's per-rank spell picks, the castable non-prepared/non-repertoire group, casting it by spending a same-rank slot (and burning the prepared spell in it), the shadow trait on those castings, and the AC-vs-Will-DC / higher-save substitution all produce nothing: sheetDiff is empty and registries is empty. I cannot settle whether this is a defect, for two reasons. (1) The app has a near-exact lane it did not use — RestrictedSlotGrant in src/rules/restrictedSlots.ts already models "one slot at every rank from N upward" (perRankFrom), "ranks up to N below your highest" (rankChoice.belowHighest), "this group consumes one of your ordinary slots of the same rank" (costsSlot, Master Summoner), an allowed-spell restriction, and per-slot notes — so the earlier note in work/choice-result.json that "no shipped lane covers any of that" is not quite true, which makes no_lane the wrong verdict. (2) There is an UNANSWERED escalation on this exact record in work/choice-lane/escalations.json asking you whether HH should "just show the rule as prose and model only the source pick" — which is precisely what shipped. If your answer is yes, the record is correct as built; if no, this is a whole level-10 feat delivering nothing. Note also that types.ts:1405 documents `inert` as "Never used to paper over a pick that SHOULD work", and lists only two agreed shapes (Kingmaker kingdom sheets, Remaster-deleted referents); Shadow Reservoir is neither, so the field is being used outside its stated contract either way.
uncertain.question: Shadow Reservoir currently ships as a free-text 'which spell source' box plus an inert 'not tracked, note it down yourself' hint. The restricted-slot lane (perRankFrom + rankChoice.belowHighest + costsSlot, as used by Master Summoner and Sin Reservoir) could model the reservoir for real: one slot per rank up to your highest minus 2, each spending one ordinary slot of that rank. Do you want it built that way — and if so, are the reservoir's spells picked once in the builder (permanent, as the text implies) or re-picked at daily preparations, and should the picker enforce 'requires a spell attack roll or a saving throw' (which no spell filter currently expresses)?

uncertain.name: Scoundrel's Surprise
uncertain.detail: The settled half is delivered: the feat reaches the action list (sheetDiff actions[3]), its popup carries the whole condition — after Impersonating with a disguise kit, before the end of your turn — and its description even ref-links "Impersonate" to the action and "off-guard" to the condition, so the player can jump from the feat to Impersonate. Nothing spurious fires, and correctly nothing models the off-guard clause (exemplar #6 plus DECIDED SCOPE: it lands on the enemy). What I cannot settle is the reader's flagged modifiesGrant question, because it turns on a policy call rather than on evidence. The facts: the reverse link does not exist — the record has no `modifiesGrant`, so nothing on the Impersonate row hints the follow-up exists; the app has the route (GrantModification.actionRider → RecordMarker, src/rules/types.ts:785) and Impersonate is a real action record that can carry a mark; and the shipped RECORD_MARKERS precedents are all feats that CHANGE the marked action's outcome (Magic Hands → Treat Wounds d10s, Quick Refugee → a successful Hide also beats lifesense), whereas Scoundrel's Surprise changes nothing about Impersonate and merely follows it. Q8 says to mark "the action the feat modifies" — and this feat arguably modifies nothing.
uncertain.question: Scoundrel's Surprise does not change how Impersonate works — it is a separate action you may take AFTER Impersonating with a disguise kit. Should a feat of that shape ("after you do X, you can do Y") put a marker on X's action row, so a player looking at Impersonate learns the follow-up exists? Or is the feat's own entry the whole surface, with markers reserved for feats that actually alter the marked action's outcome? Your answer would settle a class of feats, not just this one.

requirements.clause: "This object appears in your space or in your hand, as appropriate" … "You can spend 1 Mythic Point as part of performing this action" — the feat IS an activity, named as "this action" by its own text.
requirements.what: The activity must appear in the actions list with its action cost, and its popup must carry the full printed text — the manifestation, the 1-minute duration, the Demoralize burst, the frightened floor, the Mythic Point option and the start-of-turn save. Per Ruling E's shape for the exemplars, the action's EXISTENCE is the lane; the internal step ("attempt an Intimidation check to Demoralize") is performed by the player and needs no separate surface.

requirements.clause: "…and remains for 1 minute. As long as your sign of power remains manifested…"
requirements.what: A mode the player turns on when the sign of power is manifested. Q1 governs: an effect lasting longer than 1 round gets a mode. It changes none of the character's own numbers — everything the manifestation does lands on enemies — so per Ruling E case 3 it is a DISPLAY-ONLY mode, present so the player can see it running, carrying the full text of what it does while up (principle B: a mode carries the full text including parts the app cannot compute).

requirements.clause: "These Demoralize attempts don't take any penalty for not sharing a language."
requirements.what: A `*` on Intimidation AND on the Demoralize action (Q2: both; Ruling C: a bonus named after an ACTION stars every skill that could perform it — Demoralize is Intimidation only), carrying the waiver of the not-sharing-a-language penalty. The `when` must be able to restrict it to the Demoralize attempts made by this feat (Ruling B: a restricted bonus belongs in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, sitting outside the stat total).

requirements.clause: "You can spend 1 Mythic Point as part of performing this action; if you do, frightened creatures grovel before you…"
requirements.what: Two things. (a) A spendable Mythic Point pool on the sheet — a shared resource across mythic abilities, spent at the player's option, which is NOT the same shape as a per-day feat use; the manual has no lane for a shared spendable pool, so flag this as a possible no-lane. (b) The action must be able to express an OPTIONAL enhanced version at a cost — the same conditional-cost shape as principle H (an action whose cost changes appears under both costs, explanation in the popup), here cost-optional rather than cost-varying.

requirements.clause: "As long as your sign of power remains manifested, your enemies can't reduce the value of their frightened condition below 1." and "At the beginning of their turn, a creature that has the frightened condition from Brandish Authority must attempt a saving throw… On failure, they must Drop Prone. On a critical failure, they must Drop Prone and can't Stand this turn."
requirements.what: No sheet requirement. Both clauses land entirely on enemies — DECIDED SCOPE rules enemy conditions and battlefield effects off the sheet; they are text inside the action/mode popup only. The DC they reference ("your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher") is two numbers the sheet already carries as standard stats; "whichever is higher" is prose the player reads and reports to the GM, not a new surface (Ruling D's DC guidance concerns the character's own save DCs, not an enemy's save against the character).

requirements.lane: extraAction — NO LANE IN THE MANUAL; the nearest, `extraReaction`, covers reactions only
requirements.clause: "You're permanently quickened."
requirements.what: An always-on Quickened marker on the sheet, granting the extra action, shown with its source. Q11 settles the shape: the effect cannot be shut down, so it is a PASSIVE state, not a mode — the sheet must be able to express a condition that is permanently active rather than one the player applies and removes. The manual has `extraReaction` for an additional reaction but nothing for an additional action, so this is a candidate no-lane.

requirements.clause: "You can use your extra action only to Channel Elements, use a 1-action Elemental Blast, or use a 1-action stance impulse."
requirements.what: The restriction text must ride on that permanent Quickened marker — the player must be able to read WHICH three things the extra action may be spent on where they see the extra action (Ruling D/G: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). Nothing here is computable; it is a one-line note with click-through. Channel Elements, Elemental Blast and stance impulses are abilities the character already has; this clause grants none of them.

requirements.clause: "Make a melee Strike with your weapon innovation; your reach for that Strike is 30 feet."
requirements.what: The feat is an activity and must appear in the actions list with its action cost and full text. The popup must state that it is usable only with the weapon innovation (a targeting restriction on the action, read by the player — not a prerequisite check). Per the manual, "make a melee Strike" is an internal step of the activity: only the action's existence is the lane.

requirements.clause: "…your reach for that Strike is 30 feet."
requirements.what: A reach OVERRIDE — not a bonus — that applies to one specific Strike made through this action. Q8 settles the shape: Ruling D applies, so mark the thing the feat modifies — a `*` on the weapon innovation's Strike entry carrying "reach 30 ft via Wukong Extension", so the player sees it where they look up that Strike. The sheet must therefore be able to express a per-Strike reach value that replaces the weapon's own reach under a named condition, rather than a flat reach change to the weapon.

requirements.clause: "**Access** Tian Xia origin or worshipper of Sun Wukong"
requirements.what: No requirement. An access clause is a prerequisite line, explicitly a NOT-lane, and Q5 rules that an access clause needs nothing.

requirements.clause: "Attempt to Recall Knowledge" — the feat is an activity with a Frequency line.
requirements.what: The activity must appear in the actions list with its action cost, and its popup must carry the frequency (once per day) and the full text. The Recall Knowledge attempt itself is the internal step of the activity — the app lists the action, the player performs it; only the action's existence is the lane.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per day"
requirements.what: One spendable use per day, displayed beside the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations. This is the per-day resource shape, distinct from the situational bonus below — the bonus is not what is limited; the whole activity is.

requirements.clause: "If the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check."
requirements.what: A `*` carrying "+1 circumstance" and its printed trigger, placed on EVERY skill that can Recall Knowledge (all the knowledge skills and every Lore) and on the Recall Knowledge action itself — Q2 says both, principle D and Ruling C say every skill that could perform the named action, so the player sees it where they look up their Recall Knowledge number. Whether the bones knew the subject is GM-adjudicated, which under Ruling H means stay open — star everything plausible with the printed trigger in the note rather than narrowing it. The `when` must also be able to hold the restriction that this applies only to the check made through this feat's once-daily use (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: "You keep the bone of an ancestor or a friend to call upon for advice."
requirements.what: No requirement. Flavour — the text grants no item, and the bone is not an inventory entry, a focus, or a consumable by any printed mechanic.

requirements.clause: "You can cast Animal Form and Calm each once per day as 2nd-rank divine innate spells."
requirements.what: TWO separate innate spell entries — Animal Form and Calm — each appearing on the Spells page as an innate spell, tradition divine, cast at 2nd rank, with the spell's details reachable from the entry and Agathion Magic named as the granting source. The sheet must be able to express the rank the spell is CAST at as distinct from the spell's own base rank, so that if either spell's base rank is not 2 the entry still reads "rank 2".

requirements.clause: "…each once per day…"
requirements.what: One use per day PER SPELL, tracked independently — the word "each" means two separate single-use resources, not one use shared between them. Each use is a spendable pip beside its own innate entry, consumed when that spell is cast and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: "…as 2nd-rank **divine** innate spells."
requirements.what: The divine tradition must be legible on each entry itself. A character can hold innate grants of several traditions at once, so the sheet must not state a single tradition for a pooled group of innate spells that do not all share it — either the tradition appears per-entry beside each spell, or a pooled heading must not assert a tradition it cannot guarantee. Q12 governs: pick whichever spelling leaves the player least confused, and the sheet must not say something false about the spell. This is owed by the Spells page's display, not by anything the feat itself can carry.

requirements.clause: You gain a fighter feat.
requirements.what: A picker offering fighter class feats, and the pick must become a REAL owned feat — details surfaced and every mechanical effect it carries reaching the sheet exactly as if it had been taken natively. The text names no level cap and no sub-type restriction, so 'fighter feat' is the whole filter apart from the prerequisite rule below. This feat itself contributes nothing to any number; its entire content is the grant.

requirements.clause: For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your fighter level is equal to half your character level.
requirements.what: The picker's legality test must be evaluated with a SUBSTITUTED class level — fighter level = half character level — rather than the character's actual fighter level (zero, for anyone reaching this feat through an archetype). Per Q9 the builder offers only what the player may legally pick, so the offered pool is wrong unless the prerequisite check can run against an overridden class level. The substituted level should be legible in the picker so the player can see why an option is or is not offered. No sheet surface: this clause exists only to decide what is choosable.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another fighter feat.
requirements.what: The record must be selectable multiple times, each instance holding its OWN independent pick that neither overwrites nor is overwritten by the others; N copies of the feat must yield N distinct fighter feats. Beyond the granted feats appearing in their own right, no additional sheet surface is owed (principle K — the picks are made and re-made in the builder).

requirements.clause: Choose aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, swamp, or underground as your favored terrain.
requirements.what: A nine-option choice, recorded on the character and legible on the sheet, because every other clause of the feat is keyed to it. Forest, Mountain and Underground are three separate picks that happen to share one benefit — the pick list is nine, not seven.

requirements.clause: When in that terrain… / …you gain a second benefit while in your favored terrain
requirements.what: A state the player turns on and off, named for the chosen terrain, because the app can never know what terrain the party is standing in and the numbers below must NOT apply while out of it. Q11 settles the shape: the effect can be shut down (by leaving the terrain), so it is a mode, not a passive bonus; Q3's principle applies, that it must be plain the mode is active and what changed. The mode carries the numeric parts as real modifiers and the non-computable parts as text (principle B).

requirements.clause: When in that terrain, you can ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain.
requirements.what: No number to compute — a marker on the thing it modifies (Speed / the Stride action) carrying the clause with the chosen terrain named, so the player reads it where movement is looked up (Ruling D). Note the qualifier 'non-magical' must survive into the printed text; it is the whole limit on the clause.

requirements.clause: If you have the unimpeded journey class feature, you gain a second benefit while in your favored terrain, depending on your choice:
requirements.what: Two independent conditions gate the entire second tier: (a) possession of ANOTHER record — the Unimpeded Journey class feature — so the second benefit must be absent from a character without it and appear if they later acquire it; and (b) which of the nine options was chosen, so each option carries its own distinct grant. ⚠ The (a) shape — a grant predicated on owning a different record — is not one of the lanes in the manual; it is not a prerequisite of the feat (the feat is takeable without it), it is a live conditional on part of the feat's content.

requirements.clause: **Aquatic** You gain a swim Speed equal to your Speed. If you already had a swim Speed, you instead gain a +10-foot status bonus to your swim Speed. / **Forest, Mountain, or Underground** You gain a climb Speed equal to your Speed. If you already had a climb Speed, you instead gain a +10-foot status bonus to your climb Speed.
requirements.what: A swim (or climb) Speed whose value is a FORMULA off the character's own Speed, not a fixed number — the Wyrmling Flight shape, and it must be able to convey that (exemplar 8, Q7). Plus an either/or redundancy fallback in the same clause: if the character already has that Speed, the grant becomes a +10-foot STATUS bonus to it instead. So the requirement is 'grant this Speed, or upgrade it by +10 if it already exists', decided at build time from the character's other speeds — a fallback shape on the speed lane rather than on a skill.

requirements.clause: **Plains** You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your land Speed. / **Sky** You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed, if you have one.
requirements.what: A +10-foot bonus of the STATUS type (the type is load-bearing for stacking) applied to a NAMED movement type — land for Plains, fly for Sky — not to Speed generally. Sky adds a second condition: 'if you have one' — a character with no fly Speed gets nothing at all, so the bonus must not conjure a fly Speed nor display against an absent one.

requirements.clause: **Arctic** You need to eat and drink only one-tenth as much as usual, you aren't affected by severe or extreme cold, and you can walk across ice and snow at full Speed without needing to Balance. / **Desert** …severe or extreme heat… walk along sand… / **Swamp** You can move across bogs at full Speed, even if they are deep enough to be greater difficult terrain or to normally require you to Swim.
requirements.what: Three multi-part clauses with nothing computable in them, which must still be READABLE inside the mode (principle B): the consumption reduction is pure text; 'you aren't affected by severe or extreme cold/heat' is an immunity to an environmental effect with no number attached; and 'without needing to Balance' / 'at full Speed across bogs' are action-level exemptions that belong on the thing they modify — a marker on the skill that performs Balance (Acrobatics) and on Speed/Stride respectively, per Ruling C and D. Swamp additionally overrides both greater difficult terrain and the requirement to Swim, which are two separate exemptions in one sentence.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand
requirements.what: The feat is an activity — it must appear in the actions list with its action cost, and this Requirements line must be printed in its popup (the Minor Omen shape: the printed requirement IS the surface; the app is not asked to verify the character's hands). It also states the condition under which the stance may be entered, so it must read as a gate on the stance rather than as flavour.

requirements.clause: While you are in this stance…
requirements.what: A toggleable state — the text names itself a stance, so it is on/off, mutually exclusive with other stances, and it must be plain on the sheet that it is active and what it changed (Q3, Q11: it can be shut down, therefore a mode and not a passive bonus).

requirements.clause: …you constantly gain the benefits of the Twin Parry action.
requirements.what: The mode's content is defined by REFERENCE to another record: while active, the character continuously has whatever Twin Parry confers. Two things are owed. First, the reference must be resolved — the mode has to carry Twin Parry's actual effect (its AC bonus, at whatever value that record states, including any weapon-dependent variation) as a live modifier on AC, because this feat's own printed text states no number and naming the action alone leaves the sheet with nothing. Second, Twin Parry's own details must be reachable from the mode so the player can read what they are getting. Note 'constantly' also removes Twin Parry's own action cost while the stance is up — the benefit is standing, not something re-spent each round.

requirements.clause: Your apocalypse mount gains a fly Speed equal to its land Speed.
requirements.what: Framing for the whole feat: nothing here lands on the player's own sheet — every clause modifies the apocalypse mount, and per the DECIDED SCOPE companion ruling the correct place for all of it is the mount's own stat block, not the character's. The mount is granted by a different record, so this is principle C's shape: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing. Concretely: a fly Speed on the mount whose value is a formula off the MOUNT's land Speed (not the player's), not a fixed number, with this feat named as its source.

requirements.clause: If it already has a fly speed, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Acrobatics checks to Maneuver in Flight.
requirements.what: An either/or: the fly-Speed grant above is REPLACED by this when the mount already flies, so what the feat gives has to be decided from the mount's existing speeds rather than being fixed. The replacement is a +2 CIRCUMSTANCE bonus, situational — it applies only to Acrobatics checks to Maneuver in Flight, so per Q2 it is starred on the mount's Acrobatics and on the Maneuver in Flight action, not added to the mount's Acrobatics total.

requirements.clause: At night, or in any environment deprived of natural sunlight, your apocalypse mount gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its fly Speed,
requirements.what: A +10-foot CIRCUMSTANCE bonus to the mount's fly Speed under a condition the app cannot know (time of day / absence of natural sunlight). It must therefore be switchable or carry its condition visibly, so it is not silently included in the mount's daylight fly Speed — a state on the MOUNT, or a marker on the mount's fly Speed printing the condition. Note it presupposes a fly Speed exists — for a mount that has none and did not receive one, there is nothing to bonus.

requirements.clause: and critical failures on Acrobatics checks to Maneuver in Flight become failures instead.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success change, not a number: it moves no total and cannot be folded into the mount's Acrobatics modifier. It must be printed where the player looks up that check — on the mount's Acrobatics and on Maneuver in Flight — carrying the same darkness condition as the clause above, since it shares that trigger.

requirements.clause: You are trained in Performance.
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in Performance, reaching the skill's rank and total on the sheet.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Performance (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A redundancy test: when Performance training already arrives automatically from another source, this grant CONVERTS rather than being wasted. Two parts — detecting the redundancy against the character's other automatic grants, and then offering a free choice of any skill in its place (an unconstrained skill choice, not a fixed substitute). The wording is 'would automatically become trained', so the test is about automatic sources, not about a slot the player spent by hand.

requirements.clause: You gain the Impressive Performance feat.
requirements.what: A named feat granted outright: it must be owned in full — listed, its details surfaced, and its own mechanical content live on the sheet — not merely mentioned in this feat's text. Nothing in the clause makes it optional or a choice.

requirements.clause: When you attempt a Performance check to Make an Impression on an elf, if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success conversion with no number, under a doubly narrow trigger (Performance specifically, Make an Impression specifically, an elf target specifically). Per Q2 it is starred on BOTH the skill and the action — on Performance and on Make an Impression — carrying the full trigger text, and it must not alter the Performance modifier itself. Note the clause presumes Performance can perform Make an Impression at all, which the granted Impressive Performance feat is what supplies.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** You fail or critically fail a saving throw against a curse, death, emotion, or fear effect.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions/triggered-abilities list, with its trigger (you fail or critically fail a save against a curse, death, emotion, or fear effect) shown in its popup. This is Principle E's shape exactly, as agreed for Minor Omen (exemplar #7): the entry with its trigger legible is the surface. The printed action cost is not legible in the text I was given, so per Principle H the entry should stay where a triggered ability is found rather than asserting a cost the text does not show.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day, displayed beside the entry, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations. Same shape agreed in exemplar #10 for a once-per-day grant.

requirements.clause: You regain Hit Points. If you're a master in Athletics, you regain 4d8 Hit Points instead. If you're legendary in Athletics, you regain 6d8 Hit Points instead.
requirements.what: The amount healed is tiered off the character's own Athletics proficiency (master 4d8, legendary 6d8), so the popup must carry a value that depends on a rank the sheet already knows — the player must be able to read the tier that actually applies to them rather than a static line. Note the text as supplied has lost the base amount ('You regain Hit Points' with no dice), so the untiered value is not recoverable from this text alone.

requirements.clause: You regain Hit Points.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT for the healing itself. Ruling E is explicit that HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode; regaining Hit Points is a thing the player applies, not a stat the sheet computes.

requirements.clause: You and allies in your overwatch field gain a +2 circumstance bonus when using the Seek action to find hidden or undetected creatures within the overwatch field.
requirements.what: A situational +2 circumstance bonus that reaches YOU (the clause says 'You and allies'), so it is not ally-only and does carry a number. Per Q2 and Ruling C it must be starred in both places: on the Seek action AND on every skill that could perform Seek (Perception), so the player meets it where they look up the number. The condition — inside your overwatch field, against hidden or undetected creatures — belongs in the note; per Ruling M the positional part ('in your overwatch field') stays as a written condition on a permanent star, never a positional model or a mode.

requirements.clause: You and your allies don't have to succeed at a flat check to target a concealed creature within your overwatch field.
requirements.what: A Ruling D marker on the thing modified — the concealed condition (the same shape as The Survivor marking Dying) — saying the DC 5 flat check is waived inside your overwatch field. It changes no stat row and creates no new generic surface; the sheet must simply be able to hang a conditional note on a game condition.

requirements.clause: When you or an ally targets a hidden creature in your overwatch field, reduce the DC of the flat check to 5.
requirements.what: A second Ruling D marker, on the hidden condition, replacing the flat-check DC (11) with 5 inside the field. Per Ruling G a set/upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so this must read as the DC being 5, not as a separate '-6' line. Distinct from the concealed clause above — different condition, different rule — so it needs its own marker.

requirements.clause: ...in your overwatch field... within the overwatch field... within your overwatch field... in your overwatch field.
requirements.what: Every benefit here is conditioned on the overwatch field, which another record grants. Principle C requires the modification to be reflected in that thing: the Overwatch Field record must show that this feat upgrades what it does. This is also where Principle A is satisfied for the ally half — the ally-facing copies of all three benefits put no number on your sheet, but the player must still see on their own record that their field now does more.

requirements.clause: You and allies in your overwatch field gain a +2 circumstance bonus... You and your allies don't have to succeed at a flat check... When you or an ally targets a hidden creature...
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT for the allies' share of any of the three benefits. Ruling F: an effect landing on someone else produces no number and no star on your sheet; the wording carried by the marker above already tells the player what their allies get.

requirements.clause: While your Psyche is Unleashed, your dark persona cares only for destruction. You can Cast a Spell only if it can directly damage an enemy or object or can impose a detrimental condition or penalty on one.
requirements.what: THE SELF-FACING CLAUSE, and the one most easily missed under the frightened emanation. It is a state that can be shut down (it ends when your Psyche is no longer Unleashed), so by Q11 it is a mode, not a passive. The restriction is not computable — the app cannot judge which spells 'directly damage' or 'impose a detrimental condition' — so by Principle B the mode must carry the full printed text even though it contributes no number, and by Q3's requirement the sheet must make plain the mode is active and what changed, because while it is on, part of the player's own spell list is off limits.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You Unleash your Psyche. --- When you Unleash your Psyche, all your rage and pain... come along with it.
requirements.what: This feat does not stand alone; it fires off the Unleash Psyche action another record grants and rides for that action's whole duration. Principle C and Q8 both apply: the modification must be reflected in the thing modified — the Unleash Psyche action/mode must show that Dark Persona's Presence now comes with it (this is the Healing Sanctuary → Shield the Faithful shape from gold-set answer #3, where the second feat contributes text to the first's mode rather than a mode of its own).

requirements.clause: The force of your dark persona's negativity batters constantly against all creatures in a [emanation]... A creature must attempt a save against your spell DC the first time it enters the emanation... **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected. **Success** The target is Frightened 1. **Failure** The target is Frightened 2. **Critical Failure** The target is Frightened 3. A creature frightened by your Dark Persona's Presence can't decrease its frightened value below 1 while within the emanation.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Every part of this lands on enemies: the save is against a spell DC the sheet already computes and prints (a restatement, not a new surface), the frightened values and the can't-drop-below-1 floor are conditions on the target, and the degree-of-success table is prose. Effects on enemies are explicitly not lanes, Q4 settles that an enemy-condition entry is its own whole surface, and Ruling M settles that the emanation's extent is not a system the app owes. Note the text as supplied has lost the emanation's radius ('all creatures in a when you Unleash') — the number is not recoverable from this text.

requirements.clause: You gain the fiend and unholy traits
requirements.what: Two acquired creature traits must be recorded on the sheet. Q6 rules this directly — acquired creature traits are recorded, the Details tab already being where tags live. There is no trait lane in the lane manual's A–K table, so this is a requirement the vocabulary does not currently name.

requirements.clause: and are immune to your realm's damage type.
requirements.what: An immunity entry, but its VALUE is indirect: the damage type is whatever your planned realm's is, so the sheet must resolve the immunity from a realm already recorded elsewhere on the character rather than from a literal type printed on this feat. If the realm's type is not itself a stored, typed pick, the player must be able to state it (Principle I makes free-text player input a legitimate choice type) — otherwise the immunity has nothing to name.

requirements.clause: Your planned realm becomes a complete reality, forming within a section of Hell, the Outer Rifts, the Netherworld, its own fiendish demiplane, or some other planar space of your choosing.
requirements.what: A recorded choice of where the realm sits — a named list (Hell, the Outer Rifts, the Netherworld, its own demiplane) that ends in an open 'some other planar space of your choosing'. The open tail is exactly Principle I's free-text case, so the picker must allow an answer not on the list. This is not mere flavour because the clause above keys an immunity off the realm.

requirements.clause: If you have the Seat of Power feat, that seat of power is grafted onto your realm and the Enter Seat Of Power activity transports you to any place within your realm;
requirements.what: A conditional change to an activity another feat granted: Enter Seat of Power's destination widens to anywhere in your realm. Per Principle C and Q8 the mark must land on that activity's own entry, and it must be conditional on actually owning that feat.

requirements.clause: otherwise, you can enter and exit your realm in a similar fashion with a brief ritual that takes 10 minutes (though you can't bring anyone with you).
requirements.what: A new 10-minute travel activity that EXISTS ONLY IF you lack the Seat of Power feat — so the sheet must be able to make an action's presence conditional on another record, not merely note the condition in its text. The 'can't bring anyone with you' limit rides in its popup.

requirements.clause: Whenever you would die, you are instead reduced to 0 Hit Points, become unconscious, and are immediately transported to your seat of power within your realm. After 1 hour (or 1 round if you have the Seat of Power feat), you regain 5 Hit Points and reawaken. You can't leave your realm until you're fully healed or 1 week passes (whichever comes first).
requirements.what: A replacement of the death rules, so by Ruling D the marker lives on the thing it modifies — the dying/death condition, precisely the surface Ruling D names for The Survivor. The note must carry the substitution and its two variants (1 hour, or 1 round with Seat of Power). The 0 HP / 5 HP figures move no stat (Ruling E), and the week-in-the-realm limit is narrative text inside the same note.

requirements.clause: You are telepathically linked to these followers and can choose to speak with the group, or a specific fiend, as a three-action activity that has the concentrate trait.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list at a three-action cost, carrying the concentrate trait. The cost and trait are printed, so the entry must show both.

requirements.clause: You can either Recall Knowledge on any topic or Gather Information. If you critically fail to do either, you get a failure instead.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success adjustment (critical failure becomes failure) that must be visible where the roll is made. By Q2 that means both the action and the skill: the granted activity itself, plus the Recall Knowledge and Gather Information actions, and by Principle D/Ruling C the skills that can perform them — with the note scoping it to checks made THROUGH the fiends' surveillance, since it does not improve the character's own everyday Recall Knowledge. Principle H says keep the wording as open as the book's rather than narrowing 'any topic' to a skill list on the sheet.

requirements.clause: You don't age. ... In addition, you gain a small group of fiendish followers who reside in your realm. They never leave your realm (though one might occasionally come to your aid if you have the Marshall Fiendish Forces feat), but they constantly spy on the mortal world to keep you informed.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Ageing is flavour. The followers carry no printed statistics, never take the field, and exist only to power the telepathy activity above — so there is no companion stat block owed here; their whole mechanical footprint is that activity. The Marshall Fiendish Forces aside is a pointer to another feat, not a promise made by this one.

requirements.clause: Increase your maximum and encumbered Bulk limits by 2.
requirements.what: Both Bulk thresholds shown on the inventory must move: the encumbered limit and the maximum limit, each +2 over the value derived from Strength, with the increase attributable to this feat where the player inspects the number. This is a permanent change that cannot be switched off, so by Q11 it is a passive bonus and not a mode. Note the lane manual has no key for it — its only Bulk entry is `bulkIgnore`/`ignoredBulk`, which is an ITEM ignoring its own Bulk, a different thing from raising the carrier's limits. The flavour sentence ('You can carry more than your frame implies') promises nothing further.

requirements.clause: As long as you remain timewracked, you do not age and cannot die of natural causes.
requirements.what: No requirement. Ageless and immune to natural death are narrative facts the GM adjudicates; they touch no stat row, no track, and no roll. The feat's own text carries them. (The 'as long as you remain timewracked' qualifier is a gate on the clauses below, not a clause of its own — see requirement 2.)

requirements.clause: You're immune to hostile spells and effects related to time or aging, as well as the slowed condition (except for when you gain the slowed condition through this mythic destiny).
requirements.what: Three immunity entries from one feat, listed where the player reads immunities: hostile time-related spells/effects, hostile aging-related spells/effects, and the slowed condition. Two things the sheet must be able to express here: (a) 'time' and 'aging' are effect CATEGORIES, not damage types, so an immunity row has to accept a free-form category string and the word 'hostile' has to survive into it — an unqualified 'immune to time effects' would wrongly cover the character's own destiny; (b) the slowed entry must carry its printed exception inline (does not apply to slowed gained from this same mythic destiny), because a bare 'immune to slowed' states something false about this character — Q12, whichever spelling leaves the player least confused. Gating: if 'timewracked' is a state that can lapse, these are a mode; if the destiny makes it permanent, they are passive (Q11 — check the rules, shut-downable means mode).

requirements.clause: You reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1.
requirements.what: This is Ruling D's own worked example — 'The Survivor marks the Dying condition'. A recovery check has no stat row of its own, so the -1 attaches to the thing it modifies: the Dying condition entry / recovery-check line, value inline in parentheses, `*` linking back to this feat. The wording must say it LOWERS THE DC rather than adding to a check, since the player rolls a flat check against that DC and a '+1' printed on the roll would be a different number.

requirements.clause: Whenever you roll a flat check to end persistent damage, you roll twice and choose your desired result; this is a fortune effect.
requirements.what: A `*` on the persistent-damage flat check where the player looks that check up — the Persistent Damage condition entry — carrying 'roll twice, keep the result you want; fortune effect'. Same shape as exemplar 16's once-per-day Deception reroll: a roll-twice is not a numeric bonus, so no total anywhere changes and no stat row is owed. The 'fortune' word must survive into the note, because it is what decides whether it stacks with another fortune source.

requirements.clause: Whenever an enemy creature that you are aware of and who is within 60 feet of you gains the quickened condition, you gain the quickened condition for 1 round. The actions available to you from the acquired condition are the same as those granted by the ability that quickens your enemy.
requirements.what: Indication only — Q1 is explicit that an effect lasting 1 round is not implemented. Nothing else is owed and nothing else is possible: the trigger is a condition on an enemy 60 feet away, and the action the quickened condition grants is copied from the enemy's ability, neither of which the sheet can know. No mode, no quickened toggle, no extra-action surface, and not a reaction entry either — it fires automatically, so there is no reaction to list.

requirements.clause: Each evil creature within 30 feet of you at the end of your turn must succeed at a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC or else become Slowed 1 (Slowed 2 on a critical failure).
requirements.what: No requirement. The entire effect lands on enemies, and whether it lands at all depends on where those enemies are standing — both are settled DECIDED SCOPE, not gaps. Effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet are explicitly not a lane, and Ruling M rules that an emanation's positional question is never modelled. Ruling M's permanent star exists for an aura that might or might not include YOU; this one can never affect the character, so there is nothing on the character's own sheet to star.

requirements.clause: …a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC…
requirements.what: No requirement. The feat READS two DCs the sheet already carries and modifies neither. Ruling D's DC clause covers a feat that changes a save DC — it does not turn every feat that cites a DC into a surface. And the roll itself is the GM's: 'this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm'.

requirements.clause: …or else become Slowed 1 (Slowed 2 on a critical failure). On a successful save, the creature is temporarily immune for 10 minutes.
requirements.what: No requirement. Slowed 1/2 is a condition applied to the enemy, and the 10-minute temporary immunity is bookkeeping on the enemy's side of the table. Q4's principle — with an enemy-condition effect the entry itself is the whole surface — holds here even though this one triggers automatically at end of turn rather than as a reaction. The feat being listed with its text readable is the whole of it.

requirements.clause: Choose either natural or urban terrain.
requirements.what: A two-option pick — natural or urban terrain — offered when the feat is taken and RECORDED on the character, because the star below has to be able to name the terrain the player actually chose rather than printing both. Two fixed options, so unlike Guerrilla Dedication this is a list pick, not free text. Re-choosing it, if the rules allow it at all, is a builder action with no sheet surface (Principle K).

requirements.clause: In the chosen terrain, you can Hide and Sneak even without cover or being concealed.
requirements.what: A `*` on the Stealth skill AND on both the Hide and the Sneak actions — Q2 says star both the skill and the action, and Ruling C says a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it. The note reads the chosen terrain back to the player ('in natural terrain you can Hide and Sneak with no cover and without being concealed'). What is granted is a PERMISSION, not a number: no total moves, so it belongs in the star's `when` and outside any stat total (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or primal cantrip of your choice…
requirements.what: A pick between arcane and primal, made when the feat is taken and recorded, because three separate later clauses read it: which cantrip list is offered, which tradition's spell DC/attack proficiency is granted, and which attribute is the key attribute. It must be a stored choice, not inferred from the cantrip the player happened to pick, since a cantrip can appear on both lists.

requirements.clause: You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or primal cantrip of your choice, (as is normal for cantrips, it is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level, rounded up).
requirements.what: One cantrip added to the character and appearing on the Spells page as castable, with this feat named as its source. The picker must offer ONLY cantrips of the tradition chosen above — Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick. The parenthetical about heightening to half level rounded up restates the general cantrip rule and asks for nothing extra.

requirements.clause: If you weren't already, you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls…
requirements.what: Trained rank in the chosen tradition's spell DC and spell attack rolls — a spellcasting proficiency, not a skill, so it needs the spell-attack/spell-DC rows and not a skill row. 'If you weren't already' is a redundancy guard that must never lower a rank the character already holds higher (Q10 — apply the remap only when it makes the player better).

requirements.clause: …with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Wisdom as your spellcasting ability if you choose primal.
requirements.what: The granted cantrip needs a spellcasting statistic to compute from, and its key attribute is set by the player's tradition pick — Intelligence for arcane, Wisdom for primal. So the sheet must be able to hold an archetype spellcasting entry whose key attribute comes from a CHOICE rather than from the class, and the cantrip's attack roll and DC must resolve off that attribute, not off the class's own casting attribute if the character has one.

requirements.clause: Regardless of whether you choose an arcane or primal cantrip, you also either become trained in Arcana or Nature, or an expert in one of those skills in which you were already trained.
requirements.what: A choice between two named skills with a redundancy fallback attached — trained in the chosen one, or expert in one of them if the character was already trained. Exactly the shape flagged on Guerrilla Dedication's first sentence: a `skillChoice` plus a `redundantFallback`, where the fallback path must itself be a choice (which of the two to raise) and must not lower an existing higher rank.

requirements.clause: When you gain this feat, choose to affiliate with the Cascade Bearers, Emerald Boughs, Rain-Scribes, Tempest-Sun Mages, or Uzunjati. This grants you additional feats available to only that branch.
requirements.what: A five-option pick recorded on the character. It is not cosmetic: the recorded branch decides which of the archetype's feats the character may later take, so the feat list must be filterable by it — Q9 requires the builder to show only what the player may legally pick, which means branch-locked feats of the other four branches stay hidden unless 'show options not meeting prerequisites' is on.

requirements.clause: **Special** You cannot select another dedication feat other than Halcyon Speaker Dedication until you have gained two other feats from the archetype.
requirements.what: The two-feat dedication lock itself is the general rule and needs nothing. What is specific here is the NAMED EXEMPTION: Halcyon Speaker Dedication remains selectable before the lock is satisfied. So the lock has to be able to carry a per-feat exception rather than being a blanket rule — otherwise the builder hides a legal choice, which Q9 forbids.

requirements.clause: You become an expert in Medicine.
requirements.what: Expert rank in Medicine granted by the feat, feeding the Medicine total like any other proficiency. Q10's guard applies: if the character is already master or legendary in Medicine, this must not lower them — and it matters here specifically, because the feat's own last clause keys off being master in Medicine.

requirements.clause: When you succeed with Battle Medicine or Treat Wounds, the target gains a circumstance bonus to the number of Hit Points they regain equal to 5 HP at DC 20, 10 HP at DC 30, or 15 HP at DC 40.
requirements.what: Ruling D's own worked example is 'Magic Hands marks Treat Wounds', and this is that shape twice over: a marker on the Battle Medicine action AND on the Treat Wounds action, with the full tier table (5 HP at DC 20, 10 at DC 30, 15 at DC 40) reachable in the popup so the player can read the amount for whichever DC they chose to attempt. It must NOT be starred on the Medicine skill: the bonus is to Hit Points restored, not to any check, so a star on the skill total would promise a roll bonus that does not exist. No number lands anywhere — HP never moves a sheet stat (Ruling E), and when the target is an ally the Hit Points are theirs, not yours (Ruling F); the indication on the records it modifies is the entire requirement (Principle A).

requirements.clause: Once per day, you can use Battle Medicine on a creature that's temporarily immune due to having already been treated with Battle Medicine.
requirements.what: A once-per-day spendable use, displayed with the Battle Medicine action so the player finds it where they use it, marked spent by the player and restored at daily preparations. The popup must say what the use buys — a Battle Medicine on a creature still temporarily immune from an earlier one — since the resource is meaningless without it. Tracking the target's own immunity is not owed; that is the target's side of the table.

requirements.clause: If you're a master in Medicine, you can do so once per hour.
requirements.what: The frequency is rank-conditional: once per DAY normally, once per HOUR once the character reaches master in Medicine. So the use pool must be able to change its period off a skill rank the character may only reach several levels later, and the sheet must show the current period rather than a fixed 'once per day'. An hour is not a duration this sheet tracks, so the per-hour pool needs a refresh the player can trigger directly — it cannot ride on daily preparations the way the per-day version does.

A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger shown in the popup ("An attack or effect would reduce you to 0 Hit Points or kill you outright"). Principle E — the reaction entry with its trigger is the surface; the feat is triggered-only and has no passive presence anywhere else on the sheet.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** An attack or effect would reduce you to 0 Hit Points or kill you outright.

requirements.what: A cost of 1 Mythic Point displayed on the reaction entry, spent from a Mythic Point pool the sheet carries as a spendable, restorable resource. This is the one number in the feat that must actually move: without a pool the cost is unpayable and the entry is inert prose. Note this is a distinct resource from focus and from per-day feat uses — it is a shared pool many mythic entries draw on, so it belongs on the sheet as its own resource rather than as a use-counter private to this feat.
requirements.clause: You expend 1 Mythic Point

requirements.what: No sheet surface. The end state — conscious and standing at 10 + your level Hit Points regardless of your prior total, wounded and dying cleared, doomed not increased — is applied by the player by hand to the HP box and condition list at the moment it fires. Ruling E is explicit that HP and damage never move sheet stats, and the feat does not change how the wounded/dying/doomed rules behave in general (unlike The Survivor, which permanently modifies the Dying condition and therefore earns a marker on it) — it overrides them once. Requirement is only that the reaction's popup carry this full text so the player knows what to apply.
requirements.clause: survive the triggering attack or effect, lose the wounded or dying conditions entirely, don't increase your doomed condition, and are conscious and standing with a number of Hit Points equal to 10 + your level, regardless of how many Hit Points you had before

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list with its trigger in the popup ("An ally within 30 feet rolls a saving throw against an auditory effect"). Principle E — this is the whole surface. The 30-foot range is positional and gets nothing (the app can never know where anyone stands).
requirements.clause: **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet rolls a saving throw against an auditory effect.

requirements.what: Nothing. The degree-of-success improvement lands entirely on the ally — Ruling F/N: an effect that affects a teammate and not you does nothing on your sheet. Principle A (an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies) is already satisfied here without any extra work, because the record it modifies IS this feat's own reaction entry — unlike Resilient Touch, which modifies a separate record (Lay on Hands) and therefore needed a marker planted there. Nothing to mark elsewhere.
requirements.clause: Your targeted ally treats the result of their saving throw as one degree of success better.

requirements.what: Nothing. This is a per-TARGET lockout, not a frequency limit on you — it does not consume a use of yours, so it is not the limitedUses lane and must not be modelled as a per-day counter on your sheet (doing so would wrongly stop you using it on a second, eligible ally). Tracking which allies have been hit in the last 24 hours is player/GM bookkeeping across other creatures' sheets. Requirement is only that the clause is printed in the reaction's popup.
requirements.clause: Once an ally has been targeted by this effect, they're immune for 24 hours.

requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list as its own named entry, with its Requirements line reproduced in the popup ("You are in Flood Stance and were damaged by an enemy since your previous turn"). Principle E's shape applied to a requirement rather than a trigger. Both halves of the requirement are things the app cannot evaluate — stance state is knowable but "were damaged by an enemy since your previous turn" is not — so the requirement is that the text is legible, not that availability is gated. The feat grants no stance of its own; Flood Stance is a separate record and no mode is owed here.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are in Flood Stance and were damaged by an enemy since your previous turn.

requirements.what: Nothing. "Make a flooded river Strike" is an internal step of the activity — the app lists the action, the player performs the Strike. The feat does not grant the flooded river Strike (Flood Stance does), so no grantsStrike requirement arises here.
requirements.clause: Make a flooded river Strike against the enemy who dealt damage to you since your previous turn.

requirements.what: The extra 1d8 bleed must be visible where the player reads the damage — i.e. a `*` on the flooded river Strike's damage line naming this feat and its condition (only on the Strike made as part of this activity), in addition to appearing in the activity's own popup text. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — the player checking their flooded river Strike's damage must not see a number that silently omits this. It is `situational`, not a flat weapon rider: it applies to one Strike under one circumstance, so per Ruling B the value belongs beside the total with its restriction in the `when`, never folded into the Strike's printed damage.
requirements.clause: That Strike deals an additional 1d8 bleed damage.

requirements.what: Nothing. An access clause is a prerequisite, explicitly not a lane.
requirements.clause: **Access** You are from Absalom.

requirements.what: A skill picker in the builder offering the player's choice of skill, whose grant resolves to trained, or to expert when the chosen skill is already trained. This is the skillChoice + redundantFallback shape with a better-rank resolution: per Q10 the remap applies only when it makes the player better, so a skill already at expert or higher must not be pushed down to expert by this grant. Per Q9 the picker shows only what the player may legally pick unless they toggle the show-all option. Per Principle K the choice itself needs no sheet surface beyond the resulting proficiency rank appearing in the skill's row.
requirements.clause: You become trained in one skill of your choice, or expert in a skill of your choice in which you were trained.

requirements.what: Pathfinder Lore appears as a Lore skill on the sheet at trained, or at expert if the character was already trained in it — the same better-rank resolution as the clause above, and again never lowering an existing higher rank. No player choice is involved; the Lore is named, so this is an automatic grant, not a picker.
requirements.clause: You also become trained in Pathfinder Lore, or an expert if you were already trained.

requirements.what: ⚠ FLAGGED — I can find no lane in the vocabulary that carries this shape. Every skill in which the character is UNTRAINED must compute its total with a proficiency bonus equal to the character's level in place of the usual 0, and the change must be visible in each such skill's breakdown with this feat named as the source. This is not `rankUpgrade` (the character stays untrained — untrained-only feats and effects still apply, and "trained" prerequisites are still unmet), not `skillTrained` (no skill is named or chosen), and not `situational` (it is unconditional and applies to a whole open-ended class of skills, changing as the character's untrained set changes with level and other grants). It is a change to the proficiency FORMULA for a category of rows rather than a bonus on any one row, and it silently rewrites every untrained skill total as the character levels. If nothing expresses it, the untrained rows read as level-independent and are wrong at every level.
requirements.clause: When using a skill untrained, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level instead of 0.

requirements.what: Nothing. Q5 settles it — the inventory stays open and item rarity does not gate the shop, so an "access to <item>" clause needs no requirement at all.
requirements.clause: You gain access to wayfinders.

requirements.what: The Demoralize action's own trait line must READ correctly for this character — auditory removed, visual added — rather than carrying an annotation beside an unchanged list. Ruling G: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it; Q8: Ruling D's shape applies, mark the action the feat modifies. The traits are load-bearing rules text (auditory vs visual decides whether a deafened or blinded target can be Demoralized at all), so a player reading Demoralize on their own sheet must see the traits they actually have, with a `*` naming this feat as the reason.
requirements.clause: When you do, Demoralize loses the auditory trait and gains the visual trait

requirements.what: A `*` on BOTH the Intimidation skill and the Demoralize action, carrying the waiver of the language penalty. Q2 is directly on point — star the skill AND the action — and Ruling C requires starring every skill that could perform the named action, which for Demoralize is Intimidation alone. The note must convey what it removes (the −4 circumstance penalty the general Demoralize rules impose when the target does not understand your language); it is a removal of a penalty that only ever applies in a specific circumstance, so per Ruling B it belongs in `situational` with the circumstance in its `when` and must NOT be added into the Intimidation total.
requirements.clause: and you don't take a penalty if the creature doesn't understand your language

requirements.what: Nothing. "You can Demoralize with a mere glare" is a restatement in flavour of the trait swap in the same sentence; it grants no new action — the character already has Demoralize — so no grantsAction requirement arises.
requirements.clause: You can Demoralize with a mere glare.
**Requirements** Your united companion made a successful Strike against a creature this round. --- ... Strike the same creature that your united companion hit.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a named activity, so it must appear in the actions list with its Requirements line ("your united companion made a successful Strike against a creature this round") shown in its popup. The requirement is a battlefield state the sheet can never know, so it is printed text, not a gate. This is the same shape as Minor Omen (exemplar #7): the entry plus its trigger/requirement text in the popup is most of the whole requirement. The inner "Strike the same creature" is an internal step of the activity — the player performs it; only the activity's existence is a lane.

requirements.clause: you can immediately attempt to counteract the effect. Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and your counteract check modifier is equal to the higher of your class DC –10 or spell DC –10.
requirements.what: A counteract check whose rank and modifier are FORMULAS off the character's own numbers — rank = ceil(level ÷ 2), modifier = max(class DC, spell DC) − 10 — and which correspond to no existing roll on the sheet. The sheet must be able to resolve those two values against the actual character and show them inside the action's popup, not print the raw formula. Same failure mode Q16 flagged for Constant Levitation's hardcoded fly 40: a character-derived value that is not actually derived is wrong for every character it does not happen to fit. If it is not resolved, the player has to compute a bespoke modifier that exists nowhere else on the sheet.

requirements.clause: the targeted creature ... can't become hidden or concealed to you and your companion for 1 minute or until it moves more than 60 feet away from either you or your companion
requirements.what: No requirement. This lands on the enemy, and DECIDED SCOPE rules effects on enemies out; Q4 settles the shape — the action entry is the whole surface, its text already tells the player what the target loses. The 1-minute duration does not pull it into Q1's mode rule either, because the thing that would run for a minute is a condition on someone else's creature, not a state of your own numbers. No mode, no star, no pill.

requirements.clause: When you apply a simple poison with Poison Weapon, the poison deals 4d4 damage instead of 1d4 poison damage.
requirements.what: This feat changes a value another record already granted, so principle C applies: it must be reflected IN that thing. The Poison Weapon action's own damage must read 4d4 with a `*` back to this feat. Ruling G governs the shape — a set/upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, and the text says "instead of", so the sheet must be able to show 4d4 in place of 1d4, not "1d4 (+4d4)" or two lines. A player who reads Poison Weapon and still sees 1d4 has been told something false.

requirements.clause: When you apply an injury poison to your weapon, the DC to resist that poison increases by 2, to a maximum of your class DC.
