requirements.what: A second, wider promise: it covers ANY injury poison you apply to a weapon, not only the simple poison of clause 1. Ruling D shapes it — a value with no stat row of its own attaches to the thing it modifies, value inline, `*` to the source. So a marker on the Poison Weapon action AND on injury poisons in the inventory (Ruling H: where the rules are open, star everything plausible rather than narrowing it to one). Note the cap is character-derived: "to a maximum of your class DC" means the sheet must be able to resolve the character's class DC to state the ceiling, otherwise the +2 is printed unbounded and is wrong at low levels. This is a DC an opponent rolls against, not one of the character's own saves, so Ruling D's save-DC-breakdown route does not apply and no save row is owed.

requirements.clause: Your eidolon can fly. It gains a fly Speed equal to its Speed.
requirements.what: A fly Speed on the EIDOLON'S stat block, equal to the eidolon's own Speed, with a `*` carrying the feat's details. Two things follow from the rulings. (a) The ★ Companions ruling puts this on the companion, not on you — absence from the character's own Speed row is correct, and the companion stat block must therefore be able to carry a movement type of its own. (b) Exemplar #8 (Wyrmling Flight) is the same sentence one body over: the value is a formula off a Speed, and a bare hardcoded number cannot convey that (Q7, and the Q16 bug where fly 40 was baked in). So what must be expressible is a derived fly Speed that tracks the eidolon's land Speed, plus the star. "Your eidolon can fly" is a restatement of the second sentence, not a separate clause.

requirements.clause: You unleash a small, localized tremor in a within 30 feet. Each creature in the area takes damage with a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list carrying its range/area (within 30 feet) and its damage, with the save resolved against the character's actual class DC rather than printing the words "your class DC" — the number the opponent rolls against is a stat the character already has, and the player should not have to go fetch it mid-action. (The printed damage die is missing from the text as given; only the fact that it deals damage on a save is supported here, so I state no die value.)

requirements.clause: **Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d8.
requirements.what: The action's damage SCALES with the character's level (+1d8 per 2 levels), so the entry must be able to show the value for this character at this level, not the base value with a heightening line the player has to apply by hand. This is the second promise of the feat and the one most easily missed: a granted action whose numbers move as the character advances. If the sheet can only store a fixed damage expression on a granted action, this clause has no route.

requirements.clause: A creature that critically fails is knocked prone. Earth and stone in the area is difficult terrain until the start of your next turn.
requirements.what: No requirement, on both counts. The prone condition lands on an enemy (DECIDED SCOPE: effects on enemies are not lanes; Q4 — the action entry is the whole surface), and the difficult terrain is a battlefield effect the app has no position model for and by Ruling M never should. Both are already stated in the action's own text, which is where the player reads them.

requirements.clause: Each time you succeed at a Fortitude save against an ongoing poison, you reduce its stage by 2, or by 1 against a virulent poison.
requirements.what: A `*` on FORTITUDE carrying this text. Q2 settles the target: when a clause attaches to saves you star the save itself, and this one names Fortitude specifically, so it is Fortitude alone — not all three. The mark contributes NO number: it changes what a success does, not the modifier you roll, so per Ruling B a restricted, non-numeric clause belongs in the situational note and correctly sits outside the Fortitude total. The star must be able to carry the virulent-vs-ordinary split (2 vs 1) in its text, since the app cannot know which poison is on you.

requirements.clause: Each critical success you achieve against an ongoing poison reduces its stage by 3, or by 2 against a virulent poison.
requirements.what: No separate surface. Q15 governs the crit-trigger shape and comes first: an effect that fires on a critical success needs no implementation unless the effect is COMPLICATED, and a larger stage reduction is not complicated — it is the same operation with a bigger number. The clause rides in the text of the Fortitude star from the previous clause so the player still reads it. Explicitly do NOT propose a degree-of-success surface for this; the owner refused one for Minor Omen on identical grounds.

Magnetic Attraction appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, primal, cast at 2nd rank. The rank is stated by the feat rather than inherited from the spell, so "2nd rank" must be legible on the entry itself, and the tradition (primal) must be legible where the player reads THIS spell — not asserted only by a pooled section header that could be describing a different grant (the Q12 rule that the sheet must not state something false). The granting source must be nameable from the entry.
requirements.clause: You can cast Magnetic Attraction ... once per day each as 2nd-rank primal innate spells.

requirements.what: Magnetic Repulsion appears as a second, independent INNATE spell entry — primal, 2nd rank, same display requirements. Listed separately because the feat makes two distinct grants and either one could be present while the other is missing; a single combined entry would not express both.
requirements.clause: You can cast Magnetic Attraction and Magnetic Repulsion once per day each as 2nd-rank primal innate spells.

requirements.what: One use per day for EACH spell — two independent spendable uses, not one shared pool. Spending Magnetic Attraction must leave Magnetic Repulsion available. Each use is consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: once per day each

requirements.what: A choice that replaces ONE of the two granted spells with Enthrall. The replacement takes the slot it vacates — Enthrall becomes a 2nd-rank primal innate spell usable once per day, and the replaced spell disappears from the list rather than sitting alongside it. Per Q9 the option is offered only to a character who took the gildedsoul lineage (unless "show options not meeting prerequisites" is on), so the picker must be able to gate on an earlier lineage pick, and the choice must name which of the two spells is being given up.
requirements.clause: **Special** If you chose the gildedsoul lineage, you can replace one of the above spells with Enthrall.

requirements.what: The terrain chosen by the Favored Terrain feat must be re-selectable after character creation, to any natural terrain — and everything Favored Terrain grants off that pick must re-derive from the NEW terrain while it is in force, not stay pinned to the original selection. Per Principle C, a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing: the Favored Terrain record needs an indication that this feat can change its pick, so the player looking at Favored Terrain understands why the terrain is editable.
requirements.clause: You can spend 1 hour practicing in your current terrain in order to make it your favored terrain, replacing your current favored terrain temporarily.

requirements.what: The reversion condition is text only. Whether the character has spent a full day outside the new terrain is something the app can never know (the Ruling M principle — position and elapsed downtime are the player's and GM's to track), so no computation is owed. What IS owed is that the ORIGINAL choice remains recoverable: the player must be able to set the terrain back to what Favored Terrain originally named. Per Principle K that restoration is a builder action and needs no sheet surface of its own, but the note must say the swap is temporary or the player will read the new pick as permanent.
requirements.clause: If you spend a full day out of the new favored terrain, your favored terrain reverts back to your original choice when you took the Favored Terrain feat.

requirements.what: The 1-hour practice itself needs NOTHING. It is an unnamed downtime/exploration expenditure with no action cost, not a named activity, so it is not a grantsAction. Direct precedent: Guerrilla Dedication's "change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime" was ruled a builder action with no sheet surface (Principle K). Same shape, same answer.
requirements.clause: You can spend 1 hour practicing in your current terrain

requirements.what: Trained proficiency in Deception, applied to the Deception rank the sheet shows.
requirements.clause: You become trained in Deception

requirements.what: A conditional choice that fires only when the character is ALREADY trained in Deception: the player picks another skill and becomes trained in that instead. The list offered is unrestricted — the text names no category, only "another skill" — but per Q9 it must exclude skills the character is already trained in, since picking one would waste the grant. If the character is not already trained in Deception this choice must not appear at all.
requirements.clause: (or another skill if you're already trained in Deception)

requirements.what: A `*` carrying the equipment waiver: no disguise kit is needed for Deception checks to Impersonate a human. It carries no number — a star with text only, the same shape as Guerrilla Dedication's "Sneak without attempting a Stealth check". Per Q2 it goes on BOTH the Deception skill and the Impersonate action, so the player sees it wherever they look the check up.
requirements.clause: You don't require a disguise kit when attempting Deception checks to Impersonate a human.

requirements.what: A +4 CIRCUMSTANCE bonus that is restricted, so per Ruling B it lives in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when` and stays OUT of the flat Deception total. The `when` must carry the whole restriction, both halves: it applies only to Impersonate checks to pass as a human version of YOURSELF, and explicitly does NOT apply to other checks to Impersonate humans. Dropping the second half would let the player apply +4 to every human impersonation, which the feat forbids. Per Q2 the star goes on both Deception and the Impersonate action.
requirements.clause: you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Impersonate checks to pretend that you're a human version of yourself, rather than a leshy. This bonus doesn't apply to other checks to Impersonate humans.

requirements.what: Scout's Pounce appears in the actions list as a new named activity, at the action cost printed on the record, with its Requirements line — hidden from or undetected by ALL opponents, and not within 10 feet of any enemy — shown in its popup. This is Principle E's shape applied to an activity rather than a reaction: the entry plus its gating conditions in the popup is the surface. The requirement is a positional and detection state the app cannot evaluate, so it is printed for the player to check, never tested.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are hidden from or undetected by all of your opponents, and you aren't within 10 feet of any enemy.

requirements.what: NOTHING. These are the internal steps of the activity, which the lane manual excludes explicitly — the app lists the action and the player performs the Stride and the two Strikes. Only the activity's existence is a lane.
requirements.clause: Stride up to your Speed, then Strike twice.

requirements.what: NOTHING. Off-guard lands on the ENEMY, which DECIDED SCOPE rules off your sheet, and Q4 settles that for an enemy-condition effect the action entry is the whole surface. Same call the owner made on Mastermind's Eye, where the off-guard clause was judged to add nothing. The text lives in the action's popup and goes no further.
requirements.clause: If you were hidden or unnoticed by the target of these Strikes, your foe is off-guard against both attacks.

requirements.what: NOTHING. This restates a general rule the app already applies everywhere; it exists in the printed text only to pre-empt a player assuming the two Strikes escape the penalty. Not a lane.
requirements.clause: Your multiple attack penalty applies normally for both attacks.

requirements.what: Earworm appears in the actions list as a new named activity taking 10 minutes, with its full text in the popup. The popup must also carry the clause that the activity's traits vary with the performance chosen ("gains the traits appropriate to the type of performance") — the trait set is not fixed and cannot be computed, so it is printed rather than derived; and the targeting condition, that it reaches allies who can see or hear you for the entire activity, which is the player's and GM's to determine.
requirements.clause: Choose a composition cantrip and spend 10 minutes repeating a melody, chant, speech, series of motions, or a similar performance that embodies that cantrip. This activity gains the traits appropriate to the type of performance.

requirements.what: A recorded pick of ONE composition cantrip, and the sheet must remember which one, because the whole later payoff depends on it. Per Q9 the picker offers only what the player may legally pick: composition cantrips the character actually knows, not the full cantrip list. It is re-picked in play rather than fixed at build time — each new implant replaces the previous choice — so it cannot be a build-time-only selection.
requirements.clause: Choose a composition cantrip

requirements.what: A DISPLAY-ONLY mode showing an earworm is currently implanted, naming the chosen cantrip and carrying the activity's text. It contributes no numbers: the effect lands on allies, and Ruling F+N gives the activating character a display-only mode precisely so they can see it running while changing none of their own stats. It is not a 1-round effect, so Q1's "indication only" does not apply — it persists until one of three end conditions. Those end conditions must all be expressible: the player clears it when the earworm is activated, implanting another replaces it, and daily preparations clear it automatically — whichever comes first.
requirements.clause: You implant the earworm within all allies who can see or hear you ... Allies forget the earworm after it is activated, if you spend 10 minutes to implant another earworm, or during your next daily preparations, whichever comes first.

requirements.what: A second, separate entry: a FREE ACTION to activate the earworm, available only while one is implanted. Its popup carries the Performance check, the DC rule (the highest Will DC of the targets present, which is target-side and never computed — the player reads it and tells the GM), and both outcomes: on a success the cantrip is cast on the allies who learned it, on a failure the earworm is corrupted and lost. The Performance check is an internal step of the action, so it earns no star on the Performance skill; the free action's existence is the lane.
requirements.clause: Once you've created the earworm, you can attempt a Performance check as a free action to activate it. This check uses the highest Will DC of the earworm's targets present at the time of activation. On a success, you cast the cantrip on all allies who learned the earworm and can perceive your performance; on a failure, the earworm is corrupted and lost.

requirements.what: A restriction the player would otherwise violate: lingering composition, fortissimo composition and similar free actions cannot modify an activated earworm. It must be readable in the Earworm activation popup. ⚠ FLAGGED, NOT ASSUMED: Principle C ("a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing") and Q8 would push this further, to a mark on the Lingering Composition and Fortissimo Composition records themselves, since a player reading those records would have no way to know this exception exists. I am raising it rather than deciding it — it is a negative restriction conditional on the earworm being active, which is a shape the rulings do not clearly cover.
requirements.clause: Because it is based on the earlier repetitions, you can't use further free actions like lingering composition or fortissimo composition to modify the activated earworm.

requirements.what: The ally half needs NOTHING on your sheet. Casting the cantrip on all allies who learned the earworm is an effect landing on someone else, which DECIDED SCOPE (Ruling F+N) rules off your sheet entirely — no star, no modifier. The record's own text tells the player what the allies get, and the display-only mode above is the whole visible surface for it.
requirements.clause: you cast the cantrip on all allies who learned the earworm and can perceive your performance

requirements.what: The feat must appear in the character's action list as a triggered free action, with its trigger — "Your turn begins" — shown in its popup alongside the full text. That is principle E's shape (a triggered action's whole surface is its entry plus trigger/requirements in the popup). The "gain the effects of a Sustain a Spell action" half is the internal step of the activity: the sheet lists the action, the player performs it, so nothing further is owed for it.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** Your turn begins. --- ... You immediately gain the effects of a Sustain a Spell action

requirements.what: One spendable use per day, displayed with the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations. Without it the entry reads as unlimited and the player has no place to record that they have spent it.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: Nothing. Rounds and spell durations are not tracked (Q1 — "we dont truck rounds"), so there is no duration on the sheet to extend, and picking which of your active illusion spells to sustain is a table decision, not a stored choice.
requirements.clause: to extend the duration of one of your active illusion spells

requirements.what: A marker on the death-and-dying surface — the Dying condition and the 0 HP display — stating that this character is not knocked unconscious and does not gain dying when reduced to 0 Hit Points. This is Ruling D's shape exactly (the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters; The Survivor marks the Dying condition). If it is instead expressed as an immunity to unconscious/dying, the restriction "only when reduced to 0 HP" must travel with it (Ruling B) so it never reads as blanket immunity to dying.
requirements.clause: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, you aren't knocked unconscious and you don't gain the dying condition.

requirements.what: A mode the player switches on when the feat fires, granting immunity to ALL damage — a blanket immunity with no named damage type, which the sheet must be able to express, not just a per-type entry — and carrying as text the restriction that you cannot regain Hit Points by any means except the Strike clause below. Duration is open-ended, not one round: it persists round after round until you either heal by damaging a foe or reach wounded 4, so Q1's "a longer duration gets a mode" governs rather than its indication-only rule for 1-round effects, and Q11's shut-down test lands on mode as well (the state can be ended). Per Q3 it must be plain that the mode is active and what it changed.
requirements.clause: Until the start of your next turn, you become immune to all damage, but you also can't regain Hit Points in any way except the following... Otherwise, your wounded value increases by 1 and you remain immune to damage and healing. This cycle continues until you regain Hit Points by damaging a foe or until you reach wounded 4

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text carried by the mode. HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode (Ruling E), so the 4d8+30 is a number the player applies, not a stat the sheet computes.
requirements.clause: If you Strike and damage a foe on this turn, you regain 4d8+30 Hit Points.

requirements.what: Nothing new. Wounded, unconscious and dying are the standard conditions a sheet already carries; the feat only sequences them in an unusual order. That sequence is text inside the mode, not a new mechanism, and asking for one would be restating a general rule the app applies everywhere.
requirements.clause: your wounded value increases by 1 ... at which point you lose the wounded condition, fall unconscious, and gain the dying condition.

requirements.what: ⚠ NO REQUIREMENT CAN BE STATED — the stored text is truncated and names nothing. The entire text field is the 14 characters "You gain the .": the object of the sentence is missing, so there is no clause to specify against. The sentence frame "You gain the ___" indicates the feat grants some named record (a feat, a class feature, or a spellcasting benefit), but WHICH record is unrecoverable from the text, and I will not guess it — guessing would put an invented mechanic into the spec. Two things do follow honestly. First, this record's text must be repaired from source before any requirement for this feat can be written; treat the empty result here as a data defect, not as "this feat needs nothing". Second, whatever the sheet does mechanically, it must not print a broken sentence to the player — Q12 settles that the wording shown is the one that leaves the player least confused, and "You gain the ." fails that on its own.
requirements.clause: You gain the .

requirements.what: The Lay Down Arms action must appear in the action list as a new named activity, with its own details reachable from the entry and this feat named as its source.
requirements.clause: You gain the Lay Down Arms action.

requirements.what: A minion stat block for the severed limb, held the way a familiar is held rather than as anything on the character's own sheet: familiar statistics with every familiar ability and master ability suppressed, Speed 5 feet instead of a familiar's, the minion trait recorded on it, the ability to Interact, and — load-bearing — its own Hit Points, because the inert clause below keys off the limb reaching 0 HP. Its numbers belong on that block, per the standing companion ruling that a companion's statistics and gear live with the companion and their absence from the character's sheet is correct.
requirements.clause: When an arm is severed from your body, it gains the minion trait. While severed, your limb has the statistics of a familiar without any familiar or master abilities, except its Speed is 5 feet, it can't move further than 100 feet from you, it can Interact with things

requirements.what: The limb's Strike is not its own: it must be expressible as a reference back to the character's unarmed Strikes — the character's attack bonus and the character's damage, and specifically any unarmed Strike the limb could have made while attached (usually a fist) rather than a fixed attack invented for the limb. It also shares the character's multiple attack penalty rather than starting a fresh one, so the two attack sequences must be able to count as one. Nothing new appears among the character's own strikes; the derived entry lives on the limb.
requirements.clause: it can still make any unarmed Strikes it could have made while attached to you (usually a fist Strike). Any Strikes it makes share your multiple attack penalty and use your attack bonus and damage.

requirements.what: No positional model is owed. How far the limb is from the character is something the app can never know — the same ground on which auras were ruled not to be a missing system — so the 100-foot half is text on the limb's block. The 0 HP half needs nothing extra: it is already satisfied by the limb having its own Hit Points, required above. "Inert until reattached" is a state the player observes, not a computation.
requirements.clause: If your arm is reduced to 0 HP or is ever more than 100 feet from you, it becomes inert until reattached.

requirements.what: Nothing. This is explicit GM adjudication ("The GM might allow…"), and which other limbs qualify depends on unarmed attacks granted elsewhere. No surface should assert an answer the book leaves to the table.
requirements.clause: The GM might allow you to detach other limbs that have unarmed attacks using the below action

requirements.what: A resistance entry against physical damage that carries the adamantine exception with it. "Physical except adamantine" must be expressible as written — flattening it to plain physical resistance overstates the character's defence against exactly the material the clause was written to exclude.
requirements.clause: You gain resistance to physical damage (except adamantine)

requirements.what: The AMOUNT is a formula over the character's own build, not a constant: a live count of how many class feats they hold from the Stonebound archetype. It must recompute whenever a Stonebound class feat is added or removed, so any fixed number stored on this record is wrong at every level but the one it was written for. This is the same shape as Wyrmling Flight's "fly Speed equal to your Speed" — a value a bare number cannot convey. Note the effect is permanent and unconditional, so unlike Wyrmling Flight it earns no `*` (Q7: the star is for the conditional case; permanent grants need none).
requirements.clause: equal to your number of class feats from the Stonebound archetype
The feat is an activatable activity with a Requirements line: "You're holding an implement."
requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named, activatable entry in the actions list, with its printed Requirement (an implement in hand) shown in its popup beside the full text. Exemplar #7 (Minor Omen) sets the grain: the entry plus its trigger/requirements in the popup is frequently the entire surface. The requirement is a state the player verifies, not a gate the sheet computes — nothing here needs to check whether an implement is held.

requirements.clause: Make a Strike with your weapon against each enemy within 30 feet of you.
requirements.what: No requirement. This is the internal step of an activity — DECIDED SCOPE / NOT lanes: "make a Strike" is performed by the player; the app lists the action. The 30-foot radius and the number of targets are battlefield facts the sheet cannot know and is not asked to model.

requirements.clause: You don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after making all the attacks.
requirements.what: No requirement beyond the clause being legible in the activity's popup. It is a resolution rule that applies only while the player is executing this one activity — it does not alter any standing number on the sheet, and there is no persistent state to hold. Flagged deliberately rather than skipped: MAP is a real sheet-visible quantity, so this clause is the kind that invites a spurious requirement. It earns none because it is scoped entirely inside the activity's own resolution.

requirements.clause: If your weapon is a melee weapon and any attacks are outside your reach, you Release the weapon before the Strikes and it returns after; if your hands are full when it returns, it falls to the ground.
requirements.what: No requirement. Internal steps of the activity plus a GM-adjudicated failure case (hands full, weapon on the ground). Neither the release, the return, nor the drop is a persistent sheet state; the printed text in the popup carries all of it.

requirements.clause: Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in a weapon or weapons, you also gain that proficiency in the bo staff, chakram, katar, panabas, and urumi.
requirements.what: A weapon proficiency whose RANK is not a constant but is read off another record — whatever expert-or-better rank a class feature has granted. The sheet must be able to express a proficiency that follows a second source and is re-derived whenever that source moves (a class's weapon expertise at one level, mastery at a later one, legendary later still), so the five named weapons show the current rank rather than a rank written once at the level the feat was taken. Q10 governs the direction: apply the remap only when it makes the player better — this clause may raise a weapon's rank and must never lower one. The resulting rank must be legible where the player reads weapon proficiencies and must feed the attack bonus of any of these weapons they wield.

requirements.clause: …and all vanara weapons in which you're trained.
requirements.what: The same derived rank applied to a set defined by membership, not by enumeration: every weapon carrying the vanara trait. The sheet must express a proficiency grant keyed to a weapon trait/group rather than to weapon ids, so weapons added to that group later are covered without editing this feat. Two gates ride on it: the upgrade reaches only weapons the character is ALREADY trained in (an untrained vanara weapon gains nothing), and it is an upgrade only, never a set.

requirements.clause: Scope ambiguity: whether "in which you're trained" gates the five named weapons as well as the vanara group.
requirements.what: The printed condition must remain readable on the feat, because the sentence is genuinely open — the trained-in gate may attach only to the trailing "all vanara weapons" or to the whole list. Ruling H governs: where the rules are open, stay open and put the printed trigger in the note rather than resolving the ambiguity silently, which would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young riding drake, riding dragonet, or another animal companion with the dragon trait you have access to.
requirements.what: An animal companion the character owns, surfaced as its own record with its own stat block and its own inventory — per the standing companion ruling, gear and bonuses belong to the companion's sheet, not the character's, so their absence from the character's own numbers is correct, not a gap.

requirements.clause: …a young riding drake, riding dragonet, or another animal companion with the dragon trait you have access to.
requirements.what: A choice of WHICH companion, offered when the feat is taken. Per Q9 the picker shows only what the player may legally pick — here, companions carrying the dragon trait — unless the player toggles "show options not meeting prerequisites". The "you have access to" clause itself needs nothing: Q5 rules that access wording gates neither pickers of this kind nor the shop.

requirements.clause: Your bond lets you command it telepathically within 100 feet; you must still use Command an Animal, but don't require words or gestures.
requirements.what: A marker on the Command an Animal action carrying the telepathic range (100 feet) and the removal of the words-and-gestures requirement. Ruling D and Q8 place the mark on the thing the feat modifies — the action the player is looking at when it matters — with the value inline and a `*` back to this feat. The clause changes no number; it changes what performing the action requires, which is exactly the shape Ruling D covers. "You must still use the Command an Animal action" restates the general rule and adds nothing of its own.

requirements.clause: Designate an ally within 30 feet.
requirements.what: The feat is itself an activatable action and must appear in the actions list with its full printed text, including the 30-foot designation range. Which ally was designated is transient encounter state the sheet is not asked to hold — the text in the popup is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: This action counts as sufficient preparation to Aid that ally.
requirements.what: A marker on the Aid reaction recording that this feat can supply Aid's preparation. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling D puts the mark on the action rather than on a general stat. This is the clause most easily lost, because it reads as flavour connective tissue while actually removing Aid's normal precondition.

requirements.clause: When you use the Aid reaction to help that ally, you can roll in place of the usual check.
requirements.what: An alternative check for Aid when helping the designated ally — the sheet must be able to express "roll this instead of the usual check" on the Aid reaction, and per Principle D the alternative must be visible on every skill that could perform it, not only in the feat's own text. ⚠ FLAGGED, NOT ASSUMED: the text supplied names no substituting skill ("you can roll in place of the usual check" with the check's name absent). Which skill substitutes cannot be read from this text and I have not invented one; the requirement is the substitution mechanism, and the specific skill must be resolved from the printed feat before it can be filled in.

requirements.clause: …and the action gains the bravado trait.
requirements.what: The Aid marker must name the acquired trait, not just the reroll. A trait added to an action is load-bearing on its own — traits are what other records key off — so "Aid gains bravado when used this way" has to be readable on the Aid entry, alongside the substitution clause it shares a sentence with.

requirements.clause: The bonus Aid confers lands on the designated ally.
requirements.what: No requirement. Ruling F / N: an effect that lands on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet — no star, no modifier, no number. The Aid record's own description already tells the player what the ally receives. Principle A is satisfied by the marker on Aid required above; nothing further is owed.

requirements.clause: Your maximum HP is reduced by your level.
requirements.what: A NEGATIVE maximum-HP modifier equal to the character's level — so the sheet must express max-HP adjustments that are level-scaled formulas rather than fixed numbers, re-evaluated at every level-up rather than frozen at the level the feat was taken. It must appear in the HP breakdown attributed to this feat, since an unexplained shortfall in max HP is the kind of number a player will otherwise read as a bug.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance 1 to all damage except for force, vitality, and any damage done by a weapon with the ghost touch rune (or any other source that acts like a ghost touch rune).
requirements.what: A resistance whose type is ALL damage carrying a list of EXCEPTIONS. Two distinct capabilities: a single blanket all-damage resistance entry (not an expansion into one row per damage type), and exclusions subtracted from it. The exclusions are of two different kinds — damage types (force, vitality) and a damage SOURCE (a weapon bearing the ghost touch rune, plus the open-ended "or any other source that acts like" clause, which is GM-adjudicated and must survive as printed text rather than being narrowed to the rune alone, per Ruling H).

requirements.clause: This resistance increases to 2 if the source is non-magical.
requirements.what: A second, higher value on the same resistance, selected by a condition the sheet cannot evaluate — whether the incoming damage is magical. So the entry must be able to carry BOTH values at once and show them together with the condition that picks between them, rather than storing one number. The player resolves which applies; the sheet's job is to make both legible where they read their resistances.

requirements.clause: At 10th level the resistance increases to 2, or 4 if non-magical; at 16th level to 3, or 5 if non-magical.
requirements.what: The resistance values step by character level — a level-keyed table (1/2 → 2/4 → 3/5 at levels 1, 10, 16), not a static pair. Both branches of the magical/non-magical condition scale independently and non-proportionally, so the level table must hold a pair of values per band. This must recompute on level-up; a value written once is wrong for two thirds of the character's career.

requirements.clause: "Increase your maximum Hit Points by your level."
requirements.what: A permanent maximum-HP increase equal to the character's own level — a value that must track level as it changes, not a fixed number written once, and must be legible in the HP breakdown as coming from this feat.

requirements.clause: "When you have the Dying 1 condition, the DC of your recovery checks is equal to 9 + your dying value (instead of 10 + your dying value)."
requirements.what: Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing it modifies: the Dying condition / recovery-check entry, carrying the replaced DC formula (9 + dying value) and the Dying-1-only restriction. Ruling G: it REPLACES the printed 10 + dying value rather than sitting beside it. It moves no stat row — it changes a DC you roll against.

requirements.clause: "If you also have the Toughness feat, the Hit Points gained from it and this feat are cumulative…"
requirements.what: Nothing. Both are level-scaled maximum-HP increases and simply add; this sentence only forecloses a non-stacking reading and produces no second surface.

requirements.clause: "…and the DC of your recovery checks is equal to 6 + your dying value."
requirements.what: The recovery-DC marker's VALUE must be conditional on the character also owning another record (Toughness): 6 + dying value when both are held, and as printed that combined figure carries no Dying-1 qualifier. Principle C — the two feats must reconcile into one figure on the Dying condition, not print two contradictory ones (Toughness's 9 and this feat's 9-while-Dying-1).

requirements.clause: "You gain the Assurance (Performance) feat."
requirements.what: Assurance appears as an owned feat with its skill parameter already fixed to Performance — a grant that carries its own choice pre-made, so no picker is offered for it, and Assurance's own effect reaches the Performance skill rather than an unselected one.

requirements.clause: "With a successful [check], you can accurately recall a sound or a snippet of conversation you heard within the last week."
requirements.what: A marker on Performance — the skill the check is made with — carrying the recall clause and its one-week window. Nothing computable; the outcome is GM-adjudicated recall, not a bonus. ⚠ The text as supplied is truncated ("With a successful ," names no check), so the check this clause hangs on cannot be read out of the evidence; whatever surfaces this note must show a complete sentence.

requirements.clause: "You are memorizing by rote rather than content, and can't use this to cram facts, so this doesn't grant you any extra ability to Recall Knowledge."
requirements.what: Nothing. A negative clarification that grants no ability; it belongs inside the note's text and must specifically NOT produce a Recall Knowledge surface.

requirements.clause: "You gain the Rapid Affixture skill feat, even if you don't meet the prerequisites."
requirements.what: A named feat granted outright, and the grant must be expressible as prerequisite-bypassing — it lands among owned feats and its own effects apply even when the character does not qualify for it.

requirements.clause: "When you use it, you can affix or remove up to four talismans in 1 minute instead of just one."
requirements.what: Principle C — the change must be reflected IN the thing it modifies: the granted Rapid Affixture entry (and the Affix a Talisman activity it produces) must read four talismans within the same 1 minute, and must cover removal as well as affixing. A player who opens the granted feat must not see "one".

requirements.clause: "You gain the ability to Affix a Talisman as a 3-action activity from that feat at 12th level…"
requirements.what: Principle H — Affix a Talisman must appear under BOTH costs, its ordinary longer form and the 3-action form this feat unlocks, with the explanation in the popup.

requirements.clause: "…at 12th level, regardless of your Crafting proficiency."
requirements.what: Two gates on that same unlock: it must not appear before character level 12 (a level-conditioned change to an already-granted record), and it must ignore the Crafting-proficiency gate the base feat imposes — so a proficiency requirement on another record has to be overridable by this one.

requirements.clause: "You cease aging."
requirements.what: Nothing. Age is not a value the sheet computes or advances, so the clause lives only in the feat's own printed text.

requirements.clause: "…regardless of your actual existential state, now register as a living being to effects that can detect living creatures (such as lifesense or spiritsense)."
requirements.what: Q6 — an acquired creature-facing property recorded on the character's own Details as a tag: counts as living for creature-detecting effects. This is not an ally-facing or enemy-facing number; it changes what the character IS, which matters when the character is otherwise undead or construct-typed, and it must survive being read off the sheet without a number.

requirements.clause: "…you learn the Control Weather and Plant Growth rituals."
requirements.what: Both named rituals reach the character's ritual list, each with its own details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source.

requirements.clause: "You can use Occultism instead of Nature for these rituals."
requirements.what: A substitution SCOPED to two named rituals — Occultism must be expressible as an allowed check on the Control Weather and Plant Growth entries specifically, not as a blanket Occultism-for-Nature swap that would leak onto every other Nature use.

requirements.clause: "On a success with one of these rituals, you gain the effects of a critical success instead."
requirements.what: Ruling D — a marker on each of those two ritual entries stating that a success is treated as a critical success. There is no number to compute; the requirement is that the upgrade is visible on the ritual the player is looking at when it matters, and only on those two.

requirements.clause: "You spend 10 minutes and 1 Focus Point brewing a special potion…"
requirements.what: The brewing activity itself must appear as an action the character can take, carrying its 10-minute time and its 1 Focus Point cost, and spending that point from the focus pool when used.

requirements.clause: "…containing the power of one of your hexes that targets a creature."
requirements.what: A pick made at brew time, drawn from the character's OWN hexes and filtered (Q9) to those that target a creature — the picker must be able to offer a subset of a record the character already holds, not a free list.

requirements.clause: "Any potion you create this way loses its power the next time you make your daily preparations."
requirements.what: The brewed bottle must be holdable as a temporary item that records which hex it carries, and must expire at daily preparations rather than persisting. Three later clauses ("while the potion is in your possession", "until the potion is consumed or loses its magic") all address this object, so its existence and its lifetime have to be expressible, not just its description.

requirements.clause: "A creature that consumes this potion is targeted by the hex."
requirements.what: Ruling F — the effect lands on whoever drinks it, so no number on your sheet. The only requirement already stated above: the bottle names the hex it carries and that hex's text is reachable from it.

requirements.clause: "If the hex has a sustained duration and you have Cackle, you can cast cackle into the bottle just before you seal it… the hex's duration is extended…"
requirements.what: An optional second step at brew time, offered only when the character owns another named record (Cackle) AND the chosen hex has a sustained duration — a conditional branch inside the activity that costs a further Focus Point, and whose result must be recorded on the bottle so the extension is readable later.

requirements.clause: "While the potion is in your possession, you can render it inert using a single action that has the concentrate trait."
requirements.what: A separate 1-action concentrate action, whose availability is conditioned on currently holding such a bottle, and whose effect voids that bottle.

requirements.clause: "You can't regain the Focus Point you spent to create the potion (or the Focus Point you spent to cast cackle) until the potion is consumed or loses its magic."
requirements.what: The focus pool must be able to hold 1 point — or 2 when cackle was sealed in — LOCKED OUT: Refocus and daily preparations must not restore it while an outstanding bottle exists, and the point must return when the bottle is consumed, rendered inert, or expires. This is the only clause in this feat that moves a number on the sheet, and it is a reduction driven by an item's continued existence rather than by a duration.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** You fail a saving throw against an effect from your *warmask*'s magical tradition. **Requirements** You're wearing your *warmask*.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the REACTIONS list, with its trigger (you fail a save against an effect from your warmask's magical tradition) and its requirement (you are wearing your warmask) written out in its popup. This is the same shape the owner settled for Minor Omen (principle E): the reaction entry is the whole surface. Note the requirement is conditioned on a worn ITEM, so the popup wording must name the warmask rather than assume the app can test for it.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed on the reaction's own entry — where the player looks when they use it (Ruling D) — consumed when spent and restored at daily preparations. This is the per-day resource shape exemplar #10 gives for a 1/day frequency.

requirements.clause: You reroll the triggering check with a +2 circumstance bonus, but you must use the new result, even if it's worse than your first roll.
requirements.what: NO requirement beyond the popup text. The reroll and its +2 circumstance bonus are internal steps of the reaction the player performs; they never modify a displayed save. The owner ruled exactly this on Minor Omen — a reroll-a-failed-save feat is explicitly NOT a degree-of-success surface and gets no star on the save. The 'must use the new result' clause is likewise prose for the popup.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Athletics and Crafting.
requirements.what: Trained rank in TWO named skills — Athletics and Crafting — both reaching the skill list as real proficiency, not a note. Two separate grants from one feat; noticing only one is the failure mode here.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A redundancy test on each of the two grants: if another source would already make the character trained in Athletics or in Crafting, THAT grant is replaced rather than wasted. It must fire per-skill (a character trained in both by class converts both), and it must be sensitive to grants coming from anywhere else on the build, not just this feat.

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: When the fallback fires, the player is offered a free trained-skill pick, and the pick must reach the sheet as trained rank in the chosen skill. Per Q9 the builder offers only skills the character may legally take (i.e. not ones they are already trained in), unless they toggle showing options that fail prerequisites. The pick is a builder choice, so per principle K it needs no separate sheet surface beyond the resulting proficiency.

requirements.clause: You gain the Additional Lore general feat for Hobgoblin Lore.
requirements.what: The named feat Additional Lore is granted outright and appears among the character's feats with its own details reachable. Critically it is PARAMETERISED — 'for Hobgoblin Lore' fixes its subject, so the player must NOT be asked to choose which Lore. This is a fixed grant, not a pick-a-feat and not a pick-a-subject.

requirements.clause: the Additional Lore general feat for Hobgoblin Lore
requirements.what: The consequence of the parameterised grant must actually flow to the sheet: Hobgoblin Lore appears as a trained Lore skill with its own rollable entry. A granted feat whose own effects never surface is invisible — the grant is only real if the Lore itself is there. (Whatever further progression Additional Lore's own printed text promises is owed by that record, not by this one.)

requirements.clause: You gain the Accidental Shot activity.
requirements.what: A named activity, Accidental Shot, appears in the character's actions with its own entry and its full details reachable from it. The feat's only mechanical promise is that this activity exists and is findable; the activity's internal steps are performed by the player, not modelled.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: The frequency is printed on the feat but governs the granted activity, since granting Accidental Shot is all the feat does. So one spendable use per day must sit on the ACCIDENTAL SHOT entry — the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D) — consumed on use and restored at daily preparations. A per-day limit shown only on the dedication feat and not on the activity would be in the wrong place.

requirements.clause: Who needs skill when you've got dumb luck? Sometimes your shots hit miraculously, regardless of the fact that you seemed to slip when you pulled the trigger or that you weren't aiming at your foe when you fired.
requirements.what: NO requirement. Pure flavour. The printed text carries no archetype-access, prerequisite, or 'you can't take another dedication' clause, so nothing else is promised here and nothing should be inferred.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits.
requirements.what: ⚠ NO requirement derivable — the sentence is TRUNCATED. 'You gain the benefits' has no antecedent in the supplied text; the object of the sentence (benefits of what?) has been dropped, which is the known shape of an unsubstituted reference in this source. I am flagging it rather than guessing what was elided. Whatever this clause promises cannot be specified until the intact text is supplied, and it may well carry a real lane.

requirements.clause: Increase the spell slots you gain from the bloodrager archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank.
requirements.what: An extra spell slot at EVERY spell rank the bloodrager archetype grants — not one slot, one per rank — reaching the actual slot counts the player casts from, so the pips they spend go up by one on each affected row. The increase must track the archetype's own rank progression, so it grows as further archetype feats add ranks rather than being a fixed one-time addition.

requirements.clause: Increase the spell slots you gain from the bloodrager archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank.
requirements.what: The increase is scoped to ANOTHER record's grant: only the slots that came from the bloodrager archetype feats, never a class's or another archetype's spellcasting the same character may hold. Per principle C the change must be reflected in the thing it modifies — the bloodrager casting entry — and it must be inert (no phantom slots) for a character who has that archetype's later feats but not the slot-granting ones.

requirements.clause: when you Cast a Spell from your repertoire and you are at least Drained 2, double the extra damage dealt by that spell from Rage instead.
requirements.what: This modifies a rider Rage already grants, so per principle C it must be reflected IN that thing: the Rage mode's spell-extra-damage entry carries the doubling, stated with its two conditions (the spell comes from your repertoire, and you are Drained 2 or worse). Per principle B the mode carries the full text even for the parts it cannot compute, and per Ruling D the mark belongs on the rider being changed rather than on a general damage stat. The word 'instead' means it REPLACES the normal extra damage rather than stacking with it (Ruling G: an upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades). No unconditional number moves; a character not raging, not Drained 2, or casting outside their repertoire sees the ordinary value.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** An ally is reduced to 0 Hit Points.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the REACTIONS list with its trigger (an ally is reduced to 0 Hit Points) written in its popup. Per principle E that is often the whole requirement for a reaction. The trigger is an event on an ALLY, which the sheet cannot know — so it stays printed text the player reads, never a detected state.

requirements.clause: You Stride towards the triggering ally.
requirements.what: NO requirement. The Stride is an internal step of the activity: the app lists the reaction, the player performs the movement. Only the reaction's existence is a lane.

requirements.clause: You gain a +10-foot circumstance bonus to your Speed during this movement.
requirements.what: A `*` on the character's Speed carrying '+10 feet circumstance while Striding with Rapid Response'. Speed is a displayed stat and this clause modifies it, so per Ruling D the mark goes on the Speed itself; but the bonus is restricted to one movement, so per Ruling B it lives in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when` and must NOT be folded into the Speed total. The +10 also belongs in the reaction's own popup text so the player sees how far they get when they use it.

requirements.clause: "You trace a spiral in the air while intoning prayers to Pharasma, gaining her blessing for a time." (an activation, carrying a Frequency line)
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new activated ability, so it must appear as an entry in the actions list with its full text reachable from that entry. The text is written as something the character DOES at a moment of their choosing, not as a passive — without an action entry there is nowhere for the player to invoke it or read its frequency.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per 10 minutes
requirements.what: The recharge period must be expressible and legible on the action. It is a 10-minute interval, not a rest-restored resource: a per-day pip would be wrong in both directions (it would run out after one use in a long day, and it would not stop a second use two rounds later). So what is owed is the printed frequency on the entry, and — if a spendable counter is offered at all — one whose restore condition is an elapsed interval rather than daily preparations.

requirements.clause: "For 3 rounds, your Strikes and spells deal additional damage against undead…"
requirements.what: A toggleable state the player turns on for the duration. Q1 rules that only a 1-round effect is indication-only and that a longer duration gets a mode; 3 rounds is longer. Unlike Healing Sanctuary's per-round clause, nothing here recurs per round — it is a flat bonus that persists — so the mode carries real numbers, not text alone. Per Q3's shape, while it is on the sheet must make plain that a mode is active and what it changed.

requirements.clause: "You gain a status bonus to damage with your Strikes against these creatures equal to the number of weapon damage dice."
requirements.what: A status damage bonus on Strikes whose VALUE is a formula off the weapon in hand — the number of damage dice — so it differs per weapon and rises when a striking rune is added. It cannot be stored as one number; it must resolve per Strike and show on that Strike's damage line. Its restriction (undead, creatures possessing an imprisoned soul, or creatures you have witnessed create or command undead) is a target-side condition that gates YOUR damage, so per Ruling B it belongs in the bonus's `when` rather than folded into a flat total, and per Ruling H the printed trigger stays as written — "creatures you have witnessed create or command undead" is a judgement the app must not narrow.

requirements.clause: "Spells you cast from spell slots gain a status bonus to damage against these creatures equal to the rank of the spell; this bonus applies only to spells that deal damage and don't have a duration."
requirements.what: A second, separately-valued status damage bonus that must reach the spells themselves: its value is the rank the spell is cast at, so it changes with heightening and differs per spell entry. Three restrictions must all survive onto the marker — spell-slot casts only (not cantrips, innate, or focus spells), damaging spells only, and no-duration spells only — plus the same target restriction as the Strike clause.

requirements.clause: "If your spiral is glowing, you can target a willing creature in its light. If you do, that creature gains the bonuses instead of you."
requirements.what: Two things, neither of which is a number on your sheet. (a) The redirection is ally-facing, so per Ruling F the ally's copy of the bonuses gets no surface — but the player must be able to leave the mode OFF while still having used the action, because when redirected they themselves gain nothing. Activation and the self-bonus state must therefore be separable rather than the mode switching itself on. (b) "If your spiral is glowing" is a precondition set by some other record and unknowable to the sheet; it stays as printed text on the action, not as a computed gate.

requirements.clause: "Select one of the following benefits when you gain this feat. This choice is permanent and can't be changed."
requirements.what: A two-option choice offered at the moment the feat is taken, with the pick recorded, and each option carrying its own mechanical grant rather than being decorative text. The permanence is itself part of the requirement: this is explicitly not a re-pick, so the player must be told the choice is final at the point of choosing — Principle K's "they will change it in the builder" does not apply to a choice the rules forbid changing.

requirements.clause: "Your nectar unarmed attack deals an additional 1d4 persistent acid damage to the target. This persistent damage isn't multiplied on a critical hit."
requirements.what: The nectar unarmed Strike — a Strike granted by some OTHER record, which this feat only edits — must show +1d4 persistent acid on its damage line. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing, so the rider has to land on the existing nectar Strike, not create a second Strike beside it. The crit clause is a real second requirement: whatever doubles damage on a critical hit must leave this die out, which means the added damage cannot simply be appended to the strike's damage expression if that expression is doubled wholesale.

requirements.clause: "Your nectar unarmed attack additionally deals 1d4 acid splash damage. This splash damage isn't multiplied on a critical hit."
requirements.what: The alternative option: the same granted nectar Strike gains 1d4 acid SPLASH damage — splash is its own damage category with its own rules (it lands even on a miss and hits adjacent creatures), so it must be expressible as splash and not collapsed into ordinary added acid damage. Same crit exclusion as the other option.

requirements.clause: "**Special** This feat gains the trait for your ancestry."
requirements.what: No sheet number and no lane — but the feat's own displayed trait line must resolve to the taking character's ancestry trait rather than printing the sentence as an unresolved instruction. Nothing on the sheet changes.

requirements.clause: "Your megafauna gains your choice of the bully, racer, tracker, or wrecker specialization."
requirements.what: A choice of exactly one from a four-item named list, offered when the feat is taken. Per Q9 the picker must be filtered to those four — the general specialization list is not a legal set here — and must exclude any specialization the companion has already gained from a previous instance of this feat, since the text requires a different one each time.

requirements.clause: "Your megafauna gains… the specialization" — the effect's destination
requirements.what: The chosen specialization's effects must reach the MEGAFAUNA COMPANION's own stat block. Per the standing companion ruling, absence of any of these numbers from the character's own stat rows is correct and is not a defect — but the requirement is not "nothing": the companion's sheet has to express the specialization it was given. The feat also presumes the character has a megafauna companion granted elsewhere, so the pick must attach to that existing companion record rather than to the character.

requirements.clause: "**Special** You can select this feat up to three times… Your megafauna can't have more than three specializations."
requirements.what: The feat must be holdable more than once, with each instance recording its own distinct pick — a single stored answer would silently overwrite the earlier one. Two caps must hold: at most three instances of the feat, and at most three specializations on the companion.

requirements.clause: "…when you Drain your Bonded Item to cast one of your arcane school's curriculum spells…"
requirements.what: A marker on the Drain Bonded Item action — the thing this feat modifies — carrying what the feat adds and when. Ruling D and Q8 both put the mark on the action rather than on a general stat, because Drain Bonded Item is what the player is looking at when it matters. The trigger's condition must survive onto that marker in full: it fires only when the drained cast is one of the character's OWN arcane school curriculum spells, which is a per-character list, so the note must name that school's curriculum rather than saying "a curriculum spell" unqualified.

requirements.clause: "Once per day…"
requirements.what: A single spendable use, consumed when the player takes the benefit and restored at daily preparations. Because the trigger is a thing the player does at the table rather than something the sheet observes, the use must be spendable by the player directly from wherever the marker lives.

requirements.clause: "…you also regain 1 Focus Point."
requirements.what: A way to return one SPENT Focus Point to the pool. This is not an increase to the pool's maximum and not a Refocus — the character's focus pool size is unchanged; a point already spent comes back mid-encounter. So what must be expressible is a one-off restore of a spent point, triggered by the player, distinct from both the pool-size lane and the rest/refocus restore.

requirements.clause: "You capture the moment by striking an unforgettable pose…" (an activation carrying a Frequency line)
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear in the actions list with its full text in its popup — this is the entry the player presses when they use it. Which of Diplomacy or Intimidation they roll is an internal step of the activity, not a separate lane: the sheet lists the action, the player performs the check.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour
requirements.what: A once-per-hour frequency printed on the action. Its recharge is an elapsed hour, not daily preparations, so a rest-restored daily pip would state something false about when it comes back; the interval itself must be what the entry says.

requirements.clause: "You can substitute the result of this check for one Reflex save you would be required to attempt in the next minute."
requirements.what: A substitution of a Diplomacy or Intimidation result for a REFLEX save — the load-bearing surface is a `*` on Reflex, because per Ruling D the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, and the moment that matters is when a Reflex save is called for. Q2 adds the other half: star the skills as well, so both Diplomacy and Intimidation carry it. Note this is Reflex specifically, not saves generally, so Fortitude and Will get nothing. Two limits must ride along on the marker: it replaces exactly ONE save, and only one required within the next minute.

requirements.clause: "…for one Reflex save you would be required to attempt in the next minute." (the one-minute window)
requirements.what: ⚠ DERIVED, not owner-stated: Q1 gives a mode to any effect lasting longer than a round, and this window is a minute, so the player needs a way to see that a stored result is currently available to spend. It is display-only in the sense of Ruling E case 3 — the held value is the player's own die roll, which the sheet cannot compute and which changes no derived number. If the number is to be kept at all rather than remembered, Principle I makes free-text player input a legitimate way to hold it.

requirements.clause: Your size increases to Large
requirements.what: Your size actually becomes Large while the form is up — the sheet's size must change, not merely describe the change. Because the form can be turned off (Sustain, 10-minute cap, natural-form cooldown), Q11 makes this a MODE rather than a passive: a player-toggled Oni Form state that carries the size override, and per Q3 the sheet must make plain that the mode is active and what it changed.

requirements.clause: and you're Clumsy 1
requirements.what: The same Oni Form mode applies Clumsy 1 to the character — a condition on YOU, not an ally or enemy, so it is in scope. Q3 requires a form mode to really override the stats it names, so the -1 status penalty must reach the Dex-governed numbers (AC, Reflex, Dex-based skills and attacks) and the condition must read as active while the mode is on.

requirements.clause: This doesn't change your Speed, reach, or other statistics except as noted here.
requirements.what: A constraint, not an effect: the mode must leave Speed and reach untouched despite the size change, and the sentence itself must be readable inside the mode so the player does not assume Large reach. Nothing computed.

requirements.clause: Your worn equipment automatically resizes to suit your new form, though it immediately returns to its original size if it leaves your possession.
requirements.what: NOTHING. It exists to remove a complication (ill-fitting gear), not to move a number; no inventory, bulk, or penalty consequence is stated.

requirements.clause: This form is the same age and body type as your true form and has roughly analogous physical traits, such as hair color.
requirements.what: NOTHING. Pure flavour/appearance.

requirements.clause: Using Oni Form counts as creating a disguise for the Impersonate use of Deception.
requirements.what: A `*` carrying this clause on BOTH the Deception skill and the Impersonate action (Q2: star the skill and the action; Ruling C: Impersonate is performed by Deception alone). It grants no bonus number — it removes a step — so per Ruling B it must sit as a marker beside the roll, never as a modifier inside the Deception total.

requirements.clause: You can Sustain your Oni Form for up to 10 minutes, though you must then spend at least 10 minutes in your natural form before using Oni Form again.
requirements.what: The mode must be the player's own on/off surface — turned on, sustained, and ended by hand — and must print the 10-minute cap and the 10-minute cooldown as TEXT. Minutes are not tracked, so this contributes no number and no automatic expiry (principle B: a mode carries the full text of what it does, including the parts the app cannot compute).

requirements.clause: You swirl water around you to make a current that pulls creatures closer. Attempt an Athletics check against the Fortitude DC of a creature within 20 feet.
requirements.what: Riptide must exist as a named activity in the character's actions list, its full text reachable in its popup — the check to roll, the 20-foot range, and all four outcome lines. The Athletics check is an INTERNAL STEP of the activity, not a bonus: the app lists the action and the player rolls it, so no star and no modifier is owed on Athletics.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're in Anchor Stance, and your target is within 5 feet of the edge of a water vehicle or already in the water.
requirements.what: The Requirements line printed in the action's popup, exactly as exemplar #7 (Minor Omen) requires of a trigger and requirement. Neither the stance nor the target's distance from a vehicle edge is something the sheet can evaluate, so this is text only — it must not gate or hide the action.

requirements.clause: If the creature is willing, you increase your degree of success by one (turning a failure into a success and a success into a critical success).
requirements.what: Text inside the action's popup and nothing more. Degree of success is not a sheet surface (exemplar #7 is explicit: "not a degree-of-success surface").

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The target is pulled 10 feet toward you. **Success** The target is pulled 5 feet toward you.
requirements.what: NOTHING. Forced movement of another creature — enemy-side and positional, both settled by DECIDED SCOPE. It lives in the outcome text the player reads and reports to the GM.

requirements.clause: **Critical Failure** Your movements cause you to be off-guard until the beginning of your next turn.
requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the outcome text already in the popup. This is a self-condition, so scope does not exclude it, but Q1 (effects lasting 1 round are indication only) and Q15 (a degree-of-success-triggered effect needs no implementation unless COMPLICATED — and a bare condition is not complicated) together settle it as indication.

requirements.clause: Your shadow reservoir gains an additional spell 1 rank below the highest rank spell you can cast, in addition to the spells it already contains for all the levels below that.
requirements.what: Principle C: the extra spell must be reflected IN THE SHADOW RESERVOIR — visible where the player reads the reservoir's contents, not only in this feat's own text. Two things make a fixed value impossible: the rank is derived (highest castable rank minus one) and moves every time the character's top rank rises, and the clause is explicitly additive — it stacks on top of whatever the reservoir already holds at every lower rank rather than replacing that list.

requirements.clause: Your shadow reservoir gains an additional spell 1 rank below the highest rank spell you can cast, in addition to the spells it already contains for all the levels below that.
requirements.what: ⚠ OPEN — FLAGGED, NOT ASSUMED. The text says the reservoir gains "an additional spell" without saying who names it. If the reservoir's spells are player-chosen, this added entry needs the same picker, at the derived rank, and the pick has to persist; if the reservoir is a fixed list, it needs no choice at all. The feat's own text cannot settle which, so I record the question rather than inventing the lane.

requirements.clause: You gain void resistance equal to the highest rank of spell you can cast from spell slots
requirements.what: A resistance entry in the defences, permanent — nothing in the text shuts it off, so Q11 makes it a passive bonus and not a mode. Its value is a FORMULA off the character's highest spell-slot rank and must recompute as they level; a baked number would be wrong at every level but one. ⚠ Note this quantity is deliberately narrower than the reservoir clause above: "from spell slots" excludes innate, focus, and cantrip casting, so the two numbers in this feat are not the same number and must not be derived from one source.

requirements.clause: if you have void healing (or are otherwise harmed by vitality damage and not void damage), you instead gain vitality resistance in the same amount
requirements.what: The resistance's DAMAGE TYPE is conditional on a property of the character, and the swap is exclusive — vitality INSTEAD OF void, never both, so this cannot be expressed as a second stacked resistance. The sheet must be able to key the type off whether the character has void healing rather than hard-coding void. Because the parenthetical is open-ended ("or are otherwise harmed by vitality damage and not void damage"), Ruling H applies — stay open: the player needs a way to select the vitality variant in the cases the app cannot detect for itself.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Performance
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in Performance, applied so it reaches the Performance modifier on the sheet. The text prints NO fallback for a character who is already trained, so no redundancy alternative is owed here — inventing one would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: and gain one 1st-level Performance skill feat
requirements.what: A picker in the builder for one skill feat, filtered to 1st-level skill feats belonging to Performance and nothing wider (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, unless they toggle to show options failing prerequisites). The feat chosen must be genuinely OWNED, so every effect it carries reaches the sheet on its own terms; the pick itself is a builder action and needs no separate sheet surface beyond the granted feat appearing among the character's feats (principle K).

requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature fails or critically fails a save against your snare.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions list with this trigger printed in its popup — principle E, and the exact shape the owner gave for Minor Obtain/Minor Omen ("a reaction that needs to appear in the reactions… the Requirement needs to be written in the pop up"). Per E this is often the whole requirement, and most of it is here.

requirements.clause: If you have expert proficiency in Deception… If you have expert proficiency in Intimidation… If you have both, choose one of the two effects.
requirements.what: The reaction's content is gated on the character's CURRENT Deception and Intimidation ranks, which the sheet already knows. A character at expert in neither holds a reaction that does nothing, and one at expert in both gets a pick made at the table rather than in the builder. So the gate must be legible in the entry — ideally resolved against the character's actual ranks rather than printed flat — and the "choose one" is an in-play decision, not a build choice, so it needs no builder picker.

requirements.clause: you can Create a Diversion against the triggering creature… you can instead Demoralize the triggering creature
requirements.what: Q8 and Ruling D: mark the action the feat modifies. Create a Diversion and Demoralize each gain a marker noting this feat lets them be performed off the snare trigger, so the player sees it where they look the action up. The feat grants no bonus to the Deception or Intimidation ROLL, so no star is owed on either skill's total — the change is to when the action may be taken, not to its number.

requirements.clause: you can Create a Diversion against the triggering creature… you can instead Demoralize the triggering creature (the resulting conditions)
requirements.what: NOTHING. Whatever Create a Diversion or Demoralize inflicts lands on the triggering creature; enemy-side conditions are settled by DECIDED SCOPE and Q4 ("the reaction entry is the whole surface").

requirements.clause: You've nurtured the supernatural abilities gifted by your hag mother, particularly your sight.
requirements.what: Flavour. No requirement.

requirements.clause: You gain darkvision.
requirements.what: Darkvision appears in the character's senses, attributed to this feat. Q13 governs the collision: when the character already has low-light vision from another source, show ONLY darkvision, because it supersedes low-light — the player must not be shown two senses where the rules leave one operative. No other surface: darkvision is permanent and unconditional here, so per Q7's logic (a `*` is for a CONDITIONAL grant) it needs no star.

requirements.clause: You create a faintly glowing sigil ... on the target's body, after which you command the target to approach you, run away ..., release what it's holding, drop prone, or stand in place. The target then attempts a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: The impulse must exist as a usable activity in the character's actions list, with its action cost and traits, and its popup must carry the full printed text. Two things inside that popup are load-bearing rather than decorative: (a) the DC the target rolls against is YOUR CLASS DC, so the entry must name which of the character's DCs applies — the player should not have to guess between class DC, spell DC and a skill DC; (b) the five commands (approach / run away / release / drop prone / stand in place) are a per-use pick made at the table, not a build-time choice, so they belong in the popup text as options and must NOT be modelled as a builder `choice`.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** ... **Success** ... **Failure** ... **Critical Failure** ...
requirements.what: The four outcomes are display prose inside the action's popup and nothing more. Answer #7 (Minor Omen) settles this shape explicitly — 'there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way', and it is called out there as expressly NOT a degree-of-success surface. The requirement is only that the full outcome text is readable from the action entry.

requirements.clause: The sigil acts as a magnet for your fiery attacks, granting the creature a –1 penalty to its saves and AC against your fire impulses.
requirements.what: No requirement. The penalty lands on the enemy's saves and AC, which DECIDED SCOPE rules out ('Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet'), and Q4 settles the shape for exactly this case — the action entry is the whole surface. Note this is NOT a bonus to the character's own impulse attack or DC that has been mis-worded; the rules put the number on the creature, so nothing attaches to the character's stats.

requirements.clause: The sigil lasts until the end of your next turn or until the creature spends at least 1 action obeying your command ... it can't Delay. The sigil vanishes at the end of its turn ...
requirements.what: No requirement. Two independent rulings each dispose of it: the duration is roughly one round, and Q1 says effects lasting 1 round are not implemented (indication only); and the state being tracked belongs to the target creature, not the character, so it is not a mode on this sheet. 'It can't Delay' is a restriction on the enemy's actions — enemy-facing, nothing owed.

requirements.clause: the sigil ignites as it vanishes, dealing damage and damage to the creature.
requirements.what: No requirement beyond the text being printed. Damage dealt to a creature never moves a sheet stat — DECIDED SCOPE, Ruling E: 'HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode.' (Recorded for the record's sake, without speculating about cause: the clause as supplied reads 'dealing damage and damage', i.e. the two damage expressions are absent from the text I was given, which is why no numeric value is stated in this requirement.)

requirements.clause: **Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6, and the persistent damage increases by 1d6.
requirements.what: The damage printed in the action's popup must be the value AT THE CHARACTER'S OWN LEVEL, not a base value with a generic '+2 levels' rider left for the player to compute.
