This is the same shape the owner ruled on for Wyrmling Flight (answer #8 / Q7): a number defined as a formula over one of the character's own stats cannot be conveyed by a bare printed constant. The distinction from the clauses above is deliberate — the damage still moves no stat on this sheet, but the character's level is the input to it, so the sheet is the only place that value can be resolved.

requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion as a mount. See Animal Companions.
requirements.what: An animal companion must be granted to the character and must carry its maturity rank — YOUNG — since that rank is what sets the companion's statistics and is the thing later advancement changes. Per the ★ Companions ruling the companion is its own stat block with its own inventory; the character's sheet needs the companion to exist and be reachable, not a copy of its numbers.

requirements.clause: Typically, the steed is an animal companion with the mount ability (such as a horse).
requirements.what: The player must be offered the choice of WHICH animal companion, and the offered list is expected to be the mount-capable ones (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick). The choice must be recorded — the companion type determines the whole stat block, so it cannot be left implicit.

requirements.clause: If you have the holy or unholy trait, your mount gains it as well, as do the mount's Strikes.
requirements.what: Two things must be expressible, both on the COMPANION and not on the character (★ Companions: 'a companion's bonus marks the COMPANION, not you'). First, the companion must be able to acquire a creature trait — holy or unholy — conditionally, sourced from a trait the OWNER holds rather than chosen on the companion itself; this is Q6's 'record acquired creature traits' applied to the companion's own trait line. Second, the trait must reach the companion's STRIKES, since a holy/unholy Strike interacts with the target's weaknesses; a trait recorded only on the creature and not on its attacks would not deliver what the clause promises. It is conditional on the character's own trait, so it must be able to be absent for a character with neither trait.

requirements.clause: The GM might allow another animal companion option, or allow the creature to have a different appearance that thematically fits your deity.
requirements.what: No requirement. Explicit GM adjudication, which the lane manual lists under NOT lanes ('Anything the GM adjudicates'). Appearance is flavour.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level druid feat.
requirements.what: A picker must be offered in the builder, filtered to druid CLASS feats of level 1 or 2, and the pick must be recorded against this feat. Q9 governs the filter: only what the player may legally pick, meaning the offered feats' own prerequisites are honoured unless the player toggles 'show options not meeting prerequisites'. The substantive half of the requirement is what happens after the pick — the chosen feat must be owned outright, so every requirement the chosen feat itself carries (its own grants, choices, stars, actions, modes) must reach the sheet exactly as if the player had taken it directly. A grant that records the pick but does not deliver the picked feat's own mechanics satisfies nothing. Per Ruling G the granted thing's details must also be surfaced, so the player can read what they picked.

requirements.clause: Cities are just a new form of wilderness. You've adapted to this wilderness and now can navigate it as easily as where you once came from.
requirements.what: Flavour. No requirement.

requirements.clause: When in an urban area, you can move at your full Speed while you Track
requirements.what: A `*` on the Track action carrying the condition ('in an urban area') and the effect (move at full Speed while Tracking). Ruling D places the mark on the thing being modified — the action — and this is a relaxation of Track's own printed movement restriction rather than a bonus to a roll, so it belongs on the action's entry and NOT on the Speed stat: the character's Speed number is unchanged. Per Ruling C the same star must also be reachable from every skill that could perform Track — which for this feat means Survival AND Society (see the next clause) — since that is where the player looks when they use it.

requirements.clause: you can use your choice of Survival or Society to Track.
requirements.what: Society must be usable in place of Survival for the Track action, with the substitution restricted to the urban-area condition — the player chooses per use, so both options must remain available rather than one replacing the other. This is a genuine substitution lane, not a bonus: it changes WHICH modifier is rolled, so a star that merely narrates it beside Survival would leave the player without the Society number. Under Ruling C the star belongs on both Survival and Society, since after this feat both can perform the named action, and the restriction ('when in an urban area') travels in the `when` text per Ruling B.

A `*` on Acrobatics AND on the Squeeze action (Q2 — star both; Ruling C — every skill that could perform the named action, which for Squeeze is Acrobatics), carrying the text "critical failure becomes failure". The player must see the remap where they look up the number they are about to roll. No flat modifier is owed — this changes an outcome band, not a total.
requirements.clause: When you critically fail at Squeezing, you get a failure instead.

requirements.what: A `*` on every skill that can perform Escape — Acrobatics and Athletics — and on the unarmed-attack option Escape also permits, plus a `*` on the Escape action itself (Ruling C + Ruling H, stay open where the rules are open; Q2, star the skill and the action). The note carries "a success becomes a critical success".
requirements.clause: when you roll a success at an Escape check, you get a critical success instead

requirements.what: Text riding inside the same Escape marker: on a critical success you Step up to 5 feet instead of Striding. Q15 governs — an effect firing on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED, and swapping one 5-foot movement action for another is not. So this is printed, not modelled: no mode, no separate action entry.
requirements.clause: if you roll a critical success, you can Step instead of Striding up to 5 feet

requirements.what: The opening sentence is flavour and requires nothing.
requirements.clause: Your body is almost as flexible as your shadow.

requirements.what: Principle C — this feat changes what ANOTHER record already granted, so the change must be reflected in that thing: Scroll Esoterica's own daily-scroll list must show the added scroll and name this feat as its source. A player who opens Scroll Esoterica and counts its scrolls must get the post-feat count, not the printed base count.
requirements.clause: In addition to your daily scrolls from Scroll Esoterica, add a scroll with a 3rd-rank spell.

requirements.what: The added scroll is chosen at daily preparations, not fixed at build time: an extra scroll slot in the daily-preparation picker whose spell list is filtered to the stated rank (3rd), producing a scroll the player can then cast from and expend. Unpicked, it must read as an empty slot the player can press, not as nothing.
requirements.clause: add a scroll with a 3rd-rank spell

requirements.what: The grant is level-stepped and cumulative: one extra scroll at 3rd rank, a second at 4th rank from level 14, a third at 5th rank from level 16 — so BOTH the number of extra slots and each slot's rank filter are functions of character level. A single fixed extra slot satisfies the feat at level 12 and is wrong at 16. This is the clause most easily read as one grant when it is three.
requirements.clause: At 14th level, add a scroll with a 4th-rank spell. At 16th level, add a scroll with a 5th-rank spell.

requirements.what: Speak with Animals appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, tradition primal, at the spell's own base rank (the text names no rank), with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. The tradition must read as primal beside THIS spell — per Q12 the sheet must not state something false, so the primal label cannot be inferred from whatever tradition the character's other innate grants happen to share.
requirements.clause: You can cast Speak with Animals ... as primal innate spells once per day each.

requirements.what: Status appears as a second, independent innate spell entry — primal, at its own base rank, details reachable, source named. Two spells are granted, not one; a single entry satisfies half the feat.
requirements.clause: You can cast ... Status as primal innate spells once per day each.

requirements.what: "Once per day EACH" — two independent single-use resources, one pip beside each spell, each consumed only by casting its own spell and each restored at daily preparations. A shared pool would be wrong: casting Speak with Animals must leave Status still castable.
requirements.clause: once per day each

requirements.what: The first sentence is flavour and requires nothing.
requirements.clause: Ancestral spirits have begun to bond themselves to you, granting you powers characteristic of a rokoa.

requirements.what: Volcanic Eruption on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, tradition primal, and the entry must read rank 7 — the feat states the rank explicitly, so whatever the spell's own base rank is, 7 is what the player must see. Details reachable, this feat named as source.
requirements.clause: You can cast Volcanic Eruption as a 7th-rank primal innate spell once per day

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use beside the entry, consumed on casting, restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: once per day

requirements.what: The granted spell is NOT the printed spell, and the entry must say so — a marker on this innate Volcanic Eruption carrying both amendments: it can only be evoked on the floor of a body of water, and the effects the spell applies to flying creatures apply to swimming creatures instead. Principle C's shape (a modification must be reflected in the thing modified) applied to a grant that arrives pre-modified. Without it the player opens the entry, reads the unamended spell text, and casts it wrongly. Neither amendment is computable — the water-floor limit is a GM-adjudicated circumstance and the flying/swimming swap lands on targets, not on the sheet — so this is text, but text that is owed.
requirements.clause: except that you can only evoke the volcano on the floor of a body of water, and the effects that normally happen to flying creatures happen to swimming creatures instead

requirements.what: Ruling D / principle C — a marker on the Offer Story action showing this feat adds an alternative benefit the player may choose in place of the normal one, and that the story may be about ANY topic rather than Offer Story's usual subject. The mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, which is Offer Story.
requirements.clause: When you Offer a Story about any topic, you can choose that illumination in place of the normal benefits of Offer Story.

requirements.what: A mode the player switches on when they take the illumination benefit and off when it lapses (Q11 — it can be shut down, and it is optional per use, so it is a mode, not a passive bonus; Q1 — it runs for Offer Story's duration, not one round). Its number is a status bonus to Recall Knowledge checks, and per gold answer #6 and Ruling C it must reach EVERY skill that can Recall Knowledge, not one stat, with the Recall Knowledge action starred too (Q2 — both). Q3's requirement applies: it must be plain that the mode is active and what changed.
requirements.clause: You receive a +1 status bonus on checks to Recall Knowledge for the duration

requirements.what: The bonus is not the constant 1 the text leads with — its value is read off the character's Religion proficiency rank: +1, +2 at master, +3 at legendary. The mode's number must be derived from Religion rank so it rises on its own; a hardcoded +1 is silently wrong for every high-level character.
requirements.clause: The bonus increases to +2 if you are a master of Religion and +3 if you are legendary.

requirements.what: Principle H — an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under BOTH costs. Recall Knowledge must be listed as a free action as well as at its normal cost while this benefit is running, with the explanation in the popup: the free-action version is restricted to the topic of the story. This is a separate promise from the bonus and is the clause most likely to be dropped after the +1 is noticed.
requirements.clause: can Recall Knowledge about the topic of the story as a free action

requirements.what: Ally-facing — no number and no stat on your sheet (Ruling F/N), but principle A still applies: the fact rides as text in the marker on Offer Story, so the player knows the creature they told the story to may take the illumination benefit even when the player themselves did not.
requirements.clause: The creature you share a story with can choose this benefit even if you did not.

requirements.what: The opening sentence is flavour and requires nothing.
requirements.clause: Stories serve as beacons in the night, illuminating valuable knowledge even if the tale itself misses the mark.
Your study of the Beast of Gluttondark has taught you how to make do in the most trying of circumstances rather than succumb to weakness.
requirements.what: Flavour. Requires nothing.

requirements.clause: As long as your current Hit Points are less than half your maximum Hit Points, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival and Stealth checks.
requirements.what: A `*` on Survival AND a separate `*` on Stealth — Principle J puts situational stars on the specific skills named, and both are named, so one star is half the requirement. Each carries +1 circumstance with its `when` = current HP below half of maximum. Ruling B keeps it OUT of the skill's flat total: a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct. Note what the `when` has to be able to say: the threshold is a fraction of THIS character's own maximum HP, not a fixed number, so the star's condition text must resolve against the character (or state the fraction) rather than print a constant. ⚠ This is not the excluded HP case — the decided scope rules that HP and damage never MOVE a sheet stat; here HP is the INPUT to a condition, which is a different shape and not ruled out.

requirements.clause: If your current Hit Points are less than a quarter your maximum Hit Points, the circumstance bonus is +2 instead.
requirements.what: A second tier on the same two skills — +2 circumstance, `when` = current HP below a quarter of maximum. The load-bearing word is "instead": Ruling G says a set or upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so the sheet must be able to express one conditional entry superseding another. Left to the plain stacking-display rule this would go wrong — the two tiers have different `when` strings, and "different `when` → show both" would put +1 and +2 on screen together, which a player can read as +3. So the requirement is a two-step conditional whose lower step disappears once the higher one applies.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** You fail a Reflex save. **Requirements** You can see the night sky.
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (you fail a Reflex save), its requirement (you can see the night sky) and its once-per-day frequency shown in its popup. This is the agreed answer for this feat (exemplar #7, Principle E): the reaction entry is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: The stars warn you of danger in the nick of time. Reroll the failed save and use the new result.
requirements.what: Requires nothing further. The owner ruled this explicitly — "there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way" — so no degree-of-success surface, no fortune marker on Reflex, no star on the save. The reroll is the reaction's own text, already carried by the popup above.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You have completed your active course of action but haven't Dismissed it or chosen a new one.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with this Requirements line reproduced in its popup — the shape the owner set for Minor Omen (Principle E): requirements are written in the popup, not modelled. The requirement names a state that belongs to ANOTHER record (your active course of action), and nothing here asks the sheet to evaluate it; the player reads the line and checks.

requirements.clause: You Dismiss your current course of action
requirements.what: Requires nothing. Dismissing is an internal step of the activity — the app lists the action, the player performs it. Only the action's existence is a lane.

requirements.clause: and gain 15 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour.
requirements.what: A display-only mode the player switches on, showing Close Contract is running. Q1 draws the line at duration: effects lasting 1 round are indication only, "a longer duration gets a mode", and an hour is far past that; Ruling E case 3 gives the same shape for an ongoing effect that changes no numbers. The mode carries text only. ⚠ Flagging the tension rather than resolving it: Q15 says "temporary Hit Points alone are not complicated" and so need no implementation — but Q15 is scoped to the CRITICAL-SUCCESS trigger shape, and this is a deliberate activity, so I read Q1 as governing. If the adjudication goes the other way, this requirement collapses to nothing and only the two below survive.

requirements.clause: gain 15 temporary Hit Points
requirements.what: The temporary Hit Points themselves require no modifier anywhere. HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode — decided scope, stated in terms that cover this exactly.

requirements.clause: The number of temporary Hit Points increases by 5 at 12th level and every 2 levels thereafter.
requirements.what: The number the player reads must be their OWN, not the printed 15 — 15 up to 11th, 20 at 12th, 25 at 14th, 30 at 16th, 35 at 18th, 40 at 20th. So the granted action's displayed text has to carry a level-scaled value rather than static prose. This is computable, unlike a `note`, and the failure mode is silent: a static "15" is wrong for every character from 12th level up and looks perfectly correct.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use shown on the action's entry, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: You can spend 1 minute in focused preparation, then enter a fire your size or larger to instantly teleport to any fire that is your size or larger up to 5 miles away.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with its full text. Its cost is a DURATION — 1 minute of preparation — not a glyph count, so the sheet must be able to list an activity that has no action-cost icon at all and states a time instead. (Principle H covers an action appearing under two glyph costs; this is the neighbouring shape, an action with none.)

requirements.clause: You take no damage from entering or exiting fires when using this ability.
requirements.what: Requires nothing beyond the popup text. Explicitly NOT the `immunity` lane: the protection exists only while using this ability, so a fire immunity or resistance on the defences block would state something false about the character the rest of the time. Ruling B's principle — a restricted effect stays out of the totals — and Ruling I's — where the rules name no general trigger, mark nothing.

requirements.clause: Once you enter the fire, you instantly know the rough locations of other large fires within range and can exit from the original fire, if you prefer.
requirements.what: Requires nothing. Information the GM supplies, and an internal step of the activity.

requirements.clause: You can't carry extradimensional spaces with you when you teleport; if you attempt to do so, the activity fails.
requirements.what: Requires nothing. A failure condition inside the activity, carried by its own text; nothing on the sheet changes and no inventory check is owed.

requirements.clause: You become trained in kineticist class DC
requirements.what: A kineticist class DC must exist on the sheet as its own statistic at trained rank, with a visible number. It is not the character's own class DC — an archetype-granted class DC has to be able to sit ALONGSIDE the one the character's class already gives, keyed to the kineticist's own key attribute rather than to the character's. A sheet that has only one class DC row cannot express this clause.

requirements.clause: and impulse attack rolls.
requirements.what: An impulse attack roll statistic at trained, displayed as a rollable modifier. It is the attack number the Elemental Blast granted below rolls against, so it cannot be prose — a player needs the figure. This is a second, separate statistic from the class DC in the clause above.

requirements.clause: Choose one element to be your kinetic element (air, earth, fire, metal, water, or wood).
requirements.what: A builder choice from six named options, recorded on the character. It must be READABLE by other records, not just displayed: the element decides what the kinetic aura, the Elemental Blast and every later impulse feat actually do, so the pick has to be addressable downstream. Per Q9 the builder shows only what may legally be picked, which here is the whole list of six.

requirements.clause: You gain a kinetic aura
requirements.what: The kinetic aura class feature is granted and its details are surfaced (Principle G — a granted class feature needs its details surfaced). ⚠ Open, and I am flagging rather than assuming: an aura you switch on is the shape Q11 sends to a mode, and Ruling M covers only the positional question (whether an ally stands in it), not the on/off question. This feat's own text does not say the aura toggles, so from the text alone I require only the feature and its details.

requirements.clause: and the Channel Elements action,
requirements.what: Channel Elements appears in the actions list with its details.

requirements.clause: though you don't get to use an Elemental Blast or stance impulse when you take that action.
requirements.what: The restriction must be reflected IN the Channel Elements entry itself, not only in the dedication's own text — Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. A player who opens Channel Elements from the actions list has to see the narrowed archetype version, because that is the only place they will look when they use it. Note the awkward shape: the same feat both grants the action and cuts it down, so the modification targets a thing this record itself created.

requirements.clause: You gain the Elemental Blast action.
requirements.what: Elemental Blast appears as an action, and as an ATTACK — it rolls against the impulse attack statistic required above and deals damage, so it needs a number the player can use, not a description. The following clause talks about its damage dice, which only means anything if those dice are being computed somewhere.

requirements.clause: Your Elemental Blast does not automatically gain additional damage dice every four levels, instead requiring you to take the Improved Elemental Blast feat.
requirements.what: The granted Elemental Blast must be expressible with its every-four-levels damage-dice progression SUPPRESSED, and re-enabled later by a different record (Improved Elemental Blast). So the blast's damage scaling has to be a property that a granting record can switch off and another record can switch back on — two feats reaching into one granted thing's scaling. Silent-failure risk: an unmodified blast simply reads too high at 5th level and up, and looks right.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Nature;
requirements.what: Trained in Nature.

requirements.clause: if you were already trained in Nature, you instead become trained in another skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A redundancy fallback: when Nature is already trained, the grant converts into a free choice of another skill, offered in the builder. Two things are needed — detecting that the base grant is redundant, and then presenting a skill picker in its place. ⚠ Note this fallback is a free choice of ANY other skill, not an upgrade to expert (contrast Guerrilla Dedication, exemplar #15, whose fallback upgrades rank instead); the sheet must express both fallback shapes.

requirements.clause: You can cast Claim Curse. ... You can cast these spells ... as occult innate spells
requirements.what: Claim Curse appears on the spells surface as an INNATE spell, tradition occult, sourced to this feat. The text names no rank for it, so it is cast at the spell's own base rank — nothing to state beyond the grant itself. The tradition must be legible on the entry the player actually reads: Q12 ("whichever spelling leaves the player least confused") forbids the sheet asserting a tradition the spell does not have, and this character may well hold innate grants of other traditions from other sources.

requirements.clause: At 10th level, you can also cast Seal Fate, and at 12th level, you can also cast Inevitable Disaster.
requirements.what: Two further occult innate spells that are level-gated on the CHARACTER's level, not on the feat's own level: Seal Fate from 10th, Inevitable Disaster from 12th. The sheet must be able to hold a grant that is dormant and then switches on at a stated level, and must not offer either spell before that level. This is one feat carrying three separate spell grants with two different gates.

requirements.clause: You can cast these spells once per day
requirements.what: One use per day, spendable at cast time and restored at daily preparations. "These spells" is plural and each is a distinct casting, so the sheet must be able to express one 1/day resource PER granted spell rather than a single pooled use shared across all three — a character at 12th level has three separate once-per-day castings, not one.

requirements.clause: but only while within your curse maelstrom state
requirements.what: An availability gate, not a bonus. All three innate spells are castable only inside the curse maelstrom state — a state you enter and leave, which Q11 settles as a MODE ("if the effect can be shut down, it is a mode"). The requirement is that the granted spell entries be visibly tied to that state: the player must not read them as freely castable innate spells. Q3's shape applies — it must be plain that the state is what makes them available. This is the clause most easily lost, because the grant itself looks like an ordinary innate-spell line.

requirements.clause: If you couldn't already cast occult spells, these spells use Wisdom as your spellcasting attribute
requirements.what: A CONDITIONAL key-attribute assignment: Wisdom governs these innate spells, but only for a character who has no pre-existing occult spellcasting. A character who already casts occult keeps their own attribute. The sheet must be able to express a grant whose applicability is decided by what the character already has (the inverse of the `redundantFallback` shape — grant only if absent, rather than substitute if present), and the resulting spell attack/DC numbers must compute off Wis for the character who takes the conditional branch.

requirements.clause: and you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in BOTH the spell attack modifier and the spell DC, under the same "if you couldn't already cast occult spells" condition as the attribute clause. The consequence is structural: a character with no spellcasting class must still end up with populated spell attack and spell DC rows, keyed to Wisdom, so that the innate spells above have a number to roll and a DC to impose. Two statistics, not one.

requirements.clause: You can cast Translocate as a 4th-rank divine innate spell
requirements.what: Translocate appears as an INNATE spell, tradition divine, cast at RANK 4. The rank is stated explicitly in the text and is not Translocate's base rank, so it must be carried as an explicit heightened rank on the grant — an entry that renders at the spell's native rank is wrong here, and the player reads the rank to know the range/effect they get.

requirements.clause: at will
requirements.what: Unlimited uses. The entry must positively read as at-will, with no per-day pip and nothing consumed when cast. This is the opposite of the default 1/day shape most innate grants take, so silence is not enough — the sheet needs an affirmative at-will marker or the player will assume a daily limit.

requirements.clause: When you do, spaces adjacent to the one you leave from and the one you appear in are momentarily filled with a damaging energy common to your realm, dealing damage of your realm's damage type to creatures in the affected spaces
requirements.what: A rider that fires every time the granted spell is used. The damage lands on other creatures and on the battlefield, which DECIDED SCOPE settles as producing no number on your sheet; by the Q4 shape the granted entry itself is the whole surface. But the rider is NOT free of requirement: it must be readable on the Translocate entry the feat grants, because the player would otherwise cast a plain Translocate and never learn the burst exists. ⚠ Added by me, not ruled on by the owner: the text says "your realm's damage type", which presumes the character's planar realm — and therefore its damage type — is a recorded value. Either the sheet can resolve that reference to a concrete type, or the clause must be printed verbatim so the player supplies it; it must not silently render as a blank.

requirements.clause: ( save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher)
requirements.what: No requirement. The save is rolled by the creature caught in the burst, not by you, so no DC-side surface is owed under Ruling D (a skill/target DC gets no surface; the player remembers). "Whichever is higher" asks the player to compare two numbers that are already stat rows on their sheet — class DC and spell DC — so nothing new must be expressed to make the clause usable.

requirements.clause: Free and Fair Source Kingmaker Adventure Path pg. 531
requirements.what: No requirement. A bibliographic header that has been captured into the body of the text — the feat's own name and a source citation. It is not a mechanical clause and carries no lane; the only thing owed is that it not be read as part of the feat's rules text.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Loyalty-based checks attempted as part of the New Leadership and Pledge of Fealty activities.
requirements.what: A +2 circumstance bonus that is restricted twice over — to Loyalty-based checks, and further to two NAMED activities (New Leadership, Pledge of Fealty). Under Ruling B a restricted flat bonus belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, never folded into a stat total, and Q2 settles that it is marked in BOTH places: a star on the Loyalty statistic where the player reads the number, and a marker on each of the two named activities. ⚠ The statistic here is a KINGDOM statistic, not a personal one: the requirement this feat really imposes is that a kingdom-side stat and kingdom-side activities be able to carry situational stars at all, exactly as a skill row does.

requirements.clause: If you fail or critically fail such a check, you can spend 2 RP to reroll the check (but without the +2 circumstance bonus); attempting this adds the Fortune trait. You must take the result of the second roll, even if it is worse than the original roll.
requirements.what: A player-elected reroll, gated on a failure degree, paid for with 2 Resource Points, granting the fortune trait, and with the +2 above explicitly NOT applying to the reroll. It is not complicated in the Q15 sense (no state to apply, no duration), so it needs no separate mechanism — but it must ride in the note of the same star as the +2, the way The Truth as I See it folds its once-per-day reroll into the Deception star. The player has to be able to read "reroll without the bonus" at the moment they are looking at the bonus, or they will apply +2 to the second roll. The 2 RP spend comes out of the kingdom's own resource pool; this feat owes no new spendable-resource surface of its own.

requirements.clause: your choice of Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore
requirements.what: A recorded two-option pick between Spirit Lore and Haunt Lore. The pick is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: everything else this feat does is keyed to whichever Lore was chosen, so the choice must be stored and readable, not left implicit. Per Q9 the builder offers only the two options the feat names, and per principle K re-choosing is a builder action needing no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: You can use your choice of Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore to Make an Impression or Request things of incorporeal creatures.
requirements.what: The chosen Lore stands in for the skill that normally performs Make an Impression and Request (Diplomacy), for TWO actions, and only against incorporeal creatures. The restriction is part of the substitution and must travel with it — an unconditional "Lore replaces Diplomacy" would be wrong, and so would a substitution that covers only one of the two named actions.

requirements.clause: to Make an Impression or Request things of incorporeal creatures
requirements.what: A marker where the player looks when it matters (Ruling D, Q8: mark the action the feat modifies). Both Make an Impression and Request must carry a marker naming the alternative skill and the incorporeal-only condition, and the chosen Lore's own row must carry one too, since that is where the player reads the number they would actually roll. Ruling C's principle applies in mirror image here: the feat is named after actions, so every skill that could now perform them is marked.

requirements.clause: At the GM's discretion, an incorporeal spirit might be willing to hear you out.
requirements.what: No requirement. Explicit GM adjudication, which the lane manual excludes by name. It is flavour attached to the substitution above and needs no surface of its own.

requirements.clause: Your experience in the finer points of bargaining with a devil has awakened a sinister power that now inhabits your left eye. The eye is the same shape and iris color as your normal eye would be, but the sclera is a deep red instead of white and the pupil is a narrow, vertical slit.
requirements.what: No requirement. Pure appearance flavour — no mechanical promise, nothing to express.

requirements.clause: You gain the Objection reaction.
requirements.what: Objection appears in the reactions list as a reaction, with its own trigger and requirements shown in its popup. Principle E settles that this is often the entire requirement, and it is here. The grant presupposes an Objection record exists to point at and is reachable from the feat — a named grant with nothing on the other end is invisible to the player.

requirements.clause: You also become an expert in Legal Lore
requirements.what: Legal Lore present on the skills list at EXPERT rank. Note the shape: the feat does not say "trained", so for a character who does not already have Legal Lore this must both create the Lore and set it to expert in one step — a grant that only adds a trained Lore, or one that only upgrades an existing entry, gets the wrong number.

requirements.clause: gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any check you make to read or negotiate a treatise, contract, or similar text
requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus whose trigger the book deliberately leaves open — "any check", "or similar text". Ruling H governs: stay open, star every skill plausibly used to read or negotiate a document (Legal Lore, Society, and the Diplomacy side of negotiating are all plausible) and put the printed trigger in the note, rather than narrowing it to one skill and thereby printing a ruling of ours dressed as the book's. Ruling B keeps the +1 out of any stat total.

requirements.clause: At 7th level you become a master of Legal Lore, and at 15th level you become legendary in Legal Lore.
requirements.what: Two further level-keyed steps on the same Lore — master at character level 7, legendary at 15 — so this feat carries a three-step progression (expert / master / legendary), not a single grant. Ruling G requires each step to REPLACE the entry it upgrades rather than sit beside it: at level 7 the sheet reads master, never "expert, plus a note saying master at 7th".

requirements.clause: You can use Legal Lore in place of Perception to detect verbal loopholes, double entendres, hidden meanings, code, or contradictions in a conversation you can hear.
requirements.what: Legal Lore substitutes for PERCEPTION — a substitution across statistic kinds, not skill-for-skill — restricted to detecting loopholes, hidden meanings, code or contradictions in a conversation you can hear. The restriction must travel with the substitution, and Perception must carry a marker naming the alternative, because Perception is where the player looks up the number and would otherwise never learn the option exists.

requirements.clause: This doesn't let you fully understand coded speech but alerts you to its presence.
requirements.what: No separate requirement. A limitation on the outcome of the Perception substitution above; it changes no number and needs no surface of its own, but it belongs inside that substitution's note so the player does not over-read what the swap buys them.

A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (an opponent casts a spell and you critically succeed at a saving throw against it) and its requirement (a shield raised, or benefiting from Dueling Parry or Twin Parry) shown in its popup. Principle E / exemplar #7 (Minor Omen): for a trigger-plus-requirement reaction this is normally the whole surface, and the requirement line must be readable there because the player has to check it at the moment the trigger fires.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** An opponent casts a spell and you critically succeed at a saving throw against it. **Requirements** You have a shield raised or are benefiting from Dueling Parry or Twin Parry. --- You attempt to counteract the triggering spell...

requirements.what: The reaction's popup must state that this counteract check is rolled with the attack modifier of the shield or parrying weapon rather than any spellcasting modifier. The number itself is one the sheet already carries on that weapon's strike entry, so what is owed is the instruction sitting beside the reaction, not a new stat row and not a new counteract-check surface.
requirements.clause: Use your attack roll modifier with your shield or parrying weapon for your counteract check.

requirements.what: The reflected spell's save DC becomes your class DC and its spell attack roll uses the same weapon attack modifier as the counteract check. Both are values read off rows the sheet already has, so the requirement is that the reaction's popup says which to use. No new DC row is owed: Ruling D's DC treatment governs the DC of your OWN abilities appearing in a save breakdown, and this is the reflected spell's DC being borrowed from a stat you already display.
requirements.clause: If the spell has a save DC, it uses your class DC, and if it requires a spell attack roll, use the same attack roll modifier as the counteract check.

requirements.what: Nothing. The reflection and all its retargeting rules land on the caster and on battlefield geometry. DECIDED SCOPE puts effects on enemies and on the battlefield off your sheet, and Q4 makes the reaction entry the whole surface for exactly this shape; the printed text inside the popup is sufficient. Note also that although the trigger is a critical success, Q15 does not pull this toward a mode - the effect is a reaction resolved immediately against someone else, not a state the player applies to themselves.
requirements.clause: If you counteract the spell, it is reflected upon the caster. If the spell targeted individual creatures, it targets the caster only. If the spell targeted an area centered on a point, the new area is centered on the caster. If the spell was a cone or line, the cone or line emanates from you toward the caster.

requirements.what: Nothing. An access clause is not mechanical - 'prerequisites, access clauses' are listed under NOT lanes, and Q5 settles that access wording earns no surface.
requirements.clause: **Access** You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.

requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus that must NOT be folded into any flat save total (Ruling B - a bonus the rules restrict lives in the situational lane with the restriction carried in its condition text). It applies to saves generally rather than to one named save, so Q2 governs: star all three of Fortitude, Reflex and Will, each carrying 'against visual effects' as the condition, because any of the three can be called for against a visual effect.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against visual effects.

requirements.what: A degree-of-success upgrade the app cannot compute - it changes no number, so it must be readable as text in the same star's note on all three saves, which is where the player is looking when a visual effect makes them roll. It earns no separate stat surface and no mode: nothing here is toggled and nothing has a duration.
requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a saving throw against a visual effect, you get a critical success instead.

requirements.what: A recorded, persistent pick of one eidolon unarmed attack. The option list must be filtered to the unarmed attacks this character's eidolon actually has that carry the grapple trait - Q9: the builder offers only what the player may legally pick. The pick has to persist and be re-readable because the next clause attaches to whichever attack was chosen.
requirements.clause: Choose one of the eidolon's unarmed attacks with the grapple trait.

requirements.what: Grab shows as an action on the chosen unarmed attack in the EIDOLON's stat block, attached to that one attack and not to all of them. It belongs to the eidolon, not to the summoner: DECIDED SCOPE (companions) rules that a companion-facing effect marks the companion and that absence from the character's own sheet is correct. So what is owed is the entry on the eidolon's attack - nothing on the summoner's own actions list.
requirements.clause: It gains the Grab action on that unarmed attack.

requirements.what: Three separate language picks offered in the builder. The option list is the common languages plus the uncommon languages this character has access to, and it must exclude languages the character already knows, since the text grants NEW languages. Q9 governs the filtering - the builder shows only what the player may legally pick. Per Principle K, re-choosing is a builder action and needs no sheet control.
requirements.clause: You learn three new languages, chosen from common languages and uncommon languages you have access to.

requirements.what: The three chosen languages appear in the character's Languages list on the sheet, attributable to this feat. The pick alone is not enough - the result has to land where the player reads their languages.
requirements.clause: You learn three new languages, chosen from common languages and uncommon languages you have access to. (the resulting languages, as opposed to the picking of them)

requirements.what: Nothing. It restates the form (signed or spoken) the character's existing languages already take; it moves no number and adds no row.
requirements.clause: These languages take the same form (signed or spoken) as your other languages.

requirements.what: AMBIGUOUS IN THE SUPPLIED TEXT - flagged, not assumed. Read one way, 'the feat' means this feat and the sentence merely restates the count already given, in which case NOTHING further is owed and the sheet should show the single count that leaves the player least confused (Q12), i.e. three, never both numbers. Read the other way, 'the feat' is a DIFFERENT record that grants two languages, and this clause raises that record's grant to three - under that reading Principle C applies: the change must be reflected in the thing it modifies, so that other record's language picker offers three slots and its entry shows it was modified by this feat. The text as given does not name the other record, so the referent must be resolved before anything is built.
requirements.clause: When you select the feat, you learn three new languages instead of two.

requirements.what: A +2 circumstance star wherever the player looks up an Aid number. Q2: both - star the Aid ACTION's own entry and star the skills. Ruling C: a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it, and Aid names no skill at all, so Ruling H applies - stay open and star every skill rather than narrowing to a guess, with 'on checks to Aid' as the condition. The printed Aid rule also permits an attack roll as the check, so the same star belongs on Strikes under the same open-rules reasoning. It must not enter any flat skill total (Ruling B), because it applies only to that one use.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Aid.

requirements.what: A critical-failure floor the app cannot compute - it changes no number, so it must read as text in the same star's note and in the Aid action's popup, so the player sees it at the moment they roll the Aid check. No separate surface, and not a mode: nothing is toggled and nothing has a duration.
requirements.clause: If you roll a critical failure on a check to Aid, you get a failure instead.
You can Hide and Sneak even without cover or being concealed.
requirements.what: A `*` on Stealth AND on the Hide and Sneak actions themselves (Q2 — star both the skill and the action), carrying the clause. What must be expressible here is a LIFTED REQUIREMENT, not a bonus: the normal precondition of those two actions (cover or concealment) is removed for this character. No number joins the Stealth total, so the marker has to be able to say something other than '+N' — a prose condition attached to the action. Ruling C is what forces the star onto every skill that could perform the named action rather than onto one.

requirements.clause: When you employ an exploration tactic other than Avoiding Notice, you also gain the benefits of Avoiding Notice unless you choose not to.
requirements.what: A `*` on Avoid Notice, reachable from wherever exploration tactics are listed — that is the place the player looks when choosing a tactic, so Ruling D puts the mark there rather than on a general stat. It must state that Avoid Notice's benefits ride along with any OTHER tactic the character is running, i.e. the marker belongs to the other tactics as much as to Avoid Notice.

requirements.clause: unless you choose not to
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. An opt-out exercised at the table, per-instance, with no stored consequence — not a `choice`, not a toggle. Nothing is owed beyond the words appearing in the marker above.

requirements.clause: When you hold your breath, you can do so for an additional hour.
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to attach a duration change to the hold-your-breath/suffocation rule itself — Ruling D's shape, the same way The Survivor marks the Dying condition. No stat row moves and no number is computable into any total; the requirement is that '+1 hour of held breath' is legible at the point the player looks breath-holding up, not only buried in the feat's own text. If the sheet has no surface for that rule, the requirement is that one exists to hang this on.

requirements.clause: At the end of this hour, your body needs to rest before it can recycle air again. This rest requires 10 minutes of exposure to breathable air.
requirements.what: Text only, carried in the same marker as the clause above. This is a recharge condition measured in minutes of exposure to air, NOT a per-day resource — so no pip, no counter, no per-day use is owed. Durations of this granularity are not tracked, and Principle B is the governing shape: the player must still be able to READ the limitation even though nothing computes it.

requirements.clause: When you cast the Heal spell to heal a single creature, choose another willing living creature within range of your *heal* to regain Hit Points equal to the *heal* spell's rank.
requirements.what: A marker on the HEAL SPELL showing this feat modifies it — Principle A applied exactly as in the Resilient Touch / Amplifying Touch exemplars. The healing lands on a different creature, so Ruling F means no number reaches this character's sheet, but the player must see on Heal itself that the second recipient exists. The marker's text must carry both the gating condition (only the single-target casting of Heal, not the burst) and the amount (Hit Points equal to the spell's rank), since the amount scales with the rank the spell is cast at and cannot be reduced to a fixed figure.

requirements.clause: choose another willing living creature within range
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT beyond the marker above. Picking the recipient is a per-cast table decision, not a stored choice; and Hit Points never move sheet stats in any case (Ruling E). No target model, no range check, no `choice` field is owed.

requirements.clause: You teleport your bonded item or spellbook to you.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear as its own entry in the actions list with its action cost, and its full text in the popup. Principle E's shape applied to an activity rather than a reaction: the entry IS the surface, and nothing else on the sheet changes.

requirements.clause: It arrives in your hand if you have a free hand or at your feet if you don't.
requirements.what: NO SEPARATE REQUIREMENT — resolution prose printed inside the action's popup. Nothing is computed and no hand/held-item state needs consulting; the player and GM resolve where it lands.

requirements.clause: The item must be within 1 mile and have 1 Bulk or less.
requirements.what: A usage restriction that must be printed WITH the action, in the same place Minor Omen's Requirements line lives (Principle E). No inventory filtering, no gating of which item may be named, and no distance model is owed — the constraint only has to be readable at the moment the player uses the action.

requirements.clause: You enter a tight stance, coiled up like a lashing cobra with your hands poised as venomous fangs.
requirements.what: A toggleable stance mode — Q11 decides it: the effect can be shut down, so it is a mode and not a passive bonus. It must be mutually exclusive with other stances, and it must make plain both THAT it is active and WHAT it changed (Q3's visibility requirement). Every clause below lives inside it and none of them may apply while it is off.

requirements.clause: While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are cobra fang unarmed attacks.
requirements.what: The mode must be able to express a RESTRICTION, not only additions: while it is on, every other Strike the character has is unavailable. This must be visible where the player reads their Strikes list — a mode that can only add rows and bonuses cannot say this, so the requirement is either suppression of the other Strikes or an unmissable statement beside them.

requirements.clause: These deal 1d4 piercing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, deadly d10, finesse, unarmed, and venomous traits.
requirements.what: A cobra fang unarmed Strike, existing only while the stance is on, carrying: damage 1d4 piercing; weapon group brawling; and all five traits — agile, deadly d10, finesse, unarmed, venomous. Three of those change the strike's own numbers and so must be live rather than decorative: agile (reduced multiple-attack penalty), finesse (attack may use Dexterity), deadly d10 (extra die on a critical hit). Brawling group is load-bearing for critical specialization. Venomous must at minimum be carried and readable.

requirements.clause: While in Cobra Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves
requirements.what: +1 circumstance bonus to the Fortitude save, applied inside the mode and typed as circumstance so it stacks correctly against other circumstance sources.

requirements.clause: and your Fortitude DC
requirements.what: A SECOND, separate surface: the same +1 must also reach the Fortitude DC. Ruling D's DC-only shape governs — an entry in that save's breakdown worded to say it raises the DC rather than the check, with a star beside the DC. The requirement is that the sheet can express a save DC as a thing modifiable independently of the save check; one clause here promises two numbers.

requirements.clause: and you gain poison resistance equal to half your level.
requirements.what: Poison resistance whose value is half the character's level — a level-scaling formula, not a fixed number, so it must recompute as the character levels rather than being frozen at the level the stance was authored for. Inside the mode; gone when the stance ends.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** Your target is Doomed 2 or greater. --- You finish your target with a vicious attack. Make a Strike against the target… This is an incapacitation effect.
requirements.what: Slay must appear as a usable activity in the actions list, with its Requirements line ("Your target is Doomed 2 or greater") and its incapacitation trait visible in its popup along with the full effect text. Per Principle E's shape (Minor Omen), the entry plus its trigger/requirement text is normally the entire surface for an action-shaped feat.

requirements.clause: Make a Strike against the target.
requirements.what: Nothing. The internal steps of an activity are explicitly not a lane — the sheet lists the action and the player performs the Strike. This is not grantsStrike (no new attack is granted) and not weaponRider (no weapon's statistics change).

requirements.clause: If you hit, the target takes 4d6 extra precision damage with a save against your class DC. If the target critically fails, they die.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the text in the action's popup. The damage lands on an enemy, and damage never moves sheet stats (Ruling E). The class DC is only *referenced* as the save DC, not modified, so Ruling D's DC-only provision is not triggered — no entry in a save breakdown and no star is owed. The death-on-critical-failure result is an enemy-side degree-of-success outcome.

requirements.clause: The creature then becomes temporarily immune to your Slay for 1 day.
requirements.what: Nothing. This is explicitly NOT limitedUses: it does not cap how often the character may use Slay, only how often against the same creature. Per-target temporary immunity is bookkeeping on the enemy, which is out of scope.

requirements.clause: When using the Scout exploration activity, you grant your allies a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls instead of a +1 circumstance bonus.
requirements.what: An indication on the Scout exploration activity itself that this feat raises the bonus Scout grants from +1 to +2, with this feat named as the reason. Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — and Principle A — an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies (the Lay on Hands shape). The value shown where the player reads Scout must be the upgraded one, not the base +1 sitting unchanged beside an unread feat.

requirements.clause: …you grant your allies a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls…
requirements.what: No number on the character's own initiative. Ruling F: a bonus that goes to a teammate produces nothing on your sheet — no star, no modifier. ⚠ Flag, not an assumption: the text as printed upgrades only the ally-facing half and does not restate whether the scouting character shares Scout's bonus; on this text alone the feat contributes nothing to your own initiative, so if Scout's own wording includes the scout, that is Scout's requirement to carry, not this feat's.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** A rope is within your reach, or you have a rope or grappling weapon in your hand. --- You take hold of a nearby rope… and then swing up to twice your Speed. You can make a Strike using a one-handed weapon or unarmed attack at any point during this movement.
requirements.what: Halyard Strike must appear as a usable activity in the actions list, with its Requirements line (a rope within reach, or a rope/grappling weapon in hand) and the weapon restriction (one-handed weapon or unarmed attack) legible in its popup. Principle E's shape: the entry with its requirement is the base surface.

requirements.clause: …and then swing up to twice your Speed.
requirements.what: Nothing as a lane. This is movement *inside* an activity, not a granted movement type, so it is not `speed` and not `speedBonus`. It must, however, survive as printed text — the distance is a formula off the character's own Speed, so it cannot be reduced to a fixed number in the popup.

requirements.clause: If you critically fail on this Strike, your movement ends at the point you attempted the Strike.
requirements.what: Nothing. A degree-of-success outcome that resolves position on the battlefield; prose in the popup only.

requirements.clause: **Special** If you have Pirate Dedication and you boarded or disembarked from a boat or similar vehicle during this movement, the Strike deals one additional weapon damage die.
requirements.what: A conditional extra weapon damage die, marked on the Halyard Strike entry — the thing it modifies (Ruling D). It cannot be a flat damage bump: half the condition (boarding or disembarking a vehicle during this movement) is a circumstance only the player knows, so it must be a `*`/rider carrying the trigger text (Ruling H — stay open, printed trigger in the note). The other half means the sheet must be able to express a rider gated on the character possessing a *named other feat* (Pirate Dedication), which is knowable from the character's own build.

requirements.clause: Access You're from the Shackles. / Source High Seas pg. 93.
requirements.what: Nothing. Access clauses and source lines are not lanes; Q5 settles that an access clause needs no surface.

requirements.clause: You beseech warrior spirits to come forth and aid you. Two ghostly warriors manifest within a [range] of you and each attempt a Strike against an adjacent enemy…
requirements.what: The Dead Walk must appear as a usable activity in the actions list with its full effect text in its popup (Principle E's shape). ⚠ The printed text supplied is defective — "manifest within a of you" has lost its emanation distance — so whatever surfaces this cannot state a range from this text; a complete range must come from the source, not be invented.

requirements.clause: …each attempt a Strike against an adjacent enemy, using your spell attack modifier. The warriors' Strikes each deal 4d6 damage.
requirements.what: Nothing. The warriors are transient summons, not companions, and they roll off a statistic the sheet already carries (your spell attack modifier) — referenced, not modified, so no star on it is owed. Their damage lands on enemies, and damage never moves sheet stats (Ruling E). No stat block and no companion entry.

requirements.clause: …the warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies.
requirements.what: Nothing. Flanking is positional and ally-facing — battlefield state the app can never know (the reasoning behind Ruling M) and an effect landing on someone else (Ruling F).

requirements.clause: If you are Cursebound 2 when you use The Dead Walk, you instead summon three warriors, and if you are cursebound 3, you instead summon four warriors.
requirements.what: The action's own effect scales off a state of the character's own — their Cursebound value — so the sheet must be able to express an action whose printed result varies by a self-state, with all three tiers legible where the player reads the action (Ruling G: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). This is self-facing, not an ally or enemy effect, so none of the DECIDED SCOPE exclusions removes it; if the Cursebound value is tracked, the tier that applies is the one that matters to the player at the moment of use.

requirements.clause: The warriors disappear at the start of your next turn.
requirements.what: Nothing. A duration under one round. Q1: effects lasting 1 round are not implemented — indication only, no mode.

requirements.clause: You can more easily navigate underground tunnels by rolling up into a ball. You roll up and move up to four times your Speed in a straight line down an incline.
requirements.what: Tunnel Roll must appear as a usable activity in the actions list with its full text in its popup, including the terrain condition (a straight line down an incline).

requirements.clause: …move up to four times your Speed in a straight line down an incline. If you reach the bottom of the incline or hit an obstacle during this first turn of movement, you stop rolling.
requirements.what: Nothing as a lane. This is movement inside an activity, not a granted movement type (`speed`) and not a Speed bonus. It must survive as text because the distance is a multiple of the character's own Speed, and the stopping conditions are terrain the app cannot know.

requirements.clause: Otherwise, you automatically keep rolling at this Speed during subsequent turns until you hit the bottom of the incline or an obstacle ends this movement… You're Slowed 2 each turn after the first that you keep rolling.
requirements.what: A toggleable rolling state the player turns on and off. It runs across an indefinite number of turns — far past one round, so Q1 puts it past indication-only — and the rules can shut it down (reaching the bottom, or an obstacle), which Q11 settles as a mode rather than a passive. The mode must carry Slowed 2 applied to the character themselves (self-facing, so no scope exclusion applies) plus the text of what continues each turn, and it must be plain that the mode is active and what it changed (Q3's principle).

requirements.clause: …if you hit an obstacle on a turn after the first, you and the obstacle both take 4d6 damage, and you stop rolling.
requirements.what: Nothing. HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode (Ruling E) — so the self-damage gets no surface beyond the mode's text — and the obstacle is not on the character's sheet.

requirements.clause: "You transform into a small bird… You can Dismiss the effect to return to your normal shape, and you resume your normal shape automatically if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points."
requirements.what: A battle form is a MODE (Q3). It must be toggleable on and off — Dismiss is the off switch — and while it is on the sheet must make plain that a mode is active and what changed, because every statistic below is a replacement rather than an addition. The auto-revert at 0 HP is text inside the mode; HP never moves sheet stats (Ruling E), so it contributes no number, only the printed condition.

requirements.clause: "You become Tiny"
requirements.what: The mode must set the character's size to Tiny for as long as it runs, and restore the printed size when it ends. A set, not a step (Ruling G — a set replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it).

requirements.clause: "gain the animal trait"
requirements.what: An acquired creature trait must be recorded on the sheet (Q6 — the Details tab already carries tags), and it must be acquired only while the mode is active. ⚠ No lane in the manual covers a creature trait gained from a record; Q6 names the surface but section F has no key for it.

requirements.clause: "AC = 20 + your level"
requirements.what: An AC OVERRIDE, not a bonus: while the mode runs, AC is exactly 20 + character level, and the character's armour, Dex and other AC contributors do not apply. Q3 requires the mode to "really override" the stats it names, so the AC row must show the overridden value and be legible as overridden, not as the normal total with a modifier bolted on.

requirements.clause: "Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction."
requirements.what: While the mode runs, the worn armour's check penalty and its Speed reduction are both suppressed to zero wherever they are applied — on skill checks that take the penalty, and on Speed. ⚠ `armorStats` is the item-only lane for an armour's OWN numbers; there is no listed lane for a non-item record suppressing the wearer's armour penalties, so this may be a lane that has never been built.

requirements.clause: "Fly speed 25 feet."
requirements.what: A fly Speed of 25 feet while the mode runs. A flat printed number with no dependency on the character's own Speed, so per Q7 it needs no `*` — the mode being visibly active already carries the condition.

requirements.clause: "Weakness 5 to physical damage."
requirements.what: Weakness 5 to physical damage while the mode runs, reaching the defences display. This is a weakness the character genuinely acquires, so it must appear alongside their resistances and immunities and not only inside the mode's prose.

requirements.clause: "Low-light vision and imprecise scent 30 feet."
requirements.what: Low-light vision and imprecise scent 30 feet while the mode runs. Per Q13, if the character already has darkvision, show only darkvision rather than listing a low-light grant that supersedes nothing; the imprecise scent with its 30-foot range is additive and must appear regardless.

requirements.clause: "Acrobatics and Stealth modifiers of +10, unless your own is higher; Athletics modifier –4."
requirements.what: The mode must SET final skill modifiers, not add to them: Acrobatics and Stealth become +10 unless the character's own total is higher (take-the-higher, the same shape Q10 endorses — only apply the remap when it makes the player better), and Athletics becomes exactly –4 unconditionally, even when the character's own is far better. ⚠ No lane in the manual sets a skill's final modifier — sections A and J only grant proficiency, flat bonuses, or situational stars. This looks like a lane that has never been built.

requirements.clause: "you can't make Strikes"
requirements.what: While the mode runs the character has no Strikes at all; the strikes list must be empty or plainly disabled rather than continuing to offer the weapon and unarmed attacks the form cannot make. ⚠ Section F has `grantsStrike` but no lane for removing strikes — a probable unbuilt lane.

requirements.clause: "When Administering First Aid, Treating Disease, or Treating Wounds… you gain a +1 item bonus to your Medicine check."
requirements.what: A `*` on Medicine carrying the +1 ITEM bonus and its trigger. The bonus type is load-bearing for stacking (it must not stack with another item bonus to the same check). Per Ruling B a bonus the rules restrict belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, not in the flat total — three named activities only, and only when the character pays the cost.

requirements.clause: "When Administering First Aid, Treating Disease, or Treating Wounds"
requirements.what: Q2 says BOTH: as well as the skill, the three named activities themselves must each be marked — Administer First Aid, Treat Disease, Treat Wounds — so the player sees the modification where they look the action up. Ruling D's shape: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters.

requirements.clause: "you can take 1 damage to give someone a drop of your blood. When you do so, you don't need healer's tools"
requirements.what: Two non-numeric clauses that must ride in the same star's text: the cost (take 1 damage) and the waiver (the activities' healer's-tools requirement does not apply). The 1 damage moves no sheet stat — Ruling E, HP and damage never move sheet stats — so it is printed as a condition, not modelled. The tools waiver removes a requirement printed on ANOTHER record's activity, so it must be legible on those activities and not only on the feat.

requirements.clause: "If someone were to eat your heart and liver within an hour of your death, they would be healed of all physical injuries… and would cease to age for 8 years."
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. The effect lands entirely on another creature, after the character's death, and it modifies none of the character's own abilities — so Principle A's "indication on the record it modifies" has no record to attach to, and Ruling F leaves nothing on the sheet. The feat's own description already tells the player; this is GM-adjudicated narrative.

requirements.clause: "the GM uses the number rolled or 10—whichever is higher—as the result of your die roll, adding it to your Stealth modifier"
requirements.what: A `*` on Stealth carrying a MINIMUM DIE RESULT — not a bonus to the modifier. The distinction is load-bearing and must survive into the note: the floor applies to the d20 result before the modifier is added, so it cannot be expressed as "+N". Restricted to one circumstance (a passive observer noticing a small concealed item), so it belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when` (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: "a small item you've concealed"
requirements.what: Q2 says both the skill and the action: the Conceal an Object action must also carry the mark, since that is the activity whose outcome this feat changes and is where the player looks when it matters (Ruling D).

requirements.clause: "If you're a master in Stealth, the GM uses the number rolled or 15, and if you're legendary in Stealth, you automatically succeed at hiding a small concealed item from passive observers."
requirements.what: The star's value must key off the character's CURRENT Stealth proficiency rank: floor 10 while trained or expert, floor 15 at master, and automatic success — no roll at all — at legendary. A star whose text is fixed at 10 states something false for a master or legendary character; per Q12 the wording must be the one that leaves the player least confused, so the note must either resolve to the character's actual rank or print all three tiers.

requirements.clause: "This provides no benefits when a creature attempts a Perception check while actively searching you for hidden items."
requirements.what: The exclusion must ride inside the same star's `when`/note rather than becoming a separate surface. It narrows an already-narrow trigger; per Ruling H the printed trigger goes in the note rather than being resolved into a ruling on the sheet.

requirements.clause: "**PFS Note** This feat allows you to Earn Income with Underworld Lore with tasks of your level -1 (instead of the normal level -2)."
requirements.what: A `*` on Underworld Lore and on the Earn Income activity carrying the level −1 task clause (Q2 — both the skill and the action; Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing being looked at). ⚠ Two caveats for whoever specifies this: it is an organized-play-only clause and may be out of scope by policy, and it is conditional on the character actually having Underworld Lore, so the skill-side star has nothing to attach to otherwise.

requirements.clause: "By taking an impressive stance… Each creature in a [area] must attempt a save…"
requirements.what: Majestic Presence must exist as a named activity in the actions list, with its area, its save, and its full degree-of-success text in the popup. ⚠ The supplied text is defective — the area is missing ("each creature in a" with no emanation size, and no save type named), so the record cannot be built faithfully from this text alone; the printed area and save type must be recovered from the source before the action is authored.

requirements.clause: "a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC"
requirements.what: The action's popup must show the DC actually in force, resolved as max(your class DC, your spell DC) — a computed number off two of the character's own statistics, not a static value, and it must degrade correctly to the class DC alone for a character with no spellcasting. This is a number the player reads off their own sheet, so leaving "the higher of your class DC or spell DC" as unresolved prose is not sufficient.

requirements.clause: "**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected. **Success** The creature is Frightened 1. **Failure** The creature is Frightened 2. **Critical Failure** The creature is Frightened 4."
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT beyond the action entry itself. Every outcome is a condition on an ENEMY, which DECIDED SCOPE excludes, and Q4 settles the shape: the entry is the whole surface, with the outcome prose readable in its popup. No degree-of-success machinery is owed.

requirements.clause: "Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to your Majestic Presence for 24 hours."
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Temporary immunity is tracked per enemy creature, not on the character's sheet; it is neither a use the character spends nor a resource that recharges for them, so it is NOT `limitedUses` and must not be modelled as a per-day pip. It is printed text in the action's popup.

requirements.clause: "You gain a climb Speed of 15 feet."
requirements.what: A climb Speed of 15 feet on the movement display. Permanent, unconditional, and a flat printed number that does not derive from the character's own Speed — so per Q7 it takes NO `*`; the star is reserved for a conditional or formula-derived movement type such as Wyrmling Flight's. This is the feat's only mechanical clause; the opening sentence is flavour and requires nothing.

requirements.clause: Prerequisites Ki Strike; you follow a deity
requirements.what: Prerequisites are not a lane and need no surface of their own. Recorded here only because the deity prerequisite is the data the next clause's filter has to read — the picker below cannot be built without knowing the character's deity and its alignment components.

requirements.clause: When you select this feat, choose chaos, evil, good, or law. Your choice must match one of your deity's alignment components.
requirements.what: A build-time choice of one damage type from chaotic / evil / good / lawful, recorded on the character and readable afterwards, because every later clause names it ("your chosen alignment"). Per Q9 the picker must offer only the components of the character's own deity's alignment — the other options are not legally pickable — unless the player toggles "show options not meeting prerequisites". Per Principle K, re-choosing is a builder action and needs no sheet surface of its own; what the sheet needs is the chosen value showing up inside the markers below.

requirements.clause: When you cast the ki strike focus spell and damage a creature whose alignment is opposite your chosen alignment, you can choose for the ki strike damage to be of the chosen type.
requirements.what: The Ki Strike focus spell — a thing another record granted — must itself carry an indication that this feat changes it (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). The marker states that the spell's damage may instead be dealt as the recorded alignment type, and carries the printed condition (target of an opposite alignment) in its note. This is an OPTION offered, never an automatic damage-type swap: the target's alignment is enemy-side and the sheet can never know it, and the text says "you can choose".

requirements.clause: Additionally, you can substitute the damage from ki blast (or other ki spells that deal force damage, at the GM's discretion) with damage of your chosen alignment.
requirements.what: The same marker on Ki Blast, and on every other ki spell whose damage is force. Ruling H governs the parenthetical: where the printed rule is deliberately open ("at the GM's discretion"), stay open — mark everything plausible with the printed trigger in the note rather than narrowing the list to Ki Blast alone, which would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's. Like the clause above, this is a presented substitution option, not a computed damage-type change.

requirements.clause: Whenever you critically hit an enemy with a Strike that has the extra damage from your champion's reaction, the target also takes persistent bleed damage equal to two of the weapon's damage dice.
requirements.what: An indication on the champion's reaction — the record this feat modifies — that a critical hit with a Strike carrying its extra damage also inflicts persistent bleed equal to two of the weapon's damage dice (Principle C; Q8 confirms Ruling D's shape applies — mark the action the feat modifies). The marker must be reachable from where the player is looking when it matters, i.e. from the champion's-reaction entry the trigger names, with the full clause in its popup. The bleed amount is a formula off whichever weapon was used, so it must read as "two of the weapon's damage dice", not as a fixed die count.

requirements.clause: the target also takes persistent bleed damage equal to two of the weapon's damage dice
requirements.what: The persistent bleed itself needs no further implementation, and this is three separate rulings agreeing. It lands on the ENEMY (DECIDED SCOPE — effects on enemies rather than your own sheet are not lanes); HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode (Ruling E); and Q15 rules that an effect firing on a critical success needs no implementation unless the effect is COMPLICATED, with persistent damage of a stated size explicitly on the not-complicated side. So: no mode, no damage-total contribution, no condition tracking.

requirements.clause: Choose one of the following 1st-rank spells to your spell repertoire: Object Reading or Sure Strike.
requirements.what: A build-time pick between exactly two named 1st-rank spells. Per Q9 the picker offers only those two — it is not a free 1st-rank spell selection — and the pick is recorded on the character.

requirements.clause: You can Cast this Spell as an occult Oatia skysage spell.
requirements.what: The chosen spell must reach the Spells page in the character's repertoire at 1st rank and be castable there, with its tradition shown as OCCULT even when the character's own casting tradition is something else, and labelled as an Oatia skysage spell. The tradition must be legible at the spell itself, not merely implied by whatever section it is filed under — per Q12 the sheet must not state something false about a spell, and this grant's tradition can differ from the rest of the character's list. The granting source must be nameable from the entry.

requirements.clause: At 6th level, choose one of the following 2nd-rank spells to add to your spell repertoire: Augury or See the Unseen.
