requirements.what: A SECOND pick belonging to the same feat, gated to character level 6, between exactly those two 2nd-rank spells; the result joins the repertoire on the same occult Oatia-skysage terms as the first. This means the record must be able to hold several picks that unlock at different levels: before 6th the pick must not be offered, and on reaching 6th it must surface so the player knows a choice is owed rather than the grant silently sitting unmade.

requirements.clause: At 8th level, you choose one of the following 3rd-rank spells to add to your spell repertoire: or Locate.
requirements.what: A THIRD level-gated pick, at level 8, of a 3rd-rank spell added on the same occult Oatia-skysage terms. ⚠ The printed option list here is defective — "choose one of the following … spells: or Locate" is missing at least one option before the "or", so the legal option set cannot be read off this text. The requirement is a level-8 pick from the corrected list; the list itself must be sourced before the picker can be built, and offering Locate alone as though it were the whole list would be presenting a truncation as a rule. This is a source-text defect to resolve, not a design decision to make.

requirements.clause: Choose one spell with a sustained duration that one of your allies has in effect. You must be within 30 feet of the chosen ally. The ally can Sustain the Spell once as a free action, triggered at the start of their next turn.
requirements.what: The ability appears as its own entry in the actions list, with its requirement ("within 30 feet of the chosen ally") and its frequency shown in the popup alongside the full text. Principle E's shape applies: the entry with its trigger/requirements in its popup is the whole requirement, and there is no further sheet impact. Note the printed text carries no action cost, so the cost must come from the record's own action-cost data — it cannot be inferred from this text. Picking which ally and which sustained spell is an in-play targeting step performed by the player, not a build choice, so it needs no picker.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per round
requirements.what: Printed in the entry's popup and nothing more. Rounds are not tracked (Principle B: "Rounds are not tracked, so a per-round effect contributes no number"), so a once-per-round frequency yields no spendable pip and no daily resource. It must specifically NOT be modelled as limitedUses, which is a per-day/per-hour resource and would create a use counter that never refills correctly.

requirements.clause: The ally can Sustain the Spell once as a free action, triggered at the start of their next turn.
requirements.what: Nothing on your sheet. The entire benefit is the ally's — their action economy, their spell — which Ruling F/N settles: an effect that lands on a teammate and not on you does nothing to your sheet. Principle A's "indication on the record it modifies" has no target here, because the record modified is the ALLY's sustained spell, which is not on your sheet at all; the action entry from the previous clause already tells the player what it does. In particular this grants YOU no extra action or reaction, so no action-economy lane is owed.

requirements.clause: You have an extra spell slot of your highest rank
requirements.what: One additional spell slot, appearing with the character's other slots of that rank and spendable like them. Its rank is DERIVED from the character's current highest spell rank, so it moves up as the character levels — a fixed rank number cannot express this, and any stored constant will be wrong at every rank but one.

requirements.clause: which you can use only to cast one of your mystery's granted spells, heightened to this rank
requirements.what: The slot is RESTRICTED, and the restriction is part of the slot, not a footnote. Only the character's own mystery's granted spells may be cast from it, and a spell cast from it is heightened to the slot's rank. So the sheet needs (a) the restriction stated where the player spends the slot, and (b) the castable list for that slot computed from the character's mystery rather than offered from the whole repertoire. An unrestricted extra slot of the same rank would be wrong in the player's favour — it would let them cast anything.

requirements.clause: **Special** If you have the divine access class feature or Mysterious Repertoire feat, you can cast spells that you learned from those abilities using the additional spell slot from Gifted Power.
requirements.what: The restricted list above is CONDITIONAL on other records the character holds: it widens to include the spells learned from the Divine Access class feature and from the Mysterious Repertoire feat whenever either is present. So slot eligibility must be a membership test computed over the character's own holdings at the time of casting, not a static list attached to the mystery — and when neither of those records is held, the list must not widen.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and hold nothing else in your hands. --- ... Make a Strike with a one-handed melee weapon.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a named activity, so the activity must appear in the actions list with its Requirements line reproduced in its popup — the Minor Omen shape (principle E) applied to an action rather than a reaction. The requirement is printed for the player to read, not enforced: nothing on the sheet needs to switch off when a second item is held. "Make a Strike" is an internal step of the activity and owes nothing beyond the action's existence.

requirements.clause: If the Strike hits, you can Reposition the target up to 10 feet. You can move the target through your space during this movement.
requirements.what: Nothing required. Forced movement of the target is an effect on an enemy (DECIDED SCOPE / NOT-lanes: effects on enemies or the battlefield), and Reposition is an existing action performed as an internal step of the activity.

requirements.clause: Your Strike gains the following failure effect. **Failure** You can force the creature to move as you would on a success, but you can move the target only 5 feet.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the action's own printed text. The owner ruled on Minor Omen that the entry in the list is the whole surface and explicitly "not a degree-of-success surface", so the Failure line simply has to be legible inside this activity's popup — already owed by the grantsAction requirement above. It rides on the Strike made inside this activity, not on the character's general Strike, so it is not a weaponRider.

requirements.clause: **Access** Keleshite nationality
requirements.what: Nothing required. An access clause; Q5 settles that access/rarity gating owes no surface, and the NOT-lanes list rules out prerequisites and access clauses.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You critically fail a Diplomacy check. --- ... Reroll the triggering Diplomacy check, using the second result.
requirements.what: A reaction that must appear in the reactions list, with its trigger (you critically fail a Diplomacy check) and its Requirements (you are in a settlement or community, and haven't used it there within the past month) shown in its popup. This is exemplar #7 / principle E almost verbatim.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** ... you haven't used Courteous Comeback in this settlement or community within the past month.
requirements.what: No use pool. This is not a per-day resource — it is keyed to a named settlement and to a calendar month, neither of which the sheet tracks — so it is requirement text in the popup, carried by the reaction entry. Consistent with the owner's Minor Omen answer, which attached no countable uses even to an explicit "Frequency once per day".

requirements.clause: Reroll the triggering Diplomacy check, using the second result.
requirements.what: No star on Diplomacy. Minor Omen is the identical shape — a reaction triggered by failing a check, whose effect is to reroll that check — and the owner ruled "there isnt a need for it to impact the sheet in another way". The Truth as I See it earned a Deception star because its reroll has no reaction entry of its own to live in; this one does. ⚠ Offered, not assumed: if the owner reads Q2 ("star the skill AND the action") as reaching reroll reactions too, the star would go on Diplomacy.

requirements.clause: You are permanently quickened;
requirements.what: The sheet must show the character as permanently quickened — a standing extra action, visible where the player reads their action economy or their conditions. Q11 decides its shape: the feat gives no way to switch it off, so it is a passive, not a mode. ⚠ The lane vocabulary has `extraReaction` for a bonus reaction and nothing for a bonus ACTION or for a permanently-held condition, so this is a route the manual does not list.

requirements.clause: you can use your extra action only to cast Boost Eidolon or Reinforce Eidolon.
requirements.what: The restriction must ride with the quickened marker — the extra action is not a free slot, it may only cast those two cantrips. Text, not a number; it constrains what the player may spend, which nothing else on the sheet can convey.

requirements.clause: While in exploration mode, you can declare that you are also continually casting *boost eidolon* or *reinforce eidolon* even while using a different exploration activity. If you do, even before your first turn in a combat encounter, that cantrip is active as if you had cast it on your previous turn.
requirements.what: An indication on the Boost Eidolon and Reinforce Eidolon records themselves that this feat changes when and how they can be cast (continuous casting during exploration; already active before your first turn). Principles A and C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing is marked on that record, where the player is looking when it matters — the Lay on Hands shape from exemplars #1 and #2.

requirements.clause: Your link with your eidolon is so intense that you continuously reinforce its abilities. ... boost eidolon or reinforce eidolon ...
requirements.what: Nothing required for what the two cantrips actually do. Their benefits land on the eidolon, and a companion's bonus marks the companion, not you (DECIDED SCOPE, ★ Companions). The feat also names the cantrips without granting them, so there is no `cantrip` lane here — the character already has them from elsewhere.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** Your Spellsurge aura is active. --- You alter the aura of magic surrounding you to protect a nearby ally.
requirements.what: A named activity that must appear in the actions list, with its Requirement (your Spellsurge aura is active) reproduced in its popup — principle E's shape. The requirement is printed for the player to check; the feat does not grant the aura and so owes no aura surface of its own.

requirements.clause: You grant one creature within your *spellsurge* aura temporary Hit Points equal to your level. These temporary Hit Points last for as long as the target is in the aura.
requirements.what: No number on your sheet. The temporary Hit Points land on someone else (Ruling F/N), and HP never moves sheet stats even inside a mode (Ruling E). Whether a given creature is inside the emanation depends on where they stand, which Ruling M says is never modelled. The level-scaled amount is carried by the action's own printed text.

requirements.clause: Using this ability again cancels the temporary Hit Points from any previous usage.
requirements.what: Nothing required. Bookkeeping on the target's temporary Hit Points, which live on the target, not on your sheet.

requirements.clause: If you spend a Mythic Point as part of this action, you grant the temporary Hit Points to a number of creatures up to half your level that are within the aura.
requirements.what: The Mythic Point variant must be readable in the action's popup — a second, costlier way to use the same activity, with its own scaling target count. It spends a resource the feat does not grant, so it owes no pool of its own; and because the whole benefit is ally-facing, it contributes no number to your sheet.

requirements.clause: When you critically succeed at a Recall Knowledge check about a creature, ...
requirements.what: A `*` on every skill that can Recall Knowledge — every Lore included — so the player sees what a critical success buys them where they look up the number they are about to roll. Principle D and Ruling C, and the direct precedent of exemplar #6 Mastermind's Eye, whose effect is likewise keyed to a Recall Knowledge check: "i want the feat to have a * in every skill that can recall knolladge".

requirements.clause: you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll against the creature, to your AC against its next attack roll, and to your save against its next effect requiring a save.
requirements.what: A mode the player applies after the critical success, carrying real numbers: +1 circumstance to attack rolls, +1 circumstance to AC, and +1 circumstance to saves — all three saves, since the clause names saves generally (Q2). Each is restricted (only against that one creature, only the next such roll), so the restriction belongs in the entry's `when` rather than in a flat total (Ruling B). Q15 governs the crit-success trigger and says no implementation is owed unless the effect is COMPLICATED; three separately-consumed bonuses across three different stats is complicated in a way plain temporary Hit Points is not, so it earns the mode. ⚠ Judgement call flagged: if the owner reads it as simple, the star in the requirement above would be the entire surface.

requirements.clause: If you share this information with your allies, they gain the benefits as well.
requirements.what: Nothing required. The allies' copy of the bonus lands on them, not on you (Ruling F/N); the clause is text on the feat and on the mode it turns on, which the player reads there.

requirements.clause: If not used, these bonuses end after 1 minute.
requirements.what: No duration tracking. Q1: a longer-than-one-round effect earns a mode — already required above — and the minute is printed text the player dismisses by hand, since the app tracks neither rounds nor minutes.

The Shadow Illusion focus spell appears on the Spells page as a focus spell the character knows, with its own description reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. Casting it spends a Focus Point from the pool below.
requirements.clause: You gain the Shadow Illusion focus spell.

requirements.what: Focus pool maximum +1, stacking with every other focus-pool source the character holds (the pool is capped at 3 by the general rules). The increased maximum must be what Refocus and daily preparation restore to, not just a printed note.
requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your pool by 1.

requirements.what: Expert proficiency in occult spell attack rolls AND occult spell DC — two separate numbers, both of which must move, and both scoped to the occult tradition specifically (a character casting in a second tradition must not have that one raised). Per Ruling G a rank set REPLACES the proficiency entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, and per Q10 it must never lower an already-higher rank (a character already master in occult spell attacks stays master).
requirements.clause: You become an expert in occult spell attack rolls and DCs.

requirements.what: The player must choose WHICH of their ikons this is imbued into, and the choice must be remembered. The picker must offer only body ikons and worn ikons — per Q9 the builder shows only what may legally be picked — so a limb ikon or a weapon ikon must not appear in the list.
requirements.clause: **Usage** imbued into a body ikon or worn ikon

requirements.what: Everything this feat provides belongs to the chosen ikon, not to a free-standing feat entry. Per Principle C, a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing: the ikon the player picked must itself display the immanence effect and the transcendence activity below, so a player reading that ikon sees what it now does.
requirements.clause: Your ikon gains the following effects.

requirements.what: The immanence text must be readable on the chosen ikon, marked as an immanence effect rather than a permanent one — it applies only while this ikon is the empowered one. It computes NO number: it grants no fly Speed and no bonus, it removes a consequence (falling at end of turn without a Fly action). So the whole requirement is that the sentence is legible in the right place, per Principle B — the full text carried even where nothing can be computed.
requirements.clause: **Immanence** Your ikon keeps you hovering even without conscious effort. You can remain in the air at the end of this turn, even if you didn't use a Fly action.

requirements.what: A named activity, Race the Skies, costing 1 action and carrying the traits concentrate and transcendence, reachable as an activation of the chosen ikon. ⚠ The supplied text ends at the trait line and carries NO effect body for this activity, so nothing further about what it does can be specified from the text — only its existence, name, cost, traits, and its status as this ikon's transcendence.
requirements.clause: **Transcendence—Race the Skies** ⟨1⟩ (concentrate, transcendence)

requirements.what: One use per day: a spendable use displayed with the feat, consumed when the character performs the 10-minute reading and restored at daily preparation. The 10 minutes is the activity's duration, not a separate resource — it needs no timer, but the player must have something to press to spend the use.
requirements.clause: Once per day, you can spend 10 minutes to draw upon your readings of a recent night's sky…

requirements.what: The skill is chosen when the reading is made, not locked in at build time, and the pick resets every day — so the choice must be re-offered each time the use is spent, and the previous day's pick must not persist.
requirements.clause: …to gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice…

requirements.what: The picker must be filtered to skills whose key attribute is Charisma, Intelligence, or Wisdom (Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Performance; Arcana, Crafting, Occultism, Society; Medicine, Nature, Religion, Survival) — per Q9 only legal options are shown. Lore skills key off Intelligence and so belong in the list unless the owner rules otherwise. ⚠ Per Q10, applying the trained rank must never LOWER a skill the character is already expert or better in.
requirements.clause: the chosen skill's key attribute must be Charisma, Intelligence, or Wisdom

requirements.what: The chosen skill's proficiency must really become trained and its total modifier must move (proficiency + level), sourced to this feat in the skill's breakdown — this is a live rank change for the day, not a star or a note. It must then expire on its own at the next daily preparation, i.e. the grant is dated and cleared by rest, unlike every permanent trained-skill grant.
requirements.clause: This proficiency lasts until your next daily preparation.

requirements.what: The temporary rank must not count as a prerequisite: it cannot satisfy a skill-increase requirement or a feat's trained-in-X prerequisite. This is a genuine mechanical constraint on prerequisite evaluation, not flavour — a character who is trained only by tonight's reading must still be barred from taking a feat that requires being trained in that skill. At minimum the restriction must be printed where the temporary rank is shown.
requirements.clause: you can't use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat

requirements.what: Cold resistance whose value is a formula off level — 5 + half your level (rounded down) — and which must recompute as the character levels, so a bare stored number cannot express it. The word "increases to" makes it a SET, not an addition: per Ruling G it replaces the cold-resistance entry it upgrades (the ancestry/heritage cold resistance this feat presumes) rather than stacking beside it, and it must never reduce a higher existing cold resistance. It must appear in the resistances breakdown with this feat named as its source.
requirements.clause: Your resistance to cold increases to 5 + half your level

requirements.what: Wall of Ice appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, arcane tradition, and the entry must state rank 5 because the text names the rank explicitly — the player must not be left to guess the casting rank. Its description must be reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source.
requirements.clause: you can cast 5th-rank Wall of Ice as an innate arcane spell once per day

requirements.what: One use per day of that innate spell: a single spendable use shown beside the Wall of Ice entry, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparation.
requirements.clause: …once per day

requirements.what: Augury appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, divine tradition, with its description reachable and this feat named as the source. Its use costs 10 minutes of study rather than a combat action, so the entry must not read as something castable in a turn.
requirements.clause: you can spend 10 minutes studying your surroundings… to cast Augury as an innate divine spell

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use beside the Augury entry, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparation.
requirements.clause: Once per day…

requirements.what: A 30-minute state the PLAYER applies, because whether it starts depends on the augury's result ("nothing" or not), which only the GM's answer supplies — the app cannot know it. Per Q1 a duration longer than a round earns a mode rather than a bare indication, and per Q3's principle the sheet must make plain that the state is running and what it changed. It carries no numbers of its own; its whole content is the reaction below.
requirements.clause: Unless the result of the *augury* was "nothing," you gain… for the next 30 minutes.

requirements.what: The Call Upon the Brightness reaction must appear in the reactions list while that state is on, with its own trigger and requirements shown in its popup — per Principle E that is normally the entire surface a reaction owes. ⚠ Call Upon the Brightness is a separate record whose text is not carried here, so the requirement is that the reaction be reachable with ITS details, not that this feat restate them.
requirements.clause: you gain the Call Upon the Brightness reaction

requirements.what: The activity itself must exist as a named entry in the actions list, with its Requirements line shown in its popup. This is the Minor Omen shape (exemplar #7): the entry plus its gating condition in the popup is the surface. The inner steps — the eidolon's melee Strike, then your melee Strike at the same target — are the internal steps of an activity and are not lanes; the sheet lists the action and the player performs the Strikes. The eidolon's own Strike lives on the eidolon's stat block, not yours (DECIDED SCOPE: companions).
requirements.clause: Requirements: A creature is in your and your eidolon's reach. Your eidolon makes a melee Strike, and then you make a melee Strike against the same creature.

requirements.what: The multiple-attack-penalty exception must be readable in the action's popup as printed text. It is a per-activity sequencing rule (both Strikes count toward MAP, but the penalty does not step up between them), so it produces no computed value and no change to any displayed attack bonus — the player applies it while resolving the activity. The requirement here is only that the action's popup carries the full printed text rather than the action's name alone; a name-only entry loses the one clause that makes this activity worth taking.
requirements.clause: Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks have been made.

requirements.what: No other requirement. Nothing in this feat grants a strike, changes a proficiency, or moves a number on either sheet.
requirements.clause: (whole feat, remainder)

requirements.what: Mad Monkeys must appear on the spells page as an innate spell, with tradition primal and a cast rank of 5 legible where the player reads the spell. The cast rank is stated explicitly by the feat, so the sheet must be able to express a cast rank independently of the spell's own base rank — exemplar #10's grain: rank carries information only when it differs from base, and here the feat names one, so it cannot be left implicit. The granting source must be nameable from the entry.
requirements.clause: You can cast Mad Monkeys once per day as a 5th-rank primal innate spell.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside that innate spell, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: …once per day…

requirements.what: Expert rank in primal spell DCs and in primal spell attack rolls — two separate proficiency surfaces, both of which the player reads as numbers. Q10 governs the application: apply the set only when it makes the player better, never lowering a rank a caster already has from their class.
requirements.clause: You become an expert in primal spell DCs and primal spell attack rolls.

requirements.what: A marker on this granted Mad Monkeys entry carrying the flagrant-burglary substitution, so the option is visible on the record it modifies (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). The substitution swaps the number the monkeys use — your Thievery modifier in place of your spell DC minus 10 — inside the spell's own resolution; it is not a bonus to any check you roll, so no star is owed on the Thievery skill itself. Note the clause is conditional on a choice made at cast time, so it must read as an option, not as an always-on replacement.
requirements.clause: If you choose flagrant burglary for this casting of mad monkeys, you can have the monkeys use your Thievery modifier instead of your spell DC – 10.

requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named entry in the actions list carrying its full printed text. Making the Strike is an internal step and is not itself a lane, but the entry's existence is.
requirements.clause: Make a thrown weapon Strike…

requirements.what: A `*` on the character's thrown-weapon Strikes carrying the range clause: when Striking via this activity, the range-increment penalty in the second and third increments does not apply. This is the Ruling D / Ruling G shape — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, and the number the player would otherwise have to adjust by hand is the thrown weapon's attack roll at range. It is restricted to this one activity, so it belongs in a situational entry with that restriction in its `when`, never in a flat attack total (Ruling B).
requirements.clause: …ignoring the penalty for making ranged attacks within the second and third range increment.

requirements.what: The return-to-hand clause needs only to be readable in the activity's printed text. It is a degree-of-success branch (it fails to happen only on a critical failure) and its outcome is the physical location of a weapon, not a sheet value — Q15 says a degree-of-success-triggered effect needs no implementation unless it is complicated, and this is not. No surface beyond the printed text.
requirements.clause: The weapon returns to your hand after the attack unless you critically failed on the attack roll.

requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named entry in the actions list, with its Requirements line (you have designated prey with Hunt Prey) and its 1-minute cost shown in the popup. The requirement is a gating condition to display, not a prerequisite to model.
requirements.clause: Requirements: You have designated prey with Hunt Prey. By spending 1 minute giving guidance…

requirements.what: A toggleable state the player turns on after spending the minute, because the benefit persists until it is ended by an external event rather than expiring on its own — Q11's test: an effect that can be shut down is a mode. The mode must carry the full printed text including the parts that cannot be computed (up to five willing creatures, the loss of benefit when a creature is out of your presence for a GM-determined span, and the ending condition: it lasts until you designate a new prey or the prey dies). Principle B: a mode carries the full text of what it does even where it contributes no number.
requirements.clause: These benefits last until you designate a new prey or your prey dies, whichever comes first.

requirements.what: THE ONE CLAUSE THAT PUTS A NUMBER ON YOUR OWN SHEET, and the easy one to miss because the sentence leads with the allies. The +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls explicitly includes YOU, so it must reach the initiative surface — starred, with the restriction 'when entering combat with your prey' in its `when`, and live only while the mode is on. Because initiative is rolled with whatever statistic the character is using (Perception or a skill), the restriction cannot be folded into a flat total (Ruling B); it is a restricted bonus and belongs outside the stat total with its condition attached.
requirements.clause: You and the creatures assisting you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls when entering combat with your prey.

requirements.what: No surface. The Seek / Track / Gather Information bonuses land entirely on other creatures, and DECIDED SCOPE (Ruling F + N) settles that an effect on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet. Principle A's 'indication on the record it modifies' is already satisfied here without any extra marker, because unlike Resilient Touch — which modifies a separate record, Lay on Hands — this feat's ally half is printed in its own description, and that description is the record the player reads.
requirements.clause: They gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Seek your prey, to Track your prey, and to Gather Information about your prey.

requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named entry in the actions list, with its Requirements line (you have a creature grabbed or restrained) and its full printed procedure in the popup. That is the whole requirement for this clause — exemplar #7's shape.
requirements.clause: Requirements: You have a creature grabbed or restrained. You hurl the creature 20 feet into the air, following behind it with a powerful jump, and then make an unarmed Strike.

requirements.what: No surface. The escalating three-Strike sequence, the repeats, the 20-foot increments and the running height are the internal steps of an activity — the sheet lists the action and the player performs it. Nothing here is a per-day resource, a mode, or a value the sheet must hold between uses; the whole sequence resolves inside a single activity.
requirements.clause: …you can repeat this process up to two more times, moving the creature an additional 20 feet directly up into the air with each Strike…

requirements.what: No surface. Falling damage to you on a miss is damage, and DECIDED SCOPE (Ruling E) settles that HP and damage never move sheet stats — the player applies it with the HP control. Do not read this as a missing self-damage lane.
requirements.clause: …both you and the opponent fall, taking falling damage as normal for the total height of your jump.

requirements.what: No surface. The damage dealt to the target, and the target keeping or losing the grabbed/restrained condition, are enemy-facing throughout — outside scope by the standing ruling on effects that land on someone other than you. Likewise 'you land on your feet and take no damage from the fall' is the absence of damage, not a resistance or immunity to record.
requirements.clause: …dealing your unarmed Strike damage plus falling damage to it… the creature remains grabbed or restrained by you.

requirements.what: The Envenom action, granted by an earlier record, must show that the venom it applies is now GREATER vishkanyan venom — the upgraded stat block replacing the base one on the Envenom entry itself, not sitting beside it (principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling G: an upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades). Reading only this feat's own entry is not enough; the player looks at Envenom when it matters.
requirements.clause: You upgrade the vishkanyan venom you can apply with Envenom to greater vishkanyan venom.

requirements.what: The frequency shown on the Envenom entry must read "once per minute", replacing whatever frequency the base grant displays. This is a rewrite of the granted action's frequency line, not an addition. A per-minute cooldown is not a per-day resource and minutes/rounds are not tracked (principle B), so no spendable per-day use is owed by this clause — and if the base frequency was carried as a spendable per-day use, this feat must retire it rather than leave a stale counter on screen.
requirements.clause: Envenom's frequency becomes once per minute.

requirements.what: The greater venom's printed block — level 17, its saving throw line, Maximum Duration 6 rounds, and the three stages (7d6 / 9d6 / 11d6, 1 round each) — must be readable from the Envenom entry as the text the player consults when applying it. No numbers are owed on any stat row: the stages are damage landing on the target, and damage never moves sheet stats (Ruling E), while the round-by-round duration is untracked (principle B). Text only, but the text must be the GREATER block, not the base venom's.
requirements.clause: **Greater Vishkanyan Venom** (level 17) **Frequency** once per minute **Saving Throw** **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds **Stage 1** 7d6 damage (1 round) **Stage 2** 9d6 damage (1 round) **Stage 3** 11d6 damage (1 round)

requirements.what: Two spendable uses per day, displayed, decremented when used, and restored at daily preparations. Two — not one — is load-bearing here, since the whole feat is a two-use resource.
requirements.clause: Twice per day, you can cast a spell after you've run out of spell slots of the appropriate spell rank

requirements.what: The resource has to reach the place it acts on: a spell of a rank whose slots are all spent must remain castable while a use of this feat remains, spending the feat's use in place of the exhausted slot. Per Ruling D the surface belongs on the thing it modifies — the spellcasting/slot display on the Spells page, beside the rank rows that have run dry — not only in the feat list, where a player who has just run out of 5th-rank slots would never see it.
requirements.clause: you can cast a spell after you've run out of spell slots of the appropriate spell rank

requirements.what: The restriction that the two casts must be of DIFFERENT spell ranks must be visible at the point where a use is spent, not only in the feat's full description. The sheet must therefore be able to express which rank the first use went to (or, at minimum, print the restriction on the resource itself), because the constraint only bites when the second use is being spent and nothing else on the sheet records it.
requirements.clause: the two spells you cast with this feat must be of different spell ranks

requirements.what: A daily-preparations choice that is a MULTI-select over the character's own magic items — "any or all", so zero, one, several, or every magic item may be chosen, unlike the single-pick shape most daily choices take. The option list is the character's own owned magic items, so it is computed from inventory rather than from a fixed list on the record.
requirements.clause: During your daily preparations, you carefully tweak any or all of your magic items to appear non-magical.

requirements.what: Each chosen item must carry a visible marker in the inventory saying it currently reads as non-magical, and that state must persist until the next daily preparations rather than clearing on any other event. The marker lives on the item the player is looking at (Ruling D/G), not as a list buried on the feat.
requirements.clause: Objects adjusted in this way remain so until your next preparations.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Two settled rules cover this clause: the roll is made by someone else's spellcaster against you (an effect on another creature is not your sheet's problem, Ruling F/N), and the number it is rolled against is a SKILL DC, which per Ruling D's DC-only rule gets no surface at all — "the player remembers". Do not report the absent Deception DC as a gap.
requirements.clause: A spellcaster using Detect Magic or Read Aura must succeed at a Perception check against your Deception DC to see through your obfuscations.

requirements.what: The condition "you are piloting a vehicle" must travel with whatever surface this feat produces, so the player reads it where the effect is offered rather than only in the feat's own description. This feat has a Requirements line but no action cost or trigger — it is a standing modification gated on a circumstance, so the gate is a note attached to the marker, not a reaction entry.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are piloting a vehicle.

requirements.what: The Run Over action must carry a marker offering your class DC in place of the vehicle's collision DC, with the actual class DC value inline and a `*` to this feat (Ruling D; Q8 — mark the action the feat modifies). This is a real number the sheet already knows, so the player must not be left to look it up. Per the companion ruling the marker belongs with the vehicle's Run Over entry — the thing being looked at when it matters — and nothing is owed on the character's own stat rows.
requirements.clause: When you use Run Over, you can use your class DC in place of the vehicle's collision DC.

requirements.what: Run Over's printed targeting limits are widened by this feat, so the Run Over entry must state the new limits — any number of creatures up to one size smaller than the vehicle, or ram one creature or object up to the vehicle's own size — replacing the base action's narrower wording rather than sitting beside it (Ruling G). The sizes describe the targets, so no number is owed anywhere; but the capability change is the player's to read on the action.
requirements.clause: Your vehicle can Run Over any number of creatures up to one Size smaller than the vehicle or ram any one target creature or object in your path up to the size of your vehicle.

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list (it carries a Trigger and no other cost), with both the trigger — you succeed or critically succeed at a Reflex saving throw — and the requirement — you aren't encumbered or overburdened — shown in its popup. Per principle E that is the whole requirement.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You aren't encumbered or overburdened. **Trigger** You succeed or critically succeed at a Reflex saving throw.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT beyond the reaction's own text. Stepping is an internal step of the activity — the app lists the action and the player performs it; only the action's existence is a lane. The 10-foot distance is part of the reaction's printed text in the popup, not a speed, a speed bonus, or a modification of the Step action generally.
requirements.clause: You Step up to 10 feet.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT on the Reflex save. The trigger is a degree of success, and the owner's answer on Minor Omen — the same shape, a reaction triggered by a Reflex save result — was "there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way", explicitly not a degree-of-success surface. Q15 points the same way for the critical-success half: a crit-triggered effect needs no implementation unless complicated, and a 10-foot Step is not complicated. No star on Reflex, no marker on saving throws.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You succeed or critically succeed at a Reflex saving throw.

requirements.what: An activated ability entry for Towering Presence in the actions list, carrying its Frequency and its full text in the popup. The text as stored states no action cost, so the cost cannot be specified from it.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour --- You fill an area with your force of will, towering beyond where your true form should be.

requirements.what: A once-per-hour spendable use displayed beside the action, consumed when used. Per-hour is an explicit limitedUses shape, not a per-day one, so the recharge is an hour rather than daily preparations.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour

requirements.what: The whole stat package — size becomes Large, Clumsy 1, reach +5 feet (+10 if you started Tiny), +2 status bonus to melee damage — is indication only, printed in the action's popup. It lasts until the beginning of your next turn, i.e. one round, and Q1 rules that effects lasting 1 round are not implemented; only a longer duration earns a mode. So no size change, no condition, no reach change and no damage bonus move any number on the sheet. ⚠ Flagging the tension honestly rather than resolving it myself: this is a self-facing stat-override package of exactly the shape Q3 gives a real mode to, and Q3's mode is justified by overriding named stats rather than by duration. I read Q3 as scoped to battle forms, which replace your statistics, where this only modifies them — so Q1 governs and the answer is indication only. If the owner disagrees, this feat is the boundary case that shows it.
requirements.clause: Increase your size to Large until the beginning of your next turn. ... You're Clumsy 1. Your reach increases by 5 feet (or by 10 feet if you started out Tiny), and you gain a +2 status bonus to melee damage.

requirements.what: No requirement. Equipment resizing is GM-adjudicated narrative, and the already-Large caveat is a condition on the text above rather than a separate promise — both are lines inside the popup text already owed above.
requirements.clause: Your equipment grows with you but returns to natural size if removed. ... Towering Presence has no effect if you were already Large or larger.

requirements.what: An activated ability entry for Essence Overflow in the actions list, with its Requirements line shown in the popup — the Minor Omen shape, where trigger and requirement text in the popup is often the entire surface. The text as stored states no action cost, so the cost cannot be specified from it.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are Channeling Draconic Essence.

requirements.what: The popup must state that using this action ends your Channel Draconic Essence, and that you then cannot use it again for 1d4 rounds. Neither clause produces a tracked resource: rounds are not tracked (Principle B), and a randomly rolled round cooldown is not a per-day or per-hour pool, so limitedUses is not owed here. Text only.
requirements.clause: Your Channel Draconic Essence ends ... You then can't use Essence Overflow again for 1d4 rounds.

requirements.what: The damage this action deals is the character's own output, not a target-side number, so it belongs in the popup and must be presented at the character's current level rather than as a printed scaling rule the player computes — base dice plus 1d6 at 8th and every 2 levels thereafter. ⚠ REAL BLOCKER, and it is in the source text rather than in any requirement: the stored text has three unsubstituted template holes. The emanation size, the base damage dice and the save type are all simply absent — "in a from your spectral dragon take damage with a save". No correct damage line, area or save can be produced from this text at all, so the text must be repaired before this clause can be built or even fully specified.
requirements.clause: all creatures (except you) in a from your spectral dragon take damage with a save ... At 8th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6.

requirements.what: No requirement for the enemy-facing half. Creatures taking damage and rolling a save is an effect on enemies, which decided scope excludes from your sheet. The one piece that is the player's own number is the DC, and both class DC and spell DC are already sheet numbers — the popup names which of the two to use and no new DC surface is owed, since Ruling D's DC-only paragraph covers a bonus TO a save DC and this feat grants none. The damage type keying off the draconic benefactor likewise adds nothing: it is a property of the enemy-facing damage, resolved by a choice the sheet already records.
requirements.clause: with a save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. The damage's type matches the breath of your draconic benefactor.

requirements.what: A triggered ability entry in the actions list with its trigger — you are about to roll initiative — shown in the popup, per the Minor Omen shape. The text as stored states no action cost, so whether it is a free action or a reaction cannot be specified from it.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You are about to roll initiative.

requirements.what: A `*` carrying a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative, placed where the player reads their initiative number when it matters. Per Ruling C a bonus named after a roll marks every skill that could perform it, so this belongs on every roll usable for initiative — not Perception alone. It is restricted (it costs the triggered action) so per Ruling B it lives in situational with that condition in its `when`, outside any flat total.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your initiative roll

requirements.what: No requirement. Drawing a weapon is an internal step of the activity — the app lists the action, the player performs it. Popup text only.
requirements.clause: and can Interact to draw a weapon.

requirements.what: ⚠ NO REQUIREMENT CAN BE STATED, and that is the finding. The sentence promises something for acting first in combat but the effect itself is missing from the stored text — it ends at "you gain ." with the granted thing unsubstituted. This is a second, independent template hole in this batch. I will not guess what it grants; the source text must be repaired before this clause can be specified, and until then the feat is silently short one promise.
requirements.clause: If you are the first to act in combat, you gain .

requirements.what: A `*` recording that you are not off-guard to hidden, undetected, or flanking undead of your level or lower. Off-guard moves AC, so the marker belongs on AC with the full restriction in its `when` — a restricted defence sitting outside the flat AC total is correct per Ruling B. Per Ruling D the same marker equally belongs on the Off-Guard condition entry, which is the thing the player is actually looking at when it matters, exactly as The Survivor marks Dying. The level-of-the-undead qualifier and the flanking carve-out below must both survive into the note; narrowing them would be putting a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.
requirements.clause: You aren't off-guard to hidden, undetected, or flanking undead of your level or lower. However, the undead can still help their allies flank.

requirements.what: A `*` carrying a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls when every one of your opponents is undead. Restricted, so it stays in situational with that condition in its `when` rather than in any flat total, and per Ruling C it marks every roll usable for initiative rather than Perception alone.
requirements.clause: If all of your opponents are undead, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls

requirements.what: No requirement. Disguised undead, disguised non-undead and unnoticed extra opponents are explicitly handed to the GM, and GM adjudication is not a lane. The sentence still belongs inside the initiative star's note as printed trigger text, since Ruling H says to stay open where the rules are open — but it owes no surface of its own.
requirements.clause: the GM determines whether to apply this bonus if undead are disguised as another type of creature, if another type of creature is disguised as undead, or if there are additional opponents you haven't noticed who aren't undead.

requirements.what: An entry for the activity in the actions list with its full text in the popup, and the Leap distance resolved as the character's own total Speed rather than printed as a fixed number — the same formula-off-your-own-Speed shape as Wyrmling Flight, and the shape Q16 flagged as a live bug wherever a Speed gets hardcoded. The vertical-or-horizontal option is part of that text. The text as stored states no action cost, so the cost cannot be specified from it.
requirements.clause: Leap up to your total Speed, either horizontally or vertically

requirements.what: The multiple-attack-penalty exception must be legible wherever the player reads the attack modifiers for this activity's two Strikes: both count toward the penalty, but the penalty does not rise until both have been made, so both are rolled at the same MAP step. This is an exception to a general rule rather than a restatement of one, so it is not excluded as "restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere" — if it goes unstated the player rolls the second Strike at the wrong number.
requirements.clause: Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made both attacks.

requirements.what: No requirement for the Leap and the two Strikes as steps — internal steps of an activity are not lanes; only the activity's existence is, which is owed above. In particular no marker is owed on the standalone Leap action: unlike Black Powder Boost, which modifies Leap wherever you Leap, this modified Leap exists only inside this activity, so marking the general Leap action would overstate the feat.
requirements.clause: and Strike twice at any point or points during the Leap

requirements.what: Flavour only — an anatomical description of the throat chambers. No mechanical promise, nothing owed.
requirements.clause: Your throat has multiple separate chambers that can give your voice an eerie echo.

requirements.what: A permanent printed line on the sheet stating you can be clearly heard up to 300 feet regardless of ambient sound. This is an always-on personal capability with a concrete distance, so it is mechanical rather than flavour — but it names no check, grants no sense (it governs being perceived, not perceiving), and modifies no other record, so under Ruling I there is nothing to star and under Ruling D there is no host action or condition for the mark to live on. The requirement is therefore the weakest real one: the text must be readable as a standing property of the character, not merely buried in the feat's own entry.
requirements.clause: You can be clearly heard at distances of up to 300 feet regardless of ambient sound

requirements.what: The Silence exception must travel with the 300-foot clause in the same note — it is the limit of the capability, not a second effect, and a note that states the reach without the exception would overstate what the character can do. No separate surface.
requirements.clause: although your voice doesn't penetrate a magical Silence effect

requirements.what: "Ultimate mercy" must appear in the list of mercies the player reads when using Mercy. This is Principle C exactly — the feat modifies what ANOTHER record already granted, so it must be reflected in that thing rather than only in its own entry. The player chooses which mercy at the moment of use, so the requirement is that the option list on the Mercy entry be widened, not that a build-time pick be offered.
requirements.clause: Add ultimate mercy to the types of mercy you can provide.

requirements.what: The full text of what ultimate mercy does must be readable in that widened entry: it targets a creature that died since your last turn, returns it to life at 1 Hit Point and Wounded 1, and cannot be used if the creature died from a death effect. Every number here lands on ANOTHER creature, so under Ruling F and the HP/damage clause of Ruling E no number moves on your own sheet — but Principle A means the player must still see, on the record they are looking at, that the ability exists and what its exclusion is.
requirements.clause: When you use Mercy, you can target a creature that died since your last turn to return it to life. The target returns to life with 1 Hit Point and becomes Wounded 1. You can't return the target to life if it died from or a death effect.

requirements.what: A marker on Lay on Hands showing this feat extends it. This is the same shape the owner ruled for Resilient Touch and Amplifying Touch ("in the lay on hands spell description there needs to be indication that this effect exist"), and it applies here for two reasons: Mercy rides on Lay on Hands, and this clause explicitly routes the revived creature back through Lay on Hands' other benefits. The benefits themselves land on the target and contribute nothing numeric to your sheet.
requirements.clause: The creature gains the other benefits of Lay on Hands after it returns to life.

requirements.what: Flavour (upbringing) plus a GM-adjudicated social presumption. "Anyone who speaks with you will assume you are a noble" is a narrative consequence with no check, no number and no duration, and it is gated on an unmodellable condition ("unless you are intentionally presenting yourself differently"). The NOT-lanes list rules out social consequences and narrative access. Nothing owed.
requirements.clause: You were raised among the nobility or have learned proper etiquette and bearing... Unless you are intentionally presenting yourself differently, anyone who speaks with you will assume you are a noble or closely associated with the nobility (such as a prominent servant).

requirements.what: Two restricted substitutions: Society in place of the skill that Makes an Impression (when the target is a noble), and Society in place of the skill that Impersonates (when impersonating a type of noble or a specific noble). Both are restricted rather than blanket, so the noble restriction must travel with each. Q2 settles where they show: BOTH the skill and the action — visible on Society, and visible on Make an Impression and on Impersonate, since those are the entries the player is looking at when it matters.
requirements.clause: You can use Society to Make an Impression on a noble, as well as with Impersonate to pretend to be a type of noble or a specific individual noble.

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus on the normal skills for those same two actions when you decline the substitution — i.e. a `*` on the skill that Makes an Impression and on the skill that Impersonates, restriction "on/as a noble" in the `when`. Ruling B is decisive: this is a flat bonus the rules restrict, so it belongs in situational with the restriction stated, NOT folded into the skill total. The word "instead" is load-bearing and must be legible — the bonus and the substitution are alternatives, never both at once, so a reader of either star must be able to tell it excludes the other.
requirements.clause: If you use the normal skills in those situations, you receive a +1 circumstance bonus to the check instead.

requirements.what: Flavour restatement of the feat's purpose. Nothing owed.
requirements.clause: You rarely misidentify an item.

requirements.what: A `*` on each of the four named skills — Arcana, Nature, Occultism, Religion — and on the Identify Magic action, carrying "critical failure becomes a failure". Q2 settles the both-places question, and Ruling C's principle applies with the ambiguity removed for us: the text itself names exactly which skills can perform the action, so star those four and no others. This is a degree-of-success remap and needs no computed degree-of-success machinery — the owner's Minor Omen answer explicitly refused that surface; the star's text is the whole requirement.
requirements.clause: When using Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion checks to Identify Magic, if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

requirements.what: A second, distinct promise that must not be swallowed by the first: on a cursed item, a success that is not a critical success yields "you can't identify it" rather than a misidentification. Different trigger (success, not critical failure), different scope (cursed items only), different outcome. It can share the same four skill stars and the Identify Magic star, but its text must be present — a star carrying only the crit-fail clause would leave the player unaware of the cursed-item protection.
requirements.clause: If you would misidentify a cursed item because you roll a success but not a critical success, you simply can't identify it instead.

requirements.what: Flavour framing of the eidolon's change. Nothing owed.
requirements.clause: Your eidolon changes to make it particularly effective as your mount.

requirements.what: A toggleable "riding your eidolon" state carrying the full-actions clause. Q11 decides the shape: the effect can be shut down (you dismount), so it is a mode rather than a passive bonus, and Q3's principle applies — the sheet must make plain that the mode is active and what changed. Note this is NOT the companion-bonus exclusion: the thing that changes is YOUR action economy, not the eidolon's stat block. ⚠ Flagging honestly: the changed quantity is "how many actions you get each round", which is not among the numeric surfaces the lane vocabulary names anywhere — this may be a shape with no lane at all rather than a mode with a missing number. If there is no action-count surface for the mode to override, the mode carries the clause as text; that is the floor, not necessarily the right answer.
requirements.clause: While you ride it, you get your full number of actions each round instead of reducing them to 2.

requirements.what: The exclusivity rider must be inside that mode's own text: it applies only when YOU ride the eidolon, not when anyone else does. A mode labelled merely "mounted" would be wrong — the condition is you-on-your-own-eidolon, and the player must be able to read that from the mode rather than infer it.
requirements.clause: This applies only when you ride your eidolon, not when anyone else does.

requirements.what: Restates the general rule that a mount must be one size category larger than its rider — the NOT-lanes list rules out restating a general rule the app already applies everywhere. The word "still" marks it as a reminder that this feat does not waive it. No surface owed; at most it is prose inside the mode's text.
requirements.clause: Your eidolon still must be at least one size category larger than you to ride it.

requirements.what: The eidolon's move actions gain the tandem trait while you are mounted. Under the companion ruling this marks the COMPANION, not you: the trait belongs on the eidolon's own move actions in its stat block, conditioned on your being mounted, and absence from your own sheet is correct rather than a defect. What is owed is that the eidolon's action entries can carry a conditionally-added trait at all — the trait is not intrinsic to those actions, it is granted by a feat on the summoner and only while a state holds.
requirements.clause: Since you work together to move, your eidolon's move actions while you're mounted gain the tandem trait.

requirements.what: The feat is a triggered ability, so it must appear in the reactions list, with its trigger printed verbatim in its popup. Per Principle E that is often the whole requirement, and it is the whole requirement here — the Minor Omen exemplar is the same shape. Nothing else on the sheet moves.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** A Large or larger enemy ends a move action adjacent to you.

requirements.what: Nothing owed. This is the internal step of the activity — the app lists the reaction, the player performs the Step. Per the NOT-lanes list, 'you may Step' is not a lane; only the action's existence is. No Speed, movement-type, or position surface is implied, and the enemy's adjacency is battlefield state the app can never know.
requirements.clause: You Step to another space adjacent to the enemy.

requirements.what: Nothing owed. Flavour restating the trigger.
requirements.clause: You are an expert at avoiding the lumbering footsteps of larger creatures.

requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear in the actions list with its full text reachable from its popup. The healing itself produces no stat surface: Ruling E is explicit that HP and damage never move sheet stats, and when the target is the adjacent ally rather than you, Ruling F puts no number on your sheet at all. So the amount is text carried by the action, never a modifier.
requirements.clause: You create a minor explosion from your innovation, altering the combustion to cauterize wounds using vaporized medicinal herbs. You or a living creature adjacent to you regains Hit Points.

requirements.what: The healing value the action displays must be the value at the character's CURRENT level, not the printed base — this is a per-level scaling number living inside a granted action. A static base figure would state something false about this character, which Q12 forbids ('whichever spelling leaves the player least confused'). It is a display value, not a stat: nothing in the stat block changes.
requirements.clause: At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, increase the healing by 1d10.

requirements.what: Nothing owed beyond the action's own text. The flat check is an internal step of the activity — the player rolls it — and 'the DC reduction from appropriate assistance' is GM adjudication. The recipient may be an ally, where Ruling F removes any number from your sheet. It is prose in the action's popup.
requirements.clause: In addition, the creature you heal can attempt an immediate flat check to recover from a single source of persistent bleed damage, with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance.

requirements.what: Readable text in the action's popup, and nothing on the character's own stats. This clause only changes WHO takes the action; under the companions ruling ('a companion's bonus marks the COMPANION, not you') anything belonging to the innovation belongs on the innovation's stat block, so if the innovation is modelled as a minion the action must be listed there too, and its absence from the character's numbers is correct rather than a gap. The self-exclusion ('it can't use the ability on itself') is part of that same text.
requirements.clause: **Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you, though because it's not a living creature, it can't use the ability on itself.

requirements.what: Owner-answered directly (gold set #13): 'have Recognize a Spell apear as both free action and raction and on the pop up have explanation'. Recognize a Spell must be listed under BOTH costs — its native reaction and the free action this feat enables — with the explanation in the popup. This is exactly Principle H: an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under both costs.
requirements.clause: Once per round, you can Recognize a Spell using a skill in which you're a master as a free action.

requirements.what: No tracked resource and no skill stars. Rounds are not tracked (owner, answer #3: 'we dont truck rounds'), so 'once per round' contributes no spendable use — it is text. The master-skill gate is likewise part of the 'explanation' the owner placed in the popup; it is not a Ruling C 'star every skill that could perform it' case, because the owner ruled the surface for this exact feat and this is a cost change, not a bonus.
requirements.clause: Once per round … using a skill in which you're a master

requirements.what: Nothing owed. A summary sentence that restates the two operative clauses following it; Ruling A gives umbrella/summary text no entries of its own.
requirements.clause: You can assemble a formation even with members of ancestries that lack the hobgoblins' military discipline, and you can extend these benefits to your hobgoblin allies.

requirements.what: This changes what ANOTHER record already granted, so per Principle C it must be reflected in that thing: Formation Training's own entry must read 'at least two humanoid allies' for a character holding this feat. Per Ruling G the widened wording REPLACES the narrower hobgoblin-only condition rather than sitting beside it as a second marker. The benefit stays situational — adjacency is positional and the app can never know where you stand (Ruling M's reasoning) — so the condition lives in the `when` on Formation Training's star, not in a stat total. ⚠ Stated from THIS text only; what Formation Training's benefit actually is must be read off that record.
requirements.clause: When you are adjacent to at least two humanoid allies, you gain the benefits of Formation Training, even if they aren't hobgoblin allies.

requirements.what: Ally-facing, so no number reaches your sheet (Ruling F) — but Principle A is explicit that an ally-facing effect still needs an indication on the record it modifies. That record is Formation Training: a marker there showing this feat extends its bonus to hobgoblin allies adjacent to you and to at least one other hobgoblin ally. Display shape deferred, per the owner's 'later we can decide how its displayed'.
requirements.clause: Hobgoblin allies adjacent to you and at least one other hobgoblin ally also gain the bonuses from your Formation Training feat.

requirements.what: The chosen qi spell must reach the Spells page as a castable 1st-rank monk qi spell, with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as its granting source. Strictly from the text: it names no focus-pool clause, so no focus-pool requirement is owed by this wording — I am not inventing one.
requirements.clause: You gain Inner Upheaval, Qi Rush, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell you have access to.

requirements.what: A picker in the builder offering the two named spells plus any other 1st-rank monk qi spell the character has access to — filtered to exactly that pool, not the whole spell list, because Q9 rules the builder shows only what the player may legally pick (unless they toggle 'show options not meeting prerequisites'). The pick must be recorded and its details surfaced alongside the choice.
requirements.clause: You gain Inner Upheaval, Qi Rush, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell you have access to.

requirements.what: The feat must be selectable more than once, with each taking recording its OWN distinct pick, and the picker offered by a later taking must exclude spells already chosen — 'a different spell each time' is precisely Q9's 'only what the player may legally pick'. Every taking's spell must reach the Spells page independently.
requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

A creature that is under the effect of an infused Antidote or Antiplague that you created can choose to reroll a failed Fortitude saving throw against an appropriate affliction (poison for antidote and disease for antiplague).
requirements.what: A marker on the Antidote and Antiplague item records (and on the ongoing effect those elixirs create) showing that this feat adds a reroll to them. This is the Principle A / Ruling C shape: the beneficiary is usually the ally you handed the elixir to, so no number reaches your sheet, but the record the feat modifies must say it has been modified, and the marker must name this feat as the source. The `when` must be able to distinguish an INFUSED elixir that you created from a purchased one — the clause does not apply to elixirs you merely own.

requirements.clause: A creature that is under the effect of an infused Antidote or Antiplague that you created can choose to reroll a failed Fortitude saving throw against an appropriate affliction.
requirements.what: When you are yourself the creature under your own infused Antidote or Antiplague, a `*` on Fortitude carrying the reroll, with the restriction in its `when` (a failed Fortitude save against poison for antidote, against disease for antiplague). Q2's "star the save" applies to Fortitude only, not all three. Exemplar #16 establishes the shape: a fortune reroll is a situational star on the roll it affects, never a modifier — nothing is computable here, so no number may enter the Fortitude total (Ruling B: a restricted effect sitting outside the stat total is correct).

requirements.clause: The creature doesn't gain the elixir's usual item bonus to the reroll.
requirements.what: No requirement of its own. The elixir's item bonus is not removed from anything — it still applies to the original roll and to every other save the elixir covers; it merely does not carry to the second roll, which the app does not roll. This is a line of text inside the star's note, not a second surface, and the elixir's own bonus entry must NOT be suppressed on account of it.

requirements.clause: after the reroll, the elixir's duration immediately ends
requirements.what: Whatever carries the elixir's running effect must be dismissible early by the player. Ruling E puts an ongoing consumable that changes sheet numbers into a mode with real modifiers; this clause requires that mode to be switchable off at an arbitrary moment rather than only expiring on its printed duration, and the reason (a reroll was used) must be readable in the mode's text per Principle B.

requirements.clause: This is a fortune effect.
requirements.what: No requirement. A rules tag with no sheet consequence — it constrains stacking with other fortune/misfortune effects, which is adjudicated at the table. It belongs in the note's text so the player can read it, and nothing more.

requirements.clause: You gain the service of a young animal companion.
requirements.what: An animal companion at the YOUNG stage, with its own stat block and its own inventory (the standing companion ruling: a companion's items and bonuses mark the companion, not you). The specific animal is a builder choice offered from the animal-companion list, and per Q9 the builder must show only what this feat legally allows.

requirements.clause: You can affix your banner to your companion's saddle, barding, or a simple harness, determining the effects of your commander's banner and other abilities that use your banner from your companion's space, even if you are not currently riding your companion.
requirements.what: A marker on the commander's banner — and on the other abilities that use the banner — stating that the emanation may originate from the companion's space instead of yours. Ruling M governs the shape exactly: where the origin sits is positional and the app can never know it, so this is a permanent star carrying the condition in its note, NOT a mode, NOT a toggle, and emphatically not a positional model. The banner must also be attachable to the companion (it can live in the companion's inventory) without ceasing to be the banner your own abilities key off.

requirements.clause: A companion granted by this feat always counts as one of your squadmates and does not count against your maximum number of squadmates.
requirements.what: Squadmate membership and the squadmate maximum must both be expressible: the companion is marked as a permanent squadmate, and it is excluded from the count that fills the cap. The number being modified (your maximum number of squadmates) is a class resource on YOUR sheet, so this is not the ally-facing exclusion — it is Ruling C, a feat modifying another record's granted thing, and the exemption must be visible where the squadmate roster or its cap is read.

requirements.clause: Special When you use Command an Animal to command the companion granted by this feat, it gains a reaction it can only use in response to your tactics. This reaction is lost if it is not used by the end of your turn.
requirements.what: An extra reaction on the COMPANION's stat block, not on yours — the companion ruling is explicit that a companion's benefit marks the companion. It must carry both restrictions in its text: usable only in response to your tactics, and lost if unused by the end of your turn. Rounds are untracked (Q1), so nothing counts it down; the requirement is that the companion's block can hold a conditional reaction entry with its restriction printed.

requirements.clause: When you use Command an Animal to command the companion granted by this feat…
requirements.what: A `*` on the Command an Animal action itself, carrying what commanding this companion additionally does. Q8 and Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and the thing this clause modifies is Command an Animal.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Trigger** A creature damages you with a melee attack. **Requirements** Your attuned apparition grants Battlegrounds Lore or Volcano Lore as an apparition skill.
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (a creature damages you with a melee attack) and its requirement (your attuned apparition grants Battlegrounds Lore or Volcano Lore) shown in the popup. Principle E: that is often the whole requirement. The requirement clause depends on which apparition is attuned, which changes with daily attunement — but per Ruling H the printed trigger simply rides in the popup; the entry is not filtered out or greyed on the days it does not apply, because narrowing it would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per 10 minutes
requirements.what: The once-per-10-minutes frequency must be legible on the reaction entry. It is not a rest-restored pool — nothing in a day/rest cycle refills it and elapsed minutes are not tracked — so the requirement is that a frequency of this cadence can be displayed at all, rather than that a spendable pip be counted down and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance equal to your level against the triggering damage
requirements.what: The resistance figure must resolve from the character's actual level, not sit as a hardcoded number — this is precisely the defect shape Q16 flagged on Constant Levitation's fly Speed, where a stored constant was wrong for any character it did not happen to match. It must NOT produce a standing resistance row in the defences: it applies once, to the triggering instance only, so a permanent entry would state something false. Q1 governs — an effect this brief is indication only, so the resolved number belongs in the reaction's popup.

requirements.clause: and the triggering creature takes damage. This damage increases to 2d6 fire damage and 2 persistent fire damage at 12th level, and 3d6 fire damage and 3 persistent fire damage at 18th level.
requirements.what: No requirement. Damage dealt to the triggering creature lands on an enemy, which the DECIDED SCOPE section rules is not your sheet's problem, and HP/damage never move sheet stats in any case. The only thing owed is that the popup's text be readable — and if it prints a figure rather than the whole scaling table, that figure must be the tier for the character's own level (base, 12th, or 18th).

requirements.clause: granting you a dynamo melee unarmed attack that is in the brawling weapon group and is made of silver (which makes it more effective against certain types of creatures, such as devils and werewolves)
requirements.what: A new melee unarmed Strike on the strikes list, in the brawling weapon group, with SILVER recorded as its material so that a target's silver weakness applies and its critical specialization resolves off brawling. The material is not flavour here — it is the whole point of the parenthetical — so it must be a property of the granted strike rather than prose in the feat's description.

requirements.clause: First, choose whether you have a power driver dynamo, which deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage and has the shove trait, or a percussive striker dynamo, which deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage and has the agile and finesse traits.
requirements.what: A two-option builder choice where each option WRITES the granted strike's damage die and traits: power driver = 1d6 bludgeoning + shove; percussive striker = 1d4 bludgeoning + agile + finesse. Both trait sets are load-bearing on the numbers the sheet computes — finesse lets Dexterity drive the attack roll, agile changes the multiple attack penalty — so recording the pick as a label is not enough; it must reach the strike.

requirements.clause: Most dynamos are automated, so they don't require a free hand to use… However, you can instead choose to make your dynamo be manually controlled… to make an attack with a manually controlled dynamo, you must have a hand free to operate it… This increases the damage die by one size, to a 1d8 for a power drive dynamo or 1d6 for a percussive striker dynamo.
requirements.what: A second, independent builder choice (automated vs manually controlled) that stacks on the first: choosing manual steps the granted strike's damage die up one size — 1d8 for power driver, 1d6 for percussive striker — and attaches a free-hand requirement to the strike. The free-hand condition is a marker on the strike carrying the printed condition (Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters); the app is not required to decide whether a hand is currently free.

requirements.clause: Arm dynamos are always manual, but they use the hand on that arm to operate the dynamo when making strikes.
requirements.what: The limb the dynamo occupies must be recordable, because it is not cosmetic: an arm dynamo forces the manual option above (and therefore the larger damage die and the hand cost). So the placement pick must be able to constrain the automated/manual pick rather than sitting beside it as description. The accompanying cap — that no combination may take you past two hands or prehensile limbs — governs other effects and needs no surface of its own.

requirements.clause: If you spend 1 minute winding up your dynamo, it can remain active for 24 hours before needing additional winding… When your dynamo is out of operational time, you can still use it as a normal prosthetic, but you cannot use your dynamo unarmed attack or any other abilities from this archetype until you wind the dynamo again. You can wind the dynamo for 1 minute at any time to return it to the maximum 24 hours of operational time.
requirements.what: A wound/unwound state the player controls, with an operational-time counter: maximum 24 hours, refilled to full by a 1-minute wind taken at any time, and decremented by 1 hour per enemy Disable (2 on a critical success). Q11 settles the shape — the effect CAN be shut down, so it is a mode, not a passive. Critically, the exhausted state must switch off more than a number: it suppresses the granted dynamo Strike AND every other ability from this archetype, so the state has to be able to gate other records' grants, and Q3's rule applies that it must be plain a mode is active and what changed.

requirements.clause: enemies can attempt to Disable the dynamo, which has a level equal to your own, to reduce the remaining operational time by 1 hour, or 2 hours on a critical success. Certain other abilities that adversely affect technology might also reduce the dynamo's remaining operational time.
