requirements.what: No requirement beyond the counter above. The Disable attempt is made by an enemy against a skill DC, and Ruling D states a skill DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers it. The "certain other abilities" clause is explicitly GM-adjudicated and is not a lane.

requirements.clause: Manual control is required only in the heat of combat, not for less strenuous adventuring or everyday activities. You need to keep your sterling dynamo wound, but the process isn't particularly onerous, so in most situations, it won't be an issue.
requirements.what: No requirement. Both sentences soften a restriction for out-of-combat play and are GM-adjudicated narrative scope; they belong in the feat's readable text and produce nothing on the sheet.

requirements.clause: When you cast Toxic Cloud, modify its duration to be sustained up to 1 minute
requirements.what: This character's copy of Toxic Cloud must show a duration of "sustained up to 1 minute" in place of its printed duration, with a `*` naming this feat as the source. Ruling G is explicit that a set or upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so the original duration line must not remain visible alongside the new one. The rewrite must reach wherever the player reads the spell — the spell entry itself, not only this feat's description.

requirements.clause: and modify its standard effect to include the following: The cloud doesn't move away from you each round. Once per round when you Sustain the Spell, you can move the cloud 10 feet in the direction of your choice.
requirements.what: The added effect text must be attached to this character's Toxic Cloud so it reads there, with a marker showing the spell has been modified and by what. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing — a player reading Toxic Cloud and not this feat must still see the added clause. Nothing here is computable, so this is text plus a source marker, no numbers.

requirements.clause: The cloud doesn't move away from you each round. Once per round when you Sustain the Spell, you can move the cloud 10 feet in the direction of your choice.
requirements.what: No requirement of its own beyond the text above. Where a cloud sits and how far it drifts is battlefield geometry, which the DECIDED SCOPE section rules out — Ruling M's reasoning is that the app can never know positions. The once-per-round cadence likewise gets no counter, since rounds are untracked (Q1), and the sustained duration is not a mode: the spell's effects land on creatures in the area, not on your own numbers.

requirements.clause: You Change Shape or Dismiss the change then Stride.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear in the actions list as its own entry with its action cost, and its full text readable in the popup. The internal steps (Change Shape / Dismiss, then Stride) are steps the player performs — only the activity's EXISTENCE is owed, not a modelled movement or a shape swap. Because the activity's first step is conditional on which state you are in ("Change Shape OR Dismiss the change"), both readings must be legible in the popup text rather than the sheet picking one.

requirements.clause: Any creature adjacent to you at the end of your movement is off-guard until the end of your turn and is then temporarily immune for 1 hour.
requirements.what: NOTHING is owed. This lands entirely on the enemy — an enemy condition plus an enemy-side temporary immunity timer. DECIDED SCOPE rules enemy conditions out, and the gold set says so twice: Mastermind's Eye (#6) — "the off-guard clause itself lands on the enemy and adds nothing" — and Q4, "the reaction/action entry is the whole surface". The 1-hour temporary immunity is likewise the enemy's bookkeeping, and it is already readable in the activity's own text from the requirement above.

requirements.clause: Prerequisite-shaped dependency: the activity presumes you already have a Change Shape ability to use or dismiss.
requirements.what: No requirement. This is a prerequisite/reference to an ability you already hold, not a grant. Prerequisites are explicitly not lanes.

requirements.clause: ...you can attempt to Demoralize an onlooker of your choice within 60 feet as a free action.
requirements.what: Demoralize must appear under BOTH action costs — its native 1-action form and the free action this feat enables — with the explanation (the trigger, the 60-foot range, the onlooker target) in the popup. This is Principle H exactly, the Quick Recognition shape from gold answer #13: "have Recognize a Spell apear as both free action and raction and on the pop up have explanation". The feat does not teach a new activity; it adds a second, conditional cost to an existing one, so a duplicate free-action listing of Demoralize is the surface, not a new action.

requirements.clause: Once per minute when you succeed at a check using the type of performance that you chose with Virtuosic Performer...
requirements.what: A `*` on Performance carrying this trigger, so the player sees what happens when they look up that number. This is the Mastermind's Eye shape from gold answer #6 — the owner wanted the star on the skill whose check FIRES the effect, not only on the effect: "i want the feat to have a * in every skill that can recall knolladge so the use can see what happens when he cheks his recall knolladge number". Performance is the only skill that can make this check, so one star. The star's `when` must be scoped to the specific performance type recorded by the character's earlier Virtuosic Performer pick — the sheet has to be able to name that stored choice back to the player, not print a generic "a performance check".

requirements.clause: Once per minute...
requirements.what: The frequency must be legible on the free-action Demoralize entry. It is a per-MINUTE frequency, and minutes are not tracked (Q1 establishes that untracked time contributes no number, only text), so no spendable pip or per-day counter is owed — a per-day counter would be actively wrong, since it recharges every minute. Text on the entry is the whole requirement.

requirements.clause: If you critically succeeded on your Performance check, improve the degree of success for your Demoralize check by one step.
requirements.what: Printed in the free-action entry's popup and nothing more. Q15 governs: an effect that fires on a critical success needs no implementation unless the effect is COMPLICATED, and a one-step degree-of-success bump is not complicated — it earns no mode. Gold answer #7 (Minor Omen) settles the shape from the other side: the owner explicitly refused a degree-of-success surface. So no computed adjustment, no crit-tier machinery; the clause must simply be readable where the player reads the action.

requirements.clause: When you roll Perception for initiative, you and allies within your overwatch field receive a +2 circumstance bonus on your initiative rolls. (your half)
requirements.what: A +2 circumstance bonus that applies ONLY to initiative, and only when initiative is rolled with Perception. It is a restricted flat bonus, so per Ruling B it belongs in `situational` with the restriction stated in its `when` — it must NOT be folded into the Perception total, because it does not apply to ordinary Perception checks. Per Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action") it needs to be visible in two places: on Perception, and on the initiative roll itself, which is where the player actually looks the number up. Because a character may roll initiative with a skill other than Perception, the condition has to travel with the bonus rather than being assumed.

requirements.clause: ...and allies within your overwatch field receive a +2 circumstance bonus on your initiative rolls. (the ally half)
requirements.what: NOTHING is owed on your sheet. Ruling F: "if its an effect the effects a teamate and not you then dont do anything" — no number, no star. Principle A's carve-out (an indication on the record it modifies) is already satisfied here, because the record this clause modifies IS this feat, and the feat's own description states it. This is explicitly listed under DECIDED SCOPE and must not be reported as a gap.

requirements.clause: You're surrounded by an overwatch field aura in a 30-foot emanation... This aura has the auditory and visual traits.
requirements.what: The aura must exist as a readable, permanent entry naming its size (30-foot emanation) and its auditory and visual traits. This is load-bearing rather than flavour because the feat's only quantified clause is scoped by it ("allies within your overwatch field"), and the traits determine when it can be shut down — an aura that is auditory AND visual can be defeated by deafening or blinding, which the player has to be able to see stated. Ruling M fixes the shape: a permanent star/note carrying the positional condition, NOT a positional model and NOT a mode. Aura position is DECIDED SCOPE and is not a gap. Note the aura always includes YOU, since you are its origin, so your own half of the bonus is not positionally conditional.

requirements.clause: Your overwatch field aura grants you increased perception and allows you to call out warnings to your allies within the aura to point out threats.
requirements.what: No requirement. "Increased perception" names no value, no trigger, and no duration — it is a summary of the quantified initiative clause below it. Ruling I applies directly: where the rules name no trigger, star nothing; guessing a Perception bonus here would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's. "Calling out warnings to allies" is ally-facing and is Ruling F territory besides.

requirements.clause: With the help of enhanced visual gear (such as a specially modified telescope, goggled visor, or binoculars) and a set of carefully curated signals...
requirements.what: No requirement. Flavour — it names no item as a Requirement line, imposes no check, and grants nothing. It must not be turned into an equipment dependency the text does not actually impose.

requirements.clause: Choose four domains. These domains must be chosen from among your deity's domains, your deity's alternate domains, and up to one domain that isn't on either list and isn't anathematic to your deity.
requirements.what: FOUR separate domain picks, recorded on the character. The option list is not one list but a constrained pair: picks may come from your deity's domains and your deity's alternate domains freely, and AT MOST ONE of the four may come from the full domain list outside both. Q9 governs the picker — "The builder shows only what the player may legally pick" — so the first three-plus picks must be filtered to the deity's two lists, and the picker must enforce the cap of one off-list pick rather than presenting all domains four times. The sheet must also remember WHICH pick was the off-list one, because the next clause's penalty keys off exactly that. "Isn't anathematic to your deity" is GM adjudication and cannot be filtered mechanically.

requirements.clause: Any domain spell you cast from a domain that isn't on either of your deity's lists is always heightened to 1 rank lower than usual for a focus spell.
requirements.what: A per-spell override of the cast rank. Focus spells normally heighten automatically to half your level rounded up; a domain spell drawn from the off-list domain must display and compute at ONE RANK LOWER than that, permanently and unconditionally ("always"). This is a real number on the player's own sheet, not text — the rank shown beside the spell, and anything derived from rank, has to be the reduced value. It must also be marked so the player can see why this one focus spell is behind the others; per Ruling G the reduced rank REPLACES the normal rank rather than sitting beside it as a second figure.

requirements.clause: For the purpose of abilities that depend on your deity's domains, the four domains you chose are your deity's domains, and any of your deity's domains you didn't choose are now among your deity's alternate domains.
requirements.what: A rewrite of the character's deity domain lists, which every other domain-consuming ability then reads. The four chosen domains must BECOME the deity's domains for this character, and the deity's unchosen original domains must move into the alternate-domains list — not be deleted, and not sit alongside the originals. Ruling G: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades. The consequence is that every downstream picker filtered by "your deity's domains" (Q9's filtering rule) must read the rewritten lists, not the deity record's printed ones — so the deity's domains have to be a per-character value that a feat can overwrite, not a fixed property of the deity.

requirements.clause: If you take this feat and previously benefited from any effect that requires a domain your splinter faith doesn't include, such as a domain spell from Domain Initiate, you lose that effect.
requirements.what: Retroactive invalidation of an EARLIER record's grant. An already-taken feat's domain-dependent grant (the named example is Domain Initiate's domain spell) must be re-checked against the rewritten domain lists and removed when its domain is no longer included. This is Principle C's shape — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — but running backwards: the loss has to show up on the record that granted it, so the player is not left with a focus spell on their sheet that they no longer have. The player must also be able to see WHY it vanished, or a silently disappearing spell reads as a bug.

requirements.clause: When you select this feat, you should detail the fundamental tenets of your splinter faith, though it shouldn't affect the deity's edicts or anathema.
requirements.what: No requirement. Free-text input is a legitimate choice type (Principle I, from Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location), but only when something later reads it — there, the location scoped two situational stars. Here the clause disclaims its own mechanical effect in the same sentence ("shouldn't affect the deity's edicts or anathema") and nothing downstream references the tenets. Pure narrative.

requirements.clause: Special: Unless you take this feat at 1st level, changing the way you relate to your deity requires retraining, as described in the Changing Faith section below.
requirements.what: No requirement. Principle K: anything the player re-chooses in the builder needs no sheet surface. Retraining is a builder action.

requirements.clause: At the GM's discretion, you can take this feat with other classes or archetypes that gain access to domains through a deity.
requirements.what: No requirement. A GM-adjudicated prerequisite widening; prerequisites and access clauses are explicitly not lanes.

requirements.clause: You gain the hunter's vision warden spell.
requirements.what: Hunter's Vision must appear in the character's focus spells, identified as a warden spell, with its own details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source of the grant. It is a focus spell like any other, so it must be castable from the focus pool and heighten with level in the normal way — the grant is the whole requirement, and the spell's own text carries what it does.

requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.
requirements.what: +1 to the focus pool maximum, reflected in the pool the player spends from and in what Refocus restores. This is a real number and must sit in the total, not a note — it is unconditional and cannot be shut off, so per Q11 it is a passive bonus rather than a mode.

requirements.clause: You are so focused on your hunted prey that you can see it clearly even beyond the limits of your senses.
requirements.what: No requirement. Flavour restating what the granted spell does. It must NOT be read as a sense grant on the feat — the feat grants a spell, and any vision effect belongs to the spell's own record when cast, not to a permanent sense on the sheet.

requirements.clause: Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 132 / Prerequisites warden spells
requirements.what: No requirement. Source lines and prerequisites are explicitly not lanes.

requirements.clause: The first time each day that you regain Hit Points while you are dying, you gain a circumstance bonus to the number of Hit Points you regain equal to your level
requirements.what: A marker on the Dying condition carrying this clause — Ruling D's own worked example is The Survivor marking Dying, and Dying is exactly the thing the player is looking at when this matters. The value is a formula off your level, not a fixed number, so the marker must be able to print a level-derived amount rather than a literal. No stat moves: this is Hit Points regained, and Ruling E settles that HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode, so nothing is owed beyond the visible indication with a `*` back to this feat.

requirements.clause: and you neither gain the wounded condition nor increase the value of this condition
requirements.what: A second, separate marker on the Wounded condition: on this once-per-day recovery you neither gain Wounded nor increment it. Ruling D puts the mark on the condition being modified, so the Wounded tracker itself has to be able to carry a source-linked note. The suppression is conditional on the same once-per-day trigger, so Wounded is not disabled outright — the note must convey the condition, not a permanent immunity.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day … The first time each day that you regain Hit Points while you are dying
requirements.what: A once-per-day use that can be marked spent and refills at daily preparations. The trigger is automatic rather than activated, so there is no action, spell or reaction entry to hang the pip on — the use has to be spendable from wherever this feat surfaces (its own entry, and/or the Dying/Wounded markers above). Contrast a once-per-TURN frequency, which is untrackable because rounds are not tracked (Principle B) and is popup text only; a per-day frequency is a real resource.

requirements.clause: You gain a devotion spell of your choice
requirements.what: The chosen devotion spell reaches the Spells page as a focus spell, cast from the focus pool, with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source.

requirements.clause: of your choice listed in the devotion spells class feature, following the same restrictions listed there
requirements.what: A builder picker whose option list is not written on this feat but derived from ANOTHER record — the devotion spells class feature — and further filtered by that feature's own restrictions as they apply to this character. Q9 governs: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, unless they toggle "show options not meeting prerequisites". Per Principle K the pick is re-chosen in the builder and needs no extra sheet surface of its own beyond the granted spell appearing.

requirements.clause: (no such clause in the text)
requirements.what: The text promises no focus-pool increase and no extra focus point, so none is required. Recorded so the absence reads as deliberate rather than as an overlooked clause — judging only from the text, inferring the usual "increase your focus pool by 1" here would be invention.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Nature.
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in Nature granted by this feat, feeding the Nature total and attributable to this feat as its source.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The grant must be able to detect that Nature training already arrives automatically from another source and swap itself out rather than being silently wasted. Note the printed test is "would automatically become trained" — naming background and class as the sources — not "is already trained", so the check is about a competing automatic grant, and the swap is all-or-nothing (the Nature grant is replaced, not stacked).

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: When the fallback fires, a picker offering a free skill choice, with the resulting trained rank recorded and attributed to this feat. The feat therefore has two mutually exclusive outcomes and the sheet must be able to express whichever one applies.

requirements.clause: You also get a +1 circumstance bonus to Command an Animal if the target is a traditional halfling mount, such as a pony or riding dog.
requirements.what: A `*` carrying +1 circumstance with the restriction "target is a traditional halfling mount, such as a pony or riding dog" in its `when`. Ruling B keeps a restricted bonus out of the flat Nature total, so it must sit outside the stat as a starred entry. Ruling C stars every skill that could perform the named action — Command an Animal is a Nature action, plus any skill this character may substitute for it — and Q2 says star BOTH the skill and the action, so the Command an Animal action entry carries the same star. Ruling H applies to "traditional halfling mount": the judgement stays open in the note rather than being narrowed into an app-authored creature list.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per turn **Requirements** Your most recent action was to Cast a Spell or to Unleash your Psyche.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with its Frequency and its Requirements shown in its popup — Principle E's shape (a granted activity's entry, with trigger/requirements in the popup, is often the whole surface). The requirement is a state about your own PREVIOUS action, which nothing on a sheet can evaluate, so it is popup text the player applies. The once-per-turn frequency earns no spendable use: rounds and turns are not tracked (Principle B), unlike a per-day frequency.

requirements.clause: You siphon residual psychic energies … into one weapon you're wielding or one of your unarmed attacks … The attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage
requirements.what: An extra 1d6 force damage that lands on ONE wielded weapon or ONE unarmed attack, picked at the moment of use. The sheet must be able to scope a damage rider to a single chosen strike rather than adding it to every strike, and the chosen strike's damage breakdown must show the extra force die with this feat as its source. The rider is force damage — a damage type distinct from the weapon's own — so the breakdown has to be able to carry an added die of a different type.

requirements.clause: until the end of the current turn. If your Psyche is Unleashed, this benefit instead lasts until your psyche subsides.
requirements.what: One clause, two durations, and they resolve differently. The default (end of the current turn) is under a round, so Q1 makes it indication only — no persistent modifier is owed. The Unleashed branch outlives the turn and is pinned to another record's state (Unleashed Psyche) rather than to a round count, so it needs a mode the player holds on for as long as that state lasts, scoped to the strike chosen above; per Q3 it must be plain that a mode is active and which strike changed while it is on.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are in Ironblood Stance
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with the requirement "You are in Ironblood Stance" shown in its popup (Principle E). This is a real relationship between two records rather than loose prose — the action is only usable while another record's stance is the active one — so the requirement must name that stance and be reachable from this entry.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits of your iron sweep's parry trait (a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn)
requirements.what: The bonus lasts until the start of your next turn — one round — so Q1 rules it indication only: the +1 circumstance AC is stated in the action's popup, no AC modifier moves, and no mode is owed. The clause also borrows a trait from a specific granted strike (your iron sweep, itself granted by Ironblood Stance), so the text must name where the benefit is drawn from rather than presenting a bare +1.

requirements.clause: and your resistance from Ironblood Stance increases to your Strength modifier (if it's higher) for the same duration
requirements.what: This changes what ANOTHER record already granted, so Principle C applies: it must be reflected in that thing — the Ironblood Stance record's resistance entry has to show that this feat can raise it, so a player reading the stance sees the interaction. The value is max(the stance's own resistance, your Strength modifier): a comparison against a live attribute rather than a fixed number, and "if it's higher" means the raise can legitimately be a no-op. The duration is again one round, so per Q1 the resistance number itself does not move; what is owed is the indication on Ironblood Stance plus the explanation in this action's popup.

The feat teaches a new named activity you perform ("You declare that an enemy is fit for further punishment"), so it must exist as an entry in the actions list, with the whole of its text reachable from that entry's popup — including the sequencing condition that only the NEXT action counts and only if that action is Cast a Spell dealing damage, and the choice of one damaged creature. The text states no action cost, so none should be asserted. Per Ruling E's shape for reactions and Q4, the action entry plus its popup is the whole surface; the condition is not separately computable and must not be turned into a toggle or a tracked state.
requirements.clause: "You declare that an enemy is fit for further punishment in the sight of your deity. If the next action you perform is to Cast a Spell that deals damage, one creature of your choice that takes damage from the spell is marked for rebuke until the end of your next turn."

requirements.what: NOTHING is owed. Both halves of this clause land on the enemy: the weakness 10 is a defence on the marked creature's stat block and the 24-hour immunity is that creature's bookkeeping. DECIDED SCOPE rules out effects on enemies, and Q4 settles that the entry itself is the whole surface. The player reads it in the action's popup and tells the GM. Do not add a weakness, an immunity, a mode, or a duration tracker to the character's own sheet — the character never carries either.
requirements.clause: "A creature marked this way gains weakness 10 to all damage and becomes immune to Marked for Rebuke for 24 hours."

requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list, with its Frequency (once per round) and its Requirement (you're underwater) shown in the popup — the shape Principle E establishes for a reaction, applied here to an ordinary action. The popup must also carry the movement itself and the reaction-immunity clause, since neither is computable.
requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per round **Requirements** You're underwater. --- You move 5 feet or up to half your swim Speed vertically through the water."

requirements.what: No `limitedUses` is owed. "Once per round" is not a per-day resource — it refreshes every round, so there is nothing to spend, nothing to restore at daily preparations, and no pip to render. It is text belonging in the action's popup alongside the underwater requirement. Treating it as a spendable use would put a false depleted state on the sheet.
requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per round"

requirements.what: NOTHING is owed. The distance is an internal step of the activity, which DECIDED SCOPE explicitly excludes — the app lists the action, the player performs it. Note this is NOT Wyrmling Flight's shape: Q7's `*` marks a Speed ROW whose value is a formula, but this feat adds no movement type and writes nothing to the Speed row, so no `speed` lane and no star. It merely reads a swim Speed the character must already have; that is a usefulness condition, not a grant. The reaction-immunity clause is likewise a property of the action, carried as popup text.
requirements.clause: "You move 5 feet or up to half your swim Speed vertically through the water. This movement doesn't trigger reactions normally triggered by movement."

requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list — memorize a page-length piece of writing you can clearly see — with its full text reachable from the entry. The text states no action cost and no usage limit, so neither may be asserted: the activity may be used any number of times, each use overwriting the last. The recreation half (writing kit or other medium, once you have reached safety, no need to understand the language) is popup text.
requirements.clause: "You quickly memorize an inscription, scroll, or other piece of writing you can clearly see whose length is equivalent to no more than one page. You can then accurately recreate this writing using a writing kit, wax tablet, or other writing medium, once you have reached safety."

requirements.what: ⚠ DERIVED BY ME, not owner-stated for this feat. A display-only mode marking that the character is currently holding a memorization: an ongoing state, longer than one round, that changes no numbers and expires at the next daily preparations. This follows Q1 (one round is indication only; a longer duration gets a mode) together with Ruling E case 3 (ongoing but changes no sheet numbers → display-only mode). It must carry NO modifiers of any kind. The one-at-a-time rule means the state is a single slot, not a stack — turning it on again replaces what was there. Because the state is created and cleared entirely in play, the owner may prefer to leave this as popup text and let the player remember, which is his standing answer for uncomputable bookkeeping; I am flagging it rather than assuming it.
requirements.clause: "Your memory lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations… You can have only one piece of writing memorized at a time; any previous memorization fades the next time you use this ability."

requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, weaker than the one above and offered as a candidate only: a free-text field recording WHICH piece of writing is currently memorized, Principle I having established free-text player input as a legitimate choice type. Unlike Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location, this is transient in-play state rather than a character-defining pick made in the builder, so Principle I may not reach it. If the mode above is built, this is the natural place for the text; if it is not, nothing is owed here.
requirements.clause: "You can have only one piece of writing memorized at a time"

requirements.what: NOTHING is owed. The garbling of an un-recreated memory, the equivalence of "one page", whether the writing is clearly seen, and whether the character has reached safety are all GM adjudication, which DECIDED SCOPE excludes. The opening sentence about Pathfinders studying under poor conditions is flavour.
requirements.clause: "if you have not written down or otherwise recreated what you saw by this point, your memory fades and any attempt to recreate what you saw is garbled and unintelligible."

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (an ally within 30 feet fails a save against a mental effect) shown in its popup. This is exemplar #7's shape exactly, and Principle E says that is often the whole requirement — explicitly NOT a degree-of-success surface, and not a surface on any of the character's own saves, since the failed save is the ally's.
requirements.clause: "**Trigger** An ally within 30 feet fails a save against a mental effect."

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the reaction, consumed when the reaction is taken and restored at daily preparations. This is the same requirement exemplar #10 records for a once-per-day grant.
requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per day"

requirements.what: NOTHING is owed for the reroll or the +2 circumstance bonus. Both land on the triggering ally, and Ruling F settles that an effect on a teammate puts nothing on your sheet — the reaction's own description tells the player what the ally gets. Principle A does not add anything here either: A requires an indication on "the record it modifies", and the record modified is the ally's save, not any record of the character's own. The reaction entry IS that record, so the marker and the entry are the same thing.
requirements.clause: "the triggering ally can reroll their failed save with a +2 circumstance bonus."

requirements.what: A marker on Hypnotic Lure — the record another source granted — showing that this feat changes it, with the widened targeting in that marker's popup: all creatures in an area instead of one creature within 30 feet. Principle C is directly on point (a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing), and this is the same grain as exemplars #1 and #2, where the marker for Resilient Touch and Amplifying Touch lives on Lay on Hands rather than anywhere on the stat block. ⚠ TEXT DEFECT: the printed text is corrupt — "affect all creatures in a ," has lost its area template — so nothing built from this text alone can state the area. The real area must be recovered from the source before the popup can be written; per Q12 the surface must leave the player least confused, which forbids printing the truncated phrase as-is.
requirements.clause: "when you use Hypnotic Lure, you can affect all creatures in a , rather than one creature within 30 feet."

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use, consumed when the widened version is used and restored at daily preparations. It gates only the widened targeting, not Hypnotic Lure itself — so the pip belongs with the feat's marker on Hypnotic Lure, where the player will look when deciding which version to use, not on a separate list where it would read as a limit on the base ability.
requirements.clause: "Once per day, when you use Hypnotic Lure…"

requirements.what: NOTHING is owed. Widening your field of vision is flavour, not a sense grant — the feat gives no new vision type, no range, and no Perception change, so this must not be read as the `sense` lane. Possessing Hypnotic Lure is a prerequisite, which DECIDED SCOPE excludes.
requirements.clause: "You can widen your field of vision, allowing you to affect more creatures with your Hypnotic Lure."
You instantly use up to five Recall Knowledge actions.
requirements.what: The activity must exist as its own named entry in the actions list at its printed cost, with its full text in the popup. Its whole promise is action economy — five Recall Knowledge actions compressed into one activity — so the entry's existence and its text ARE the mechanic; there is no number to compute.

requirements.clause: If you have any special abilities or free actions that would normally be triggered when you Recall Knowledge, you can't use them for these actions.
requirements.what: A self-suppression caveat that can only be honoured by the player reading it, so it must be carried verbatim inside this activity's own popup rather than dropped as flavour. It is not computable: the app cannot know which of the character's other abilities the player would have wanted to trigger. No surface anywhere else.

requirements.clause: (the Recall Knowledge actions themselves)
requirements.what: NOTHING OWED, stated explicitly because this is the tempting invention. Unlike Mastermind's Eye — where the owner asked for a `*` on every Recall Knowledge skill because the feat changed the CHECK the player looks up — this feat changes no check, no DC, and no bonus. Recall Knowledge here is an internal step of the activity ("the app lists the action; the player performs it"), and Ruling I says where the rules name no roll modifier, star nothing. No star on Lore/Arcana/Society/etc., no star on the Recall Knowledge action.

requirements.clause: You gain the Impaling Briars order spell.
requirements.what: Impaling Briars must appear in the character's focus spells, filed as an order spell, castable from the focus pool, with the spell's own details (area, damage, sustain) reachable from the entry and the granting feat named as its source. A named single spell — no choice, no picker.

requirements.clause: You gain the Impaling Briars order spell.
requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not present in the printed text: gaining a focus spell is what feeds the focus pool (+1 Focus Point, cap 3, and a pool of 1 if the character had none). Flagged rather than assumed because this is the general focus-spell rule keyed off possessing the spell, not a clause this feat prints — so it may already be handled wholesale for every focus grant, in which case this feat owes nothing extra. If the pool is instead driven per-record, this record must contribute.

requirements.clause: You can fill an area with devastating briars.
requirements.what: Flavour restating the granted spell. Nothing owed.

requirements.clause: You can use the body of a monster to help Craft items, using Survival instead of Crafting for the Craft activity when you do so.
requirements.what: Survival must be selectable in place of Crafting for the Craft activity — and CONDITIONALLY, only when a monster's body is being used, so the condition has to travel with the substitution rather than being a blanket swap. Under Ruling C ("a bonus named after an ACTION marks every skill that could perform it") and Ruling D, the mark belongs where the player looks it up: a `*` on Survival carrying the when-clause, and the alternative surfaced on the Craft entry itself.

requirements.clause: If you spend additional days working on the item, reduce the Price using the monster's level instead of your own.
requirements.what: A change to how the Craft activity's downtime price reduction is computed — the substituted level is the monster's, which the sheet can never know. Not computable, but it is a real rules change to a named action, so Ruling D applies: the clause must be legible on the Craft action where the player performs it, not only buried in the feat. No stat row moves.

requirements.clause: If parts of the monster's body are valuable, you can expend them toward the item's raw material cost as well. (The GM makes the determination if the monster's entry doesn't list any valuable materials from its body.)
requirements.what: Nothing owed. Explicitly GM-adjudicated ("the GM makes the determination") and it operates on raw-material cost supplied at the table, so it is exactly the "anything the GM adjudicates" exclusion. It is worth being inside the same Craft-action note as the clause above so the player reads them together, but it requires no surface of its own.

requirements.clause: Certain items may require specific creatures in their Craft requirement.
requirements.what: Nothing owed. Crafting requirements are named in the manual as a non-lane, and this sentence only warns that item records carry such requirements — it makes no promise about this character.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** Your turn begins. --- You immediately Sustain one of your active impulses that can be sustained.
requirements.what: A triggered action that must appear in the actions list at its printed cost with its trigger ("Your turn begins") shown in the popup. This is the Minor Omen shape from Principle E: the entry, its trigger, and its text are the ENTIRE requirement — no other part of the sheet moves. Because the trigger fires at the start of every turn rather than on a die result, it must be visible where the player scans at turn start, not only in the feats list.

requirements.clause: You immediately Sustain one of your active impulses that can be sustained.
requirements.what: Nothing further owed. Sustaining is an internal step the player performs, and which impulses are currently active and sustainable is table state the sheet is not being asked to model here. No sustain tracker, no rounds, no duration — and no marker on the individual impulses, since the feat changes none of them.

requirements.clause: A steady ripple from your kinetic gate maintains one of your impulses.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing owed.

requirements.clause: When you use Double Shot, you can make the attacks against the same target.
requirements.what: This feat is entirely parasitic on another record — it grants no action of its own. Principle C governs: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be REFLECTED IN THAT THING. So the Double Shot entry must show that its two Strikes may be aimed at one creature, sourced to this feat. A player who reads only Double Shot must not be misled about the targeting restriction it prints.

requirements.clause: You can add an additional action to Double Shot to make three ranged Strikes instead of two. If you do, the penalty is –4.
requirements.what: Principle H, exactly: an action whose cost changes conditionally must appear under BOTH costs, with the explanation in the popup. Double Shot must therefore be reachable at its printed cost (two Strikes, its own penalty) AND at that cost plus one action (three Strikes, –4), the two variants distinguishable at a glance and the –4 stated on the three-Strike variant rather than left for the player to remember. The –4 is a per-Strike penalty inside the activity, so it belongs in the variant's text, not as a flat attack modifier.

requirements.clause: All attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you've made all of them.
requirements.what: A rules exception to how MAP escalates, and the one clause most likely to be silently contradicted — a strike display that steps the penalty per attack would show the wrong numbers for this activity. It is not computable from the activity entry alone, so it must be carried verbatim in the Double Shot / three-Strike popup so the player applies the flat penalty across all attacks.

requirements.clause: You can quickly fire multiple shots with greater control.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing owed — and note that this feat requires NO entry of its own in the actions list, since every clause lands on Double Shot.

requirements.clause: You become trained in your choice of Athletics or Acrobatics
requirements.what: A builder choice offering exactly two options — Athletics and Acrobatics — whose result is real trained proficiency in the picked skill, visible in the skill list and folded into that skill's modifier. Per Q9 the picker must offer only these two, not the whole skill list.

requirements.clause: if you are already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in another skill of your choice
requirements.what: A fallback branch that fires only when the character is already trained in BOTH Athletics and Acrobatics, replacing the two-option picker with an open skill choice. The sheet must therefore be able to evaluate the character's existing proficiency in two named skills at the moment the choice is offered, and to change which picker is shown as a result — the same shape flagged on Guerrilla Dedication. Note the redundancy test reads 'both', so being trained in only one of them still routes to the ordinary two-option pick.

requirements.clause: You gain the Toughness general feat.
requirements.what: Toughness itself is granted — present in the character's feats with its details reachable, and its own mechanics live rather than merely named. A grant that only prints the feat's name is not this clause; whatever Toughness's own record does to the sheet must happen.

requirements.clause: If you already have this feat, you gain another general feat of your choice.
requirements.what: A second redundancy fallback, this one on the feat lane rather than the skill lane: when the character already holds Toughness, the grant becomes a picker over general feats instead. The sheet must express 'a feat grant that becomes a feat CHOICE conditional on already owning the named feat' — the choice must be recorded per-character, and per Q9 the picker should show only general feats the character may legally take.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are riding your mount. --- You Command an Animal to order your mount to Stride twice.
requirements.what: The activity exists in the character's actions list, with its Requirement ('You are riding your mount') printed in its popup alongside the full text. The requirement is prose the player checks, not a gate the sheet enforces — a character with no mount still sees the action. This is the primary surface for the whole feat.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll.
requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus restricted to the Strike made during this activity. Per Q2 it goes in BOTH places: inside the action's own popup, and as a `*` on the attack rolls it could modify. Because the Strike may be melee 'within reach' or ranged 'within the first range increment', Ruling H (stay open) means every Strike the character could make qualifies — the star belongs on the Strikes generally, with the printed trigger ('as part of Cavalier's Charge') in its note, not narrowed to one weapon. The bonus must sit outside the flat attack total (Ruling B), since it applies only inside this activity.

requirements.clause: You Command an Animal to order your mount to Stride twice. At any point during this movement, you can Strike one enemy within reach or within the first range increment of a ranged weapon.
requirements.what: Nothing further. These are the internal steps of an activity — the app lists the action, the player performs the Command an Animal check, the mount's two Strides, and the Strike. The mount's movement is the companion's, not the character's, so no speed or movement surface is owed here.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per minute **Trigger** You're about to attempt a saving throw against a mental effect.
requirements.what: The ability appears in the triggered/reactions list with its Trigger and its Frequency printed in the popup. Per the owner's Minor Omen ruling this entry is normally the entire requirement. The frequency needs no spendable use pip: 'once per minute' is a duration the sheet does not track (Q1 — rounds and minutes are not tracked), so it is printed text, unlike a once-per-day resource which is a real per-day counter.

requirements.clause: Roll the saving throw twice, and take the higher result.
requirements.what: No further surface — specifically no star on Fortitude, Reflex or Will. This is exactly Minor Omen's shape (a triggered entry whose whole content is a reroll of a save), and the owner ruled there that the reaction entry is the whole requirement with no other sheet impact. It differs from The Truth as I See it, whose reroll has no action entry to live in and therefore has to be carried by a `*` on Deception. Where a reroll owns a triggered entry, that entry is its home.

requirements.clause: However, subsuming your identity is disturbing, and you're Frightened 1.
requirements.what: Nothing owed by this feat beyond the cost being legible in the popup. Frightened is a standard condition applied by the player after using the ability; the general ability to carry a condition is not this record's promise, and the feat grants no persistent condition to model.

requirements.clause: You gain a Climb Speed equal to your half your land Speed (minimum 5 feet).
requirements.what: A climb Speed on the movement list whose VALUE IS DERIVED, not stored: half the character's current land Speed, floored at 5 feet, recomputed whenever land Speed changes (armour penalty, a speed-boosting item, a mode). A hardcoded number is wrong here for the same reason Q16 called out the hardcoded fly 40 — it is right only for one land Speed. Wyrmling Flight's shape applies: because the value is a formula off your own Speed, it carries a `*` with the feat's details so the player can see where the number came from.

requirements.clause: If you have the Quick Climb feat, your climb Speed is equal to your land Speed.
requirements.what: The same climb Speed takes a different formula — full land Speed instead of half — conditional on the character owning a specific other feat. The sheet must be able to express a granted value that is re-derived based on another record being present, and per Ruling G the upgraded value REPLACES the half-Speed entry rather than appearing beside it: one climb Speed row, showing the correct number, with the reason readable in its note. This condition is on feat ownership, not on a situation, so it must re-evaluate if Quick Climb is taken later.

requirements.clause: In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC to avoid being Disarmed.
requirements.what: A bonus to a DC rather than to a check. Per Ruling D's DC clause this needs an entry in the Reflex save's breakdown, worded to say it raises the DC others roll against and not the character's own Reflex check, with a `*` beside the DC. The restriction ('only to avoid being Disarmed') lives in the entry's `when` and the +2 must stay outside the flat Reflex total (Ruling B). Two things must therefore be expressible: a Reflex DC the player can read at all, and a modifier that lands on the DC side only.

requirements.clause: You are trained in Loremaster Lore, a special Lore skill
requirements.what: Loremaster Lore exists as a real Lore skill on the character at trained rank, with a computed modifier like any other skill. It is a fixed named Lore, not a Lore choice.

requirements.clause: that can be used only to Recall Knowledge, but on any topic
requirements.what: The skill entry carries its usage restriction: it performs Recall Knowledge and nothing else, but on ANY topic. Per Ruling D's principle the mark lives where the player looks — the Loremaster Lore entry itself. And per Principle D (Mastermind's Eye), Loremaster Lore must count as a skill that can Recall Knowledge wherever Recall Knowledge skills are gathered, since 'any topic' means it is always an eligible option there.

requirements.clause: If you have legendary proficiency in a skill used to Decipher Writing, you gain expert proficiency in Loremaster Lore
requirements.what: A conditional rank upgrade whose trigger is ANOTHER skill's rank, not the character's level: Loremaster Lore becomes expert the moment any Decipher Writing skill reaches legendary, and must re-evaluate as the character levels rather than being decided once. Per Ruling H the qualifying set stays open — every skill that could Decipher Writing counts, not a narrowed list. Per Q10 the upgrade should only apply when it makes the character better, i.e. it never lowers an existing rank.

requirements.clause: but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Loremaster Lore by any other means
requirements.what: No sheet surface, but a real builder-side constraint: Loremaster Lore must be excluded from ordinary skill-increase allocation, so the skill-increase picker never offers it (Q9 — the builder shows only what the player may legally pick). ⚠ Worth flagging: this is 'a skill that is ineligible for skill increases', a shape none of the listed lanes covers — the vocabulary has ranks and rank upgrades but nothing that forbids a rank from being raised.

requirements.clause: You can take feats in the loremaster's additional feats entry even if you don't meet the Enigma Muse prerequisite.
requirements.what: A prerequisite WAIVER, so no sheet surface but a builder requirement under Q9: those feats must become legally pickable for a character who lacks the Enigma Muse prerequisite. This is not the ordinary 'prerequisites are not a lane' case — an ordinary prerequisite only describes a gate, whereas this clause changes which options the builder may legally show.

requirements.clause: If you have the Bardic Lore class feat, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks with Bardic Lore.
requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus that exists only when the character owns a different feat, and lands on THAT feat's granted skill. Per Principle C the mark must be reflected in the thing it modifies — the Bardic Lore entry — rather than sitting only in this dedication's text, and per Ruling B it is a restricted bonus with its condition in its `when`. When the character does not have Bardic Lore, nothing appears at all.

requirements.clause: **Usage** imbued into a body ikon
requirements.what: The ability must be tied to a specific body ikon, not stand free. Which ikon receives it is a pick restricted to the character's BODY ikons (the Usage line is the legality filter, so per Q9 only body ikons may be offered), and once picked the granted ability must be displayed on that ikon's entry — the player reads their ikons to find it.

requirements.clause: The imbued ikon gains the following ability. **Immanence** …
requirements.what: An Immanence ability functions only while the exemplar's spirit rests in that ikon, and the spirit moves between ikons, so this is a state that can be shut down — Q11 makes that a mode, not a passive grant. The sheet must make plain whether the ikon is currently immanent and therefore whether the two feats below are live (Q3's requirement that an active mode and what it changed be visible).

requirements.clause: You gain the Powerful Leap and Quick Jump skill feats, allowing you to jump further and faster, even if you do not meet the prerequisites for them.
requirements.what: Two named feats granted: Powerful Leap and Quick Jump. Both must appear as feats the character owns, with their own full text reachable from the entry and this feat named as their source, and both must carry their own downstream effects on Leap/High Jump/Long Jump as if taken normally. The 'even if you do not meet the prerequisites' clause means the grant must bypass each feat's prerequisite check (Athletics rank, level) rather than being blocked or silently dropped by it.

requirements.clause: Choose an ally you can see and attempt a … check against the hard DC for the target's level. On a success, the target gains resistance 5 to either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage…
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new activity, so it must appear as an entry in the character's actions with its full printed text in the popup — including the escalation option below. The action's EXISTENCE is the whole lane here; the check it asks for is an internal step the player performs.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per round
requirements.what: The frequency must be printed on the action entry, but it cannot become a spendable resource: rounds are not tracked in this project (owner, answer 3 — 'we dont truck rounds'), so this contributes no counter, no pip, and nothing that resets. Text only.

requirements.clause: attempt a  or  check against the hard DC for the target's level
requirements.what: ⚠ TEXT DEFECT, visible in the printed text itself: the two skill names are missing — the sentence reads 'attempt a or check', which is ungrammatical and cannot be shown to a player. Whatever displays this action must carry a repaired sentence naming the skills. Until the names are restored, no judgement can be made about which skills the check uses; note this is only a text-integrity requirement, since per the lanes manual the internal check of an activity earns no star of its own.

requirements.clause: the target gains resistance 5 to either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, chosen when you use this ability
requirements.what: No requirement. The resistance lands on an ally, so nothing appears on your sheet (Ruling F + N) — the action's own description already tells the player what the ally gets. The damage-type choice is made at the table when the ability is used and belongs to the target, so it is neither a builder choice nor stored sheet state.

requirements.clause: You can instead attempt your check against a very hard DC for the target's level to give them resistance to two damage types, adding acid, fire, cold, electricity, and sonic…
requirements.what: No separate requirement beyond the action entry: this is an alternative way to use the same activity, with a harder DC and a wider list, and it must simply not be truncated out of the action's text. Both the hard-DC and very-hard-DC versions are DCs the player looks up against the target's level — a DC the character rolls against, which gets no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: All of the spells in your repertoire are signature spells for you.
requirements.what: Every spell in the repertoire must be flagged as a signature spell where the player reads it, and each must consequently offer casting at any spell rank the character has slots for — the heighten / 'cast at' option on ALL of them, not on a chosen few. This is a live rule, not a one-time write: spells added to the repertoire later must become signature too. (Naming this lane explicitly because the lane manual's Magic section has no key for a spell's signature status; judge the promise from the text, not from what exists.)

requirements.clause: You can flexibly cast all of your spells … All of the spells in your repertoire are signature spells for you.
requirements.what: The spellcasting class feature already grants a LIMITED, per-rank selection of signature spells. This feat supersedes that selection wholesale, so per Principle C the change must be reflected in that thing: the signature-spell picker must show as fully satisfied — every repertoire spell already signature — rather than continuing to demand picks or cap how many the player may mark. Ruling G's shape applies: the upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it.

requirements.clause: You gain the greater order benefit for the Hellknight order to which you belong.
requirements.what: Which benefit is granted depends entirely on an earlier pick — the Hellknight order the character already belongs to. So the grant must resolve from that recorded order automatically and hand over that order's specific greater benefit; it must NOT re-ask the player which order they are in, and it must grant nothing (or be inert) when no order is recorded rather than defaulting to one.

requirements.clause: You gain the greater order benefit …
requirements.what: Per Principle G, the granted greater order benefit needs its details surfaced on the sheet AND any choice it carries offered. It must be a live grant, not a prose note: whatever the resolved benefit does mechanically — bonuses, an action, a resistance, whatever that order's benefit prints — must reach the sheet exactly as it would if that benefit had been taken directly, with this feat named as its source.

requirements.clause: You no longer have the weakness to fire from the flammable ability.
requirements.what: A REMOVAL of something another record already granted. The fire weakness that the flammable ancestry ability contributed must disappear from the defences display entirely — not be annotated, struck through, or left standing beside a note (Ruling G: the change replaces the entry it modifies). Two constraints follow from the wording: it is scoped to the weakness 'from the flammable ability', so a fire weakness arriving from any other source must survive untouched; and no fire RESISTANCE is granted — 'protecting you from fire' is flavour, the only mechanical change is the weakness going away.

requirements.clause: You no longer have the weakness to fire from the flammable ability.
requirements.what: Per Principle C, a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing: the flammable ability's own entry must show that its fire weakness has been negated by this feat, so a player reading their ancestry ability is not told they have a weakness the defences no longer list.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can't take this feat if you're a stuffed poppet.
requirements.what: No sheet surface. This is a negative prerequisite, and prerequisites are not a lane; its only consequence is on the builder's offer, where per Q9 only what the player may legally pick is shown unless they toggle 'show options not meeting prerequisites' — so a stuffed poppet should not be offered this feat by default.

requirements.clause: You gain an additional ikon.
requirements.what: An extra ikon selection offered in the builder, over and above the ikons the character already has, and filtered to the ikons this character may legally take (Q9 — the builder shows only what the player may pick unless they toggle the prerequisite override). The pick must be recorded as belonging to this feat so the player can tell which ikon came from where.

requirements.clause: You gain an additional ikon.
requirements.what: Whatever the chosen ikon confers must reach the sheet exactly as a natively chosen ikon does — its details surfaced, its immanence effect readable, and its transcendence listed as an activity the player can find. This feat carries no numbers of its own; every number it produces belongs to the ikon that was picked, so the requirement is that an ikon acquired through a feat is not a second-class ikon (principle G: a granted feature needs its details surfaced AND its choice offered).

requirements.clause: When you Spark Transcendence, your spark moves automatically from the ikon you just used to the other ikon.
requirements.what: A marker on the Spark Transcendence activity — the record this feat modifies — carrying this sentence (principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). No number and no automation is owed: the spark's location is state the base class feature owns, and this clause only changes where it goes when the player uses the activity in play.

requirements.clause: You can use Thievery instead of Athletics when you attempt a Disarm.
requirements.what: Disarm must be performable from Thievery as well as Athletics, and both must remain available because the text is permissive ("can … instead"), not a replacement. Per Ruling C the mark belongs on every skill that could perform the named action — so Thievery shows that it can Disarm, and the Disarm action itself names both Athletics and Thievery as legal checks, so the player sees it wherever they look the number up.

requirements.clause: When you use Thievery to attempt a Disarm and succeed, the target is off-guard against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.
requirements.what: Nothing. The condition lands on the enemy, and the owner has already ruled on exactly this shape — the off-guard clause of Mastermind's Eye "lands on the enemy and adds nothing." The sentence stays in the feat's own printed description; it earns no star, no modifier, and no tracked duration.

requirements.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage.
requirements.what: A jaws unarmed Strike in the strikes list, damage die 1d8, damage type piercing, attack and damage totals built the way any unarmed strike is (so handwraps and unarmed-strike riders reach it). No traits are promised by the text beyond it being unarmed — none should be invented.

requirements.clause: Your jaws are in the brawling group.
requirements.what: The granted strike must record its weapon group as brawling. This is a second, separate promise: the group is what critical specialization and every brawling-group-keyed effect read, so a strike that exists but carries no group silently drops those without the player ever seeing an error.

requirements.clause: When you succeed at your Strike while using an unstable Megaton Strike, your target must attempt a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: A marker on the Megaton Strike activity — specifically its unstable/full-power use — stating that a successful Strike forces a save against your class DC, with the feat's full text reachable from the popup (principle C: the modification must be reflected in the thing modified; Ruling D: the mark goes on the action, not on a general stat). The DC named is your own class DC, a stat that already exists; nothing is owed to your saves, because it is the enemy rolling.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected. **Success** The creature is pushed back 5 feet. **Failure** The creature is pushed back 10 feet. **Critical Failure** The creature is pushed back 20 feet.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond that text being readable in the marker's popup. Every outcome is forced movement applied to the enemy — an effect on an enemy rather than on your own sheet, which the lane manual excludes explicitly. It needs no degree-of-success surface and no tracked distance.

requirements.clause: **Special** If your innovation is a minion, this benefit applies on its unstable Megaton Strikes.
requirements.what: When the character's innovation is a minion, the same marker must appear on the COMPANION's unstable Megaton Strike, not on the player's — the owner's companion ruling puts a companion-facing effect on the companion's own stat block. So this is a conditional surface: present on the minion innovation's action when the innovation is a minion, absent otherwise, and it must be able to be conditional on the innovation's type.

requirements.clause: Your companions with wings gain a gust ranged unarmed attack, which deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage with a range of 30 feet and has the air and propulsive traits.
requirements.what: A gust ranged unarmed Strike on the COMPANION's stat block — 1d4 bludgeoning, range 30 feet, traits air and propulsive — never on the player's own strikes list, per the owner's companion ruling that a companion-facing grant marks the companion. Two further things the text demands: it says "companions" plural, so it must reach every companion the character has, and it is conditional on that companion having wings, so the grant must be able to test a companion's own trait/anatomy rather than being applied blindly to all of them.

requirements.clause: On a critical hit, the target is pushed back 5 feet. This is forced movement.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the sentence being readable in that granted strike's own description. It is an enemy-side forced movement fired on a critical hit, and Q15 settles the shape — an effect on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is complicated, and a flat 5-foot push is not.

A mode the player turns on for the 1-minute invisibility. Q1 governs: an effect lasting longer than 1 round gets a mode, and 1 minute qualifies. It is a DISPLAY-ONLY mode — Ruling E case 3 names "you are concealed" as exactly this shape, and being invisible changes none of your own numbers (it changes what other creatures must roll to target you, which is not your sheet's problem per Ruling F). The mode must carry the full printed text and must make plain it is running, so the player can see the minute is in effect.
requirements.clause: Once per day, when you roll Stealth for initiative at the start of a combat, you can choose to be invisible for 1 minute.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed with the feat/mode and restored at daily preparations. The frequency attaches ONLY to this clause — the Mythic Point version below carries no frequency and must not share this counter.
requirements.clause: Once per day, when you roll Stealth for initiative at the start of a combat…

requirements.what: A `*` on Stealth carrying this clause, worded to the trigger (only when Stealth is rolled for initiative at the start of combat). This is the option's only moment, and Ruling D/principle J put the mark on the thing the player is looking at when it matters — the player reads their Stealth number when rolling initiative and must see there that this choice is available. No number changes; the star is the whole surface.
requirements.clause: when you roll Stealth for initiative at the start of a combat, you can choose to be invisible

requirements.what: A `*` on Avoid Notice carrying the Mythic Point clause. Direct precedent: the owner's answer to Guerrilla Dedication put a `*` on Avoid Notice for a clause of exactly this shape.
requirements.clause: If you spend a Mythic Point while beginning the Avoid Notice exploration activity…

requirements.what: The expenditure must draw down a tracked Mythic Point resource — a spendable pool the player decrements when using this. This feat does not grant the pool; it requires that spending from one be expressible. Unlimited by frequency: gated only by points remaining.
requirements.clause: If you spend a Mythic Point…

requirements.what: A second display-only mode for the sustained invisibility, distinct from the 1-minute one: no fixed duration, it persists "as long as you continue to Avoid Notice". Q1 puts any non-1-round duration into a mode; the app cannot know when the player stops Avoiding Notice, so the ending condition is text the player reads and dismisses by hand. Again no numbers move.
requirements.clause: you are invisible for as long as you continue to Avoid Notice

requirements.what: Two picks the player makes, each selecting a spell from their own repertoire to designate as a signature spell. Two separate choices, not one choice of two. Q9 governs the filter: the picker must offer only spells whose minimum (base) rank is 3rd or lower — the player should not see 4th-rank-and-up spells as pickable. Per principle K, re-choosing is a builder action and owes no sheet surface of its own.
requirements.clause: You gain two additional signature spells, each of which must have a minimum rank of 3rd or lower.

requirements.what: The count granted by the class's own signature-spell feature must increase by two. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — so the addition shows up in the signature-spell allotment itself, not as a detached note. ⚠ These two are NOT tied to a spell rank the way the class's per-rank signature designations are; they must not consume one of those slots.
requirements.clause: You gain two additional signature spells

requirements.what: The two chosen spells must read as signature where the player casts from — the Spells page entry marked as signature, and castable using a slot of any rank the character has, since that is the entire mechanical meaning of the designation. Without this the two picks are recorded and inert.
requirements.clause: You gain two additional signature spells

requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list with a 10-minute cost (not an action-icon cost), its Frequency and its Requirements line reproduced in its popup. Direct precedent: the owner's answer to Minor Omen — the entry in the list plus trigger/requirements in the popup was the whole requirement, with no other sheet impact.
requirements.clause: You can spend 10 minutes channeling this power to transport you and all target creatures or objects…

requirements.what: One use per day: a spendable use shown on the activity's entry and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** Once per day

requirements.what: The requirements are a gate the GM adjudicates (standing at the bottom of an open grave, adjacent willing targets). They need to be READABLE in the popup — see the grantsAction requirement above — but they must not be modelled as a checkable state; nothing on the sheet knows where the character is standing.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are standing at the bottom of an open grave adjacent to up to four willing target creatures or objects…

requirements.what: Nothing. The transport itself, the 100-mile range, the choice of destination grave, and where the party lands when the target grave is occupied are all narrative and GM-adjudicated, and the creatures carried along are other people's business (Ruling F). The internal steps of an activity are explicitly not a lane — only the activity's existence is.
requirements.clause: …to a chosen grave you are aware of (unoccupied or occupied) within 100 miles. When you target an occupied or filled grave, you and all transported creatures and objects appear scattered aboveground…

requirements.what: The named Explode action must appear in the actions list, pointing at the existing Explode record so its own full text — cost, damage, area, save — is reachable from the entry, with this feat named as the source. That is the entire requirement: the granted action's own contents belong to that record, and its effects land on enemies and the battlefield, which is not a lane.
requirements.clause: You gain the Explode action.

requirements.what: Nothing. Pure flavour.
requirements.clause: Your innovation can explode on command.

requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions/triggered-abilities list with its Trigger reproduced in the popup. Principle E is explicit that this is often the whole requirement, and Q4 says that where the effect lands on someone else's roll, the entry IS the whole surface. Note the trigger's own condition — concealed or hidden due to DIM LIGHT OR DARKNESS specifically, not concealment from any source — must survive into the popup text intact.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature attempts a flat check to target you while you're concealed or hidden due to dim light or darkness.

requirements.what: The +2 is not a number on your sheet: the flat check is rolled by the creature targeting you, and Ruling F is explicit that target-side numbers the app does not model get no surface — the player tells the GM. The value must be legible in the entry's popup and nowhere else. ⚠ ONE OPEN READING, flagged rather than assumed: this is not really an enemy-side number, it is your own concealment DC, and Ruling D's shape (mark the thing modified — The Survivor marks the Dying condition) would put a marker on the Concealed and Hidden conditions reading "flat check DC 7 / DC 13". If those conditions are surfaced anywhere the player reads them, that marker is the Ruling D-consistent home for this clause; if they are not, the reaction entry stands alone and nothing further is owed.
requirements.clause: Increase the DC of the flat check by 2.

requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour.
requirements.clause: You draw shadows close to create a shroud.

requirements.what: The eidolon's stat block gains a new RANGED unarmed attack: range increment 30 feet, 1d4 damage, traits magical and propulsive. Three things must be expressible that a melee unarmed grant does not need — a range increment on an unarmed attack, the propulsive trait (which changes how the damage modifier is figured), and the fact that the attack and damage are rolled off the EIDOLON's numbers, not the summoner's. Per the companion ruling the strike belongs on the eidolon's own block and its absence from the summoner's own strike list is correct, but it must be present and rollable there, not merely described in prose.
requirements.clause: "It gains a ranged unarmed attack with a range increment of 30 feet that deals 1d4 damage and has the magical and propulsive traits."

requirements.what: A build-time pick from a fixed nine-option list (acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing, vitality, void). The pick is not decorative: it must write through to the strike granted by the previous clause, so the granted strike's damage type IS the chosen value. Choice and grant therefore cannot be two independent records — the strike has no damage type until the pick is made. Re-picking is a builder action and needs no sheet surface (Principle K).
requirements.clause: "When you select this feat, choose a damage type: acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing, vitality, or void."

requirements.what: The option list is conditionally WIDER depending on the eidolon's own type and alignment, so the picker's contents must be computed from the companion's record rather than being a static list of nine (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick). ⚠ Flagging rather than inventing: this text never enumerates what "a damage type in its alignment" resolves to, and it is written in pre-remaster alignment vocabulary; the legal extra options are not derivable from the printed text alone, so whoever builds it needs a ruling on the mapping, not a guess.
requirements.clause: "If your eidolon is a celestial, fiend, or monitor with an alignment other than true neutral, you can choose a damage type in its alignment."

requirements.what: Shadow Blast appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the OCCULT tradition, with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. Per Q12 the entry must not be filed under a tradition it does not have — the occult tradition has to be legible on or beside this specific spell, not merely asserted by a pooled heading.
requirements.clause: "You can cast Shadow Blast as an innate occult spell once per day."

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: "...once per day."

requirements.what: The rank this spell is cast at is a FORMULA off another record, not a constant: (the rank of your shadowdancer focus spells) − 1, which rises every time that archetype's focus rank rises. A stored number cannot express it — the sheet must re-derive the rank whenever the focus rank changes, and the rank the player reads at the point of casting must be the derived one. This is the same shape as the Q16 finding about a hardcoded speed value: a hardcoded rank here is wrong for every character whose focus rank is not the one that was baked in. If the derivation cannot be run, the entry owes at minimum a `*` stating the rule instead of printing a wrong constant.
requirements.clause: "Its level is always 1 level lower than the rank of your shadowdancer focus spells."

requirements.what: Expert rank in spell attack rolls and spell DC, scoped to the OCCULT tradition specifically rather than to every tradition the character casts, and reaching the printed spell attack modifier and spell DC totals. Per Q10 the rank is applied only when it improves the character — an already-higher occult proficiency must not be lowered to expert.
requirements.clause: "You become an expert in occult spell attack rolls and DCs."

requirements.what: The feat is an activity and must appear in the actions list as its own entry, with its Requirements line — "You're in your moose or hybrid shape" — carried in its popup. Per Principle E's shape (stated there for reactions, and Q8 for actions the feat touches) this is usually the whole surface: the entry plus its gating text, nothing else on the sheet. Note the requirement names a shape the player turns on and off, so the printed requirement is what tells them when the entry is usable. ⚠ The printed text carries no action cost; whatever lists this action must get the cost from somewhere other than this text.
requirements.clause: "**Requirements** You're in your moose or hybrid shape."

requirements.what: NOTHING is required. These are the internal steps of an activity — the app lists the action, the player performs the Strides and picks Disarm/Shove/Strike at the table. The antlers themselves are not granted here; the feat only refers to a Strike the moose/hybrid shape already provides, so this is not a grantsStrike clause. "Within your antlers' reach" is a positional condition the sheet can never evaluate.
