requirements.clause: "Stride twice. If you end your movement within your antlers' reach of an enemy, you can Disarm, Shove, or Strike with your antlers."

requirements.what: The player must designate WHICH owned ranged weapon this ikon is imbued into. The ikon is not free-floating: both clauses below have no subject without it — "your weapon ikon's damage dice" is a value read off one specific owned weapon. So the requirement is a pick whose options are the character's own ranged weapons, and the result must be stored on (or linked to) that weapon.
requirements.clause: "**Usage** imbued into a ranged weapon ikon"

requirements.what: A marker on that designated weapon's Strike entry carrying the immanence text, because that is the record the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D) and the clause quotes that weapon's own damage dice (Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). The spirit damage itself lands on adjacent ENEMIES, so it contributes no number to your sheet — that half is decided scope, not a gap. ⚠ "Immanence" is a keyed ability rather than an always-on rider; this record's text does not print the condition under which it is live, so the surface must present it as an ability of the ikon (and, if the rules make it something the player switches off, Q11 makes it a display-only mode per Ruling E case 3) rather than as an unconditional strike rider.
requirements.clause: "**Immanence** Whenever you successfully Strike an enemy with your weapon ikon, up to two enemies adjacent to the target take spirit damage equal to your weapon ikon's damage dice..."

requirements.what: A named activity, "Heaven Rains an Ending", costing 3 actions and carrying the transcendence trait, must appear in the actions list, tied to the designated weapon ikon. ⚠ Evidence gap, flagged not invented: the record's text contains the name, the cost and the trait and NO effect body at all, so what the activity does cannot be specified from this text. Anything that surfaces it from this record alone will render an activity with an empty description.
requirements.clause: "**Transcendence—Heaven Rains an Ending** ⟨3⟩ (transcendence)"

requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list. Choosing the target condition (fascinated, frightened, stunned, or stupefied) happens at the table each time it is used — it is an internal step of the activity, not a stored build choice, so it needs no picker and no sheet state. "Adjacent ally" is targeting, which the sheet does not model.
requirements.clause: "Attempt a Medicine check on an adjacent ally who is fascinated, frightened, stunned, or stupefied and choose one of those conditions."

requirements.what: The activity is rolled with MEDICINE, so it must be reachable where the player reads their Medicine number, not only from a separate actions list (Principle D: the player sees it where they look up the number). Carries no bonus — the marker conveys only that this action exists and rolls this skill.
requirements.clause: "Attempt a Medicine check..."

requirements.what: NOTHING is required beyond printing the sentence in the popup. The DC comes from an outside effect the GM adjudicates; it is not derivable from anything on the sheet.
requirements.clause: "The DC is the DC for the effect that caused the condition."

requirements.what: The four outcomes must be readable as text in the activity's popup — that is the record the effect belongs to, so that is where the indication lives. No computation: every outcome changes a condition VALUE on someone else (reducing frightened by 1 or 2, ending fascinated, extending a duration by a round on a critical failure). Ally-facing condition arithmetic and round durations are decided scope, so their absence from any stat is correct and must not be reported as a gap.
requirements.clause: "**Critical Success** Reduce the value of the chosen condition by 2... **Success** Reduce the value... by 1... **Failure** The target is unaffected. **Critical Failure** You increase the value... by 1. If you chose fascinated, increase the duration by 1 round instead."

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger ("You would be moved by a forced movement effect") and its requirements ("You are wielding a melee weapon and are within reach of a hard surface") shown in its popup. This is the exemplar #7 / principle E shape: the reaction entry is the whole surface.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You would be moved by a forced movement effect. **Requirements** You are wielding a melee weapon and are within reach of a hard surface.

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the reaction's popup text. Forced-movement distance is not a sheet stat and the app has no number to change; this is the reaction's resolution, which principle E already places in the popup. Do not invent a movement-modifier surface for it.
requirements.clause: If you would be moved 20 feet or more, you are moved only 5 feet. Otherwise, you don't move at all.

requirements.what: A mode carrying YOUR half as real numbers: +1 status bonus to Reflex saves and +1 status bonus to Acrobatics checks while your kinetic aura is up. You always shed the embers yourself, so this is certain for you (it is not Ruling M's "aura you might not be standing in" — that ruling governs only the ally half). Q11 decides mode vs passive: a kinetic aura can be shut down, so it is a mode, not a permanent bonus. Per Q1's Shield the Faithful shape, the mode carries numbers for your half and text for the ally half.
requirements.clause: You shed faint, glowing embers, as do your allies while they're in your kinetic aura. Anyone shedding these embers gains a +1 status bonus to Reflex saves and Acrobatics checks

requirements.what: The allies' copy of the bonus needs no number on your sheet (Ruling F/N). Principle B still requires the mode to print the full text so the player can read what their allies get, and principle A's marker is satisfied by that same mode text sitting on the kinetic aura it modifies.
requirements.clause: as do your allies while they're in your kinetic aura

requirements.what: Step must be reachable at free-action cost as well as its native single-action cost — principle H's Quick Recognition shape: the action appears under BOTH costs with the explanation in the popup. The "once per round" cadence is popup text only, not a spendable resource: rounds are not tracked (principle B), so no limitedUses pip is owed.
requirements.clause: and can Step as a free action once per round

requirements.what: A `*` on your Strikes carrying "+2 damage until the end of your turn after you take a move action". The condition is a move action you took this turn and the duration is until end of turn — one turn, so Q1 makes it indication only, no computed number added to strike damage. Ruling D puts the mark on the thing it modifies (the Strike), and the same clause must also appear in the mode's text per principle B. The ally half of this clause needs nothing.
requirements.clause: When an affected creature takes a move action, its Strikes deal an extra 2 damage until the end of its turn.

requirements.what: The mode's numbers must be level-conditional: at character level 12 the status bonus to Reflex saves and Acrobatics becomes +2, and the Strike rider stops being flat extra damage and instead applies the *Flaming* rune. Two distinct level-12 rescalings, both of which change what the player reads and (for the save/skill bonus) the number they total. Note the printed text is internally inconsistent about the base rider — "an extra 2 damage" above, "the extra 2 fire damage" here.
requirements.clause: **Level (12th)** The status bonus to Reflex saves and Acrobatics checks is +2, and the Strikes gain the *Flaming* rune instead of the extra 2 fire damage.

requirements.what: No sheet requirement. The empowerment lands on the summoned creature, not on you (Ruling F/N, and the companion ruling — a summoned ally's stats are not your sheet's problem). The air/earth/fire/water pick is made when the spell is cast and belongs to the spell's own text, not to a builder choice. This sentence is a preamble restating what the granted spell does.
requirements.clause: Whenever you summon an ally, you can empower it with the elemental power of air, earth, fire, or water.

requirements.what: Primal Summons appears on the Spells page as a focus spell granted by this feat, with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source. The text does not say the focus pool increases, so no focusPool requirement is owed from this record — the first-focus-spell pool rule is a general rule, not a promise this feat makes.
requirements.clause: You gain the Primal Summons order spell.

requirements.what: Trained proficiency in Stealth AND trained proficiency in Survival — two skills, both from one clause. The usual failure here is to grant one and stop.
requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Stealth and Survival.

requirements.what: A redundancy fallback: if either Stealth or Survival is already granted automatically by background or class, that half of the grant converts instead into a free skill choice. Note the trigger is narrow — "automatically become trained" from another source, not any route to trained — and the fallback can fire twice if both are already covered.
requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

requirements.what: The fallback's replacement is a player choice of any skill, offered in the builder. Per principle K, re-choosing it is a builder action with no sheet surface, but the choice itself must be offered rather than auto-assigned.
requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice

requirements.what: Grants the named general feat Additional Lore, and whatever that feat itself confers must flow through to the sheet rather than being re-authored here. Principle G's shape applies to the details being surfaced, but with one inversion: the granted feat's own subject choice is PRE-SET by this text, so the player must NOT be asked to pick a Lore — the pick is fixed at Kholo Lore.
requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Kholo Lore.

requirements.what: Kholo Lore must end up in the skill list as a trained Lore, arriving via the granted Additional Lore feat with the subject already filled in.
requirements.clause: the Additional Lore general feat for Kholo Lore

requirements.what: Felling Shot appears in the actions list at its printed cost, with its full text in the popup — including that the Strike must be ranged and the target must already be off-guard. The Strike itself is an internal step of the activity, not a separate lane; the player performs it.
requirements.clause: Make a ranged Strike against an off-guard creature.

requirements.what: No surface. The save is rolled by the enemy against your class DC — this feat does not modify your class DC, it only spends it, and using an existing stat is not a lane. Ruling D's DC-only case covers a feat that CHANGES a DC, which this is not. Naming the class DC in the popup text is enough.
requirements.clause: If the Strike is a success and deals damage, the target must attempt a save against your class DC.

requirements.what: No surface beyond the popup prose. All three outcomes land entirely on the enemy — falling, fall damage, and a ground-lock condition — and enemy-facing effects and enemy conditions are settled as out of scope (Q4, and the DECIDED SCOPE list). Degree-of-success text is display-only prose inside the action's popup.
requirements.clause: **Success** The target is unaffected. **Failure** The target falls up to 120 feet. If it hits the ground, it takes no damage from the fall. **Critical Failure** As failure, and the target can't fly, jump, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground until the end of your next turn.
Your understanding of life expands, allowing you to mimic a wider range of creatures.
requirements.what: Flavour. Requires nothing.

requirements.clause: Add the shapes in Insect Form to your Untamed Form list.
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to widen a list that ANOTHER record already granted. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — so the Insect Form shapes have to appear inside the Untamed Form shape list itself, where the player goes to choose a shape, not only in this feat's own description. They must arrive as real selectable options carrying whatever the shapes already on that list carry: Q3 rules that a battle form gets a mode that really overrides the stats it names and must make plain that a mode is active and what changed, so a shape added to that list and left as prose is a shape the player cannot actually use.

requirements.clause: Whenever you use untamed form to polymorph into the non-flying insect shapes listed in pest form, the duration is 24 hours instead of 10 minutes.
requirements.what: A duration override that applies to only SOME of the shapes on the list. Durations are not tracked, so this contributes no number (principle B); the requirement is that the 24-hour figure be readable at the moment it matters — on the Untamed Form entry and/or on those specific non-flying insect shape options, per Ruling D/G (the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). Note that the qualifying set is defined by pointing at a third record's contents ("the non-flying insect shapes listed in pest form"), so the marker must be able to name that subset rather than apply to the whole list.

requirements.clause: Your tongue can momentarily latch on as readily as your hands.
requirements.what: Flavour. Requires nothing.

requirements.clause: So long as you can freely open your mouth, you do not need free hands in order to Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition, or Trip.
requirements.what: A `*` on each of the four named actions — Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition, Trip — saying the free-hand requirement is waived. Ruling J puts situational stars on the specific actions affected rather than on a general stat, and Ruling C stars every skill that could perform a named action, so the Athletics entry the player reads when rolling Disarm/Reposition/Trip carries the same mark. What this waives is an action's REQUIREMENT line, not a check modifier, so no number moves — the requirement is purely that the four action entries can carry a clause altering their own prerequisites. The condition "so long as you can freely open your mouth" is not knowable by any sheet, so per Ruling H it stays printed in the marker's `when` rather than being modelled.

requirements.clause: If you have the Long Tongue feat, you can Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition, and Trip with your tongue at a distance that is 5 feet beyond your normal reach.
requirements.what: A second, separately-gated clause on the same four actions: +5 feet of reach for these actions specifically. Two things must be expressible. (1) A reach figure attached to non-Strike actions — reach here is not the weapon reach on a strike line but the range at which Disarm/Grab an Edge/Reposition/Trip may be attempted, and it is derived ("5 feet beyond your NORMAL reach"), so a bare number will not do. (2) The clause is conditional on the character OWNING A DIFFERENT FEAT (Long Tongue), so the marker must either appear only when Long Tongue is held or state that condition inline — a predicate over the character's own feat list, which is knowable and therefore should gate the display rather than being left as prose the player has to filter.

requirements.clause: Your animal companion continues to grow in power and ability, and it is now cunning enough to become specialized.
requirements.what: Flavour. Requires nothing.

requirements.clause: Your animal companion gains one specialization of your choice.
requirements.what: A pick, offered in the builder, from the animal companion specializations. Per Q9 the picker shows only what the player may legally pick, so it must filter to specializations this character's companion can actually take — and, given the Special clause below, must exclude any specialization already recorded by an earlier instance of this feat.

requirements.clause: Your animal companion gains one specialization of your choice.
requirements.what: The chosen specialization must land on the ANIMAL COMPANION's own stat block — the creature granted by a different record — changing that creature's numbers and abilities, and its details must be readable there. The DECIDED SCOPE companion ruling settles the other half: nothing about this appears among the character's own stats, and that absence is correct, not a gap. So the requirement is a write into another record's granted creature (principle C), not a modifier on you.

requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat up to three times. Each time, add a different specialization to your companion.
requirements.what: The feat must be takeable more than once — up to three times — with each instance holding its OWN independent pick, and with the picks forced to be distinct from one another. A single-instance feat record with one stored choice cannot express this; the requirement is a repeat count plus per-instance choice state plus a cross-instance uniqueness rule feeding the filter in the requirement above.

requirements.clause: You carry your ammunition in a way that allows you to reload while holding two weapons.
requirements.what: Flavour restating the mechanical clause. Requires nothing of its own.

requirements.clause: While you're wielding two one-handed weapons, each in a different hand, you don't need a free hand to reload a one-handed ranged weapon you're wielding.
requirements.what: A `*` on Reload, marked on the wielded one-handed ranged weapon's own entry — Ruling D and Q8: mark the action the feat modifies, value/explanation inline, star linking back to the feat. What it changes is the Reload action's free-hand requirement, not any roll or number, so nothing else on the sheet moves. Two qualifications must be carried by the marker: it applies only while two one-handed weapons are wielded one per hand, and only to a one-handed ranged weapon you are wielding — both are facts about the character's OWN equipped/wielded state and are therefore knowable, so they can gate when the marker shows rather than being left entirely as prose the player must apply.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Requirements** Your previous action was a Strike with your spectral dagger that dealt spirit damage.
requirements.what: The feat is an activated ability, not a passive one: it must appear as an entry in the actions list with its Frequency and its Requirements line shown in the popup. This is principle E's shape (a reaction needs to appear in the reactions list with its trigger and requirements in its popup) applied to an activity. The requirement — that your previous action was a spectral dagger Strike dealing spirit damage — is a sequencing condition no sheet can verify, so it is printed for the player to honour, not enforced.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day, displayed with the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: Your *spectral dagger* gains the effects of a Keen property rune… This effect lasts for 10 minutes or until that target dies, whichever comes first.
requirements.what: Ten minutes is well past one round, so Q1 gives this a mode the player turns on and off, and Q11 agrees (the effect ends on a condition, so it is a mode rather than a passive bonus). The mode must be able to apply a PROPERTY RUNE's effect temporarily to one specific weapon — the spectral dagger — which is a shape distinct from the permanent etched runes on an inventory item: nothing is etched, nothing is bought, and the effect must come off again. Keen's effect is an expanded critical range (a natural 19 on the attack roll becomes a critical hit), so the sheet must be able to express a changed crit threshold on a strike, which is not a bonus to any total.

requirements.clause: Your *spectral dagger* gains the effects of a Keen property rune…
requirements.what: The spectral dagger is a weapon granted by ANOTHER record (the splinter of finality feature), so principle C applies: the effect must be reflected in that granted strike's own entry — the player must see the change where they read the dagger's attack line, not only inside this feat's text.

requirements.clause: …that applies only to Strikes against the target of the required Strike. This effect lasts for 10 minutes or until that target dies, whichever comes first.
requirements.what: The restriction is scoped to ONE enemy creature, which is target-side information the sheet can never hold, and the end condition ("until that target dies") is likewise unknowable. Per Ruling B and Ruling H this stays printed in the marker's/mode's `when` text — the player applies it — rather than being modelled; and per Ruling F the target itself gets no surface here. So the requirement is that the mode be able to carry a restriction and an expiry as text alongside a real crit-range change, not that the app track the enemy.

requirements.clause: Your weapon and unarmed Strikes gain the effects of a *disrupting* property rune until the start of your next turn.
requirements.what: The effect lasts exactly one round ("until the start of your next turn"), and Q1 rules a one-round effect not implemented — indication only, so no mode and no computed damage rider. What is owed is a marker carrying this feat's text on the things it modifies (Ruling D/G): EVERY Strike entry the character has, weapon and unarmed alike, not one chosen weapon and not a general damage stat. Because no number will move, the marker itself has to state what the rune does while it is live. The clause also has a start point the text implies but never states (something must begin the round), so the feat must be findable at the moment the player turns it on.

requirements.clause: If you're 14th level or higher, your Strikes instead gain the effects of a *greater disrupting property rune*.
requirements.what: The indication is level-dependent: the sheet must be able to express which of two versions this character currently gets, switching at level 14, and show only the applicable one — Ruling G says an upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, and Q12 says pick the spelling that leaves the player least confused. A marker that hardcodes one version, or prints both with an "if", fails this clause.

requirements.clause: The DC for the rune's effect is equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
requirements.what: A derived DC the player must be able to read as a resolved NUMBER — max(class DC, spell DC) computed for this character — not a restated formula. It is not one of the character's saving-throw DCs, so Ruling D's "save DC gets an entry in that save's breakdown" does not house it; it belongs beside the effect it governs, inside the marker/popup from clause 1. ⚠ Nothing in the lane vocabulary covers "a DC for a granted effect, computed as the higher of two of the character's own DCs" — flagged as possibly unlaned rather than assigned a home I cannot justify.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Repair non-magical items
requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus whose `when` must carry the whole restriction — only to Repair, and only on non-magical items. Ruling B puts it in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, never in the flat Crafting total. Q2 settles the surface: BOTH — a star on the Crafting skill, where the player reads the number, and a star on the Repair action itself. The `when` must be able to express a restriction on the TARGET's properties ("non-magical item"), which nothing can evaluate; it is text the player applies.

requirements.clause: and you don't need a Repair Kit for such repairs as long as you have any amount of junk, spare parts, or debris at your disposal
requirements.what: A waiver of an action's equipment requirement, itself conditional on having scrap to hand. It moves no number and cannot be computed, so it is a note attached to the Repair action (Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). It must ride alongside the star from clause 1 rather than be folded into it or dropped: recording the bonus and losing the waiver is the exact two-promise failure this feat invites.

requirements.clause: Choose a second kinetic element to add to the one you already have.
requirements.what: A recorded pick from the kinetic element list that is ADDITIVE — the character now holds a set of elements, not one value — so the sheet must store multiple elements and must know which one is already owned so the picker can exclude it (Q9: the builder offers only what the player may legally pick). Re-choosing happens in the builder, so the pick owes no sheet surface of its own (Principle K); what it does owe is storage that other records can read (see the fourth clause).

requirements.clause: You gain an impulse feat for that element.
requirements.what: A feat picker granted by this feat whose option list is DERIVED from the element chosen in the first clause — impulse feats of that element only, the same filtering shape Q9 imposed on Domain Fluency and the mystery's domains. The dependency runs pick → picker, so the picker cannot be populated until the element is answered, and an unanswered pick has to stay visible as an outstanding choice rather than silently granting nothing.

requirements.clause: For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your kineticist level is equal to half your level.
requirements.what: The picker from the previous clause must evaluate prerequisites against an effective kineticist level of half the character's level rather than their actual level, so the sheet must hold a per-source effective class level and the prerequisite check must consult it. This is not an ordinary "prerequisite line" (which the manual excludes as a non-lane) — it changes which options the builder is allowed to offer, which Q9 makes load-bearing. ⚠ The lane vocabulary has no route for an effective-level substitution used in prerequisite evaluation; flagged as possibly unlaned.

requirements.clause: If you gain more kineticist feats, you can select hybrid impulses that have both your elements, as normal for a kineticist.
requirements.what: The element set recorded by the first clause must be legible to EVERY later kineticist/impulse picker, not just to this feat's own picker, so that hybrid impulses requiring both elements become selectable once the second element exists. This is a requirement about reach: a pick stored where only its own feat can see it satisfies clause 1 and fails this clause invisibly.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** An undead creature within your reach critically fails a Strike against you.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions list, with the full trigger text in its popup — including the two conditions nothing can evaluate for the player (the creature is undead; it is within your reach). Principle E: appearing in the reactions list with trigger and requirements in the popup is often the entire requirement, and it is here.

requirements.clause: You attempt to Disarm, Shove, or Trip the triggering creature.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. The three options are internal steps of the activity — the app lists the reaction, the player performs the check — and their outcomes land on the enemy, which Q4 settles: for an enemy-facing reaction the reaction entry is the whole surface. The three choices must be readable in the popup text from clause 1, but they need no picker, no star on Athletics (the feat grants no bonus to those actions, only permission to attempt one), and no modifier anywhere.

requirements.clause: For the next 2 rounds, at the start of your turn, you regain Hit Points equal to half your level.
requirements.what: A duration longer than a single round, so Q1 gives it a mode rather than a bare indication — but a mode the PLAYER applies, since the trigger ("when you're about to die") is a moment nothing can detect. Rounds are untracked and HP never moves a sheet stat, so this is Ruling E's third case: a display-only mode that carries the full text and contributes zero numbers, while still making plain that it is running and what it does. The per-round amount is derived from the character's level, so the mode's text must be able to resolve "half your level" for this character rather than leave arithmetic to the player.

requirements.clause: You regain Hit Points equal to your level.
requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT beyond the text. HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode, and a healing effect must not be flagged for failing to change one. The only expressible part is the amount, which is derived from level rather than fixed — worth resolving in the text for this character — but nothing on the sheet changes as a result of this clause.

requirements.clause: The first time you regain Hit Points at the start of your turn, you reduce your wounded condition by 1.
requirements.what: Unlike the healing, this lands on the character's OWN tracked condition and so is genuinely expressible: the sheet must be able to hold a Wounded value and decrement it, and per Ruling D the feat's marker belongs on the Wounded condition itself — the same shape as The Survivor marking Dying. "The first time" is a once-per-activation limit inside the mode from the first clause that nothing can police; it is text the player applies. This is the clause most likely to be missed, because the two preceding ones are both healing and healing is specified to owe nothing.

requirements.clause: Choose an ally within 30 feet and then attempt a Diplomacy or Intimidation check against a hard DC for that ally's level. This counts as a preparatory action to Aid that ally.
requirements.what: The activity itself must appear in the actions list with its action cost and traits, and its popup must carry the whole procedure: an ally target within 30 feet, the choice of Diplomacy OR Intimidation, the target number (hard DC for that ally's level), and the fact that it counts as a preparatory action to Aid that ally. The skill check is an internal step of the activity, not a bonus — the feat gives no bonus to Diplomacy or Intimidation, so no `*` is owed on either skill (the manual's NOT-lanes rule: 'attempt an Athletics check' is a step, only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane).

requirements.clause: Regardless of your result, the ally is then temporarily immune to your further uses of Seasoned Command for 1 minute.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text in the action's popup. Temporary immunity is tracked per target, on the target — Ruling F territory, and the sheet has no surface for it. Not a limitedUses resource either: it is not a pool the character spends, it is a per-ally lockout.

requirements.clause: Critical Success You immediately gain an additional reaction that can be used only to Aid the chosen ally, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your skill check or attack roll to Aid. Success As critical success, but you don't gain the circumstance bonus. Failure You don't gain an additional reaction.
requirements.what: Per Q15 an effect that fires on a degree of success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED; the three outcomes are printed in the action's popup and that is the surface. ⚠ FLAGGED AS MY JUDGEMENT, not the owner's: the payload here is two things at once — an extra reaction restricted to Aiding one named ally, plus a +1 circumstance bonus to that Aid check — which is more than Q15's 'temporary Hit Points alone'. If the owner rules it complicated, it becomes a player-applied mode carrying both the extra restricted reaction (the reactions area would have to show a second, Aid-only reaction) and the +1 on the Aid roll. I am not asserting that; I am naming the boundary the owner has to sit on.

requirements.clause: Special Once per hour, you can Take the Lead of a troop as a free action (rather than 2 actions).
requirements.what: Take the Lead must be listed under BOTH costs — its native 2 actions and the free action this feat enables — with the explanation in the popup. This is exactly Principle H / the Quick Recognition shape (#13). It also requires reaching the Take the Lead record this feat modifies and marking it there (Principle C, Q8): the change belongs on the action the player is looking at, not only in this feat's own text.

requirements.clause: Special Once per hour, you can Take the Lead of a troop as a free action (rather than 2 actions).
requirements.what: A once-per-hour use attached to the free-action version — a spendable, visible use beside that entry, so the player can see whether the free-action option is still available. The per-hour period is the unusual part: the lane vocabulary admits 'N times per day/hour', but an hour is neither a rest boundary nor a round, so what refreshes it must be answerable.

requirements.clause: Outside of combat, you can establish leadership of a troop and grant a skirmish bond in half the normal time (5 minutes and 4 hours, respectively).
requirements.what: The halved times must be legible where the player looks up those two procedures — a marker on establishing leadership and on granting a skirmish bond carrying 5 minutes and 4 hours (Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). Per Ruling G it REPLACES the printed time rather than sitting beside it, since it is an upgrade of an existing value, not an addition. These are real numbers, not GM adjudication, so this clause is not exempt as flavour or exploration prose.

requirements.clause: You can ask questions of, receive answers from … rodents, including beavers, mice, porcupines, rats, and squirrels, but not with other mammals, such as dogs or bats.
requirements.what: A communication grant listed where the character's languages/communication live, naming the creature group (rodents) and carrying the exclusion (not other mammals such as dogs or bats). It is two-way — ask questions AND receive answers — so it is a conversation grant, not a one-way 'you can speak to' line. No numbers.

requirements.clause: …and use the Diplomacy skill with rodents…
requirements.what: A `*` on Diplomacy carrying that it may be used on rodents. This is a separate promise from the speech clause and must not be collapsed into it: it is a permission to run the skill against a creature type it would not normally reach. Principle J / Ruling C put the mark on the specific skill affected, where the player reads the number. No bonus value — the star carries text only.

requirements.clause: The GM determines which animals count as rodents.
requirements.what: Nothing. GM adjudication is explicitly not a lane. The sentence still belongs in the feat's printed text so the player reads it, but it asks nothing of the sheet.

requirements.clause: You learn a shadowdancer focus spell of your choice: Dance of Darkness or Shadow Jump.
requirements.what: A builder pick between exactly two named options, Dance of Darkness and Shadow Jump. Per Q9 the picker must offer only those two — the whole focus-spell list is not a legal option set here — and each option's own details must be readable at the point of choosing.

requirements.clause: You learn a shadowdancer focus spell of your choice: Dance of Darkness or Shadow Jump.
requirements.what: Whichever spell was picked appears as a focus spell the character can cast, with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as its source.

requirements.clause: If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus…
requirements.what: A focus pool of 1 Focus Point, but CONDITIONALLY: the grant is 'if you don't already have one', so a character who already has a pool gains nothing from this clause. That is a redundancy-conditional grant, not an unconditional +1 — expressing it as a flat pool increment would over-grant to any character with existing focus spells.

requirements.clause: …which you can Refocus by meditating within an area of dim light or darkness.
requirements.what: A marker on Refocus carrying this feat's refocus method and its condition (meditating within an area of dim light or darkness). Ruling D: the mark belongs on the activity the player is looking at when it matters, i.e. on Refocus, not buried in the feat's own text. It changes no number.

requirements.clause: Shadowdancer focus spells are occult spells.
requirements.what: The granted focus spell must carry the occult tradition on its own entry — this is a distinct promise from the grant itself and matters for anything that keys off tradition. It must not inherit the tradition of whatever other spellcasting the character happens to have.

requirements.clause: You become trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs…
requirements.what: A trained proficiency rank for occult spell attack rolls AND for occult spell DCs — both, as their own visible stat rows, since the character may have no other occult casting. Per Q10 the rank is applied only when it makes the player better; it must never lower an existing higher occult rank.

requirements.clause: …and your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.
requirements.what: That occult attack/DC entry must compute from Charisma specifically, independent of any other spellcasting attribute the character already uses, and the attribute must be visible in the breakdown so a character with, say, a Wisdom-keyed tradition can see why this number differs.

requirements.clause: You can lay claim to up to three additional domains, to a total maximum of four.
requirements.what: Up to three further domain picks, capped at four claimed domains in total counting any already claimed. The cap is on the total, not on this feat's own grants, so the counter has to see domains claimed elsewhere.

requirements.clause: When you gain this feat, you can choose not to lay claim to one or more domains immediately, instead leaving the space open until later in your story.
requirements.what: Unpicked claims must be representable as EMPTY SLOTS that persist and can be filled later, rather than the choice being forced at the moment the feat is taken or silently lost. This is the shape the owner already specified for the formula book at Q14 point 8 — an empty slot the player can press later to open that feature's option list.

requirements.clause: This domain remains a part of your portfolio forever and cannot be changed after this point.
requirements.what: A claimed domain must LOCK — a one-time write, not a re-editable builder pick. This is the Q14 point 9 shape ('the grant is a one-time write, never a live derivation'): once the slot is filled it cannot be re-chosen, which is the opposite of how an ordinary builder choice behaves. Principle K ('anything re-chosen in the builder needs no sheet surface') does NOT apply here, because this one explicitly cannot be re-chosen.

requirements.clause: each day during your daily preparations, decide which of your domains you are currently drawing power from; you gain access to this domain for the day and can cast its domain spells as normal, while your ability to access the power of your other domains lies dormant.
requirements.what: A daily-preparations choice of exactly ONE active domain among those claimed. The active domain's domain spells are castable; the other claimed domains' spells must be visibly present-but-dormant rather than simply absent, or the player loses sight of what they own. This is a gating choice, not a grant — it takes access away as well as giving it.

requirements.clause: You learn the advanced domain spell for any domain that you have claimed with your godling abilities.
requirements.what: The advanced domain spell of EVERY claimed domain is learned — all four, not just the active one. Combined with the daily-preparations clause, the sheet must distinguish 'known' from 'castable today': the advanced spells of dormant domains are known but dormant.

requirements.clause: As long as you have one or more domains unclaimed, you can spend a Mythic Point as a single action to claim a domain, even in the heat of battle, immediately making this your active domain.
requirements.what: A single action in the actions list, available only while an unclaimed slot remains, whose cost is a Mythic Point drawn from a Mythic Point resource. Using it does two things the sheet must express mid-play: it writes permanently into an empty domain slot (opening the domain picker from the sheet, not the builder) and it switches the active domain immediately, overriding that day's daily-preparations choice.

requirements.clause: You can also spend a Mythic Point to overcharge your divine power, gaining access to all the domains you have claimed for the next minute and passing this access on to your hierophant as normal.
requirements.what: A one-minute mode (Q1: a duration longer than a round earns a mode) activated by spending a Mythic Point, which while on opens every claimed domain's spells instead of just the active one. It must be plain that the mode is running and what it changed (Q3's principle — this genuinely overrides the daily gate). The hierophant half is ally-facing: per Principle A/B it is TEXT inside the mode, carried so the player can read it, contributing no number to this sheet.

requirements.clause: After the minute ends, you can choose which of the four domains you retain access to until your next daily preparations.
requirements.what: The active-domain choice must be re-openable when the overcharge mode ends, not only at daily preparations. So the choice cannot be wired exclusively to the rest/daily-prep event — it needs a second entry point tied to this mode expiring.

requirements.clause: While you're in this stance…
requirements.what: A toggleable stance the player turns on and off, mutually exclusive with other stances, entered by this feat's own stance activity. Per Q3's principle it must be plain that the stance is active. The mode contributes no numbers (Principle B) — its whole content is the text below — but it still must exist as a switchable state, because the rider only applies while it is on.

requirements.clause: …your ranged Strikes don't trigger Reactive Strike or other reactions that are triggered by a ranged attack.
requirements.what: A marker on the character's ranged Strikes, shown while the stance is active, carrying this text. It is a permission/immunity on the player's own attack, not an effect on the enemy, so it is not excluded by the enemy-side rule — Ruling D puts the mark on the thing it modifies (the ranged Strike entry), which is where the player is looking when it matters. Value-less: the star carries text only. Note it is worded openly ('or other reactions that are triggered by a ranged attack'), so per Ruling H the printed trigger goes in the note rather than being narrowed to Reactive Strike alone.

requirements.clause: Special If you have Reactive Strike, you can use it with a loaded ranged weapon you're wielding. The triggering creature must be within 5 feet of you for you to do so.
requirements.what: A marker on the Reactive Strike reaction ITSELF (Principle C / Q8: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing), carrying the loaded-ranged-weapon permission and the 5-foot proximity limit in that reaction's popup. Two things make this easy to get wrong: it is conditional on the character actually having Reactive Strike, so it must appear only then; and it is NOT gated on the stance — the Special makes no reference to being in the stance, so hiding it inside the mode would make it invisible whenever the stance is off, which is most of the time.
Flavour/summary sentence announcing what the feat is about. No mechanical promise of its own — everything it gestures at is delivered by the clauses below.
requirements.clause: You can take the shape of a plant creature.

requirements.what: An innate-spell entry for Plant Form, reachable from the spells surface with the spell's own details, granted ONLY when the character lacks Untamed Form. This branch and the Untamed Form branch are mutually exclusive, so acquiring or losing Untamed Form must flip which of the two the sheet shows — a character who has Untamed Form must not see a Plant Form innate spell at all. The text names no tradition, so nothing about a tradition is owed here beyond whatever the grant itself establishes.
requirements.clause: If you don't have untamed form, you can cast Plant Form once per day

requirements.what: The entry's rank is a FORMULA off the character, not a fixed number: it must read as (and be castable at) the rank of the character's highest-rank druid spell slot, and must follow that rank upward as the character levels. A hardcoded rank would be wrong at every level but one. Same shape as Wyrmling Flight's Speed-derived value (Q7) — where the value cannot be conveyed by a bare number, the derivation has to be visible to the player at the entry.
requirements.clause: heightened to the same rank as your highest-rank druid spell slot

requirements.what: One use per day attached to that innate spell: a spendable use shown beside the entry, consumed on casting and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: once per day

requirements.what: When the character DOES have Untamed Form, the shapes printed in Plant Form must be added to the Untamed Form shape list and be selectable there — the addition must be reflected in the thing it modifies (Principle C), not merely stated in this feat's own description. The player looks for their available shapes on Untamed Form, so that is where the new options must appear.
requirements.clause: If you do have Untamed Form, add the shapes listed in Plant Form to your Untamed Form list

requirements.what: Resistance 5 to poison that exists only while the character is polymorphed via Untamed Form — it must ride on the untamed-form shape state and appear in the resistances breakdown while that state is active, not as a permanent sheet resistance. Per Q3 a battle form is a mode that really overrides the stats it names and must make plain a mode is active and what changed, so this resistance is part of what those modes must show as changed. It applies to ANY untamed-form shape, not only the plant shapes this feat adds.
requirements.clause: whenever you're polymorphed into another shape using untamed form, you gain resistance 5 to poison

requirements.what: A new named activity, Acknowledge Fan, in the actions list, with its full text in its popup — the targeting restriction (one creature who can see you), the save, and the four outcome lines. Per Q4's shape, for an ability whose whole payload is a condition on an enemy, the entry itself is the surface; the player reads it there and tells the GM.
requirements.clause: Choose one target creature who can see you to acknowledge.

requirements.what: The action's popup must state which DC the target rolls against and resolve it: the HIGHER of the character's class DC and spell DC. Both numbers exist elsewhere on the sheet, but which one applies is derived and changes as the character levels, so the player must be able to read the single governing number where the action lives rather than compare two stats by hand. A character with no spellcasting has only one of the two, and the resolution must still produce a usable number.
requirements.clause: The target must attempt a save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

requirements.what: Nothing. Temporary immunity is bookkeeping on the target, not on this character's sheet — DECIDED SCOPE puts effects on enemies out of scope, and the printed text in the action's popup already tells the player what to track with the GM. This is NOT a per-day use of the character's own, so no limitedUses is owed by it.
requirements.clause: Regardless of the result, the target becomes temporarily immune to Acknowledge Fan for 1 minute.

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text in the action popup already required above. Stunned 1, Stunned 2 and paralyzed all land on the target; enemy conditions are decided scope and produce no marker, no mode, and no number on this character's sheet.
requirements.clause: Critical Success The target is unaffected… Success The target is Stunned 1… Failure The target is Stunned 2. Critical Failure The target is paralyzed until the end of your next turn.

requirements.what: The feat/action must display exactly ONE of the arcane or occult traits, resolved from the choice the player already made on Mesmerizing Gaze — not both, and not neither. This is a real trait of a magical effect, so it must be legible where the player reads the action, and it is derived from an earlier pick on a different record rather than fixed on this one. If the earlier choice is not recoverable, the popup must at minimum carry the clause so the player knows the trait tracks that pick.
requirements.clause: Special This feat has either the arcane or occult trait, matching the choice you made when you took Mesmerizing Gaze.

requirements.what: Flavour and roleplay guidance about a peri's spirit and an impulse to right wrongs. No mechanical promise; the GM adjudicates behaviour, and nothing on the sheet is owed.
requirements.clause: A peri's roaring spirit burns in your soul… You have a direct impulse to right wrongs and better the world.

requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus that must NOT sit in the flat save totals (Ruling B) — it belongs in the situational lane with 'against fire effects' as its condition. Per Q2, because it applies to saving throws generally rather than to one named save, it must be starred on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — so the player finds it wherever they look up the number, with the +1 circumstance value and the fire-effect restriction in the note.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against fire effects

requirements.what: A star on Perception carrying the clause verbatim: the character's Perception is unaffected by non-magical flames, fog and smoke. There is no number here — it removes concealment/vision impediments the app does not model — but the mark must live on Perception, the stat the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D/J). Note the non-magical restriction is load-bearing and must survive into the note: magical fog and smoke still impede normally.
requirements.clause: your perception is unaffected by non-magical flames, fog and smoke

requirements.what: Restatement of the feat's premise. No independent mechanical promise.
requirements.clause: You have perfected the formulas for bombs that impede your enemies.

requirements.what: An indication on Debilitating Bomb itself — the record this feat changes — that its outcome has been altered, with the changed wording in that record's popup (Principle C; Q8 applies Ruling D's shape: mark the thing the feat modifies). The player looks at Debilitating Bomb when they throw one, so the change has to be visible there and not only in this feat's own description. What changes is the degree-of-success threshold on the TARGET's save (only a critical success now avoids the condition), and the condition itself lands on the enemy, so no number moves on this character's sheet — the marker on Debilitating Bomb is the entire surface owed.
requirements.clause: When you use Debilitating Bomb, your target avoids the condition the bomb imposes only if it critically succeeds at its saving throw.

requirements.what: Flavour about Maelstrom-touched blood. No mechanical promise.
requirements.clause: Your blood bubbles with the roiling quintessence of the Maelstrom, the infinite sea of primal chaos that long ago spawned the other Outer Planes.

requirements.what: A resistance entry in the defences breakdown whose VALUE is half the character's level — a level-scaling formula that must recompute as the character levels, not a fixed number. Exactly one damage type is resisted at a time (the one currently determined), so this must not appear as three simultaneous resistances.
requirements.clause: You gain resistance to a single damage type equal to half your level

requirements.what: A daily-preparation selection recording which of acid, electricity or sonic the resistance currently applies to, re-set each day (rest = daily preparations). The determination is random, so the sheet's job is to RECORD the rolled outcome rather than to let the player freely pick a preferred type — but whichever way the roll is made, the chosen type must persist for the day and drive the resistance entry above. Until the day's type is set, the resistance has no damage type and the sheet must not silently assume one.
requirements.clause: at the beginning of each day, determine randomly whether this resistance applies to acid, electricity, or sonic damage

requirements.what: A restricted +1 circumstance bonus kept out of the flat save totals (Ruling B), starred on ALL THREE saves per Q2 since it names saving throws generally, with 'against effects that would cause you to gain the controlled condition' as the condition in the note. The rules name no single save for such effects, so per Ruling H stay open — star everything plausible rather than narrowing it to one save on the sheet's own authority.
requirements.clause: You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would cause you to gain the controlled condition.
**Trigger** Your turn begins.
requirements.what: A triggered activity in the actions list (the text gives a Trigger but no cost, so it belongs wherever triggered entries live), with the trigger "your turn begins" shown in its popup. Per Principle E's shape — trigger and requirements in the popup — this is much of the whole surface.

requirements.clause: You continue Juggling until the end of your next turn.
requirements.what: A marker on the Juggle activity (granted by an earlier record, not by this feat) showing this feat can extend its duration. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. The duration itself is "until the end of your next turn" — the one-round shape, which Q1 rules is indication only, so no mode and no timer; the player reads the text.

requirements.clause: Increase the maximum number of items you can juggle by one.
requirements.what: The item maximum the player reads on the Juggle activity must show this +1. The number lives on Juggle, not on any general stat, so per Ruling D and Principle C the increment must reach that entry rather than sit only in this feat's own text. ⚠ The text does not say whether the increase is permanent or lasts only for the extended juggling; either reading still requires the same surface on Juggle, so the marker must carry the printed wording rather than resolve the ambiguity.

requirements.clause: Select a magical effect that has made an adjacent member of your crop clumsy, grabbed, paralyzed, restrained, or slowed. Attempt a counteract check using your attack modifier (including your multiple attack penalty) with a melee weapon with which you have expert proficiency.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list, with its full procedure in the popup: the eligible conditions, that the counteract check uses your attack modifier including MAP rather than a spell or skill modifier, and that it requires a melee weapon you are expert with. The check itself is an internal step the player performs — the app's obligation is that the action EXISTS and that these constraints are legible where the player opens it.

requirements.clause: Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: A level-derived value, so a fixed printed number would be wrong at every level but one. The action's popup must carry the rank resolved for this character (or the formula), the same shape as the counteract-rank clause folded into The Truth as I See it's star.

requirements.clause: On a success, you free that member from the effect.
requirements.what: NOTHING on your sheet. The effect ends on someone else — Ruling F, the DECIDED SCOPE case: an effect landing on a teammate produces no star and no modifier. The action's own description already tells the player what the ally gets, and that description is already required by the grantsAction clause above.

requirements.clause: On a failure, you can't attempt to use Cut the Bonds on that effect on that crop member until 24 hours have passed.
requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the printed text in the popup. This is not a limitedUses resource: it is not a pool of your own uses but a lockout keyed to one specific effect on one specific creature and triggered only by failure. There is no countable thing to spend, so no per-day tracker is owed; the player and GM remember which target is locked out.

requirements.clause: Once per year, when you die, your remains become protected as if under the effects of a 5th-rank Peaceful Rest spell.
requirements.what: NOTHING. This is not an innateSpell — you never cast Peaceful Rest, your corpse merely benefits from its effect — and it fires only on your death, which is not a sheet state the character plays from. "Once per year" is not a trackable resource in the per-day/per-hour sense the limitedUses lane covers, and there is nothing to spend while alive. Considered and rejected rather than absent.

requirements.clause: If your remains are brought and buried within 1 mile of where you were born, after a week, you return to life with the effects of a successful (but not critically successful) 9th-rank Resurrect ritual.
requirements.what: NOTHING. This is not a ritual grant — the character does not learn Resurrect and cannot perform it; the outcome is delivered to them. Every condition (who carries the remains, where you were born, a week passing) is GM-adjudicated narrative with no number, no action, no choice, and no other record modified. This feat legitimately requires nothing of the sheet beyond its own description being readable.

requirements.clause: Your body transforms into a swarm of bees. You Fly up to twice your Speed… At the end of your movement, you return to your original form.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list with its full text in the popup. Explicitly NOT a mode: the form begins and ends inside the single action ("at the end of your movement, you return to your original form") and overrides none of your stats, so Q3's battle-form ruling — a mode that really overrides the stats it names — is not triggered here. There is no duration to display.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour
requirements.what: A single spendable use displayed beside the action and consumed when used. The limitedUses lane covers "N times per day/hour" explicitly, so the hourly period is in scope; what the sheet must express is that the use is expended and can be restored, since the app has no hour clock to restore it automatically.

requirements.clause: You Fly up to twice your Speed
requirements.what: The distance is a formula off your own Speed, so the popup must carry it as such (or resolved for this character) rather than as a fixed number — the same reason Wyrmling Flight's Speed-derived value could not be conveyed by a bare figure. This grants no persistent fly Speed: the flight is an internal step of the activity, spent and over, so no `speed` entry is owed.

requirements.clause: during this movement you can pass through any space that would be small enough for a single insect, and your movement does not trigger reactions
requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the printed text in the popup. Both are battlefield/enemy-facing facts about one movement — what an enemy may react to, and what spaces the GM lets you cross — not numbers on your sheet.

requirements.clause: If you pass through an enemy's space, you can inflict a storm of stings that deals damage, with a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: NOTHING new. Damage lands on enemies and, per DECIDED SCOPE, damage never moves sheet stats; the save is against your class DC, a stat the sheet already carries. ⚠ Worth flagging as a TEXT defect rather than a requirement: this text names no base damage at all, only the later increase — the printed clause is incomplete.

requirements.clause: At 10th level and every two levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4 piercing damage and 1d4 poison damage.
requirements.what: A level-scaling value the player must be able to read at their current level. The damage does not move any sheet stat, but Principle B's requirement — the player must still be able to read what it does — means the action's entry must present the amount for this character rather than leaving static prose the player recomputes each level.

requirements.clause: You spend 10 minutes meditating with your harrow deck, then draw a card. **Requirements** You do not have an active harrow omen.
requirements.what: An activity in the actions list, with its requirement ("you do not have an active harrow omen") and its 10-minute duration in the popup — exactly the Minor Omen shape, where requirements printed in the popup are most of the obligation. The harrow deck it names is an item prerequisite mentioned in the text, not a separate lane.

requirements.clause: The suit of the card grants you a new harrow omen.
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to record WHICH harrow omen is currently held, identified by suit, and let the player set it — the card is drawn at random, so this is a player-recorded selection rather than a build-time pick, which Principle I's free-text/player-input ruling establishes as a legitimate choice type. The omen's own text must be readable from that record.

requirements.clause: You do not have an active harrow omen. / …grants you a new harrow omen.
requirements.what: The feat's own Requirements line proves the sheet must express a binary state — omen active vs not — and this action's legality reads off it. So an active omen is a state the character carries and can clear, which Q11 classifies as a mode rather than a passive bonus because it can be ended. What the omen itself does is not in this text, so nothing further is specified from here; the requirement is the holdable, clearable state and its visibility.

requirements.clause: (no Frequency line)
requirements.what: NOTHING — no limitedUses is owed. The action carries no frequency; it is repeatable and gated solely by not already having an active omen, which the mode clause above already covers. Stated explicitly so the absence is not later read as a missing per-day tracker.

requirements.clause: Strike twice, once with your weapon and once with its haft… Then Strike twice again, once with your weapon and once with its haft.
requirements.what: Haft Beatdown must exist as its own named activity in the actions list, with its full routine text reachable in its popup. The Strikes inside it are internal steps the player performs — the sheet owes the activity's EXISTENCE and text, not four synthesized attack entries.

requirements.clause: Each attack counts towards your multiple attack penalty, but do not increase your penalty until you have made both attacks.
requirements.what: The multiple-attack-penalty exception must be legible in the activity's popup. It is a deviation from the standard MAP ladder that a printed Strike line cannot convey — the second Strike of each pair uses the SAME attack number as the first — and it is not computable, so it is carried as text on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D / principle G).

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are in Haft Striker Stance.
requirements.what: The requirement line printed in the activity's popup. This is the shape the owner gave Minor Omen — "the Requirement needs to be writen in the pop up" — and it is the whole of what a Requirements line owes. Nothing needs to gate or hide the entry.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per minute
requirements.what: Printed in the entry/popup only; no spendable resource is owed. The Minor Omen answer settled that a granted activity's Frequency line is satisfied by the popup text ("there isnt a need for it to imact the sheet in another way"), and a per-minute window sits below anything the sheet's resource cycle could restore — the same reason principle B gives for rounds contributing no number.

requirements.clause: once with its haft
requirements.what: NOTHING owed by this feat. The ability to Strike with the weapon's haft is presupposed by the Requirements line (Haft Striker Stance), not granted here, so this feat carries no grantsStrike requirement. ⚠ Flagged rather than assumed: if no other record makes a haft attack available, the routine is unperformable — but that is the stance's requirement to meet, not this feat's.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level ranger feat.
requirements.what: A picker in the builder offering ranger class feats of level 1 or 2. Per Q9 it must show only what the player may legally pick — the level bound AND each candidate feat's own prerequisites — unless the player toggles "show options not meeting prerequisites".

requirements.clause: You gain a … ranger feat.
requirements.what: Whatever is picked must be OWNED in full, not recorded as a label: every lane the chosen feat itself promises must fire exactly as if the feat had been taken normally (its own grants, stars, actions, spells), and its details must be readable from the character's feat list with this feat named as the source. A feat grant that only stores a name expresses nothing.

requirements.clause: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level ranger feat.
requirements.what: The act of choosing needs no sheet surface of its own — principle K, anything the player re-chooses in the builder is a builder action. The only sheet consequence is the picked feat itself.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day --- …for one moment, this raw material from the Great Beyond envelops you and your comrades.
requirements.what: The feat must appear as an activatable entry in the actions list (the Frequency line means it is used, not passive), with its Frequency and its full effect text in the popup. Per the Minor Omen answer, the once-per-day Frequency is satisfied by that printed entry and owes no further sheet impact.

requirements.clause: Until the end of your next turn, you and any allies adjacent to you get a +4 circumstance bonus to AC
requirements.what: YOUR half of the AC bonus must be readable, as a number, in the entry's text — but it must NOT become an AC modifier or a mode. Q1 governs: an effect lasting until the end of your next turn is one round, and one-round effects are indication only. So the requirement is that the +4 circumstance to AC is stated where the player reads the ability, not that AC moves.

requirements.clause: …and are quickened. The additional action can be used only to Strike or Stride.
requirements.what: The quickened condition on YOU, and the restriction that the extra action may only Strike or Stride, must be carried in the same entry's text. Same one-round window, so under Q1 it is indication only — no applied condition, no extra-action surface, no mode.

requirements.clause: you and any allies adjacent to you
requirements.what: The ally-facing half requires NOTHING beyond the indication already owed above. DECIDED SCOPE (Ruling F/N): an effect that lands on a teammate puts no number on your sheet. Principle A's "indication on the record it modifies" is satisfied here because the record it modifies is this feat's own entry, whose text already states what adjacent allies get. Adjacency is positional and, like Ruling M's auras, is not a thing the sheet can know.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wearing medium or heavy armor in which you have expert proficiency. **Trigger** An undead hits you with an unarmed attack.
requirements.what: A REACTION in the reactions list, with its trigger (an undead hits you with an unarmed attack) and its requirement (wearing medium or heavy armour you are expert in) shown in the popup. Principle E — for a reaction this is often the whole requirement, and the requirement text is printed, not enforced.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance 5 to physical damage and resistance 10 to void damage against the triggering attack.
requirements.what: Two resistances with distinct values and types — 5 physical, 10 void — must be expressible as applying ONLY to the triggering attack. They must not be folded into the character's standing resistance totals: Ruling B's shape is that a bonus the rules restrict lives with its restriction rather than in the stat total. If resistances are surfaced with their sources, this one belongs there as a conditional entry carrying "against the triggering attack"; at minimum both numbers must be legible in the reaction's popup.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on any saving throws against effects from the undead's natural attack;
requirements.what: A `*` on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — since the clause says "any saving throws" and Q2 rules that a bonus applying to saves generally stars all three. Each star carries +2 circumstance and its condition (against effects from the triggering undead's natural attack), so the player sees it where they look up the save number.

requirements.clause: if you succeed at the saving throw, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success promotion (success → critical success). This is not a number and gets no computed surface; it rides in the same save stars' note text alongside the +2, so a player reading the star learns both what the bonus is and what a success turns into. Nothing else is owed.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're under the effects of Enter Spirit Trance.
requirements.what: Invoke Defense must appear as its own action entry, with the requirement (you are under the effects of Enter Spirit Trance) printed in its popup, plus the text of what it manifests. The entry is what the player presses to make the choice below.

requirements.clause: Choose bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
requirements.what: A three-option pick — bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Crucially this is a USE-TIME choice, not a build-time one: it is made when the action is taken and remade whenever it is taken again, so it cannot live only in the builder (principle K does not apply). The pick must be visible, showing which type is currently chosen.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance … to that damage type for the duration of your spirit trance.
requirements.what: A mode — a state that is on for the duration of the spirit trance and off otherwise. Q11 decides it: the effect can be shut down (the trance ends), so it is a mode rather than a passive bonus. Q3's rider applies — while it is on, the sheet must make plain that a mode is active and what it changed.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance equal to half your level to that damage type
requirements.what: A resistance whose VALUE is derived from the character's level (half your level), not a stored constant — it must recompute as the character levels, and it must apply to whichever of the three types is currently chosen. While the mode is on it belongs in the resistance display with this feat named as its source; a text-only note would leave the player computing their own defence.

requirements.clause: If you use Invoke Defense again, you can choose a different type of damage, but you lose the previous resistance.
requirements.what: The three types are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Choosing a new damage type must remove the previous resistance rather than adding a second one — the sheet must never show two of the three at once. This is an exclusivity constraint on the pick, distinct from the pick itself, and it is the clause most easily lost if the choice is modelled as an additive grant.

requirements.clause: "If the next action you use this turn is to Cast a non-cantrip Spell that affects an area, expand the area of the spell."
requirements.what: The feat is itself an activity the player performs immediately before Casting a Spell, so it must appear in the actions list as a usable entry with its full text in the popup. The sheet must be able to express an action whose effect attaches to the NEXT action taken this turn; that sequencing is player-tracked and needs no state (the printed text is the whole instruction). The text as given states no action cost, so no cost is asserted here — whatever cost the record carries must be shown on the entry.

requirements.clause: "For bursts, expand the radius by 5 feet; for cones, expand the cone by 10 feet; and for lines, expand the length by 15 feet."
requirements.what: No computed surface is owed. These are the internal effect of the activity, read from its own popup; the sheet is not required to recompute any spell's printed area. The requirement is only that the three shape-specific values be legible in full on the action's entry rather than truncated to a summary.

requirements.clause: "If the next action you use this turn is to Cast a non-cantrip Spell that affects an area, expand the area of the spell." (viewed from the spell's side)
requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not stated by the owner: an indication on the spells this feat can modify that the option exists — the Lay on Hands shape from principles A and C ("there needs to be indication that this effect exist"), applied to an open class of records rather than one named record. Ruling H ("where the rules are open, stay open") argues for marking every non-cantrip spell with an area. Flagged rather than assumed because unlike Lay on Hands the affected records are identified by a property (non-cantrip + has an area), not named, and the owner has not ruled on metamagic.

requirements.clause: "The spell gains the wood trait."
requirements.what: No requirement. A trait added to one casting only, for that casting; it changes no number on the sheet and is carried by the activity's own text.

requirements.clause: "When you fail a Deception check, reroll with your Diplomacy modifier."
requirements.what: A `*` on Deception carrying the reroll clause — this is where the player looks up the number that can fail, so per principle J the mark goes on the specific skill, not on a general stat. The note must convey that the reroll is made with a DIFFERENT skill's modifier, since neither skill's own total changes.

requirements.clause: "...reroll with your Diplomacy modifier."
requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME: a `*` on Diplomacy as well. The reroll is performed by reading the Diplomacy modifier, so under Ruling C's shape (star every skill the player would look up when it matters) and Ruling H (star everything plausible) Diplomacy is a place the player needs to see this exists. Lower confidence than the Deception star; flagged rather than assumed.

requirements.clause: "On a success, there are no hard feelings and the other person's attitude condition doesn't worsen."
requirements.what: No requirement. The effect lands on another creature's attitude condition — DECIDED SCOPE (effects on someone else / on the target's condition produce nothing on your sheet). The wording still belongs inside the Deception star's text so the player can read the outcome.

requirements.clause: "On a critical success, you can attempt the Deception again with no consequences."
requirements.what: No requirement. Q15: an effect firing on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED; re-attempting a check is not complicated. Text only, inside the same note.

requirements.clause: "Whenever you critically succeed at an attack roll against an enemy and use Lethal Edge, add the following effects to the list you can choose from."
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to express that this feat ADDS two options to a list another record (Lethal Edge) already grants, and the addition must be visible in Lethal Edge itself — principle C, "a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing." The two new options must appear as choosable entries alongside Lethal Edge's native ones, attributed to this feat, not only as prose in the feat's own description.

requirements.clause: "The target is cursed and can't benefit from circumstance or status bonuses. This is a curse effect."
requirements.what: No requirement beyond the option's text. The condition lands on the enemy — DECIDED SCOPE, enemy conditions are not the sheet's problem. The full wording (including that it is a curse effect) must be readable in the option entry added above.

requirements.clause: "The target gains weakness 10 to spirit damage."
requirements.what: No requirement. A weakness on the TARGET, not on you; the `weakness` lane describes your own weaknesses and must not be used here. Text only, inside the option entry.

requirements.clause: "Whenever you critically succeed at an attack roll against an enemy..."
requirements.what: No requirement. Q15 — a critical-success trigger needs no implementation unless the effect is complicated. Choosing from a list of printed effects is not complicated; the trigger is stated on the option entry and applied at the table.

requirements.clause: "While in this stance..." / "**Requirements** You are unarmored."
requirements.what: A toggleable stance mode (Q11 — it can be shut down, therefore a mode, not a passive bonus), mutually exclusive with other stances, and it must be plain that it is active. The mode entry must carry the printed Requirement "You are unarmored" the way a reaction carries its trigger (principle E) — the sheet must be able to show a precondition it does not necessarily enforce.

requirements.clause: "You stand firm... While in this stance..."
requirements.what: Entering the stance is an action, so it must also be reachable as an entry in the actions list with its full text and requirement in the popup — the player performs it, then the mode runs.

requirements.clause: "you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by using actions with the concentrate or manipulate traits"
requirements.what: A restricted AC bonus: +4 circumstance, applying only against reactions triggered by your own concentrate or manipulate actions. Ruling B — a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in the situational lane with the restriction as its `when`, and sitting OUTSIDE the AC total is correct. It must be visible in the AC breakdown as a starred conditional entry, and only while the mode is on.

requirements.clause: "when you cast a spell that requires one or more actions while in this stance, your unarmed Strikes gain a +1 circumstance bonus to damage"
requirements.what: A `*` on every unarmed Strike carrying +1 circumstance damage, with its `when` = after Casting a Spell that costs one or more actions, while this stance is active. Ruling D/J — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (the Strike entries), not on a general damage stat. Doubly conditional: gated by the mode AND by the spell condition, so the sheet must be able to nest a situational marker inside a mode.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Trigger** You gain the doomed condition."
