requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (you gain the doomed condition) shown in its popup — principle E. This is the entry point for everything below.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per 10 minutes"
requirements.what: The frequency must be legible on the reaction's entry. It is a display requirement, not a counter: the reset is a 10-minute clock, which is neither a per-day resource restored at daily preparations nor anything the sheet tracks, so no spendable use pip is owed. The requirement is that the sheet can print a frequency whose reset event it does not model.

requirements.clause: "You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level and a +1 status bonus to all saving throws, both of which last for 1 minute."
requirements.what: A mode the player turns on when the reaction fires. Q1 — one round is not implemented, but a longer duration gets a mode, and one minute is longer. The mode must state its 1-minute duration and make plain it is running.

requirements.clause: "a +1 status bonus to all saving throws... last for 1 minute"
requirements.what: Inside that mode, a REAL number: +1 status bonus to Fortitude, Reflex and Will alike (Q2's "when it applies to saves generally, all three"). This is the Shield the Faithful shape from Q1 — the self-facing half of a timed effect carries actual modifiers, not just text, and they must appear in each save's breakdown while the mode is active.

requirements.clause: "You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level"
requirements.what: Text inside the same mode, stated as a formula off your level rather than a fixed number so it stays correct as the character levels. Per Ruling E, HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode, so this contributes no automatic change — the requirement is that the mode can carry a level-scaled value the player applies to the HP control themselves.

requirements.clause: "It gains one of the following effects." — Baleful Body / Chimeric Heads / Energy Aegis / Magnificent Flight / Protective Skin
requirements.what: A builder choice of exactly ONE of five named options, recorded on the character, with each option's full text readable at the point of choosing (each option carries several distinct promises, so the description is load-bearing, not flavour).

requirements.clause: "Your united companion must have a head and at least one unarmed attack that uses its mouth or head (such as a beak, jaws, or mandible attack) to select this."
requirements.what: Per Q9 the option list must offer only what the player may legally pick, so Chimeric Heads must be filtered out unless the united companion actually has a head-or-mouth unarmed attack. This is a prerequisite evaluated against ANOTHER record's granted creature, not against the character.

requirements.clause: "Choose acid, fire, or poison" (Baleful Body); "immune to your choice of acid, cold, electricity, or fire" (Energy Aegis)
requirements.what: A second, dependent choice that only exists once the parent option is picked. The picked type then has to name the damage type of the reactive damage / the immunity, and Energy Aegis's "+1 status bonus to AC and saves that originate from creatures with the listed trait and to effects and spells with the listed trait" resolves against that same pick.

requirements.clause: All the numeric effects: "deals half your level in damage", "gains all-around vision", "becomes immune to your choice of...", "+1 status bonus to AC and saves", "gains a Fly speed equal to its Speed and it gains the mount special ability", "maximum Hit Points increase by 30 but it gains a weakness of 10 to either cold iron or silver"
requirements.what: Every one of these lands on the UNITED COMPANION, a creature another record already granted, so it must be reflected in that companion's stat block (Principle C) and NOT on the character's sheet (DECIDED SCOPE — a companion's bonus marks the companion). What the companion's block must be able to express: a damage-dealing retaliation keyed to half the character's level, a sense (all-around vision), an immunity, a situational +1 status to AC and to saves restricted by trait, a fly Speed derived from its own Speed, a special ability (mount), a maximum-HP increase, and a weakness. Absence from the character's sheet is correct here, not a gap.

requirements.clause: "If your united companion already had the mount special ability or a Fly speed equal to its Speed, it instead increases its Speed by 10 feet."
requirements.what: A redundancy test against what the companion ALREADY has, resolving to a different grant (+10 feet Speed) when it fires. The test reads two separate prior facts about the companion, and the substitute grant is of a different kind from the thing it replaces.

requirements.clause: "By spending a Mythic Point when you Command your united companion, ..." — one such activity in each of the five options
requirements.what: The chosen option teaches a new named activity, available where the player Commands the companion, and the sheet must carry its action cost (2-action activity / single action / single action with the concentrate trait / two-action activity), its Mythic Point cost, and its full effect text. Two values inside must resolve rather than print as formulas: Baleful Body's basic Reflex save is "against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher" — a higher-of-two DC computed from the CHARACTER, the one player-side number in this feat — and Protective Skin's "fast healing equal to your level for 1 minute". The fast healing moves no stat (HP and damage never move sheet stats) and belongs as text.

requirements.clause: "**Trigger** You would take cold, electricity, fire, poison, or sonic damage."
requirements.what: A triggered ability that appears in the triggered-ability (reactions) list, with the full trigger text — all five damage types — shown in its popup. Per Principle E that listing is most of the requirement.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per day"
requirements.what: One spendable use per day, displayed with the ability, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: "You gain resistance equal to your level against the triggering damage type."
requirements.what: The value is a formula off the character's level, so the ability's popup must show the resolved number, not the words "equal to your level" (the Wyrmling Flight shape — a bare printed value cannot convey it). It must NOT become a standing resistance: it lasts only for the one triggering damage instance, and which of the five types it applies to is not known until the trigger fires, so no entry may appear in the character's resistances.

requirements.clause: "**Trigger** You're about to roll initiative."
requirements.what: A triggered ability listed among the character's triggered abilities, with its trigger printed in the popup.

requirements.clause: "Spend a Mythic Point"
requirements.what: An activation cost paid from the Mythic Point pool — the ability has no Frequency of its own, so the only limit is the pool. The sheet must be able to show that this ability costs 1 Mythic Point and to spend from that shared pool when it is used.

requirements.clause: "roll your initiative check using mythic proficiency"
requirements.what: A proficiency SUBSTITUTION on one specific roll: for this roll only, the normal proficiency behind initiative is replaced by a mythic proficiency rank. Two things must be expressible — a mythic proficiency value existing on the character at all, and a marker on the initiative entry (and, per Ruling C, on whatever skill or Perception is currently set to roll initiative) carrying this substitution so the player sees it where they look the number up.

requirements.clause: "Until the end of your first turn, you have a +1 status bonus to AC and all saves."
requirements.what: Duration is a single turn, so per Q1 this is indication only and contributes no computed number — no mode, no bonus in the AC or save totals. The requirement is that the text be readable in the ability's popup, stating the +1 status bonus and that it covers AC and all three saves.

requirements.clause: "You adopt a stance that allows your apparitions to channel spiritual energy..."
requirements.what: A stance the player turns on and off — it can be shut down, so per Q11 it is a mode, and per the stance rules it is exclusive with other stances. Everything else this feat grants exists only while the stance is on, so the mode has to be able to own a granted strike, not just modifiers.

requirements.clause: "You call forth roots, vines, or other plant growth native to the region and can use them to make unarmed attacks. These deal 4d8 damage, are in the brawling group, and have the finesse, grapple, and reach 30 feet traits."
requirements.what: A granted unarmed attack that appears in the strikes list while the stance is active, carrying damage dice 4d8, the brawling weapon group, and the traits finesse, grapple, and reach 30 feet. Two of those are demanding: finesse must actually let the strike's attack roll use Dexterity, and reach must be expressible as 30 feet — an arbitrary value far outside the normal 5/10-foot reach, not a boolean reach trait. The text names no damage type, so none may be invented.

requirements.clause: "Attacks made with these unarmed attacks don't gain additional damage from striking runes, but can benefit from the item bonus to attack rolls and property runes of Handwraps of Mighty Blows you wear."
requirements.what: A per-strike exception to how Handwraps of Mighty Blows normally propagate: this strike must take the handwraps' potency item bonus to attack rolls and their property runes, while suppressing the striking rune's extra damage dice. The sheet must be able to split those three normally-inseparable effects of one worn item on one strike, and the strike's damage breakdown must show the striking dice absent while the attack breakdown shows the item bonus present.

requirements.clause: "**Requirements** Your attuned apparition grants Forest Lore or Herbalism Lore as one of its apparition skills."
requirements.what: No sheet requirement. This is a prerequisite/requirement clause, and prerequisites are not a mechanical lane. It gates whether the feat may be taken (a condition read off another record's granted apparition), which is builder-side eligibility, not a surface on the sheet.

requirements.clause: "You ignore difficult terrain from underbrush within forests and jungles."
requirements.what: A `*` on the character's Speed carrying this clause — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D), and difficult terrain is read off Speed. It contributes no number; the note must keep the printed restriction intact (underbrush specifically, and only within forests and jungles), since narrowing or widening it would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's (Ruling H).

requirements.clause: "You can always use the Take Cover action when you're within forest or jungle terrain to gain cover, even if you aren't adjacent to an obstacle you can Take Cover behind."
requirements.what: A marker on the Take Cover action itself (Q8 — mark the action the feat modifies), stating that the adjacency requirement is waived in forest or jungle terrain. This requires Take Cover to exist as a reachable action record on the sheet that a feat can attach a marker to. The cover the action grants is positional and GM-adjudicated, so nothing is owed on AC.

requirements.clause: You gain the hand of the apprentice universalist spell. Universalist spells are a type of focus spell, much like school spells.
requirements.what: The Hand of the Apprentice spell must reach the Spells page as a FOCUS spell the character can cast, with its own full description reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. The second sentence is classification, not a second promise: 'universalist spell' is a label for a focus spell, so it must file among focus spells rather than as a separate spell category or a loose note on the feat. What the spell itself does (hurling your weapon) is the spell record's text, not this feat's obligation.

requirements.clause: You start with a focus pool of 1 Focus Point.
requirements.what: A focus pool of 1 point: a spendable Focus Point displayed beside the focus spells, consumed when the spell is cast, and restored by Refocus. It is an increase, not an assignment — a character who already holds a pool from another source must end up with a larger pool, not a pool reset to 1.

requirements.clause: Prerequisites universalist wizard ... See here for more information about focus spells. Hand of the Apprentice leads to... Universal Versatility
requirements.what: No requirement. The prerequisite line is explicitly excluded from the lanes, and 'See here for more information' plus 'leads to... Universal Versatility' are Archives-of-Nethys cross-reference and navigation furniture carried into the text field, not printed mechanics. Neither owes any sheet surface.

requirements.clause: Choose one of the eidolon's unarmed attacks with the shove trait.
requirements.what: A choice recorded on the character, offering the eidolon's own unarmed attacks and only those carrying the shove trait. Per Q9 the builder shows only what may legally be picked, so the picker must be filtered to that eidolon's attack list rather than to weapons or strikes generally, and the pick must be remembered so the grant below knows which attack it lands on.

requirements.clause: It gains the Push action for that attack.
requirements.what: The Push action must become available and must be attached to the ONE attack that was chosen, not to the eidolon's attacks generally. Two constraints on where it shows: the companion ruling puts a companion-facing effect on the companion, so the mark belongs on the eidolon's stat block and nothing is owed on the summoner's own action list or stats; and Principle C — the eidolon's unarmed attacks were granted by another record, so a feat that modifies one of them must be reflected in that attack's own entry (a `modifiesGrant`-shaped obligation), not left as prose hanging off the feat.

requirements.clause: Your eidolon has an attack that pushes away enemies.
requirements.what: No requirement. Flavour restating the granted action, and the effect it describes (moving an enemy) lands on the enemy, which is out of scope by decided policy.

requirements.clause: Make a Strike. On a hit, you and all allies within 30 feet gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level. **Failure** You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level.
requirements.what: The activity itself must exist in the actions list with its cost and traits, and its popup must carry the full printed text intact — including BOTH outcome lines, the on-a-hit line and the Failure entry. 'Make a Strike' is an internal step of the activity and is not itself a lane; the app lists the action and the player performs the Strike. This is the whole of what this feat owes.

requirements.clause: you and all allies within 30 feet gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level
requirements.what: No requirement for the ally half. An effect that lands on a teammate produces nothing on your sheet — no number, no star; the action's own description already tells the player what allies get. The 30-foot radius is a positional fact the app cannot know and the player tells the GM.

requirements.clause: you ... gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level / **Failure** You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level.
requirements.what: No requirement for your own half either, on two independent grounds: HP and damage never move sheet stats (Ruling E), and Q15 names temporary Hit Points specifically as NOT complicated enough to earn an applied mode. The degree-of-success branch likewise gets no mechanical surface — the outcome lines are printed prose in the popup, exactly as Minor Omen was ruled. The 'half your level' amount is text the player reads and applies to their own temporary HP.

requirements.clause: You learn the formulas for two alchemical items each time you level up instead of one
requirements.what: The per-level formula grant made by ANOTHER record must itself become two picks per level instead of one, at every level, and the change must be visible in that grant rather than only on this feat (Principle C). The picks are formulas, so per Q14 they must reach the character's formula book — and taking a feat that involves a formula book must ensure the character has one. Per Q14 point 9 the write is one-time: once chosen, the formulas belong to the book and are never re-derived from this feature.

requirements.clause: these must still be elixirs or tools
requirements.what: A picker offering only alchemical items that are elixirs or tools — Q14 point 7 requires a feat that grants formulas to offer only the options that feat allows, not the whole item list, and Q9 requires the builder to show only legal picks. Unpicked grants show as empty slots in the formula book's popup, and pressing one opens that filtered selection (Q14 point 8). Because the pick recurs at every level-up, the number of outstanding slots must track the character's level.

requirements.clause: The number of versatile vials you can create each day increases by one if you're an expert in Crafting, two if you're a master, or three if you're legendary.
requirements.what: The daily versatile-vial count the player sees and spends must include this increase, and the increase must be derived live from the character's CURRENT Crafting proficiency — +0 while untrained or trained (the text names no benefit below expert), +1 expert, +2 master, +3 legendary — so it re-evaluates on its own when Crafting improves rather than being frozen at the level the feat was taken. The vial pool is granted by another record, so per Principle C and Ruling G the larger number replaces the pool's number rather than sitting beside it as a separate note.

requirements.clause: Your innovation gains an additional initial modification from the list for innovations of its type.
requirements.what: One extra initial-modification pick offered in the builder, filtered two ways: to INITIAL modifications (not advanced ones) and to the list belonging to the innovation's own type — weapon, armour, or construct — which means the picker must read which innovation the character actually has (Q9: only what the player may legally pick). Mild inference, flagged rather than assumed: 'an additional' implies the already-chosen initial modification is excluded from the list.

requirements.clause: Your innovation gains an additional initial modification
requirements.what: Whatever the chosen modification does must land on the innovation itself. The innovation is a record another feature granted, so Principle C applies — the extra modification must be reflected IN the innovation's entry (its strike, damage, traits, or armour stats, whichever that modification changes), and any grant carried by the chosen option must fire the same way it does when the innovation's first modification is picked. A note on this feat naming the modification would not satisfy it; the player must see the changed innovation where they read the innovation.

The activity must exist as a named entry in the actions list, with its action cost and its Requirement line printed in its popup. This is the Minor Omen shape (Principle E) applied to an action rather than a reaction: the entry plus its requirement text is the surface. The requirement is a condition on the character's current loadout (a staff in hand), so the popup must carry it as printed text — nothing here asks for the wielded weapon to be tested.
requirements.clause: "Requirements You are wielding your staff." / "You Leap and then Strike using your staff."

requirements.what: A circumstance damage bonus that is a FORMULA, not a literal: twice the number of the wielded staff's weapon damage dice, so it grows as the staff's striking runes advance and differs per staff. A stored number cannot express it, the same problem Wyrmling Flight's Speed-derived fly Speed raises. It applies only to the Strike made inside this activity, so per Ruling B/J it belongs as a situational marker whose `when` names this activity, legible both in the action's popup and where the player reads that staff's Strike damage.
requirements.clause: "You gain a circumstance bonus to damage for the Strike equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice."

requirements.what: NO requirement. The Leap, the Strike, and the follow-up Shove or Trip are the internal steps of the activity — the sheet lists the action and the player performs the steps. The only thing worth noting is that the Shove/Trip is granted regardless of the Strike's outcome, which is text the action's own printed body already carries; it is not a degree-of-success surface and the Shove/Trip result lands on the enemy.
requirements.clause: "Regardless of whether your Strike hit, you can then attempt to Shove or Trip the target."

requirements.what: Inner Upheaval's own entry must show that its list of available damage types has been widened by this feat, per Principle C (a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing) and Q8 (mark the record the feat modifies). The addition is six paired options that must be legible together, because each one changes two things at once: the damage type AND the element trait the effect gains — air/electricity, earth/bludgeoning, fire/fire, metal/slashing, water/cold, wood/bludgeoning. It is additive: the normally available types stay, so the surface must extend the existing list rather than replace it.
requirements.clause: "When you cast Inner Upheaval, in addition to the damage types normally available, you can deliver the extra damage with elemental magic, adding the element's trait and changing the damage type to the listed one" + the six listed pairs

requirements.what: NO persistent requirement for the pick itself. Which element is used is decided at the moment of casting and lasts only as long as that casting; nothing needs to be recorded or chosen in advance. The requirement is that the options be READABLE at the point of casting (covered above), not that the sheet store a selection. The element trait the effect acquires matters only against the target's resistances, which is enemy-side and out of scope.
requirements.clause: "you can deliver the extra damage with elemental magic" (a per-cast selection)

requirements.what: A communication grant, listed where the player reads what they can talk to: two-way comprehension with bats, rats, and wolves specifically. It is not a language and not a general speak-with-animals, so the entry must name the three creature kinds rather than being folded into a generic 'speak with animals' line — the restriction IS the content of the grant.
requirements.clause: "You can ask questions of, receive answers from ... with bats, rats, and wolves."

requirements.what: A `*` on Diplomacy recording that the skill can be used on bats, rats, and wolves at all. This is a change of legal target, not a bonus — without it, Diplomacy against an animal is not a check the player may attempt. Per Ruling D/J the mark lives on the thing the player looks at when it matters, which is the Diplomacy skill entry.
requirements.clause: "and use the Diplomacy skill with bats, rats, and wolves"

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus with `when` = the target is a bat, rat, or wolf. Per Q2 this stars BOTH the action and the skill: the Make an Impression action entry and every skill that can perform it (Diplomacy). The bonus is narrower than the communication grant above — it is only on Make an Impression, not on every Diplomacy use against those animals — so its `when` must carry both restrictions, and it must sit as a restricted situational entry rather than inside the flat Diplomacy total (Ruling B).
requirements.clause: "You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on such animals."

requirements.what: The activity must exist as an entry in the actions list, carrying its action cost and, in its popup, its full printed text — the Cost line, the auto-failure clause, the manipulate-trait clause, and the wasted-spell clause. Per Principle B a record carries the full text of what it does including the parts nothing can compute; here the popup is the whole surface for everything except the resource cost below.
requirements.clause: "Make a melee Strike. On a hit, you cast the 1-action version of the expended spell to damage the target, in addition to the normal damage from your Strike."

requirements.what: The activity is paid for out of a resource the sheet already tracks elsewhere: one of the character's own Harm or Heal castings (a spell slot, or a divine font use). Two things follow. First, the cost must be stated in the action entry so the player knows which pool to decrement. Second — and this is the part no lane in the vocabulary covers — the lane list only has `limitedUses` for a record's OWN per-day uses; there is no lane for 'this action spends a different record's resource', so an action whose cost is another spell has no route to link to the pool it drains. Flagging that as an unmodelled shape rather than asserting the pool must be auto-decremented.
requirements.clause: "Cost Expend a Harm or Heal spell."

requirements.what: NO requirement. The forced failure (or critical failure on a critical Strike) lands entirely on the target's saving throw. Effects on enemies are DECIDED SCOPE — the player tells the GM. The degree-of-success wording here is not a degree-of-success surface on this character's sheet.
requirements.clause: "The target automatically gets a failure on its save (or a critical failure if your Strike was a critical hit)."

requirements.what: NO requirement beyond the printed text in the action's popup. Suppressing the manipulate trait matters only for whether an enemy's reaction triggers, which is enemy-side; the expended-with-no-effect clause is a play-time outcome the player resolves. Neither moves a number on this sheet.
requirements.clause: "The spell doesn't have the manipulate trait when cast this way." / "The spell is expended with no effect if your Strike fails or hits a creature that isn't damaged by that energy type"

requirements.what: A circumstance-bonus star on three named actions and, per Q2 and Ruling C, on every skill that could perform each of them — Gather Information and Make an Impression (Diplomacy), Demoralize (Intimidation). Two properties make this more than an ordinary star. (1) The VALUE is not printed here: it is whatever Binding Vow's circumstance bonus currently is, so the star must derive its number from that other record rather than hardcode one, or it will be wrong the moment Binding Vow's bonus differs. (2) The `when` — 'directly in service of fulfilling the vow' — is not something any engine can evaluate; per Ruling H it is printed verbatim in the note and left open rather than narrowed into a rule the book did not write.
requirements.clause: "The circumstance bonus from your Binding Vow also applies to attempts to gather-information, make-an-impression, or demoralize you make directly in service of fulfilling the vow."

requirements.what: Binding Vow's own entry must reflect that its bonus now reaches three further actions. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — a player reading Binding Vow to find out where its bonus applies must see the widened scope there, not only in this feat's text.
requirements.clause: "The circumstance bonus from your Binding Vow also applies to ..."

"You make a Strike. Regardless of whether the Strike succeeds, spirits of warriors who died gloriously in battle surge out to attack with you. They appear in a [area] if you make a melee Strike or in a [area] around your target if you made a ranged Strike."
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so Battle Hymn to the Lost must appear as its own entry in the actions list with its action cost, and its full text reachable in the popup — the Strike, the two area shapes (melee vs ranged), the save against your class DC, and the damage-type choice. Per the NOT-lanes rule the app lists the action and the player performs it, so nothing beyond the entry's existence and its legible text is owed for the internal steps. ⚠ The supplied text cannot fully populate that entry: both area templates are unsubstituted ("in a if you make a melee Strike", "in a around your target") and the action cost is absent from the text, so the entry's shape and cost cannot be derived from this text alone.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per hour"
requirements.what: A per-hour use limit: one spendable use displayed beside the action entry, consumed when used, with the frequency wording visible. An hour boundary is not a resource the sheet can derive from rest or daily preparations the way a per-day limit is, so the reset must be expressible by the player rather than computed.

requirements.clause: "Each enemy in the area takes [damage] with a save against your class DC... At 12th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d10."
requirements.what: The damage the action prints must resolve at the character's CURRENT level, not sit as a static line — it steps up by 1d10 at 12th and every 4 levels after, so it is a level formula rather than a fixed number. The class DC is a stat the sheet already carries and needs no new row. The damage landing on enemies gets no further surface (DECIDED SCOPE: effects on enemies are not your sheet's problem). ⚠ The supplied text omits the base damage dice entirely ("takes damage with a save"), so the level formula has no starting value in this evidence.

requirements.clause: "you choose whether the damage is bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing"
requirements.what: Nothing separate. This is a choice made at the moment of use inside the activity, not a build-time choice — an internal step of the activity, which the NOT-lanes list excludes. It must simply be legible in the action's popup, which the grantsAction requirement already covers.

requirements.clause: "Any of your allies in the area who are dying regain Hit Points equal to the damage you rolled. This is a divine, healing, vitality effect."
requirements.what: Nothing. The healing lands on allies (Ruling F — an effect on a teammate produces no star and no modifier), and HP never moves sheet stats even inside a mode (Ruling E). Principle A's "indication on the record it modifies" is already satisfied: the record being modified is this feat's own action, whose text carries the clause. There is no other record to mark. The trait line is labelling, not a lane.

requirements.clause: "You can use High Jump... as a single action instead of 2 actions."
requirements.what: High Jump must appear under BOTH costs — its native 2-action form and the 1-action form this feat enables — with the explanation in the popup. This is Principle H exactly (the owner's Quick Recognition answer: "have Recognize a Spell apear as both free action and raction and on the pop up have explanation"). Both remain available because the 1-action version carries a real drawback, so this is a conditional cost change, not a replacement of the entry.

requirements.clause: "You can use... Long Jump as a single action instead of 2 actions."
requirements.what: Long Jump must likewise appear under both costs, 2-action and 1-action, with the explanation in its popup. The feat names two separate action records and the mark lives on each thing the player is looking at when it matters (Ruling D/G), so satisfying one does not satisfy the other.

requirements.clause: "If you do, you don't perform the initial Stride (nor do you fail if you don't Stride 10 feet)."
requirements.what: The 1-action variants' popup text must differ from the 2-action originals: the initial Stride is not performed, and the normal failure condition for not Striding 10 feet does not apply. Principle H's "explanation in the popup" is what carries this — the two cost entries cannot share identical text, because the difference between them is the whole point of the choice.

requirements.clause: "Increase your maximum Hit Points by an amount equal to your level."
requirements.what: A permanent increase to maximum Hit Points equal to the character's level. The value is a level formula, not a fixed number — it must re-derive at every level-up rather than being written once — and it must be attributable to this feat in the max-HP breakdown.

requirements.clause: "If you rest for 10 minutes, brilliant light from the First World seeps into your form... causing you to regain a number of Hit Points equal to your level; this is cumulative with any Hit Points you regain from Treat Wounds."
requirements.what: A marker on the thing it modifies (Ruling D's shape, whose own worked example is Magic Hands marking Treat Wounds): the 10-minute-rest recovery must be visible where the player looks when it matters — on Treat Wounds, which the clause names explicitly, and on any 10-minute rest activity the sheet surfaces, since the trigger is the rest itself and Ruling H says stay open where the rules are open. The note carries the amount (HP equal to your level, a level formula) and the explicit stacking with Treat Wounds. It moves no stat: HP and damage never move sheet numbers (Ruling E).

requirements.clause: "However, you gain weakness 5 to cold iron."
requirements.what: Weakness 5 to cold iron, appearing in the character's defences/IWR block alongside resistances and immunities, with this feat named as its source. A flat value that does not scale.

requirements.clause: "While you are more susceptible to cold iron than most of the Wingless, you also have an incredible resilience and a deeper connection to the healing energies of the First World."
requirements.what: Nothing. Pure flavour restating the three mechanical clauses that follow it.

requirements.clause: "You can cast Frostbite as a primal innate cantrip."
requirements.what: Frostbite appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the primal tradition, marked as a cantrip and cast at will — a cantrip carries no per-day limit, so no spendable use should be shown beside it, and it auto-heightens to half your level by the general cantrip rule the app applies everywhere (not a separate requirement). The granting source must be named. The tradition specifically must be legible AT this entry: Q12 requires whichever spelling leaves the player least confused, and a primal grant must not be filed under a tradition it does not have.

requirements.clause: "You gain resistance to cold damage equal to half your level"
requirements.what: Cold resistance in the defences/IWR block whose value is half the character's level — a level formula that re-derives at every level-up, not a fixed number written once — with this feat named as the source so the breakdown shows where it came from.

requirements.clause: "and you're protected from severe cold temperatures."
requirements.what: A printed, readable clause on the character. This changes no number and there is no record on the sheet to attach it to — no environment or temperature row exists to mark, and no action performs it — so what is owed is that the protection is legible, capped at about a line with click-through to the full text (Ruling H). If the sheet ever surfaces the environmental-cold save, Ruling D would put the mark there; absent such a record, star nothing (Ruling I) and print the clause.

requirements.clause: "You establish a safe house where you can prepare for your hunt... This sanctum is in a location you have access to and can be part of a larger structure, such as the basement of a temple or hidden room of a library."
requirements.what: A FREE-TEXT field where the player names their sanctum's location. Principle I makes free-text player input a legitimate choice type, and this is the same shape the owner answered directly for Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location — the feat requires the player to designate one specific, discrete place that the rules deliberately leave to them. The 20-foot-cube size is descriptive of the place, not a sheet number.

requirements.clause: "Your sanctum protects objects and people inside it from magical detection and the prying eyes of undead. This has the effects of Veil of Privacy, using your Religion modifier for the counteract DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract rank."
requirements.what: The clause must be printed with its two derived values readable: the counteract DC comes off your Religion modifier and the counteract rank is half your level rounded up (a level formula). Neither earns a new stat row — Ruling D's DC-only clause says a skill DC gets no surface at all, the player remembers it, and the Religion modifier and level are already on the sheet. What is owed is that the borrowed spell is not opaque: the feat's text names Veil of Privacy and grants its effects, so that spell's description must be reachable from here or the player cannot know what the sanctum does.

requirements.clause: "Your sanctum protects objects and people inside it..." (the protection as it lands on other people and on the place itself)
requirements.what: Nothing on your sheet. The protection covers a location and everyone inside it rather than you specifically (Ruling F — an effect on a teammate produces nothing), and whether you are inside the 20-foot cube is positional, which the app can never know (Ruling M's reasoning for auras). The feat's own printed text is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: "Setting up or moving your sanctum takes a week of downtime."
requirements.what: No sheet surface. Establishing or relocating the sanctum is something the player re-chooses outside play (Principle K), and the owner ruled exactly this shape on Guerrilla Dedication — "if the user wants to change they wil do it in the builder" — for a clause with the identical 1-week-of-downtime relocation cost.

requirements.clause: "Additionally, undead attempting to locate the entrance to your sanctum via mundane Perception must succeed against either your Religion DC or the normal DC to find the sanctum, whichever is higher."
requirements.what: Nothing. This is a check made BY enemies against a skill DC of yours: effects on enemies are not lanes, and Ruling D states plainly that a skill DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers their Religion DC. The "whichever is higher" comparison is a GM adjudication against a DC the app does not know.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are under the effects of a mutagen. --- You redirect a mutagen within your body to spit a stream of stomach acid at a foe.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear in the actions list as its own entry, with the Requirements line ("You are under the effects of a mutagen") and the full text in its popup. That requirement is a state of the character, but the text states it as a usage gate rather than a computed value, so printing it in the popup is the whole obligation — the Minor Omen shape, where the trigger and requirement live in the popup and nothing else moves.

requirements.clause: A creature within 30 feet takes 1d6 acid damage for every 2 levels you have (), with a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: The damage is a formula off the character's own level (1d6 acid per 2 levels) and the save is against the character's own class DC, so the action entry has to express what THIS character rolls and which DC applies, not a bare printed string. Note the supplied text carries an EMPTY parenthesis "()" exactly where the scaling value and the save type belonged — the printed prose alone cannot tell the player what to roll or what kind of save the target attempts, so something must supply it.

requirements.clause: On a failure, the creature is also Sickened 1 (or Sickened 2 on a critical failure).
requirements.what: Nothing. The acid damage and the Sickened condition both land on the target. Enemy conditions and enemy-side damage are decided scope — the action's own text tells the player what the foe suffers and no number moves on the character's sheet.

requirements.clause: The mutagen's duration immediately ends.
requirements.what: This is the one clause that touches the character's own sheet. A mutagen is an ongoing effect that changes the drinker's numbers, i.e. a state the player has switched on; using this action switches it off. The player must be able to see the mutagen state running and to end it here, and the action's popup must say that using it costs them the mutagen.

requirements.clause: You gain access to repeating hand crossbows and repeater bandoliers.
requirements.what: Nothing. Q5 settles this: item rarity does not gate the shop and an "access to uncommon X" clause needs no requirement at all. Q9's "only what the player may legally pick" governs builder choices, not the item list.

requirements.clause: If you have Running Reload or a similar feat that allows you to reload and perform another action or activity as a single action, you can use that action more efficiently with a repeating weapon.
requirements.what: A marker on the action this feat changes — Running Reload, and on any other reload-plus-action feat the character holds, because "or a similar feat" is deliberately open and Ruling H says stay open rather than narrowing it to the one named feat. Principle C: the change must be reflected in the thing it modifies, not merely stated in this feat's own text. The requirement is conditional — a character holding no such feat gets no surface from this clause.

requirements.clause: You can use the action as a 3-action activity to reload a magazine into a repeating weapon after you perform its other granted action, or as a 2-action activity if you use a magazine from a repeater bandolier.
requirements.what: Principle H — an action whose cost changes conditionally must appear under both (here, all) of its costs, with the explanation in the popup. So the modified reload action needs to be listed at its native cost and additionally as a 3-action activity (reload a magazine into a repeating weapon after its other granted action) and as a 2-action activity (magazine drawn from a repeater bandolier), each variant's condition readable in the popup. This is the Quick Recognition shape: one action, several cost entries, explanation in the popup.

requirements.clause: Make a ranged weapon Strike against a creature you previously attacked this turn.
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list, with its full text in the popup, including the "a creature you previously attacked this turn" condition — a fact about the current turn nothing can know, so it is printed and the player applies it. The Strike itself is an internal step of the activity, not a separate requirement: only the action's existence is owed.

requirements.clause: You ignore the target's concealed condition and all cover.
requirements.what: Nothing. Both halves are target-side. Concealed is a condition on the enemy, and cover is explicitly named in decided scope as a target-side number that gets no surface ("this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm"). The clause is printed in the action's popup and goes no further — so the action entry above is the whole surface of this feat.

requirements.clause: Add Brilliant, Corrosive, Flaming, Frost, Holy, Shock, Thundering, and Unholy to the list of property runes you can add to your weapon during your daily preparations.
requirements.what: This feat grants nothing of its own — it widens the option list of a choice ANOTHER record already granted. Principle C: the eight named runes must show up inside that record's picker, not merely be listed in this feat's text. Q9 also bounds it — the picker offers exactly the options the player may legally pick, so the list must become the base grant plus these eight and nothing more.

requirements.clause: …the list of property runes you can add to your weapon during your daily preparations.
requirements.what: The pick is re-made at daily preparations, not fixed at build time, so the widened list has to be reachable where that daily choice is actually made (daily prep / rest), and the rune chosen today must be the one riding on the weapon today.

requirements.clause: Your weapons have greater power available to them.
requirements.what: Nothing — flavour.

requirements.clause: Source Divine Mysteries pg. 294 Archetype Rivethun Emissary Prerequisites Consult the Spirits (Rivethun Emissary)
requirements.what: Nothing. Source, archetype, and prerequisite lines are not mechanical clauses.

requirements.clause: Whenever you Consult the Spirits, you gain a +1 status bonus to Will saving throws until the next time you make your daily preparations.
requirements.what: A state that switches on when the character Consults the Spirits and runs until the next daily preparations — far longer than a round and not always on, so per Q1/Q11 it is a mode rather than a passive bonus, and it carries a real number: +1 status bonus to Will saves while active. The player must be able to see that it is running.

requirements.clause: This bonus increases to +2 against emotion and fear effects.
requirements.what: Inside that mode, a restricted upgrade: +2 status to Will against emotion and fear effects, with the restriction carried in its own condition text (Ruling B — a rules-restricted flat bonus is situational, not part of the flat total). Ruling G: it is an upgrade, so against emotion and fear it replaces the +1 entry rather than sitting beside it and reading as +3.

requirements.clause: In addition, until the next time you make your daily preparations, you can do each of the following once.
requirements.what: Three separate, independently spendable uses — not one shared use. Each is consumed on its own and all three are restored at daily preparations (the same clock as the mode above), so each needs its own trackable use rather than a single per-day counter.

requirements.clause: Roll a Will save twice and use the better result.
requirements.what: A marker on the Will save carrying this once-per-day fortune reroll, so the player sees it where they look up the Will number — the same place the mode's +1/+2 is already showing.

requirements.clause: Roll an attack roll twice and use the better result.
requirements.what: A marker on attack rolls — every Strike the character can make — carrying the once-per-day fortune reroll. Q2's "star both" logic applies at the level the clause is written: it names attack rolls generally, so it goes on all of them, not on one chosen weapon.

requirements.clause: …this skill check must be made with the skill that the spirits blessed during Consult the Spirits.
requirements.what: Which skill is blessed is decided each time Consult the Spirits happens, on the same until-daily-preparations clock, so there must be somewhere to record that pick and re-pick it each day. Without the recorded pick, the next requirement has no target.

requirements.clause: Roll a skill check twice and use the better result; this skill check must be made with the skill that the spirits blessed during Consult the Spirits.
requirements.what: A marker on the recorded blessed skill carrying the once-per-day fortune reroll. It must follow the pick — landing on whichever skill was blessed this day, not on a fixed skill and not on every skill.

requirements.clause: Whenever you Consult the Spirits…
requirements.what: A marker on the Consult the Spirits action itself (granted by the prerequisite feat) showing that this feat rides on it — Principle C plus Q8: mark the action the feat modifies, so the player sees at the moment of using it that doing so starts the Will-save mode, sets the blessed skill, and refreshes the three rerolls.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You are the target of a physical ranged Strike. **Requirements** You're aware of the attack, not off-guard against it, and either have a hand free or are wielding a melee weapon.
requirements.what: The feat is a reaction and must appear in the reactions list, with its trigger (you are the target of a physical ranged Strike) and all three requirement conditions (aware of the attack; not off-guard against it; a hand free or wielding a melee weapon) written out in its popup. Principle E / exemplar #7 (Minor Omen): for a triggered reaction this is usually the whole surface. None of the three requirements is computable — 'aware of the attack' and 'not off-guard against it' are per-attack facts only the GM and player know — so they are printed text, not a gate.

requirements.clause: You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
requirements.what: A `*` on the character's own AC carrying '+4 circumstance vs. the triggering ranged Strike when you use Cut from the Air'. This is the player's own defence, not an ally-facing effect, so it does reach the sheet — but it is a bonus restricted to one specific attack, so per Ruling B it belongs in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, sitting outside the AC total, and per Q2 the mark goes on both the AC stat and the reaction entry. The sheet must therefore be able to express a circumstance bonus to AC whose `when` is 'against the attack that triggered this reaction'.

requirements.clause: If the attack misses, you knocked or cut it out of the air.
requirements.what: Nothing. This is narrative colour describing the outcome of a miss the app already resolves through the AC comparison; it grants no benefit, consumes nothing, and destroys no ammunition in the printed text.

requirements.clause: Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency in Falchions, Ranseurs, Scimitars, Tridents…
requirements.what: Falchion, Ranseur, Scimitar and Trident must each carry a weapon proficiency rank that is DERIVED from another record — whatever rank the character's class weapon-expertise feature grants — rather than a rank written into this feat. The sheet must be able to express 'the rank of the class feature that granted expert-or-better weapon proficiency', so that these four weapons appear at the correct rank in the weapon proficiency list and in every Strike built from them.

requirements.clause: Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons…
requirements.what: The word 'whenever' makes this a standing rule, not a one-time write: when the class feature later improves (weapon mastery, weapon legend), the four named weapons must rise with it. So the rank must be recomputed at every level rather than stamped once at the level the feat was taken, and the sheet must show the raised rank without the player retaking anything.

requirements.clause: …and all geniekin weapons in which you are trained.
requirements.what: A second, gated set: every weapon that counts as a geniekin weapon AND in which the character is already trained also rises to that rank. Expressing this needs two things the four named weapons did not — the sheet must know which weapons belong to the 'geniekin weapons' group (a trait/group membership test over the whole weapon list, not an enumerated list on this feat), and it must apply the upgrade conditionally on the character's existing trained-or-better rank in each such weapon.

requirements.clause: you also gain that proficiency in Falchions, Ranseurs, Scimitars, Tridents, and all geniekin weapons in which you are trained.
requirements.what: The remap must never lower a rank the character already has by another route — Q10 rules that a proficiency remap applies only when it makes the player better, explicitly rejecting RAW's strict replacement. So the requirement is 'raise to the class feature's rank if higher, otherwise leave alone', and the displayed rank must be the better of the two.

requirements.clause: You recharge your Kobold Breath whenever you score a critical hit with a Strike.
requirements.what: Kobold Breath is a limited-use action granted by another record, and this feat adds a second, non-time-based way to get its use back. The sheet must be able to restore a spent use of a specific granted action on demand — outside daily preparations, refocus, or any rest — because the recharge trigger (scoring a critical hit) is an in-combat event the app cannot observe. In practice that means the Kobold Breath use tracker must be player-resettable, not read-only between rests.

requirements.clause: You recharge your Kobold Breath whenever you score a critical hit with a Strike.
requirements.what: An indication on the Kobold Breath entry itself that this feat has changed it, carrying the recharge condition verbatim. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — the player looks at Kobold Breath, not at this feat, at the moment the recharge matters.

requirements.clause: In addition, if you score a critical hit with a Strike and then use your Kobold Breath on the same turn, you can reroll any 1s on the damage dice. You must use the new result, even if it's a 1.
requirements.what: A note on the Kobold Breath entry stating the conditional damage-die reroll and that the new result stands. It contributes no number: the condition is a same-turn sequence of events the app does not track (turns/rounds are not tracked, Q1), and damage-die handling never moves a sheet stat. The requirement is that the player can read the clause where they use the breath weapon.

requirements.clause: You possess the confidence of a dragon, and your success emboldens you to draw on power reserves you didn't know you had.
requirements.what: Nothing. Pure flavour.

requirements.clause: You become trained in your choice of Guild Lore, Legal Lore, Mercantile Lore, or Underworld Lore.
requirements.what: A bounded picker offering exactly those four Lores and nothing else (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick), and the chosen Lore then appearing on the sheet as a trained skill with its own modifier row, indistinguishable in use from any other trained Lore. The text supplies no redundancy fallback for a character who already has the chosen Lore, so none should be invented.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks to Gather Information…
requirements.what: A `*` carrying '+1 circumstance' on Diplomacy AND on the Gather Information action — Q2 rules 'both', and Ruling C says a bonus named after an action stars every skill that could perform it. The bonus is restricted to one use of the skill, so it sits in `situational` with 'to Gather Information' as its `when` and stays out of the flat Diplomacy total (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: …and to checks made to investigate crimes.
requirements.what: A second, separately-worded `*` carrying '+1 circumstance to checks made to investigate crimes'. The text names a trigger but names no skill, so Ruling H governs: stay open — star every skill that could plausibly be used to investigate a crime and print the trigger verbatim in the note, rather than the app picking one skill and putting its own ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's. It must be a distinct entry from the Gather Information star, not merged with it: the two have different `when` text, and the stacking rule shows both when the `when` differs.

requirements.clause: You may spend a Mythic Point when you attempt an Escape or Force Open check to do so at mythic proficiency.
requirements.what: A `*` on every skill that could perform the two named actions and on the actions themselves (Ruling C + Q2): Force Open is Athletics; Escape can be attempted with Athletics, with Acrobatics, or with an unarmed attack modifier, so all of those get the mark. The note carries the cost (1 Mythic Point) and the effect (the check is made at mythic proficiency).

requirements.clause: …to do so at mythic proficiency.
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to express a proficiency rank ABOVE legendary — 'mythic' — and to show it as a conditional alternate value for those checks rather than as the character's standing rank. The star should carry the resulting number, not only the prose, since the whole point of a star is that the player sees what happens to the number they are looking up (the Mastermind's Eye principle).

requirements.clause: You may spend a Mythic Point when you attempt an Escape or Force Open check…
requirements.what: A spendable Mythic Point resource the player can decrement and restore. The feat does not grant the pool, but the clause is inert without one — the sheet must be able to express Mythic Points as a countable, spendable resource for this option to be usable at all.

requirements.clause: Additionally, you gain the Ultimatum of Liberation action…
requirements.what: Ultimatum of Liberation appears in the actions list with its own action cost, traits and full details reachable from the entry, sourced to this dedication.

requirements.clause: …but you also gain the anathema, "You must not use Ultimatum of Liberation on a creature you don't believe to be oppressing others or who has conceded their power".
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to record an anathema that comes from a FEAT rather than from a deity, and show it wherever the character's anathema are listed — this is a real constraint on the character that they must be able to find without reopening the feat. Additionally, per Principle C, the Ultimatum of Liberation entry granted just above should carry an indication that its use is anathema-constrained, since that is the record the player is looking at when it matters.

requirements.clause: If you break this anathema, you lose access to abilities granted by this archetype until you atone or make amends.
requirements.what: Nothing computed. Whether the anathema was broken is a GM adjudication, and 'atone or make amends' is a narrative event — the app cannot detect either. The clause is carried as part of the anathema text above; no toggle, mode, or suppression of the archetype's grants is owed.

requirements.clause: Your Calling was sparked by your outrage at tyrants… Your GM has final say about what constitutes oppression… When a tax collector levies higher charges against the less fortunate because it's the law, they are participating in a system of oppression.
requirements.what: Nothing. The opening sentence is flavour and the closing block is an explicit GM-adjudication guide with worked examples; both belong in the feat's description text and generate no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** An ally within your reach leaves a square during a move action they're using and ends their movement adjacent to an enemy. --- ... You Stride up to half your speed.
requirements.what: A reaction entry in the reactions list. Its trigger (an ally within your reach leaves a square during a move action and ends that movement adjacent to an enemy) must be readable in the popup, together with the full effect text. This is the whole surface — same shape as Minor Omen (principle E): the sheet must be able to say 'you have this reaction, here is when it fires'.

requirements.clause: You Stride up to half your speed.
requirements.what: Nothing. The internal steps of an activity are performed by the player, not modelled — only the action's existence is a lane. Half your Speed is not a second movement type and needs no speed row; the number is your own Speed, which the sheet already carries.

requirements.clause: This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the enemy your ally moved adjacent to.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the popup text. This suppresses an ENEMY's reaction, which is enemy-facing and out of decided scope; the clause is carried as prose inside the reaction's own popup and needs no separate surface.

requirements.clause: When you cast Fireball, you can modify its effects, decreasing the base damage to 5d6 and causing it to deal 2 persistent fire damage to creatures that fail their save, doubled as normal on a critical failure.
requirements.what: A marker on the Fireball spell entry — the record this feat modifies — showing that this feat offers an alternative profile, with the alternative values readable there: base damage 5d6 instead of the printed value, plus 2 persistent fire on a failed save. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing, and Ruling D/G puts the mark on the thing the player is looking at when it matters — the spell, at the moment of casting. It is a per-cast option, not a persistent state, so what the sheet must express is 'this spell has a second, feat-supplied version', not a toggle that changes a stat.

requirements.clause: If you do, replace its heightened entry with the following. --- **Heightened (+1)** The damage is increased by 1d6 and the persistent fire damage is increased by 2.
requirements.what: The substitute heightened entry must REPLACE Fireball's printed Heightened (+1) line when the modified version is read, not sit beside it (Ruling G: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades). So wherever heightened values are shown for this spell, the sheet must be able to express two mutually exclusive scaling tracks — the printed one, and this feat's +1d6 / +2 persistent — and make plain which one is in play. A marker that only says 'this feat exists' is not enough here, because the player reads a scaled number off that line.

requirements.clause: ...deal 2 persistent fire damage to creatures that fail their save, doubled as normal on a critical failure.
requirements.what: Nothing on your own sheet. The persistent damage and the save-degree doubling land on enemies, and 'doubled as normal on a critical failure' restates a general rule. Both are carried as prose in the alternative profile above.

requirements.clause: You can cast Flicker as a 4th-rank occult innate spell once per day.
requirements.what: Flicker appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, with its own tradition — occult — legible at the entry itself, and readable at 4th rank. The tradition must belong to this entry and must not be inherited from or averaged with other innate grants the character holds; the sheet must not state something false about the spell (Q12). The spell's details must be reachable from the entry and the granting feat named.

requirements.clause: ...once per day.
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when the spell is cast and restored at daily preparations. The entry must not read as unlimited.

requirements.clause: When you Sustain the spell, increase the distance you teleport to 15 feet.
requirements.what: The increased teleport distance must be reflected on the Flicker entry this feat grants — principle C, a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. Because it replaces a printed distance rather than adding to it, the 15 feet must supersede the spell's own Sustain distance where the player reads it (Ruling G), and it must be scoped to this grant rather than to every copy of Flicker the character might hold.

requirements.clause: You can use Nature to Recall Knowledge to identify any creature.
requirements.what: Nature usable in place of whatever skill would normally identify a given creature type, for the Recall Knowledge action, with no creature-type restriction. The sheet must be able to express 'this skill stands in for the others, for this action only' — the substitution is the mechanical fact, not a bonus.

requirements.clause: You can use Nature to Recall Knowledge to identify any creature.
requirements.what: A `*` on BOTH Nature and the Recall Knowledge action (Q2: both — star the skill and the action), carrying the clause, so the player sees it where they look up the number. It is a restriction-lifting star, not a modifier, so it contributes no value to the Nature total (Ruling B — a restricted/qualified effect sits outside the stat total).

requirements.clause: In addition, you gain the benefits of Monster Hunter ... on a success as well as a critical success.
requirements.what: A reflection on the Monster Hunter record itself: its benefit now triggers on a success as well as a critical success. Principle C — the change belongs in the record it modifies, so the player reading Monster Hunter sees the widened degree band rather than having to remember a second feat. Monster Hunter's own benefit is unchanged in value; only the condition under which it fires widens.

requirements.clause: (and Monster Warden, if you have it)
requirements.what: The same widening reflected on Monster Warden, but ONLY when the character actually holds Monster Warden — a conditional modification whose presence depends on another owned record. If Monster Warden is not held, nothing about it should appear.

requirements.clause: Step and attempt a single one-action finisher.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so it must appear in the actions list with its full text in the popup. Only the action's existence is the lane; 'Step' and 'attempt a finisher' are internal steps the player performs. The text as given states no action cost, so none should be asserted — whatever cost the record carries is what must be shown, under a single cost (this is not the Quick Recognition dual-cost shape).

requirements.clause: This Strike gains the bravado trait, possibly replenishing your Panache;
requirements.what: Nothing separate. The trait is conferred on a Strike made inside this activity, not a persistent change to any weapon in inventory, so it is carried as prose in the action's own popup. Regaining panache via bravado is the general rule for that trait, restated here, not a new promise.

requirements.clause: if you regain panache, you can immediately attempt another finisher as part of this action, ignoring the restriction of using actions with the attack trait after a finisher.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the popup text. This is an exception to a general rule that applies only inside this activity and only in the moment, so its entire surface is the action's own description. It creates no extra action, no extra reaction, and no per-day resource — the text states no frequency or limit.

requirements.clause: Increase your maximum and encumbered Bulk limits by 4.
requirements.what: Two numbers the sheet already shows must move: the encumbered Bulk limit and the maximum Bulk limit, each +4, so the encumbrance readout trips at the raised thresholds rather than the defaults. It is unconditional and cannot be shut off, so by Q11 it is a passive bonus, not a mode; and because the player reads it as a number, a note beside the feat saying "+4 Bulk limits" would not discharge it — the limits themselves have to change. ⚠ There is no lane for this in the manual: the only Bulk lane listed, `bulkIgnore`, is item-only and covers an item's own Bulk contribution, not the carrier's capacity. This is the "no lane at all, but the text is clearly mechanical" shape.

requirements.clause: You can rest normally while wearing medium armor.
requirements.what: An exemption from the sleeping-in-armour penalty. It moves no stat, so per Ruling D the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters — the Rest / daily-preparations control, and secondarily the worn medium armour — printed as a one-line note sourced to this feat. Where a rest flow imposes the armour penalty, this feat suppresses it for medium armour; that is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: When you use Merciful Elixir, your elixir can instead attempt to counteract the blinded, deafened, sickened, or slowed condition.
requirements.what: The feat changes what ANOTHER record already granted. Principle C plus Q8: the widened condition list has to be reflected in the Merciful Elixir entry itself — that action's own text/popup must read blinded, deafened, sickened, slowed, with this feat named as the source — because that is the record the player is looking at when they spend the action. Nothing lands on this sheet's stats.

requirements.clause: ...can instead attempt to counteract...
requirements.what: No further requirement. Counteracting is a general rule the app applies everywhere; the counteract rank/DC and the frequency belong to Merciful Elixir's own record, not to this feat. This feat grants no action of its own (it modifies one), grants no per-day resource, and the choice of which of the four conditions to target is an internal step the player makes at use time — not a builder choice.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are adjacent to an enemy. --- You sweep your foe into your dance.
requirements.what: The feat IS an activity, so it must appear in the actions list under its printed action cost, with "Requirements: You are adjacent to an enemy" shown in its popup. This is the Minor Omen (#7) shape: the entry plus its requirement in the popup is often the entire requirement.

requirements.clause: Attempt a Performance check against an adjacent enemy's Will DC.
requirements.what: Nothing owed. The check is the activity's internal step, and no bonus is named — Ruling C stars every skill that could perform an action only when a BONUS is attached, and there is none here, so Performance gets no `*`. The enemy's Will DC is a target-side number the app does not model (Ruling F). The clause needs only to be legible inside the action's popup text.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** You both move up to 10 feet in the same direction... **Success** As critical success, but you both move only 5 feet. **Failure** ...You can move 5 feet if you choose, but this movement triggers reactions normally.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond display. Forced movement of the foe lands on the enemy (Ruling F, Q4: the entry is the whole surface), and your own 5–10 foot move is an internal step the player performs; positions and reaction-triggering are not modelled. The requirement is that all four degrees of success are readable IN FULL in the action's popup, not truncated to a summary.

requirements.clause: **Critical Failure** You stumble, falling prone in your space.
requirements.what: No implementation owed. This is Q15's crit-trigger shape (Q15 names critical success; a critical-failure rider is the same shape): a degree-triggered effect needs nothing unless it is COMPLICATED, and prone is a single standard condition the player applies themselves. The outcome text in the popup is the surface.

requirements.clause: An artificial metal object forms in the hands of you or a willing ally within 30 feet... The item is entirely made from metal, making some items impossible or impractical to use (if it's unclear, the GM decides). You can make items with simple moving parts or magnetism...
requirements.what: The feat is an activity and must appear in the actions list with its printed cost and its full text — the metal-only constraint, the worked examples (compass, poor lock, merchant's scale), the GM's call where unclear, and the destruction clause. The metal-impracticality judgement is explicitly the GM's and is not a lane. ⚠ The printed text opens with "Flash Forge Source Rage of Elements pg. 30" — a stray title/source header sitting inside the prose. Whatever renders the action must not print that line as part of the action's text.

requirements.clause: You can choose a level 0, common, handheld weapon or piece of adventuring gear of 1 Bulk or less.
requirements.what: A pick from a filtered set, made when the impulse is USED, not when the character is built — so no builder surface is owed. Whatever offers the pick must offer only legal options (Q9's principle): level 0, common, handheld weapon or adventuring gear, 1 Bulk or less. ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not stated by the owner: the formed object is a weapon or usable gear held for 10 minutes, so the pick has to land somewhere the player can actually wield and use it, not exist only as prose in the popup — the Q14 principle that a granted pick must reach a real place.

requirements.clause: The item lasts for 10 minutes, but each time it's used, the user must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or the item is destroyed after the action is completed.
requirements.what: A duration longer than a round, so by Q1 it earns a mode. A level 0 mundane object supplies no bonus, so it is display-only (Ruling E case 3): the mode names the object that was formed, states the 10-minute duration, and carries the DC 5 flat check and the destruction outcome as text (Principle B — the mode carries the full text including the parts the app cannot compute; the flat check is the player's to roll and rounds/minutes are not tracked).

requirements.clause: ...in the hands of you or a willing ally within 30 feet.
requirements.what: Nothing when the target is an ally — Ruling F: an effect that lands on a teammate produces no surface on your sheet, and the action's own description already tells the player what the ally receives. The 30-foot range is positional and not modelled. (The self-target half is covered by the choice and mode requirements above.)

requirements.clause: You can choose to activate Nanite Surge when you attempt an attack roll, instead of when you attempt a skill check.
requirements.what: The feat changes the trigger of another record's granted thing. Principle C plus Q8: Nanite Surge's own entry must reflect it — its trigger line has to read that an attack roll qualifies as well as a skill check, sourced to this feat — because that entry is what the player reads when deciding to spend it. Note the clause widens the trigger for that activation; it removes nothing, so the existing skill-check trigger must remain visible too.

requirements.clause: If you do, you gain a +1 status bonus to the triggering attack roll.
requirements.what: A bonus to one specific roll is situational, never a flat attack bonus. It is named against attack rolls generally, so — by Q2's shape (a bonus to saves generally stars all three saves) and Ruling C (star everything that could perform the named thing) — a `*` goes on every attack roll surfaced on the sheet, i.e. each Strike's attack entry, carrying "+1 status bonus when you activate Nanite Surge on this attack roll" with the feat as its source. It sits outside the stat total by Ruling B, since the rules restrict it to the triggering roll.

requirements.clause: You can choose to activate Nanite Surge... (frequency)
requirements.what: No per-day resource is owed by this feat. Whatever frequency Nanite Surge carries stays on Nanite Surge's own record; this feat only adds a trigger to an existing activation and creates no second pool of uses. Nor is a new action owed — this feat grants nothing new to the actions list.

The feat is a triggered ability and must exist as its own entry among the character's actions/reactions. Its text gives a trigger but no cost, so whatever cost the entry carries, its popup must show "Trigger: You Rage" and the full effect text. Per Q4 and the Minor Omen precedent (#7), the entry itself is the whole surface for the enemy-facing part.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You Rage.

requirements.what: A marker on the Rage action showing this feat fires off it. Ruling D / Q8 shape — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and the player looks at Rage, not at the feat list, at the moment this resolves. (This is the analogue of Magic Hands marking Treat Wounds; I assert it because the trigger is another action the character already has on the sheet.)
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You Rage.

requirements.what: Nothing. Damage that lands on enemies is out of scope ("Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet" is a NOT-lane, and Ruling E says HP and damage never move sheet stats). The class DC is USED here, not modified, so Ruling D's DC-only case is not triggered either — no star beside the class DC is owed. The number "equal to your level" is read off a stat the player already has.
requirements.clause: Each enemy within 20 feet takes damage equal to your level ( save against your class DC)

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text in the entry's popup. The damage type is inherited from the instinct's Rage damage, which the player already reads on Rage, and it is applied to enemies.
requirements.clause: of the same type as your additional damage during that Rage.

requirements.what: Trained rank in Crafting. The text carries no "if you are already trained" clause, so no redundancy fallback is owed here.
requirements.clause: You become trained in Crafting

requirements.what: An advanced-alchemy daily preparation the character can perform: a per-day budget of 4 + half your level (rounded up) consumables, recomputed as level changes, chosen at daily preparations and reset on rest. The picker must be filtered to bombs and alchemical ammunition only — no other alchemical items.
requirements.clause: gain the advanced alchemy benefits. You can use the advanced alchemy benefits to create a number of daily consumables equal to 4 + half your level (rounded up); these consumables must be bombs or alchemical ammunition.

requirements.what: A quantity multiplier inside that same daily preparation: one budget point spent on alchemical ammunition (including black powder in doses or rounds) must yield 4 items, not 1. So the prepared QUANTITY has to be able to differ from the number of budget points spent, and the resulting stack must show its real count.
requirements.clause: When crafting alchemical ammunition, including black powder in doses or rounds, using advanced alchemy, you create the ammunition in batches of 4 (meaning that if you were 4th level and used all of your advanced alchemy consumables to create alchemical ammunition, you could create a maximum of 24 rounds).

requirements.what: An exclusion on that picker: horns and kegs of black powder must not be offerable through advanced alchemy even though they are black-powder items. If the exclusion cannot be enforced in the picker, it must at least be printed on the daily-preparation entry.
requirements.clause: You cannot use advanced alchemy to Craft horns or kegs of black powder.

requirements.what: The character must end up owning a formula book — per Q14 point 6, taking a feat that grants one ensures they have one, adding it if they have none — and the black powder formula must be written INTO that book as a reference, never as an inventory copy (Q14 points 2 and 9: a one-time write, not a live derivation). Note: the lane manual has no formula-book lane; the book is specified only by Q14, which also requires the popup to support search and a 100-formula capacity.
requirements.clause: You gain a formula book that includes the formula for black powder

requirements.what: A builder picker of four separate picks, offering ONLY 1st-level common or uncommon alchemical ammunition and bombs (Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick; Q14 point 7: only the options this feat allows, not the whole item list). The chosen formulas are written into the book once and thereafter belong to it (Q14 point 9); unpicked picks must show as empty slots in the book's inventory popup, and pressing one opens this feat's option list (Q14 point 8).
requirements.clause: and four 1st-level types of common or uncommon alchemical ammunition or bombs of your choice.
