requirements.what: The persistent bleed damage entry must show its recovery flat-check DC as 10, REPLACING the printed 15 rather than sitting beside it (Ruling G: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades), with a `*` naming this feat. Ruling D's shape — the mark lives on the condition, exactly as The Survivor marks the Dying condition. It must apply only to bleed, not to other persistent damage types.
requirements.clause: Reduce the DC of flat checks to stop persistent bleed damage you have from 15 to 10

requirements.what: A new single action with the concentrate trait in the character's action list, its popup carrying the effect (an early flat check against your persistent bleed without binding the wounds).
requirements.clause: and you can use a single action that has the concentrate trait to gain an early flat check without physically binding the wounds

requirements.what: A marker on the drained condition carrying this clause. The rate of natural recovery from drained is not a number the sheet totals — it resolves over days of rest — so the requirement is the printed clause visible where the player reads drained, starred to the feat.
requirements.clause: You recover naturally from the drained condition twice as quickly as normal.

requirements.what: Unfettered Pack appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the DIVINE tradition, at the spell's own base rank (the text names no other rank), with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. The tradition must be legible on the entry itself — a per-entry label, or a pooled section that does not assert a tradition it does not have — since a divine grant filed under another tradition would state something false about the spell (Q12: whichever spelling leaves the player least confused).
requirements.clause: Once per day, you can cast Unfettered Pack as a divine innate spell.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: Once per day

requirements.what: Nothing. This describes the fiction of how the casting looks, not a mechanical effect — it changes no cost, trait, target, or tradition.
requirements.clause: When you do so, you cast the spell by performing a divinely inspired prank.

requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour restating what the granted spell does for allies; ally-facing effects carry no number on your sheet (Ruling F), and the spell's own description already tells the player what allies get. The one indication Principle A would require is already satisfied by the innate-spell entry above, which IS the record this feat modifies.
requirements.clause: You can uplift all around you with your pranks, causing you and your allies to receive divine guidance in all your movements to effortlessly avoid environmental hindrances.

requirements.what: The activity itself must exist as an entry in the character's action list with its full text in the popup. The internal step "Make a ranged weapon Strike" is not itself a lane — the app lists the action, the player performs the Strike; only the action's EXISTENCE is owed.
requirements.clause: Make a ranged weapon Strike.

requirements.what: A `*` on every ranged weapon Strike the character can make, carrying "+2 circumstance to the attack roll when made as part of Sniper's Aim" with the value inline. Ruling C / Principle D: a bonus named after an action stars every thing that could perform it, so this cannot live on one weapon or on a general attack stat — it must reach each ranged strike entry where the player reads the number.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this Strike's attack roll

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text in the action's popup. Concealment is a target-side condition and its flat check is not a number on your sheet — decided scope: target-side numbers the app does not model get no surface.
requirements.clause: and ignore the target's concealment

requirements.what: A `*` on Strikes made with a kickback firearm stating that the circumstance penalty for lacking the required Strength modifier, and for firing without a stabilizer, does not apply to this Strike. This is a WAIVER of a penalty the sheet itself applies to that weapon's strike, so the requirement is that the strike's modifier breakdown can express a penalty being suppressed under a named condition — not merely a line of prose in the feat. It is conditional twice over: only on kickback firearms, and only for this action's Strike.
requirements.clause: If you're using a kickback firearm, you don't take the normal circumstance penalty on this Strike for not having the required Strength modifier or firing without using a stabilizer.

requirements.what: Critical specialization must become available on strikes made with a bo staff, longbow, composite longbow, scythe, or staff — and only those. The grant is weapon-scoped, not a blanket crit-spec unlock, so the surface has to be keyed to a named weapon list and light up per-weapon: a character wielding a scythe sees it, the same character wielding a greatsword does not. Per Ruling D/G the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters — the strike entry for the qualifying weapon — and the effect it shows must be the critical specialization effect of that weapon's own group, with the text reachable from there so the player can read what happens on a crit rather than being told only that something does.
requirements.clause: Whenever you critically hit using a bo staff, longbow, composite longbow, scythe, or staff, you apply the weapon's critical specialization effect.

requirements.what: No requirement. 'Prerequisites Vanth's Weapon Familiarity' is a prerequisite line and the opening sentence is flavour; neither is a lane. The source line is bibliographic.
requirements.clause: Source Ancestry Guide pg. 30 Prerequisites Vanth's Weapon Familiarity You've trained in the finer points of dealing death.

requirements.what: The feat must appear as a triggered action in the character's action list, with its trigger — 'You're airborne at the end of your turn' — shown in its popup alongside the effect text. Per Principle E this is often the entire requirement, and it is here: the player needs to find the thing and know when it fires.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** You're airborne at the end of your turn.

requirements.what: No requirement beyond the effect text living in the action's popup. 'You don't fall' is a positional outcome — whether the character is airborne, and what happens to them if they stop being so, is not a sheet number. It changes no stat, grants no speed, and sets no condition on the character sheet. The clause is read, not computed.
requirements.clause: You remain airborne through sheer effort. You don't fall, even if you didn't use Fly or a similar action this turn.

requirements.what: Two languages chosen by the player must be added to the character's known languages and appear in the languages list on the sheet, attributed to this feat. This is two independent picks, not one pick of a pair.
requirements.clause: You learn two new languages, chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others you have access to.

requirements.what: Two picker slots in the builder whose option list spans BOTH common and uncommon languages — uncommon is explicitly permitted here, so a picker filtered to common only is wrong. Per Q9 the builder offers what the player may legally pick, which for the 'any others you have access to' tail means languages the character's own ancestry, region, or other sources have opened; that tail widens the list rather than adding a separate mechanic.
requirements.clause: chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others you have access to

requirements.what: A third language pick that exists only once Society proficiency reaches master, and a fourth once it reaches legendary. 'Are or become' is load-bearing: this is not evaluated once at the moment the feat is taken but re-evaluated as the character's Society rank rises, so a character who takes the feat while expert must have the extra slots appear on their own when they later hit master and legendary. Each is a further language choice from the same option list, and the resulting languages join the sheet's language list.
requirements.clause: You learn an additional language if you are or become a master in Society and again if you are or become legendary.

requirements.what: The feat must be selectable more than once, and each selection must carry its own independent set of picks — a second taking gives two more languages (plus its own rank-gated extras), and the picks from instance one must not overwrite or collapse into instance two. So the choices have to be addressed per-instance rather than per-feat.
requirements.clause: **Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, you learn additional languages.

requirements.what: A melee unarmed attack named 'lash' must appear in the strikes list, rollable — attack bonus from the character's unarmed proficiency and the usual attribute, damage 1d4. It must be recorded as belonging to the flail weapon group, because the group is what determines which critical specialization effect applies and which weapon-group-keyed effects reach it; a groupless unarmed attack loses that. Note the printed text names a die but no damage type.
requirements.clause: You gain a lash melee unarmed attack that is in the flail weapon group, deals 1d4 damage

requirements.what: The strike must carry the grapple and reach traits, and both must be live rather than decorative: reach has to extend this strike's reach beyond the character's normal melee reach where reach is displayed or used, and grapple has to be visible on the strike so the player knows this attack can be used to Grapple. Traits stored as inert labels on the strike would satisfy the wording and not the promise.
requirements.clause: and has the grapple and reach traits

requirements.what: No requirement. Which appendage delivers the lash — the tongue or tail named in the opening line — carries no mechanical difference: the attack's group, die, and traits are the same either way. This is descriptive colour about how the granted strike is performed, not a choice that changes a number, so it needs no picker and no sheet surface.
requirements.clause: The attack can be performed with any appendages you used to qualify for this feat.

requirements.what: One additional known halcyon spell at EVERY rank of halcyon spell the character can cast except their highest — so the number of picks is a formula over the character's current halcyon casting, not a fixed count. It must recompute on level-up: the moment a new highest rank comes online, the rank that was previously highest becomes eligible and a new pick must appear. The chosen spells then have to show up among the character's halcyon spells on the spells page, castable, attributed to this feat.
requirements.clause: You gain one more common halcyon spell of each level of halcyon spell you can cast other than your highest

requirements.what: A picker per eligible rank, filtered to COMMON halcyon spells of exactly that rank — per Q9 the builder offers only what may legally be picked, so uncommon and rarer halcyon spells must be excluded from this particular grant even if the character can otherwise reach them. Two separate filters are in play at once: rarity (common) and rank (the specific eligible rank, not 'that rank or lower').
requirements.clause: one more common halcyon spell of each level

requirements.what: An explicit carve-out that must be honoured rather than left to fall out of the arithmetic: rank 0 is excluded, so no additional cantrip pick may be offered even though cantrips are a level of halcyon spell the character can cast. A naive 'every castable rank except the highest' loop would wrongly produce a cantrip slot.
requirements.clause: (you do not gain an additional cantrip)

requirements.what: +1 halcyon spell slot at every rank of halcyon spell the character can cast other than the highest. These must be real slots in the halcyon casting's slot counts — expendable when casting, restored with the rest of that casting at daily preparations — not a note. Like the spells above, the set of affected ranks moves every time the character gains a new highest rank, so the bonus has to be derived from current casting rather than written once. Cantrips are unaffected here since they consume no slot.
requirements.clause: You also gain one additional halcyon spell slot for each level of halcyon spell you can cast, other than the highest.

requirements.what: The feat is something the character DOES — it produces a fruit — so it must reach the actions list as a named activity with its full printed text in the popup. ⚠ The supplied text has had its action-cost glyph stripped (visible in the empty `()` later in the same text), so the cost cannot be read from the text; whatever cost the record prints must be the one shown. Nothing here is a passive number.
requirements.clause: The plants covering your body sprout a single, ripe fruit.

requirements.what: The healing lands on a creature OTHER THAN YOU, and HP never moves sheet stats in any case — so no number is owed on your sheet (Ruling F + Ruling E's HP clause). What IS owed is the amount as text in the action's entry, level-scaled so the player reads the value at their own level rather than a printed formula. ⚠ The dice term is missing from the supplied text ("is healed Hit Points for every 2 levels"), so the source text is damaged and the actual die/quantity must come from the printed record.
requirements.clause: A creature other than you who eats this fruit ... is healed Hit Points for every 2 levels you have

requirements.what: A conditional variant of the healing text above, active only if the character has this Awakening. The sheet must be able to show the upgraded version of a record's own text when a separately-acquired Awakening is held — i.e. the action's text is not fixed at authoring time. Still no number on your sheet (ally-facing healing), so this is text substitution only. ⚠ The parenthetical is empty in the supplied text, so the die-size upgrade's full wording is truncated at source.
requirements.clause: **Awakening** The fruit is more potent. Increase the healing from d4s to d6s ().

requirements.what: This one is on YOUR side of the action, not the ally's: how many fruits your body produces, derived from your level (1, plus one per 5 levels beyond 2), and gated on holding this Awakening. There is no stat row for "fruits", so per Ruling D the count belongs in the action's own entry, computed for the character's current level. The text states no frequency, so no per-day counter or resource pip is owed by this text.
requirements.clause: **Awakening** The fruit is plentiful. You sprout one additional fruit for every 5 levels you have beyond 2.

requirements.what: Condition reduction on the eater — an ally-facing effect, so nothing on your sheet (Ruling F). It rides along as text in the same Awakening clause on the action's entry; it must appear only when that Awakening is held, since it is bundled into the plentiful-fruit Awakening rather than the base feat.
requirements.clause: Also, those who eat a fruit may reduce a condition affecting them by 1.

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. The three-action breakdown is the EATER's action cost, spent by another creature, and it is also the internal step-list of an activity — both are explicitly not lanes.
requirements.clause: as a three-action activity (1 Interact action to pluck the fruit and 2 Interact actions to eat it)

requirements.what: A builder choice of TWO spells from a closed list of exactly six named options (Clear Mind, Everlight, Humanoid Form, Revealing Light, Share Life, Sure Footing). Two distinct picks, not one; the list is fixed and must not offer anything outside it (Q9 — the builder shows only what the player may legally pick).
requirements.clause: Choose two of the following spells: Clear Mind, Everlight, Humanoid Form, Revealing Light, Share Life, or Sure Footing.

requirements.what: Each option in that list must itself carry the grant — picking an option is what produces the innate spell. A choice that records the pick without granting the spell satisfies nothing.
requirements.clause: Choose two of the following spells ... You can use each of the chosen spells ... as 2nd-rank divine innate spells.

requirements.what: Each chosen spell appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, divine tradition, cast at 2nd rank, with its details reachable and this feat named as the source. The rank is fixed at 2nd by the feat, so for any of the six whose own base rank is lower the granted rank must be carried explicitly — absent-means-base-rank (exemplar #10) would silently render those at the wrong rank. The tradition must also be legible where the player reads the spell, not asserted only by a pooled header (Q12 — the sheet must not state something false about the spell).
requirements.clause: You can use each of the chosen spells once per day as 2nd-rank divine innate spells.

requirements.what: One use per day for EACH chosen spell — two independent single uses, not a shared pool of two. Each is a spendable use displayed beside its own innate spell entry, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: You can use each of the chosen spells once per day

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. Flavour guidance about which lineages typically pick which pair; it neither restricts nor pre-selects the choice ('typically'), so it must not narrow the six-option list.
requirements.clause: Angelkin typically take *clear mind* and *humanoid form*, lawbringers typically have *everlight* and *share life*, and musetouched typically have *revealing light* and *sure footing*.

requirements.what: This changes the outcome of a reaction ANOTHER record granted, so per Principle C it must be reflected in that thing: a marker on the Call on Ancient Blood reaction's entry stating that a critical failure on the save becomes a failure when the reaction is used against a divine spell. That marker is the whole surface — there is no degree-of-success stat to move, and exemplar #7 settles that a save-outcome change is not owed a degree-of-success surface. Note the feat is inert on a character without Call on Ancient Blood, so the marker only exists where that reaction does.
requirements.clause: When you use your Call on Ancient Blood reaction against a divine spell and roll a critical failure on the saving throw against that spell, you get a failure instead.

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED on the saves themselves. The trigger is not 'saves generally' — it fires only inside one named reaction against one spell trait — so Q2's 'star all three saves' does not apply and Principle J puts the mark on the specific thing affected, which is the reaction. Starring Fortitude/Reflex/Will would advertise a benefit the player does not have on an ordinary save.
requirements.clause: roll a critical failure on the saving throw against that spell

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. An access clause; Q5 rules that access needs nothing, and access/prerequisite lines are explicitly not lanes.
requirements.clause: **Access** Vahird ethnicity

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. Flavour.
requirements.clause: Your ancestors' defiance of magic and your people's strictly egalitarian mindset mean that certain forms of magic have little effect on you.

requirements.what: This raises the participant count of a thing another record granted — Paired Link — from its normal number to up to six willing allies plus a piece kept for yourself. Per Principle C it must be reflected IN Paired Link's own entry, so the player reading Paired Link sees the enlarged version rather than having to remember a separate feat. This is a set/upgrade, so per Ruling G it replaces the number it upgrades rather than sitting beside it.
requirements.clause: When you use Paired Link during your daily preparations, you can exchange linking esoterica with up to six willing allies, keeping one piece for yourself.

requirements.what: Printed in Paired Link's entry as added text. The effect itself runs ally-to-ally — one linked ally's touch spell reaching another linked ally — so no number is owed on your sheet (Ruling F); the indication on the record it modifies is the entire requirement (Principle A). ⚠ OPEN READING, flagged not resolved: as printed the clause names 'a linked ally' as the caster, and you hold a piece too, so whether YOUR own touch-range spells gain the 30-foot reach against linked allies is not settled by the text. Per Ruling H the clause must be carried as written and not narrowed; if the table reads it as including you, it would additionally be a situational marker on touch-range spells.
requirements.clause: In addition to the normal effects of Paired Link, if a linked ally casts a spell with a range of touch, they can target linked allies within 30 feet with that spell.

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED beyond the marker above. The daily-preparations timing is Paired Link's own, not a new preparation choice this feat adds, and WHO is linked is party bookkeeping about allies — Ruling F puts that off your sheet. Do not invent a roster of linked allies from this text.
requirements.clause: When you use Paired Link during your daily preparations

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. Flavour, and the 'seven-part set' is descriptive — the text does not ask you to own or track seven inventory items, and inferring an esoterica inventory from it would be invention.
requirements.clause: Many traditions hold the number seven as significant. By exchanging pieces of a seven-part set of esoterica, you create a magical web by which your allies can affect each other at a distance.

requirements.what: Quick Stow must appear in the actions list as its own named activity with its printed action cost, its frequency and prerequisite shown in the popup, and its text reachable there. ⚠ The supplied text carries no action-cost glyph — 'You Interact to store one item' describes the effect, not the cost — so the cost must be taken from the printed record and not guessed.
requirements.clause: You Interact to store one item you're holding in your cheek pouches (provided it fits).

requirements.what: The frequency is printed in the action's popup, and that is all that is owed: it is per ROUND, and rounds are not tracked (Principle B), so no per-day counter, resource pip, or spendable use is owed for it. It must not be modelled as a limitedUses resource.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per round

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. A prerequisite line; prerequisites are explicitly not a lane. The cheek pouches themselves — whether stored items get an inventory location — are established by the prerequisite feat, not by this one, which only changes how quickly you put something in.
requirements.clause: **Prerequisites** Cheek Pouches

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. A size/fit judgement left to the table; the GM adjudicates it. It rides along inside the action's printed text.
requirements.clause: (provided it fits)

requirements.what: NOTHING REQUIRED. Name and source citation are not mechanical text.
requirements.clause: Quick Stow Source Player Core 2 pg. 30

requirements.what: Two instances of the Additional Lore general feat, each with its Lore subject PRE-SET (Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore) rather than offered as a pick. The sheet must be able to hold the same granted feat twice with two different fixed subjects, and each instance must carry Additional Lore's own later rank increases so both Lores advance — the promise is the feat, not merely the training.
requirements.clause: You gain the Additional Lore general feat for both Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore.

requirements.what: Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore each appear in the skill list as trained Lore skills with their own rollable modifier, attributed to this dedication.
requirements.clause: You gain the Additional Lore general feat for both Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore.

requirements.what: A redundancy fallback that fires PER COLLISION — the text says "one or both", so a character already trained in both is owed two picks. Each pick offers a Lore skill of the player's choice (Lore only, not any skill), and per Q9 the builder offers only Lores the player may legally take. The pick must appear only when it is actually owed.
requirements.clause: If you were already trained in one or both of those Lore skills, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.

requirements.what: A free action that exists at the moment you roll initiative: Recall Knowledge about one enemy you can see. It must appear among the character's actions with its free-action cost, its trigger (rolling initiative), and the GM-arbiter caveat in its popup.
requirements.clause: When you roll initiative, you can attempt a Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, or Society check to Recall Knowledge about one enemy you can see as a free action, if that skill would be applicable.

requirements.what: A `*` on each of the three NAMED skills — Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, Society — and on the Recall Knowledge action itself (Q2: star both the skill and the action), carrying the initiative free-action clause. The feat enumerates its skills, so unlike Mastermind's Eye this must NOT star every Recall Knowledge skill; only these three. (The supplied text carries unsubstituted `recall-knowledge skill=…` templates; those three are what they resolve to.)
requirements.clause: you can attempt a Devil Lore, Hellknight Lore, or Society check to Recall Knowledge

requirements.what: Nothing. An access clause is not a lane, and the standard archetype-dedication restriction is a general rule applied everywhere rather than a promise of this record.
requirements.clause: **Access** You're a member of the Hellbreakers league.

requirements.what: Three named spells — Illusory Disguise, Illusory Object, Illusory Scene — joined to the character's own spell list so they are REACHABLE wherever spells are chosen (prepared into slots, or added to a repertoire), not merely described in the feat's prose. Each must be tagged primal and cast with the character's spellcasting statistic, so a caster whose own tradition is not primal still sees them filed and labelled truthfully; per Q12 the entry must not assert a tradition these spells do not have here.
requirements.clause: Add Illusory Disguise, Illusory Object, and Illusory Scene to your spell list, which you cast as primal spells.

requirements.what: Create a Diversion must be performable with Performance in place of Deception. This changes the number actually rolled, so the player has to reach the Performance modifier where they look up Create a Diversion: the action carries Performance as its statistic for this character, and Performance is starred as a skill that can perform it (Q2 — star both the skill and the action).
requirements.clause: You Create a Diversion, except you roll a Performance check instead of Deception

requirements.what: An indication on the Create a Diversion record that the benefit of a success lands on an ally of your choice and NOT on you (Principle A — an ally-facing effect still needs a marker on the record it modifies; Ruling F — no number on your own sheet). The marker must be explicit that the character does not become hidden themselves, or the sheet silently implies the action's normal benefit.
requirements.clause: the benefits of successful checks apply to an ally of your choice instead of you

requirements.what: Printed text in that same popup and nothing more. The duration is turn-scoped and runs on someone else, so per Q1 it is indication-only — no mode, no timer, no numbers — and the targeting condition is prose the player applies at the table.
requirements.clause: The effects of a success last until the end of that ally's turn, and can end early based on the ally's actions. You don't need to be observing your ally or know where they are, but you need to know they're present to choose them.

requirements.what: Stealth and Survival both trained, attributed to this record.
requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Stealth and Survival.

requirements.what: A fallback that detects an automatic training collision from another source (background, class) and REPLACES that grant with a free choice of any skill — the choice is not restricted to Lore, unlike Hellbreaker Dedication's. ⚠ Flagged, not assumed: the text spells out only the single-collision case ("one of those skills"), so whether a character automatically trained in BOTH Stealth and Survival is owed two picks or one is not stated here and needs a ruling rather than an implementation guess.
requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

requirements.what: Goloma Lore appears as a trained Lore skill with its own rollable modifier.
requirements.clause: You also become trained in Goloma Lore.

requirements.what: Nothing further. The record as given carries no attribute boosts and no granted skill feat, so none should be inferred from the shape of the record.
requirements.clause: You lived an insulated life focused on avoiding danger.

requirements.what: Venipuncture appears in the actions list as its own activity, with its cost line and full text in its popup. ⚠ The supplied text has two unresolved holes — the area ("lacerating foes in a .") and the save type ("must attempt a save") — so whatever prints this must not render an incomplete sentence at the player; the missing area and save name are owed before the popup is truthful.
requirements.clause: A shell made up of hundreds of razor-thin needles of blood forms around you before exploding outward, lacerating foes in a .

requirements.what: The cost is a spend against a pool that exists elsewhere on the sheet, so that pool must be a readable, spendable counter for the cost to mean anything: the action shows its cost, is unavailable while sanguimancy Hit Points are under 3, and empties the pool when used. "All your remaining" makes the spend VARIABLE, so the amount actually spent must be visible at the moment of use — it is the input to the damage the player then rolls.
requirements.clause: **Cost** all your remaining sanguimancy Hit Points (minimum 3)

requirements.what: A resolved NUMBER, not a restatement of the rule for finding it. The action's entry must show the DC as the higher of the character's class DC and spell DC, computed from their own statistics, and say which one won. Unlike a target-side number (which DECIDED SCOPE excludes), this DC is read off the player's OWN sheet, so it is genuinely computable and owed.
requirements.clause: The DC for this save is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

requirements.what: Nothing on your own sheet. The damage and the save land on enemies, which DECIDED SCOPE rules out as a lane, and per Ruling E HP and damage never move sheet stats. The only requirement is that the formula stays legible in the popup so the player can compute double the points spent, capped at 80.
requirements.clause: The needles deal piercing damage equal to double the number of sanguimancy Hit Points you spent, to a maximum of 80 damage. Creatures caught in the blast must attempt a save.
Add the following property runes to the list you can choose for your blessed armament: Animated, Greater Fearsome, Grievous, Keen, and Greater Vitalizing.
requirements.what: The five named runes must become selectable options inside the OTHER record's rune list — the Blessed Armament feature's pick — not a sentence printed on this feat. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing. So the sheet must express 'this feat widens that feature's option list', and the player must meet the five where they make the pick.

requirements.clause: If you have the Radiant Armament feat, add greater Greater Astral and Greater Brilliant to the list as well.
requirements.what: A SECOND, CONDITIONAL widening of the same list, gated on the character also owning the Radiant Armament feat. The list-widening must therefore be able to depend on another owned record, and per Q9 (the builder shows only what the player may legally pick) Greater Astral and Greater Brilliant must be absent from the rune list when Radiant Armament is not held, rather than shown-and-disallowed.

requirements.clause: you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list as a single action that has the concentrate and divine traits
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list: 1 action, traits concentrate and divine, whose effect is re-opening the blessed armament rune pick. The action's existence is the lane; the swap itself is its effect.

requirements.clause: you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list
requirements.what: The blessed armament rune is a per-day choice; this feat makes it re-choosable at will. The sheet must be able to re-open that daily pick OUTSIDE daily preparations/rest — offering the same, widened list — instead of locking it until the next rest.

requirements.clause: Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times.
requirements.what: A caveat in the action's popup, and a real constraint on the re-pick: swapping runes must not reset any limited-use counter carried by the rune being swapped away from or to. Not computable prose alone — it is a rule about how the re-pick behaves.

requirements.clause: You gain the Pet general feat.
requirements.what: The named Pet general feat is granted outright — it must appear as an owned feat with its own details reachable, and whatever the Pet feat itself grants must follow from it.

requirements.clause: Instead of the normal choice of pet abilities, your eel has aquatic, Fast Movement, and the Damage Avoidance familiar ability for Reflex saves.
requirements.what: This SUPPRESSES a choice the granted feat normally offers and substitutes three fixed abilities. The sheet must express 'the Pet feat's ability choice is replaced, not added to' — the player must not be asked to pick pet abilities here, and the three named abilities (aquatic; Fast Movement; Damage Avoidance, specified for Reflex saves) must be fixed in place of that pick. Damage Avoidance needs its save keyed to Reflex specifically, since the ability is normally chosen per save.

requirements.clause: your eel ... serves as your pet
requirements.what: A pet companion exists as its own record with its own stat block, carrying the three abilities above. Per DECIDED SCOPE the companion's abilities mark the COMPANION, so their absence from the character's own sheet is correct — but the companion stat block itself must be able to hold them.

requirements.clause: The aquatic ability means it gains the aquatic trait, breathes water instead of air, and has a swim Speed instead of a land Speed.
requirements.what: On the companion's stat block: the aquatic creature trait recorded as a trait (Q6's shape — acquired creature traits are recorded), and a swim Speed that REPLACES the land Speed rather than sitting beside it (Ruling G — a replacement replaces the entry it replaces). 'Breathes water instead of air' is a note on the companion; it changes no number.

requirements.clause: When you aren't in an aquatic environment, you can easily carry your pet eel around in a small water-filled globe that has light Bulk.
requirements.what: No requirement. No item is granted to inventory — the text says you CAN carry it in a globe, it does not add one — and no number on either sheet changes. Borderline only in that it names light Bulk; if the globe were ever treated as granted equipment it would be an inventory item at L Bulk, but the text does not grant it.

requirements.clause: When you take this dedication, choose one willing, non-minion ally to be your student in the ways of the Iridian Choir.
requirements.what: FREE-TEXT player input naming the student (Principle I, the Guerrilla Dedication shape). The student is another player's character — never a record in the data — so no picker can offer them; the sheet must be able to store and display a typed name, and the whole archetype's other clauses refer back to it.

requirements.clause: they gain the benefits of your abilities without having to take any feats of their own
requirements.what: No requirement on this sheet. Purely ally-facing (Ruling F/N) — the benefit lands on the student, whose own sheet the app is not modelling here, and the dedication's own description already tells the player what the student gets. No number, no star.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits of your Iridian Choirmaster archetype feats only if both you and your student are alive and conscious.
requirements.what: This one conditions YOUR OWN benefits on a fact the app can never know — the ally's state. Ruling M's shape applies: a permanent marker carrying the condition in its note, placed on each Iridian Choirmaster archetype feat the character holds (Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters), rather than a computed shutdown. Q11 would also permit a player-flipped mode since the benefits genuinely can be switched off; either way the sheet must be able to say 'these feats are conditional on the student' at the feats themselves, not only in this dedication's paragraph.

requirements.clause: You and your student can trade nonverbal messages as a single action, which have the effects of the Message spell but are non-magical. This requires a single action, has the concentrate, mental, and linguistic traits, and requires that you be able to see each other.
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list: 1 action, traits concentrate/mental/linguistic, with the requirement 'you can see each other' in its popup (Principle E's popup shape) and its effect stated as Message's but explicitly NON-magical — so it must not be filed as a spell, must consume no slot, and must carry no tradition.

requirements.clause: If your student dies, or if you and your student choose to part ways, you can choose and develop a new student by spending 1 week of downtime training another willing, non-minion ally.
requirements.what: No sheet surface. Re-choosing the student is a builder action (Principle K, exactly as Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location) — the only requirement is that the free-text field be editable there. The 1 week of downtime is GM-adjudicated.

requirements.clause: **Special** Your student can't be the student of another character with the Iridian Choirmaster Dedication, and if your student takes the Iridian Choirmaster Dedication, they must choose you to be their student.
requirements.what: No requirement. A constraint spanning two different characters' choices, which the table enforces; nothing on either sheet computes it.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are attuned to an apparition that grants Circus Lore or Fey Lore as one of its apparition skills.
requirements.what: The Requirements line must appear in the stance's popup (exactly the Minor Omen shape — trigger/requirement live in the popup). Note this is a USAGE requirement checked when the stance is entered, and it turns on which apparition is currently attuned — a state that changes day to day — so it must be printed as a condition to read, not resolved into a static prerequisite that hides the feat.

requirements.clause: You adopt a stance that makes your movements carefree and sublimely unpredictable
requirements.what: A stance-entering activity in the actions list.

requirements.clause: You adopt a stance ...
requirements.what: A toggleable stance mode, exclusive with other stances (one stance at a time), carrying both effects below. Per Q3's principle for modes, the sheet must make plain that the mode is active and what it changed.

requirements.clause: You ignore difficult terrain
requirements.what: Text inside the mode. Principle B — a mode carries the FULL text of what it does, including the parts the app cannot compute. Difficult terrain is a map fact, so this contributes no number to Speed; it must still be readable on the active mode.

requirements.clause: you gain resistance equal to half your level against damage dealt to you by animals, beasts, fey, fungi, and plants
requirements.what: A real resistance inside the mode, with two shapes a plain number cannot carry: (a) its VALUE is a formula off your level (half your level), so it must scale rather than be a fixed figure; (b) its applicability is keyed to the ATTACKER'S creature type — animal, beast, fey, fungus, plant — not to a damage type, so the sheet must express a resistance restricted by the source creature's trait and show all five traits in the resistance breakdown, so the player can see when it applies.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You regain Hit Points while you are unconscious.
requirements.what: A triggered action listed with the character's reactions/triggered actions, with its trigger stated in the popup (Principle E — often the whole requirement). One wrinkle worth stating: the trigger fires while the character is unconscious, so the entry must stay reachable and legible on a sheet at 0 HP / dying rather than being suppressed with the rest of the action economy.

requirements.clause: You expend 1 Mythic Point
requirements.what: A Mythic Point pool expressed on the sheet as a spendable resource, and this action's cost of 1 point shown on its entry and decrementable when used. Without the pool the cost has nothing to spend from — this is the only clause in the feat that consumes a tracked resource.

requirements.clause: return to consciousness, Stand, and regain additional Hit Points equal to your level
requirements.what: No requirement. HP never moves sheet stats even inside a mode (Ruling E), and Stand and 'return to consciousness' are internal steps of the activity — the app lists the action, the player performs it. The only surface is the popup text; because the amount is level-scaled, that text must be able to state a formula rather than a fixed number.

requirements.clause: You then erupt in flames, dealing fire damage equal to twice your level () to adjacent foes, with a save against your class DC.
requirements.what: No requirement. The damage lands on enemies (out of scope), and the save is rolled against your class DC — a stat the sheet already carries and which this feat does not modify, so no entry is owed in any DC breakdown (Ruling D's DC case only fires when something changes the DC). Flagging one text problem visible in the printed clause itself: it carries an empty '()' where the damage value was meant to be substituted, so as printed the popup cannot state the number it promises.

requirements.clause: Foes that critically fail the save are also pushed 5 feet away from you.
requirements.what: No requirement. Enemy-side forced movement — an effect on enemies rather than on your own sheet, and positional besides. Nothing to express.

No requirement. The automatic categorisation is pure information with no roll, no number, no action and no cost — it fires on perception, not on a check — so there is no record for a marker to attach to and nothing for the sheet to compute. The feat's own printed text is the whole surface. (The following sentence, "At the GM's discretion, similar effects can also fall into these categories", is GM adjudication and is likewise not a lane.)
requirements.clause: When you become aware of a magical effect or see a spell being cast, you can immediately determine if it twists minds (with the mental trait), fights against fortune (with the fortune or misfortune trait), or reveals secrets (with the detection, prediction, revelation, or scrying traits).

requirements.what: The sheet must be able to express that Occultism may be used in place of the tradition-matched skill (Arcana/Nature/Religion) for Identify Magic and for Recall Knowledge, and used without penalty — but ONLY for effects with the mental, fortune, misfortune, detection, prediction, revelation or scrying traits. The substitution is restricted, so the restriction has to ride with it (Ruling B: the restriction lives in the `when`, not in a flat grant).
requirements.clause: When you Identify Magic or Recall Knowledge to learn more about these effects, you can always use Occultism without penalty

requirements.what: A situational `*` on Occultism carrying a +2 circumstance bonus, with the restriction in its `when` — only when Identifying Magic or Recalling Knowledge about mental / fortune / misfortune / detection / prediction / revelation / scrying effects. Per Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action") the same mark must also reach the Identify Magic and Recall Knowledge action entries, so it is visible both where the player reads the number and where they read the activity. The bonus is named for Occultism specifically, so Ruling C's "star every skill that could perform the action" does not widen it to Arcana/Nature/Religion.
requirements.clause: and gain a +2 circumstance bonus

requirements.what: The activity must appear in the actions list as a named action, with its Requirements line — "You gained a terrain attunement benefit this turn, and it matched the terrain you're in" — shown in its popup. Per the Minor Omen shape (Principle E), listing the activity with its trigger/requirement text is a requirement in its own right; the app lists the action, the player performs it.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You gained a terrain attunement benefit this turn, and it matched the terrain you're in.

requirements.what: Indication only, no number. The value must be legible in the action's popup as a formula off your own level ("temporary Hit Points equal to your level"), because a bare number cannot convey it. It gets no stat surface and no mode: Q1 rules that an effect lasting 1 round is not implemented, and Ruling E rules that HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode. Q15 also confirms temporary Hit Points alone are not "complicated" enough to earn an applied mode.
requirements.clause: You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level. They last for 1 round.

requirements.what: No requirement beyond printing it. This is a stacking clarification between two untracked temporary-HP effects; with no rounds tracked and no temp-HP number derived, there is nothing to combine. It belongs in the same popup text as the clause above.
requirements.clause: If you previously gained the plains terrain attunement effect this turn, combine the temporary Hit Points together.

requirements.what: The activity must appear in the actions list as a named action with its Requirements line — "You are Exploiting a creature's Vulnerability using mortal weakness" — in its popup. Selecting which esoterica object you hand over is an internal step of the activity performed at the table, not a stored choice, so it needs no field.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are Exploiting a creature's Vulnerability using mortal weakness. --- You select an object from your esoterica that has great personal value to you… and you grant it to an adjacent ally

requirements.what: No number on your sheet. The benefit lands entirely on the ally's Strikes; Ruling F/N settles that an effect on a teammate produces no star and no modifier for you, and the target-side application of a weakness is not something your sheet models. Do not report the ally's benefit failing to reach them as a defect.
requirements.clause: The ally's Strikes apply the weakness from your mortal weakness the same way your Strikes do.

requirements.what: A display-only mode the player can see running, carrying the full text of what was shared and ending when Exploit Vulnerability ends or you Share Weakness again. Ruling F is explicit: an ally-facing effect that runs for a limited time gives the activating character a display-only mode so they can see it running, changing none of their own numbers. The duration here is not the 1-round case Q1 excludes — it persists for the life of your Exploit Vulnerability — and Principle B requires the mode to carry the full text even though it contributes no computable value.
requirements.clause: This benefit ends when your Exploit Vulnerability ends or you Share Weakness again.

requirements.what: ⚠ DERIVED FROM PRINCIPLE A, not stated by the owner for this feat: an indication on the record this modifies — your Exploit Vulnerability / mortal weakness entry — showing that this feat can extend that weakness to an adjacent ally. Principle A is the round-1 correction: an ally-facing feat still needs a visible marker on the source ability even though no number reaches your sheet, exactly as Resilient Touch marks Lay on Hands.
requirements.clause: establishing a personal link that allows your ally to affect an enemy as if they were you

requirements.what: A second reaction on the sheet, refreshing at the start of each of your turns alongside your normal one — so the reaction economy the player reads must be able to show a count greater than one, not just "reaction: used / unused".
requirements.clause: At the start of each of your turns, you gain an additional reaction

requirements.what: The restriction must be legible on that extra reaction: it can be spent only on Aldori Riposte, Saving Slash, or any dueling action. Without it the sheet asserts something false — a free second reaction usable for anything. Ruling B puts the restriction in the bonus's own `when` rather than granting it flat, and Ruling D/Q8 puts the mark on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, so the named reaction entries (Aldori Riposte, Saving Slash, dueling actions) are the other legitimate home for it.
requirements.clause: that you can use only for Aldori Riposte, Saving Slash, or any dueling action

requirements.what: An alchemical poison in inventory must be able to carry a per-item marker showing it is a *blessed* alchemical poison and that it has gained the void trait — a trait added to the item, displayed where the item's traits are read (Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at). This also requires the sheet to distinguish HOW a poison was obtained: only ones you Craft qualify, and ones produced by advanced alchemy, Quick Alchemy or any other means explicitly do not, so provenance has to be expressible per item rather than the marker applying to every poison you hold.
requirements.clause: When you Craft an alchemical poison (rather than create it with advanced alchemy, Quick Alchemy, or another means), it becomes a blessed alchemical poison and gains the void trait.

requirements.what: No sheet number. The reduction applies to the afflicted creature's healing — an effect on an enemy, and on Hit Points, both of which are settled as producing nothing on your own sheet (DECIDED SCOPE: effects on enemies are not lanes; Ruling E: HP and damage never move sheet stats). Its 1-round duration is separately covered by Q1 — indication only.
requirements.clause: When a creature is afflicted with a blessed alchemical poison, for 1 round, any Hit Points it would regain from a vitality effect are reduced by 5

requirements.what: The value printed on the blessed-poison marker must be able to vary with the character's own Crafting proficiency rank — 5 normally, 10 at legendary. The player reads it off the poison, so the text riding on that item marker has to be rank-aware rather than a fixed string; a static "reduced by 5" would be wrong on a legendary crafter's sheet.
requirements.clause: or by 10 if you are legendary in Crafting
**Trigger** You would be hit by an attack or targeted by an effect, or you are within an effect's area. **Requirements** You have Perfect Distraction ready to use.
requirements.what: The feat IS a reaction (the Trigger line marks it as one), so it must appear as its own entry in the reactions list, and its popup must carry the trigger verbatim — all three branches (would be hit by an attack / targeted by an effect / standing inside an effect's area) — and the requirement line. Per Principle E that is normally the whole surface. Note the requirement is a pointer at another record's resource ("Perfect Distraction ready to use"), so the popup's wording must send the player to that action's remaining use rather than implying a resource of its own; this feat promises no frequency or per-day counter of its own and none should be invented.

requirements.clause: You use Perfect Distraction, even if you were observed, as long as you end the movement of your Sneak while concealed or in a location with cover or greater cover.
requirements.what: A marker on the Perfect Distraction action itself, showing that this feat changes how that action may be used — it becomes usable on this reaction's trigger, and its normal "only while unobserved" restriction is lifted at the cost of a new condition (the Sneak must END in concealment, cover, or greater cover). Ruling D / Q8: the mark lives on the record the feat modifies, so a player reading Perfect Distraction sees that a feat has altered it. Display shape deferred; the condition text must be reachable from the marker.

requirements.clause: Your decoy is targeted by the attack or effect instead of you. In the case of an area effect, if your Sneak doesn't move you out of the area, both you and the decoy are targeted by the effect.
requirements.what: Nothing. Redirecting an incoming attack or effect onto the decoy is resolution on the attacker's side of the table and moves no number on your own sheet; the area-effect caveat is likewise a table adjudication of where you ended up. Both are prose the player reads in the reaction's popup, which requirement 1 already owes.

requirements.clause: You can communicate with all bears
requirements.what: An entry in the languages / communication block reading that you can communicate with bears, sourced to this feat. It is not a spoken-language slot and must not be presented as one — it is a granted ability to communicate with a named creature category, and the player needs to see it where they look up what they can talk to.

requirements.clause: as well as other ursine creatures at the GM's discretion
requirements.what: Nothing to express as a mechanic — the scope beyond "bears" is explicitly handed to the GM. If the entry from requirement 1 carries a note it should quote this clause so the player can raise it at the table, but it earns no separate surface, no toggle, and no list of creature types.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You are targeted by an attack. **Requirements** Your familiar is adjacent to you or in your space.
requirements.what: The feat is a reaction, so it must appear in the reactions list with its trigger (you are targeted by an attack) and its requirement (familiar adjacent to you or in your space) in the popup, and the full effect text reachable from there. Per Principle E this is the bulk of what the feat owes.

requirements.clause: You are concealed from the triggering attack.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the popup text. The concealment covers a single incoming attack and is consumed at that instant — shorter even than the one-round floor Q1 sets for "indication only" — and it resolves on the attacker's roll rather than on any stat of yours. No toggle, no mode, no number.

requirements.clause: Until the start of your next turn, your familiar can't be targeted
requirements.what: Nothing on your own sheet. This lands on the familiar, and a companion's own state belongs to the companion, not to you; the duration is under one round, which Q1 rules is indication only rather than an implemented effect. The words in the reaction's popup are the whole surface.

requirements.clause: your enemies treat all spaces adjacent to you as difficult terrain
requirements.what: Nothing. An effect on enemies and on the battlefield, and one that depends on positions the sheet cannot know — explicitly outside scope. It stays as text in the reaction's popup.

requirements.clause: Your familiar gains the Patron's Claim activity.
requirements.what: A named activity attached to the FAMILIAR, not to you: the familiar's stat block must list Patron's Claim among its actions, with its action cost and its own full details reachable from that entry, and attributed to this feat. Two things follow. First, the grant must attach to the familiar the character already has — the feat creates no companion, so the attachment point is an existing familiar. Second, per the companions ruling the activity's absence from YOUR actions list is correct, not a defect; the requirement is that a familiar be able to hold a granted activity at all and show it where the player reads the familiar.

requirements.clause: Choose two skills.
requirements.what: A builder choice of two DISTINCT skills, plus the assignment of which one is yours and which is the eidolon's. This is a two-part pick — the skills and the ownership — and a single skill picker cannot express it; the record of who got which must persist, because requirement 4's level-7 upgrade has to follow the same assignment.

requirements.clause: you become trained in the other skill
requirements.what: Your assigned skill reaches trained on your own skill rows, sourced to this feat. The text promises no redundancy fallback for a skill you are already trained in, so none should be invented — this feat says only "become trained".

requirements.clause: Your eidolon becomes trained in one of those skills
requirements.what: The eidolon's assigned skill reaches trained on the EIDOLON's stat block, sourced to this feat. The eidolon must be able to carry a skill proficiency of its own, displayed where the player reads the eidolon's skills; it must not appear on your skill rows.

requirements.clause: At 7th level, you each become an expert in the chosen skills.
requirements.what: A level-gated upgrade to expert that fires automatically at 7th level and applies TWICE — once to your assigned skill on your sheet, once to the eidolon's assigned skill on the eidolon. No new choice is made at 7th; it follows the assignment stored at requirement 1, so the upgrade must be able to target a skill chosen earlier rather than a fixed named skill.

requirements.clause: These skill proficiencies are not shared between you and your eidolon.
requirements.what: A storage constraint, and a real one: the eidolon's skill proficiency must be held independently of yours. Your trained/expert skill must not raise the eidolon's same skill, and the eidolon's must not raise yours. This is an explicit exception to sharing rather than a restatement of a general rule, so it is expressible only if an eidolon's skill ranks can diverge from the summoner's; a design that mirrors one from the other has no route for this clause.

requirements.clause: You can use Lucky Escape once per hour instead of once per day.
requirements.what: The use pool gating Lucky Escape must be expressible as ONCE PER HOUR, not once per day: a spendable use the player can restore between encounters without a rest or daily preparation, and a printed frequency that reads "once per hour". A pool whose only refill point is rest cannot express this clause — the whole content of the feat is the recharge period.

requirements.clause: You can use Lucky Escape once per hour instead of once per day.
requirements.what: The change must land ON the Lucky Escape record, which some other record granted — Principle C ("a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing"). "Instead of" means replacement, so per Ruling G the upgrade replaces the frequency it upgrades rather than sitting beside it: a player who opens Lucky Escape sees "once per hour", never "once per day" with a second note contradicting it. The feat itself owes no independent numeric surface.

requirements.clause: If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, [the whole effect follows]
requirements.what: The feat is something the player USES immediately before Casting a Spell — "if the next action you use is to Cast a Spell" only parses if this feat is itself an activity taken first. So it must exist as an entry the player can find and read at the table, with the full effect text in its popup. That entry is the entire surface of this feat; everything else it does happens on other creatures. ⚠ The supplied text carries no action-cost or trait line, so the cost this entry should display cannot be established from the text alone.

requirements.clause: any creature that attempts to use a reaction triggered by your Cast a Spell activity takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and skill checks rolled as part of the reaction
requirements.what: No requirement. The penalty applies to an ENEMY's attack rolls and skill checks, on a roll the enemy makes. Effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet are explicitly not lanes; the printed text inside the action's popup is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: if the spell includes a spell attack or requires a saving throw, creatures you hit or that fail their saves are fascinated with you until the start of your next turn
requirements.what: No requirement, on two independent grounds. It is an enemy condition — Q4: the entry is the whole surface. And it lasts until the start of your next turn — Q1: effects lasting 1 round are not implemented, indication only.

requirements.clause: You can cast [spell] as a primal innate spell once per day.
requirements.what: The named spell must appear on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the PRIMAL tradition, cast at the spell's own base rank (the text names no other rank), with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. The tradition must be legible where the player reads this particular spell rather than only in a pooled header, since a character can hold innate grants of several traditions at once (Q12 — the sheet must not state something false about the spell). ⚠ The supplied text has LOST the spell's name — the sentence reads "You can cast as a primal innate spell" — so which spell is granted cannot be established from the text I was given and must be read off the printed feat.

requirements.clause: ...once per day.
requirements.what: One spendable use per day displayed beside the innate spell entry, consumed when the spell is cast and restored at daily preparations. The entry must not read as at-will.

requirements.clause: If you're a songbird strix, you can cast it twice per day instead.
requirements.what: The number of uses is not a constant on this feat — it must be DERIVED FROM THE CHARACTER'S HERITAGE: two per day for a songbird strix, one for everyone else. A fixed count of 1 authored on the feat cannot express this clause. "Instead" is replacement, not addition (Ruling G), so the songbird strix sees 2 uses and never 1+1 shown side by side.

requirements.clause: Your advanced alchemy level increases to 7.
requirements.what: "Advanced alchemy level" must exist as a real, readable number on the character — a value owned by the alchemy feature this feat builds on — and this feat SETS it to 7. Ruling G: a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so the player must see one advanced alchemy level, not the previous value and 7 both.

requirements.clause: For every level you gain beyond 12th, your advanced alchemy level increases by 1.
requirements.what: The value is not a constant 7. It must be a formula recomputed on level-up — 7 at 12th level, +1 per character level thereafter (so 8 at 13th, 15 at 20th). A record that can only store the literal 7 loses everything above 12th level. This is the second promise in the feat and the one most easily read past.

requirements.clause: Your advanced alchemy level increases to 7. For every level you gain beyond 12th, your advanced alchemy level increases by 1.
requirements.what: The number's only function is to bound which alchemical items the character may make with advanced alchemy, so it must REACH the place where the player prepares those items during daily preparations — the offered list bounded by the current value, and the value visible there. Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters; a number stored where the player never chooses items tells them nothing.

requirements.clause: Source Core Rulebook pg. 220 Archetype Alchemist Prerequisites Expert Alchemy; Master in Crafting
requirements.what: No requirement. Source line, archetype tag, and prerequisites are explicitly not mechanical lanes.

requirements.clause: You do not take circumstance penalties to ranged spell attacks ... caused by weather
requirements.what: A `*` on the spell attack roll carrying this clause. It cancels a penalty the GM applies from the weather, which the sheet can never know is present, so it contributes NO number — a marker whose note carries the printed condition (Ruling B: a bonus the rules restrict lives in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, outside the stat total). The star must sit on the spell attack modifier itself, where the player reads the number they are about to roll.

requirements.clause: ...or Perception checks caused by weather
requirements.what: A second `*`, on PERCEPTION, carrying the same clause. Principle J / Q2: the star goes on the specific stat affected and Perception is a stat the player reads directly, so this clause needs its own marker there rather than being folded into the spell-attack one. Two different stats are named in one sentence and both are owed a surface.

requirements.clause: your targeted spells don't require a flat check to succeed against a target concealed by weather (such as fog)
requirements.what: A marker on the character's SPELLCASTING carrying the no-flat-check clause. The concealment flat check is a roll YOU make, so this is your own surface and not a target-side number the app declines to model. "Targeted spells" covers save-based spells as well as attack spells, so the spell-attack star alone does not reach it — the clause must also be readable where the player casts spells. No number: whether the target is concealed by weather is a battlefield fact the sheet cannot know, so this is note-shaped (Ruling H — printed trigger in the note).

Nothing. Leaving and reading chemical trails is the fiction that justifies the bonus in the next sentence — navigation the GM adjudicates, with no number, no action, and no sheet surface of its own. It is not a `sense` (nothing is detected at a stated range) and not a `speed`.
requirements.clause: You can leave a faint chemical trail as you move and can use the chemical trails of other surkis to navigate.

requirements.what: A `*` carrying "+1 circumstance, to Sense Direction or reorient yourself" on EVERY skill that could perform Sense Direction — Survival, and any other skill the character can substitute for it — and, per Q2 ("Both — star the skill AND the action"), also on the Sense Direction action entry itself. The bonus is restricted to one named action, so per Ruling B it lives in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, never as a flat skill bonus sitting inside the Survival total.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all checks ... to Sense Direction or reorient yourself.

requirements.what: The clause also covers SAVES, and names no particular one. Per Q2, when a bonus applies to saves generally it stars all three — so a `*` on Fortitude, Reflex and Will, each carrying "+1 circumstance to a save to Sense Direction or reorient yourself". Ruling H governs the wording: the printed trigger goes in the note rather than narrowing it to whichever save the app guesses is meant, which would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all ... saves to Sense Direction or reorient yourself.

requirements.what: The feat is itself something you do — "if your next action is to cast" is the metamagic shape, performed before the spell — so it must exist as its own entry in the actions list, with its full text (non-cantrip, polymorph, single target only) in its popup. That entry is the primary surface: the player fires it, then casts.
requirements.clause: If your next action is to cast a non-cantrip polymorph spell that targets only one creature ...

requirements.what: A marker on the records this feat modifies — the character's own non-cantrip polymorph spells — showing that Healing Transformation can attach to them. This is Principle A/C in exactly the Lay on Hands shape (exemplars 1 and 2), with one difference worth flagging: the target here is not one named spell but a CLASS of spells (non-cantrip, polymorph, single-target), so whatever carries the marker has to select spells by trait and target count rather than by id. Display shape deferred, as with Lay on Hands.
requirements.clause: your polymorph spell also restores 1d6 Hit Points per spell rank to that creature.

requirements.what: The healing itself owes NO number anywhere. Ruling E: HP and damage never move sheet stats, so 1d6 per spell rank is text in the entry and nothing more. And when the target is an ally, Ruling F removes the number from your sheet entirely — the ally-facing half needs only the indication above. "This is a healing effect" is a trait line for the popup, restating a general rule the app already implements, not a lane.
requirements.clause: restores 1d6 Hit Points per spell rank to that creature. This is a healing effect.

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger — "an enemy within reach attempts to move away from you" — shown in its popup. Principle E: that is very nearly the whole requirement, and no other part of the sheet moves.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** An enemy within reach attempts to move away from you.

requirements.what: Nothing. Striding, following the enemy and keeping it in reach are the internal steps of the activity — the app lists the reaction, the player performs the movement. Only the reaction's EXISTENCE is a lane. "Up to your Speed" needs no computed value; the character's Speed is already on the sheet.
requirements.clause: Stride up to your Speed, following the enemy and keeping it in reach throughout its movement until it stops moving or you've moved your full Speed.

requirements.what: Nothing beyond the text already in the reaction's popup. This clause grants no movement type — it only permits substituting one the character already has, so there is no `speed` to add and no `*` to hang (Q7's star is for a movement type the feat itself confers conditionally). Whether the character has Burrow/Climb/Fly/Swim is already legible from the speed rows.
requirements.clause: You can use No Escape to Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

requirements.what: The Fly activity must appear as its own entry granted by this feat, with the full text in its popup — including the 20-foot conditional value and the fall clause. Crucially the entry must be reachable for a character with NO fly Speed, since that is the case the feat exists to cover; anything that gates a Fly entry on owning a fly Speed would hide it from exactly the character who needs it.
requirements.clause: You Fly.

requirements.what: "Once per round" gets NO spendable resource. The owner has ruled rounds are not tracked ("we dont truck rounds", answer 3; Q1), so this contributes no pip and no counter — it is printed frequency text in the entry, and the player polices it. Do not read this as a per-day use.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per round

requirements.what: The 20-foot fly Speed is momentary — "for this movement" — not a standing movement type, so it is NOT a `speed` row the way Wyrmling Flight's permanent fly Speed is. Its correct home is the action's own entry, per Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and when it matters the player is using this action. ⚠ Judgement call worth the owner's eye: IF a fly row were surfaced anyway, Q7 makes it a `*` conditional row rather than a bare 20, because it exists only during this one movement and only when the character has no fly Speed of their own.
requirements.clause: If you don't normally have a fly Speed, you gain a fly Speed of 20 feet for this movement.

requirements.what: Nothing computable. Where the character ends up is battlefield position, which the app can never know (the same reasoning as Ruling M on auras). It is a printed caveat inside the action's popup.
requirements.clause: If you aren't on solid ground at the end of this movement, you fall.

requirements.what: This changes what an EARLIER record already granted: the existing corpselike construct companion must be upgraded in place to an advanced construct companion, so the companion's own stat block shows the advanced tier's stats rather than the base ones. It must not produce a second, separate companion. Per the DECIDED SCOPE ruling on companions the change lands on the companion's stat block, not on the character's sheet — absence from the character's sheet is correct, but the companion actually becoming advanced is the requirement.
requirements.clause: It becomes an advanced construct companion.

requirements.what: A note on the construct companion's own stat block stating that in an encounter it may take 1 action to Stride or Strike on your turn without a Command a Minion action. Action economy is not modelled, so this contributes no number and no resource — but it is a real rule the player must read, and by the companion ruling its home is the companion's block rather than the character's actions list.
requirements.clause: During an encounter, even if you don't use the Command a Minion action, your construct companion can still use 1 action on your turn that round to Stride or Strike.

requirements.what: Nothing. "Much more powerful" and "limited autonomy" are flavour restating the two mechanical clauses above.
requirements.clause: Your corpselike construct companion becomes much more powerful and can act with limited autonomy to follow your greater directives.
You can perform a 10-minute ritual, which has the conjuration and magical traits, to divert a set of heavy armor you are wearing into an extradimensional space connected to you.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list at a 10-minute cost, carrying the conjuration and magical traits, with its requirement (a set of heavy armor you are currently wearing) shown in its popup. ⚠ This is NOT the `ritual` lane — 'ritual' is lowercase here and describes this feat's own activity, not a Ritual spell the character learns; filing it as a learned Ritual would be wrong.

requirements.clause: While the armor is in this space, you can use a three-action activity, which has the concentrate, conjuration, and teleportation traits, to phase the armor back and instantly don it.
requirements.what: A SECOND, separate entry in the actions list at a three-action cost, carrying the concentrate, conjuration, and teleportation traits. Its popup must state the condition that gates it — it is available only while the armor is in the extradimensional space — and that it dons the armor as part of the activity, with no separate donning time.

requirements.clause: …to divert a set of heavy armor you are wearing into an extradimensional space… / …to phase the armor back and instantly don it.
requirements.what: The stowed vs. carried state must be expressible: while the armor is in the extradimensional space it is not worn and therefore contributes no AC (and the retrieve activity restores it to worn). This is the ordinary 'item owned but not donned' state of an armor in inventory — no new lane is owed, but the pair of activities is meaningless unless that state can be held.

requirements.clause: The armor automatically phases away if you don another set of armor, if you become unconscious, or if you die. If you are incapable of wearing the armor when it phases back, it appears in your square instead.
requirements.what: Printed text on the two activity entries. None of the three auto-phase triggers is computable (donning other armor is an inventory action the player takes; unconscious and dead are not states this drives), and 'appears in your square' is positional and GM-adjudicated. Text only — no number, no marker on any stat.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are adjacent to an ally and have one or more hands free. --- Pick up an adjacent ally of your size or smaller and throw them to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.
requirements.what: An entry in the actions list carrying the action's printed cost, with its Requirements line (adjacent to an ally, one or more hands free) and its full effect text in the popup. The size limit (your size or smaller), the 30-foot range, and the unoccupied-space targeting are the internal steps of the activity — the player performs them; only the action's existence is owed.

requirements.clause: Their movement doesn't trigger reactions. Your ally ends this movement on their feet and doesn't take damage from the fall.
requirements.what: Wholly ally-facing (Ruling F) — no number and no star on your sheet. The record this modifies is this feat's own granted action, so the text already sitting in that action's popup is the entire indication Principle A asks for. Nothing further is owed.

requirements.clause: If your ally ends this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, they can use their reaction to make a melee Strike against such an enemy.
requirements.what: The ALLY spends the ALLY's reaction. This is not an `extraReaction` for you and must NOT produce a reaction entry in your reactions list — the reaction does not belong to you. It stays as text inside the Friendly Toss popup.

requirements.clause: You upgrade the vishkanyan venom you can apply with Envenom to lesser vishkanyan venom.
requirements.what: The upgrade must be reflected in the thing it modifies (Principle C): the Envenom entry itself must name lesser vishkanyan venom. Per Ruling G an upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so the superseded base vishkanyan venom must no longer be shown as an option on Envenom once this feat is held.

requirements.clause: Envenom's frequency becomes once per hour.
requirements.what: Envenom's printed frequency and any use counter attached to it must read 'once per hour', replacing the frequency Envenom carried before (again on the Envenom entry, not only in this feat's text). This demands a refresh PERIOD of an hour — distinct from per-day, so it cannot be modelled as a pip that only clears at daily preparations/rest; the player must be able to clear it independently.

requirements.clause: **Lesser Vishkanyan Venom (level 1)** **Saving Throw** **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds **Stage 1** 1d6 damage (1 round) **Stage 2** 1d6 damage (1 round) **Stage 3** 2d6 damage (1 round)
requirements.what: The venom's full stat block — level, save line, maximum duration, and the three stages with their damage and 1-round intervals — must be readable from the point of use (the Envenom entry), not only buried in this feat's description.
