It all lands on the target and moves no number on your sheet, so it is display text. ⚠ The printed Saving Throw line carries no DC in the source text, so no DC value is owed here — do not invent one.

requirements.clause: You are no longer limited to casting only a single hex each turn.
requirements.what: The once-per-turn restriction printed on your hex focus spells must be shown as lifted on those hex entries themselves (Principle C — reflected in the thing it modifies; Ruling G — the removal replaces the restriction rather than sitting beside a still-visible 'one hex per turn' line). It moves no number: turns/rounds are not tracked, so what is owed is that the restriction text on every spell with the hex trait stops asserting a limit this character no longer has.

requirements.clause: In addition, when you cast Cackle to sustain a hex, you gain the effects of Sustain for all your active hexes that have a duration of sustained.
requirements.what: A marker on the Cackle focus spell showing this feat modifies it, carrying the clause's text (Principles A and C). Which hexes are currently active, and their sustained durations, are round-by-round battlefield state that is not tracked, so this contributes no number — the indication on Cackle's own entry is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.
requirements.what: A climb Speed of 10 feet in the Speeds list. It is unconditional and a fixed value, so per Q7 ('most granted speeds are permanent and need no star') this clause on its own earns no `*`.

requirements.clause: If you also have the Cave Climber ancestry feat, your total climb Speed increases to your land Speed when climbing trees.
requirements.what: A climb-Speed value contingent on ANOTHER record being owned: the upgrade exists only when the character also holds the Cave Climber ancestry feat, and it must vanish when that feat is not held. The upgraded value must resolve off the character's own land Speed at display time, not be stored as a number — Q16's warning applies directly (a hardcoded speed is wrong for any character whose Speed is not the default).

requirements.clause: If you also have the Cave Climber ancestry feat, your total climb Speed increases to your land Speed when climbing trees.
requirements.what: The upgrade is circumstantial — trees only — so it cannot silently replace the 10 feet. Per Q7 a conditional movement value needs the `*`: when Cave Climber is held, the climb Speed entry carries a `*` whose note states that the Speed rises to your land Speed while climbing trees, so the player can see when the higher value applies.

requirements.clause: You become trained in martial weapons.
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in the martial weapon category, feeding the attack bonus of every martial-weapon strike the character wields. Category-wide, not a single weapon.

requirements.clause: You gain one ikon
requirements.what: The ikon class feature arrives on the sheet as a granted record with its details surfaced, not as prose buried in this feat's text (principle G — a granted class feature needs its details surfaced AND its choice offered).

requirements.clause: You gain one ikon
requirements.what: A builder pick of exactly ONE ikon, each option showing its full description and what it grants so the player can compare before choosing. Per Q9 the picker lists only ikons the character may legally take, unless the player toggles "show options not meeting prerequisites".

requirements.clause: the ability to use the ikon's immanence and transcendence actions and effects
requirements.what: The chosen ikon's transcendence (Spark Transcendence) must exist as a usable action entry with its text, and the ikon's immanence effect must be reachable as a thing the player can read and use. Which ones appear depends on the ikon picked, so the grant has to follow the earlier choice rather than be a fixed list on this feat.

requirements.clause: the ability to use the ikon's immanence and transcendence actions and effects ... when you Spark Transcendence, your divine spark recedes back to the depths of your soul and must be recalled with Shift Immanence to re-empower your ikon
requirements.what: The immanence effect is on only while the divine spark sits in the ikon, and off from the moment you Spark Transcendence until Shift Immanence returns it — a state the player turns on and off, carrying whatever numbers the chosen ikon's immanence grants. Q11 decides the shape: the effect can be shut down, so it is a mode rather than a passive bonus, and the sheet must make plain when it is running.

requirements.clause: and the Shift Immanence action
requirements.what: Shift Immanence appears in the actions list with its cost and text — the action's existence is the lane; the player performs its internal steps.

requirements.clause: Because you have only a single ikon, when you Spark Transcendence, your divine spark recedes back to the depths of your soul and must be recalled with Shift Immanence to re-empower your ikon.
requirements.what: This restriction changes how the granted ikon and Shift Immanence behave for an archetype character (a full exemplar juggles several ikons), so per principle C it must be reflected IN those granted records — a note on the ikon / on Shift Immanence — not left as a line only on the dedication. It contributes text explaining the cycle the mode's toggle represents, no number.

requirements.clause: You become trained in exemplar class DC.
requirements.what: A trained exemplar class DC on the sheet, held alongside the character's own class DC rather than replacing it, because an archetyping character now has two. The number is load-bearing: the ikon's transcendence effects are resolved against it.

requirements.clause: When you generate a wellspring surge, roll twice on the Wellspring Surges table and take the result of your choice.
requirements.what: An indication on the wellspring-surge record the character already has — the feature that tells them to roll on the Wellspring Surges table — saying that this feat turns that roll into two rolls, keep whichever you prefer. Principle C: it modifies another record's granted thing, so it must be reflected in that thing rather than sitting only on this feat's own line. No stat moves and no star belongs on any skill or save: the surge roll is a table lookup, not a d20 check against a number the sheet carries.

requirements.clause: This doesn't apply when you cause another creature to generate a wellspring surge.
requirements.what: Nothing of its own. It is a restriction on the clause above and rides inside that same indication's text; the excluded case is another creature's surge, which is not on your sheet.

requirements.clause: You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light for another 30 feet beyond that) until the end of your next turn.
requirements.what: The activity itself must exist as an entry the player can find and open, carrying whatever action cost the record holds plus its full text. That entry is the surface for everything below.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed with the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're below 20 Hit Points.
requirements.what: The requirement line printed in the action's popup so the player sees the gate when they go to use it (principle E's shape: trigger and requirements live in the popup). Nothing needs to be computed against current HP for the feat to work.

requirements.clause: You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light for another 30 feet beyond that) until the end of your next turn.
requirements.what: No mode and no modifier. The duration is one round, which Q1 settles as indication only, and the effect is battlefield illumination rather than any number on your sheet. The printed text in the action's popup is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: Enemy creatures in the area that rely on sight must attempt a save equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
requirements.what: The player has to quote a DC at the table, and the feat names two of their own numbers and a comparison between them. The action's entry should resolve that — showing the higher of the character's class DC and spell DC (or at minimum naming both) — so the player is not left doing the comparison from two different parts of the sheet. Q12: whichever spelling leaves the player least confused.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected. **Success** The creature is dazzled for 1 round. **Failure** The creature is blinded for 1 round and dazzled for 1 minute. **Critical Failure** The creature is blinded for 2 rounds and dazzled for 1 minute.
requirements.what: Nothing. These are conditions landing on enemies — decided scope (Ruling F, and Q4: the entry itself is the whole surface). The degree-of-success prose printed in the popup is all that is owed.

requirements.clause: You can use Halfling Luck when an ally within 30 feet fails a skill check or a saving throw to allow the ally to reroll the triggering check instead of you rerolling your own failed check.
requirements.what: An indication on the Halfling Luck reaction the character already owns, showing that its trigger now also fires on an ally's failed skill check or saving throw within 30 feet. Principle C plus principle A: the ally-facing effect still needs a visible marker on the record it modifies, and Ruling D puts that marker on the thing the player is looking at when the reaction comes up. This feat grants no new reaction of its own.

requirements.clause: allow the ally to reroll the triggering check instead of you rerolling your own failed check. As usual, your ally must use the new result, even if it's worse than their first roll.
requirements.what: Nothing on your sheet — the reroll and its downside land entirely on the ally (Ruling F). No extra uses either: "instead of you rerolling your own" spends the same Halfling Luck use, so the existing per-day resource is unchanged and must not be doubled.

requirements.clause: If you have Guiding Luck, you can't use Guiding Luck's effect that applies to attack rolls and Perception checks to use Shared Luck to benefit an ally.
requirements.what: A restriction that exists only when the character also holds Guiding Luck, and it constrains what Guiding Luck offers — so it must be reflected in the Guiding Luck entry (or in the same Halfling Luck marker) where the player would otherwise reach for it. Nothing computable; it limits a player choice.

requirements.clause: **Access** Ulfen ethnicity
requirements.what: Nothing. Access clauses are not a lane — Q5 rules that access text gates nothing and needs no surface.

requirements.clause: You gain the Shield Block reaction
requirements.what: The named Shield Block ability arrives as a granted record in its own right, carrying its own details, rather than as a sentence quoted inside this feat.

requirements.clause: You gain the Shield Block reaction
requirements.what: Shield Block appears in the reactions list, with its trigger and requirements shown in its popup (principle E). For most characters that is the entire further impact of this clause.

requirements.clause: are trained in your choice of the battle axe or longsword
requirements.what: A builder pick between exactly two named weapons — battle axe or longsword — recorded on the character so the proficiency knows which one it applies to.

requirements.clause: are trained in your choice of the battle axe or longsword
requirements.what: Trained proficiency in that ONE named weapon, not in a category or a weapon group: a strike with the chosen weapon must compute at trained even for a character who is untrained in martial weapons generally, while every other martial weapon stays at its old rank. The text prints no redundancy fallback for a character already trained in it, so none should be invented.

requirements.clause: You can cast Animal Messenger and Marvelous Mount as primal innate spells once per day each.
requirements.what: Two separate innate spells on the Spells page — Animal Messenger and Marvelous Mount — both filed as INNATE, both PRIMAL, each with its own details reachable from the entry and Bone Caller named as the granting source. The text names no rank for either, so each is cast at its own base rank. The tradition must be legible where the player reads the spell itself: this feat grants two primal spells, and a character can hold innate grants of other traditions at the same time, so a per-entry tradition (or a section that does not assert one it cannot honour) is what the sheet must be able to express.

requirements.clause: …once per day each.
requirements.what: Two INDEPENDENT once-per-day resources, one per spell — not a shared pool. Each shows a single spendable use beside its own spell entry, consumed when that spell is cast and restored at daily preparations. Spending Animal Messenger must leave Marvelous Mount available.

requirements.clause: The animal messenger is always a Tiny dinosaur or lizard, and your innate spell transforms it from bones to flesh, even if there are no dinosaurs or lizards nearby.
requirements.what: A marker on the granted Animal Messenger entry showing this feat modifies it, carrying the clause. This is not pure flavour: the base spell is bounded by what animals are present, and the last phrase lifts that bound for this casting. Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — so the note has to live on the spell entry the player is looking at when it matters, not only in the feat's own text.

requirements.clause: The phantom steed looks like a dinosaur rather than a horse but functions identically.
requirements.what: Nothing is required. The clause states its own null result — 'functions identically' — so it changes no value, grants no option, and gates nothing. Appearance only; it needs no surface beyond the feat's printed text.

requirements.clause: If your next action is to Cast a Spell from your spell slots, you gain a benefit.
requirements.what: The feat has to be reachable as a thing the player invokes and reads in the moment, with its full branching text in the popup. The whole feat hangs on a sequence the sheet cannot observe — that the player's NEXT action will be a Cast a Spell, and that it comes from a spell slot rather than an innate or focus casting — so nothing here can be computed or auto-applied; what the sheet must be able to express is the feat's presence and its complete text at the point of use. (The text field carries no action-cost or trigger header, so no cost is claimed here.)

requirements.clause: If the spell is arcane, you can attempt a skill check to Recall Knowledge with a +1 status bonus to the check after casting the spell, or a +2 status bonus if the spell is 7th rank or higher.
requirements.what: A situational star on EVERY skill that can Recall Knowledge and on the Recall Knowledge action itself (Ruling C, Principle D, and Q2's 'both'). Its `when` must carry the full condition — that the check follows a slot-cast ARCANE spell — and both tiers of the value, +1 status, rising to +2 when that spell was 7th rank or higher. The rank test is a property of the spell just cast, not of the character, so the value cannot be resolved to a single number: the star has to be able to state a conditional value.

requirements.clause: If the spell is primal, you gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to the spell's rank for 1 round.
requirements.what: Indication only — no computed number. Two standing rulings both land on it: Q1, effects lasting 1 round are not implemented, and Ruling E, HP never moves a sheet stat even inside a mode. The requirement is that the clause is legible where the player invokes the feat, including that the amount is the cast spell's rank.

requirements.clause: If the spell is a halcyon spell, you gain both benefits.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the two clauses above. It adds no third effect — it names the case in which both fire — so it needs only to be present in the feat's text. No separate star and no separate note.

requirements.clause: When you use Phantom Visage, you gain the effects of…
requirements.what: A marker on the Phantom Visage record showing this feat modifies it, and carrying what it adds. Principle C: this feat grants no ability of its own — it rides on one the character already has — so the surface belongs on the thing being modified, where the player is looking when they use it.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day, restored at daily preparations. It must be spendable independently of Phantom Visage's own resource: the underlying ability can still be used after this rider is exhausted, so the sheet needs a use-counter attached to the rider rather than to the host ability.

requirements.clause: you gain the effects of a 3rd-rank Illusory Disguise for 1 hour or until you shift back, whichever comes first.
requirements.what: A player-toggled mode. Q1 puts it here — the duration is an hour, far past the one-round line — and Q11 confirms it, because the effect can be shut down at will ('until you shift back'). The mode must express what a 3rd-rank Illusory Disguise actually does, at that rank specifically and not at the spell's base rank, with the spell's own details reachable from the mode; naming the spell without its effects would leave the player with nothing to read. Both end conditions belong in the mode — the 1 hour and the voluntary shift back — and per Q3's principle the sheet must make plain that the mode is running and what it changed.

requirements.clause: Stride. You can Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type. You then plant your fist or weapon into the ground at your feet…
requirements.what: The activity itself must exist as an entry the player can find and read, with its full text in the popup. The movement substitution is an internal step, not a separate lane, but it is conditional on the character actually possessing a burrow, climb, fly, or swim Speed, so the popup text has to carry it rather than being reduced to 'Stride'.

requirements.clause: creating a in an aura around you that lasts for 1 minute … The effect ends immediately if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points.
requirements.what: A display-only mode running for 1 minute, turned on when the activity is used and off by the player. Q1 puts a 1-minute effect in a mode; Ruling E keeps it display-only, since everything it does is damage redistribution and HP never moves a sheet stat. Ruling M's aura caveat does not bite here — the emanation is centred on you, so you are always inside it. The mode must carry the full text (Principle B), including the end condition at 0 Hit Points, which the player applies. NOTE: the printed text is defective — a noun is missing after 'creating a' — so whatever the mode displays is displaying a broken sentence.

requirements.clause: Whenever an ally within this aura takes damage, you can use your reaction to take half the damage in their stead while they take the remainder.
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list with its trigger stated — an ally inside the aura takes damage — per Principle E. Its availability is conditional on the aura running, so the sheet must be able to tie a reaction to an active mode rather than showing it as always available. The split itself (half to you, remainder to them) is text; no number moves.

requirements.clause: When you take damage through this link, you don't apply any resistances, weaknesses, or other abilities you have to that damage; you simply take that amount of damage.
requirements.what: A note on the reaction (and in the mode text) stating that your own resistances, weaknesses, and damage-altering abilities are suppressed for damage taken through the link. This is the one clause that contradicts what the character's own defences otherwise say, so it must be legible at the point the player uses the reaction — the player is being told to ignore numbers the sheet is showing them elsewhere.

requirements.clause: Whenever you take damage while this effect is active, an ally within the aura can use their reaction to take half the damage for you in the same manner.
requirements.what: Text inside the mode, nothing more. It spends the ALLY's reaction and is theirs to declare, so Ruling F applies — no star, no modifier, no reaction entry on your sheet. The player needs only to be able to read that the link runs both ways.

requirements.clause: Make two frenzied claw attacks against the same target, increasing the multiple attack penalty normally.
requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named entry the player can find and read, with its full text in the popup. Its internal steps are not lanes: the two Strikes are performed by the player, and 'increasing the multiple attack penalty normally' restates a general rule. It grants no strike of its own — the frenzied claw comes from claw stance, not from here — so no unarmed attack is owed.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are in claw stance and have two open hands.
requirements.what: The Requirements line shown in the action's popup, exactly as printed — both halves, the stance and the two open hands. This mirrors Minor Omen: requirements belong in the popup of the entry they gate. The stance half points at a state the character can be in or out of, so the sheet must at minimum be able to state the precondition; whether the entry is also hidden or dimmed while the stance is off is a display choice, not a separate requirement.

requirements.clause: If both attacks hit, the target must succeed at a save against your class DC or be Enfeebled 2 for 1 round; if it critically fails, it's instead enfeebled 2 for 1 minute.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the popup text. The condition lands on the ENEMY, which is out of scope, and Q4's principle holds — the entry is the whole surface. The class DC is USED here, not modified, so Ruling D's DC-only case does not apply and no star belongs beside the class DC. The printed text names no save type; per Ruling H it should be shown as written rather than narrowed to a guess.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You or your designated ally takes damage, and you're capable of entering a Rage.
requirements.what: A triggered entry for Wounded Party in the reactions list, with its trigger printed verbatim in the popup — both halves of it: the damage condition (to you OR to your designated ally) and the "you're capable of entering a Rage" condition. Principle E: for a triggered feat this is normally the whole surface, and it is here. (The supplied text gives a Trigger but no cost glyph, so whatever cost the record carries must be shown on the entry rather than assumed.)

requirements.clause: You Rage.
requirements.what: A marker on the Rage action showing this feat gives a second, triggered route into it (Q8 / Ruling D — mark the action the feat modifies, star linking back to this feat). If the Quick Recognition reading is preferred instead, the same clause resolves as Principle H: Rage appears under both costs — its native cost and this triggered one — with the explanation in the popup. What Rage itself does is already owed by the class feature; this clause adds only the alternative route, never a second Rage.

requirements.clause: your designated ally
requirements.what: No requirement. The feat REFERENCES a designation made by something else (its prerequisite) — it does not create one, so no ally picker and no free-text field is owed by this text. Principle I's free-text lane is earned only where a feat itself says "choose"; this one does not. The phrase only has to be readable inside the trigger.

requirements.clause: You gain two common 2nd-rank halcyon spells and two 3rd-rank halcyon spells.
requirements.what: Four builder picks — two at 2nd rank, two at 3rd — each offering ONLY what the player may legally take (Q9): common rarity, the stated rank, and only spells that qualify as halcyon spells. Unpicked grants show as empty slots that open that pick's own filtered list.

requirements.clause: You gain two common 2nd-rank halcyon spells and two 3rd-rank halcyon spells.
requirements.what: The four chosen spells must reach the Spells page as part of the character's halcyon spell list — readable, castable through the halcyon slots, with their details reachable and this feat named as the source. A pick that is recorded but never appears where the player casts from satisfies nothing.

requirements.clause: You also gain a 2nd-rank halcyon spell slot and a 3rd-rank halcyon spell slot.
requirements.what: One extra slot at rank 2 and one at rank 3, each a spendable slot that is consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations. Two separate slots at two separate ranks, not a rank-agnostic pair.

requirements.clause: These and all future halcyon spell slots work like the 1st-rank halcyon spell slot you gained from Halcyon Speaker Dedication.
requirements.what: The new slots must be the same RESTRICTED kind as the dedication's — belonging to the halcyon spellcasting entry and usable only for halcyon spells the character knows — not generic slots added to some tradition's ordinary pool. This is a cross-reference: the slot's behaviour has to be inherited from the record the dedication already established (Principle C's direction, reversed — here the later feat must adopt the earlier record's shape). The forward reference to "all future halcyon spell slots" asks for nothing extra of this feat beyond that shape being reusable.

requirements.clause: When you make your daily preparations, you can either gain the expert proficiency rank in one skill in which you're untrained or raise your proficiency rank to master in one skill in which you're trained or better.
requirements.what: A choice made at daily preparations (rest), presenting the two branches as mutually exclusive — one or the other, never both — and re-made each day rather than fixed at build time.

requirements.clause: gain the expert proficiency rank in one skill in which you're untrained
requirements.what: Branch one SETS the chosen skill to expert, and the resulting rank must drive that skill's modifier on the sheet, replacing the untrained entry rather than sitting beside it (Ruling G). The picker for this branch lists only skills the character is currently untrained in (Q9).

requirements.clause: or raise your proficiency rank to master in one skill in which you're trained or better
requirements.what: Branch two SETS the chosen skill to master, driving that skill's modifier. Its picker lists only skills the character is trained or better in (Q9). Per Q10 the set applies only where it improves the rank — a legendary skill must not be dropped to master by taking this branch.

requirements.clause: You also gain one skill feat with a minimum requirement of your new rank in the chosen skill.
requirements.what: A picker for one skill feat, offering only skill feats whose skill prerequisite is the NEW rank in THAT specific chosen skill — the filter depends on the pick made in the previous clause, so the two choices are ordered. The feat chosen is owned for the day, and whatever it in turn grants must reach the sheet like any other owned feat.

requirements.clause: For the purpose of meeting level prerequisites for this feat, your level is equal to half your level.
requirements.what: A second filter on that same picker: level prerequisites are checked against half the character's level, not their real level. The text states no rounding, so nothing about rounding should be invented here.

requirements.clause: This proficiency and feat last until you make your daily preparations again.
requirements.what: Both the granted rank and the granted feat are temporary — they expire at, and are re-chosen at, the next daily preparations, and the previous day's pair must be dropped rather than accumulating. While active, both must be visibly marked as temporary where they are read.

requirements.clause: Since the proficiency is temporary, you can't use it as a prerequisite for any permanent character option.
requirements.what: The temporary rank has to be distinguishable from a permanent one, so that prerequisite gating for permanent options does not count it — while the one skill feat this feat itself grants explicitly DOES count it. At minimum this restriction is printed where the temporary rank is shown; anywhere prerequisites are checked against skill rank, the temporary rank must be excluded.

requirements.clause: You can sense living creatures and any creature with the electricity trait as an imprecise sense with a range of 20 feet.
requirements.what: A new sense in the senses list carrying all three of its facts: that it is IMPRECISE, that its range is 20 feet, and what it detects — living creatures and creatures with the electricity trait. It is not a general-purpose sense; its subject matter has to be readable on the entry, because that restriction is the whole point of it.

requirements.clause: This range doubles while you are underwater, though only in the body of water you're in.
requirements.what: The range is conditional, so the sense entry needs a `*` carrying the condition and the alternative value: 40 feet while you are underwater, and only within the body of water you occupy. Q7's shape — a value that depends on circumstance needs the player to see WHEN it applies, since a bare number cannot convey it.

requirements.clause: Choose either the gale blast or spout cantrip.
requirements.what: A builder choice between exactly two named options — gale blast or spout — with each option's details readable at the point of choosing. Unpicked shows as an empty slot that opens those two options and nothing wider.

requirements.clause: You can cast the chosen spell as a primal innate spell at will.
requirements.what: The chosen cantrip appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell with the primal tradition legible on the entry itself, its details reachable, and this feat named as the granting source. Per Q12 the sheet must not state a tradition this spell does not have — whatever pooling or grouping is used, primal must be what the player reads beside this spell.

requirements.clause: at will
requirements.what: No use count. The entry must read as unlimited — no per-day pip, no spendable resource, nothing consumed on casting and nothing to restore at daily preparations. This is the explicit opposite of the ordinary once-per-day innate grant, so the absence of a use track is itself the requirement.

requirements.clause: A cantrip is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: No new requirement — this restates the general cantrip rule that applies to every cantrip everywhere. The only thing it implies is that the grant be recorded as a CANTRIP rather than as a fixed-rank innate spell, so the standing rule reaches it and the entry shows its current heightened rank and heightened values; that is already covered by the innate-spell requirement above.

requirements.clause: Touch of the Sea Source High Seas pg. 19
requirements.what: No requirement. Title and source-citation boilerplate captured in the text field, not mechanical prose.

A new unarmed Strike named Magma Spike must appear in the strikes list, carrying its traits (agile, finesse, unarmed), its weapon group (brawling), and its damage as two instances on one Strike — 1d4 piercing plus 1 fire. Being unarmed, it must ride the character's unarmed attack proficiency and pick up handwraps runes like any other unarmed attack.
requirements.clause: You gain a magma spike unarmed attack ... This is an agile, finesse, unarmed attack in the brawling weapon group that deals 1d4 piercing damage, as well as 1 fire damage.

requirements.what: The Strike entry must state that it needs a free hand to use. The app cannot know what the character is holding, so this is printed on the Strike the player is looking at rather than gating whether the Strike exists.
requirements.clause: which requires a free hand to use

requirements.what: This Strike's critical specialization must REPLACE the brawling group's normal crit-spec effect rather than sit beside it (Ruling G — a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades), and must show the substitute: 1d6 persistent fire damage plus a bonus equal to the character's own item bonus to unarmed attack rolls. That addend is computed from the player's own gear, so the resolved number has to be legible where the crit-spec effect is read — a bare "1d6 persistent fire" understates it. The persistent damage arriving on the target is not itself a sheet surface.
requirements.clause: Instead of the normal critical specialization effect, the target takes 1d6 persistent fire damage; you gain a bonus on this persistent damage equal to your item bonus to attack rolls on unarmed attacks.

requirements.what: The feat is a triggered ability and must appear in the character's action list at the cost it carries, with its Trigger (you attempt a skill check requiring three actions or fewer) and its Frequency shown in the popup. Per Principle E that is often the whole surface of such an entry.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour **Trigger** You attempt a skill check requiring three actions or fewer.

requirements.what: One spendable use, refreshing hourly: a use displayed on the ability, consumed when used, and the hourly period stated. The period is neither daily preparations nor per encounter, so the sheet must at minimum print "once per hour" beside the use rather than silently treating it as a daily resource.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour

requirements.what: A `*` on every skill, carrying "+2 status bonus, once per hour, when you attempt a skill check of three actions or fewer". The clause names no particular skill and nearly every skill action costs three actions or fewer, so Rulings C and H apply — star every skill that could be the triggering check, with the printed trigger in the note, rather than narrowing it to a guess. Being a status bonus, it must be able to lose to a larger status bonus sharing the same `when`.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 status bonus to the triggering skill check.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. It is a one-round effect, which Q1 settles as indication only, and emitted light is not a sheet stat. The sentence belongs in the ability's popup text and nowhere else.
requirements.clause: In addition, your circuitry glows, lighting a with dim light for 1 round.

requirements.what: Trained proficiency in primal spell attack rolls and primal spell DC, shown on the spellcasting proficiency rows. The character may hold no primal spellcasting other than the innate spell this feat grants, so the proficiency must be able to exist on its own; and where a higher primal rank already exists the grant must not lower it (Q10 — apply the remap only when it makes the player better).
requirements.clause: You become trained in primal DCs and spell attack rolls.

requirements.what: The fey creature trait must be recorded on the character, per Q6 (acquired creature traits go on the sheet, where the Details tab carries tags). Flagging that the lane manual has no key for acquired creature traits; I am naming this lane `trait`.
requirements.clause: You gain the fey trait

requirements.what: A choice of exactly one of eight named features — Anteater, Cat Sith, Cursed Bluebird, Dryad, Faun, Gremlin, Monarch, Unicorn — with each option's own description surfaced at the point of choosing, and the chosen feature named on the sheet afterwards.
requirements.clause: and one of the following features ... - **Anteater** ... - **Unicorn** ...

requirements.what: The chosen option grants one named innate spell of the primal tradition, which must appear on the Spells page as an innate primal spell at the spell's own rank with its granting option named: Grim Tendrils (Anteater), Pest Form (Cat Sith), Ill Omen (Cursed Bluebird), Summon Plant or Fungus (Dryad), Fleet Step (Faun), Bane (Gremlin), Spider Sting (Monarch), Heal (Unicorn). Cat Sith's restriction — cat only — must ride with the Pest Form entry, since the spell itself offers more forms than this grant allows.
requirements.clause: which grant an innate primal spell ... gaining Grim Tendrils / Pest Form (cat only) / Ill Omen / Summon Plant or Fungus / Fleet Step / Bane / Spider Sting / ... cast Heal

requirements.what: One use per day on whichever innate spell was chosen: a single spendable use displayed beside the innate entry, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: an innate primal spell that can be used once per day

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT — no sheet surface. It governs which ancestry-feat slot the feat may legally fill, which is builder eligibility (Q9 — the builder shows only what the player may legally pick); a trait acquired by the FEAT rather than by the character, like prerequisite and access wording, is not a lane.
requirements.clause: **Special** This feat gains the trait appropriate for your ancestry (human for human, goblin for goblin, etc.)

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. An access clause gates nothing on the sheet (Q5 — access wording needs nothing), and access lines are named in the NOT-lanes list.
requirements.clause: **Access** You are an automaton or are otherwise from the ancient Jistka Imperium.

requirements.what: A `*` on all three saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — carrying "+1 status vs magic" (Q2: when a bonus applies to saves generally, star all three). Because the bonus is restricted to saves against magic it must NOT be folded into the flat save totals; it sits outside the total with the restriction in its `when` (Ruling B).
requirements.clause: You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against magic

requirements.what: The magical trait must be added to every Strike the character's dynamo provides, and must be visible on those Strike entries — magical is load-bearing against resistance to non-magical damage. The dynamo and its Strikes are granted by ANOTHER record, so this change has to be reflected in that granted thing rather than stated only in this feat's own text (Principle C, the `modifiesGrant` shape).
requirements.clause: and your dynamo Strikes become magical

requirements.what: A marker on the Wall Jump action entry itself, saying this feat lets it be used off creatures larger than you as if they were walls. Wall Jump is granted by another record, so the extension must reach that entry — Q8 and Ruling D: mark the action the feat modifies, because the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters.
requirements.clause: You can use Wall Jump to make additional jumps off of creatures larger than you as if they were walls.

requirements.what: Shove and Trip must each appear under a free-action cost in addition to their native cost, with the enabling condition (immediately after an additional Wall Jump off a creature) explained in the popup — Principle H, the Quick Recognition shape of an action listed under both costs. The Shove/Trip outcome lands on the creature and needs no further surface.
requirements.clause: you can also attempt to Shove or Trip that creature as a free action

requirements.what: The once-per-turn cap must be printed with that free action. It is a per-turn frequency, not a per-day or per-hour resource, and the app does not keep a turn clock (the same basis Q1 gives for not implementing one-round effects), so this is text in the popup rather than a spendable use.
requirements.clause: Once per turn when you make an additional jump off of a creature in this way
Aldori dueling swords you're wielding gain the parry trait.
requirements.what: Every Aldori dueling sword the character wields carries the parry trait, added by this feat rather than printed on the weapon. The trait must arrive functionally, not as a cosmetic label — the parry usage and the +1 circumstance AC the trait itself confers must follow from it, exactly as they would on a weapon that ships with the trait. It must apply to any Aldori dueling sword the character picks up, not to one recorded copy.

requirements.clause: If you have your other hand or hands free while wielding an Aldori dueling sword, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC while parrying instead of the usual +1.
requirements.what: A conditional +2 circumstance bonus to AC in the AC breakdown, whose `when` carries the full printed condition — while parrying, wielding an Aldori dueling sword, other hand or hands free. Two things make this more than a flat bonus: (a) per Ruling G it REPLACES the parry trait's usual +1 rather than sitting beside it, so the player must never see +1 and +2 listed together; (b) the app cannot know whether a hand is free or whether the player has spent the action to parry, so per Ruling H the condition stays printed and open rather than being narrowed into a computed test.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wielding only an Aldori dueling sword.
requirements.what: No separate sheet surface. This is a restriction, and per Ruling B a restriction lives in the `when` of the entry it limits — here the AC entry above and the feat's own popup. Note the tension worth carrying in the printed text rather than resolving: the requirement says ONLY an Aldori dueling sword, while the +2 clause presumes a free hand, and the trait-granting sentence carries no 'only' at all. Ruling H says stay open — print all three as written; do not pick a reading.

requirements.clause: Whenever you critically hit using a glaive, greatclub, hatchet, scythe, sickle, or ghoran weapon, you apply the weapon's critical specialization effect.
requirements.what: Critical specialization becomes available on a named set of weapons, independent of whatever the character's class or proficiency would otherwise grant. The set is heterogeneous and both halves must be expressible: five specific weapons BY NAME (glaive, greatclub, hatchet, scythe, sickle) plus an open category, 'ghoran weapon' — the ancestry's own weapon set, which is membership-defined and will grow with new ghoran weapons, so a hardcoded five-name list is not sufficient. Per Ruling D the effect must be legible on the thing the player is looking at when it matters: the Strike entry for one of those weapons, showing that its crit spec effect applies and what that effect is.

requirements.clause: Whenever you critically hit ... you apply the weapon's critical specialization effect.
requirements.what: The 'whenever you critically hit' trigger needs no degree-of-success surface of its own. Firing on a critical hit is inherent to what critical specialization IS — a general rule already stated wherever crit spec is shown — and Q15 rules that a crit-triggered effect needs no implementation unless it is complicated. This one is not.

requirements.clause: With plenty of practice, the memories of previous fights from previous lives come flooding back.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing.

requirements.clause: When you use Hijack Undead, if the undead fails its save, it becomes your minion for 10 minutes. If it critically fails, it becomes your minion for 24 hours.
requirements.what: An indication ON the Hijack Undead action showing this feat has changed it, with the revised outcomes readable there — fail = minion 10 minutes, critical fail = minion 24 hours. This is Principle C ('a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing') and Principle A's shape: the number does not belong on your own stat rows, but the player must SEE that their own ability now behaves differently. Note the modification is to an action the character already holds from another record, so the requirement is a marker written onto an existing entry, not a new grant — and the marker must survive the case where the player reads Hijack Undead without ever opening this feat.

requirements.clause: it becomes your minion for 10 minutes ... it becomes your minion for 24 hours.
requirements.what: The minion outcome itself gets no sheet surface. It lands entirely on another creature, and the outcome is keyed to that creature's save result — both squarely inside DECIDED SCOPE ('effects on enemies ... rather than on your own sheet' is not a lane) and Q4's shape, where the entry is the whole surface. The 10-minute and 24-hour durations are text inside that entry, not a tracked timer; nothing on the character changes for their duration, so there is no mode to run and no resource to spend. The controlled creature is not a companion under the companion lane either — it is not gained, chosen, or statted by the character.

requirements.clause: You gain the Opportune Riposte reaction.
requirements.what: Opportune Riposte appears in the reactions list, with its trigger and any requirements shown in its popup. Per Principle E this is normally the whole requirement — a reaction that is present, triggered, and readable, with no further impact on any stat row. The internal steps of the reaction (making the Strike, the Disarm alternative) are performed by the player; only the reaction's existence is the lane.

requirements.clause: You gain the Opportune Riposte reaction.
requirements.what: The grant names an existing record, so it must RESOLVE to that record rather than to a stub bearing the same label. Everything the player needs — the printed trigger, the requirements line, the full text — belongs to Opportune Riposte itself and must travel from it; a locally re-typed summary would be a second copy that drifts. Nothing about the reaction is re-specified by this feat, so this feat contributes no text of its own beyond the source attribution.

requirements.clause: You've learned to riposte against ill-conceived attacks.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits.
requirements.what: A whole spellcasting entry sourced from the bard archetype: occult tradition, spontaneous casting from a repertoire, with its own spell slots, its own attribute and its own proficiency, kept distinct on the Spells page from any casting the character's class already provides (the second sentence proves the entry is separately identified — it speaks of 'a spell slot of a new rank FROM THE BARD ARCHETYPE'). ⚠ This sentence is elliptical: 'the benefits' is a cross-reference to the archetype's basic-spellcasting benefit block, which this text does not reproduce. So the level-by-level slot table cannot be derived from this feat's words and must come from the referenced block; do not treat this feat's text as the source of those numbers.

requirements.clause: Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the bard archetype
requirements.what: Spell slots that arrive at new ranks as the character levels, shown per rank, spendable and restored at daily preparations, and attributed to the bard-archetype entry rather than pooled with another class's slots. The arrival of a slot of a NEW rank must be a distinguishable event, because it is the thing that fires the repertoire pick below — gaining a second slot of a rank you already have does not.

requirements.clause: add a common occult spell of the appropriate rank, or another appropriate occult spell you learned or discovered, to your repertoire
requirements.what: One repertoire pick offered each time a new slot rank arrives — so a choice that recurs and is keyed to the rank, not a single pick at the moment the feat is taken. Per Q9 the picker shows only legal options: occult spells of that specific rank. The 'or another appropriate occult spell you learned or discovered' branch means the filter must not be a hard common-only cut — a non-common occult spell the character has otherwise learned or discovered stays selectable. The chosen spell must land in this archetype entry's repertoire and be castable from its slots. Per Principle K, re-choosing happens in the builder and needs no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day --- **Effect** You call out to The Godclaw to heal your allies.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a named, usable ability, so it must appear as an entry in the actions list carrying its full printed text — both the heal use and the raise-dead use — with the Frequency line shown in its popup (Principle E's shape: the entry plus its trigger/frequency/requirements is the surface). The text as printed carries no action-cost glyph for the ability itself (the ⟨3⟩ belongs to the Heal it casts), so the sheet must be able to hold an activity whose own cost the text does not state, rather than being forced to assert one.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day: a single tracked use displayed on the ability, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations. It must be ONE pool covering both branches — spending it on the mass Heal and spending it on the raise-dead option draw on the same use — because the text offers them as alternatives ("You can instead use this ability"), not as two frequencies.

requirements.clause: You cast the 3‐action version of Heal, heightened to a rank one lower than half your level rounded up.
requirements.what: Heal must be reachable and castable FROM this ability — the spell's own entry and details available where the ability is, not merely named in prose. Two things the text pins that a plain reference cannot carry: (a) the 3-action version specifically, so the variant must be selectable/fixed rather than left to the player to pick a cost; (b) the rank is a FORMULA off your own level — ⌈level ÷ 2⌉ − 1 — so the sheet must resolve and display the actual rank at the character's current level and re-resolve it every time the level changes. A stored fixed rank cannot express this (same shape as Wyrmling Flight's Speed-derived value, exemplar 8).

requirements.clause: You can select up to five creatures in the area to remain unaffected by the spell.
requirements.what: No requirement. A targeting decision made at the moment of use, landing on other creatures in the area; it changes no number of yours. It only has to remain readable inside the ability's text (Principle B — the record carries the full text including the parts nothing computes).

requirements.clause: You can instead use this ability to bring a creature within 30 feet that has died within the last round back from the dead. If you do, the creature is restored to 1 Hit Point and is Doomed 1.
requirements.what: No requirement beyond the entry itself. Everything here lands on ANOTHER creature — their Hit Points, their Doomed condition — which Ruling F puts off your sheet entirely, and HP never moves sheet stats in any case. The only thing owed is that this alternative use is legible as an alternative within the same entry, sharing the one daily use already required above.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** Another creature within 60 feet uses a linguistic effect in a language you understand. --- You bridge a language gap, repeating the message in a different language that you know.
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger printed in the popup (another creature within 60 feet uses a linguistic effect in a language you understand) and the effect text alongside it. Per Principle E this is the whole surface — this feat needs nothing else on the sheet.

requirements.clause: Choose a language you understand to repeat the message in.
requirements.what: No requirement. A pick made at the moment of use, from the languages the character already knows; it is not a build-time choice and nothing about it needs storing or offering in a picker.

requirements.clause: The linguistic effect counts as both languages, rather than only the language the triggering creature is using, potentially allowing it to affect a wider range of creatures.
requirements.what: No requirement. This alters someone else's effect and which creatures it can reach — it neither changes a number of yours nor lands on your sheet; the GM adjudicates the widened reach.

requirements.clause: As normal, you can translate normal speech without Spot Translate and without using a reaction, but this reaction allows you to apply the benefits of translation to spells and actions such as command or Demoralize.
requirements.what: No requirement. A clarification restating the general rule about ordinary translation and naming examples; it promises nothing mechanical of its own.

requirements.clause: Once per day for each target, you can spend 1 hour treating that target and attempt a Medicine check to remove a disease or the blinded, deafened, doomed, or drained condition.
requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list, carrying its 1-hour duration and the exact list of what it can remove (a disease, or blinded / deafened / doomed / drained). The activity's existence is the lane; the check itself is an internal step the player performs.

requirements.clause: Once per day for each target
requirements.what: The frequency is PER TARGET, not per character: the same day may see this used on several different creatures, once each. A single character-wide daily pip would be wrong — it would lock the player out after one use. Expressing this faithfully needs either a per-creature tally or, failing that, the frequency printed as text on the entry with no consumable resource attached. The requirement is that the sheet not model it as one daily use.

requirements.clause: attempt a Medicine check
requirements.what: ⚠ DERIVED, not owner-stated: a `*` on Medicine carrying this use, so the player meets it where they look up the number (Principle D / Q2 — star the skill as well as the action, for a use named after a skill). No number attaches; the star's text is the activity.

requirements.clause: Use the DC of the disease or of the spell or effect that created the condition. If the effect's source is an artifact, above 20th level, or similarly powerful, increase the DC by 10.
requirements.what: No requirement. The DC belongs to an outside effect the sheet cannot know — a disease, a spell, an artifact — and the +10 rider is explicitly GM adjudication ("or similarly powerful"). The text only has to stay readable in the activity's popup.

requirements.clause: When you throw an alchemical item with the bomb trait, its range increment increases to 60 feet
requirements.what: The range increment shown for a thrown bomb must read 60 feet, REPLACING the item's printed increment rather than sitting beside it (Ruling G — a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades). Critically it must be expressible by TRAIT and not by name: it applies to every alchemical item carrying the bomb trait, including ones bought or crafted after the feat is taken, so the sheet must be able to hold a rider scoped to "all items with trait X" rather than a per-item edit. The changed number must appear wherever the player reads the bomb's range — on the strike and on the item.

requirements.clause: you reduce any circumstance bonus to the target's AC from cover by 1
requirements.what: No requirement. This is a target-side number — the enemy's AC and their cover — which the DECIDED SCOPE names outright as getting no surface; the player tells the GM. The clause only needs to remain readable in the feat's own text (and in the note the flat-check clause already puts on bomb Strikes).

requirements.clause: you automatically succeed at the flat check when targeting a concealed creature
requirements.what: A `*` on your bomb Strikes — and reachable from the bomb items themselves — carrying the automatic success on the concealment flat check. This one changes a roll YOU make, so by Ruling D the mark lives on the thing being looked at when it matters. Note the shape: it is an automatic success, not a bonus, so there is no value to add anywhere; the requirement is that the sheet can attach a text-only conditional marker (no number) to a strike, scoped again by the bomb trait rather than to a named weapon.

requirements.clause: Your companions with a qualifying unarmed attack learn the Sweeping Tail activity.
requirements.what: The activity must land on the COMPANION's own sheet — its action list, its stat block — and not on the character's. Its absence from your own actions list is correct, not a defect (the companions ruling: a companion's gains mark the companion). It says "companions" plural, so it must reach every qualifying companion the character has, not just one.

requirements.clause: with a qualifying unarmed attack
requirements.what: The grant is CONDITIONAL on the companion possessing the right unarmed attack (a tail — the activity makes tail Strikes). So it must be expressible as a grant gated on the companion's own attack set: a companion without a tail attack does not learn it, and gaining such an attack later should make it appear. A flat unconditional grant to every companion would be wrong.

requirements.clause: **Sweeping Tail** ⟨2⟩
requirements.what: The granted activity carries a 2-action cost, displayed on the companion's entry alongside its text.

requirements.clause: This companion makes two tail Strikes against different creatures within its reach, increasing its multiple attack penalty as normal.
requirements.what: No requirement. These are the internal steps of the activity plus a restatement of the standing multiple-attack-penalty rule; the entry exists and the player performs it.

requirements.clause: On a hit, it pushes a target back 5 feet or 10 feet on a critical hit. This is forced movement.
requirements.what: No requirement. Forced movement applied to an enemy — off the sheet by decided scope. The text stays readable in the activity's popup on the companion.

Flavour only — describes shielding runes absorbing spell energy. It names no number, no trigger and no new capability; the wording is a restatement of what the granted focus spell does. Nothing is owed.
requirements.clause: You can create a number of powerful shielding runes that bolster your defenses against damaging spells by absorbing the worst of the energy to keep you safe.

requirements.what: Spellmaster's Ward must appear on the Spells page as a FOCUS spell, with this feat named as the source that granted it, its full description reachable from the entry, and casting it spending a point from the focus pool. A focus spell's rank rises with the caster, so the entry must show the rank it is actually cast at as a value derived from level, not a fixed rank frozen at the level the feat was taken.
requirements.clause: You gain the Spellmaster's Ward focus spell.

requirements.what: +1 to the MAXIMUM size of the focus pool, with the pool visible and its points spendable, and Refocus restoring toward the raised maximum. The sheet must express this as an increment contributed by this feat rather than a fixed pool size, because the pool is the sum of several such grants and is capped at 3; and if the character has no pool at all, taking this feat must bring one into existence.
requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

requirements.what: Flavour — the arcane-lens framing. No mechanics.
requirements.clause: You understand the common underpinnings of the four traditions of magic and magical essences, allowing you to understand them all through an arcane lens.

requirements.what: THREE substitutions, not one: Arcana may stand in for Nature, for Occultism, and for Religion. Each must be expressible as a RESTRICTED substitution, not a blanket one — it applies only to a skill action or skill feat that calls for that check because of the magic tradition involved, so the sheet must be able to carry the restriction alongside the substitution rather than silently replacing those three skills' modifiers everywhere. It must also reach actions supplied by SKILL FEATS the character owns, not only the base skill actions, so the substitution has to attach to the skill-check requirement generally rather than to a hand-listed set of actions. Because the substitution is conditional, the player has to see it where they look the number up: a marker on Nature, Occultism and Religion (and on Arcana) carrying the condition, so they know when the Arcana modifier is the one to roll.
requirements.clause: Whenever you use a skill action or a skill feat that requires a Nature, Occultism, or Religion check, depending on the magic tradition, you can use Arcana instead.

requirements.what: A separate second promise, and the easy one to miss. This clause REMOVES a penalty rather than granting a bonus, so it contributes no number of its own — it only matters if a wrong-tradition penalty or raised DC is ever imposed on an Arcana check in the first place, and per Ruling D the DC half gets no surface at all. What the sheet must be able to express is readable text on the thing being looked at: a marker on the Identify Magic action (and on Arcana) stating that the usual penalty and higher DC for using Arcana on non-arcane magic do not apply to you. If a wrong-tradition penalty IS modelled anywhere, this feat must suppress it for Arcana.
requirements.clause: If you would normally take a penalty or have a higher DC for using Arcana on other magic (such as when using Identify Magic), you no longer do so.

requirements.what: Flavour — calling on light to reveal what is hidden. No mechanics.
requirements.clause: You've learned to call upon light to reveal what is hidden.

requirements.what: Light of Revelation must appear on the Spells page as a focus spell with this feat named as its source, its full description reachable from the entry, and casting it spending a Focus Point. One wrinkle here that Spellmaster's Ward does not have: the text calls it a DEVOTION spell, which is the class-specific name for this focus spell category. Per Q12 the sheet must use whichever spelling leaves the player least confused — the entry has to be findable under the name the player's own class uses, while still behaving as a focus spell drawing on the focus pool.
requirements.clause: You gain the Light of Revelation devotion spell.

requirements.what: +1 to the maximum size of the focus pool, expressed as an increment from this feat (the pool is the sum of such grants, capped at 3), the pool visible with spendable points, and Refocus restoring toward the raised maximum. If the character has no pool yet, this feat must create one.
requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

requirements.what: Flavour — targeting pressure points. No mechanics.
requirements.clause: You carefully target a creature's pressure points to block its inner life force.

requirements.what: This feat IS an activity, so it must appear in the actions list as its own named entry carrying its action cost and its traits, with the full printed text in its popup. That is the whole surface. 'Make an unarmed Strike' is an internal step of the activity — the player performs it with an unarmed attack they already have — so it owes no separate strike, no new attack entry and no damage plumbing; only the activity's EXISTENCE is owed. The popup should make plain that the activity is performed with an unarmed Strike, since that is its precondition.
requirements.clause: Make an unarmed Strike.

requirements.what: Lands entirely on the target: persistent void damage and the Enfeebled 1 condition are the enemy's numbers, not yours, and the condition's end is tied to the persistent damage ending — an enemy-side duration. DECIDED SCOPE rules effects on enemies and enemy conditions off the sheet, and Q4 settles the shape: the entry's own text is the whole surface. Nothing further is owed. (Note the text as supplied omits the base persistent-damage amount — 'that creature takes damage' — so whatever the complete printed line is must be what the popup carries.)
requirements.clause: If it deals damage to a living creature, that creature takes damage and is Enfeebled 1 until the persistent damage ends.

requirements.what: A level-conditional value inside the activity's own text, and the third clause the reader is likely to stop before. No sheet number moves — the damage is enemy-facing — but the sheet must be able to express a value that changes at 18th level and show the player which line applies to them, so a character at 18th or higher is not reading 'the persistent void damage increases to 3d6' as hypothetical text sitting beside a lower base figure.
requirements.clause: If you're 18th level or higher, the persistent void damage increases to 3d6.

requirements.what: Flavour — your physiology responds well to first aid. No mechanics.
requirements.clause: Your physiology responds well to first aid.

requirements.what: A marker on the TREAT WOUNDS action carrying '+your level (circumstance) to the Hit Points you regain', value inline, `*` linking back to this feat. Three things the sheet must be able to express here: (a) the value is derived from the character's current level, not a number frozen when the feat was taken; (b) the bonus applies to the HIT POINTS REGAINED, not to the Medicine check — it must never be folded into the Medicine modifier, and per Ruling E healing moves no sheet stat, so this is a marker and not a bonus to any total; (c) it applies to healing you RECEIVE, so the wording must hold when an ally is the one performing the action on you. It is also gated on a SUCCESSFUL attempt.
requirements.clause: You gain a circumstance bonus to the number of Hit Points you regain equal to your level from a successful attempt to Treat your Wounds or use Battle Medicine on you.

requirements.what: The same clause names a SECOND action, and per Ruling C / Q2 the mark goes on every action that can perform it — so Battle Medicine needs its own marker, identical in substance: '+your level (circumstance) to the Hit Points you regain', derived from current level, on the healing rather than on the check, and worded for the case where an ally uses Battle Medicine on you. Marking only Treat Wounds would leave half the feat invisible at the place the player looks.
requirements.clause: …from a successful attempt to Treat your Wounds or use Battle Medicine on you.

requirements.what: A wholly separate second promise, and the one most likely to be missed after the healing bonus. It changes the DURATION of the temporary immunity that follows Battle Medicine — 1 hour instead of 1 day — and it is per-recipient ('that Battle Medicine'), i.e. it governs how soon you can benefit again, not how often you can act. The sheet must be able to express this as text on the Battle Medicine entry; hours and days are not tracked, so it contributes no number. But if the once-per-day immunity is ever modelled as a lockout or a per-day use, this feat must shorten that window rather than leave the action locked for the day.
requirements.clause: After you or an ally use Battle Medicine on you, you become temporarily immune to that Battle Medicine for only 1 hour, instead of 1 day.
When your spectral dragon shares your space, the status bonus to saves against sleep and paralysis increases to +2.
requirements.what: This feat writes nothing of its own — it edits a bonus ANOTHER record already granted (the spectral dragon's +1 status bonus to saves vs sleep and paralysis). Per principle C and ruling G, the sheet must express an UPGRADE that REPLACES the existing entry: wherever the +1 is displayed today, it must now read +2, not sit beside a second +1 star. The sheet therefore needs a way for one record to raise the value of another record's already-granted save bonus, and to show the result in one place so the player never has to add two stars together.

requirements.clause: When your spectral dragon shares your space, the status bonus to saves against sleep and paralysis increases to +2.
requirements.what: The bonus is doubly conditional — a positional condition (the dragon shares your space) the app can never evaluate, plus an effect-type condition (sleep, paralysis). Ruling M settles the positional half: a permanent star carrying the condition in its note, not a mode and not a positional model. Ruling H settles the placement: sleep is normally resisted by Will and paralysis by Fortitude, so the star stays open and goes on the saves that could plausibly be called for (Q2's shape — when it lands on saves rather than one named check, mark the saves themselves), with the printed trigger in the note. The value must not enter any save total.

requirements.clause: In addition, you can use Draconic Salvation if you succeeded or failed on your saving throw, not only if you critically failed.
requirements.what: A second, separate promise: it rewrites the TRIGGER of another granted record (the Draconic Salvation action). Per principle C and Q8, the change must be reflected in that thing — the Draconic Salvation entry's own trigger line and popup must read the widened condition (critical failure, failure, or success) rather than the printed critical-failure-only trigger. Nothing else is owed; the character sheet needs no new stat, and the substitution must be legible on the action itself, not as a loose note on this feat.

requirements.clause: Prerequisites Economy 14
requirements.what: No requirement. A prerequisite line, and prerequisites are explicitly not a mechanical lane. (Economy is a kingdom statistic, not a character statistic, so it is not even a character-sheet prerequisite the sheet could check.)

requirements.clause: The first time during a Kingdom turn in which you are forced to spend RP as the result of a failed skill check or a dangerous event, and that expense reduces you to 0 RP, you may instead reduce your RP to 1 and treat the expense as if it were paid in full.
requirements.what: No character-sheet requirement. Every noun in the clause belongs to the kingdom subsystem — Kingdom turn, Resource Points, a kingdom skill check, a dangerous event — and none of them is a statistic of the character whose sheet this is. The character gains no action, no resource, no bonus, and no roll. The 'first time during a Kingdom turn' frequency is a limit on the kingdom's own clock, not a per-day character resource, so it earns no use-tracking pip either. The feat's printed text, readable where the player took it, is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: At the start of your next Kingdom turn, roll 4 fewer Resource Dice than normal.
requirements.what: No character-sheet requirement. A delayed cost paid in Resource Dice, again a kingdom-sheet quantity. The clause does imply state carried from one Kingdom turn to the next (the kingdom must remember it liquidated), but that state lives on the kingdom, not on the character; nothing about the character's abilities, defences, skills, or actions changes.

requirements.clause: You can cast Mask of Terror on yourself as an innate spell once per day.
requirements.what: Mask of Terror must appear on the Spells page as an INNATE spell, with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source. The text names no rank, so the entry must read at the spell's own rank (4th) — a granted spell whose displayed rank drifts from the printed one is a lie about the spell. The text also names no tradition, so nothing here obliges a tradition; what it does oblige, by Q12's least-confused test, is that the entry must not assert a tradition this grant does not give it.

requirements.clause: You can cast Mask of Terror on yourself as an innate spell once per day.
requirements.what: A separate promise inside the same sentence, easy to read past: 'on yourself'. The base spell targets another creature; this grant narrows it to self only. That narrowing is mechanical and must be legible ON the granted spell entry (ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters), because a player reading the spell's own description would otherwise be told they can target any creature.

requirements.clause: once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use tied to this grant, displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when it is cast and restored at daily preparations. The sheet must distinguish a once-per-day innate grant from an at-will one.

requirements.clause: When you do, you appear as a skeletal lizardfolk ancestor, twisted in a way that inspires the deepest fears of those who observe you.
requirements.what: Nothing. Pure description of what the already-granted spell looks like when you cast it. It grants no disguise mechanic, no impersonation bonus, and no effect on your own statistics; the fear it inspires is the spell's own effect landing on observers, which by ruling F is not this sheet's problem.

requirements.clause: You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed.
requirements.what: A permanent +10-foot bonus folded into the land Speed total, carried with its BONUS TYPE (status), because the type is what decides whether it stacks with another status bonus to Speed. It must be attributable in the Speed's breakdown to this feat. It is unconditional, so per Q11 it is a passive bonus, not a mode, and per Q7 an unconditional speed change needs no star.

requirements.clause: When calculating your travel speed, this increases to a +20-foot status bonus.
requirements.what: A second promise, and the one most likely to be missed: the SAME bonus takes a different, larger value in one circumstance. The sheet must be able to express a conditional alternative value of an already-applied bonus — and per ruling G it REPLACES rather than adds, so travel speed carries +20 total, never +30. Concretely: either a travel/exploration speed figure that computes with +20, or, if no such figure is displayed, a `*` on Speed whose note gives the travel-speed value. What the sheet must not do is show only the +10 and leave the player to discover the travel clause in the feat text.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Deception and Occultism.
requirements.what: Two skill grants from one sentence: trained rank in Deception AND trained rank in Occultism, each reaching that skill's proficiency rank and therefore its modifier, with this feat attributable as the source.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: The sheet must be able to detect that one of the two grants above is redundant — another source already makes the character trained in Deception or in Occultism — and convert THAT grant, not both, into something else. Note it can fire twice: if the character is already trained in both, both grants convert. A redundancy that silently evaporates (the character simply gets less) is the failure mode this clause exists to prevent.

requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice
requirements.what: What the redundant grant converts INTO: an open choice of any skill, offered in the builder, resolving to trained rank in the picked skill. Per Q9 the picker must offer only what the player may legally take, and per principle K the re-choosing itself needs no sheet surface — only the resulting rank does.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Hag Lore.
requirements.what: A named feat granted outright, with its own parameter already decided — Hag Lore. So the sheet must express a grant that carries a pre-set selection: Additional Lore appears in the feat list with its details reachable, and NO Lore picker is offered, because the feat text has made the pick. The granted feat's own effects must then flow through as if taken normally, including its automatic rank advancement, rather than the grant stopping at the feat's name.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Hag Lore.
requirements.what: The visible consequence of that grant: Hag Lore appears as a Lore skill on the skills list with a real, rollable modifier. Because the rank comes from the granted feat's own advancement rather than from this feat, the sheet must let a second-order grant reach a skill row — a Lore that exists in name only, frozen at trained while the granted feat says it should climb, is the defect shape here.

requirements.clause: Your construct companion becomes an incredible construct companion.
requirements.what: The construct companion's advancement tier must be settable to "incredible", and every stat that tier changes must move on the COMPANION's own stat block. Per the standing companion ruling, a companion's numbers live on the companion, so this is a requirement against the companion record, not against any row of the character's sheet.

requirements.clause: Your construct companion becomes an incredible construct companion.
requirements.what: The upgrade edits something an EARLIER record already granted (the construct companion itself), so per Principle C the change must be reflected in that companion rather than existing only as text on this feat. It must also bind to the right creature: if the character holds more than one companion, the tier bump applies only to the construct one.

requirements.clause: You have rebuilt your creation once more. It is greater now, more than it once was. Soon, it shall be greater still.
requirements.what: Flavour, and — stated so a reader does not hunt for one — this feat owes the character's own sheet NOTHING. No stat, star, or note on the player's numbers; the entire mechanical payload is on the companion.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Occultism and Survival.
requirements.what: Two flatly named skills reach trained rank. No choice, no condition — both Occultism and Survival must be raised by this feat and show it as their source.

requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
requirements.what: A redundancy fallback that must fire per redundant skill: for each of Occultism/Survival the character is already trained in from another source, the grant converts into a free skill-of-your-choice pick. So the feat must be able to hold up to two open skill picks, and the fallback must detect training that arrives from any other source, not just from the two skills' own entries.

requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Jotunborn Lore.
requirements.what: The Additional Lore general feat is granted outright, with its Lore subject PRE-SET to Jotunborn Lore — the text fixes the subject, so no picker is offered for this instance (Principle K: nothing for the player to choose means nothing to surface as a choice). Whatever Additional Lore's own record grants must then run against that fixed subject, and "Jotunborn Lore" must exist as an addressable Lore skill so it can appear in the skills list.

requirements.clause: **Special** If you have the Sage Jotunborn heritage, you gain the Additional Lore feat a second time for a lore of your choice.
requirements.what: A second, heritage-gated instance of the same granted feat. Three things are needed: the grant must be conditional on holding the Sage Jotunborn heritage; the sheet must tolerate holding Additional Lore TWICE with different subjects (a duplicate grant that does not collapse into or overwrite the first); and this second instance, unlike the first, must offer a free choice of Lore subject, with its own progression applying to that second Lore independently of the Jotunborn one.
