requirements.clause: You can use the Aid reaction to grant a bonus to an ally's Reflex save.
requirements.what: A marker on the Aid reaction saying it can now target an ally's Reflex save, with this feat named as the source. This is Principle A applied exactly as to Lay on Hands (the ally gets the number, but the player must still SEE that their own ability has been widened) and Q8 (mark the action the feat modifies). It presumes Aid is an addressable record on the sheet that a marker can attach to.

requirements.clause: ...to grant a bonus to an ally's Reflex save.
requirements.what: The bonus itself lands on someone else, so it produces no number anywhere on this character's sheet — no star on your own Reflex save, no modifier. Ruling F, and explicitly NOT a defect. Note also that the text names no check for YOU to roll when Aiding a save, so under Ruling I nothing on your own skill list gets starred either.

requirements.clause: As usual for Aid, you need to prepare by using an action on your turn to encourage the ally.
requirements.what: Restates Aid's own standing rule, which the app already implements everywhere; it is worth carrying as text inside the marker's popup but owes no separate surface of its own.

requirements.clause: When you Refocus, you regain all your Focus Points instead of 1.
requirements.what: A real computed change: the amount Refocus restores becomes the character's whole focus pool rather than the default 1, so performing Refocus fills the pool to maximum at any pool size. This is a set/replace, not an addition — a +N to the restore amount would give the wrong answer for a 2- or 3-point pool.

requirements.clause: ...you regain all your Focus Points instead of 1.
requirements.what: The Refocus entry the player reads must state the new amount, and per Ruling G an upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it — so the default "regain 1 Focus Point" wording must not remain visible alongside it, with this feat named as the source of the change.

requirements.clause: You can use the Craft activity to create snares.
requirements.what: A marker on the Craft activity (and therefore on Crafting, the only skill that can perform it, per Ruling C) recording that this character may Craft snares. This is a permission clause of the same shape as Guerrilla Dedication's "you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check" — it is not restating a general rule, because snares are not craftable without it. It is also the authority that makes the granted formulas usable at all: under Q19 a feat's formulas are craftable when the feat's text says so, and this sentence is that statement.

requirements.clause: you add the formulas for four common 1st-level snares to your formula book
requirements.what: A builder picker of exactly FOUR picks, filtered to only what this feat legally allows — common rarity, snare, 1st level — never the whole item list (Q14 point 7, Q9). Until picked, the grants must show as empty slots that open that filtered selection when pressed (Q14 point 8).

requirements.clause: you add the formulas for four common 1st-level snares to your formula book
requirements.what: The four picks must land in the formula book as formula REFERENCES listed "<snare name> formula", never as item copies in inventory (Q14 points 1-2), and the write must be ONE-TIME: once chosen, the formulas belong to the book and are severed from this feat, so they are not re-derived from the owned feat and are lost for good if the book is lost (Q14 point 9). The clause also presumes a book exists to receive them — a character with none needs one (Q14 point 6). ⚠ The manual lists no lane for this; Q14 states the formula book itself still needs building, so this is a "no lane at all" case, not a promised-but-empty one.

requirements.clause: "Strike with an unarmed attack. If you hit and the target is a living creature, it takes an additional 4d6 damage, depending on its Fortitude save."
requirements.what: Siphon Life must appear in the actions list as its own named activity with its action cost, and its popup must carry the full printed text — including all four degree-of-success lines (crit success: no void damage + temporarily immune 1 minute; success: half; failure: full; crit failure: double). The 4d6 and the save land on the enemy, so no number reaches the player's sheet; the existence of the activity plus its readable text IS the requirement. "Strike with an unarmed attack" is an internal step the player performs — it is not a separate strike entry and must not become one.

requirements.clause: "If the target takes any void damage, you gain an equal number of temporary Hit Points, which last for 1 minute."
requirements.what: The temporary-HP clause must be legible in the action's popup. No computed value is owed: the amount equals damage the sheet never sees, and HP never moves sheet stats even inside a mode (Ruling E). ⚠ Open point I am flagging rather than deciding: Q1 would ordinarily give a one-minute effect a mode, but Q15 rules that temporary Hit Points alone are not complicated, so on my reading this earns text only, not a mode. If a mode is wanted for the 1-minute clock, it would be display-only and carry no numbers.

requirements.clause: "casting you in a deathlike pallor, chilling your body temperature to be ice-cold, turning your very blood black"
requirements.what: Nothing. This is appearance flavour. It names no acquired creature trait, no sense, no immunity and no stat, so Q6's record-the-trait rule is not triggered and nothing is owed.

requirements.clause: "When you Relinquish Control, you add Grapple, Reposition, Shove, and Trip to the list of actions you can take."
requirements.what: This feat changes what the Relinquish Control feature already grants, so it must be reflected IN that thing (Principle C, Q8): the Relinquish Control entry — and, if that relinquished state is carried as a mode, that mode's text — must show Grapple, Reposition, Shove and Trip as added to the permitted action list, attributed to this feat. It does not grant those four actions to the character generally; they are already universal, and the whole promise is the widened list on the other record.

requirements.clause: "You gain a +2 status bonus to the Athletics check to attempt these actions."
requirements.what: A restricted +2 status bonus, so it belongs in the situational lane with the printed restriction in its `when` (Ruling B) — it must NOT be added into the flat Athletics total. Per Q2 both surfaces are owed: a `*` on Athletics, and a `*` on each of Grapple, Reposition, Shove and Trip, each carrying "+2 status when attempting these actions while you have Relinquished Control". The scope of the restriction should be quoted from the text rather than narrowed by a ruling (Ruling H).

requirements.clause: "Make a beast gun Strike against a creature within the first range increment... you can continue to make Strikes against new targets in this same way until your attack misses, at which point your shot dissipates."
requirements.what: Controlled Bullet must appear in the actions list as a named activity with its action cost, and its popup must carry the full chaining text: first target within the first range increment, each new target within one range-increment distance of the previous target, no repeating a target already attacked this use, sequence ends on a miss. The chained Strikes are internal steps the player performs — the sheet owes their existence and their rules as text, not a generated row per bounce, and not a range or targeting model.

requirements.clause: "**Frequency** once per day"
requirements.what: One spendable use per day shown beside the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations, so the player can see whether it is still available.

requirements.clause: "Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you've made all your attacks."
requirements.what: A note on the action, printed in its popup: every Strike in the sequence uses the multiple attack penalty you had when you began, and the penalty only steps up once the activity is finished. ⚠ Worth flagging: unlike the chaining text, this clause really does change the numbers on the rolls — it suspends the standard MAP progression — but the sheet cannot know a Controlled Bullet sequence is in progress, so text on the action is the only honest surface. It is a deviation from a general rule, not a restatement of one, so it must not be dropped as boilerplate.

requirements.clause: "When you Change Shape, you can assume the shape of a priest or other religious official... While in your false priest form..."
requirements.what: A togglable False Priest Form state the player turns on and off, which must make plain it is active and what changed (Q11 — the form can be shut down, so it is a mode, not a passive bonus; Q3's visibility requirement). The mode carries the feat's full text (Principle B) and is what gates the substitution and the cantrips below. Duration is open-ended rather than one round, so Q1's indication-only carve-out does not apply.

requirements.clause: "When you Change Shape, you can assume the shape of a priest or other religious official from a religion of your choosing."
requirements.what: The Change Shape action this feat extends must itself show the new option (Principle C, Q8) — a marker on Change Shape naming the false priest form and pointing to this feat, so the player meets it where they look the action up rather than only in the feat list.

requirements.clause: "While in your false priest form, you can attempt Deception checks to Recall Knowledge about Religion"
requirements.what: While the mode is active, Deception can perform Recall Knowledge in Religion's place. Because it is state-gated it is a substitution with a `when`, not an unconditional one. Per Q2 both surfaces are owed: a `*` on Deception and a `*` on the Recall Knowledge action, each carrying "while in false priest form, Deception may Recall Knowledge about Religion", so the player sees it where they read the number.

requirements.clause: "you can cast Divine Lance and Haunting Hymn as primal innate cantrips"
requirements.what: Divine Lance and Haunting Hymn must reach the Spells page as innate cantrips — at-will, no per-day uses — with this feat named as the source and their availability tied to the form being active. The tradition must read PRIMAL as printed, even though both spells read as divine elsewhere; the sheet must not state something false about the spell (Q12), so the tradition has to be legible on these two entries specifically and not inferred from any pooled or majority tradition.

requirements.clause: "If you critically fail at a Deception check while in your false priest form, your transformation is broken... you can't resume your False Priest Form until your next daily preparations, after you've taken a night to sleep on it."
requirements.what: The break condition and the lockout must be printed inside the mode's own text, since the mode is what the player is looking at when it matters. Nothing is detected automatically — the sheet never sees a critical failure — so ending the form is the player switching the mode off. ⚠ I am not claiming a per-day counter here: the lockout is conditional, not a consumed resource, and only bites if the crit failure happens; on my reading text in the mode is the whole requirement.

requirements.clause: "...from a religion of your choosing."
requirements.what: Nothing. The religion is picked at the moment you Change Shape, differs from use to use, and drives no number — unlike Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location, which had mechanics hanging off it. It stays part of the action's text; no free-text field and no stored choice is owed.

requirements.clause: "Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks."
requirements.what: A builder pick offering ONLY that eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks (Q9 — the builder shows only what may legally be picked), recorded on the character. Ranged attacks and any attack that is not one of the eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks must not be offered.

requirements.clause: "It gains one of the following traits, chosen when you gain the feat: disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, or versatile bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing."
requirements.what: A second builder pick from exactly the nine listed options — disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, versatile bludgeoning, versatile piercing, versatile slashing — with the whole trait list, not a free choice of weapon traits. The text fixes it "when you gain the feat", so it is a permanent recorded pick; re-choosing is a builder action and needs no sheet surface (Principle K).

requirements.clause: "Your eidolon's attack evolves... It gains one of the following traits."
requirements.what: The chosen trait must land ON the chosen eidolon attack and be live there, not merely printed on the feat: the attack's entry shows the added trait, and a versatile choice actually offers that alternate damage type on that attack. Per the standing companion ruling this surfaces on the EIDOLON's stat block and attack entry — its absence from the summoner's own sheet is correct, not a gap, and no unpicked choice should leave the attack silently unmodified.

The activity must exist as its own entry in the actions list under its printed action cost, with its full text reachable from the entry's popup. Per the Minor Omen exemplar, for a feat of this shape the action entry IS effectively the whole surface.
requirements.clause: You can use your training in combat medicine to revive the recently deceased. Attempt a DC 40 Medicine check to revive a dead creature that has been dead for no more than 3 rounds.

requirements.what: All three requirements printed inside that action's popup: holding or wearing a Healer's Toolkit AND a free hand; the body mostly intact; not killed by a death effect. Nothing has to be evaluated — the app is not required to check whether a toolkit is held or a hand is free, only to show the condition where the player reads the action (Minor Omen: 'the Requirement needs to be writen in the pop up').
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are holding a Healer's Toolkit or are wearing one and have a free hand; the target's body is mostly intact; the target was not killed by a death effect.

requirements.what: Nothing. No star on Medicine. The check is an internal step of the activity and the feat grants no bonus to it; and a fixed SKILL DC gets no surface at all (Ruling D, DC-only clause — 'the player remembers'). Only a save DC would earn a breakdown entry.
requirements.clause: Attempt a DC 40 Medicine check

requirements.what: Nothing. Every outcome here lands on the target's sheet — their return to life, their wounded value stepping up by 1. Ruling F: an effect that affects someone else and not you produces no surface on your sheet; the record's own description already tells the player what happens.
requirements.clause: If you succeed, the target returns to life with the effects of Raise Dead, except it still has the wounded condition it had before dying, increased by 1 (or Wounded 1 if it wasn't wounded before dying).

requirements.what: Explicitly NOT limitedUses, and this is the easy misread. The frequency is per TARGET, not a per-day resource of yours — you may use it on a different creature a minute later. So no per-day pip, no usage counter, no daily-preparations reset on your sheet. The clause is text in the action's popup, and the immunity itself is tracked on the target.
requirements.clause: Whether you succeed or fail, the target is temporarily immune to Desperate Resuscitation for 1 day.

requirements.what: The Rage mode must carry this text. Rage is a state you turn on and off, so it is a mode (Q11 — if it can be shut down it is a mode), and a feat that modifies another record's granted thing has to be reflected IN that thing (principle C). The mode carries the full text even though the app computes no number from it (principle B).
requirements.clause: While you are raging, damage from your melee Strikes ignores the first 5 Hardness of an object.

requirements.what: A `*` on melee Strikes carrying 'ignores the first 5 Hardness of an object (while raging)'. Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and when you swing at a door you are looking at the Strike. Hardness belongs to the object, so no number on your own sheet moves — the marker is the entire numeric surface, and it must be conditioned on raging.
requirements.clause: While you are raging, damage from your melee Strikes ignores the first 5 Hardness of an object.

requirements.what: The displayed figure must be derived from whether the character owns the Devastator class feature, and when they do it must read 10 REPLACING the 5, not sitting beside it (Ruling G — a set or upgrade replaces the entry it upgrades). Both surfaces above have to show the upgraded number, so the value cannot be a hardcoded 5 in either the mode text or the strike marker.
requirements.clause: If you have the Devastator class feature, the damage instead ignores the first 10 points Hardness of an object.

requirements.what: A builder choice offering exactly two options — Asterism and Touch of the Moon — each option itself granting its focus spell (effectGrant). Q9 governs the list: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, so no other domain spell may appear here.
requirements.clause: You gain your choice of the Asterism or Touch of the Moon domain spell.

requirements.what: The chosen spell reaches the Spells page as a FOCUS spell (a domain spell), with this feat named as its granting source and its full description reachable from the entry. ⚠ FLAGGED, not asserted: PF2e's general rule increases the focus pool by 1 when a feat grants a focus spell, but this text does not say so and I am judging only from the text — so I am not claiming a focusPool requirement here.
requirements.clause: You gain your choice of the Asterism or Touch of the Moon domain spell.

requirements.what: The feat must be takeable a SECOND time rather than being blocked as already owned, and the second instance's pick must depend on the first: it offers only the spell not already gained, or simply grants it. This is a pick whose content is determined by an earlier pick, and both spells must end up on the Spells page for a character who took it twice.
requirements.clause: **Special** You can take this feat a second time, gaining the focus spell that you didn't gain the first time.

requirements.what: A climb Speed of 10 feet in the speeds list. Flat, unconditional and not derived from your land Speed, so it takes NO `*` — Q7 reserves the star for a conditional speed like Wyrmling Flight's, and rules that most granted speeds are permanent and need no star.
requirements.clause: You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.

requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour. In particular it does NOT grant a claw unarmed Strike — it presumes claws the character already has from another source, and names no damage die, no traits and no damage type, so there is nothing here to build a strike from.
requirements.clause: You can extend your claws to aid you in climbing.

requirements.what: Nothing on the sheet. This is a downtime procedure the GM adjudicates; the check is an internal step of it with no bonus attached, and a fixed skill DC gets no surface (Ruling D, DC-only). No star on Nature from this clause.
requirements.clause: You can spend 7 days of downtime regularly interacting with a normal animal (not a companion or other special animal) that is friendly or helpful to you. After this duration, attempt a DC 20 Nature check against the animal's Will DC.

requirements.what: The sheet must be able to hold a bonded animal: a named creature attached to the character, listed among its companions, carrying its own stat block — the later clauses read the animal's LEVEL and write a trait onto it, so a bare text label is not enough. Per the standing companion ruling, anything the animal owns or gains belongs to the animal's own record and inventory, never to the character's.
requirements.clause: If successful, you bond with the animal. The animal is permanently bonded to you until you form a bond with a different animal or do something egregious to break your bond.

requirements.what: The minion trait recorded on the BONDED ANIMAL's record, not on the character's Details tab, and gated on that animal's level. This is a trait acquired by the companion, so the companion ruling puts it on the companion's stat block.
requirements.clause: A helpful animal is easier to direct. If your bonded animal is level –1, it gains the minion trait, allowing you to command it more efficiently.

requirements.what: A value derived from the character's NATURE proficiency rank — maximum minion level −1 below master, 3 at master, 11 at legendary — shown on the bonded-animal entry and re-derived when the rank changes, since it is the number that tells the player which animals still qualify. It is not a bonus to Nature checks, so it takes no star on the Nature skill: the mark goes on the thing affected (principle J / Ruling D).
requirements.clause: The maximum level of creature that can be your minion increases to 3 if you're a master in Nature and to 11 if you're legendary.

requirements.what: The bonded animal must be replaceable and removable — swapping to a new animal clears the old bond. Whether the bond breaks through misconduct is GM adjudication and needs no model; the only requirement is that the record can be swapped or cleared. Per principle K the swap is a builder action and earns no sheet surface of its own.
requirements.clause: …until you form a bond with a different animal or do something egregious to break your bond.

requirements.what: A mutual exclusion the builder must enforce: a character who has an animal companion may not take a bonded animal, and vice versa — while pets and familiars are explicitly NOT excluded and must remain available alongside it. Q9: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick.
requirements.clause: **Special** You can't have both a bonded animal and an animal companion (though you can have both a bonded animal and a pet or familiar).
**Trigger** Your turn begins. --- Your apparition takes over and shields you from outside influence.
requirements.what: The feat is a triggered activity and must appear in the actions list at whatever cost the record carries, with the trigger text "Your turn begins" shown in its popup (principle E). Because everything else the feat does happens only after it is used, this entry is the anchor the rest of the requirements hang off.

requirements.clause: Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +4 status bonus on saves against spells and effects that give you the controlled condition or attempt to influence your actions (such as Charm, Command, or a nosoi's haunting melody).
requirements.what: A `*` on the saving throws carrying "+4 status vs. effects that control you or influence your actions", with the trigger and the until-start-of-your-next-turn duration in its note. The duration is exactly one round, so Q1 governs: indication only, no mode and no number folded into any save total. The text names no single save, so Ruling H applies — star all three saves rather than narrowing it to Will, which would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: However, the only actions you can take are to Recall Knowledge, Step, Strike, Cast an apparition Spell, Cast a vessel Spell, Sustain a vessel spell, or use an action that has the apparition trait.
requirements.what: The restriction list must be legible in the triggered action's popup and in the note attached to the save star, because the bonus and the cost are one bargain and a player shown only the +4 is seeing half the clause. The app cannot enforce which actions the player takes — this is text the player reads and honours (principle B's shape: carry the full text including the part that cannot be computed).

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all Recall Knowledge checks made using Lore skills granted by your attuned apparitions.
requirements.what: A `*` on each Lore skill currently granted by an attuned apparition, carrying "+2 circumstance on Recall Knowledge". This clause sits outside the one-round duration and is permanent, so unlike the save bonus it is a standing star. The set of starred Lores is not fixed at build time — it must resolve against whichever apparitions are attuned right now, so the star has to follow the attunement rather than a hardcoded skill list. Ruling B: a bonus the rules restrict to one kind of check lives in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, never in a flat skill total.

requirements.clause: **Special** This feat requires a particularly strong bond with a specific apparition to learn. Choose one apparition you have access to.
requirements.what: A pick of one apparition made when the feat is taken, offering only apparitions the character actually has access to (Q9). The pick must be recorded and readable, since the Lore star above and the daily lock below both depend on knowing which apparition was named.

requirements.clause: once you learn this feat, you must always choose that apparition as one of the apparitions you attune to each day
requirements.what: The daily apparition attunement must reflect the chosen apparition as an always-included, non-removable selection — one of the day's attunement slots is spoken for by this feat. This is a constraint the feat imposes on a choice another record owns, so principle C applies: it has to be visible in the attunement picker itself, not only in this feat's text, or the player meets it as a rule to remember rather than a slot they can see is filled.

requirements.clause: While you're in Arcane Cascade stance, you ignore difficult terrain caused by water, such as walking along a flooded path or swimming in rough water.
requirements.what: The Arcane Cascade stance is the record this feat modifies, so its mode must carry this clause and show it while the stance is on (principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). A player reading Arcane Cascade while the stance is active has to see the water-terrain clause there; a note living only on this feat's own entry does not satisfy it, because the stance is what they are looking at when it matters.

requirements.clause: you ignore difficult terrain caused by water
requirements.what: No number is owed. Terrain cost is not a sheet stat and no Speed value changes, so this contributes text to the stance and nothing else (principle B — a mode carries the full text of what it does, including the parts that produce no computation). This feat requires nothing beyond the entry above.

requirements.clause: You gain the critical specialization effects of the battle axe, hatchet, longsword, and shortsword.
requirements.what: Critical specialization must be active on strikes made with those four specific weapons — battle axe, hatchet, longsword, shortsword — and the effect must be readable from the strike itself, since that is where the player is standing when a crit lands. The grant is per-named-weapon, not per-group and not blanket, so a character wielding an axe that is not one of the four must not show it.

requirements.clause: Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency rank in the above four weapons.
requirements.what: The four named weapons must track the character's class-granted weapon proficiency at expert or better — a derived rank, not a fixed one. It has to re-evaluate as the character levels, because the class feature that triggers it arrives later than the feat, and the resulting rank must reach the attack bonus on strikes with those four weapons rather than merely being listed. The clause is worded as a floor keyed to expert-or-greater, so a character whose class already gives those weapons a higher rank keeps the higher one (Q10 — apply a remap only when it makes the player better).

requirements.clause: Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 198 Archetype Viking Prerequisites Viking Weapon Familiarity
requirements.what: Nothing owed. Source, archetype tag and prerequisite lines are not mechanical clauses.

requirements.clause: If the next action you use is to cast Harm or Heal to damage one creature…
requirements.what: The feat is an activity the player spends immediately before casting, so it must appear in the actions list with its cost and its full text in the popup. The entire feat is conditioned on "the next action you use", so a player who cannot find and use the thing has no route to any of its effects.

requirements.clause: If the next action you use is to cast Harm or Heal to damage one creature…
requirements.what: A marker on the Harm spell and on the Heal spell showing this feat modifies them (Q8 — Ruling D's shape applies: mark the action the feat modifies; the same shape the owner specified for Lay on Hands in the gold set). A player reading Harm on the Spells page must see that Cast Down exists and applies to it; naming Harm and Heal only inside the feat's own text puts the information where they are not looking when they cast.

requirements.clause: the target is knocked prone if it takes any damage from the spell
requirements.what: No requirement. The condition lands on the enemy, which DECIDED SCOPE settles as not this sheet's problem — the feat's own text already tells the player what happens, and Q4 makes the action entry the whole surface for an enemy-condition effect.

requirements.clause: If the target critically fails its save against the spell, it also takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 minute.
requirements.what: No requirement. Doubly excluded: it is an enemy-side number (a penalty to the target's Speed, which the app does not model), and it fires on a degree of success, which Q15 exempts unless the effect is complicated — a flat Speed penalty is not. Nothing is owed beyond the sentence being readable in the popup.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** An ally benefiting from one of your composition spells is subject to an effect with the auditory, illusion, linguistic, sonic, or visual trait.
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list with that trigger shown in its popup (principle E). The trigger's trait list — auditory, illusion, linguistic, sonic, visual — must be legible there, because it is the whole test for whether the player may use the reaction.

requirements.clause: All allies affected by your composition spell gain your +1 circumstance bonus from Well-Versed until the start of your next turn.
requirements.what: No number on this character's sheet — the bonus goes to allies (Ruling F). But principle A still applies: an indication on the record this feat modifies, which here is the Well-Versed class feature and, since the reaction rides on them, the composition spells. The marker says this feat can extend Well-Versed to allies; the value itself stays off the sheet.

requirements.clause: your personal circumstance bonus from Well-Versed also increases to +2 until the start of your next turn
requirements.what: This half is the character's own number, so it must be visible — but it lasts until the start of your next turn, one round, which Q1 settles as indication only: no mode, no computed change to any save total. The indication belongs on the existing Well-Versed star, so that where the player reads "+1 circumstance vs. auditory/illusion/linguistic/sonic/visual" they also read that this feat can raise it to +2 for a round. Per Ruling G it reads as an upgrade of that entry rather than a second star sitting beside it, and it must appear wherever Well-Versed's bonus is starred — all three saves, since the text names no single save (Q2, Ruling H).

requirements.clause: You gain the appropriate qi spell for your School of Perfection: Unblinking Flame Revelation for Unblinking Flame, Unbreaking Wave Advance for Unbreaking Waves, Unfolding Wind Rush for Unfolding Wind, or Untwisting Iron Buffer for Untwisting Iron.
requirements.what: One focus spell must appear on the Spells page as a focus spell with its details reachable and this feat named as the source. WHICH of the four it is is not a choice the player makes here — it is determined by an earlier pick (the character's School of Perfection), so the sheet must resolve the grant off that earlier selection and offer no picker. Four possible outcomes, exactly one live at a time; if the school is unset the grant must be visibly unresolved rather than silently absent.

requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.
requirements.what: +1 to the maximum size of the focus pool, feeding the pool's displayed maximum and the number of points restored by Refocus. Nothing else is owed — the 3-point cap is a general rule the sheet applies everywhere, not a promise of this text.

requirements.clause: you can focus to temporarily attain a perception beyond the ordinary. A lightless flame appears in the center of your forehead. For 1 minute...
requirements.what: The activity must exist as an entry in the character's actions list, with its frequency and its 1-minute duration readable in its popup. This is the surface the player looks at to use the feat at all.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: A single spendable use displayed with the activity, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: For 1 minute, you gain the benefits of a See the Unseen spell.
requirements.what: A duration longer than 1 round, so per Q1 this is a mode the player turns on and off, and per Q3's shape it must be plain that the mode is running. The mode carries See the Unseen's benefit as text reachable from the mode entry (the feat grants the spell's BENEFITS, not the spell — so nothing is owed on the Spells page). It moves no number of its own; per Ruling E case 3 a display-only mode is the correct outcome if the referenced benefit changes no stat.

requirements.clause: when you attempt a Strike during this time against a creature about which you could Recall Knowledge using Occultism or Religion, the attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being concealed or hidden
requirements.what: A `*` on Strikes carrying this clause, live while the mode is active. It contributes no number: whether it applies depends on the target (could you Recall Knowledge about it with Occultism or Religion?) and on penalties that come from the target's condition, none of which the sheet knows — so per Principle B the mode/star carries the full printed text and computes nothing. Two separate promises inside the one clause (circumstance penalties to the attack roll; the concealed/hidden flat check) must both survive into the text.

requirements.clause: When you use Shield Wallop, after its other effects, the target attempts a saving throw against your class DC.
requirements.what: Per Principle C, this feat changes what ANOTHER record granted, so the change must be reflected in that thing: the Shield Wallop action's own entry must show that it now forces a save, and the added save and its outcomes must be readable there — not only in this feat's description. The save is against your class DC, a stat the sheet already carries; naming it in the action's popup is the whole of that sub-clause.

requirements.clause: If your shield is a tower shield, fortress shield, or another shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus to AC when you Take Cover behind it, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to this saving throw.
requirements.what: The conditional –2 is a penalty to the TARGET's roll, so no number lands on your sheet; it must appear as text on the Shield Wallop entry, including its condition (the shield you are wielding). Note the condition is about your own equipment, so the text must state it rather than assume it — the open-ended "or another shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus when you Take Cover" is a Ruling H case: stay open, print the trigger.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The target takes no additional effect. **Success** The target is off-guard to you until the end of the current turn. **Failure** The target is knocked prone. **Critical Failure** The target is knocked prone and Stunned 1.
requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the four outcomes being readable in the action's popup. Every outcome is a condition on the enemy (off-guard, prone, stunned), which DECIDED SCOPE places off your sheet, and Q4 settles the shape: the action entry is the whole surface. No degree-of-success stat, no condition tracking on your side.

requirements.clause: When you gain this feat, select a common 1st-level mutagen.
requirements.what: A one-time builder pick recorded on the character, whose picker is filtered to exactly what the text allows — common rarity, 1st level, mutagen — per Q9 ("the builder shows only what the player may legally pick"). This is a builder-side restriction on a CHOICE, not the Q5 shop-access case, so the filter is genuinely owed. Per Principle K, re-choosing it needs no sheet surface.

requirements.clause: Each day during your daily preparations, you can make one temporary vial of the selected mutagen.
requirements.what: At daily preparations the character gains one vial of the chosen mutagen as a usable consumable, quantity 1, that behaves as that item does (drinkable, carrying the mutagen's own benefit and drawback). It is produced automatically from the recorded pick — the player chooses nothing at prep time, only whether to make it.

requirements.clause: It dissipates by your next daily preparations if not consumed.
requirements.what: The vial must be temporary: it is cleared at the next daily preparations whether or not it was used, and it must not stockpile into a second vial. A permanent inventory copy would be wrong.

requirements.clause: If the mutagen has multiple versions (such as a greater version), your mutagen automatically becomes this higher-level version when your level equals the mutagen's level.
requirements.what: The vial produced must be DERIVED from character level, not frozen at the picked item: it resolves to the highest-level version of that mutagen's family whose item level is at or below the character's level, changing by itself as the character levels with no re-pick and no builder prompt. The stored pick names the family; the level chooses the version.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not immediately killed.
requirements.what: A triggered ability, so per Principle E it appears in the reactions list with its trigger printed in its popup. That entry is where the player reads the whole effect. Its access line (chrysanthemum leshy heritage) is a prerequisite and is not itself a lane.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: A single spendable use shown on the reaction, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: Your ally avoids being knocked out and remains at 1 Hit Point, and their wounded condition increases by 1
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the reaction's own description. The rescue and the ally's wounded land entirely on someone else's sheet (Ruling F/N), and Hit Points never move sheet stats in any case. No star, no modifier, no number.

requirements.clause: ...as does your own.
requirements.what: THE ONE SELF-FACING PROMISE, and it is hidden at the end of an ally-facing sentence: using this reaction raises YOUR OWN wounded condition by 1. The reaction's entry must state this cost explicitly so it is not read as a purely altruistic ability, and the sheet must be able to express the resulting wounded value on the character — the effect lands on a condition the player carries, not on the ally.

No requirement. An access clause names who may take the feat; per the NOT-lanes list (prerequisites and access clauses) and Q5 ("item rarity does not gate the shop" — access clauses need nothing), it produces no sheet surface.
requirements.clause: **Access** You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.

requirements.what: An immunity entry on the defences list reading as a QUALIFIED immunity — "splash damage from your own Strikes with bombs and firearms" — not a bare damage-type keyword. The expressiveness demand is the qualifier: the sheet must be able to carry an immunity whose scope is a source (my own bomb/firearm Strikes) rather than a damage type, because an entry rendered as plain "immune to splash damage" would state something false — it would read as immunity to every bomb thrown at the character, including an enemy's. The parenthetical ("such as the splash damage from the scatter trait") is an example, not a second grant, and needs no separate surface. Nothing is owed on the Strikes themselves: this has a stat row of its own (the immunities list), so Ruling D's "attach it to the thing it modifies" does not apply.
requirements.clause: You are immune to splash damage caused by your own Strikes with bombs and firearms (such as the splash damage from the scatter trait).

requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so Venom Purge must appear as an entry in the character's actions list, with its full text reachable from that entry. Per the NOT-lanes rule, the activity's internal steps are not separate requirements — "attempt a Medicine check to counteract" is something the player performs; only the action's EXISTENCE is the lane. This is principle E's shape applied to an activity rather than a reaction: the entry plus its popup is essentially the whole surface. Note the text as supplied carries no action-cost glyph, so no cost is asserted here.
requirements.clause: You produce a specialized venom that burns out other toxins and impurities in your body. For each disease or poison currently affecting you, attempt a Medicine check to counteract that disease or poison.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed on the action's entry, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations, with the frequency line also legible in the popup alongside the action's text.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: No requirement. "As normal" flags this as a restatement of a general rule the system already applies to every counteract attempt; per the NOT-lanes list, restating a general rule is not a lane. It rides along as printed text in the action's popup and owes nothing of its own. Note also that this feat grants no bonus to the Medicine check, so no star on Medicine is owed — Q2/Ruling C star a skill when a feat MODIFIES a check, and this one only calls for one.
requirements.clause: As normal, your counteract rank is equal to half your level rounded up.

requirements.what: Nature usable in place of Medicine, scoped to the single action Treat Wounds. The player must be able to reach and roll Treat Wounds off their Nature number, and see that it is Nature being used — a substitution that is action-scoped rather than skill-wide is the shape required here.
requirements.clause: You can use Nature instead of Medicine to Treat Wounds

requirements.what: The substitution must carry PROFICIENCY RANK, not just the modifier: which Treat Wounds DC tiers the character may attempt (the expert/master/legendary escalations) must be gated by the Nature rank when Treat Wounds is performed this way. A substitution that swaps only the total number would silently deny a high-Nature character the harder checks the feat explicitly promises.
requirements.clause: including higher Nature proficiency letting you attempt more difficult checks

requirements.what: The substitution's scope must be expressible as a negative as well as a positive: it must NOT apply to other Medicine uses, and it must NOT count when prerequisites ask for Medicine training/rank. So whatever expresses the substitution has to be invisible to the prerequisite check — the character is not treated as trained in Medicine by virtue of this feat.
requirements.clause: It doesn't replace Medicine for uses of the skill other than Treat Wounds or for feat prerequisites.

requirements.what: A `*` carrying "+2 circumstance bonus to Treat Wounds using Nature while in the wilderness (GM's determination)" — and per Q2, on BOTH surfaces: on the Nature skill, where the player looks up the number, and on the Treat Wounds action, per Ruling D/G (the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). The bonus stays situational rather than flat (Ruling B), and "subject to the GM's determination" does not suppress it — per Ruling H, print the trigger in the note and leave the condition open rather than narrowing it.
requirements.clause: If you're in the wilderness, you might have easier access to fresh ingredients, allowing you to gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check to Treat Wounds using Nature, subject to the GM's determination.

requirements.what: ⚠ NO REQUIREMENT CAN BE DERIVED — the text is incomplete, not empty of mechanics. "You gain the benefits" has no antecedent: no benefit, list, tier, or cross-reference survives in the text supplied, so there is nothing to split into clauses and nothing to state a sheet requirement against. I am deliberately not inferring what a snowcasting benefit ought to be; that would be invention, and the brief forbids speculating. This should be treated as a TEXT DEFECT to be resolved by supplying the record's real printed text, after which the feat needs re-reading. Judged strictly on what is here, the requirement set is empty.
requirements.clause: You draw ever more magical cold into your being, learning how to manipulate it to your whims. You gain the benefits.

requirements.what: No requirement. This is narrative access adjudicated in downtime/exploration, which the NOT-lanes list rules out explicitly ("exploration outcomes, social consequences, narrative access"). It names no action with a cost, grants no bonus, and the text pointedly removes the only roll that could be starred — entry is secured "without the need for a skill check" — so per Ruling I, where the rules name no roll or trigger, star nothing. The 1d4 hours is an elapsed-time cost the GM tracks, not a resource on the sheet. The feat's own entry, read in full, is the whole surface.
requirements.clause: Any time you encounter a social event you would ordinarily be denied access to, such as a coronation, royal gala, or other society function, you can spend 1d4 hours to secure entry without the need for a skill check. You find invitations, invitees looking for fashionable dates, temporary jobs with the caterers, event staff willing to look the other way, or some other mode of access for yourself and your allies.

requirements.what: No requirement. A negative scope limit on an ability that itself has no sheet surface has nothing to attach to; it is GM adjudication and rides in the feat's printed text. Also note the "for yourself and your allies" in the preceding clause is ally-facing and, per Ruling F, adds nothing — and unlike Resilient Touch there is no record of the character's own that it modifies, so principle A produces no marker either.
requirements.clause: This ability doesn't apply to secret events or other small private gatherings with no staff, dates, or outsiders involved.

requirements.what: Two separate resistance entries — piercing 2 and slashing 1 — in the defences list, each sourced to this feat so the player can see where they came from. They are two distinct damage types with two distinct values, not one combined entry. Per Q11 the rules were checked: nothing in the text lets the character switch this off, and the head gem is part of the athamaru body rather than a worn item, so this is a passive bonus and not a mode. The 'while you possess your head gem' condition rides along as the qualifier on the entry rather than gating it behind a toggle.
requirements.clause: While you possess your head gem, you gain resistance 2 to piercing damage and resistance 1 to slashing damage.

requirements.what: Both resistance values must be a LEVEL-DRIVEN FORMULA, not stored constants. '+1 at 9th and every 4 levels thereafter' means the pair reads 2/1 at levels 1–8, 3/2 at 9th, 4/3 at 13th, and 5/4 at 17th. The requirement is that the sheet re-derives both numbers whenever the character's level changes; a record that can only express a fixed number satisfies the resistance lane while still being wrong at most levels. This is the presence-vs-value blind spot the lane manual warns about, so it is stated as its own requirement rather than folded into the entry above.
requirements.clause: The resistance to each type of damage increases by 1 at 9th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. The opening sentences about hunting, battle and the waxing moon are flavour explaining why the gem protects you. No surface owed.
requirements.clause: A life of hunting and battle has caused your head gem to attune to the waxing moon…

requirements.what: A construct entity — the animated hut — must exist on the sheet as its own addressable creature with its own stat block, the way an animal companion or eidolon does. Everything else this feat promises hangs off that entity; without a place to put a creature that is not the character, none of the rest can land anywhere. The 1-day rite that creates it is a downtime action and needs no surface of its own (the same shape as Guerrilla Dedication's week of downtime).
requirements.clause: you create an animated object from a hut, small house, covered wagon, tent, or similar construction of up to Huge size

requirements.what: The hut's defensive block: AC, all three saving throw modifiers, and Perception must be DERIVED LIVE from the character's own values, not copied as numbers at creation time — otherwise they stop tracking the moment the character levels, changes armour, or gains an item bonus. Alongside them two fixed values of its own: 150 HP (trackable and damageable, since the ability below keys off it) and Hardness 10.
requirements.clause: The hut uses your AC, saving throw modifiers, and Perception modifier and has 150 HP and Hardness 10.

requirements.what: The construct armor ability on the hut's block: −4 AC once it drops below half its Hit Points or immediately on taking a critical hit, lasting until repaired. At minimum the ability's text must be legible on the hut. The below-half-HP half of the trigger is genuinely computable — the hut's own HP is already tracked per the requirement above — so the reduced AC can be shown rather than left to the player to remember; the critical-hit half and the 'until it is repaired' clearing condition are player-driven state.
requirements.clause: once it's reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its AC is reduced by 4 until it is repaired

requirements.what: A 1-action activity in the character's OWN actions list — this is the one part of the feat that lands on the player's sheet rather than the hut's. It must carry its action cost (single action) and both of its traits (auditory, concentrate), since those traits are what expose it to silence and counter effects.
requirements.clause: You can give the hut a command as a single action, which has the auditory and concentrate traits

requirements.what: The standing command is a persistent, mutually exclusive state on the hut — exactly one of Guard, Hide, Leap, Lock, Move is in force at a time, and it persists across turns until replaced, so it is a state the sheet must HOLD rather than a momentary effect. All five options need their full text readable. One of them contributes a real number: Move gives the hut a Speed of 60 feet, which the hut otherwise does not have, so the hut's block needs a Speed that exists only under that command. The rest are text — Guard's 120-foot watch using your Perception, Hide's 10th-rank illusion, Leap's 10th-rank Teleport, Lock's sealed entrances. The 1-round reconfiguration delay before a command takes effect belongs in that text.
requirements.clause: after 1 round of reconfiguring itself, the hut then follows that command until you give it a different command

requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not stated in the authority documents: the player picks what the structure IS and how big it is (up to Huge). The list ends in 'or similar construction', so it is open-ended — Principle I makes free-text player input a legitimate choice type — and the size is mechanical because it is a creature's size category. Flagged rather than assumed.
requirements.clause: from a hut, small house, covered wagon, tent, or similar construction of up to Huge size

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. 'The hut can't attack or attempt skill checks' is the ABSENCE of strikes and skills on the hut's block, not something to add — a block with no strike entries and no skill entries already expresses it. Nothing owed beyond the printed text.
requirements.clause: The hut can't attack or attempt skill checks.

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. The one-at-a-time cap and the reversion of a previous hut need no separate surface: holding a single hut entity per character already expresses it, and performing the rite again replaces that entity. The 'if you die, the hut continues following the last order' clause is GM narrative with no sheet consequence.
requirements.clause: You can have only one witch's hut at a time… If you die, the hut continues following the last order you gave it indefinitely.

requirements.what: The feat teaches an activity, so it must appear in the actions list with its full text reachable — the 20-foot burst within 120 feet, the direction choice, the 3 rounds of continued movement, and all four degree-of-success entries. Only the action's EXISTENCE is the lane; its internal steps are performed by the player.
requirements.clause: You create a massive wave of water that crashes in a 20-foot burst within 120 feet that moves in the direction of your choice.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed on the action, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: Frequency once per day

requirements.what: THE ONE NUMBER THIS FEAT OWES THE PLAYER'S OWN SHEET. The DC is neither fixed nor printed — it is 'your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher', a comparison between two of the character's own stats that changes as either advances, and it is asked for twice (the Reflex save and the Escape check). Per Ruling D the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, so the resolved number belongs in this action's popup rather than on a general stat row. A character holding both a class DC and a spell DC cannot read this off any single existing line.
requirements.clause: a DC equal to your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Everything else lands somewhere other than the character's sheet and owes nothing beyond being readable in the action's popup: the 14d6 bludgeoning damage, the swept-away state, the movement of trapped creatures and all four degree-of-success outcomes are enemy-facing; the wave's 30-foot advance over 3 rounds is round-tracking that is not done; extinguishing non-magical fires is battlefield/GM adjudication.
requirements.clause: All creatures in the area take 14d6 bludgeoning damage and could be swept away… The wave also extinguishes all non-magical fires in its path automatically.

requirements.what: An indication on the records this feat modifies — the character's DOMAIN SPELLS — showing that casting one grants resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn, in an amount equal to that spell's rank. This is Principle A and C's shape (a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing) and Ruling D's placement (the player is looking at the domain spell at the moment of casting). Because the trigger is 'a domain spell' rather than one named spell, the marker must reach EVERY domain spell the character holds, not just one — and the amount is not a constant, so the indication has to state the rule (equal to the rank cast, which rises when the spell is heightened) rather than a number.
requirements.clause: After you cast a domain spell, you gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn. The amount of resistance is equal to the rank of the domain spell you cast.

requirements.what: NO RESISTANCE ENTRY, no number, and no mode. The duration is 'until the start of your next turn' — one round — and Q1 rules that effects lasting 1 round are not implemented, indication only; a mode is what a LONGER duration earns. A resistance line standing in the defences list would also be false most of the time, since it is absent until a domain spell is cast and its value depends on which rank was cast. Stated explicitly because the resistance lane is the obvious place a reader would reach for here, and reaching for it would be wrong.
requirements.clause: you gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn

requirements.what: One use per day, spent when the ability is activated and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: Frequency once per day

requirements.what: A mode the player turns on, carrying the feat's text. The duration is 5 minutes — far longer than a round — and Q1 rules that a longer duration gets a mode, so this is the toggle that makes the flight visibly active and tells the player it is running. Activating it is what spends the daily use above.
requirements.clause: You can maintain this redirected energy for 5 minutes.

requirements.what: A fly Speed equal to your Speed, present only while the mode is on, with a `*` carrying the feat's details. Two independent reasons a bare number will not do: the value is a FORMULA off the character's own Speed — exactly Wyrmling Flight's shape, where a stored number silently breaks for any character whose Speed is not the assumed value and stops tracking Speed bonuses and armour penalties — and Q7 gives the star specifically to a CONDITIONAL movement type, which this is, the flight existing only while the energy is redirected.
requirements.clause: You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed while redirecting the energy.

requirements.what: The Enhancement must be recordable as taken, and taking it must reach back into this same feat and DELETE BOTH of its limits: the once-per-day use disappears and the 5-minute duration disappears, leaving the fly Speed permanently available. That flips the two requirements above — the daily use should no longer be shown or spent, and per Q7 a permanent speed needs no conditional gating, so the flight stops being mode-dependent. A sheet that can only ADD on top of a feat cannot express this, because the Enhancement's entire content is the REMOVAL of the two restrictions the base feat printed. The Enhancement text should be readable whether or not it has been taken.
requirements.clause: You can redirect your energy at all times, allowing you to fly whenever you want, rather than just once per day for 5 minutes.

requirements.what: Dueling Parry must exist as a usable activity in the actions list, with its Requirements line readable in its popup ("You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and hold nothing else in your hands"). Per Principle E's shape — an activated entry whose trigger/requirements live in its own popup — this is the load-bearing surface for the feat.
requirements.clause: Requirements You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and hold nothing else in your hands. You can parry attacks against you with your one-handed weapon.

requirements.what: The +2 circumstance bonus to AC, its duration ("until the start of your next turn"), and the standing condition that it lapses the moment you stop meeting the requirements, all stated as text in that action's popup. Q1 governs: an effect lasting 1 round is not implemented — indication only — so this contributes no number to the AC total and earns no mode. The sustain-condition ("as long as you continue to meet the requirements") is also not computable, since whether both hands are still free mid-turn is not a sheet quantity.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn as long as you continue to meet the requirements.

requirements.what: ⚠ FLAGGED, NOT ASSERTED — an open question I am raising rather than a requirement I am claiming. One could argue AC should carry a `*` so the player sees the +2 where they read the number an attacker rolls against (Ruling D's "the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters"). Two standing rulings point the other way: Q1 strips the number from a 1-round effect, and Principle J puts situational stars on the specific skills or actions affected "not on a general stat". I record it as open because the owner has not ruled on an activated, self-targeting, 1-round bonus to a stat that DOES have a row.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn

requirements.what: No requirement. "Source Player Core pg. 141", the "Archetypes Duelist (Level 4)" access line, and the trailing "Dueling Parry (Fighter) leads to… Dueling Dance (Fighter), Dueling Riposte, Selfless Parry" are AoN page scaffolding — access clauses and successor listings, explicitly not lanes.
requirements.clause: Source Player Core pg. 141 Archetypes Duelist (Level 4) … leads to… Dueling Dance (Fighter), Dueling Riposte, Selfless Parry

requirements.what: A physical-damage resistance entry that appears in the character's defences, sourced to this feat. Its VALUE is not a constant: it is a live count of how many Living Monolith archetype class feats the character currently owns, so it must recompute upward every time another Living Monolith feat is taken (and downward if one is removed in the builder). A resistance whose magnitude is a formula over the character's own owned-feat set — filtered to one named archetype — is what must be expressible; a hardcoded number would be wrong at every level but one.
requirements.clause: You gain resistance to physical damage (except adamantine) equal to your number of class feats from the Living Monolith archetype.

requirements.what: The resistance must carry an EXCEPTION, not just a type and a value: adamantine damage bypasses it entirely. The player reading their physical resistance has to see the carve-out at the point where they read the number, otherwise they will apply it against an adamantine weapon. This is a qualifier on the resistance entry itself (type = physical, minus adamantine), distinct from the value question above.
requirements.clause: resistance to physical damage (except adamantine)

requirements.what: No requirement. "Your flesh takes on the hardness of stone" is flavour — despite the word "hardness", it grants no hardness value; the mechanical sentence that follows grants resistance.
requirements.clause: Your flesh takes on the hardness of stone.

requirements.what: Frighten Undead must appear under BOTH action costs — its own native cost and the free action this feat enables — with the explanation in the popup (that the free-action version is available only immediately after a successful Slayer's Identification, and only against the creature you identified). This is Principle H exactly, the Quick Recognition shape: "An action whose cost changes conditionally appears under both costs, with the explanation in the popup." The feat grants no new activity of its own; it re-costs one the character already has.
requirements.clause: When you use Slayer's Identification and succeed at your check, you can Frighten Undead as a free action, targeting the creature you identified.

requirements.what: A marker on Slayer's Identification itself showing that this feat modifies it — that a success on its check now unlocks a free Frighten Undead. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Q8 confirms Ruling D's shape applies to a modified action. The player is looking at Slayer's Identification when they use it, and that is when they need to know a success buys them something extra. Note this feat touches two separate records — the identification action (new consequence on success) and Frighten Undead (new cost) — and each needs its own indication.
requirements.clause: When you use Slayer's Identification and succeed at your check…

requirements.what: No requirement — nothing beyond the printed text already in the feat's own description. This clause is an enemy-side condition (fleeing on the target), which the DECIDED SCOPE section rules out of the sheet twice over: effects on enemies are not lanes, and Q4 settles that for an enemy-condition the entry itself is the whole surface. Q15 independently disposes of it: an effect firing on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED, and "the target is fleeing for 1 round" is not. The level comparison (target's level lower than yours) is a GM-side check against a creature the sheet does not model.
requirements.clause: Any time you get a critical success to Frighten Undead, if the target's level is lower than yours, the target is fleeing for 1 round.

requirements.what: Fire resistance 4 as a flat, permanent, always-on value in the character's defences, attributed to this feat so the player can see where it came from when several resistance sources stack. Nothing conditional — Q11's test (can the effect be shut down?) answers no, so it is a passive bonus, not a mode.
requirements.clause: You gain resistance 4 to fire.

requirements.what: A printed, non-computing note that environmental heat is treated as one step less extreme, with the worked example the text supplies (incredible→extreme, extreme→severe, and so on). Nothing on a character sheet can compute this: environmental heat severity is a property of the scene the GM is running, not a sheet quantity, so there is no value to adjust and no roll to modify. What must be expressible is the clause being READABLE in the place the player looks when heat matters — its natural home is beside the fire resistance entry, since that is the only fire-facing row on the sheet. ⚠ I explicitly do NOT claim a `*` on Fortitude saves: the feat downgrades the environment's step, it does not give you a bonus on any check, and inventing a save star would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's (Ruling H).
requirements.clause: You treat environmental heat effects as if they were one step less extreme (incredible heat becomes extreme, extreme heat becomes severe, and so on).

requirements.what: No requirement. "Your have a love for extreme heat" is flavour.
requirements.clause: Your have a love for extreme heat.

requirements.what: The Eidolon's Wrath focus spell must be granted and surfaced with its details reachable — but attributed to the EIDOLON as its caster, not to the summoner. The text is explicit that the eidolon casts it "instead of you", so a focus spell that simply lands in the summoner's own spell list would state something false about who casts it. The DECIDED SCOPE companion ruling points the same way: what belongs to the companion is presented on the companion. What must be expressible is a focus spell whose owner and whose caster are different records.
requirements.clause: Your eidolon gains the Eidolon's Wrath focus spell, which it casts, instead of you.

requirements.what: A one-time choice of damage type, made when the feat is taken, from the seven listed options (acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, vitality, void). The chosen type must then be reflected in the granted spell — the player reading Eidolon's Wrath needs to see THEIR damage type on it, not a generic list of seven. So the pick is not just recorded on the feat; it feeds the spell's displayed damage.
requirements.clause: You determine the damage type when you gain the feat: acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, vitality, or void.

requirements.what: The option list itself is CONDITIONAL on another record: if the eidolon is a celestial, fiend, or monitor whose alignment is anything other than true neutral, additional alignment-matched damage types join the list. Per Q9 the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, so the picker must read the eidolon's subtype AND its alignment and widen (or not widen) the seven-option list accordingly. This is a distinct expressive demand from the base pick: a choice whose legal options are derived from a different, separately-chosen record. ⚠ The text does not enumerate which types count as "in its alignment", so the option set has to come from somewhere other than this feat's own words.
requirements.clause: If your eidolon is a celestial, fiend, or monitor with an alignment other than true neutral, you can choose a damage type in its alignment.

requirements.what: +1 to the maximum size of the focus pool, applied to the summoner's own pool and visible in the pool's total. A plain, permanent, computable increase.
requirements.clause: Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

requirements.what: No requirement. This is a restatement of the standard summoner rule that eidolon and summoner draw on one pool — the NOT-lanes list rules out "restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere". It carries one consequence worth naming but not owed by this feat: casting the eidolon-side spell must spend the SAME pool the summoner spends, which is the base rule's job rather than this feat's.
requirements.clause: As normal, your eidolon shares your Focus Points.
"You channel your commitment to removing the divine from the world as you recite the Laws of Mortality. Strike a foe that can cast divine spells."
requirements.what: The activity itself must exist as a named action the player can find and read — an entry in the actions list carrying its full text, including its targeting restriction (the foe must be able to cast divine spells). Per the manual, the internal steps of an activity ('make a Strike') are not their own lanes; only the activity's EXISTENCE is.

requirements.clause: "The Strike deals two extra weapon damage dice."
requirements.what: No separate strike surface is owed. This rider exists only inside this activity — it does not modify your Strikes generally, so it must not appear as a standing damage bonus on any weapon. The number belongs in the activity's own popup text, which the grantsAction requirement above already carries (Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters, and here that thing IS the activity).

requirements.clause: "The target must also attempt a save against your class DC."
requirements.what: Nothing. This consumes an existing sheet stat rather than modifying one — the feat adds no bonus to your class DC, so Ruling D's DC-breakdown shape is not triggered. The activity's text names the DC; the player reads their class DC where it already lives.

requirements.clause: "On a failure, it loses its highest-rank available divine spell prepared or its highest unused spell slot to cast a divine spell. If it has multiple spells at its highest rank available, it randomly selects which spell is lost. On a critical failure, it also can't cast divine spells until the start of your next turn."
requirements.what: Nothing. Entirely enemy-facing — it removes the TARGET's spells and gates the TARGET's casting. Effects on enemies are explicitly not lanes, and the degree-of-success prose is text inside the activity's popup, not a degree-of-success surface (per the Minor Omen answer).

requirements.clause: "**Trigger** A creature targets you with an attack. **Frequency** once per hour"
requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger (a creature targets you with an attack) and its frequency (once per hour) shown in its popup. Per the owner's Minor Omen answer this is often the whole requirement — the frequency is text in the popup, not a tracked resource; an hourly frequency has no daily-preparations reset shape to hang a use-pip on.

requirements.clause: "...creating a natural lattice of wood that grants standard cover. The circumstance bonus from the cover applies to your AC when you're determining the outcome of the triggering attack."
requirements.what: No AC entry and no star on AC. The bonus is yours, not an ally's, but it exists only for the single triggering attack while the reaction resolves — shorter than the one-round threshold, so indication only (Q1). The indication is the reaction's own popup text, which must state that standard cover's circumstance bonus applies to your AC against that attack. A star on AC would assert a bonus that is not live at any moment the player is reading the sheet, and Ruling J keeps situational stars off general stats.

requirements.clause: "If the triggering attack still hits and deals physical damage to you, the ward reduces the damage by 30 and is immediately destroyed."
requirements.what: No resistance entry. This is a one-shot damage reduction consumed inside the reaction, not a standing resistance to physical damage — and HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode (Ruling E). The 30 and the ward's destruction are text in the reaction's popup.

requirements.clause: "If the attack misses, the ward instead persists for 3 rounds before withering back into the earth."
requirements.what: A display-only mode the player turns on when the ward survives, so they can see it is up. Three rounds is longer than the one-round threshold that Q1 rules 'indication only', and the ward is a thing that can be shut down (destroyed), which Q11 puts on the mode side. It contributes NO numbers: rounds are not tracked, and whether the lattice is still between you and a given attacker is positional, which the app can never know (Ruling M). Its whole content is the printed text of what the ward does.

requirements.clause: "Creatures can cross the ward, but it's difficult terrain."
requirements.what: Nothing. A battlefield effect on other creatures' movement, not on your sheet.

requirements.clause: "Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level."
requirements.what: A picker that runs at daily preparations offering exactly TWO talisman selections, and the resulting talismans must reach the character's inventory as real, usable items (a talisman is affixed and activated — it is not a formula reference). The offered list must be capped at item level ≤ half your level, so the cap has to be recomputed as the character levels.

requirements.clause: "You must know each talisman's formula." / "You know the formulas for all common talismans in GM Core of your level or lower."
requirements.what: The set the picker draws from must exist and be derived, not authored once: all COMMON talismans of level ≤ your level. It grows every time the character levels, so it is a live derivation — unlike Q14's formula-book grant, which is a one-time write. Q9 governs the picker: it offers only what the character may legally pick, i.e. the intersection of formulas known and the half-level item cap. Any talisman formula the character knows from another source must also feed this picker, since the text conditions on knowing the formula rather than on this feat's own list.

requirements.clause: "A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations."
requirements.what: The produced talismans must be distinguishable from bought ones and must not survive the next daily preparations — the previous day's unused talismans are cleared (or marked expired) when the picker is run again. Without this the inventory silently accumulates free permanent talismans.

requirements.clause: "You remember your talisman formulas through oral tradition or mnemonics, so you don't need a formula book for them."
requirements.what: Nothing — and specifically a negative requirement worth recording: this feat must NOT trigger the 'taking a feat that grants a formula book ensures the character has one' rule from Q14, and these formulas must not be written into a formula book. The text explicitly waives the book, and Q14's severed-from-the-book one-time write would be wrong here anyway, since this knowledge keeps growing with level.

requirements.clause: "You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against mental effects."
requirements.what: A situational star on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — reading +1 circumstance, when: against mental effects (Q2: when a bonus applies to saves generally, star all three). It belongs in the restricted/situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, not in the flat save total (Ruling B) — a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct.

requirements.clause: "This bonus increases to +2 against mental effects originating from undead."
requirements.what: A SECOND situational entry on all three saves, +2 circumstance, when: against mental effects originating from undead. It must be its own entry rather than replacing the first, because the two have different `when` text — and the stacking display rule is that the same bonus type with different `when` shows both, with no attempt to reason about whether the triggers overlap. The player reading a save against an undead's mental effect must be able to see the +2 and not just the +1.

requirements.clause: "You gain the Protector's Sacrifice domain spell as a devotion spell."
requirements.what: Protector's Sacrifice must appear among the character's focus spells, filed as a DEVOTION spell (the champion's focus-spell category) rather than as a generic domain spell, with the spell's own details reachable from the entry and this feat named as its source. The spell is castable from the focus pool like any other focus spell.

requirements.clause: "Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1."
requirements.what: +1 to the focus pool maximum, so the pool's displayed size and its spendable points both go up by one, and Refocus restores toward the raised maximum. This is a real number on the sheet, not a note.

requirements.clause: Select one weapon or Handwraps of Mighty Blows when you make your daily preparations.
requirements.what: A pick made at daily preparations, offering only the weapons and Handwraps of Mighty Blows the character actually owns, and remembering the selection until the next preparation. Everything else this feat does hangs off that pick, so the chosen item must be identifiable on the sheet — the player has to see WHICH weapon is currently blessed, not just that a blessing exists.

requirements.clause: the weapon ... deals an additional 1d8 spirit damage
requirements.what: The selected weapon's Strike gains +1d8 spirit damage, visible in that Strike's damage line and its breakdown, attributed to this feat. The load-bearing part is that the rider follows the daily pick: it must attach to whichever item was chosen today and be absent from every other weapon, rather than sitting on the character generally.

requirements.clause: creatures who wield it gain the weapon's critical specialization
