requirements.what: The selected weapon gains its critical specialization effect regardless of the character's proficiency with it, surfaced on that weapon's Strike where crit effects are read. The 'creatures who wield it' wording also covers allies who pick it up — that half is ally-facing and per Ruling F needs no number on this sheet.

requirements.clause: The weapon sheds light like a torch
requirements.what: Text only, carried on the selected weapon. It computes nothing on the sheet (lighting is a battlefield fact the GM adjudicates), but it must be readable on the blessed weapon because a later clause depends on it — the Mythic action's area is 'the bright light of your nimbus'.

requirements.clause: When you critically hit a target with the weapon, the target must succeed at a save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) or be blinded for 1d4 rounds.
requirements.what: A printed rider on the blessed weapon's Strike, next to where a crit is read (Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). No computed effect is owed: the condition lands on an enemy, and Q15 rules that a critical-success trigger needs no implementation unless the effect is complicated, which blinded for 1d4 rounds is not. The one thing the sheet must actually express is the DC: the rider names 'your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher', so both numbers must be legible to the player at the moment they read this rider, and the note must say which comparison to make rather than asserting a single DC.

requirements.clause: As a single action that has the concentration trait, you can hold your hand aloft and call this weapon back to your possession; it immediately teleports into your hand.
requirements.what: A new named single action with the concentration trait in the actions list, with its text in the popup. Its requirement is implicit — it works on the currently blessed weapon — so the entry must tie back to today's pick.

requirements.clause: While you're holding this weapon, you can spend 1 Mythic Point as a single action to temporarily grant a blessing to weapons wielded by your allies.
requirements.what: A second named single action, distinct from the recall action, with its requirement (you are holding the blessed weapon) shown in its popup, per Principle E's shape for triggered/conditional entries.

requirements.clause: you can spend 1 Mythic Point
requirements.what: The action's cost of 1 Mythic Point must be shown on the entry and must spend from the character's Mythic Point pool — a resource the sheet has to hold, display, decrement on use, and restore at whatever interval refreshes it. Without a pool to draw on, the action's cost is unexpressible.

requirements.clause: Each ally within the bright light of your nimbus when you take this action selects one weapon in their possession. For 1 minute, the selected weapons gain the following benefits: the weapon sheds light like a torch, the weapon deals an additional 1d6 spirit damage, and creatures who wield the weapon gain the weapon's critical specialization.
requirements.what: A display-only mode on the activating character, carrying the full clause text and contributing no numbers. Every benefit here lands on an ally's weapon, so Ruling F removes the numbers from this sheet; but the same ruling grants the activator a display-only mode when the effect runs for a limited time, and Q1 confirms a duration longer than 1 round earns a mode. Principle B governs the contents: the mode prints what it does — the 1d6 spirit, the crit specialization, the light — even though it computes none of it. Whether a given ally was inside the nimbus is positional and per Ruling M is never modelled; it belongs in the mode's text.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You're reduced to less than half your maximum Hit Points by a creature within your reach.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions list with its trigger printed verbatim in its popup — Principle E, which is often the whole requirement for a shape like this. The trigger's own contents are not modelled: the half-HP threshold is a state the player reads off their own HP bar, and 'a creature within your reach' is positional (Ruling M). No degree-of-success surface and no HP surface is owed — HP and damage never move sheet stats.

requirements.clause: You gain the effects of Haste for 1 minute.
requirements.what: A mode the player switches on, lasting 1 minute — Q1 puts anything longer than a round in a mode, and Q11's test agrees since the state ends and can be shut off. It must make plain that a mode is active and what changed (Q3's shape). What it carries is Haste itself: quickened, with the extra action usable only to Stride or Strike. That is an action-economy change rather than a stat, so per Principle B the mode prints the full text of what it does even though nothing numeric moves. Because the feat names another record rather than restating it, Haste's own description must be reachable from the mode — the player cannot apply 'the effects of Haste' from a sheet that only says the words.

requirements.clause: You can choose to activate Nanite Surge when you attempt a saving throw, instead of when you attempt a skill check.
requirements.what: Nanite Surge's own entry — granted by a different record — must show the widened trigger: it can now be activated on a saving throw as well as on a skill check, with this feat named as the source. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing, and Q8 confirms Ruling D's shape applies to a modified action. The choice is per-activation ('instead of'), so the entry must present both triggers as alternatives rather than replacing the skill-check trigger with the save one. Nothing about Nanite Surge's frequency or cost changes.

requirements.clause: If you do, you gain a +2 status bonus to the triggering saving throw.
requirements.what: A restricted +2 status bonus that sits outside the flat save total (Ruling B) and is surfaced as a star on all three saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — because the clause names saving throws generally and Q2 says a general save clause stars all three. Q2 also requires the action to be starred as well as the stat, so the same marker appears on the Nanite Surge entry. Its `when` must carry the real gate: only on a save you spent a Nanite Surge activation on, and only on that one triggering save.

requirements.clause: When attempting a check to Recall Knowledge about a city you have visited, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus
requirements.what: A +2 circumstance bonus surfaced as a star on every skill that could perform Recall Knowledge — Ruling C and Principle D both say a bonus named after an action stars every skill able to perform it, not one — and, per Q2, on the Recall Knowledge action itself. The restriction ('about a city you have visited') stays in the `when` text and is never modelled: which cities the character has visited is narrative and GM-adjudicated. Note the feat asks the player to choose nothing, so unlike Guerrilla Dedication's favoured location there is no free-text field owed here.

requirements.clause: and can use an associated Lore skill (such as Nerosyan Lore) ... [for that check]
requirements.what: For that Recall Knowledge check the character may roll an associated city Lore in place of the skill that would normally apply. So the sheet must be able to express 'use this Lore instead' as an option attached to the Recall Knowledge marker, with the example (Nerosyan Lore) preserved as an example rather than baked in as the pick — the associated Lore varies with the city and is never fixed.

requirements.clause: with your level as your proficiency bonus even if you're untrained
requirements.what: The harder half, and the one the lane vocabulary does not cleanly cover. This is NOT training: trained would give level + 2, while the feat gives level + 0 — your level as the whole proficiency bonus, where untrained normally yields no level at all. Worse, the Lore in question need not exist on the sheet: a character who has never taken Nerosyan Lore must still be able to roll it at level-as-proficiency. So what is required is a rollable check for a Lore the character does not possess, computed at level plus the relevant attribute and item modifiers with a rank bonus of zero. If that cannot attach to a skill row (because there is no row), it must at minimum be stated on the Recall Knowledge marker so the player can build the number themselves. Flagging this as a possible no-lane-at-all shape rather than forcing it into `loreTrained`, which would overshoot by +2.

requirements.clause: When in the water within 20 feet of a sea vehicle or climbing aboard one, you can move at your full Speed while Sneaking.
requirements.what: A star on the Sneak action carrying the full clause, and — per Ruling C and Q2 — on Stealth as well, since Stealth is the skill that performs Sneak. Nothing numeric moves: this lifts Sneak's normal half-Speed movement cap rather than granting a bonus, so the requirement is that the allowance is readable where Sneak is read, not that a modifier appears in a total. The whole condition is positional (in the water within 20 feet of a sea vehicle, or climbing aboard one) and per Ruling M the app can never know where the character stands, so it lives verbatim in the marker's `when` and is never evaluated. The opening sentence is flavour and requires nothing.

requirements.clause: At the start of your turn, you gain an additional reaction
requirements.what: A second reaction must be visible and trackable on the sheet — the reaction the player counts down each round becomes 2, refreshing at the start of your turn alongside the normal one. The 'at the start of your turn' timing itself asks for nothing new; it is the ordinary reaction-refresh rule restated.

requirements.clause: which you can use for only reactions granted by your implements
requirements.what: The restriction must travel with that extra reaction rather than being dropped — the slot is not a free second reaction, it is spendable only on implement-granted reactions. Nothing can decide for the player which reaction they are spending, so this is text carried on the extra slot (Ruling B/H shape: the restriction lives in the entry's condition, printed, not enforced). An extra reaction shown bare would overstate what the feat gives.

requirements.clause: Once per day, you can cast Impaling Spike as a 7th-rank innate occult spell
requirements.what: Impaling Spike must reach the Spells page as an INNATE spell, occult, cast at 7th rank, with its own details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source. Two specifics: (a) the rank is raised above the spell's printed base rank, so 7 must be stated explicitly on the grant — a grant that defaults to the spell's own rank would show the wrong number; (b) the tradition must be legible on the entry itself, since a character can hold innate grants of several traditions and a pooled heading cannot assert one tradition truthfully for all of them (Q12 — the sheet must not state something false about the spell).

requirements.clause: Once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when it is cast and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: except the spike is made of bone instead of cold iron. The bone from the spell has the effects of the ghost touch property rune and can Immobilize incorporeal creatures as if they were corporeal.
requirements.what: A marker on this Impaling Spike entry carrying the alteration — bone rather than cold iron, the ghost touch effect, and that it can Immobilize incorporeal creatures. The player reads the spell's own text at the moment they cast it, so the change has to be visible there and not only inside the feat's description (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). No number moves on your sheet — the ghost touch effect and the Immobilize both act on the target.

requirements.clause: If you're Small or smaller, you can end your movement in the same square as a Small or smaller ally.
requirements.what: NOTHING is required. This is a permission about where you may end movement relative to an ally on the board, and board position is not modelled (Ruling M — positional questions are answered at the table, not on the sheet). It grants no bonus, so Ruling D has no value and no stat row to attach to; it is not a named activity, so it is not an action grant. The size gate reads off your own size, which the sheet already carries, and the feat's printed text in the feats list is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: No more than two creatures can share the same space when using this ability or a similar one.
requirements.what: NOTHING. A cap on the same table-adjudicated permission — it constrains what the GM allows on the board, not any value on your sheet, and it is printed in the same feat text the player already reads.

requirements.clause: You gain the Advanced Undead Benefits
requirements.what: The named Advanced Undead Benefits record must actually be acquired, its details surfaced from this feat, and whatever that record itself grants must flow through to the sheet — including any choice it offers the player (Principle G: a granted feature needs its details surfaced AND its choice offered). The failure mode is a package that is printed in the feat's prose but never acquired, so everything nested inside it stays silent.

requirements.clause: and can't be destroyed by sunlight
requirements.what: A defensive entry where the player looks up what can harm them, stating that sunlight cannot destroy you. This is a standing, non-suppressible fact (Q11 — it cannot be shut down, so it is a passive entry, not a mode).

requirements.clause: and can't be destroyed by sunlight
requirements.what: The same fact must also be reflected on the record that states the sunlight-destruction rule this feat cancels — the vampire's own sunlight vulnerability. A vulnerability printed on one record and silently made untrue by another is exactly what Principle C forbids; the player looking at the vulnerability must see it struck through or annotated by this feat.

requirements.clause: This doesn't prevent you from becoming slowed by exposure to the sun.
requirements.what: No independent surface. The caveat must ride with the sunlight entry above so the immunity is not read as 'sunlight is harmless' — it is a limit on the previous clause, not a second effect. Becoming slowed is a condition the player applies when it happens, not a standing number on the sheet.

requirements.clause: Three Large trees appear in unoccupied spaces within 500 feet... Each tree has AC 40, Fortitude +33, Reflex +24, Will +30, and 200 HP... The tree's melee Strike is a branch that has reach 10 feet; on a hit, the target is grabbed (escape dc=40). The ranged Strike... range increment of 60 feet. Either Strike has a +30 attack modifier and deals damage.
requirements.what: The impulse must exist as a usable action on the sheet, with its FULL printed text reachable from the entry — the trees' AC 40 / Fort +33 / Ref +24 / Will +30 / 200 HP, the +30 attack modifier, the branch's reach 10 feet and escape DC 40, and the ranged Strike's 60-foot increment. Here the stat block IS the text: the player reads those numbers off the action when they use it, so truncating the description is the defect to avoid. Nothing is computed.

requirements.clause: Each tree has AC 40, Fortitude +33, Reflex +24, Will +30, and 200 HP... The trees can flank, but are unable to move.
requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the text above. None of these numbers belong on your own sheet: the trees are not you, and they are not a companion (they cannot move and expire in a round), so they get no stat block, no Strike entry among your Strikes, and no HP tracker. Their attacks land on enemies, and HP and damage never move sheet stats. Flanking is a board question.

requirements.clause: The trees last until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. Each time you Sustain the impulse, you can have one tree make a Strike.
requirements.what: Indication only — no mode and no timer. The duration is one round, and a one-round effect is not implemented as a mode (Q1; Q1's mode threshold is longer durations). That the impulse is sustainable, and that each Sustain buys one tree Strike, is text inside the action's entry — the Sustain and the Strike are internal steps of the activity, performed by the player.

requirements.clause: Level (20th) The attack modifier is +32 and the Strike damage is 5d10+9.
requirements.what: The entry must present the values that apply at the reading character's level — a 20th-level character has to see +32 and 5d10+9 rather than the base +30 line, since a level-scaling clause shown only as a footnote makes the player compute which line is live. Two cautions from the text itself: the base clause as printed says only that the Strike 'deals damage' with no die expression, so no base damage value can be surfaced from this text (flagging the hole rather than inventing a number), and the 20th-level line is the only damage figure the feat actually states.

A named activity the player can find and perform: it appears in the actions list, and its popup carries the whole printed procedure — a single target chosen within 30 feet, the save it forces, and the four outcome lines. Range (30 feet) is part of the action's own description, not a sheet stat.
requirements.clause: With a look and a gesture... Choose a target within 30 feet

requirements.what: The action must show that performing it costs a Mythic Point, and using it must draw that point down from the character's Mythic Point pool. This is NOT a per-feat frequency — the feat prints no Frequency line, so the pool is its only limiter; the sheet therefore needs a shared, spendable Mythic Point resource that this action consumes, not a counter belonging to this feat.
requirements.clause: and spend a Mythic Point

requirements.what: The popup must state the DC the target actually rolls against, and it must be a real number derived from this sheet: the higher of the character's class DC and spell DC, RECOMPUTED at mythic proficiency. Printing the character's ordinary class/spell DC would print a number this feat does not use, so the sheet must be able to express a proficiency rank above legendary and to derive a DC from it. This is the one clause here that the player cannot read off an existing stat row.
requirements.clause: The target must attempt a save against your class DC or spell DC (whichever is higher) at mythic proficiency.

requirements.what: NOTHING is required. Every outcome lands on the target — damage to it, Stunned 1 on it, or no effect. Enemy conditions and enemy damage are DECIDED SCOPE ("effects on enemies... are not lanes"), and degree-of-success text is printed prose. The four lines belong in the action's popup as text and owe the sheet no number, no mode, and no marker. Q15 also applies to the Critical Success line, which is 'the target is unaffected' — as uncomplicated as a trigger outcome gets.
requirements.clause: Critical Success ... Success ... Failure ... Critical Failure (12d8 damage, 12d8 mental damage, Stunned 1)

requirements.what: Trained rank in BOTH Crafting and Religion, reaching the skill list as ordinary trained proficiency from this feat.
requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Crafting and Religion.

requirements.what: A per-skill overlap test with a fallback: if another source (background, class, ancestry) would already make the character trained in Crafting, or in Religion, that half of the grant converts instead into a free choice of any skill. The test is written per skill ("one of those skills"), so it can fire twice — once for Crafting and once for Religion — and the sheet must be able to produce two independent free choices, not one.
requirements.clause: If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

requirements.what: The replacement grant is a player choice of skill, offered in the builder and resolvable to a real trained skill on the sheet. It is conditional — it exists only when the overlap above fires — so the choice must be able to appear and disappear as the rest of the build changes.
requirements.clause: you instead become trained in a skill of your choice

requirements.what: The Additional Lore general feat is granted and owned — it shows in the feats list with its own details reachable — and its Lore subject arrives PRE-SET to Dwarf Lore. The player must not be offered the Lore picker Additional Lore normally carries, because this feat names the subject. Q9's "the builder shows only what the player may legally pick" degenerates here to a single fixed option.
requirements.clause: You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Dwarf Lore.

requirements.what: Dwarf Lore itself must appear on the skills list as a trained Lore, and must go on receiving whatever rank increases the granted Additional Lore feat provides at later levels. Ruling C's shape: the parameter this feat writes into another record's grant has to be visible in that grant's own result, not only in this feat's text.
requirements.clause: the Additional Lore general feat for Dwarf Lore (its subject, resolved)

requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list whose popup carries the printed procedure: it affects ALL enemies within 30 feet (an area, not a chosen target) and forces a save. Only the action's existence and its text are owed; the app lists it, the player runs it.
requirements.clause: You let out a mighty howl... All enemies within 30 feet must attempt a save

requirements.what: One use per day: a spendable use shown on the action entry, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: Frequency once per day

requirements.what: The requirement line must be legible in the action's popup — principle E's shape ("the Requirement needs to be writen in the pop up"). Being in yaoguai form is a state the character enters elsewhere; this feat owes only the printed condition, not gating machinery, and the action should not be hidden when the form is off any more than Minor Omen is hidden when its trigger has not fired.
requirements.clause: Requirements You're in yaoguai form.

requirements.what: NOTHING beyond printing the clause. Both class DC and spell DC are already stat rows the player can read, and "whichever is higher" is a comparison of two numbers already in front of them — Ruling D's "a skill DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers" is the governing shape. (Contrast the mythic case, where the DC is recomputed at a rank the sheet does not otherwise show.)
requirements.clause: must attempt a save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher

requirements.what: NOTHING is required. Frightened 1/2 and off-guard all land on the enemies. Enemy conditions are DECIDED SCOPE and Q4 settles the shape — the action entry is the whole surface. The four lines are popup text.
requirements.clause: Critical Success ... Success ... Failure ... Critical Failure (Frightened 1, frightened 1 and off-guard, Frightened 2 and off-guard)

requirements.what: The sheet must be able to express a PERMANENTLY ACTIVE Quickened condition — i.e. an extra action every turn — as a standing property of the character. Q11 decides the shape: the effect cannot be shut down, so it is a passive, not a mode; it needs no toggle and no duration. The lane manual has no route for this: `extraReaction` covers "you gain an additional reaction" and nothing covers an additional ACTION or a permanently-on condition. Worth checking as a possibly-unbuilt lane rather than assuming an existing one covers it.
requirements.clause: You're permanently quickened.

requirements.what: The restriction must travel with the extra action wherever that action is shown — the player must never see a bare "quickened" and read it as a free action. Ruling B's shape: a restricted grant carries its restriction in its own `when`/note rather than sitting in the general total. The restriction names two specific siege-weapon activities (Aim, Launch), which this feat references but does not grant.
requirements.clause: You can only use the extra action to Aim or Launch a siege weapon.

requirements.what: NOTHING. The opening sentence about artillery mastery is flavour.
requirements.clause: What you don't know about artillery isn't worth knowing...

requirements.what: One more follower must exist on the sheet as its own entity — the character can hold MULTIPLE followers simultaneously, so this is an additive grant to a collection, not a single slot that gets overwritten. Per the standing companion ruling, whatever the follower carries belongs to the follower's own record, not to the character's stats; the requirement here is purely that the additional entity exists and is distinguishable from the followers already held.
requirements.clause: Another follower joins you in your travels.

requirements.what: The follower must record two printed properties: a rank of NOVICE, and the minion trait. Q6's shape — creature traits are recorded on the record they belong to — so the minion trait must be stored on the follower and visible there.
requirements.clause: They are a novice follower that has the minion trait.

requirements.what: The feat is REPEATABLE with a CAP, and both halves are mechanical. (a) It must be selectable more than once, with each selection granting one further follower — so the builder must permit re-taking it and the sheet must count instances rather than treating ownership as a boolean. (b) The cap of four is on TOTAL FOLLOWERS, not on takings of this feat, so the limit has to be evaluated against followers from every source, not just the ones this feat added. The lane manual lists no route for a repeatable feat or for a cross-source cap; flagged as possibly unbuilt rather than folded into an existing lane.
requirements.clause: Special You can select this feat more than once, gaining an additional follower each time, to a maximum of four total followers.

requirements.what: The activity must exist as a named entry in the actions list, with its Requirements line ("You are wielding a thrown weapon") shown in its popup alongside the full text of what it does. This is the Minor Omen shape (Principle E): for an activity whose body is a sequence of Strikes, the entry's existence plus its trigger/requirement text in the popup is the surface.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are wielding a thrown weapon. --- You bounce your weapon off one foe to strike another. Make a ranged Strike with a thrown weapon. If this Strike hits, the weapon rebounds toward an enemy within 10 feet of the original target. Make an additional Strike against this second target.

requirements.what: The multiple-attack-penalty exception must be printed where the player reads the activity (its popup). This is not the app restating a rule it already implements everywhere — it is a deliberate DEPARTURE from the standard MAP progression, so it cannot be left implicit. No number moves on the sheet: the two Strikes happen inside the activity, and which MAP step each uses is resolved at the table, not carried as a stat.
requirements.clause: Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you've made both attacks.

requirements.what: No requirement. "Make a ranged Strike", the 10-foot rebound geometry, and the second target are the internal steps of an activity and the position of an enemy — the app lists the action, the player performs it. Only the action's existence is a lane.
requirements.clause: Make a ranged Strike with a thrown weapon. If this Strike hits, the weapon rebounds toward an enemy within 10 feet of the original target. Make an additional Strike against this second target.

requirements.what: This feat changes what ANOTHER record (Esoteric Polymath) already granted, so per Principle C the widening must be reflected in that thing: the spell pool Esoteric Polymath draws from must accept arcane, primal, and divine spells in addition to occult. Each tradition is gated on a separate condition — arcane requires trained in Arcana, primal trained in Nature, divine trained in Religion — so the three unlock independently and the character can hold one, two, or all three. Per Q9 the picker must offer only the traditions the character's actual training legally unlocks, and the fact that the pool has widened must be visible on the Esoteric Polymath entry, not only on this feat.
requirements.clause: As long as you're trained in Arcana, you can add arcane spells to your book from Esoteric Polymath; as long as you're trained in Nature, you can add primal spells to your book; and as long as you are trained in Religion, you can add divine spells to your book.

requirements.what: The daily pick that moves one spell from the book into the repertoire must be able to select one of these cross-tradition spells, and the spell once picked is cast AS AN OCCULT SPELL — so its tradition where the player reads it must say occult, not the tradition it was drawn from. Per Q12 (whichever spelling leaves the player least confused) the entry must not assert a tradition it does not have in play. The daily-preparation timing is what makes this a daily choice rather than a builder choice.
requirements.clause: Like your other spells in your book, you can add one of these spells from another tradition to your repertoire as an occult spell each day using Esoteric Polymath

requirements.what: A retention restriction that overrides a THIRD record: a cross-tradition spell must not survive the next daily preparation, and this holds even for a character who has Eclectic Polymath (whose whole purpose is retention). Two things are owed — the cross-tradition pick must actually clear at the next preparation rather than persisting like a native occult pick, and the exception must be legible on Eclectic Polymath itself (Principle C), because that is the record whose promise is being narrowed and the record the player will be looking at when they expect to keep the spell.
requirements.clause: but you can't retain any spells from another tradition when you prepare again, even if you have Eclectic Polymath.

requirements.what: A `*` on ALL THREE saves — Fortitude, Reflex, and Will — carrying "+2 circumstance bonus against effects from beasts and dragons". Q2 settles the spread: when a bonus applies to saving throws generally, star all three saves rather than picking one. Ruling B settles the shape: a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, NOT folded into the save totals — sitting outside the printed total is the correct behaviour here, because the enemy's creature type decides whether it applies and the app cannot know that.
requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects from beasts and dragons.

requirements.what: Feet to Fins must appear on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the arcane tradition, cast at 3rd rank, with the spell's details reachable from the entry and this feat named as its source. The rank is stated explicitly in the printed text, so 3rd is what the player must read; where the granted rank differs from the spell's own base rank, the heightened rank has to be carried explicitly rather than inferred from the spell, or the sheet will understate what the character actually gets.
requirements.clause: You gain 3rd-rank Feet to Fins ... as arcane innate spells.

requirements.what: Water Breathing must appear as a second, separate innate spell entry — arcane tradition, cast at 2nd rank, details reachable, source named. Two distinct spells are granted by one feat, so one entry is not enough; the printed rank (2nd) is what must display.
requirements.clause: You gain ... 2nd-rank Water Breathing as arcane innate spells.

requirements.what: One use per day for EACH spell, tracked separately — the text says "each of these", so casting Feet to Fins must not consume the Water Breathing use. Each entry needs its own spendable use displayed beside it, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: You can cast each of these arcane innate spells once per day.

requirements.what: The resistance belongs on the EIDOLON's stat block, in the eidolon's own defences — per the standing companion ruling, a companion's bonus marks the companion, not you. The value is a formula, not a constant: it must resolve from the EIDOLON's Constitution modifier (not the summoner's), and it must re-resolve as that modifier changes with level and boosts, so a hardcoded number would be wrong for most characters.
requirements.clause: It gains resistance to physical damage equal to its Constitution modifier.

requirements.what: No requirement on the character's own sheet. Per DECIDED SCOPE (companions), the absence of this resistance from the summoner's own defences is the specified behaviour, not a defect — do not report it as one.
requirements.clause: Your eidolon is resilient against attacks.

requirements.what: Purge of Moments must exist as a usable activity in the actions list, with its full text reachable from that entry. The activity's entire resolution is manual, so the entry plus its popup is the surface — there is nothing to compute behind it.
requirements.clause: The feat is an activated ability: "a truth that you can put into practice by accelerating your passage through time to shake off harmful effects. Five rounds of apparent time occur for you."

requirements.what: One spendable use, displayed with the action and consumed when used. ⚠ The recharge cadence is HOURLY, not daily — the sheet must be able to express a use that returns on a cadence other than daily preparations, or this feat's frequency cannot be stated truthfully.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour

requirements.what: The resolution text must be legible at the point of use and nothing more is owed. Advancing five rounds of afflictions, conditions and persistent damage is exactly the per-round bookkeeping the owner ruled is not tracked (Principle B / Q1), so this clause contributes no number and clears no condition automatically; the player reads it and resolves it. The instructions to "roll saving throws, flat checks, damage" are internal steps of an activity and are not a lane. "No one, including you, can act during this time" is a GM-table statement with no sheet consequence.
requirements.clause: "effects on you run their course, including beneficial effects, negative effects, afflictions, conditions, and persistent damage. Roll saving throws, flat checks, damage, and any other rolls for those effects normally as if the time had passed."

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus to AC carried on the VEHICLE's stat block, in its AC breakdown, naming this feat as the source. Typed as circumstance so it can be compared against other circumstance bonuses to the vehicle's AC.
requirements.clause: "Your signature vehicle gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC"

requirements.what: A +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves on the VEHICLE's stat block. Fortitude only — the other two saves must not receive it, so the vehicle's saves have to be addressable individually rather than as one block.
requirements.clause: "and Fortitude saves"

requirements.what: An increase to the vehicle's maximum Hit Points equal to twice the CHARACTER's level. This is a formula reaching across records — the vehicle's HP total depends on its owner's level — and it must rescale on every level-up, so a fixed number written once cannot express it. It raises maximum HP (the permanent hpBonus shape), not temporary HP.
requirements.clause: "and increases its Hit Points by an amount equal to twice your level"

requirements.what: All three bonuses must attach to the one vehicle designated as "signature" by whatever record granted it, not to the character and not to every vehicle owned. The sheet therefore needs the notion of a designated signature vehicle that a later feat can address and modify.
requirements.clause: "Your signature vehicle" — the possessive singular naming a specific previously-granted companion record.

requirements.what: Nothing appears on the character's own AC, Fortitude or HP rows. Per the standing companion ruling, a companion's bonus marks the companion and its absence from the character's sheet is correct — this must not be reported as a gap.
requirements.clause: (whole feat, as it relates to the character's own stat rows)

requirements.what: Discerning Strike must appear as a usable action, with its Requirement — that you have already successfully identified this target with Recall Knowledge during this combat — printed in its popup. Per the Minor Omen exemplar, requirement text living in the popup is a real, sufficient surface for a clause the app cannot verify.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You have successfully identified the target with Recall Knowledge during this combat. --- "Attempt a Strike against the target"

requirements.what: The action's damage line must read as the wielded weapon's Strike damage PLUS 1d6 precision, so the player reads one number where they look it up rather than doing the addition from prose. Precision typing matters — it is what a precision-immune target ignores. The rider is not conditional in any interesting way: "if successful" on a Strike is just a hit, so it needs no degree-of-success surface.
requirements.clause: "if successful, you deal an additional 1d6 precision damage"

requirements.what: Text in the action's popup only; nothing computed. Two reasons: persistent bleed lands on the ENEMY, which is out of scope, and the clause is gated on a second record (Thorough Reports) plus a fact the app cannot hold — whether that creature's type was previously recorded. If the sheet can suppress this sentence for a character who lacks Thorough Reports it should, since it is dead text for them; that is the only expressible part.
requirements.clause: "If you have succeeded on a Recall Knowledge check against the target during this combat and their creature type was previously recorded using Thorough Reports, you also deal 1 point of persistent bleed damage."

requirements.what: No requirement. Temporary immunity is a per-enemy state, tracked on the target, and effects on enemies are explicitly not a lane. It is not a per-day use of the feat and must not be modelled as one — the character may use Discerning Strike again immediately on a different creature.
requirements.clause: "The creature is then temporarily immune to Discerning Strike for 1 day."

requirements.what: A usable ranged attack the player can roll: an attack entry at 30-foot range with an attack modifier, damage of 1d6 per 2 character levels, and the Requirement "you have a free hand" in its popup. The damage is a level-scaling formula (floor(level/2) d6), so it must be stored as an expression that rescales on level-up — a fixed die count is wrong at every level but one. The text names no damage type, only "heat or an arc of lightning" as flavour, so none can be asserted.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You have a free hand. --- "Make an attack roll against a creature within 30 feet. If you succeed, the beam deals 1d6 damage for every 2 levels you have to the target"

requirements.what: No requirement. Doubling damage on a critical hit is the general attack-roll rule, restated here for the reader; restating a rule the system already applies everywhere is not a lane.
requirements.clause: "or double damage on a critical success"

requirements.what: The same ability must be expressible under a SECOND action cost — 2 actions — resolved as an area effect with a saving throw instead of an attack roll, with the difference explained in the popup (Principle H: an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under both costs). The two versions differ in more than cost: one rolls an attack, the other calls for a save, so the entry cannot simply reuse the first version's attack modifier. ⚠ The printed text is defective — "damage all creatures in a , with a save" is missing both the area shape and the save type, so no area, no DC and no save can be stated from this source; whatever is built can only print what is there, and the missing values need to come from a corrected source.
requirements.clause: **Awakening** "Instead of making an attack roll to damage a single creature within 30 feet, you can use Blasting Beams as a 2-action activity to damage all creatures in a , with a save."

requirements.what: A second selectable version of the attack, chosen per use, that changes numbers the player reads: damage die drops from d6 to d4 (same per-2-levels scaling), the attack gains the AGILE trait (which changes the multiple-attack penalty and so changes the second and third attack modifiers on the line), and the free-hand Requirement is replaced by "your eyes must be uncovered". Because agile and the die size both move numbers, this cannot be prose alone — the sheet must carry the eye-beam form as its own attack entry or as a switchable variant of the first.
requirements.clause: **Awakening** "You can choose to launch smaller, quicker beams from your eyes instead. These deal d4s instead of d6s, but the attack has the agile trait, and you don't need a hand free to make it, though your eyes must be uncovered."

requirements.what: Both variants are printed under an "Awakening" heading, which marks them as later unlocks rather than things this feat gives immediately. The text states no trigger, level or condition for an Awakening, so no gate can be specified from it — but the sheet must be able to say which of the three versions are currently available, otherwise a character who has just taken the feat is shown two attacks they cannot make.
requirements.clause: The two **Awakening** headings themselves, as a gating structure on the clauses beneath them.

requirements.what: Each animal companion advances to the MATURE type, and that advancement's stat consequences must be reflected on the companion's own stat block — the mature grade is a real change to the creature, not a label. The character's own sheet gains nothing; per the standing companion ruling that absence is correct.
requirements.clause: "All of your animal companions grow up, becoming mature animal companions and gaining additional capabilities."

requirements.what: The advancement must apply to EVERY animal companion the character has, not to one designated companion. This plural is the entire difference between this feat and the ordinary Mature Animal Companion, so a single-target upgrade silently under-delivers for a beastmaster holding several companions — and it means the upgrade has to reach companions granted later, after this feat was taken, as well as ones already owned.
requirements.clause: "ALL of your animal companions" (plural), as against the singular companion the base version upgrades.

requirements.what: The independence rule must be readable on the companion (or on the feat entry the companion points to): one action per round without spending Command an Animal, limited to Strike or Stride, or Burrow/Climb/Fly/Swim if the companion has that Speed; usable at any point in your turn while you are not mid-action; and if used, the companion gets nothing else that round and cannot be Commanded later. This computes nothing — it is action economy inside an encounter, and no number on any sheet moves — but it is the operative half of the feat and must not be lost. The speed-conditional list needs no separate expression: the companion's stat block already carries which Speeds it has.
requirements.clause: "Your animal companion has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the Command an Animal action, your animal companion can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim if it has that Speed)… If it does, that's all the actions it gets that round—you can't Command it later."

**Requirements** You have Spun a Tale. **Trigger** The villain of the tale you've spun makes an attack roll with a given weapon or unarmed attack, uses a particular special ability (such as a Breath Weapon), or Casts a Spell against the hero, and they used that same attack, special ability, or spell against the hero on the previous turn.
requirements.what: A triggered activity that appears in the reactions list, with its full Trigger (the villain repeats the same attack, special ability, or spell against the hero) and its Requirement (you have Spun a Tale) written in its popup. Per Principle E that listing is normally the entire requirement.

requirements.clause: You narrate a tale of the hero's success, granting them a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC or saving throw against the triggering effect.
requirements.what: Nothing. The +2 lands on the hero — another creature — so no number and no star on your own AC or saves (Ruling F/N). Nor is this Principle A's shape: the feat modifies no other record, it IS the record, so its own description is already the whole indication. The ally also elects AC or save, a target-side choice the sheet has no reason to model.

requirements.clause: If the villain has used the same effect against the hero on both of their last two turns, and you used Rule of Three on that effect last turn as well, the bonus increases to +4.
requirements.what: Nothing computable. The escalation keys off turn history the sheet does not track, and the value it raises belongs to someone else. The sentence must simply survive verbatim in the activity's popup rather than being summarised away, since the player is the one who has to judge it.

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks made as initiative rolls.
requirements.what: A `*` on Perception carrying +2 circumstance with its restriction printed — only when the Perception check is made as an initiative roll. This must NOT be a flat Perception bonus: it applies to one specific roll, so it belongs in the restricted/situational surface and stays outside the Perception total (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks made as initiative rolls.
requirements.what: The same +2 must also be visible wherever the sheet presents the initiative roll itself, not only on the skill — Q2 rules 'both', star the skill AND the action, and Ruling D puts the mark on the thing the player is looking at when it matters. If initiative can be rolled with something other than Perception, the star applies only to the Perception version.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** Your nimbus is active. --- ... you launch your celestial armament into the air, where it flies with a mind of its own, attacking every enemy within your nimbus.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with its Requirement (your nimbus is active) and its full text in the popup. The requirement is text the player checks — nothing needs to gate the action on the nimbus's state.

requirements.clause: Spend 1 Mythic Point.
requirements.what: The action must state a cost of 1 Mythic Point, and spending it must draw down a Mythic Point pool the sheet tracks and can restore. The feat does not grant that pool, it consumes it — so what is required is that a spendable mythic resource exists to be named and decremented, and that this action's cost is legible beside it.

requirements.clause: Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your penalty doesn't increase until you have made all your attacks.
requirements.what: Nothing to compute — the player performs the Strikes — but this is an EXCEPTION to the general multiple-attack-penalty rule, not a restatement of it, so it must be carried verbatim in the activity's popup. Dropping it would leave the player applying the ordinary escalating penalty, which is the opposite of what the feat says.

requirements.clause: If you're not currently wielding your celestial armament, it immediately teleports into your hand. ... After these attacks are complete, your weapon returns to your hand.
requirements.what: Nothing. Internal steps of the activity, and they cancel out — the armament starts and ends in your hand, so no equipped/wielded state changes and no inventory surface is owed.

requirements.clause: Make a Strike with that weapon against each enemy in the bright light of your nimbus.
requirements.what: Nothing. Internal steps the player performs, and the set of targets is decided by who is standing in the nimbus's bright light — position the sheet can never know (Ruling M). The Strike itself is the character's existing celestial-armament Strike, unmodified by this feat.

requirements.clause: When you're attempting a skill check involving the drawing of cards or resolving the effects of a divination effect ... you gain a +2 status bonus to the check.
requirements.what: A `*` carrying +2 status with the printed trigger, on every skill that could plausibly be called for. The text names no skill at all, so per Ruling H stay open — star everything plausible with the trigger in the note rather than narrowing it to one skill, which would put a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: (including attempting a saving throw against a hostile divination effect against you)
requirements.what: A `*` on all three saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will — carrying +2 status against hostile divination effects. Q2: when a bonus applies to saves generally rather than to one named save, star all three, because the text does not say which save a hostile divination will call for.

requirements.clause: When you draw a card to determine your harrow omen, perform Harrow Casting, cast Harrowing, or if you activate a magical deck of cards, draw 2 cards, and choose the one you prefer as your actual card drawn.
requirements.what: A marker on each record this feat modifies, wherever the character actually holds it — the harrow omen feature, the Harrow Casting action, the Harrowing spell, and any activatable magical deck of cards in inventory — each reading 'draw 2, keep the one you prefer'. Principle C and Q8: a feat that changes what another record does must be reflected in that record, on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, not only in this feat's own text.

requirements.clause: You can even use this ability when drawing from a Deck of Many Things, but only once per deck. The unused card is shuffled back into the stack.
requirements.what: The same draw-2-keep-1 marker on a Deck of Many Things, but carrying the limit 'once per deck'. This is not a per-day resource and not a per-character one — it is scoped to an individual item — so what is required is that the restriction is legible as text on that item's marker; the shuffling back of the unused card is narrative and needs nothing.

requirements.clause: You create an auditory illusion that comes from a square within 500 feet and can be as loud as four normal humans talking. ... You can have any creature within 40 feet of the illusion, or that comes within 40 feet of it during the duration, attempt a save against your class DC. This is a mental effect.
requirements.what: The impulse appears in the actions list with its complete text in the popup — the 500-foot placement, the four-humans loudness limit, the 40-foot save radius (including creatures that enter it later), and the mental trait. Nothing here is computed; the entry's existence and its full text are the requirement.

requirements.clause: attempt a save against your class DC
requirements.what: Nothing. The DC is your existing class DC, an ordinary character stat the sheet already presents, and this feat neither raises nor restricts it. The popup naming which DC applies is part of carrying the text, not a separate surface — and Ruling D's DC guidance concerns a DC on your own save breakdown, which this is not.

requirements.clause: The illusion lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse.
requirements.what: Nothing. Q1: an effect lasting a round is not implemented — indication only — and this one changes none of your numbers even while running, so it earns no mode. Sustaining is a general rule; the duration line just needs to be readable in the popup.

requirements.clause: **Success** The creature is unaffected, disbelieves the illusion, and is temporarily immune for 1 hour. **Failure** The creature is fascinated with the source of the sound until the end of its next turn. ... **Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is fascinated for 1 minute or until it disbelieves.
requirements.what: Nothing computed. Every outcome is a condition on an enemy plus that enemy's temporary immunity — Q4: the entry itself is the whole surface. The degree-of-success block is prose that must be present and readable in the popup, nothing more.

requirements.clause: though the GM might require you to attempt a check or know a language for it to be convincing
requirements.what: Nothing. Explicit GM adjudication, and the check it hints at is neither named nor bonused — Ruling I: where the rules name no trigger, star nothing.
A permanent resistance 5 to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing — three separate physical damage types from one source, all shown in the defences breakdown and attributed to this feat.
requirements.clause: You gain resistance 5 to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

requirements.what: The same three resistances must be able to carry a CONDITIONAL higher value (10) whose condition has two halves the sheet must express together: your own sanctification (do you have the holy or the unholy trait) selects WHICH condition applies, and the damage source's opposing trait selects WHEN it applies. So the entry is not a second flat number but a value that reads "5 (10 against unholy creatures)" for a holy character and "5 (10 against holy creatures)" for an unholy one, and shows only the plain 5 for a character who is neither. The character-side half is derivable from the sheet and must drive which text appears; the creature-side half is a condition the player reads, per Ruling H's "printed trigger in the note".
requirements.clause: If you're holy, this resistance increases to 10 against unholy creatures, and if you're unholy it increases to 10 against holy creatures.

requirements.what: A note on AC — the number the player looks at when this matters (Ruling D: the mark attaches to the thing it modifies, not to a new generic surface) — stating that a natural 20 on an attack roll against you does not improve the result by one degree. Not computable: the app never sees the enemy's die. This is a defence of your own, not an ally-facing or enemy-facing effect, so DECIDED SCOPE does not remove it; what it removes is any expectation of a number.
requirements.clause: creatures and effects that roll a natural 20 on an attack roll against you don't improve their result by one degree of success.

requirements.what: A +2 circumstance bonus that must appear on AC and on ALL THREE saves — "all defenses" is the generic case Q2 settles by starring Fortitude, Reflex and Will together, plus AC. Ruling B puts it in the situational lane rather than the flat total, because its `when` carries TWO independent restrictions that must both be legible: your shield is raised, and the effect has the light or visual trait. The shield-raised half is a state the player turns on and off (Q11), so whatever expresses it must be able to key a situational bonus to a toggleable state rather than to a permanent condition.
requirements.clause: While your shield is raised, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all defenses against effects with the light or visual trait.

requirements.what: A degree-of-success floor on saves: critical failure becomes failure, under the same double condition as the bonus. Not computable, so it is text — but it must ride the same star on all three saves, because that is where the player is looking when a light or visual effect makes them roll. It is a distinct promise from the +2 and must not be swallowed by it: the +2 changes a number, this changes an outcome band.
requirements.clause: If you critically fail your save against such an effect while your shield is raised, you fail instead.

requirements.what: The mirror clause lands on YOUR DC, not on a check you roll — an effect that critically succeeds against your DC gets a success instead. Ruling D's DC-only shape governs: an entry in the DC's own breakdown, worded to say it hits the DC and not the check, with the star beside the DC. The rules do not name which DC a light or visual effect rolls against, so per Ruling H stay open — surface it on every DC plausibly targeted rather than narrowing it to one and putting a ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.
requirements.clause: Likewise, if such an effect critically succeeds against your DC, it's a success instead.

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list named Preserve the Moment, with its trigger (your turn ends) and its frequency (once per day) shown in its popup. Principle E: for a reaction this is often the whole surface. Because the printed text is long — a full worked example of which rolls are and are not recorded — the note caps at about one line with a click-through to the complete text (Ruling H).
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** Your turn ends. --- [the reaction itself]

requirements.what: One use per day: a spendable use displayed with the reaction, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. Noting which actions you took and which die results you rolled is player and GM bookkeeping about a turn that has already happened; the sheet has no knowledge of your actions or your dice, and the distinction the text draws (your own actions yes, saves forced on you by others or the environment no) is adjudication, not computation. The full text being readable in the reaction's popup is already owed by the clause above, and that is the entire surface. Do not invent a recorded-actions store for this.
requirements.clause: Note the actions you took during the turn that just ended … including the die roll results (not the actual check results). Die rolls you made as a result of others' actions on you or from the environment are not recorded.

requirements.what: A SECOND, separately-listed reaction — Restore the Moment — reachable from the reactions list with its own details. This is a granted record in its own right and is easy to miss behind the first reaction; the feat makes two promises, not one.
requirements.clause: You gain the Restore the Moment reaction

requirements.what: A single use on a 24-HOUR window measured from when Preserve the Moment fired — not a per-day resource that resets at daily preparations, and not permanently available. Two things must be expressible: the use exists only after Preserve the Moment has been spent, and its clock is a rolling 24 hours rather than the rest cycle every other limited use in the game keys to. If the window itself cannot be tracked, the availability condition must at minimum be carried as text on the Restore the Moment entry so the player is not shown an untriggered reaction as though it were live.
requirements.clause: which you can use once during the next 24 hours.

requirements.what: A marker reflected in the Adaptive Stratagem action itself, showing that this feat widens what that action may do. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing — the player reads Adaptive Stratagem when they use it, not this feat's entry. Nothing lands on a stat.
requirements.clause: When you use Adaptive Stratagem, you can replace any master tactics or legendary tactics you have prepared with any other tactics in your folio.

requirements.what: The prepared-tactics list must permit a swap on entries that hold MASTER and LEGENDARY tactics, with the replacement drawn from the folio. Without this, the feat's only promise is undeliverable: the swap has to reach the higher-tier prepared slots specifically, which are precisely the ones the base action leaves alone. Two things the choice surface must express — which prepared entries are eligible to be replaced (all of them, once this feat is held), and that the pool being chosen from is the folio, not the whole tactics list. Per Q9 the picker offers only what is legally available, so it filters to the folio's contents.
requirements.clause: you can replace any master tactics or legendary tactics you have prepared with any other tactics in your folio.

requirements.what: Grant the Deny Advantage class feature and surface its details where the player can read them, exactly as Principle G requires. Deny Advantage offers no choice, so unlike Devout Blessing this grant carries no picker — the details half of Principle G is the whole obligation. Whatever Deny Advantage itself does to the sheet is owed by that feature's own record, not by this feat; this feat's single promise is that the feature is present and legible.
requirements.clause: You gain the Deny Advantage class feature.
**Trigger** You roll initiative or a hazard attacks you.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions/triggered-actions list named Rapid Manifestation, with its trigger — "You roll initiative or a hazard attacks you" — printed in its popup. Principle E: for a triggered ability that is what the entry itself is, and the trigger belongs in the popup rather than anywhere else on the sheet. Both halves of the trigger must survive; a trigger reduced to "you roll initiative" drops the hazard case.

requirements.clause: You Manifest your Soulforged Armament.
requirements.what: The entry must name the action it performs — Manifest your Soulforged Armament — and reach that action's own details, since the whole content of this feat is a route to an activity the character already owns. Performing the Manifest is an internal step of the activity and needs nothing further: the app lists the action, the player performs it.

requirements.clause: You Manifest your Soulforged Armament.
requirements.what: A marker on the Manifest Soulforged Armament action itself showing it can also be taken by this trigger, with the explanation in that action's popup. Principle H (Quick Recognition, answer 13) is exactly this shape — an action reachable at a different cost appears where the player looks the action up, not only on the feat — and Q8 confirms Ruling D's shape applies to marking the action a feat modifies. Without it the player who opens Manifest sees only its printed cost.

requirements.clause: Your unwavering soul brings up your defenses as soon as you're in danger.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing required.

requirements.clause: You call upon fate, divinity, or whatever other power has carried you this far, demanding that it carry you just a little bit farther.
requirements.what: An entry in the actions list for Summon Mythic Power that the player can take and read. There is no Trigger line, so this is an activity the character chooses, not a reaction; its cost and text belong in its popup.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day displayed on the entry, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations/rest. The frequency is the only limit the text states, so the use counter must be visible and clickable rather than left as prose.

requirements.clause: You regain 1 Mythic Point.
requirements.what: A Mythic Point pool on the sheet — a current value against a maximum — that this action increments by 1, not above its maximum. ⚠ NO LANE IN THE MANUAL COVERS THIS. The closest analogue is `focusPool` (`focusPoolBonus`/`refocusRestore`), which restores a different named pool; nothing in sections A–K names Mythic Points. This is the "clearly mechanical, no lane at all" bucket the manual asks a classifier to emit. It is not excluded by any DECIDED SCOPE ruling: it lands on your own sheet, it is not HP or damage, and it is not an ally-, enemy-, aura-, or companion-facing effect. Note the requirement is a REGAIN, so a bare per-day counter is not a substitute — the pool must already exist and be spendable for a restore to mean anything.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** Your turn begins.
requirements.what: A triggered entry in the reactions/triggered-actions list named Effortless Captivation, with its trigger — "Your turn begins" — printed in its popup. Principle E: the entry plus its trigger is the surface.

requirements.clause: You immediately gain the effects of the Sustain a Spell action
requirements.what: A marker on Sustain a Spell showing it is also available free at the start of your turn through this feat, with the explanation in that action's popup. Principle H, from the owner's Quick Recognition answer: an action whose cost changes conditionally must appear under BOTH costs, because the player looks the action up, not the feat. Performing the Sustain is otherwise an internal step and needs nothing.

requirements.clause: which you can use only to extend the duration of an enchantment or illusion spell
requirements.what: The restriction must be legible wherever this free Sustain is offered — enchantment or illusion spells only. It is not computable (the app cannot know which spell the player will sustain), so it is printed text on the entry and on the Sustain marker, not a filter. Losing this clause turns a narrow free action into an unrestricted one.

requirements.clause: extend the duration of an enchantment or illusion spell
requirements.what: No duration tracking is owed. Rounds are not tracked (Principle B / Q1), so an extension of a spell's duration contributes no number anywhere.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits.
requirements.what: Wizard-archetype spellcasting must reach the sheet: spell slots that appear on the Spells page under the wizard archetype and open new ranks as the archetype's basic benefits specify. ⚠ The printed text here is elliptical — "You gain the benefits" names them without listing them — but the next sentence's own wording, "Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the wizard archetype", is the text's own evidence that this feat is what causes slots of new ranks to arrive. Without slots the second sentence can never fire.

requirements.clause: Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the wizard archetype
requirements.what: The arrival of a slot of a NEW rank must be an event the sheet can recognise, because it is the trigger for the two-spell grant below. A slot count that simply grows is not enough; the sheet has to distinguish "a rank you already had" from "a rank you have just reached", and it must do so once per rank rather than once per slot.

requirements.clause: add two common spells of that rank to your spellbook
requirements.what: Two picks per newly reached rank, offered to the player, filtered to COMMON spells OF THAT RANK. Q9 governs: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, unless they toggle "show options not meeting prerequisites". Q5's "rarity does not gate the shop" is explicitly about the ITEM list and does not license offering uncommon spells here — the restriction is written into this grant. Unpicked picks must remain visible as outstanding slots rather than silently vanishing.

requirements.clause: add two common spells of that rank to your spellbook
requirements.what: A spellbook must exist for the picks to land in, and taking this feat has to ensure the character has one — the text presumes "your spellbook" without granting it. This is the Q14 point 6 shape ("taking a feat that grants a formula book ensures the character has one") applied to the repository this feat writes into.

requirements.clause: You gain the benefits.
requirements.what: The granted slots are prepared casting — the text names both a "spell slot" and a "spellbook" — so the sheet must let the player fill those slots at daily preparations from what the spellbook holds, and the slot must show what is prepared in it.

requirements.clause: add two common spells of that rank to your spellbook
requirements.what: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not by the owner, and flagged rather than assumed: Q14 point 9 ruled that formulas granted into a formula book are a ONE-TIME WRITE owned by the book, never a live derivation, because losing the book must lose them. A spellbook is the same shape — a losable container the grant writes into. If that reasoning carries across, these two spells belong to the book once chosen; if it does not, this needs an owner ruling. I am not asserting the answer.

requirements.clause: Your patron grants you a leshy familiar.
requirements.what: A familiar on the sheet, typed as a leshy, with its own stat block and its own inventory. Per the companions ruling, anything the familiar itself gains marks the FAMILIAR, not you — absence of the familiar's own numbers from your sheet is correct, but the familiar's existence and its leshy typing are this feat's promise and must be visible.

requirements.clause: If you already had a familiar, this leshy replaces your previous familiar, as if your previous familiar had been slain.
requirements.what: The grant must REPLACE an existing familiar rather than add a second one — the character ends with one familiar, and the replacement has to be legible to the player so they know what happened to the old one. This is a redundancy rule of the same family as `redundantFallback`, but pointed at a companion grant rather than a proficiency. Missing it produces a character holding two familiars, which the text forbids.

requirements.clause: as if your previous familiar had been slain
requirements.what: The "as if slain" wording is narrative framing for the replacement above; it carries no separate requirement.

requirements.clause: You don't take circumstance penalties to ranged spell attacks ... caused by foliage
requirements.what: A `*` on spell attack rolls carrying the foliage clause. There is no number to add — it is the negation of a penalty — so it is a situational marker with the printed trigger in its note (Ruling B: a restricted effect belongs in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, not in the flat total).

requirements.clause: You don't take circumstance penalties to ... Perception checks caused by foliage
requirements.what: A `*` on Perception carrying the same foliage clause. Ruling J/D: the mark goes on the specific thing the player is looking at when it matters — here the Perception entry itself.

requirements.clause: your targeted attacks don't require a flat check to succeed against a target concealed only by such vegetation
requirements.what: A `*` on your attack rolls — Strikes and spell attacks, since "targeted attacks" names no narrower set — carrying the no-flat-check clause. Ruling H applies: the rules leave the scope open, so star everything plausible and print the trigger rather than narrowing it into a ruling of your own. The concealed condition sits on the enemy and gets no surface, but the removal of YOUR flat check is a change to your own roll and does.

requirements.clause: In addition, you gain the ability to see through leaves, vines, and other foliage.
requirements.what: No sense requirement. This sentence is the umbrella statement whose mechanics are the two sentences that follow it; it names no sense the manual recognises (not darkvision, low-light, scent, tremorsense, or echolocation) and adds nothing beyond the two stars above. Per Ruling A, an umbrella restatement earns no entry of its own.

requirements.clause: You have a particular affinity for leafy plants.
requirements.what: Flavour. Nothing required.

requirements.clause: When you consume one of your alchemical items that has the elixir and infused traits and a duration of 1 minute or longer, that elixir's duration is doubled.
requirements.what: The doubled duration must be reflected in THE ELIXIR ITSELF, not on a general stat (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing; Ruling D: the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). So every inventory item carrying BOTH the elixir and infused traits whose printed duration is 1 minute or longer must show the doubled figure where the player reads that item's duration, with a `*` naming this feat as the source. This also requires the sheet to be able to select items by the conjunction of two traits plus a duration threshold — an item qualifies only if it is elixir AND infused AND lasts 1 minute or more; a 1-round or instantaneous elixir, or an infused non-elixir, must NOT be marked.

requirements.clause: If you created the item with Quick Alchemy, this can't cause it to exceed the 10-minute duration limit.
requirements.what: A cap clause carried in the same marker's text. The sheet cannot know which specific vial in the inventory came out of Quick Alchemy versus Advanced Alchemy, so this is not a computed ceiling — it is printed text on the doubled-duration marker reading that a Quick Alchemy elixir is capped at 10 minutes. This is the capped-note shape (Ruling H: printed trigger in the note, one line with a click-through to the full text).

requirements.clause: Integrating your own personal energy into the elixirs you create causes them to affect you for longer.
requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour.

requirements.clause: (whole-feat shape check)
requirements.what: NOT a mode. The doubling cannot be switched off — it applies whenever you consume a qualifying elixir — so per Q11 this is a passive modification, not a toggleable state. It also grants no action, no resource, and no per-day use.

requirements.clause: You can cast Translate, Sound Body, and See the Unseen as innate spells, each once per day.
requirements.what: Three separate innate spell entries on the Spells page — Translate, Sound Body, See the Unseen — each identified as innate, each at its own base rank (the text names no heightened rank, so each casts at the rank it is printed at), each with its full details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source.

requirements.clause: …each once per day.
requirements.what: Three INDEPENDENT once-per-day uses, one per spell — not a shared pool of three. Each spell shows a single spendable use beside it, consumed when that spell is cast, restored at daily preparations, and spending one must not spend the others.

requirements.clause: If you could already cast spells, these spells are of the same tradition.
requirements.what: The tradition of these three grants is NOT a fixed value on the feat — it resolves from the character. If the character already has spellcasting, all three inherit that tradition; a stored constant cannot express this. The sheet must therefore be able to state a tradition computed from the rest of the build, and must state it truthfully beside the spells (Q12: whichever spelling leaves the player least confused — the tradition shown must be the tradition these spells actually have, not one inferred from the character's other innate grants). ⚠ OPEN, flagged rather than assumed: the text says "the same tradition" as though there were exactly one; a character with two spellcasting traditions has no answer in the printed text. Per Ruling H, staying open means offering the player the choice rather than the app silently picking one.

requirements.clause: Otherwise, they are arcane spells, you use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability…
requirements.what: The fallback branch, live only when the character had no prior spellcasting: the three spells are arcane, and their spell attack roll and spell DC key off INTELLIGENCE. The default key attribute for innate spells is overridden here, so the attribute used by these entries must be settable per grant and must be visible where the player reads the attack/DC — otherwise the sheet shows a number computed from the wrong attribute.

requirements.clause: …and you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for arcane spells.
requirements.what: A trained proficiency in arcane spell attack rolls and arcane spell DCs, appearing in the proficiency list — and it is CONDITIONAL, granted only in the non-caster branch. A character who could already cast spells gets no proficiency from this feat at all, so the proficiency grant must be able to depend on whether other spellcasting exists on the build rather than being granted unconditionally.

requirements.clause: You see what others don't, and you've developed magical tricks to find hidden truth.
requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour.

requirements.clause: You gain resistance 10 to physical damage…
requirements.what: Resistance 10 to physical damage — the category, not a single type — appearing in the defences with this feat named as its source. It must cover bludgeoning, piercing and slashing together rather than requiring three separate entries, or the player reading their resistances sees the wrong shape.

requirements.clause: …but weakness 5 to mental damage.
requirements.what: Weakness 5 to mental damage, displayed in the same defences area as the resistance and actually applied, not merely printed inside the feat's description. A downside is as load-bearing as an upside and must not be silently dropped while the resistance lands.

requirements.clause: You can change your appearance on a whim. This takes a single action, which has the concentrate trait, has the effects of Illusory Disguise, and lasts until you change your appearance again.
requirements.what: A new named activity in the actions list at a cost of 1 action, carrying the concentrate trait, with its popup stating that it has the effects of Illusory Disguise (that spell reachable/linked from the popup rather than re-described) and that it lasts until you change your appearance again.

requirements.clause: …lasts until you change your appearance again.
requirements.what: An ongoing state the player turns on and can end at will (Q11: it can be shut down, so it is a mode rather than a passive). It changes NO sheet numbers — an illusory disguise alters appearance only — so this is the display-only shape of Ruling E case 3: the player can see the disguise is running and read what it does, and it contributes no modifiers. No duration timer is owed; "until you change it again" is player-ended, not clock-ended.

requirements.clause: Once per year, when you die, you automatically return to life the next day as long as one living sentient creature on your plane remembers you; the memories enable you to reconstruct yourself from their thoughts. You appear in the vicinity of the creature that remembers you most strongly.
requirements.what: A marker on the death/Dying condition carrying this clause, following Ruling D's own worked precedent ("The Survivor marks the Dying condition") — the mark lives on the thing the player is looking at when it matters, and the moment this matters is the moment they die. The conditions (a living sentient creature on your plane remembers you; you reappear near whoever remembers you most strongly) and the next-day timing are printed text in that marker; the GM adjudicates them, so nothing is computed.

requirements.clause: Once per year, when you die…
