requirements.what: A once-per-YEAR use. If it is represented as a spendable resource at all, its refresh must not be daily preparations or a rest — a per-year frequency is the only one this feat has, and restoring it overnight would be wrong. ⚠ If no yearly frequency can be expressed, the honest surface is the printed frequency inside the marker above and no pip at all, rather than a pip that refreshes on the wrong schedule.

requirements.clause: When you transform using Monstrosity Shape, you can take on a kaiju form.
requirements.what: Kaiju must appear as a selectable form ON THE MONSTROSITY SHAPE RECORD itself (Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). The player who opens Monstrosity Shape to choose a form must see kaiju listed there alongside the spell's native forms — a description on this feat alone does not satisfy it, because that is not where the player is looking when they transform.

requirements.clause: When you take this feat, choose acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage; this is the damage your breath weapon deals. You can't change this later.
requirements.what: A five-option choice — acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic — offered when the feat is taken and recorded on the character, because the pick is not cosmetic: it determines the breath weapon's damage type in the form's stat block below. The chosen type must flow through to the breath weapon entry so the player reads their actual damage type rather than a list of five. ("You can't change this later" is a rules statement about re-picking; per Principle K re-choosing lives in the builder and owes no sheet surface.)

requirements.clause: The battle form is Gargantuan size with the following specific abilities… **Kaiju** Speed 40 feet; physical resistance 5;
requirements.what: A battle-form mode that REALLY OVERRIDES the stats it names, and that makes plain both that a mode is active and what changed (Q3, verbatim). Specifically: override size to Gargantuan, override Speed to 40 feet (override, not add — a character with a 25-foot Speed must read 40, and one with a 50-foot Speed must also read 40), and grant physical resistance 5. Size and Speed here are replacements, so the mode needs the ability to SET a stat, not only to add to it.

requirements.clause: **Melee** ⟨1⟩ jaws (reach 20 feet), **Damage** 3d12+20 piercing; **Melee** ⟨1⟩ claws (agile, reach 20 feet), **Damage** 3d8+20 slashing;
requirements.what: Two form strikes available while the mode is active: jaws — 1 action, reach 20 feet, 3d12+20 piercing; and claws — 1 action, agile, reach 20 feet, 3d8+20 slashing. Their damage is a FIXED printed value, not derived from the character's Strength or from weapon runes, so the strike display must be able to show a flat authored damage expression and a per-strike reach that differs from the character's normal reach. ⚠ The printed text names no attack modifier for these strikes, so none should be invented — only what the text gives (cost, traits, reach, damage) can be surfaced.

requirements.clause: **Breath Weapon** ⟨2⟩ (evocation, primal) Each creature in a takes damage (of your chosen damage type), with a save against your spell DC. Once activated, your breath weapon can't be used again for 1d4 rounds.
requirements.what: A Breath Weapon action available while the form is active: 2 actions, traits evocation and primal, dealing the damage type chosen above, with the save taken against YOUR spell DC — so the popup must show the DC the enemies roll against, resolved from this character's own spell DC rather than printed as a constant. The 1d4-round lockout is text only: rounds are not tracked (Principle B), so it contributes no counter, but the player must still be able to read it. ⚠ The printed text is defective at source — "Each creature in a takes damage" states neither the AREA nor the damage amount. Nothing can be authored for the missing area or dice without inventing it; the requirement is that the entry carry what the text actually gives and that the omission stay visible rather than be papered over.

requirements.clause: the damage values already include the extra die from being a 9th-rank spell
requirements.what: Nothing. An explanatory aside about how the printed numbers were derived; it asks for no surface.

requirements.clause: Witnessing the might of the kaiju King Mogaru, Alru, and Toraloa up close awoke a new ferocity within you.
requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour.

requirements.clause: When you Treat a Disease or a Poison… increase the circumstance bonus granted on a success to +4
requirements.what: A `*` on BOTH the skill and the actions (Q2: both). That means a star on every skill that could perform Treat a Disease or Treat a Poison (Ruling C — star every skill that could perform the named action, not just the obvious one), AND a star on the Treat a Disease and Treat a Poison action entries themselves. The star's text states the circumstance bonus granted on a success is +4 instead of the standard +2. Note the bonus lands on the PATIENT's later saving throw, not on your Medicine check, so the marker must say what it modifies — it must not read as +4 to the check.

requirements.clause: …or someone else uses one of these actions on you…
requirements.what: The self-facing half is a genuine bonus on YOUR sheet and is the clause most easily missed: when another character Treats your Disease or Poison, the +4 circumstance bonus lands on your own saving throw against that disease or poison. That earns a `*` on the saving throw the player will actually roll, carrying the +4 and carrying the condition that it applies only when someone has treated you. It is a restricted bonus, so it belongs in the situational lane rather than in the flat save total (Ruling B: a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct).

requirements.clause: and if the result of the patient's saving throw is a success, the patient gets a critical success.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success UPGRADE — success becomes critical success on the treated creature's save. The lane vocabulary has no computed route for a result upgrade, and this one fires on a roll the sheet does not make, so the requirement is that the clause be carried as text in the same markers as the bonus: on the Treat a Disease / Treat a Poison actions, and on your own save's star for the case where you are the patient. It changes no number, so it must not be modelled as one — but it must be READABLE in both places, because it is the more valuable half of the feat and would otherwise vanish.

requirements.clause: When you Treat a Disease or a Poison [on someone else] — the bonus and the upgrade land on the ally.
requirements.what: No number on your sheet for the ally-facing direction (Ruling F). Per Principle A the requirement it does carry is already covered above: an indication on the record it modifies — the Treat a Disease and Treat a Poison actions. Nothing further is owed, and "the ally's bonus never reaches them" is not a defect.

requirements.clause: You learned folk medicine to help recover from diseases and poison, and using it diligently has made you especially resilient.
requirements.what: Nothing. Flavour — "especially resilient" is not a bonus.

A triggered ability entry named Ruby Resurrection, appearing wherever triggered abilities are listed, with its Trigger (you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points) and its Frequency shown in the popup along with the full effect text. Per Principle E, that entry is usually the whole surface — nothing further is owed for the effect body itself.
requirements.clause: Frequency once per day; Trigger you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points

requirements.what: One spendable use per day displayed on the entry, consumed when the ability fires and restored at daily preparations. The count is load-bearing here because the second, automatic trigger only exists while the use is unspent.
requirements.clause: Frequency once per day

requirements.what: No requirement. Setting current HP to a fixed value is a Hit Point change, and HP and damage never move sheet stats even inside a mode; the player applies it. The number only needs to be readable in the ability's own text.
requirements.clause: Change your current Hit Points to 30

requirements.what: No requirement — no innate-spell entry is owed. This is an internal step of the activity (the app lists the action, the player performs it), and its damage lands on other creatures. The rank and the you-are-excluded caveat need only be readable in the ability's text.
requirements.clause: cast a 6th-rank fireball centred on yourself, which does not affect you

requirements.what: The same entry's popup must carry the second, automatic trigger — that if the ability is still unspent when you die you remain in initiative and it fires at the start of your next turn, returning you at 0 HP before its normal effects, and only if remains exist. This is a distinct trigger condition from the printed Trigger line and is easily lost if only the Trigger field is surfaced.
requirements.clause: if unused and you die, it triggers automatically at the start of your next turn, bringing you back at 0 HP, only if remains exist

requirements.what: The entry's trait list is character-dependent: it must resolve to the tradition trait matching the spells that character casts, or say in words that it does. A fixed trait list authored on the record cannot express this. Flagging as open: the text names no trait for a character who casts no spells.
requirements.clause: Special — this feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast

requirements.what: A named activity, Boaster's Challenge, in the actions list: select one creature you can see, then attempt a check with one of the skills the text names against that creature's Will DC. The choice of which skill to use is made per use, so the entry must present the skills as alternatives rather than fixing one. NOTE: the skill names are stripped out of the evidence text (it reads "attempt a , , or check"), so I cannot name them; the requirement is that whichever skills the printed text names all appear.
requirements.clause: select a creature you can see and attempt a skill check against its Will DC to declare a challenge

requirements.what: The popup must carry that the challenge needs a linguistic, auditory, or visual component and gains the matching trait. The trait varies with how the player performs it, so this is text on the entry, not a computed trait set.
requirements.clause: the challenge must include a linguistic, auditory, or visual component and gains the corresponding trait

requirements.what: A `*` on every skill the printed text allows for the challenge check, so the player sees the feat where they look up that skill's number (Principle D / Ruling C — star every skill that could perform the named action, and Q2 — star the skill AND the action).
requirements.clause: the challenge is rolled with one of several named skills

requirements.what: A `*` on your Strike damage — weapon and unarmed alike — carrying the +2 status bonus against the challenged foe, and the tiering: +4 if you are master in the skill you used, +6 if legendary. The tier depends on your rank in the skill actually used for the challenge, so the star must state all three tiers rather than resolve one. Because the effect lasts only until the end of your next turn, Q1 makes this indication only — no computed modifier, no mode.
requirements.clause: on a success, +2 status bonus to damage with weapon or unarmed Strikes against that foe until the end of your next turn; +4 if master in the skill used, +6 if legendary

requirements.what: No requirement. Q15: an effect that fires on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED, and a longer duration on an already-described bonus is not complicated. It rides along in the star's text.
requirements.clause: on a critical success the status bonus lasts 3 rounds instead

requirements.what: No requirement. This raises the WITNESSES' Will DCs against your later challenges — a target-side number the app does not model, which DECIDED SCOPE settles as the player telling the GM. It gets no surface on your sheet; the feat's own text states it.
requirements.clause: creatures who witnessed the challenge gain a +4 circumstance bonus to their Will DCs against your challenges for 1 minute

requirements.what: A marker on the Change Shape action this feat modifies, carrying what is retained: you can speak while in a fox form, and you gain a tail while in a tailless form so that abilities requiring a tail remain usable. Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — and Q8, mark the action the feat modifies. The feat itself grants no action; Change Shape comes from elsewhere.
requirements.clause: when you Change Shape you retain kitsune elements — speak in a fox form, gain a tail in a tailless form to use abilities that require one

requirements.what: The kitsune unarmed Strikes the character already owns must remain available while shape-changed into a tailless form. Nothing new is granted, so no new strike entry is owed — the requirement is on whatever expresses the changed form: it must not suppress those Strikes for a character with this feat.
requirements.clause: use kitsune unarmed attacks in a tailless form

requirements.what: An additional use of the same Change Shape action, listed on that action: re-detailing your hybrid form without changing fully into your true form or your alternate form. This is a second, separate promise about Change Shape and is the one most easily missed once the first is noticed.
requirements.clause: you can Change Shape to alter the details of your hybrid form without fully changing into your true or alternate form

requirements.what: No requirement. The text names no number and grants no bonus or penalty; whether being visibly non-humanoid matters is GM adjudication. Do not invent a Deception or Impersonate penalty the text does not print.
requirements.clause: while in hybrid form your foxlike features make it obvious you aren't a normal humanoid

requirements.what: A named 10-minute activity in the actions list, with its popup carrying: the legal targets (a willing ally, or your construct companion), that it requires a healer's toolkit instead of a disguise kit, that it counts as preparing a disguise to Impersonate, and that a second 10-minute surgery reverses it. Per Principle E the entry with its requirements in the popup is the substance of what is owed.
requirements.clause: perform 10 minutes of surgery with a healer's toolkit to disguise a willing ally or your construct companion, counting as preparing a disguise to Impersonate; reversible with another 10-minute surgery

requirements.what: No requirement. Ruling D's DC-only clause is explicit: a SKILL DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers it. This is your Medicine DC, and the comparison against the disguised character's Deception DC is the GM's to make. Do not build a Medicine-DC row for it.
requirements.clause: the DC to see through the disguise with Seek is your Medicine DC unless the disguised character's Deception DC is higher

requirements.what: No requirement on your sheet. The bonus goes to the disguised character — an ally (Ruling F: an effect landing on someone else is not your sheet's problem) or your own construct companion (★ Companions: a companion's bonus marks the companion). Principle A's indication is already satisfied, because the record that describes the effect IS this feat, not some other ability being modified.
requirements.clause: if the target directly interacts with someone while disguised they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their Deception check

requirements.what: No requirement on your sheet. The free action belongs to the disguised character; if that character is your construct companion it belongs to the companion's block, not yours. No reaction or free-action entry is owed to you.
requirements.clause: the disguised character can end the effect as a free action when they receive any healing effect

requirements.what: A `*` carrying a +2 circumstance bonus restricted to Deception checks to Impersonate a version of yourself who is not a strix — placed on both Deception and the Impersonate action (Q2: star the skill AND the action; Ruling C: every skill that could perform the named action, which for Impersonate is Deception). The restriction lives in the star's `when`; per Ruling B this must NOT become a flat Deception bonus in the stat total, because the bonus applies to one narrow use only.
requirements.clause: +2 circumstance bonus to Deception checks to Impersonate a version of yourself who is not a strix

requirements.what: A separate `*` carrying a +2 circumstance bonus to Stealth checks to Conceal an Object — on both Stealth and the Conceal an Object action (Q2). A distinct clause with a distinct trigger from the Deception one, so it is a second star, not a widening of the first; per the stacking rule, differently-worded `when`s show as two entries.
requirements.clause: +2 circumstance bonus to Stealth checks to Conceal an Object, using your folded wings

requirements.what: The impulse must exist as a named activity in the actions list, carrying its printed action cost, traits, area, and full text. It teaches a new named thing the character can do, so its EXISTENCE is the lane; the internal steps (who is in the area, who rolls) are performed by the player.
requirements.clause: A healing wave splashes across creatures in a [area], its cleansing water driving afflictions from the body.

requirements.what: NOTHING. Healing in an area, landing on you and on allies alike. DECIDED SCOPE / Ruling E: HP and damage never move sheet stats, and an ally-facing effect adds no number to your sheet. The amount lives in the action's own printed text and nowhere else. Do not flag the absent healing number as a defect.
requirements.clause: Each creature in the area regains [N] HP

requirements.what: NOTHING beyond the action's printed text. This is an ordinary save the affected creature attempts — no bonus, no modifier, no new roll on your sheet — and the 'doesn't worsen on a failure' clause is an affliction-track outcome the player and GM apply. It is an internal step of the activity.
requirements.clause: can attempt a new save against one poison or disease affliction affecting it; on a failed save, the condition doesn't worsen

requirements.what: The reuse limitation must be legible in the impulse's popup. It is NOT a per-day resource and must not become a spendable use: it is a per-target 10-minute immunity, and it applies to you as well whenever you benefited. Nothing is tracked or counted down — the clause has to be readable, that is all.
requirements.clause: Each creature that benefited from this impulse becomes temporarily immune to Torrent in the Blood for 10 minutes.

requirements.what: The impulse's value scales with the character's level, so the entry must carry the heightening — either by showing the healing already resolved for this character's level, or by printing the +2 progression alongside the base. A single fixed number here would be wrong for every character above the base level. This is a display requirement on the granted action, not a sheet stat (Ruling E still bars healing from touching any stat).
requirements.clause: **Level (+2)** The healing increases by 1d8.

requirements.what: A reaction in the reactions list, with its trigger — a creature targets you with an attack, even if you aren't aware of it — shown in its popup. Exactly the Minor Omen shape (principle E): the reaction entry is often the whole requirement.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature targets you with an attack, even if you aren't aware of it.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the reaction, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: NOTHING further. A misfortune effect imposed on the ATTACKER's roll — an enemy-facing effect, and the enemy's rolls are not on your sheet. Q4 settles the shape: the reaction entry is the whole surface. Explicitly not a degree-of-success surface and not a modifier anywhere.
requirements.clause: The attacker must roll the attack twice and use the worse result.

requirements.what: Interplanar Teleport appears on the Spells page as an INNATE spell of the divine tradition, at the spell's own rank, with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the granting source.
requirements.clause: You can cast Interplanar Teleport once per day as an innate divine spell

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when cast and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: once per day

requirements.what: The granted casting differs from the spell's printed casting time — 1 minute, not the base spell's. Principle C: a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected IN that thing, so the innate entry must show the 1-minute casting time rather than the spell's native one. A player reading the spell entry must not be shown the unmodified cost.
requirements.clause: with a casting time of only 1 minute

requirements.what: The granted casting is restricted — one legal destination (your deity's realm), you supply the planar key, and arrival is always at the realm's centre. Principle C again: this narrowing must be visible on the innate spell entry, because reading the base spell alone would tell the player something untrue about what this casting can do.
requirements.clause: You act as the planar key for the destination, and you can only travel to your deity's realm. You and the other targets of the spell always appear in the center of your deity's realm

requirements.what: A conditional immunity whose contents are open-ended and GM-determined ('such as toxic air or extreme temperatures') and whose condition is positional — you must be in the realm. It must be readable on the innate spell entry, but it must NOT become an entry in an immunities list: the app cannot enumerate 'the realm's harmful conditions', and Ruling I says where the rules name no specific target, mark nothing rather than guess a mapping. The 'you but not necessarily your allies' half is ally-facing and adds nothing (Ruling F).
requirements.clause: you (but not necessarily your allies) are immune to all the realm's harmful conditions (such as toxic air or extreme temperatures) while there

requirements.what: A distinct capability that costs no spell use and no daily use — a 1-minute return trip carrying up to 8 willing creatures, with no requirement that they were the outbound targets. It must survive somewhere the player will find it. The risk this flags is that surfacing only the spell grant loses this clause entirely, since it is not part of Interplanar Teleport. Whether it also deserves its own exploration-activity entry is an open call I am not making; the minimum is that the text reaches the player alongside the grant.
requirements.clause: You can return to your previous location by spending 1 minute picturing your destination; you can bring up to 8 willing creatures back with you in this way, and they need not be the same targets of the previous casting of interplanar teleport.

requirements.what: A named activity in the actions list — 10 minutes, performed on a willing creature who must stay within your reach the whole time — with its frequency and that requirement shown in its popup.
requirements.clause: It takes 10 minutes to perform these rites on a willing creature, who must remain within your reach the entire time.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed beside the activity, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: A counteract rank derived from the character — half your level rounded up — which must be computed and shown in the activity's entry, not left as prose for the player to work out. It changes at every odd level.
requirements.clause: your counteract rank is half your level rounded up

requirements.what: The player picks which of the two modifiers the text names to use as the counteract modifier, and the resulting number must be computed from the character and shown on the activity. ⚠ The evidence text has both modifier names stripped ('you use either your or modifier') — the requirement is the two-way choice plus a live computed value; I am deliberately not naming the two options, since the text I was given does not contain them.
requirements.clause: you use either your [X] or [Y] modifier as your counteract modifier

requirements.what: A `*` on this activity's counteract check carrying a +1 circumstance bonus, with its condition in the note: the afflicted creature, or whoever laid the curse, is your active Pursue a Lead target. Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing it modifies, which here is this action's own check, not a general stat and not a skill row.
requirements.clause: If the afflicted creature or the individual who placed the curse on the afflicted creature is the target of your active investigation through Pursue a Lead, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this counteract check.

requirements.what: NOTHING. Degree-of-success prose whose effect lands on the target creature and on a cursed item — someone else's sheet and an object's state, both GM-adjudicated. It is printed text inside the activity, not a surface.
requirements.clause: If the curse comes from a cursed item or other external source, a success indicates that the target creature can rid itself of the cursed item, but it doesn't remove the curse from the item.

requirements.what: The action appears in the actions list with its printed action cost and with 'You are in Tiger Stance' shown as its requirement in the popup. The player must be able to see the gate without having to remember it.
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You are in Tiger Stance

requirements.what: NOTHING from this feat. The tiger claw Strike itself is granted by Tiger Stance, not here; making a Strike is an internal step of the activity, and only the activity's existence is a lane.
requirements.clause: Make a tiger claw Strike.

requirements.what: The Strike this action makes deals extra weapon damage dice — two, stepping to three at 14th level. The damage shown for this action must therefore be the tiger claw's damage plus the extra dice, resolved for the character's current level; a bare reprint of the tiger claw's normal damage would be a wrong number, and a fixed '+2 dice' would be wrong from 14th on. This is a level-stepped modification of a specific strike used by a specific action.
requirements.clause: It deals two extra weapon damage dice (three extra dice if you're 14th level or higher)

requirements.what: NOTHING. Forced movement imposed on the enemy — DECIDED SCOPE: effects on enemies and on the battlefield are not your sheet's problem. It stays as printed text in the action.
requirements.clause: you can push the target 5 feet away as if you had successfully Shoved them

requirements.what: Q15 governs and comes first: an effect firing on a critical success needs no implementation unless it is COMPLICATED, and adding an ability modifier to persistent damage is not complicated. So NO computed surface is owed. What remains is principle C's shape — this feat modifies a thing ANOTHER record granted (Tiger Stance's tiger claw and its persistent bleed) — which argues for a marker on that bleed so a player reading the tiger claw sees their own claw has been changed. I flag this as the one judgement call in these five rather than assert it: Q15 says no implementation, principle C says the modified record should show a mark, and the two point different ways for a crit-triggered modification of another record's grant.
requirements.clause: If the attack is a critical success and deals damage, add your Strength modifier to the persistent bleed damage from your tiger claw.
After you deal spirit damage due to Divine Castigation…
requirements.what: A marker on Divine Castigation showing this feat riders it. Principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing — and Q8, which says Ruling D's shape applies: mark the action the feat modifies. The player looks up Divine Castigation when they use it, and that is where they must learn a follow-on effect now exists. This feat is not itself an action and has no trigger of its own to list; it is entirely a rider on another record.

requirements.clause: your weapon or unarmed Strikes gain your holy or unholy trait … until the end of your turn
requirements.what: A `*` on every weapon and unarmed Strike carrying the temporary trait addition. It must NOT be written as a permanent weapon trait — the trait only exists after Divine Castigation and only until end of turn, and a permanent trait entry would state something false about the Strike (Q12: whichever spelling leaves the player least confused). Q1 governs the duration: an effect lasting a round or less is not implemented, indication only, so no mode is owed. The marker must resolve to the character's OWN sanctification — holy or unholy, whichever they have — rather than printing both and leaving the player to work it out.

requirements.clause: and deal additional spirit damage until the end of your turn. The spirit damage is equal to the rank of harm or heal you dealt spirit damage with
requirements.what: A `*` on the damage of every weapon and unarmed Strike carrying the extra spirit damage. The value cannot be a number: it equals the rank of the harm or heal that dealt the spirit damage, a per-cast quantity, so the requirement is text stating the rule, not a computed die. Same duration reasoning as the trait clause — indication only under Q1. This shares a surface with the trait clause and should read as one marker, but it is a second, separate promise and losing it would be a distinct defect.

requirements.clause: and is in addition to any spirit damage the weapon already deals (such as from a holy rune)
requirements.what: No separate surface. This is a stacking clarification that belongs in the wording of the damage marker above — it tells the player the feat's spirit damage does not replace a holy rune's. It creates no second entry and no second number.

requirements.clause: Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own.
requirements.what: A builder pick of one cantrip, with the option list FILTERED to cantrips whose tradition is not the character's own. Q9 is explicit: the builder shows only what the player may legally pick, unless they toggle 'show options not meeting prerequisites'. So the picker must know the character's tradition and exclude it — offering the whole cantrip list would let the player make an illegal choice.

requirements.clause: If you prepare spells, you can choose this spell when you prepare your cantrips, in addition to your other options.
requirements.what: For a prepared caster, the chosen cantrip must join the pool of options available at daily preparation. It is an addition to the OPTIONS, not an extra prepared cantrip — the number of cantrips the character prepares must not increase. So the requirement is pool membership plus reachability from the daily-preparation picker, never an extra slot.

requirements.clause: If you have a spell repertoire, replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell.
requirements.what: For a spontaneous caster, a SECOND choice: which known cantrip is given up. The chosen cantrip replaces it, so the total number of cantrips known is unchanged and the replaced one must actually leave the repertoire. The branch is decided by the character's own casting type — the same feat owes a different shape to a prepared caster than to a repertoire caster, and a character with neither gets nothing.

requirements.clause: You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition.
requirements.what: The granted cantrip must appear inside the character's own class spellcasting entry and be labelled with the character's tradition, not the tradition it was borrowed from. It is cast with the class's spell attack and spell DC. Q12 settles the labelling: the sheet must not assert something false about the spell, and a cantrip filed under the source tradition would be wrong for every tradition-sensitive ruling the player makes at the table.

requirements.clause: If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.
requirements.what: No sheet surface. Principle K — anything the player re-chooses in the builder needs none. The only thing this clause constrains is that the picker must remain re-openable and must not be locked to the alternate tradition chosen the first time; the filter is 'any tradition other than your own', re-evaluated on each pick.

requirements.clause: Strike with your fist unarmed attack and then attempt a High Jump or Long Jump
requirements.what: The activity itself must appear in the actions list with its full text in its popup. Its internal steps — make the fist Strike, then attempt the jump — are performed by the player and are not separate lanes; only the activity's existence is one. The popup should name the fist unarmed attack it uses so the player knows the activity is unavailable without one.

requirements.clause: you count as having a running start and do not need to Stride before this activity to avoid failure
requirements.what: A `*` on High Jump and on Long Jump carrying the running-start clause, with its `when` scoped to jumping as part of this activity. Q8 and Ruling D put the mark on the action the feat modifies, and Q2 says star the skill AND the action, so Athletics carries it too — the player checking their jump number is exactly the moment this matters. It changes no number, so it is text on those entries, not a modifier.

requirements.clause: you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Athletics check to High Jump or Long Jump when you do so
requirements.what: A restricted +2 circumstance bonus on Athletics, its `when` naming the condition — you Struck an unattended object or unoccupied flat surface. Ruling B: a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in the situational lane with the restriction in its `when`, NOT in the passive total, so it must not be added into the Athletics modifier. Q2 again: star the skill and the High Jump / Long Jump actions both.

requirements.clause: You can attempt this Strike against an unattended object or unoccupied flat surface. / *PFS Note:* For the purposes of this feat, the AC of an unoccupied surface is 10.
requirements.what: No requirement beyond the text sitting in the activity's popup. The permission is a rule about a legal target and the AC 10 line is a target-side number — DECIDED SCOPE rules that target-side numbers the app does not model (the target's AC, cover) get no surface: 'this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm'.

requirements.clause: When you Stride in a straight line, if you move at least half your Speed over ground, you can move any amount of the remaining distance across a level body of water.
requirements.what: A `*` on the Stride action and on the land Speed entry carrying the whole clause — straight line, at least half your Speed over ground first, remainder across level water. It changes no number: the Speed value is unaltered, this only widens the terrain it may cross. Ruling H governs the placement — where the rules are open, star everything plausible with the printed trigger in the note, since the player may be reading either Stride or their Speed line when this matters.

requirements.clause: (the feat grants no movement type)
requirements.what: Explicitly NO speed entry is owed. The feat grants no swim, fly, or water-walk Speed and adds no feet to your Speed — it is a conditional permission on ordinary Stride movement. Q7 reserves the starred-speed shape for a granted movement type whose value is conditional; inventing a speed row here would state a movement type the character does not have. Recorded as a requirement so the absence is not later read as a gap.

requirements.clause: If you don't end your Stride on solid ground, you fall into the water.
requirements.what: No separate surface — the failure consequence is part of the same marker's text. It is an outcome the GM adjudicates and it moves no stat, so it needs wording, not a lane of its own.

requirements.clause: If you're legendary in Athletics, as long as you start on solid ground, any part of your Stride can cross the water's surface, even if you aren't moving a straight line, though you still fall into the water if you don't end your movement on solid ground.
requirements.what: The marker's text must be conditional on the character's Athletics proficiency rank and must show the upgraded version once Athletics is legendary — start on solid ground, no straight-line requirement, any part of the Stride. Ruling G: an upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it, so a legendary character must not see both the straight-line restriction and its removal at once. The fall-in-if-you-don't-end-on-solid-ground clause survives the upgrade and must remain in the replacement text.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use per day displayed with the ability, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations.

requirements.clause: When you use this ability… or until you use this action again to return to your normal form
requirements.what: The ability must appear in the actions list, and it must be usable a second time to end the form early. That second use is not a second daily use — it is the off switch — so ending the form must not spend the once-per-day resource.

requirements.clause: you gain the benefits of both the 4th-rank Enlarge and Fly spells. This form lasts for 5 minutes or until you use this action again to return to your normal form.
requirements.what: A mode carrying the REAL numbers of both named spells at 4th rank, not a description of them. Q1 gives a mode to anything lasting longer than a round and this runs 5 minutes; Q11 confirms it — the effect can be shut down, so it is a mode rather than a passive bonus. Q3's requirement for a form applies: the mode must really override the stats it names and must make plain that a mode is active and what changed. The 5-minute duration is text inside the mode; minutes are not tracked, so duration is never a timer.

requirements.clause: the benefits of the 4th-rank Enlarge spell
requirements.what: The mode changes the character's size to Huge (Enlarge heightened to 4th) and must apply that spell's riders as numbers rather than prose: the reach increase, the status bonus to damage rolls, and the clumsy condition Enlarge imposes. The values must be taken from Enlarge at 4th rank rather than restated beside it, so the mode stays correct if the spell's own record is the authority.

requirements.clause: the benefits of the 4th-rank Fly spell
requirements.what: A fly Speed inside the mode, equal to the character's Speed as the Fly spell grants it. Because it derives from the character's own Speed rather than a fixed number, it must resolve against that Speed and not be stored as a literal — and it exists only while the mode is on, so it must disappear when the mode is switched off.

requirements.clause: If you have your head gem, it radiates an aura of moonlight, causing creatures that start their turn adjacent to you to become dazzled until the beginning of their turn unless they succeed at a save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
requirements.what: Text inside the mode only, conditional on having the head gem. Nothing lands on the character's own numbers: the dazzled condition falls on enemies (DECIDED SCOPE — effects on enemies are not your sheet's problem) and whether a creature is adjacent is positional, which Ruling M says the app can never know and which the owner settled as a note carrying the positional condition rather than a positional model. The one thing this note MUST state precisely is the DC the enemy rolls against — the higher of the character's class DC and spell DC — because that is a number the player has to read off their own sheet at the table.

The feat is itself an activity the player performs, so it must appear in the actions list as its own entry with its full text in the popup — including that it is only available while the curse maelstrom state is running, since every clause it makes is scoped to that state.
requirements.clause: You gather your curse around you and impel it to pour outward, expanding your maelstrom. … You attempt to Demoralize a creature within the emanation of your curse maelstrom

requirements.what: This feat changes a thing ANOTHER record granted — the curse maelstrom state's emanation radius, +5 feet for the remainder of that state. Principle C: the change must be reflected in the record it modifies, so the curse maelstrom state entry (and its mode, if the state is one) has to show that this feat can expand its emanation by 5 feet, rather than the fact living only in this feat's own text. Ruling M applies to the positional half: the radius is a number and a note on that record, never a modelled aura position.
requirements.clause: The radius of the emanation of your curse maelstrom state increases by 5 feet until the end of your curse maelstrom state.

requirements.what: A `*` on Intimidation AND on the Demoralize action (Q2: both), carrying the clause that you take no penalty for not sharing a language with the target when Demoralizing inside your curse maelstrom emanation. Ruling C means the star goes on every skill that could perform Demoralize, and the note must keep the printed restriction (inside the emanation) rather than reading as a blanket exemption.
requirements.clause: you don't take penalties for not sharing a language with that creature

requirements.what: NOTHING required. The Demoralize attempt itself is an internal step of the activity, and the frightened condition it would impose lands on the enemy — decided scope, not a gap.
requirements.clause: You attempt to Demoralize a creature within the emanation of your curse maelstrom

requirements.what: The feat teaches a named activity, so it needs an entry in the actions list with its printed Requirements line — wielding an UNLOADED hand crossbow or gauntlet bow — shown in its popup (Principle E's shape for a reaction, applied here to an activity: trigger/requirements belong in the popup).
requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're wielding an unloaded hand crossbow or an unloaded gauntlet bow. --- You can fire off a single shot even when it seems like you are unprepared.

requirements.what: NOTHING required. Reloading via Interact and making the ranged Strike are the internal steps of the activity; the app lists the action and the player performs it.
requirements.clause: You Interact to reload your hand crossbow or gauntlet bow and attempt a ranged Strike with it.

requirements.what: The Special clause must be readable in the action's popup: with Repeating Hand Crossbow Training the activity extends to a repeating hand crossbow, loading a whole magazine but firing only one bolt before that magazine jams and is destroyed, and the magazine must be fully replaced before firing again. It is conditional on owning a second feat, so it must not read as unconditional; the magazine's destruction is prose the player applies to their own ammunition, not a computed consumption.
requirements.clause: **Special** If you have the Repeating Hand Crossbow Training feat, you can use this feat with a repeating hand crossbow to load an entire magazine, but the speed means you can fire only one bolt before the magazine jams and becomes useless. You must fully replace a magazine as normal before firing with a repeating hand crossbow after using this ability.

requirements.what: A reaction entry in the reactions list with its trigger — a creature enters a square that would flank you — shown in the popup. Principle E: for most reactions that is the whole requirement.
requirements.clause: **Trigger** A creature enters a square that would flank you. --- Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature.

requirements.what: Principle E is NOT the whole requirement here, because this reaction also states a real numeric exception: the Strike is rolled without the multiple attack penalty and does not advance it. The player needs that where they make the Strike — the reaction's popup must say to use the un-penalized attack number and not to count the Strike toward MAP, otherwise the sheet's attack figures are wrong for this one roll.
requirements.clause: This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

requirements.what: NOTHING required. Disrupting the triggering creature's movement on a critical hit lands on the enemy (decided scope) and is a crit-triggered effect that is not complicated (Q15) — the printed text in the reaction's popup is all that is owed.
requirements.clause: If your attack is a critical hit, the movement is disrupted.

requirements.what: NOTHING required as a granted strike. The text says only "a melee Strike" — the tail is flavour, not a new unarmed attack this feat confers, so no strike needs to be created.
requirements.clause: Enemies who attempt to stab you in the back will be unhappy to find your lashing tail on guard. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature.

requirements.what: A reaction entry in the reactions list, with its trigger — you are targeted by or are in the area of a mental spell or effect — and its frequency shown in the popup, along with the auditory/linguistic descriptor that tells the player when it cannot be used.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** You are targeted by or are in the area of a mental spell or effect. … This is an auditory linguistic effect.

requirements.what: One use per day: a single spendable use displayed on the reaction, consumed when used and restored at daily preparations/rest.
requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per day

requirements.what: A `*` on Intimidation AND on this reaction (Q2: both), carrying that Intimidation is the modifier for this counteract check and that the counteract rank is half your level rounded up. The rank is a formula off your own level, so a bare number cannot convey it — the player needs the derived value or the formula legible where the check is made. This is the same shape the owner accepted for The Truth as I See it's counteract clause.
requirements.clause: attempting a counteract check using your Intimidation modifier with a counteract rank of half your level rounded up

requirements.what: NOTHING required. Ignoring the triggering effect is the reaction's outcome, other creatures remaining affected is an ally/enemy-side fact, and the stupefied condition lands on the source creature — all decided scope.
requirements.clause: If you succeed, you ignore the triggering effect, though any other creatures that were also targeted or in the area are still affected. If the source of the effect you successfully counteracted has an Intelligence modifier of –3 or higher, that creature becomes stupefied for 1 round.

requirements.what: Performance may be rolled in place of Acrobatics, but ONLY for Tumble Through — the substitution must carry its restriction, because an unscoped Performance-for-Acrobatics swap would be wrong everywhere else. Expressed so the Tumble Through action can be attempted with the character's Performance modifier.
requirements.clause: When you attempt to Tumble Through an enemy's space, you can use Performance instead of Acrobatics.

requirements.what: Q2 (both the skill and the action) and Ruling D: the Tumble Through action entry must show that Performance is a legal skill for it and expose that number, and a `*` on Performance must say it can stand in for Acrobatics on Tumble Through — otherwise the substitution exists nowhere the player looks when they roll it.
requirements.clause: you can use Performance instead of Acrobatics

Your shadow reservoir contains a single spell of each spell rank at least 2 levels lower than the highest-rank spell you can cast from your spell slots. This spell must come from your spell list, you must have access to it, and it must require a spell attack roll or a saving throw.
requirements.what: One spell pick per qualifying rank — every rank up to (your highest slot rank minus 2). The number of picks is DERIVED and grows as your top slot rank rises, so new empty picks must appear on level-up rather than being a fixed count fixed at the moment the feat was taken. Per Q9 the picker offers only what may legally be chosen: spells of that rank from your own spell list, that you have access to, and that require a spell attack roll or a saving throw — a filter on the roll-type of the spell, not just on rank and list.

requirements.clause: These spells don't need to be prepared and aren't in your repertoire. Regardless of the way in which you cast spells, you can spontaneously cast a spell from your shadow reservoir by using one of your spell slots of the same rank. If you're a prepared spellcaster, you lose the spell you prepared in that slot.
requirements.what: A castable group on the Spells page that is neither the prepared list nor the repertoire, and that exists identically for a prepared caster and a spontaneous one. Casting from it must be possible from the reservoir entry itself and must spend a spell slot of the SAME rank; for a prepared caster it must additionally consume one specific slot of that rank and expend whatever spell was prepared in it, so the slot must be individually addressable rather than a bare per-rank counter. These picks are permanent, not a daily-preparation choice.

requirements.clause: Spells cast from your shadow reservoir gain the shadow trait, and affected creatures might be able to disbelieve them.
requirements.what: The reservoir entry must show the shadow trait on the spell — the same spell cast any other way does not have it, so the trait belongs to this casting route and not to the spell record. The disbelieve clause is text only; disbelief resolves on the target and is the GM's.

requirements.clause: If the spell requires an attack roll, use the higher of the target's AC or their Will DC. If the spell requires a saving throw, the target uses their Will saving throw or the spell's normal saving throw, whichever is higher.
requirements.what: Printed text carried on the reservoir entries, where the player is standing when they cast from the reservoir. Both halves are target-side numbers the sheet never models (the enemy's AC, Will DC, and save choice), so no computation is owed — but the substitution changes how the roll is resolved, so it must be legible at the point of casting rather than buried in the feat's own description.

requirements.clause: Each time a creature fails its saving throw against a spell cast from your reservoir, you gain a small tattoo inked on your flesh out of pure shadowstuff.
requirements.what: Nothing. Purely cosmetic accumulation with no mechanical consequence anywhere in the text — no counter, no resource, no threshold it feeds.

requirements.clause: If you have more than one source of spells you can cast with spell slots, such as if you're a spellcaster with a multiclass archetype, choose one source of spells for your shadow reservoir.
requirements.what: A builder choice of WHICH slot-based casting source the reservoir attaches to, offered only when the character actually has more than one. The answer is load-bearing for the clause above it: the chosen source determines both the spell list the picks are filtered against and which 'highest-rank spell you can cast' sets the reservoir's ceiling. Per K, re-choosing is a builder action and needs no separate sheet surface.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** You succeed at a check to Tumble Through or use Tumbling Strike, and you moved through an enemy's space. --- You attempt to Disarm the enemy whose space you moved through.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list at its printed cost, with its trigger stated in the popup — succeeding at Tumble Through, or using Tumbling Strike, having moved through an enemy's space. Per E/exemplar 7 the entry plus its trigger is the whole surface for the trigger clause.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per minute
requirements.what: The once-per-minute frequency shown on the entry. This is not a per-day or per-rest resource and must not be modelled as one — a spendable use that only refills at daily preparations would be wrong. The requirement is that the frequency is legible on the action the player is about to use.

requirements.clause: You can use Acrobatics instead of Athletics for this check.
requirements.what: Acrobatics may be rolled in place of Athletics, scoped to the Disarm made by THIS action only — not a general Athletics-to-Acrobatics substitution, and not a general licence to Disarm with Acrobatics. The substitution has to be visible where the player looks up the number they are about to roll, which for a feat named after an action means the Disarm the action performs (Ruling C/D).

requirements.clause: You attempt to Disarm the enemy whose space you moved through.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the action existing. Performing the Disarm is an internal step of the activity — the sheet lists the action, the player performs it — and the disarm lands on the enemy.

requirements.clause: You can cast Eclipse Burst as a primal innate spell once per day.
requirements.what: Eclipse Burst appears on the Spells page as an innate spell of the PRIMAL tradition, cast at the spell's own rank (the text names no other rank), with its details reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source. The tradition must be legible for this entry specifically — a character can hold innate grants of several traditions at once and the sheet must not state a tradition this spell does not have (Q12).

requirements.clause: once per day
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed beside the innate spell, consumed when it is cast and restored at daily preparations. The entry must not read as unlimited.

requirements.clause: When you Cast the Spell, the sun or moon appears to eclipse to all creatures within 500 feet of you. For 1 round after Casting the Spell, the area is reduced to dim light.
requirements.what: A marker on THIS innate Eclipse Burst entry carrying the rider, because the feat changes what its own granted casting does relative to the printed spell (principle C — a feat that modifies another record's granted thing must be reflected in that thing). Indication only, no numbers: the duration is 1 round (Q1), and the dim light is an environmental change in a 500-foot area rather than anything on your sheet.

requirements.clause: When you cast Heal, you roll d10s instead of d8s.
requirements.what: The Heal spell's displayed healing formula must read d10 everywhere it would read d8 — its 1-action, 2-action and 3-action variants and its heightened line all quote the die, so every one of them changes — and the new die REPLACES the printed one rather than sitting beside it as a separate bonus (Ruling G). The feat is named as the source of the change. The change follows the spell, not one casting route: it applies wherever the character casts Heal from, including a grant from another feat or an item. Nothing else is owed — Heal restores Hit Points, and HP never moves a sheet stat (Ruling E), so there is no stat total to adjust.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're wielding a firearm or crossbow in one hand and a slashing (or versatile S) melee weapon in the other. --- Make two Strikes, one each against two separate targets.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list at its printed cost, with the Requirements line — a firearm or crossbow in one hand and a slashing or versatile-S melee weapon in the other — stated in its popup. Both halves of the requirement are a wielding state, so the popup text is the surface a player checks before using it.

requirements.clause: Each of these attacks takes a –2 penalty to the attack roll, but the two count as only one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty.
requirements.what: Two separate promises in one sentence. (a) The –2 attack penalty must be visible where the player rolls the two Strikes this action makes — it is a penalty to a specific roll under a specific circumstance, so it belongs on the strikes this action performs, not on the character's attack modifier generally. (b) The multiple-attack-penalty clause is text: the two Strikes together advance MAP by one step instead of two. MAP sequencing within a turn is not tracked on a sheet, so this is a printed clause the player applies, but it must travel with the action.

requirements.clause: The targets must be adjacent to each other and within your weapon's maximum range.
requirements.what: Nothing beyond the printed text in the popup. Target adjacency and range to the enemy are battlefield positioning the sheet can never know, and the Strikes themselves are internal steps of the activity.

requirements.clause: **Trigger** Your turn begins. --- You can use unstable clockwork devices in your innovation to push your invention to act more quickly.
requirements.what: The feat teaches a triggered ability, so it must appear as its own entry in the character's action list with its trigger — "Your turn begins" — printed in its popup. This is Principle E's shape (exemplar #7, Minor Omen): the entry plus its trigger is the whole surface. Note what the text does NOT print: no action cost and no Frequency line appear in it, so neither may be invented — the entry must be able to carry a triggered ability whose cost the source does not state, rather than being forced into a guessed cost or a fabricated per-day counter.

requirements.clause: You are quickened for this turn.
requirements.what: NOTHING is owed beyond the printed text. Q1 governs: an effect lasting 1 round is not implemented — indication only, and "for this turn" is exactly that. So no mode (a mode is for longer durations), no tracked quickened condition, and no action-economy model: the app is not required to know the character has an extra action this turn. The word "quickened" and its meaning live in the action's popup text and nowhere else.

requirements.clause: How you can use the extra action depends on your innovation. - **Armor** You can use the extra action to Step, Stride, or use another movement action granted by your innovation (such as Swim if you have the Diving Armor feat). - **Construct** ... - **Weapon** ...
requirements.what: The popup must carry the FULL text of the three innovation branches, because what the extra action may legally be spent on differs by which innovation the character built — the player cannot use the ability from a summary. This is Principle B's shape applied to an action rather than a mode: carry the whole text including the parts the app cannot compute. The individual uses named inside the branches (Step, Stride, Swim, Command your construct, Strike, Reload) are internal steps of an activity and are explicitly NOT lanes — the sheet lists the ability, the player performs it. Filtering the text down to only the character's own innovation would be a display nicety, not a requirement.

requirements.clause: As you use your magic to manipulate air or water, you spin off some of its currents to form a barrier around you. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with the air or water trait...
requirements.what: The feat gives the character something they DO — the whole effect is conditioned on what their NEXT action is, which only makes sense as a discrete action spent first — so it needs a reachable entry in the action list, with the condition (your next action must be a Cast a Spell carrying the air or water trait) legible in its popup. The printed text states no action cost, so no cost should be invented; the entry must tolerate that. Nothing links this to the spell list: the condition is checked by the player at the table, not by the sheet.

requirements.clause: until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC or a +2 circumstance bonus against ranged attacks
requirements.what: Indication only, no computed number. Q1 is decisive: "until the start of your next turn" is a 1-round duration, and effects lasting 1 round are not implemented — a longer duration would earn a mode, this does not. So no AC modifier, no ranged-attack-AC modifier, no display-only mode either. What the popup text MUST convey is that there are two mutually exclusive branches and the player picks one (+1 circumstance to AC, or +2 circumstance specifically against ranged attacks) — an either/or the player resolves at the table. Because it is not implemented, no picker is owed for that choice.

requirements.clause: You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all saves against effects with the air trait, water trait, or both until the start of your next turn, depending on the spell's traits.
requirements.what: A second, separately-worded promise that is easy to read past — and it too is 1 round, so Q1 again yields indication only: the sentence must be readable in the action's popup, and no save modifier is owed. Worth recording the counterfactual so the reasoning is auditable rather than accidental: had this bonus persisted long enough to be implemented, Q2 would apply it to all three saves (star the skill AND the action; when it applies to saves generally, star all three). As printed, it is untracked text.

requirements.clause: This effect has the air or water trait, or both, depending on the traits of the spell you cast.
requirements.what: No requirement. This is trait bookkeeping on an effect the sheet does not track at all (per Q1), and it exists so the GM can adjudicate later interactions with air/water effects. It is printed prose inside the popup, nothing more.

requirements.clause: You gain a vitality blast ranged unarmed Strike that deals 1d4 damage, has a range of 30 feet, and has the unarmed and versatile vitality traits.
requirements.what: A new Strike named Vitality Blast must appear among the character's Strikes, carrying all four printed facts: it is RANGED (with a 30-foot range shown — an unarmed strike with a range is unusual and the range must survive onto the entry), its damage die is 1d4, and it carries the unarmed and versatile vitality traits. Its attack bonus and damage must compute as an unarmed strike does for this character — proficiency, attribute modifier, and anything that legitimately applies to unarmed attacks. ⚠ The text names no damage TYPE for the 1d4; the sheet must be able to show the strike as printed rather than having a type guessed for it.

requirements.clause: ...has the unarmed and versatile vitality traits.
requirements.what: Versatile is a functional trait, not a label: it means the player may deal vitality damage instead of the strike's normal damage. So the strike entry must be able to express a selectable alternate damage type, or at minimum surface the option where the player reads the strike's damage. A strike that merely prints the word "versatile" without any route to the vitality damage type has not delivered the clause.

requirements.clause: Additionally, when you use Stunning Fist, instead of saving against being stunned, you can choose to have the target make a Fortitude save against your class DC with the following results. You must choose to do this before the target rolls its save.
requirements.what: This feat changes what ANOTHER record already granted (Stunning Fist, which the character holds from a different feat), so Principle C and Q8 both apply: the alternative must be reflected IN Stunning Fist — a marker on that action showing this feat offers a different save — with the alternative's terms in its popup. Two details must survive into that popup: the save is Fortitude against YOUR class DC (a stat the sheet already carries; no bonus is granted to it, so no star on class DC is owed), and the choice is locked in BEFORE the target rolls. A marker parked only on this feat's own entry fails the clause, because the moment the player needs it is when they use Stunning Fist.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The target is unaffected. **Success** ...the target is Enfeebled 2, and any time it attempts to take an action with the manipulate trait, the action is disrupted unless it succeeds at a flat check with a DC equal to 5 + its enfeebled value. **Failure** As success, but the duration is 1 minute. **Critical Failure** ...–10-foot status penalty to all Speeds...
requirements.what: No surface beyond printed text. Every outcome lands on the ENEMY — a condition on the target, a flat check the target rolls, a Speed penalty the target takes — and DECIDED SCOPE settles that enemy conditions and target-side numbers get nothing on your sheet ("this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm"). The four degrees of success are display prose inside the Stunning Fist marker's popup. The 1-minute durations do not promote this to a mode either: the duration runs on the enemy, not on you.

requirements.clause: ⚠ ADDED BY ME, not present in the printed text: the record is named a Stance.
requirements.what: ⚠ FLAGGED, NOT ASSUMED. The printed text never says "stance", never describes an action to enter, and grants the strike in flat unconditional language — read strictly, the Strike and the Stunning Fist option are always available. But the record's name declares it a Stance, and if the stance trait in fact applies then both clauses belong to a toggleable state: an action to enter it, exclusivity against other stances, and the strike appearing only while it is on. I am raising this rather than deciding it, because resolving it changes whether the strike is a permanent entry or a mode-gated one, and the text I was given cannot settle it.

requirements.clause: You create a tune so catchy, your foes can't help but dance along. Attempt a Performance check against the Will DCs of all enemies in a [area].
requirements.what: The feat teaches a new named activity, so Catchy Tune must exist as its own entry in the character's action list with its full text — the Performance check it calls for, the area it covers, and the four degrees of success — reachable from that entry. The text prints no action cost and no frequency, so neither may be invented.

requirements.clause: ...against the Will DCs of all enemies in a .
requirements.what: ⚠ THE PRINTED AREA IS MISSING. The sentence ends "in a ." — the area template did not substitute, so the source text states no radius and no shape. The area is mechanical and load-bearing: without it the player cannot know who the action reaches, and no other clause supplies it. So whatever displays this action must be able to carry a real area, and this record's text cannot currently supply one. This is a defect in the text itself rather than a missing sheet capability, and it must not be silently papered over by inventing a radius.

requirements.clause: Attempt a Performance check...
requirements.what: No requirement. Rolling the check is an internal step of the activity — the sheet lists the action, the player performs it — and the manual is explicit that "attempt an [skill] check" is not a lane. Note also that no BONUS is named here, so Ruling C / Principle D do not fire: there is nothing to star on Performance. A star would put a mark on the skill for no modifier, which is exactly the noise those rulings exist to prevent.

requirements.clause: **Critical Success** The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speed and is off-guard, both for 1 round. **Success** ...a –5-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 round. **Critical Failure** The target is temporarily immune for 1 hour.
requirements.what: Nothing on your sheet. Every result lands on an enemy — their Speed, their off-guard state, their temporary immunity — and DECIDED SCOPE rules that effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet are not a gap. The 1-hour temporary immunity is likewise the enemy's bookkeeping, tracked by the GM, not a per-day resource of yours, so it is not limitedUses. The prose belongs in the action's popup and stops there.

requirements.clause: After you Impersonate someone else using a disguise kit, you can remove your disguise with a dramatic gesture.
requirements.what: The feat teaches something the character DOES at a specific moment, so it needs its own entry in the action list, with its condition in the popup: it may only be used after Impersonating someone with a disguise kit, and its window is the current turn. The disguise-kit requirement is an equipment condition printed in that popup — a requirement, not a lane of its own, and not a reason to touch inventory. The text states no action cost, so none should be invented for the entry.

requirements.clause: After you Impersonate someone else using a disguise kit...
requirements.what: ⚠ MY READING, extending Q8/Ruling D rather than quoting an owner ruling on this feat. The moment this feat matters is while the player is Impersonating, so the mark belongs on Impersonate (and hence wherever the character's Deception actions are read) — "the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters." Strictly, the feat keys off Impersonate rather than altering its outcome, so a reader could argue the feat's own entry is the whole surface; I am flagging it because the difference is whether a player who never opens the feat ever learns the follow-up exists.

requirements.clause: Any creatures that previously failed to see through your disguise are off-guard against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.
requirements.what: No requirement. This is settled twice over: the owner's own answer to exemplar #6 (Mastermind's Eye) states that "the off-guard clause itself lands on the enemy and adds nothing," and DECIDED SCOPE rules target-side numbers — the enemy's AC while off-guard — out of the model entirely. It is not a situational star on your attack rolls either: the sheet does not know which creatures failed the earlier check, and the bonus is a consequence of the target's lowered AC rather than a modifier on you. The sentence is text in the action's popup.

Ranger's Bramble appears among the character's spells as a FOCUS spell (a warden spell), castable by spending a Focus Point, with its own description reachable from the entry and this feat named as the source that granted it.
requirements.clause: "You gain the Ranger's Bramble warden spell."

requirements.what: +1 to the focus pool's MAXIMUM, so the pool the sheet displays (and the number Refocus restores toward) is one larger. This is a second, separate promise from the spell grant and is the one commonly missed when a feat's headline is the spell.
requirements.clause: "Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1."

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. "You can cause plants to grow and trap your foes with thorns" is flavour.
requirements.clause: opening sentence

requirements.what: Activating this costs one Mythic Point. The sheet must hold a spendable Mythic Point resource that this activation draws from and decrements — the cost is part of the promise, not preamble.
requirements.clause: "Spend a Mythic Point"

requirements.what: A one-minute duration is longer than a round, so per Q1 this is a MODE the player turns on, and per Q3's shape the sheet must make plain the mode is active and what it changed. The mode carries real numbers: a +10-foot STATUS bonus applied to every Speed the character actually has — land plus any fly, swim, climb or burrow — not to the land Speed alone.
requirements.clause: "for the next minute, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to all your Speeds"

requirements.what: Quickened, and the restriction that the extra action may only be used to Stride, Step, or Leap, must be carried as TEXT inside that same mode. Per-round action economy produces no number the app computes (principle B: the mode carries the full text including the parts it cannot compute), but the player must be able to read what the quickened action may be spent on, because this feat's version is narrower than the general condition.
requirements.clause: "and are quickened. You can use the extra action each round to Stride, Step, or Leap."

requirements.what: A +2 ITEM bonus to AC that applies only while unarmored. The condition is one the sheet can read off the character's own equipment, so this is a computed conditional passive rather than a star (Q11: the player cannot shut it off, so it is a passive bonus) — the AC total must actually change when armour comes off, and the breakdown must name the source. ⚠ "Unarmored" here must include the unarmored-category armours: the feat's own next sentence assumes you are wearing explorer's clothing while benefiting.
requirements.clause: "When you're unarmored, the scales give you a +2 item bonus to AC with a Dexterity cap of +3."

requirements.what: A Dexterity CAP of +3 on that unarmored AC. This is a second number in the same sentence and is the one usually dropped: while unarmored and benefiting from the scales, the Dex modifier contributed to AC is limited to +3, which must be visible in the AC breakdown for a high-Dex character to understand their number.
requirements.clause: "...with a Dexterity cap of +3."

requirements.what: An explicit STACKING EXCEPTION. The general rule is that only the highest item bonus to AC applies; this clause says this one is cumulative with armor potency runes on explorer's clothing, with mage armor, and with bracers of armor. So the AC computation must be able to ADD this item bonus on top of another item bonus to AC from those named sources instead of taking the highest, and the breakdown must show both lines. Nothing in a plain "+2 item bonus to AC" conveys this; it is a distinct promise.
requirements.clause: "The item bonus to AC from Scales of the Dragon is cumulative with armor potency runes on your explorer's clothing, mage armor, and bracers of armor."

requirements.what: This feat changes a value ANOTHER record already granted: the resistance from Dragon Disciple Dedication becomes 3 + half your level. Per principle C it must be reflected in that thing, and per Ruling G an upgrade REPLACES the entry it upgrades rather than sitting beside it — the defences must show one resistance entry at the new value, not the dedication's original number plus a second line. The value is level-scaling, so it must be a formula that moves as the character levels, not a fixed number.
requirements.clause: "Your resistance from Dragon Disciple Dedication increases to 3 + half your level."

requirements.what: A choice made during DAILY PREPARATIONS recording up to five participants. The participants are arbitrary people, so this is free-text player input (principle I) — up to five named entries, each standing for a token the character holds. Re-performing the ritual replaces the previous set rather than adding to it, and that set is what the rest of the feat reads from.
requirements.clause: "During your daily preparations, you can perform a simple ritual with up to five willing Small or Medium humanoids... participants exchange minor tokens of personal significance."

requirements.what: This feat extends an ability granted by another record — Change Shape. Per principle C the modification must be reflected in that thing: the Change Shape entry must show that the recorded participants are available forms, so a player reading Change Shape sees the added options rather than having to remember the feat.
requirements.clause: "As long as you hold onto a participant's token, you can assume their form with your Change Shape ability"

requirements.what: A `*` carrying a +4 STATUS bonus to Deception when passing as a token-holder. Per Q2 star BOTH the skill and the action: Deception itself, and the Impersonate action that "pass as that person" names, so the player meets the note wherever they look the number up. The restriction (only while impersonating a recorded participant) belongs in the star's condition, not in the flat Deception total (Ruling B).
requirements.clause: "gaining a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to pass as that person"

requirements.what: ⚠ A separate promise in the same sentence, and one a flat situational bonus cannot express: the check ADDS YOUR LEVEL even while untrained. That is a change to how the check's proficiency is computed, not an extra number added to it — for an untrained character it is worth your full level, not +4. If a situational entry can only contribute a flat modifier, this clause has no lane and is worth flagging as such rather than being silently folded into the +4.
requirements.clause: "and adding your level to the check even if you're untrained"

requirements.what: Losing a form because the participant is not carrying your token is GM-adjudicated and unknowable to the sheet, so it is text only, printed with the recorded participant list. The other half — losing the forms when you use the ritual again — is already covered by the daily choice replacing its previous set.
requirements.clause: "You lose access to a participant's form if they're not carrying your token or if you use the ritual again."

requirements.what: The Requirements line is the state gate for BOTH effects below and must be legible on the record. The printed text describes no action the character takes — the effects are continuous while the grab persists — so nothing is owed in an actions list from this clause; what is owed is that the condition travels with the effects it gates (it is the wording of the AC star's condition, below).
requirements.clause: "**Requirements** You have an opponent grabbed or restrained."

requirements.what: NO REQUIREMENT. This penalty lands on the enemy, and enemy-side numbers are DECIDED SCOPE — the record's own description is the whole surface (Ruling F, Q4). Do not report the missing penalty as a defect.
requirements.clause: "Your opponent takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their next attempt to Escape from being grabbed or restrained by you"

requirements.what: A `*` on AC carrying a +1 CIRCUMSTANCE bonus, with its restriction in the condition: only against attacks made against you by a creature you currently have grabbed. This is your own number, so it is owed even though the first half of the sentence is not. Per Ruling B it stays out of the flat AC total and sits in the situational list with the restriction spelled out — a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct, not a bug.
requirements.clause: "and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your AC against any attacks they make against you while you have them grabbed"
You gain a +1 circumstance bonus on saving throws against emotion effects.
requirements.what: A +1 circumstance `*` on all three saves — Fortitude, Reflex and Will. "Emotion effects" names no single save (most call for Will but not all), and Q2 settles the shape: when a bonus applies to saves generally, star all three.
