Ruling B keeps it out of the flat save totals — the restriction "against emotion effects" lives in the star's `when`, and a restricted bonus sitting outside the stat total is correct, not a defect. Ruling H forbids narrowing it to Will alone: that would put my ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's.

requirements.clause: If you roll a success on a saving throw against an emotion effect, you get a critical success instead.
requirements.what: A degree-of-success upgrade, which contributes no number at all — nothing on the sheet moves. The requirement is that the text is printed where the player looks the save up: carried in the same three saves' star/popup alongside the +1 (Ruling D — the mark lives on the thing you are looking at when it matters). No separate stat surface, no new row; the player applies the upgrade when the save is actually rolled.

requirements.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Sense Motive
requirements.what: A `*` on Perception AND on the Sense Motive action, carrying "+1 circumstance, Sense Motive only" — Q2 rules both, and Ruling C stars the action's home as well as the skill. Restricted, so it does not enter the flat Perception total (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: and Perception DCs against attempts to Lie to you.
requirements.what: The DC half is defensive — the roll belongs to the creature lying to you, not to the player. Ruling D grants a breakdown entry only to a SAVE DC; this is a Perception DC, and the nearest ruling on it ("a skill DC gets no surface at all — the player remembers") gives it none. So the requirement is only that the same star's note states the +1 also applies to your Perception DC against Lie, worded to say it hits the DC and not the check, so the player does not double it into their own Sense Motive roll. ⚠ Perception DC is not literally named in Ruling D — I am reading it as the nearest case rather than assuming.

requirements.clause: You descend from one of the truly ancient vampires, a nosferatu cursed to eternal life but not eternal youth. People call you straveika, or ancient-born.
requirements.what: Flavour and naming only. No requirement.

requirements.clause: You wrap shadow around a single unattended light source within 120 feet that's no larger than a torch. Any non-magical light source you target is automatically extinguished.
requirements.what: Extinguish Light must exist as a named activity in the actions list, with its action cost, its frequency line and its full printed text reachable in the popup — the same shape the owner gave Minor Omen (principle E: the entry with its trigger/requirements in the popup is often the whole requirement). The target's light going out happens off your sheet and needs no further surface.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once every 10 minutes
requirements.what: The frequency must be legible on the action entry. Note the shape: this is a 10-minute recharge, not a per-day pool — nothing about it is restored by rest or daily preparations, so the surface owed is the printed frequency on the entry rather than a daily use pip.

requirements.clause: If you're in dim light or darkness when you Extinguish Light, its range is 240 feet.
requirements.what: The action has two ranges, not one, and which applies depends on the light you are standing in. Both values must be legible on the entry — this is principle H's shape (an action whose cost changes conditionally appears under both costs, with the explanation in the popup) applied to range instead of cost. A single hardcoded "120 feet" would state something false half the time, which Q12 rules against.

requirements.clause: For magical light sources, attempt a counteract check using your Fortitude or Thievery modifier against the target's DC. Your counteract rank is equal to half your level rounded up. Successfully counteracting the light source suppresses its ability to produce light for 1 minute, but not any other effects.
requirements.what: No requirement. This is the internal step of an activity — the app lists the action, the player performs the check — which the lane manual excludes explicitly. It is NOT a `skillSubstitution`: that lane is for "you can use X in place of Y" as a general licence, whereas this only tells you which modifier this one activity's own check uses. The 1-minute suppression lands on an object on the battlefield, not on your sheet.

requirements.clause: You become trained in Crafting.
requirements.what: Trained rank in Crafting, raising the Crafting proficiency itself.

requirements.clause: If you're already trained in Crafting, you instead gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat for stonemasonry.
requirements.what: A redundancy branch: when the character already has Crafting trained, the trained grant is replaced (not stacked, not silently dropped) by the alternative below. The branch must be evaluated against the character's actual Crafting rank at the time the feat is taken.

requirements.clause: you instead gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat for stonemasonry
requirements.what: On the fallback branch, the character owns the named feat Specialty Crafting, with its details surfaced like any owned feat. Its specialty is fixed at stonemasonry by this feat's own text — so the choice Specialty Crafting normally offers must arrive pre-set and not be presented to the player as an open pick (Q9's principle: the player is only offered what they may legally choose, and here they may choose nothing).

requirements.clause: You also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to notice unusual stonework.
requirements.what: A +2 circumstance `*` on Perception and on the Seek action — Q2 stars the skill and the action, Ruling C stars every route that could perform the noticing. The trigger "to notice unusual stonework" lives in the star's `when`, and the bonus stays out of the flat Perception total (Ruling B).

requirements.clause: This bonus applies to checks to discover mechanical traps made of stone or hidden within stone.
requirements.what: Not a second bonus — the same +2, with its `when` widened. It must be carried in the same star's note so the player sees the trap case where they read the stonework case; two separate stars would read as two stacking bonuses, which Ruling B's stacking display rule warns against.

requirements.clause: If you aren't using the Seek action or searching, the GM automatically rolls a secret check for you to notice unusual stonework anyway. This check doesn't gain your normal circumstance bonus.
requirements.what: The roll is the GM's and is secret, so nothing is computed and no number surfaces — and the clause explicitly denies the +2 to that check. What the player still needs is the printed text in the same star's note, both so they know the passive check exists and so they do not believe the +2 applies to it. Ruling H's shape: printed trigger in the note, one line with a click-through.

requirements.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice
requirements.what: An open choice of one skill, recorded on the character, raising that skill to trained. The pick must be stored, not just displayed, because the next clause depends on it.

requirements.clause: and the Assurance skill feat in that skill as a bonus feat.
requirements.what: The character owns the named feat Assurance, granted by this feat rather than spent from a feat slot, with its details surfaced like any owned feat.

requirements.clause: the Assurance skill feat in that skill
requirements.what: The Assurance instance is bound to the skill chosen in the first clause — "in that skill", not a free pick. The grant must inherit the earlier choice rather than offering the player a second, independent Assurance skill selection; two independent picks would let the character take Assurance in a skill this feat never gave them. Assurance's own consequence (roll 10 + proficiency instead of rolling) is owed by the Assurance record, not by this feat.

requirements.clause: [the feat is an activity — the **Frequency** / **Requirements** / `---` block marks it as one] "You consume a piece of your enemy, absorbing their strength."
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list as a usable entry, with its Requirement ("You are adjacent to an enemy's corpse who has been dead for no longer than 1 minute") printed in its popup. This is principle E's shape applied to an activity rather than a reaction: the entry plus trigger/requirement text in the popup is often the whole requirement. The requirement is a battlefield fact the sheet can never check, so it is printed, never enforced.

requirements.clause: **Frequency** once per hour
requirements.what: One spendable use displayed beside the entry, consumed when used. The recharge period is an HOUR, not a day, so it cannot be folded into daily preparations or rest — the period itself must be legible on the use, and clearing it is the player's act.

requirements.clause: You gain temporary Hit Points equal to the enemy's level that last for 1 minute.
requirements.what: No computed surface and no modifier. The amount is the dead enemy's level, which the sheet can never know, so the number can only be entered by the player, not derived. Ruling E settles the rest: "HP and damage never move sheet stats, even inside a mode." Q15 adds that "temporary Hit Points alone are not complicated", so no mode is earned either. ⚠ Judgement recorded: Q1 would give a 1-minute duration a mode, but a mode here would carry no numbers at all (HP is excluded from modes by name), and Q15 explicitly declines to implement plain temp HP. Ruled: no mode. The requirement is only that the formula ("= enemy's level") and the 1-minute duration are readable in the action's popup.

requirements.clause: You have a fly Speed of 20 feet at all times.
requirements.what: A fly Speed of 20 feet listed in the speeds. NO `*`: Q7 rules the star is for a CONDITIONAL movement type — "Most granted speeds are permanent and need no star" — and "at all times" states the unconditional case outright. It also differs from the Wyrmling Flight exemplar in the way that mattered there: that fly Speed was a formula off your own Speed and needed a star to convey it, whereas this is a flat printed number a speeds row can state exactly. This one clause is the entire feat; nothing else is owed.

requirements.clause: **Requirements** You're not fatigued. --- ... You can attempt to Escape any effect that is currently immobilizing you ... can Stride up to three times. At any point during each of these Strides, you can Strike with a weapon you have familiarity with from this archetype and can then immediately Interact to reload that weapon.
requirements.what: The activity appears in the actions list with its Requirement ("You're not fatigued") in its popup. The internal steps — the Escape attempt, the three Strides, the Strike during each Stride, the Interact to reload — need NO separate surface: the manual excludes the internal steps of an activity, and only the action's existence is a lane. The weapon restriction ("a weapon you have familiarity with from this archetype") is likewise a restriction inside that resolution and belongs in the popup text, not on any weapon entry.

requirements.clause: You gain a +10-foot circumstance bonus to your Speed and can Stride up to three times.
requirements.what: A `*` on Speed carrying "+10 ft circumstance while using Infiltrator's Blitz". Ruling B: a flat bonus the rules restrict belongs in `situational` with the restriction in its `when`, sitting OUTSIDE the stat total — that is correct, not a defect. It earns a surface rather than being written off as an internal step because it is a modifier to a number that has its own row, and the player must read that modified Speed to resolve the three Strides. Principle J puts the star on the specific thing affected, which here is Speed itself.

requirements.clause: After using Infiltrator's Blitz, you become fatigued for 1 minute.
requirements.what: The drawback printed in the activity's popup. It interlocks with the Requirement — using the activity makes you fail your own requirement for the next minute — so both halves must be visible in the same place; showing the requirement without the self-inflicted fatigue would mislead. Duration is not tracked, so applying and clearing the fatigued condition is the player's act. No mode: this is an existing condition landing on the character, not a state the feat itself turns on and off.

requirements.clause: You gain the Jumping Jenny fireworks display.
requirements.what: The named display must reach the sheet as its own usable entry with its details surfaced from that entry — principle G's shape for a granted thing ("its details surfaced"), and the same standard the manual sets for `grantsAction`: the record teaches a new named activity. If the display happens to be stored as a feat record rather than an action record the lane reads `grantsFeat` instead, but the requirement is identical either way: the grant must resolve to a REAL, reachable record, not a dangling name. Everything mechanical (action cost, effect, any DC or duration) lives in that granted record — this feat's own text states no numbers, so nothing else is owed here and the grant is the entire requirement.

requirements.clause: This multi-sequence rocket blasts confetti at a series of altitudes. While the design is intended to delight children of all ages, you've found it has an unexpected side effect of confounding enemy fliers.
requirements.what: Flavour. "Confounding enemy fliers" is narrative framing for what the granted display does, not a second promise this feat makes, and any effect on fliers lands on enemies — excluded by the manual. No surface.

requirements.clause: You call forth a fog bank in a within 120 feet. [an impulse, with a burst area and a 120-foot range]
requirements.what: The impulse appears as a usable entry with its range (120 feet), its burst area, and its duration reachable from the entry. ⚠ The printed text is CORRUPT: "in a within 120 feet" has lost the burst size — no radius survives in the text at all. This is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because the Level (+3) clause below scales "the radius of the burst" from a base this text no longer states, so the area cannot be displayed correctly, at any level, from this record as written. The source text needs the burst size restored before the area clause can be satisfied.

requirements.clause: All creatures in the fog are concealed, and all creatures outside the fog become concealed to creatures within it. The fog is so magically dense it impedes movement, making the area difficult terrain.
requirements.what: No sheet surface. These land on the battlefield and on other creatures, which the manual excludes outright, and whether the fog touches YOU depends on where you are standing — Ruling M: position is something the app can never know, and is not a missing system. No concealed status and no terrain state on your sheet; the printed text inside the impulse's popup is the whole surface.

requirements.clause: The fog lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute.
requirements.what: A DISPLAY-ONLY mode carrying the fog's text and the Sustain cap, with no modifiers whatever. Two standing rulings converge on this: Ruling F/N — "if it runs for a limited time, the character who activated it gets a display-only mode so they can see it running; it changes none of their numbers" — and Ruling E case 3, an ongoing effect that changes no numbers ("you are concealed" is its named example) gets a display-only mode. ⚠ Judgement recorded: the BASE duration is one round, which Q1 would leave as indication only; the mode is earned by the Sustain extension out to 1 minute. If the base duration is taken to govern, indication only is the defensible alternative reading.

requirements.clause: **Level (+3)** You can make the radius of the burst larger. Increase its maximum size by 5 feet.
requirements.lane: no lane in the manual (level-scaled area on a non-spell record)
requirements.what: The area shown must resolve at the character's CURRENT level — base radius +5 feet for every 3 levels above the impulse's own level — the same shape a spell's heightened value takes, so that the player reads one true number instead of a base that has been wrong since the level they gained it. The lane manual lists no route for a level-scaled value on a record that is not a spell, so if no such route exists this is a no-lane candidate rather than an empty field. Minimum acceptable surface if the value cannot be computed: the "(+3): +5 feet" scaling line printed with the entry so the player can resolve it themselves. Blocked in practice by the missing base radius noted above.
